entries.en: Han Xian and Cao Zhen remonstrated with Huai: "By ritual, when the main line lacks heirs a collateral son of the lesser branch carries it on. The law never sanctions adopting heirs of another surname.
entries.literal: Chief of Gentlemen Han Xian and Commandant of Palace Guards Cao Zhen remonstrated with Huai, saying, "By ritual, when the great lineage lacks heirs, a younger-house collateral son succeeds it; there is no text for taking an heir of different surname.

entries.zh: 無令先公懷腆后土，良史書過，豈不痛心。」
entries.en: Do not make your late husband blush before Heaven and earth while historians record the scandal—that should break your heart."
entries.literal: Do not let the former Duke harbor shame toward soil and earth; good historians record faults—would it not pain the heart."

entries.zh: 槐不從。
entries.en: She refused.
entries.literal: Huai did not follow.

entries.zh: 咸等上書求改立嗣，事寢不報。
entries.en: They memorialized to overturn the adoption, but the petition vanished without answer.
entries.literal: Xian and others submitted memorials requesting changing the established heir; the affair slept without reply.

entries.zh: 槐遂表陳是充遺意。
entries.en: Lady Guo then claimed the adoption had been Chong's dying wish.
entries.literal: Huai thereupon memorialized stating this was Chong's dying intention.

entries.zh: 帝乃詔曰：「太宰、魯公充，崇德立勳，勤勞佐命，背世殂隕，每用悼心。
entries.en: The emperor responded: "Grand tutor and duke of Lu Jia Chong served the dynasty with merit until death—Our grief is constant.
entries.literal: The Emperor thereupon issued an edict stating, "Grand Tutor, Duke of Lu Chong, elevated virtue and established merit, toiled in assisting the mandate; departed from the age and fell—each time Our mourning heart.

entries.zh: 又胤子早終，世嗣未立。
entries.en: His natural heirs died young; the main line stood empty.
entries.literal: Moreover heir sons ended early; lineage succession was not established.

entries.zh: 古者列國無嗣，取始封支庶，以紹其統，而近代更除其國。
entries.en: Ancient states without heirs adopted cadets from the founding line, though modern precedent sometimes abolished fiefs outright.
entries.literal: In antiquity when feudal states lacked heirs, they took collateral sons from the first enfeoffment to continue its line; yet in recent generations states were abolished.

entries.zh: 至於周之公旦，漢之蕭何，或豫建元子，或封爵元妃，蓋尊顯勳庸，不同常例。
entries.en: Zhou's Duke of Zhou and Han's Xiao He enjoyed special privileges—early designation of heirs or honors for wives—because extraordinary merit broke ordinary rules.
entries.literal: As for Zhou's Duke Dan, Han's Xiao He—some beforehand established eldest sons, some enfeoffed chief consorts—covering honoring and displaying merit achievement, different from ordinary precedent.

entries.zh: 太宰素取外孫韓謐為世子黎民後。
entries.en: The grand tutor had already chosen grandson Han Mi to continue Limin's line.
entries.literal: The Grand Tutor long ago took grandson-by-daughter Han Mi as heir-apparent Limin's successor.

entries.zh: 吾退而斷之，外孫骨肉至近，推恩計情，合于人心。
entries.en: We weighed the matter: a daughter's son is close kin, and extending favor to him fits human feeling.
entries.literal: We withdrew and judged it: grandson-by-daughter flesh and bone extremely close; extending grace calculating sentiment accords with men's hearts.

entries.zh: 其以謐為魯公世孫，以嗣其國。
entries.en: Let Han Mi inherit the duchy of Lu as Chong's designated grandson.
entries.literal: Let Mi be Duke of Lu's lineage grandson, to succeed its state.

entries.zh: 自非功如太宰，始封無後如太宰，所取必以己自出不如太宰，皆不得以為比。」
entries.en: Unless merit equals the grand tutor's, unless the founding line fails as his did, and unless the heir springs from one's own issue as Han Mi did, no one may cite this case."
entries.literal: Unless merit be like the Grand Tutor, first enfeoffment lacking heirs like the Grand Tutor, those taken must issue from oneself not inferior to the Grand Tutor—none may take this as precedent."

entries.zh: 及下禮官議充諡，博士秦秀議諡曰荒，帝不納。
entries.en: When ritual officers debated Chong's posthumous name, Erudite Qin Xiu proposed "Desolate"; the emperor rejected it.
entries.literal: When it came to handing down to ritual officials deliberating Chong's posthumous title, Erudite Qin Xiu deliberated posthumous title as wasteful; the Emperor did not adopt.

entries.zh: 博士段暢希旨，建議諡曰武，帝乃從之。
entries.en: Erudite Duan Chang, angling for imperial favor, suggested "Martial," which the emperor accepted.
entries.literal: Erudite Duan Chang hoped for imperial intention, proposed deliberating posthumous title as martial; the Emperor thereupon followed it.

entries.zh: 自充薨至葬，賻賜二千萬。
entries.en: Between his death and burial the court lavished twenty million cash in funeral grants.
entries.literal: From Chong's death until burial, burial gifts totaled twenty million.

entries.zh: 惠帝即位，賈后擅權，加充廟備六佾之樂，母郭為宜城君。
entries.en: Under Emperor Hui, Empress Jia dominated politics: Chong's shrine gained six rows of ritual dancers and Lady Guo received the title lady of Yicheng.
entries.literal: When Emperor Hui assumed the throne, Empress Jia monopolized authority; Chong's temple was augmented with six-row music; mother Guo became Lady of Yicheng.

entries.zh: 及郭氏亡，諡曰宣，特加殊禮。
entries.en: When Lady Guo died she received the posthumous name "Declarative" and honors beyond the usual.
entries.literal: When the Guo clan lady died, her posthumous title was Declarer; exceptionally added special rites.

entries.zh: 時人譏之，而莫敢言者。
entries.en: Contemporaries sneered but kept silent.
entries.literal: People of the time mocked this, yet none dared speak.

entries.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
entries.en: Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui's firstborn—his mother was Lady Xie of Talented rank.
entries.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

entries.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
entries.en: Wu Di doted on the bright boy and kept him always near.
entries.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

entries.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
entries.en: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'
entries.literal: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'

entries.zh: 惠帝乃止。
entries.en: Hui broke off his greeting.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.

entries.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
entries.en: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.
entries.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

entries.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
entries.en: Five-year-old Yu pulled his grandfather into the dark.
entries.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

entries.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
entries.en: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."
entries.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

entries.zh: 由是奇之。
entries.en: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.
entries.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.

entries.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
entries.en: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"
entries.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'

entries.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
entries.en: Wu Di approved and had them slaughtered.
entries.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

entries.zh: 因撫其背，謂廷尉傅祗曰：「此兒當興我家。」
entries.en: He stroked the boy's back and told Court Commandant Fu Zhi, "This child will bring prosperity to our house."
entries.literal: He therefore stroked the boy's back and said to Court Commandant Fu Zhi, 'This child will bring prosperity to our house.'

entries.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。
entries.en: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.
entries.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.

entries.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
entries.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
entries.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

entries.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
entries.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
entries.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

entries.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
entries.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
entries.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

entries.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
entries.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
entries.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

entries.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
entries.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

entries.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
entries.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
entries.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

entries.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
entries.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
entries.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

entries.zh: 九年六月，有桑生於宮西廂，日長尺餘，數日而枯。
entries.en: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the palace’s west wing. It grew more than a chi each day, then withered after several days.
entries.literal: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the west wing of the palace; it grew more than a chi each day and withered after several days.

entries.zh: 十二月，賈后將廢太子，詐稱上不和，呼太子入朝。
entries.en: Twelfth month Jia feigned imperial illness to lure Yu to court.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, when Empress Jia would depose the crown prince, she falsely claimed the emperor was unwell and summoned the crown prince to court.

entries.zh: 既至，後不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞賜以酒棗，逼飲醉之。
entries.en: She hid him, fed him wine and dates through Chen Wu until he was drunk.
entries.literal: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.

entries.zh: 使黃門侍郎潘岳作書草，若禱神之文，有如太子素意，因醉而書之，令小婢承福以紙筆及書草使太子書之。
entries.en: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.
entries.literal: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the crown prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.

entries.zh: 文曰：「陛下宜自了；
entries.en: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;
entries.literal: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;

entries.zh: 不自了，吾當入了之。
entries.en: Or I will finish you.
entries.literal: if you do not end it yourself, I shall come in and end it for you.

entries.zh: 中宮又宜速自了；
entries.en: The empress too should quickly end her own life;
entries.literal: The empress too should quickly end her own life;

entries.zh: 不了，吾當手了之。
entries.en: Or I will kill her myself.
entries.literal: if she does not, I shall end her life with my own hands.

entries.zh: 並謝妃共要克期而兩發，勿疑猶豫，致後患。
entries.en: Consort Xie and I strike together—no delay.
entries.literal: Together with Consort Xie we agreed a joint date for simultaneous rising—do not hesitate and breed later trouble.

entries.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣為內主。
entries.en: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.
entries.literal: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.

entries.zh: 願成，當三牲祠北君，大赦天下。
entries.en: Then sacrifice to the Northern Lord and amnesty all.
entries.literal: When wish is fulfilled we shall sacrifice three victims to the Northern Lord and proclaim an empire-wide amnesty.

entries.zh: 要疏如律令。」
entries.en: So commands the spell.'
entries.literal: Let this sworn petition take effect as commanded.

entries.zh: 太子醉迷不覺，遂依而寫之，其字半不成。
entries.en: Too drunk and confused to realize what he was doing, the crown prince copied it, but half the characters were incomplete.
entries.literal: The crown prince was too drunk and confused to notice; he copied accordingly; half the characters failed to form.

entries.zh: 既而補成之，后以呈帝。
entries.en: Helpers patched characters before Jia showed Hui.
entries.literal: They afterward filled them in; the empress presented it to the emperor.

entries.zh: 帝幸式乾殿，召公卿入，使黃門令董猛乙太子書及青紙詔曰：「遹書如此，今賜死。」
entries.en: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: "Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death."
entries.literal: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: 'Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death.'

entries.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者，惟張華、裴頠證明太子。
entries.en: Silence fell until Zhang Hua and Pei Wei defended Yu.
entries.literal: No one among lords and dukes spoke except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei who verified the crown prince's innocence.

entries.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各有不同，若有不從詔，宜以軍法從事。」
entries.en: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: "Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law."
entries.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: 'Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law.'

entries.zh: 議至日西不決。
entries.en: Debate stalled till dusk.
entries.literal: Deliberation lasted until sunset unresolved.

entries.zh: 後懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
entries.en: Jia feared delay—demoted Yu to commoner instead.
entries.literal: The empress feared events might shift and therefore memorialized to degrade the crown prince to commoner status; an edict approved.

entries.zh: 於是使尚書和郁持節，解結為副，及大將軍梁王肜、鎮東將軍淮南王允、前將軍東武公澹、趙王倫、太保何劭詣東宮，廢太子為庶人。
entries.en: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.
entries.literal: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.

entries.zh: 是日太子游玄圃，聞有使者至，改服出崇賢門，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車。
entries.en: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.
entries.literal: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.

entries.zh: 澹以兵仗送太子妃王氏、三皇孫于金墉城，考竟謝淑妃及太子保林蔣俊。
entries.en: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.
entries.literal: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.

entries.zh: 明年正月，賈后又使黃門自首，欲與太子為逆。
entries.en: Next New Year Jia staged a Yellow Gate confession implicating Yu.
entries.literal: The next first month Empress Jia again had a Yellow Gate confess plotting rebellion with the crown prince.

entries.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿。
entries.en: An edict circulated the Yellow Gate eunuch’s confession among the dukes and ministers.
entries.literal: An edict circulated the confession among dukes and ministers.

entries.zh: 又遣澹以千兵防送太子，更幽于許昌宮之別坊，令治書御史劉振持節守之。
entries.en: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.
entries.literal: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.

entries.zh: 先是，有童謠曰：「東宮馬子莫聾空，前至臘月纏汝閤。」
entries.en: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: "Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber."
entries.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: 'Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber.'

entries.zh: 又曰：「南風起兮吹白沙，遙望魯國郁嵯峨，千歲髑髏生齒牙。」
entries.en: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'
entries.literal: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'

entries.zh: 南風，后名；
entries.en: South Wind' meant Empress Jia.
entries.literal: South Wind' was the empress's name.

entries.zh: 沙門，太子小字也。
entries.en: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
entries.literal: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.

entries.zh: 太子既廢非其罪，眾情憤怨。
entries.en: Injustice against Yu enraged the capital.
entries.literal: After the crown prince was deposed without crime, popular feeling seethed with anger.

entries.zh: 右衛督司馬雅，宗室之疏屬也，與常從督許超並有寵于太子，二人深傷之，說趙王倫謀臣孫秀曰：「國無適嗣，社稷將危，大臣之禍必起。
entries.en: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: "The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.
entries.literal: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: 'The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.

entries.zh: 而公奉事中宮，與賈后親密，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一旦事起，禍必及矣。
entries.en: "You serve the empress and are close to her. Everyone says you knew in advance of the prince’s deposition. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you too."
entries.literal: You serve the inner palace in the empress's confidence; all say you foreknew the crown prince's deposition—should trouble erupt, disaster will reach you too.

entries.zh: 何不先謀之！」
entries.en: Why not plot first!"
entries.literal: Why not plot first!'

entries.zh: 秀言于趙王倫，倫深納焉。
entries.en: Sun Xiu sold the plot to Sima Lun.
entries.literal: Xiu reported to Lun, Prince of Zhao, and Lun accepted fully.

entries.zh: 計既定，而秀說倫曰：「太子為人剛猛，若得志之日，必肆其情性矣。
entries.en: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, "The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.
entries.literal: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, 'The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.

entries.zh: 明公素事賈后，街談巷議，皆以公為賈氏之黨。
entries.en: Lun was branded Jia's man.
entries.literal: You have long served Empress Jia; street talk names you a Jia partisan.

entries.zh: 今雖欲建大功于太子，太子雖將含忍宿忿，必不能加賞於公，當謂公逼百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳。
entries.en: Yu would not thank Lun for a late defection.
entries.literal: Now even if you wish to build great merit for the crown prince, though he may swallow old rage for a time he cannot reward you—he will think you only reversed under popular pressure to escape blame.

entries.zh: 若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。
entries.en: One slip and Lun's head would roll.
entries.literal: If any flaw appears you will still not escape execution.

entries.zh: 不若遷延卻期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，猶足以為功，乃可以得志。」
entries.en: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will."
entries.literal: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will.'

entries.zh: 倫然之。
entries.en: Lun assented.
entries.literal: Lun agreed.

entries.zh: 秀因使反間，言殿中人欲廢賈后，迎太子。
entries.en: Sun Xiu spread rumors of a palace plot to restore Yu.
entries.literal: Xiu therefore launched counter-espionage, saying men of the palace meant to depose Empress Jia and welcome the crown prince.

entries.zh: 賈后聞之憂怖，乃使太醫令程據合巴豆杏子丸。
entries.en: Jia panicked and had Cheng Ju mix purgative poison.
entries.literal: When the empress heard it she was terrified and ordered Court Physician-in-Chief Cheng Ju to compound croton and apricot-kernel pills.

entries.zh: 三月，矯詔使黃門孫慮齋至許昌以害太子。
entries.en: Third month a fake edict sent Sun Lü to kill Yu at Xuchang.
entries.literal: In the third month a forged edict sent Yellow Gate Sun Lü to Xuchang to murder the crown prince.

entries.zh: 初，太子恐見鴆，恆自煮食於前。
entries.en: Yu had cooked for himself to avoid cup poison.
entries.literal: Earlier the crown prince had feared being poisoned and always cooked his own food before him.

entries.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子于小坊中，絕不與食，宮中猶於牆壁上過食與太子。
entries.en: Lü reported this to Liu Zhen, who moved the crown prince to a small compound and denied him food. Palace personnel still passed food to him over the walls.
entries.literal: Lü reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen thereupon moved the crown prince to a small ward, cut off all food, yet the palace still passed food over the wall to the crown prince.

entries.zh: 慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。
entries.en: Sun Lü beat Yu to death in the latrine with a pestle—screams escaped.
entries.literal: Lü then forced medicine on the crown prince; the crown prince refused to swallow; while using the privy Lü killed him with a medicine pestle; the crown prince cried loudly—the sound carried outside.

entries.zh: 時年二十三。
entries.en: He died at twenty-three.
entries.literal: He was twenty-three sui.

entries.zh: 將以庶人禮葬之，賈后表曰：「遹不幸喪亡，傷其迷悖，又早短折，悲痛之懷，不能自己。
entries.en: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: "Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.
entries.literal: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: 'Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.

entries.zh: 妾私心冀其刻肌刻骨，更思孝道，規為稽顙，正其名號。
entries.en: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.
entries.literal: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.

entries.zh: 此志不遂，重以酸恨。
entries.en: She claimed thwarted maternal hopes.
entries.literal: That aim failed—doubly bitter regret.

entries.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。
entries.en: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.
entries.literal: Though Yu's guilt was utmost he remains an imperial grandson—to dispatch him as a mere commoner truly pity—may Heaven grant kingly burial.

entries.zh: 妾誠暗淺不識禮義，不勝至情，冒昧陳聞。」
entries.en: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize."
entries.literal: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize.'

entries.zh: 詔以廣陵王禮葬之。
entries.en: The court buried him as Guangling prince.
entries.literal: An edict buried him with rites due Prince of Guangling.

entries.zh: 臧字敬文。
entries.en: Second son Zang, styled Jingwen.
entries.literal: Zang, courtesy name Jingwen.

entries.zh: 永康元年四月，封臨淮王。
entries.en: Yongkang fourth month made Linhuai prince.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of Yongkang year one he was enfeoffed Prince of Linhuai.

entries.zh: 己巳，詔曰：「咎征數發，奸回作變，遹既逼廢，非命而沒。
entries.en: On jisi day an edict stated: "Ill omens pile; crafty factions stir; Yu was driven from office and died unnaturally.
entries.literal: On jisi day an edict stated: 'Ill omens pile; crafty factions stir; Yu was driven from office and died unnaturally.

entries.zh: 今立臧為皇太孫。
entries.en: Zang named grand-heir.
entries.literal: Now we establish Zang as imperial grandson-heir.

entries.zh: 還妃王氏以母之，稱太孫太妃。
entries.en: Let Consort Wang return to act as his mother, with the title Grand Consort Dowager of the Imperial Grandson-Heir.
entries.literal: Consort Wang returns to mother him—styled Grand Heir Consort Dowager.

entries.zh: 太子官屬即轉為太孫官屬。
entries.en: Staff slid from heir to grand-heir titles.
entries.literal: Eastern Palace staff transferred to grand-heir posts.

entries.zh: 趙王倫行太孫太傅。」
entries.en: Lun, Prince of Zhao, acted Grand Tutor to the imperial grandson-heir."
entries.literal: Lun, Prince of Zhao, acted Grand Tutor to the imperial grandson-heir.'

entries.zh: 五月，倫與太孫俱之東宮，太孫自西掖門出，車服侍從皆湣懷之舊也。
entries.en: May procession exited the west palace gate in Yu's old livery.
entries.literal: In the fifth month Lun and the grand heir went together to the Eastern Palace; the grand heir exited the Western Side Gate—carriages, dress, and attendants all followed Minhuai's old train.

entries.zh: 到銅駝街，宮人哭，侍從者皆哽咽，路人抆淚焉。
entries.en: Luoyang wept along Bronze Camel Street.
entries.literal: Reaching Bronze Camel Avenue palace women wept; attendants choked; passersby wiped tears.

entries.zh: 桑復生於西廂，太孫廢，乃枯。
entries.en: Omen mulberry mirrored heir's fall.
entries.literal: The mulberry sprouted again west of the wing; when the grand heir was deposed it withered.

entries.zh: 永甯元年正月，趙王倫篡位，廢為濮陽王，與帝俱遷金墉，尋被害。
entries.en: Yongning coup demoted Zang—murdered at Jinyong.
entries.literal: In the first month of Yongning year one Lun, Prince of Zhao, usurped the throne and demoted Zang to Prince of Puyang. Zang moved with the emperor to Jinyong and was murdered soon afterward.

entries.zh: 太安初，追諡曰哀。
entries.en: Tai'an era canonized Ai.
entries.literal: Early in Tai'an posthumous title Ai was granted.

entries.zh: 喪之發也，大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂。
entries.en: Storm shattered funeral umbrellas.
entries.literal: When the hearse set out great wind and thunder came—canopies and coverings flew torn.

entries.zh: 又為哀策曰：「皇帝臨軒，使洗馬劉務告于皇太子之殯曰：咨爾遹！
entries.en: They further composed a condolence text: "The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!
entries.literal: They further composed a condolence text: 'The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!

entries.zh: 幼稟英挺，芬馨誕茂。
entries.en: From childhood you were outstanding, and your fine qualities flourished abundantly.
entries.literal: You drew from youth heroic sap, fragrance ripe at birth.

entries.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
entries.en: Even in early boyhood you displayed lofty brilliance and exceptional talents.
entries.literal: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.

entries.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
entries.en: Your august grandfather cherished your fine virtues.
entries.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.

entries.zh: 顯詔仍崇，名振同軌。
entries.en: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 是用建爾儲副，永統皇基。
entries.en: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.
entries.literal: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.

entries.zh: 如何凶戾潛構，禍害如茲！
entries.en: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!
entries.literal: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!

entries.zh: 哀感和氣，痛貫四時。
entries.en: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.
entries.literal: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.

entries.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
entries.en: Alas, how grievous!
entries.literal: Alas, alas the sorrow!

entries.zh: 爾之降廢，實我不明。
entries.en: Your degradation was truly due to my lack of discernment.
entries.literal: Your degradation was truly my blindness.

entries.zh: 牝亂沈烖，釁結禍成。
entries.en: A woman’s disorder brought deep calamity; hostility accumulated and disaster took shape.
entries.literal: Female chaos sank calamity; omens knotted into disaster.

entries.zh: 爾之逝矣，誰百其形？
entries.en: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?
entries.literal: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?

entries.zh: 昔之申生，含枉莫訟。
entries.en: Long ago Shen Sheng bore false charges, with none to plead his case.
entries.literal: Long ago Shen Sheng bore wrong yet could not plead.

entries.zh: 今爾之負，抱冤於東。
entries.en: Now you too bear unjust blame and nurse your grievance in the east.
entries.literal: Now your burden of grievance hugs the eastern lands.

entries.zh: 悠悠有識，孰不哀慟！
entries.en: Among all who understand, who would not grieve?
entries.literal: Far and near anyone with insight—who fails bitter grief!

entries.zh: 壺關幹主，千秋悟己。
entries.en: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.
entries.literal: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.

entries.zh: 異世同規，古今一理。
entries.en: Across different ages, the pattern is the same; past and present share one principle.
entries.literal: Different age, same rule—past and present one principle.

entries.zh: 皇孫啟建，隆祚爾子。
entries.en: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.
entries.literal: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.

entries.zh: 雖悴前終，庶榮後始。
entries.en: Though your own end was sorrowful, may the new beginning afterward be glorious.
entries.literal: Though front end withered, rear blossom may yet flourish.

entries.zh: 窀穸既營，將寧爾神。
entries.en: Your burial chamber is now prepared, to bring your spirit peace.
entries.literal: Burial vault now built—we pacify your spirit.

entries.zh: 華髦電逝，戎車雷震。
entries.en: Splendid plumes flash past like lightning; war chariots rumble like thunder.
entries.literal: Flower feathers flash like lightning; war wagons thunder.

entries.zh: 芒芒羽蓋，翼翼縉紳。
entries.en: Feathered canopies stretch far and wide; the gentry advance in orderly ranks.
entries.literal: Vast feather-canopies; crowded sash-and-hat ranks.

entries.zh: 同悲等痛，孰不酸辛！
entries.en: Courtiers weep together.
entries.literal: Shared grief and equal pain—who lacks bitter sorrow!

entries.zh: 庶光來葉，永世不泯。」
entries.en: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages."
entries.literal: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages.'

entries.zh: 諡曰湣懷。
entries.en: Canonized Crown Prince Minhuai.
entries.literal: Posthumous title Minhuai was granted.

entries.zh: 六月己卯，葬于顯平陵。
entries.en: Buried sixth month at Xianping.
entries.literal: On jimao day of the sixth month he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 帝感閻纘之言，立思子台，故臣江統、陸機並作誄頌焉。
entries.en: Yan Zuan's plea built Son-Lament Terrace—Jiang Tong and Lu Ji wrote elegies.
entries.literal: Moved by Yan Zuan's words the emperor raised a Terrace of Longing for Sons; former ministers Jiang Tong and Lu Ji both composed dirges.

entries.zh: 太子三子：虨、臧、尚，並與父同幽金墉。
entries.en: Three sons shared Yu's prison.
entries.literal: The crown prince had three sons—Bin, Zang, and Shang—all imprisoned with their father at Jinyong.

entries.zh: 愍懷太子
entries.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
entries.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

entries.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！
entries.en: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
entries.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

entries.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。
entries.en: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
entries.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

entries.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
entries.en: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
entries.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

entries.zh: 祗爾德行，以從保傅，事親孝敬，禮無違者。
entries.en: You were to revere virtuous conduct and follow your tutors, serve your parents with filial respect, and never violate ritual.
entries.literal: I charged you to follow tutors in virtue, serving parents with filial respect—ritual unbreached.

entries.zh: 而朕昧於凶構，致爾於非命之禍，俾申生、孝己復見於今。
entries.en: Yet I failed to perceive wicked intrigues and brought you to an unnatural death, so that Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji appeared again in our time.
entries.literal: Yet I, dim to vicious plots, brought you to the misfortune of untimely death, making Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji again appear in our day.

entries.zh: 賴宰相賢明，人神憤怨，用啟朕心，討厥有罪，咸伏其辜。
entries.en: Fortunately, wise ministers and the indignation of men and spirits opened my eyes; I punished the guilty, and all paid the penalty for their crimes.
entries.literal: Thanks to wise ministers, human and spirit alike resented, opening my heart to punish the guilty—each has met sentence.

entries.zh: 何補於荼毒冤魂酷痛哉？
entries.en: But how can that make amends for the cruel suffering inflicted upon your wronged spirit?
entries.literal: What use mending poisoned wronged souls' cruel pain?

entries.zh: 是用忉怛悼恨，震動於五內。
entries.en: Thus I grieve in anguish and regret, shaken to my innermost being.
entries.literal: Therefore grief tears my vitals and shakes my five inner organs.

entries.zh: 今追復皇太子喪禮，反葬京畿，祠乙太牢。
entries.en: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.
entries.literal: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.

entries.zh: 魂而有靈，尚獲爾心。」
entries.en: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart."
entries.literal: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart.'

entries.zh: 帝為太子服長子斬衰，群臣齊衰，使尚書和郁率東宮官屬具吉凶之制，迎太子喪于許昌。
entries.en: Court mourned and fetched Yu's bier from Xu.
entries.literal: The emperor wore unhemmed mourning for the crown prince as for an eldest son; the ministers wore hemmed mourning. He sent Minister He Yu to lead the Eastern Palace officials in preparing the prescribed auspicious and mourning rites and bringing the crown prince's bier back from Xuchang.

entries.zh: 初，太子之廢也，妃父王衍表請離婚。
entries.en: Wang Yan filed for divorce the moment Yu fell.
entries.literal: When the crown prince was first deposed, his father-in-law Wang Yan memorialized requesting divorce.

entries.zh: 太子至許，遺妃書曰：「鄙雖頑愚，心念為善，欲盡忠孝之節，無有惡逆之心。
entries.en: After reaching Xu he sent his consort a letter: "Though I am coarse and foolish, at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.
entries.literal: After the crown prince reached Xu he sent his consort a letter: 'Though I am coarse and foolish at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.

entries.zh: 雖非中宮所生，奉事有如親母。
entries.en: He claimed dutiful service to Jia despite birth.
entries.literal: Though not born of the inner palace I served her as my own mother.

entries.zh: 自為太子以來，敕見禁檢，不得見母。
entries.en: Palace rules barred him from Lady Xie.
entries.literal: Since becoming crown prince edicts confined me—I could not see my mother.

entries.zh: 自宜城君亡，不見存恤，恆在空室中坐。
entries.en: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.
entries.literal: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.

entries.zh: 去年十二月，道文疾病困篤，父子之情，實相憐湣。
entries.en: Last twelfth month Daowen became gravely ill; the affection between father and son made us deeply pity one another.
entries.literal: Last twelfth month Daowen's illness grew desperate—father and son pitied each other truly.

entries.zh: 于時表國家乞加徽號，不見聽許。
entries.en: His plea for son's title failed.
entries.literal: Then I petitioned the throne for honors—permission never came.

entries.zh: 疾病既篤，為之求請恩福，無有噁心。
entries.en: He denied malice in praying for the boy.
entries.literal: When illness grew grave I sought blessings for him—I bore no evil intent.

entries.zh: 自道文病，中宮三遣左右來視，云：'天教呼汝。
entries.en: Since Daowen fell ill, the empress sent attendants three times to see me, saying, "His Majesty summons you."
entries.literal: Since Daowen fell ill, the empress sent attendants three times to see me, saying, "His Majesty summons you."

entries.zh: '到二十八日暮，有短函來，題言東宮發，疏云：'言天教欲見汝。
entries.en: On the evening of the twenty-eighth a short letter arrived, marked as a dispatch from the Eastern Palace. It said, "His Majesty wishes to see you."
entries.literal: On the evening of the twenty-eighth a short letter arrived, marked as a dispatch from the Eastern Palace. It said, "His Majesty wishes to see you."

entries.zh: '即便作表求入。
entries.en: He requested audience.
entries.literal: At once I drafted a memorial begging entry.

entries.zh: 二十九日早入見國家，須臾遣至中宮。
entries.en: He saw Hui briefly then reached Jia's halls.
entries.literal: On the twenty-ninth morning I entered and saw His Majesty; presently I was sent to the inner palace.

entries.zh: 中宮左右陳舞見語：'中宮旦來吐不快。
entries.en: Chen Wu claimed Jia was sick.
entries.literal: Inner attendants Chen Wu told him: 'The empress vomited ill this morning.'

entries.zh: '使住空屋中坐。
entries.en: They parked him in an empty room.
entries.literal: She told you to wait seated in an empty chamber.

entries.zh: 須臾中宮遣陳舞見語：'聞汝表陛下為道文乞王，不得王是成國耳。
entries.en: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'
entries.literal: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'

entries.zh: '中宮遙呼陳舞：'昨天教與太子酒棗。
entries.en: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."
entries.literal: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."

entries.zh: '便持三升酒、大盤棗來見與，使飲酒啖棗盡。
entries.en: Chen Wu forced three sheng wine and dates.
entries.literal: She brought three sheng of ale and a great tray of jujubes and made him finish both.

entries.zh: 鄙素不飲酒，即便遣舞啟說不堪三升之意。
entries.en: Yu pleaded low tolerance.
entries.literal: I never drink ale yet sent Chen Wu back explaining I could not manage three sheng.

entries.zh: 中宮遙呼曰：'汝常陛下前持酒可喜，何以不飲？
entries.en: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'
entries.literal: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'

entries.zh: 天與汝酒，當使道文差也。
entries.en: His Majesty has given you wine; it should make Daowen recover.
entries.literal: His Majesty has given you wine; it should make Daowen recover.

entries.zh: '便答中宮：'陛下會同一日見賜，故不敢辭，通日不飲三升酒也。
entries.en: Yu cited earlier imperial banquet.
entries.literal: I answered the inner palace: His Majesty granted ale one day—therefore I dared not refuse—but all day I never drank three sheng.

entries.zh: 且實未食，恐不堪。
entries.en: Empty stomach worried him.
entries.literal: Moreover I had not eaten—I feared I could not endure it.

entries.zh: 又未見殿下，飲此或至顛倒。
entries.en: Besides, I had not yet seen Your Highness, and drinking this might leave me confused and unsteady.
entries.literal: Nor had I yet seen Your Highness—I feared drink might overturn me.

entries.zh: '陳舞復傳語云：'不孝那！
entries.en: Chen Wu called him unfilial.
entries.literal: Chen Wu relayed another message: "You unfilial wretch!

entries.zh: 天與汝酒飲，不肯飲，中有惡物邪？
entries.en: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?
entries.literal: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?

entries.zh: '遂可飲二升，餘有一升，求持還東宮飲盡。
entries.en: I then managed to drink two sheng. With one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.
entries.literal: I then managed to drink two sheng. With one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.

entries.zh: 逼迫不得已，更飲一升。
entries.en: Cornered he drank more.
entries.literal: Pressed helplessly he drank another sheng.

entries.zh: 飲已，體中荒迷，不復自覺。
entries.en: After drinking it, I became dazed and lost awareness.
entries.literal: After drinking his body grew confused and he lost awareness.

entries.zh: 須臾有一小婢持封箱來，云：'詔使寫此文書。
entries.en: Presently a young maid brought a sealed case and said, "The emperor orders you to copy this document."
entries.literal: Presently a young maid brought a sealed case, saying, 'The edict orders you to write out this document.'

entries.zh: '鄙便驚起，視之，有一白紙，一青紙。
entries.en: He found white and green paper inside.
entries.literal: I started in alarm and looked: there was one sheet of white paper and one of green.

entries.zh: 催促云：'陛下停待。
entries.en: Runners said the emperor waited.
entries.literal: They pressed: 'His Majesty is waiting.'

entries.zh: '又小婢承福持筆研墨黃紙來，使寫。
entries.en: Chengfu added brush and yellow paper for the copy.
entries.literal: Another small maid, Chengfu, brought brush, inkstone, and yellow paper, making him write.

entries.zh: 急疾不容復視，實不覺紙上語輕重。
entries.en: Rush left no time to read the forgery's sense.
entries.literal: Haste would not let me reread; I truly did not notice the import of the words on the page.

entries.zh: 父母至親，實不相疑，事理如此，實為見誣，想眾人見明也。」
entries.en: Parents are kin closest of all—I truly did not doubt them; though matters went so, I have been slandered, and I trust the multitude will see it clear.'
entries.literal: Parents are kin closest of all—I truly did not doubt them; though matters went so, I have been slandered, and I trust the multitude will see it clear.'

entries.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷挺岐嶷之姿，表夙成之質。
entries.en: The historiographers say: Minhuai was endowed with exceptional wisdom and displayed precocious gifts.
entries.literal: The historiographers say: Minhuai bore a posture keen and wise, displaying precocious substance.

entries.zh: 武皇鍾愛，既深詒厥之謀；
entries.en: Wu Di planned Yu as future pillar.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.

entries.zh: 天下歸心，頗有後來之望。
entries.en: The realm expected greatness.
entries.literal: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.

entries.zh: 及於繼明宸極，守器春坊，四教不勤，三朝或闕，豹姿未變，鳳德已衰，信惑奸邪，疏斥正士，好屠酤之賤役，耽苑囿之佚遊，可謂靡不有初，鮮克有終者也。
entries.en: When the new ruler ascended the imperial throne and the prince guarded the succession in the Eastern Palace, he neglected the four teachings and sometimes omitted the three daily greetings. His leopard’s form was not yet transformed, while his phoenix virtue had already declined. He trusted wicked deceivers and drove away upright men, enjoyed the lowly work of butchering and selling wine, and indulged in idle outings in the parks. Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."
entries.literal: When the new ruler ascended the imperial throne and the prince guarded the succession in the Eastern Palace, he neglected the four teachings and sometimes omitted the three daily greetings. His leopard’s form was not yet transformed, while his phoenix virtue had already declined. He trusted wicked deceivers and drove away upright men, enjoyed the lowly work of butchering and selling wine, and indulged in idle outings in the parks. Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."

entries.zh: 既而中宮凶忍，久懷危害之心，外戚諂諛，競進讒邪之說；
entries.en: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.
entries.literal: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.

entries.zh: 坎牲之謀已構，斃犬之譖遂行；
entries.en: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.
entries.literal: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.

entries.zh: 一人乏探隱之聰，百辟無爭臣之節。
entries.en: The ruler lacked the discernment to uncover hidden matters, and the ministers lacked the integrity to remonstrate.
entries.literal: Thus one man lacked keen insight into hidden matters; the hundred ministers showed no temper of remonstrating subjects.

entries.zh: 遂使冤逾楚建，酷甚戾園。
entries.en: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.
entries.literal: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.

entries.zh: 雖復禮備哀榮，情深憫慟，亦何補於荼毒者哉！
entries.en: Posthumous honors could not resurrect him.
entries.literal: Though mourning rites ran full and grief ran deep, what did they mend for the poisoned innocent!

entries.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。
entries.en: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.
entries.literal: The encomium says: Minhuai clever and keen—truly Heaven-endowed.

entries.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。
entries.en: His imperial grandfather cherished him deeply; the assembled officials looked forward in expectation.
entries.literal: Imperial ancestor pinned hope on him; hosts of officials craned necks.

entries.zh: 震宮肇建，儲德不恢。
entries.en: When he first entered the heir’s palace, his princely virtue failed to grow.
entries.literal: When Thunder Palace first rose, heir virtue never broadened.

entries.zh: 掇蜂構隙，歸胙生災。
entries.en: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.
entries.literal: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.

entries.zh: 既罹凶忍，徒望歸來。
entries.en: Death ended every hope of restoration.
entries.literal: Once brutal cruelty struck, vain hope alone remained of return.

entries.zh: 及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲，不能尊敬保傅。
entries.en: Adult Yu spurned books, slighted tutors, and played with pages.
entries.literal: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.

entries.zh: 賈后素忌太子有令譽，因此密敕黃門閹宦媚諛于太子曰：「殿下誠可及壯時極意所欲，何為恆自拘束？」
entries.en: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'
entries.literal: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'

entries.zh: 每見喜怒之際，輒歎曰：「殿下不知用威刑，天下豈得畏服！」
entries.en: Whenever they saw him pleased or angry, they would sigh: "Your Highness does not know how to use authority and punishments. How could the realm fear and obey you?"
entries.literal: Whenever they saw him pleased or angry, they would sigh: "Your Highness does not know how to use authority and punishments. How could the realm fear and obey you?"

entries.zh: 太子所幸蔣美人生男，又言宜隆其賞賜，多為皇孫造玩弄之器，太子從之。
entries.en: When Consort Jiang bore a son they pushed costly toys and stipends—Yu complied.
entries.literal: When Lady Jiang, whom the crown prince favored, bore a son, they also said rewards should be lavish and many toys fashioned for the imperial grandson; the crown prince obeyed.

entries.zh: 於是慢弛益彰，或廢朝侍，恆在後園遊戲。
entries.en: He skipped audiences for back-garden games.
entries.literal: Thereupon his arrogance and laxness grew plainer; sometimes he skipped court attendance and constantly played in the rear garden.

entries.zh: 愛埤車小馬，令左右馳騎，斷其鞅勒，使墮地為樂。
entries.en: He loved low carts and ponies; he had attendants gallop them, then cut their harness straps and bridles to amuse himself by making them fall.
entries.literal: He loved low carts and ponies; he had attendants gallop them, then cut their harness straps and bridles to amuse himself by making them fall.

entries.zh: 或有犯忤者，手自捶擊之。
entries.en: He thrashed servants himself.
entries.literal: If anyone offended him he personally beat them.

entries.zh: 性拘小忌，不許繕壁修牆，正瓦動屋。
entries.en: He banned builders from touching plaster or tiles—superstition.
entries.literal: Given to petty taboos, he forbade plastering walls, repairing fences, or straightening roof-tiles.

entries.zh: 而于宮中為市，使人屠酤，手揣斤兩，輕重不差。
entries.en: Yet he set up a market inside the palace, had others butcher animals and sell wine, and judged weights with his own hands without error.
entries.literal: Yet inside the palace he opened a market, had people butcher and sell ale, and weighed purchases in his own hands to the exact ounce.

entries.zh: 其母本屠家女也，故太子好之。
entries.en: His mother was originally a butcher’s daughter, which is why the crown prince enjoyed this.
entries.literal: His mother had been a butcher's daughter; therefore the crown prince delighted in it.

entries.zh: 又令西園賣葵菜、藍子、雞、面之屬，而收其利。
entries.en: He peddled greens, dye seed, chicken, and flour from West Garden for cash.
entries.literal: He also ordered the Western Garden to sell mallow, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and the like, pocketing the profit.

entries.zh: 東宮舊制，月請錢五十萬，備於眾用，太子恆探取二月，以供嬖寵。
entries.en: The Eastern Palace normally received five hundred thousand cash a month for all its expenses; he habitually drew two months in advance to provide for his favorites.
entries.literal: Eastern Palace precedent allotted five hundred thousand cash monthly for general expenses; the crown prince habitually drew two months ahead to supply favorites.

entries.zh: 洗馬江統陳五事以諫之，太子不納，語在《統傳》中。
entries.en: Jiang Tong's five memorials went unheard—see his chapter.
entries.literal: Groom of the Household Jiang Tong presented five admonitions; the crown prince rejected them—the account appears in Jiang Tong's biography.

entries.zh: 舍人杜錫以太子非賈后所生，而後性凶暴，深以為憂，每盡忠規勸太子修德進善，遠於讒謗。
entries.en: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.
entries.literal: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.

entries.zh: 太子怒，使人以針著錫常所坐氈中而剌之。
entries.en: Angered, Yu had someone put needles into the felt mat where Du Xi usually sat, so that they would prick him.
entries.literal: The crown prince grew angry and had someone sew needles into Du Xi's usual felt mat to stab him.

entries.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃後之貴，不能假借之。
entries.en: Yu refused to flatter Jia Mi.
entries.literal: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.

entries.zh: 謐至東宮，或舍之而於後庭遊戲。
entries.en: He left Jia Mi cooling heels while he played inside.
entries.literal: When Mi came to the Eastern Palace he sometimes left him waiting while he played in the inner courts.

entries.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「賈謐甚有寵于中宮，而有不順之色，若一旦交構，大事去矣。
entries.en: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: "Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.
entries.literal: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: 'Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.

entries.zh: 宜深自謙屈，以防其變，廣延賢士，用自輔翼。」
entries.en: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings."
entries.literal: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings.'

entries.zh: 太子不能從。
entries.en: Yu ignored him.
entries.literal: The crown prince would not follow.

entries.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。
entries.en: Guo Huai once pushed a Han match—Yu wanted it too.
entries.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.

entries.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。
entries.en: Jia Wu and the empress forced Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng instead.
entries.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.

entries.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。
entries.en: Yu resented losing Wang's elder beauty to Jia Mi.
entries.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.

entries.zh: 謐嘗與太子圍棋，爭道，成都王穎見而訶謐，謐意愈不平，因此譖太子于後曰：「太子廣買田業，多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。
entries.en: Once while playing go with the crown prince Mi quarreled over a move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: "The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
entries.literal: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.

entries.zh: 密聞其言云：'皇后萬歲後，吾當魚肉之。
entries.en: Mi quoted Yu vowing to slaughter the Jias after Jia died.
entries.literal: I have secretly heard him say: "After the empress dies, I shall butcher them."

entries.zh: '非但如是也，若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等而廢後於金墉，如反手耳。
entries.en: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.
entries.literal: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.

entries.zh: 不如早為之所，更立慈順者以自防衛。」
entries.en: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves."
entries.literal: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves.'

entries.zh: 後納其言，又宣揚太子之短，布諸遠近。
entries.en: Jia adopted the plot and smeared Yu empire-wide.
entries.literal: The empress accepted his words and further broadcast the crown prince's faults throughout near and far.

entries.zh: 于時朝野咸知賈后有害太子意。
entries.en: Everyone saw Jia meant to kill the heir.
entries.literal: Then court and countryside knew the empress meant to harm the crown prince.

entries.zh: 中護軍趙俊請太子廢後，太子不聽。
entries.en: Zhao Jun urged preemptive deposition—Yu declined.
entries.literal: Central Guard Zhao Jun asked the crown prince to depose the empress first; the crown prince refused.

entries.zh: 尚字敬仁。
entries.en: Shang, styled Jingren.
entries.literal: Shang, courtesy name Jingren.

entries.zh: 永康元年四月，封為襄陽王。
entries.en: In Yongkang fourth month he was made Prince of Xiangyang.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of Yongkang year one he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 永寧元年八月，立為皇太孫。
entries.en: In Yongning eighth month he was made imperial grandson-heir.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of Yongning year one he was established as imperial grandson-heir.

entries.zh: 太安元年三月癸卯，薨，帝服齊衰期，諡曰沖太孫。
entries.en: On guimao in Tai'an third month he died; the emperor wore trimmed mourning for a year and granted the posthumous title Chong Imperial Grandson.
entries.literal: On the guimao day of the third month of Tai'an year one he died; the emperor wore trimmed mourning for one year; posthumous title Chong Imperial Grandson was granted.

entries.zh: 虨字道文，永康元年正月，薨。
entries.en: Eldest Bin (Daowen) died Yongkang first month.
entries.literal: Bin, courtesy name Daowen, died in the first month of Yongkang year one.

entries.zh: 四月，追封南陽王。
entries.en: Fourth month titled Prince of Nanyang.
entries.literal: In the fourth month posthumous investiture as Prince of Nanyang.

entries.zh: 太子洗馬陳留江統以為戎、狄亂華，宜早絕其原，乃作《徙戎論》以警朝廷曰：「夫夷、蠻、戎、狄，地在要荒，禹平九土而西戎即敘。
entries.en: Jiang Tong of Chenliu, Groom of the Heir Apparent, argued that the Rong and Di were already unsettling the realm and that their root cause should be severed at once. He wrote the "Discourse on Relocating the Rong" to admonish the court, saying: "The Yi, Man, Rong, and Di inhabit the far marches. After Yu brought order to the nine domains, the western Rong at once came to allegiance.
entries.literal: The Groom of the Heir Apparent, Jiang Tong of Chenliu, held that the Rong and Di were disturbing China and that their source ought to be cut off early; he therefore composed the "Discourse on Relocating the Rong" to warn the court, saying: "The Yi, Man, Rong, and Di dwell in the remote borderlands. When Yu pacified the nine regions, the western Rong forthwith submitted.

entries.zh: 其性氣貪婪，凶悍不仁。
entries.en: By nature they are greedy, brutal, and devoid of human feeling.
entries.literal: Their nature and temperament are greedy, fierce, and lacking in humaneness.

entries.zh: 四夷之中，戎、狄為甚，弱則畏服，強則侵叛。
entries.en: Of the four barbarian peoples, the Rong and Di are the most troublesome: when weak they bow in awe, when strong they raid and revolt.
entries.literal: Among the four Yi, the Rong and Di are the worst: when weak they fear and submit; when strong they invade and rebel.

entries.zh: 當其強也，以漢之高祖困於白登，孝文軍於霸上；
entries.en: When they grew strong, Han Gaozu was trapped at Baideng and Emperor Wen camped at Bashang;
entries.literal: When they were strong, Gaozu of Han was besieged at Baideng and Emperor Xiaowen encamped at Bashang;

entries.zh: 及其弱也，以元、成之微而單于入朝。
entries.en: when they weakened, under the enfeebled reigns of Yuan and Cheng the Chanyu presented himself at court.
entries.literal: when they grew weak, under the feebleness of Emperors Yuan and Cheng the Chanyu came to court.

entries.zh: 此其已然之效也。
entries.en: This is the pattern history has already shown.
entries.literal: These are effects that have already come to pass.

entries.zh: 是以有道之君牧夷、狄也，惟以待之有備，御之有常，雖稽顙執贄，而邊城不弛固守，強暴為寇，而兵甲不加遠征，期令境內獲安，疆場不侵而已。
entries.en: That is why a ruler who holds to the Way deals with the Yi and Di by standing ready and governing them through steady discipline. Even when they prostrate themselves and bring tribute, frontier garrisons never slacken their guard; even when they turn violent and raid, no distant punitive expedition is launched—the goal is only domestic tranquility and an unmolested border.
entries.literal: Therefore when a ruler possessed of the Way governs the Yi and Di, he only treats them with preparedness and controls them by constant measures: though they knock their foreheads and present tribute, the border cities do not relax their firm defense; though violence makes them raiders, arms and armor are not sent on distant campaigns—the aim is simply that the interior may gain peace and the frontier not be violated.

entries.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之下元康九年（
entries.en: Under Emperor Hui of Jin, Yuankang, year 9 (
entries.literal: The lower portion of the first reign of Emperor Xiaohui, ninth year of Yuankang (

entries.zh: 己未，公元二九九年）
entries.en: jiwei, CE 299)
entries.literal: jiwei, common era year 299)

entries.zh: 散騎常侍賈謐侍講東宮，對太子倨傲，成都王穎見而叱之；
entries.en: Jia Mi, Regular Attendant Within the Encampment, lectured in the Eastern Palace and treated the heir apparent with insolence. Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, witnessed it and rebuked him;
entries.literal: Jia Mi, Regular Attendant Within the Encampment, lectured in the Eastern Palace and was arrogant toward the Heir Apparent; the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, saw it and rebuked him;

entries.zh: 謐怒，言於賈后，出穎為平北將軍，鎮鄴。
entries.en: Furious, Mi complained to Empress Jia, who had Ying transferred out as General Who Pacifies the North and posted to Ye.
entries.literal: Mi grew angry and spoke to Empress Jia, who sent Ying out as General Who Pacifies the North, stationed at Ye.

entries.zh: 征梁王肜為大將軍、錄尚書事；
entries.en: Sima Rong, Prince of Liang, was summoned to serve as Grand General and Recorder of the Masters of Writing;
entries.literal: The Prince of Liang, Sima Rong, was summoned as Grand General and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing;

entries.zh: 以河間王顒為鎮西將軍，鎮關中。
entries.en: and Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, was appointed General Who Guards the West to hold Guanzhong.
entries.literal: the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, was made General Who Guards the West and stationed in Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 初，武帝作石函之制，非至親不得鎮關中；
entries.en: Earlier Emperor Wu had decreed in the stone casket that only the closest imperial kin might garrison Guanzhong;
entries.literal: Earlier Emperor Wu had established the stone-casket rule: none but the closest kin might garrison Guanzhong;

entries.zh: 顒輕財愛士，朝廷以為賢，故用之。
entries.en: but Yong was generous and cultivated men of talent, so the court considered him worthy and appointed him anyway.
entries.literal: Yong was generous with wealth and cherished scholars; the court regarded him as worthy and therefore employed him.

entries.zh: 夏，六月，戊戌，高密文獻王泰薨。
entries.en: In summer, the sixth month, on the day wuxu, Sima Tai, the Cultured and Sacrificial King of Gaomi, died.
entries.literal: In summer, the sixth month, on the day wuxu, the Cultured and Sacrificial King of Gaomi, Sima Tai, died.

entries.zh: 賈后淫虐日甚，私於太醫令程據等；
entries.en: Empress Jia's debauchery and cruelty grew worse by the day. She took Cheng Ju, Director of the Imperial Physicians, and others as private lovers;
entries.literal: Empress Jia's debauchery and cruelty grew daily worse; she took private relations with the Director of the Imperial Physicians, Cheng Ju, and others;

entries.zh: 又以簏箱載道上年少入宮，復恐其漏洩，往往殺之。
entries.en: and she had young men smuggled into the palace in bamboo crates. Fearing exposure, she often had them killed afterward.
entries.literal: she also used bamboo cases to bring in young men from the roads to the palace, and fearing leaks often killed them.

entries.zh: 賈模恐禍及己，甚憂之。
entries.en: Jia Mo feared the scandal would engulf him and was deeply alarmed.
entries.literal: Jia Mo feared disaster would reach him and was deeply troubled.

entries.zh: 裴頠與模及張華議廢后，更立謝淑妃。
entries.en: Pei Wei discussed with Mo and Zhang Hua deposing the empress and elevating Lady Xie, the Pure Consort, in her stead.
entries.literal: Pei Wei discussed with Mo and Zhang Hua deposing the empress and installing Lady Xie, the Pure Consort, in her place.

entries.zh: 模、華皆曰：「主上自無廢黜之意，而吾等專行之，倘上心不以為然，將若之何！
entries.en: Mo and Hua both objected: "The emperor himself has no wish to depose her. If we act on our own and he disapproves, what then?
entries.literal: Mo and Hua both said: "Our lord himself has no intent to depose her; if we act on our own authority and his heart does not approve, what then shall we do!

entries.zh: 且諸王方強，朋黨各異，恐一旦禍起，身死國危，無益社稷。」
entries.en: Besides, the princes are strong and their factions divided. If trouble erupts, we may die and the realm fall into peril, with no gain for the state."
entries.literal: Moreover the princes are now strong and their factions differ; we fear that if disaster should suddenly arise, we would die and the state be endangered, with no benefit to the altars of soil and grain."

entries.zh: 頠曰：「誠如公言。
entries.en: Pei replied: "You are right.
entries.literal: Pei said: "It is indeed as you say.

entries.zh: 然中宮逞其昏虐，亂可立待也。」
entries.en: Yet the empress indulges her cruelty and folly. Chaos may come at any moment."
entries.literal: Yet the central palace indulges its benighted cruelty; disorder may be awaited at once."

entries.zh: 華曰：「卿二人於中宮皆親戚，言或見信，宜數為陳禍福之戒，庶無大悖，則天下尚未至於亂，吾曹得以估游卒歲而已。」
entries.en: Zhang Hua said: "You are both related to the empress and may be heard. Warn her often of the consequences. If she avoids the worst excesses, the realm may yet hold together and we can live out our days in peace."
entries.literal: Hua said: "You two are both kin to the central palace; your words may win belief. You ought often to set forth warnings of fortune and calamity, so that with luck there will be no great outrage; then the realm may not yet come to disorder, and we may idle through the year as merchants do."

entries.zh: 頠旦夕說其從母廣城君，令戒諭賈后以親厚太子，賈模亦數為后言禍福；
entries.en: Pei pressed his aunt, the Lady of Guangcheng, day and night to warn Empress Jia to treat the heir apparent kindly. Jia Mo likewise urged the empress repeatedly about the risks she was courting;
entries.literal: Pei day and night urged his mother's younger sister, the Lady of Guangcheng, to admonish Empress Jia to treat the Heir Apparent with affection; Jia Mo also repeatedly spoke to the empress of fortune and calamity;

entries.zh: 后不能用，反以模為毀己而疏之；
entries.en: but she would not listen. She took Mo for a slanderer and estranged herself from him;
entries.literal: the empress would not heed them and instead, taking Mo for one who slandered her, kept him at a distance;

entries.zh: 模不得志，憂憤而卒。
entries.en: and Mo, frustrated and despairing, died of grief.
entries.literal: Mo, unable to achieve his aim, died of grief and anger.

entries.zh: 秋，八月，以裴頠為尚書僕射。
entries.en: In autumn, the eighth month, Pei Wei was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Pei Wei was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 頠雖賈后親屬，然雅望素隆，四海唯恐其不居權位，尋詔頠專任門下事，頠上表固辭，以「賈模適亡，復以臣代之，崇外戚之望，彰偏私之舉，為聖朝累。」
entries.en: Though Pei was related to Empress Jia, his reputation was so high that the empire wished only that he take office. Soon he was ordered to handle Gate Affairs exclusively. He memorialized to refuse, writing: "Jia Mo has just died and I am put in his place. That elevates the empress's kin, displays favoritism, and burdens the court."
entries.literal: Though Pei was kin to Empress Jia, his refined reputation had long been lofty and all within the four seas feared only that he might not hold power; soon an edict made Pei solely responsible for Gate Affairs. Pei submitted a memorial firmly declining, saying: "Jia Mo has just died, and your servant is again put in his place—exalting the hopes of the empress's kin, displaying a partial favoritism, and becoming a burden to the sagely court."

entries.zh: 不聽。
entries.en: The emperor would not accept his resignation.
entries.literal: The emperor would not heed him.

entries.zh: 或謂頠曰：「君可以言，當盡言於中宮；
entries.en: Someone advised Pei: "If you have influence, speak plainly to the empress;
entries.literal: Someone said to Pei: "If you may speak, you ought to speak fully to the central palace;

entries.zh: 言而不從，當遠引而去。
entries.en: and if she will not listen, withdraw from office.
entries.literal: if you speak and are not obeyed, you ought to withdraw far away.

entries.zh: 倘二者不立，雖有十表，難以免矣。」
entries.en: If you do neither, ten memorials will not save you."
entries.literal: If neither course is established, though you submit ten memorials, it will be hard to escape harm."

entries.zh: 頠慨然久之，竟不能從。
entries.en: Pei sighed for a long time but could not bring himself to follow that counsel.
entries.literal: Pei sighed deeply for a long while but in the end could not follow the advice.

entries.zh: 帝為人戇騃，嘗在華林園聞蝦蟆，謂左右曰：「此鳴者，為官乎，為私乎？」
entries.en: The emperor was dull-witted by nature. Once in the Hualin Garden he heard frogs croaking and asked his attendants: "Are those creatures croaking for the state or for themselves?"
entries.literal: The emperor was by nature dull and foolish. Once in the Hualin Garden he heard frogs and said to those at his side: "These that croak—do they croak for office or for private gain?"

entries.zh: 時天下荒饉，百姓餓死，帝聞之，曰：「何不食肉糜？」
entries.en: Famine ravaged the land and people were starving to death. When he heard of it he said: "Why do they not eat meat porridge?"
entries.literal: At that time the realm suffered famine and the common people starved to death. When the emperor heard of it he said: "Why do they not eat meat porridge?"

entries.zh: 由是權在群下，政出多門，勢位之家，更相薦托，有如互市。
entries.en: Power therefore rested with his ministers. Policy issued from many quarters. Powerful families traded favors and appointments like merchants in a market.
entries.literal: From this power lay with the multitude below; government issued from many gates; powerful families recommended and entrusted posts to one another like a mutual marketplace.

entries.zh: 賈、郭恣橫，貨賂公行。
entries.en: The Jia and Guo factions ruled without restraint, and bribery flourished openly.
entries.literal: The Jia and Guo clans acted with unbridled license; bribes walked openly in public.

entries.zh: 南陽魯褒作《錢神論》以譏之曰：「錢之為體，有乾坤之象，親之如兄，字曰孔方。
entries.en: Lu Bao of Nanyang wrote the "Discourse on the God of Money" to satirize the age, saying: "Money embodies heaven and earth. Men treat it like an elder brother and call it Kongfang.
entries.literal: Lu Bao of Nanyang composed the "Discourse on the God of Money" to satirize them, saying: "Money as a substance bears the image of heaven and earth; one treats it as an elder brother and styles it Kongfang.

entries.zh: 無德而尊，無勢而熱，排金門，入紫闥。
entries.en: Without virtue it is honored; without rank it is courted. It pushes through golden gates and enters the purple chambers of power.
entries.literal: Without virtue it is honored; without power it is sought; it pushes through the golden gate and enters the purple portal.

entries.zh: 危可使安，死可使活，貴可使賤，生可使殺。
entries.en: It can turn danger into safety, death into life, honor into shame, and the living into the dead.
entries.literal: Danger it can make safe; death it can make live; the noble it can make base; the living it can make dead.

entries.zh: 是故忿爭非錢不勝，幽滯非錢不撥，怨仇非錢不解，令聞非錢不發。
entries.en: Angry disputes are not won without it. The imprisoned are not freed without it. Feuds are not settled without it. Reputation is not made without it.
entries.literal: Therefore angry disputes are not won without money; the obscure and detained are not released without money; enmity and grievance are not resolved without money; good repute is not spread without money.

entries.zh: 洛中朱衣、當塗之士，愛我家兄，皆無已已，執我之手，抱我終始，凡今之人，惟錢而已！」
entries.en: The grandees of Luoyang and those who hold power love our elder brother without end, seize my hand and cling to me forever. For the men of today, only money matters!"
entries.literal: The scarlet-clad in Luoyang and those who hold the road all love our elder brother without end, grasp my hand and embrace me to the finish—of all people today, only money matters!"

entries.zh: 又，朝臣務以苛察相高，每有疑議，群下各立私意，刑法不壹，獄訟繁滋。
entries.en: Meanwhile officials competed in harsh scrutiny. Whenever a case was doubtful, each faction pressed its own view. The law lost uniformity and lawsuits multiplied.
entries.literal: Moreover the court ministers strove to outdo one another in harsh scrutiny; whenever there was a doubtful case the subordinates each held a private opinion; penal law was not uniform and lawsuits multiplied.

entries.zh: 裴頠上表曰：「先王刑賞相稱，輕重無二，故下聽有常，群吏安業。
entries.en: Pei Wei memorialized: "The former kings matched punishment to offense and reward to merit, with no arbitrary doubling of severity. Subordinates then knew what to expect and officials pursued their duties in peace.
entries.literal: Pei Wei submitted a memorial saying: "The former kings made punishment and reward correspond, with no doubling of light and heavy; therefore those below heard with constancy and the host of officials rested secure in their duties.

entries.zh: 去元康四年大風，廟闕屋瓦有數枚傾落，免太常荀寓；
entries.en: In the fourth year of Yuankang a great wind blew several tiles from the ancestral temple gate-towers, and Minister of Ceremonies Xun Yu was dismissed;
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yuankang past there was a great wind; several roof-tiles of the ancestral temple gate-towers fell, and the Minister of Ceremonies Xun Yu was dismissed;

entries.zh: 事輕責重，有違常典。
entries.en: a light offense punished with excessive severity, contrary to precedent.
entries.literal: the affair was light but the responsibility heavy, contrary to the regular statutes.

entries.zh: 五年二月有大風，蘭台主者懲懼前事，求索阿棟之間，得瓦小邪十五處，遂禁止太常，復興刑獄。
entries.en: In the second month of the fifth year another great wind blew. The chief of the Orchid Terrace, dreading a repeat of the earlier scandal, searched the side beams and found fifteen slightly misaligned tiles. He had the Minister of Ceremonies detained and criminal prosecutions revived.
entries.literal: In the second month of the fifth year there was again a great wind; the chief of the Orchid Terrace, fearing the former affair, searched between the side beams and found fifteen places where tiles were slightly askew; he thereupon placed the Minister of Ceremonies under detention and revived criminal prosecutions.

entries.zh: 今年八月，陵上荊一枝圍七寸二分者被斫；
entries.en: In the eighth month of this year a thorn branch seven inches and two tenths around on the imperial mound was cut down;
entries.literal: In the eighth month of this year, on the imperial mound a branch of thorn with a circumference of seven inches and two tenths was cut down;

entries.zh: 司徒、太常奔走道路，雖知事小，而按劾難測，騷擾驅馳，各競免負，於今太常禁止未解。
entries.en: the Minister over the Masses and the Minister of Ceremonies raced about in panic. Though the offense was trivial, no one could predict how prosecution would fall. Officials scrambled to escape blame, and the Minister of Ceremonies remains under detention to this day.
entries.literal: the Minister over the Masses and the Minister of Ceremonies rushed along the roads; though they knew the matter was small, prosecution was hard to foresee, and with disturbance and hurried driving each strove to escape blame—down to today the Minister of Ceremonies' detention has not been lifted.

entries.zh: 夫刑書之文有限而舛違之故無方，故有臨時議處之制，誠不能皆得循常也。
entries.en: Penal statutes are finite, but the causes of violation are endless. Hence there is provision for ad hoc deliberation, and not every case can follow routine precedent.
entries.literal: The text of penal statutes is limited while the causes of violation are boundless; therefore there is a system of ad hoc deliberation and disposition, and truly one cannot in every case follow the regular rule.

entries.zh: 至於此等，皆為過當，恐奸吏因緣，得為淺深也。」
entries.en: Cases like these, however, go too far. I fear corrupt clerks will seize the chance to twist punishments to their own ends."
entries.literal: As for cases such as these, all are excessive; I fear corrupt clerks will seize the opportunity to make punishment light or heavy at will."

entries.zh: 既而曲議猶不止，三公尚書劉頌復上疏曰：「自近世以來，法漸多門，令甚不一，吏不知所守，下不知所避，奸偽者因以售其情，居上者難以檢其下，事同議異，獄犴不平。
entries.en: Yet twisted legal debate continued. Liu Song, Master of Writing to the Three Excellencies, memorialized again: "In recent times laws have multiplied and ordinances conflict. Officials no longer know what to enforce; commoners no longer know what to avoid. Fraud flourishes, superiors cannot control subordinates, identical cases yield different rulings, and justice in the prisons is uneven.
entries.literal: Yet twisted deliberation still did not cease. Liu Song, the Three Excellencies' Master of Writing, again submitted a memorial saying: "Since recent times the law has gradually multiplied its gates and ordinances are very inconsistent; clerks do not know what to uphold, the people below do not know what to avoid; the deceitful thereby sell their inclinations, those above find it hard to inspect those below, the same affair receives different deliberations, and the prisons are not fair.

entries.zh: 夫君臣之分，各有所司。
entries.en: Ruler and minister each have their proper sphere.
entries.literal: The distinction between ruler and minister has its respective duties for each.

entries.zh: 法欲必奉，故令主者守文；
