entries.en: Because the law must be obeyed, the presiding officer holds to the statute;
entries.literal: The law must be surely obeyed, therefore the presiding officer is made to hold to the text;

entries.zh: 理有窮塞，故使大臣釋滯；
entries.en: because principle can reach an impasse, great ministers resolve deadlocks;
entries.literal: principle has its impasses, therefore great ministers are made to release obstructions;

entries.zh: 事有時宜，故人主權斷。
entries.en: and because affairs have their timely demands, the sovereign holds discretionary power.
entries.literal: affairs have their timely fitness, therefore the sovereign holds discretionary judgment.

entries.zh: 主者守文，若釋之執犯蹕之平也；
entries.en: The presiding officer who holds to the text is like Zhang Shizhi insisting on the law when the emperor's progress was violated;
entries.literal: The presiding officer holding to the text is like Zhang Shizhi's upholding the law on violating the imperial progress;

entries.zh: 大臣釋滯，若公孫弘斷郭解之獄也；
entries.en: the great minister who resolves deadlock is like Gongsun Hong judging the case of Guo Jie;
entries.literal: the great minister releasing obstruction is like Gongsun Hong's deciding the case of Guo Jie;

entries.zh: 人主權斷，若漢祖戮丁公之為也。
entries.en: the sovereign's discretionary act is like Gaozu of Han executing Lord Ding.
entries.literal: the sovereign's discretionary judgment is like Han's Founder's execution of Lord Ding.

entries.zh: 天下萬事，自非此類，不得出意妄議，皆以律令從事；
entries.en: For all other affairs under heaven, unless they fall into these categories, no one may debate at will. All must proceed by statute and ordinance;
entries.literal: For the myriad affairs under heaven, unless they fall into these categories, one may not venture opinion and reckless debate—all must be handled according to statutes and ordinances;

entries.zh: 然後法信於下，人聽不惑，吏不容奸，可以言政矣。」
entries.en: then the law will be trusted below, the people will not be confused, clerks will have no room for fraud, and government may be called sound."
entries.literal: then the law will be trusted below, the people's hearing will not be confused, clerks will not harbor deceit, and one may speak of good government."

entries.zh: 乃下詔：「郎、令史復出法駁案者，隨事以聞。」
entries.en: An edict followed: "When gentlemen and clerks again raise statutory objections to cases, report each matter as it arises."
entries.literal: An edict was then issued: "When gentlemen and clerks again produce legal rebuttals of cases, report the matter according to circumstances."

entries.zh: 然亦不能革也。
entries.en: Yet the abuse could not be reformed.
entries.literal: Yet the practice still could not be reformed.

entries.zh: 裴頠薦平陽韋忠於張華，華辟之，忠辭疾不起。
entries.en: Pei Wei recommended Wei Zhong of Pingyang to Zhang Hua. Hua summoned him, but Zhong pleaded illness and refused to serve.
entries.literal: Pei Wei recommended Wei Zhong of Pingyang to Zhang Hua; Hua summoned him, but Zhong declined on grounds of illness and did not take office.

entries.zh: 人問其故，忠曰：「張茂先華而不實，裴逸民欲而無厭，棄典禮而附賊後，此豈大丈夫之所為哉！
entries.en: Asked why, Zhong said: "Zhang Hua is showy but hollow; Pei Wei is grasping and never satisfied. They abandon ritual and cling to the empress's faction. Is that the conduct of a true gentleman?
entries.literal: When people asked his reason, Zhong said: "Zhang Maoxian is flowery but not solid; Pei Yimin is covetous and never satisfied. They abandon canonical rites and attach themselves to the empress's faction—is this what a great man should do!

entries.zh: 逸民每有心托我，我常恐其溺於深淵而餘波及我，況可褰裳而就之哉！」
entries.en: Wei keeps trying to draw me in. I always fear that if he falls into the abyss the splash will reach me. How could I wade in after him!"
entries.literal: Yimin often wishes to entrust affairs to me; I constantly fear that if he falls into the deep abyss the dregs will splash upon me—how much less could I lift my robe and go to him!"

entries.zh: 初，廣城君郭槐，以賈后無子，常勸后使慈愛太子。
entries.en: Earlier Guo Huai, Lady of Guangcheng, because Empress Jia had no son of her own, often urged her to treat the heir apparent kindly.
entries.literal: Earlier the Lady of Guangcheng, Guo Huai, because Empress Jia had no son, often urged the empress to treat the Heir Apparent with kindness.

entries.zh: 賈謐驕縱，數無禮於太子，廣城君恆切責之。
entries.en: Jia Mi was arrogant and repeatedly insulted the heir apparent. The Lady of Guangcheng scolded him harshly again and again.
entries.literal: Jia Mi was arrogant and unrestrained, repeatedly disrespectful toward the Heir Apparent; the Lady of Guangcheng constantly rebuked him sharply.

entries.zh: 廣城君欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固；
entries.en: The Lady of Guangcheng wanted Han Shou's daughter as the heir apparent's consort, and the heir apparent likewise hoped to marry into the Han clan to strengthen his position;
entries.literal: The Lady of Guangcheng wished to make Han Shou's daughter the Heir Apparent's consort; the Heir Apparent also wished to marry into the Han clan to secure himself;

entries.zh: 壽妻賈午及后皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍少女。
entries.en: but Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress refused and betrothed the heir apparent to Wang Yan's younger daughter instead.
entries.literal: Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress would not agree, and instead betrothed to the Heir Apparent the younger daughter of Wang Yan.

entries.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而后為賈謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。
entries.en: The heir apparent heard that Yan's elder daughter was beautiful, yet the empress gave her to Jia Mi. He was bitter and complained openly.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent heard that Yan's elder daughter was beautiful, yet the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; he could not compose his heart and spoke of it with some resentment.

entries.zh: 及廣城君病，臨終，執后手，令盡心於太子，言甚切至。
entries.en: When the Lady of Guangcheng fell mortally ill, she took the empress's hand at the end and urged her with utmost earnestness to devote herself to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: When the Lady of Guangcheng fell ill, at the end she took the empress's hand and ordered her to devote her heart to the Heir Apparent, her words very earnest.

entries.zh: 又曰：「趙粲、賈午，必亂汝家事；
entries.en: She also said: "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely ruin your household.
entries.literal: She also said: "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely ruin your household affairs;

entries.zh: 我死後，勿復聽入。
entries.en: After I die, do not let them near you again.
entries.literal: after my death, do not again let them enter your counsel.

entries.zh: 深記吾言。」
entries.en: Remember this well."
entries.literal: Remember my words deeply."

entries.zh: 后不從，更與粲、午謀害太子。
entries.en: The empress ignored her and instead joined Can and Wu in plotting against the heir apparent.
entries.literal: The empress did not obey and instead joined with Can and Wu to plot harm to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 太子幼有令名，及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲。
entries.en: The heir apparent had a good name as a child, but as he grew he neglected study and played only with his attendants.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent in youth had a fine reputation; when he grew up he did not love learning and only played with those at his side.

entries.zh: 賈后復使黃門輩誘之為奢靡威虐，由是名譽浸減，驕慢益彰。
entries.en: Empress Jia also set Yellow Gate attendants to lure him into extravagance and cruelty. His reputation faded and his arrogance grew.
entries.literal: Empress Jia again had the Yellow Gate attendants entice him into extravagance and cruel arrogance; thereby his reputation gradually declined and his insolence grew more manifest.

entries.zh: 或廢朝侍而縱游逸，於宮中為市，使人屠酤，手揣斤兩，輕重不差。
entries.en: He sometimes skipped court to roam freely, opened a market inside the palace, had men butcher meat and sell wine, and weighed goods himself without missing by an ounce.
entries.literal: He sometimes skipped court attendance to roam in idleness, set up a market within the palace, had men butcher and sell wine, and weighed goods in his own hand without error in light and heavy.

entries.zh: 其母，本屠家女也，故太子好之。
entries.en: His mother had been a butcher's daughter, which is why he took to such pursuits.
entries.literal: His mother had originally been a butcher's daughter, and therefore the Heir Apparent delighted in such things.

entries.zh: 東宮月俸錢五十萬，太子常探取二月，用之猶不足。
entries.en: The Eastern Palace received five hundred thousand cash a month, yet he often drew two months' stipend at once and still found it insufficient.
entries.literal: The Eastern Palace's monthly stipend was five hundred thousand cash; the Heir Apparent often drew two months' worth at once and still found it insufficient.

entries.zh: 又令西園賣葵菜、藍子、雞、面等物而收其利。
entries.en: He also had the Western Garden sell vegetables, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and other goods for profit.
entries.literal: He also ordered the Western Garden to sell mallow, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and the like and collect the profit.

entries.zh: 又好陰陽小數，多所拘忌。
entries.en: He was also fond of yin-yang lore and petty numerology and observed many taboos.
entries.literal: He also loved yin-yang lore and petty numerology and was much bound by taboos.

entries.zh: 洗馬江統上書陳五事：「一曰雖有微苦，宜力疾朝侍。
entries.en: Jiang Tong, Groom of the Heir Apparent, memorialized with five recommendations: "First, though you are slightly unwell, you should force yourself to attend court.
entries.literal: The Groom of the Heir Apparent, Jiang Tong, submitted a memorial setting forth five points: "First, though there is slight illness, you ought to force yourself to attend court.

entries.zh: 二曰宜勤見保傅，咨讒善道。
entries.en: Second, you should often consult your tutors and seek the path of virtue.
entries.literal: Second, you ought diligently to see your tutors and consult them on the good path.

entries.zh: 三曰畫室之功，可且減省，後園刻鏤雜作，一皆罷遣。
entries.en: Third, cut back on the painting studios and dismiss all carved and inlaid work in the rear garden.
entries.literal: Third, the work of the painting studios may for now be reduced; carved and inlaid miscellaneous tasks in the rear garden should all be dismissed.

entries.zh: 四曰西園賣葵、藍之屬，虧敗國體，貶損令聞。
entries.en: Fourth, selling vegetables and indigo from the Western Garden disgraces the state and harms your reputation.
entries.literal: Fourth, selling mallow, indigo, and the like in the Western Garden damages the state's dignity and lowers your fine reputation.

entries.zh: 五曰繕牆正瓦，不必拘攣小忌。」
entries.en: Fifth, when repairing walls and resetting tiles, you need not be bound by petty taboos."
entries.literal: Fifth, when repairing walls and straightening tiles, you need not be bound by petty taboos."

entries.zh: 太子皆不從。
entries.en: The heir apparent ignored every point.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent would not follow any of them.

entries.zh: 中舍人杜錫，恐太子不得安其位，每盡忠諫，勸太子修德業，保令名，言辭懇切。
entries.en: Du Xi, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, fearing the heir apparent might lose his position, repeatedly urged him in loyal remonstrance to cultivate virtue and preserve his good name, his words earnest and forceful.
entries.literal: Du Xi, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, fearing the Heir Apparent could not secure his position, each time offered loyal remonstrance, urging the Heir Apparent to cultivate virtue and preserve his fine name, his words earnest.

entries.zh: 太子患之，置針著錫常所坐氈中，刺之流血，錫，預之子也。
entries.en: The heir apparent resented this, hid needles in the mat where Xi usually sat, and pricked him until he bled. Xi was the son of Du Yu.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent resented this, placed needles in the mat where Xi usually sat, and pricked him until he bled. Xi was the son of Du Yu.

entries.zh: 壬戌，帝幸式乾殿，召公卿入，使黃門令董猛以太子書及青紙詔示之曰：「遹書如此，今賜死。」
entries.en: On the day renxu the emperor went to the Shiqian Hall and summoned the ministers. Yellow Gate Commandant Dong Meng showed them the heir apparent's letter and a blue-paper edict, saying: "Yu wrote this. He is to die."
entries.literal: On the day renxu the emperor visited the Shiqian Hall, summoned the excellencies and ministers in, and had the Yellow Gate Commandant Dong Meng show them the Heir Apparent's letter and the blue-paper edict, saying: "Yu's letter is thus—now grant death."

entries.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者。
entries.en: He showed it to all the princes and nobles. No one spoke.
entries.literal: He showed it to all the princes and lords; none spoke.

entries.zh: 張華曰：「此國之大禍，自古以來，常因廢黜正嫡以致喪亂。
entries.en: Zhang Hua said, "This is a great calamity for the state. Since antiquity disorder has often followed the deposition of the legitimate heir.
entries.literal: Zhang Hua said: "This is a great calamity for the state. Since antiquity disorder has often come from deposing the legitimate heir.

entries.zh: 且國家有天下日淺，願陛下詳之！」
entries.en: Moreover the dynasty has held the realm only a short time. I beg Your Majesty to consider carefully!"
entries.literal: Moreover the state has held the realm but a short time—I beg Your Majesty to consider carefully!"

entries.zh: 裴頠以為宜先檢校傳書者，又請比較太子手書，不然，恐有詐妄。
entries.en: Pei Wei urged that the messenger be examined first and the handwriting compared with the heir apparent's own script, lest the letter be a forgery.
entries.literal: Pei Wei held that one ought first to examine and verify the person who transmitted the letter, and also requested comparison with the Heir Apparent's own handwriting; otherwise he feared there might be fraud.

entries.zh: 賈后乃出太子啟事十餘紙，眾人比視，亦無敢言非者。
entries.en: Empress Jia then produced more than ten sheets of the heir apparent's memorials. When the assembly compared them, no one dared say they did not match.
entries.literal: Empress Jia then produced more than ten sheets of the Heir Apparent's memorials; when the assembly compared them, none dared say they did not match.

entries.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各不同，其不從詔者，宜以軍法從事。」
entries.en: Empress Jia had Dong Meng report to the emperor in the name of the Princess of Changguang: "This must be decided at once. The ministers are divided. Those who disobey the edict should be dealt with by military law."
entries.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng, falsely in the name of the Princess of Changguang, report to the emperor: "The affair ought to be decided quickly, yet the ministers all differ; those who do not follow the edict ought to be handled by military law."

entries.zh: 議至日西，不決。
entries.en: Debate continued until sunset without resolution.
entries.literal: Deliberation continued until the sun was in the west, without decision.

entries.zh: 后見華等意堅，懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
entries.en: Seeing Zhang Hua and the others hold firm and fearing the plot might fail, the empress memorialized to depose the heir apparent as a commoner. The edict was approved.
entries.literal: The empress, seeing that Hua and the others were firm in intent and fearing the affair might change, submitted a memorial to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner; an edict approved it.

entries.zh: 於是使尚書和郁等持節詣東宮，廢太子為庶人，太子改服出，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車，車武公澹以兵仗送太子及妃王氏、三子虨、臧、尚同幽於金墉城。
entries.en: He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace. The heir apparent changed his garments, bowed twice, received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart. Sima Dan, Marquis of Chewu, escorted him with armed guards, together with his consort Lady Wang and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang, to confinement at Jinyong.
entries.literal: Thereupon He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner. The Heir Apparent changed his garments and came out, bowed twice and received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, rode a rough ox-cart, and the Marquis of Chewu, Sima Dan, with arms escorted the Heir Apparent, his consort Lady Wang, and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang together to be confined at Jinyong.

entries.zh: 王衍自表離婚，許之，妃慟哭而歸。
entries.en: Wang Yan memorialized to divorce her, and permission was granted. The consort returned home in bitter tears.
entries.literal: Wang Yan himself submitted a memorial requesting divorce; it was granted, and the consort returned home weeping bitterly.

entries.zh: 殺太子母謝淑媛及虨母保林蔣俊。
entries.en: The heir apparent's mother, Lady Xie the Gracious Lady, and Xian's mother, Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were executed.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent's mother, the Gracious Lady Xie, and Xian's mother, the Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were killed.

entries.zh: 西戎校尉司馬閻纘輿棺詣闕上書，以為：「漢戾太子稱兵拒命，言者猶曰罪當笞耳。
entries.en: Yan Xun, Major under the Colonel of the Western Rong, came to the palace gate with his coffin on a cart and submitted a memorial, arguing: "When Emperor Wu's heir apparent Liu Ju took up arms in rebellion, critics still said his offense deserved only a beating.
entries.literal: Yan Xun, Major of the Colonel of the Western Rong, came to the gate with his coffin on a cart and submitted a memorial, holding: "When the Han Heir Apparent Li raised troops and defied orders, those who spoke still said his crime merited only the bastinado.

entries.zh: 今遹受罪之日，不敢失道，猶為輕於戾太子。
entries.en: Now Yu stands condemned yet has not strayed from duty; even so his case is still treated more leniently than that of Crown Prince Li.
entries.literal: Now on the day Yu received punishment he did not dare stray from the Way, yet this is still lighter than the Heir Apparent Li.

entries.zh: 宜重選師傅，先加嚴誨，若不悛改，棄之未晚也。」書奏，不省。
entries.en: The court should appoint new tutors and admonish him strictly. If he does not reform, deposing him would not yet be too late." The memorial was submitted, but it was not examined.
entries.literal: One ought to choose tutors anew and first apply stern instruction; if he does not repent and reform, to discard him would not be too late." The memorial was submitted, but it was not examined.

entries.zh: 纘，圃之孫也。
entries.en: Xun was the grandson of Yan Pu.
entries.literal: Xun was the grandson of Yan Pu.

entries.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃中宮驕貴，不能假借之。
entries.en: The heir apparent was proud by nature. Knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent was by nature stern; knowing that Jia Mi relied on the central palace's arrogant eminence, he could not show him favor.

entries.zh: 謐時為侍中，至東宮，或捨之，於後庭遊戲。
entries.en: Mi was then Attendant of the Yellow Gate. When he visited the Eastern Palace the heir apparent sometimes dismissed him and amused himself in the rear court.
entries.literal: Mi was then Attendant of the Yellow Gate; when he came to the Eastern Palace the Heir Apparent sometimes dismissed him and played in the rear court.

entries.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「謐，后所親暱，一旦交構，則事危矣。」
entries.en: Steward Pei Quan warned him: "Mi is the empress's favorite. If you quarrel with him, disaster will follow."
entries.literal: The Steward Pei Quan remonstrated: "Mi is one the empress cherishes; if you should clash, the affair would be perilous."

entries.zh: 不從。
entries.en: He would not listen.
entries.literal: He did not heed him.

entries.zh: 謐譖太子於后曰：「太子多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。
entries.en: Mi slandered the heir apparent to the empress, saying: "He hoards private wealth to win over petty men because he means to destroy the Jia clan.
entries.literal: Mi slandered the Heir Apparent to the empress, saying: "The Heir Apparent amasses private wealth to win over petty men because of the Jia clan.

entries.zh: 若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等，廢后於金墉，如反手耳。
entries.en: When the emperor dies and he takes the throne, he will follow the Yang clan precedent, execute us, and imprison you at Jinyong. It will be as easy as turning his hand.
entries.literal: If the imperial carriage should halt forever and he take the great position, following the Yang clan precedent he would execute us ministers and depose the empress at Jinyong—it would be like turning the hand.

entries.zh: 不如早圖之，更立慈順者，可以自安。」
entries.en: Better act early and set up another heir who is mild and obedient. Then we may be safe."
entries.literal: Better to plot early, set up another who is kindly and obedient, and thus secure ourselves."

entries.zh: 后納其言，乃宣揚太子之短，佈於遠近。
entries.en: The empress accepted his counsel and spread the heir apparent's faults far and wide.
entries.literal: The empress accepted his words and thereupon spread abroad the Heir Apparent's faults, broadcasting them far and near.

entries.zh: 又詐為有娠，內蒿物、產具，取妹夫韓壽子慰祖養之，欲以代太子。
entries.en: She also feigned pregnancy, hid birthing supplies inside, took her brother-in-law Han Shou's son Weizu to rear, and planned to replace the heir apparent with him.
entries.literal: She also feigned pregnancy, hid artemisia and birthing gear within, took her brother-in-law Han Shou's son Weizu to rear, and intended to replace the Heir Apparent with him.

entries.zh: 十二月，太子長子虨病，太子為虨求王爵，不許。
entries.en: In the twelfth month the heir apparent's eldest son Sima Xian fell ill. The heir apparent asked that he be made a prince, but the request was denied.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month the Heir Apparent's eldest son Sima Xian fell ill; the Heir Apparent sought a princely title for Xian but was not granted it.

entries.zh: 虨疾篤，太子為之禱祀求福。
entries.en: As Xian grew gravely ill, the heir apparent prayed and offered sacrifices on his behalf.
entries.literal: When Xian's illness grew grave, the Heir Apparent prayed and offered sacrifices to seek blessing for him.

entries.zh: 賈后聞之，乃詐稱帝不豫，召太子入朝，既至，后不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞以帝命賜太子酒三升，使盡飲之。
entries.en: Empress Jia heard of this and falsely announced that the emperor was ill, summoning the heir apparent to court. When he arrived she refused to see him, placed him in a side room, and sent the maid Chen Wu with the emperor's name to give him three pints of wine and order him to drink it all.
entries.literal: When Empress Jia heard of it she falsely announced the emperor was unwell and summoned the Heir Apparent to court; once he arrived the empress did not see him but placed him in a separate room and sent the maid Chen Wu, in the emperor's name, to bestow three pints of wine on the Heir Apparent and order him to drink it all.

entries.zh: 太子辭以不能飲三升，舞逼之曰：「不孝邪！
entries.en: He declined, saying he could not drink so much. Wu pressed him: "Are you unfilial?
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent declined, saying he could not drink three pints; Wu pressed him: "Are you unfilial!

entries.zh: 天賜汝酒而不飲，酒中有惡物邪！」
entries.en: Heaven grants you wine and you refuse. Do you think it poisoned?"
entries.literal: Heaven bestows wine upon you and you will not drink—is there something evil in the wine!"

entries.zh: 太子不得已，強飲至盡，遂大醉。
entries.en: Unable to refuse further, he drank it all and became thoroughly drunk.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent had no choice, forced himself to drink to the end, and became very drunk.

entries.zh: 后使黃門侍朗潘岳作書草，令小婢承福，以紙筆及草，因太子醉，稱詔使書之，文曰：「陛下宜自了，不自了，吾當入了之。
entries.en: The empress had Pan Yue, Yellow Gate Attendant, draft a letter and sent the maid Cheng Fu with paper, brush, and draft. While the heir apparent was drunk she claimed an imperial order and made him copy it. The text read: "Your Majesty ought to settle this yourself. If you do not, I shall enter and settle it.
entries.literal: The empress had the Yellow Gate Attendant Pan Yue draft a letter, ordered the little maid Cheng Fu to bring paper, brush, and draft; taking advantage of the Heir Apparent's drunkenness she claimed an edict and made him write it. The text read: "Your Majesty ought to settle matters yourself; if you do not settle them, I shall enter and settle them.

entries.zh: 中宮又宜速自了，不自了，吾當手了之。
entries.en: The empress too ought quickly to settle matters herself. If she does not, I shall settle them with my own hand.
entries.literal: The central palace too ought quickly to settle matters herself; if she does not, I shall settle them with my own hand.

entries.zh: 並與謝妃共要，刻期兩發，勿疑猶豫，以致後患。
entries.en: I have agreed with Consort Xie. We have set a date for both to act. Do not hesitate and bring later trouble.
entries.literal: Together with Consort Xie we have agreed; set a date for both to act—do not doubt or hesitate and bring later trouble.

entries.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣氏為內主。
entries.en: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood under heaven. August Heaven has promised to sweep away the harm, establish Daowen as king, and make the Jiang clan the inner mistress.
entries.literal: Eating raw flesh and drinking blood beneath the three luminaries—August Heaven has promised to sweep away the harm, establish Daowen as king, and make the Jiang clan the inner mistress.

entries.zh: 願成，當三牲祠北君。」
entries.en: When it succeeds, we shall offer the three sacrificial beasts to the Northern Lord."
entries.literal: When the wish is fulfilled, we shall offer the three sacrificial beasts to the Northern Lord."

entries.zh: 太子醉迷不覺，遂依而寫之。
entries.en: Drunk and unaware, he copied it as dictated.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent, drunk and dazed and unaware, thereupon copied it as given.

entries.zh: 其字半不成，后補成之，以呈帝。
entries.en: Half the characters were incomplete. The empress finished them and presented the letter to the emperor.
entries.literal: Half his characters were incomplete; the empress completed them and presented it to the emperor.

entries.zh: 於時朝野咸知賈后有害太子之意，中護軍趙俊請太子廢后，太子不聽。
entries.en: By then everyone knew Empress Jia meant to destroy the heir apparent. Zhao Jun, Central Protector of the Army, urged him to depose her, but he refused.
entries.literal: At that time court and commonalty alike knew Empress Jia meant harm to the Heir Apparent; the Central Protector of the Army Zhao Jun asked the Heir Apparent to depose the empress, but the Heir Apparent would not listen.

entries.zh: 左衛率東平劉卞，以賈后之謀問張華，華曰：「不聞。」
entries.en: Liu Bian of Dongping, Colonel of the Left Guards, asked Zhang Hua about the empress's plot. Hua said, "I have heard nothing."
entries.literal: Liu Bian of Dongping, Colonel of the Left Guards, asked Zhang Hua about Empress Jia's plot; Hua said: "I have not heard of it."

entries.zh: 卞曰：「卞自須昌小吏，受公成拔以至今日。
entries.en: Bian said, "I was only a petty clerk in Xuchang until you raised me to what I am today.
entries.literal: Bian said: "Bian rose from a petty clerk in Xuchang through your grace's full promotion to reach today.

entries.zh: 士感知己，是以盡言，而公更有疑於卞邪！」
entries.en: A gentleman repays his patron with full candor. Do you still doubt me?"
entries.literal: A gentleman who knows gratitude to his patron therefore speaks fully—yet does Your Excellency still doubt Bian!"

entries.zh: 華曰：「假令有此，君欲如何？」
entries.en: Hua asked, "Suppose it were true. What would you do?"
entries.literal: Hua said: "Suppose there were such a thing—what would you intend?"

entries.zh: 卞曰：「東宮俊乂如林，四率精兵萬人；
entries.en: Bian said, "The Eastern Palace has talent in abundance, and the four colonels command ten thousand elite troops.
entries.literal: Bian said: "The Eastern Palace has talented men like a forest; the four colonels command elite troops of ten thousand;

entries.zh: 公居阿衡之任，若得公命，皇太子因朝入錄尚書事，廢賈后於金墉城，兩黃門力耳。」
entries.en: You hold the chief minister's power. With your order the heir apparent could enter court, take charge of the Masters of Writing, and depose Empress Jia at Jinyong. It would take only two Yellow Gate attendants."
entries.literal: Your Excellency holds the office of chief minister; if we obtain your command, the Heir Apparent can enter at court to record the Masters of Writing affairs and depose Empress Jia at Jinyong—it is only the strength of two Yellow Gate attendants."

entries.zh: 華曰：「今天子當陽，太子，人子也，吾又不受阿衡之命，忽相與行此，是無君父而以不孝示天下也。
entries.en: Hua said, "The emperor reigns in his own right. The heir apparent is his son, and I have received no commission as chief minister. To act suddenly in this way would be to cast aside ruler and father and show the world an act of filial impiety.
entries.literal: Hua said: "Today the Son of Heaven faces the sun; the Heir Apparent is a human son, and I have not received the chief minister's commission—suddenly to act together in this would be to have no ruler or father and display filial impiety to the realm.

entries.zh: 雖能有成，猶不免罪。
entries.en: Even if we succeeded, we would still be guilty.
entries.literal: Even if we could succeed, we would still not escape guilt.

entries.zh: 況權戚滿朝，威柄不一，成可必乎？」
entries.en: Besides, powerful kin fill the court and power is divided. Can success be certain?"
entries.literal: Moreover the powerful kin fill the court and authority is not unified—can success be certain?"

entries.zh: 賈后常使親黨微服聽察於外，頗聞卞言，乃遷卞為雍州刺史；
entries.en: Empress Jia often had her kin spy in disguise and learned of Bian's words. She transferred him to Inspector of Yongzhou;
entries.literal: Empress Jia often had her kin in plain dress listen and observe outside and heard much of Bian's words; she thereupon transferred Bian to be Inspector of Yongzhou;

entries.zh: 卞知言洩，飲藥而死。
entries.en: and Bian, knowing his plot had leaked, took poison and died.
entries.literal: Bian, knowing his words had leaked, took poison and died.

entries.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之下永康元年（
entries.en: Under Emperor Hui of Jin, Yongkang, year 1 (
entries.literal: The lower portion of the first reign of Emperor Xiaohui, first year of Yongkang (

entries.zh: 庚申，公元三零零年）
entries.en: gengshen, CE 300)
entries.literal: gengshen, common era year 300)

entries.zh: 賈后使黃門自首欲與太子為逆。
entries.en: Empress Jia had a Yellow Gate attendant confess a plot to rebel with the heir apparent.
entries.literal: Empress Jia had a Yellow Gate attendant confess that he wished to rebel with the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿，遣東武公澹以千兵防衛太子，幽於許昌宮，令持書御史劉振持節守之，詔宮臣不得辭送。
entries.en: An edict showed the confession to the ministers, sent Sima Dan, Marquis of Dongwu, with a thousand troops to guard the heir apparent at Xuchang Palace, and ordered Liu Zhen, Attendant Secretary with credentials, to hold him under guard, forbidding palace officials to escort him on departure.
entries.literal: An edict displayed the Yellow Gate confessor's testimony to the excellencies and ministers, dispatched the Marquis of Dongwu Sima Dan with a thousand troops to guard the Heir Apparent, confined him at the Xuchang palace, ordered the Attendant Secretary with credentials Liu Zhen to hold him under guard, and decreed that palace officials might not take leave to escort him.

entries.zh: 洗馬江統、潘滔、舍人王敦、杜蕤、魯瑤等冒禁至伊水，拜辭涕泣。
entries.en: Jiang Tong, Pan Tao, Wang Dun, Du Rui, Lu Yao, and others defied the ban, went to the Yi River, bowed farewell, and wept.
entries.literal: The Groom Jiang Tong, Pan Tao, Attendant Wang Dun, Du Rui, Lu Yao, and others braved the prohibition to reach the Yi River, bowed in farewell, and wept.

entries.zh: 司隸校尉滿奮收縛統籌送獄。
entries.en: Colonel of the Censorate Man Fen arrested Tong and the others and sent them to prison.
entries.literal: The Colonel of the Censorate Man Fen arrested and bound Tong and his companions and sent them to prison.

entries.zh: 其系河南獄者，樂廣悉解遣之；
entries.en: Those held in the Henan prison were all released by Yue Guang;
entries.literal: Those held in the Henan prison were all released by Yue Guang;

entries.zh: 系洛陽縣獄者，猶未釋。
entries.en: those held in the Luoyang county prison were not yet released.
entries.literal: those held in the Luoyang county prison were still not released.

entries.zh: 都官從事孫琰說賈謐曰：「所以廢徙太子，以其為惡故耳。
entries.en: Director of Justice Sun Yan told Jia Mi: "The heir apparent was deposed because he was wicked.
entries.literal: Director of Justice Sun Yan said to Jia Mi: "The reason for deposing and relocating the Heir Apparent is that he was wicked.

entries.zh: 今宮臣冒罪拜辭，而加以重辟；
entries.en: Yet you would punish palace officials who came to bid him farewell;
entries.literal: Now palace officials offend the law to bid farewell; yet you add heavy punishment;

entries.zh: 流聞四方，乃更彰太子之德也，不如釋之。」
entries.en: If word spreads abroad it will only highlight the heir apparent's virtue. Better release them."
entries.literal: if this spreads to the four quarters it will only make the Heir Apparent's virtue more manifest—better to release them."

entries.zh: 謐乃語洛陽令曹攄使釋之；
entries.en: Mi then told Cao Shu, Magistrate of Luoyang, to release them;
entries.literal: Mi thereupon told the Magistrate of Luoyang Cao Shu to release them;

entries.zh: 廣亦不坐。
entries.en: Guang was not punished either.
entries.literal: Guang was also not punished.

entries.zh: 敦，覽之孫；
entries.en: Dun was the grandson of Wang Lan;
entries.literal: Dun was the grandson of Wang Lan;

entries.zh: 攄，肇之孫也。
entries.en: Shu was the grandson of Cao Zhao.
entries.literal: Shu was the grandson of Cao Zhao.

entries.zh: 太子至許，遺王妃書，自陳誣枉，妃父衍不敢以聞。
entries.en: At Xu the heir apparent wrote to his consort proclaiming his innocence; her father Wang Yan did not dare report it.
entries.literal: When the Heir Apparent reached Xu he sent a letter to the consort stating his false accusation; the consort's father Yan did not dare report it.

entries.zh: 秀因使人行反間，言殿中人欲廢皇后，迎太子。
entries.en: Xiu spread disinformation that palace insiders meant to depose the empress and restore the heir apparent.
entries.literal: Xiu therefore sent men to spread counter-intelligence, saying those in the palace wished to depose the empress and welcome the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 賈后數遣宮婢微服於民間聽察，聞之甚懼。
entries.en: The empress often sent maids in disguise to listen among the people and was terrified.
entries.literal: Empress Jia often sent palace maids in plain dress among the people to listen; hearing this she was greatly afraid.

entries.zh: 倫、秀因勸謐等早除太子，以絕眾望。
entries.en: Lun and Xiu urged Mi and others to kill the heir apparent at once and end public hope.
entries.literal: Lun and Xiu therefore urged Mi and the rest to eliminate the Heir Apparent early and cut off public hope.

entries.zh: 癸未，賈后使太醫令程據和毒藥。
entries.en: On guimao the empress had Cheng Ju, Director of Imperial Physicians, prepare poison.
entries.literal: On the day guimao Empress Jia had the Director of Imperial Physicians Cheng Ju compound poison.

entries.zh: 矯詔使黃門孫慮至許昌毒太子。
entries.en: A forged edict sent Sun Lv of the Yellow Gate to Xuchang to poison the heir apparent.
entries.literal: A forged edict sent the Yellow Gate Sun Lv to Xuchang to poison the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 太子自廢黜，恐被毒，常自煮食於前；
entries.en: Since his deposition he feared poison and often cooked for himself;
entries.literal: Since his deposition the Heir Apparent feared poison and often cooked his own food beforehand;

entries.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子於小坊中，絕其食，宮人猶竊於牆上過食與之。
entries.en: Lv told Liu Zhen, who moved him to a small compound and cut off food, though palace women still passed food over the wall.
entries.literal: Lv reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen then moved the Heir Apparent to a small compound and cut off his food, yet palace women still secretly passed food over the wall.

entries.zh: 慮逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，慮以藥杵椎殺之。
entries.en: Lv forced the drug on him; he refused; Lv beat him to death with the pestle.
entries.literal: Lv forced the Heir Apparent to take the drug; he refused; Lv killed him with the drug pestle.

entries.zh: 有司請以庶人禮葬，賈后表請以廣陵王禮葬之。
entries.en: Officials requested commoner burial; the empress asked for princely rites as for the Prince of Guangling.
entries.literal: The authorities requested burial with commoner rites; the empress memorialized for burial with the rites of a Prince of Guangling.

entries.zh: 倫陰與秀謀篡位，欲先除朝望，且報宿怨，乃執張華、裴頠、解系、解結等於殿前。
entries.en: Lun secretly plotted usurpation with Xiu, first removing leading ministers and settling old scores; he seized Zhang Hua, Pei Wei, Xie Ji, Xie Jie, and others in the hall.
entries.literal: Lun secretly plotted with Xiu to usurp the throne, wishing first to remove men of court esteem and also settle old scores; he seized Zhang Hua, Pei Wei, Xie Ji, Xie Jie, and others before the hall.

entries.zh: 華謂張林曰：「卿欲害忠臣邪？」
entries.en: Hua said to Zhang Lin: "Do you mean to kill loyal ministers?"
entries.literal: Hua said to Zhang Lin: "Do you wish to harm loyal ministers?"

entries.zh: 林稱詔詰之曰：「卿為宰相，太子之廢，不能死節，何也？」
entries.en: Lin, citing the edict, demanded: "As chief minister, when the heir apparent was deposed why did you not die for principle?"
entries.literal: Lin, claiming the edict, interrogated him: "You were chief minister; when the Heir Apparent was deposed you could not die for principle—why?"

entries.zh: 華曰：「式乾之議，臣諫事具存，可覆按也。」
entries.en: Hua said: "My remonstrance at the Shiqian deliberation is on record and may be reviewed."
entries.literal: Hua said: "On the deliberation at Shiqian my remonstrance is fully recorded and may be reviewed."

entries.zh: 林曰：「諫而不從，何不去位？」
entries.en: Lin said: "If remonstrance failed, why not resign?"
entries.literal: Lin said: "If you remonstrated and were not obeyed, why not leave office?"

entries.zh: 華無以對。
entries.en: Hua had no answer.
entries.literal: Hua had no reply.

entries.zh: 遂皆斬之，仍夷三族。
entries.en: All were beheaded and their clans exterminated to the third degree.
entries.literal: They were all beheaded and their clans exterminated to the third degree.

entries.zh: 解結女適裴氏，明日當嫁而禍起，裴氏欲認活之，女曰：「家既若此，我何以活為！」
entries.en: Xie Jie's daughter was to marry into the Pei clan next day when disaster struck; the Peis wished to save her; she said: "With my house destroyed, how can I live!"
entries.literal: Xie Jie's daughter was betrothed to the Pei clan; the wedding was due the next day when disaster struck; the Pei wished to claim her alive; the girl said: "With my house thus, how can I live!"

entries.zh: 亦坐死。
entries.en: She died as well.
entries.literal: She too died for it.

entries.zh: 朝廷由是議革舊制，女不從死。
entries.en: The court then debated abolishing the old rule that wives and daughters die with the clan.
entries.literal: The court thereupon debated abolishing the old rule that daughters follow their kin to death.

entries.zh: 甲午，倫坐端門，遣尚書和郁持節送賈庶人於金墉；
entries.en: On jiawu Lun sat at the Duan Gate and sent He Yu with credentials to convey the deposed empress to Jinyong;
entries.literal: On the day jiawu Lun sat at the Duan Gate and sent the Masters of Writing He Yu with credentials to convey the deposed Jia commoner to Jinyong;

entries.zh: 誅劉振、董猛、孫慮、程據等；
entries.en: Liu Zhen, Dong Meng, Sun Lv, Cheng Ju, and others were executed;
entries.literal: Liu Zhen, Dong Meng, Sun Lv, Cheng Ju, and others were executed;

entries.zh: 司徒王戎及內外官坐張、裴親黨黜免者甚眾。
entries.en: Minister over the Masses Wang Rong and many inner and outer officials were dismissed as kin to Zhang and Pei.
entries.literal: the Minister over the Masses Wang Rong and inner and outer officials dismissed as kin to Zhang and Pei were very numerous.

entries.zh: 閻纘撫張華屍慟哭曰：「早語君遜位而不肯，今果不免，命也！」
entries.en: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I urged you to resign and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"
entries.literal: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I told you early to yield your post and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"

entries.zh: 太子既廢，眾情憤怒。
entries.en: Once the heir apparent was deposed, public anger boiled over.
entries.literal: Once the Heir Apparent was deposed, public sentiment was furious.

entries.zh: 有衛督司馬雅、常從督許超，皆嘗給事東宮，與殿中郎士猗等謀廢賈后，復太子。
entries.en: Sima Ya, Colonel of the Guards, and Xu Chao, Regular Colonel of the Followers, both former Eastern Palace attendants, joined Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others to plot deposing Empress Jia and restoring the heir apparent.
entries.literal: The Colonel of the Guards Sima Ya and the Regular Colonel of the Followers Xu Chao, who had both once served the Eastern Palace, joined the Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others in plotting to depose Empress Jia and restore the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 以張華、裴頠安常保位，難與行權，右軍將軍趙王倫執兵柄，性貪冒，可假以濟事。
entries.en: They judged Zhang Hua and Pei Wei too cautious to act, while Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, held the armies and was greedy—he could be used.
entries.literal: They judged Zhang Hua and Pei Wei content to preserve their posts and hard to move to action, while the General of the Right Army the Prince of Zhao Sima Lun held military power and was greedy—he could be borrowed to accomplish the affair.

entries.zh: 乃說孫秀曰：「中宮凶妒無道，與賈謐等共誣廢太子。
entries.en: They told Sun Xiu: "The empress is vicious and lawless. With Jia Mi she framed and deposed the heir apparent.
entries.literal: They thereupon said to Sun Xiu: "The central palace is fierce, jealous, and without the Way, and together with Jia Mi and others falsely deposed the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 今國無嫡嗣，社稷將危，大臣將起大事，而公名奉事中宮，與賈、郭親善，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一朝事起，禍必相及，何不先謀之乎！」
entries.en: The realm lacks a legitimate heir and the altars are endangered. Great ministers will act, yet you serve the empress and are close to the Jia and Guo clans. When the heir apparent fell, men said you knew beforehand. When trouble erupts you will not escape—why not strike first?"
entries.literal: Now the state has no legitimate heir and the altars are in peril; the great ministers will raise a great affair, yet you by name attend the central palace and are intimate with the Jia and Guo—when the Heir Apparent was deposed all said you foreknew it. Once trouble rises disaster must reach you—why not plot first!"

entries.zh: 秀許諾，言於倫，倫納焉，遂告通事令史張林及省事張衡等，使為內應。
entries.en: Xiu agreed and told Lun, who accepted and enlisted Zhang Lin and Zhang Heng as inside agents.
entries.literal: Xiu promised and spoke to Lun; Lun accepted, and reported to the clerks Zhang Lin and Zhang Heng among the communications staff to serve as inside agents.

entries.zh: 趙王倫、孫秀將討賈后，告右衛佽飛督閭和，和從之，期以癸巳丙夜一籌，以鼓聲為應。
entries.en: Lun and Xiu prepared to move against the empress, won over Lü He, Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants, and set guisi night, second watch of the bing hour, drums as signal.
entries.literal: The Prince of Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu were about to attack Empress Jia; they told the Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants Lü He, who joined them, fixing the night of guisi on the second watch of the bing hour, with drumbeats as signal.

entries.zh: 癸巳，秀使司馬雅告張華曰：「趙王欲與公共匡社稷，為天下除害，使雅以告。」
entries.en: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join you to save the realm and remove this evil."
entries.literal: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join with you to steady the altars, remove harm for the realm—Ya reports this."

entries.zh: 華拒之。
entries.en: Hua refused.
entries.literal: Hua refused.

entries.zh: 雅怒曰：「刃將加頸，猶為是言邪！」
entries.en: Ya snapped: "The blade is at your neck and you still talk like that!"
entries.literal: Ya angrily said: "The blade is at the neck—yet you speak thus!"

entries.zh: 不顧而出。
entries.en: He strode out without a backward glance.
entries.literal: He left without looking back.

entries.zh: 及期，倫矯詔敕三部司馬曰：「中宮與賈謐等殺吾太子，今使車騎入廢中宮，汝等皆當從命，事畢，賜爵關中侯，不從者誅三族。」
entries.en: At the hour Lun forged an edict to the three departments: "The empress and Jia Mi killed the heir apparent. The Cavalry General enters to depose her. Obey and receive marquisates; disobey and face extermination."
entries.literal: When the hour came Lun forged an edict instructing the three departments' majors: "The central palace and Jia Mi and others killed our Heir Apparent; the Cavalry General will enter and depose the central palace—you must all obey. When done, enfeoffment as marquis within the passes; disobedience exterminates three clans."

entries.zh: 眾皆從之。
entries.en: All obeyed.
entries.literal: All obeyed.

entries.zh: 又矯詔開門，夜入，陳兵道南，遣翊軍校尉齊王冏將百人排冏而入，華林令駱休為內應，迎帝幸東堂，以詔召賈謐於殿前，將誅之。
entries.en: He forged orders to open the gates, entered at night, lined troops along the southern route, sent Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, with a hundred men to force entry, Luo Xiu of Hualin as inside agent, escorted the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and summoned Jia Mi to execution.
entries.literal: He also forged an edict to open the gates, entered by night, arrayed troops along the southern way, sent the Colonel of the Supports the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong with a hundred men to force the gates and enter, the Commandant of the Hualin Park Luo Xiu as inside agent, brought the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and by edict summoned Jia Mi before the hall to be executed.

entries.zh: 謐走入西鐘下，呼曰：「阿后救我！」
entries.en: Mi fled to the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"
entries.literal: Mi ran beneath the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"

entries.zh: 就斬之。
entries.en: He was beheaded at once.
entries.literal: He was beheaded on the spot.

entries.zh: 賈后見齊王冏，驚曰：「卿何為來？」
entries.en: Seeing Sima Jiong the empress cried: "Why are you here?"
entries.literal: When Empress Jia saw Sima Jiong she exclaimed: "Why have you come?"

entries.zh: 冏曰：「有詔收后。」
entries.en: Jiong said: "An edict commands your arrest."
entries.literal: Jiong said: "There is an edict to take the empress."

entries.zh: 后曰：「詔當從我出，何詔也！」
entries.en: She said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"
entries.literal: The empress said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"

entries.zh: 后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢矣。」
entries.en: She climbed to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor: "You have a wife; when others depose her, you will be deposed yourself."
entries.literal: She went up to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor from afar: "Your Majesty has a consort; when others deposed her, you too will be deposed."

entries.zh: 是時，梁王肜亦預其謀，后問冏曰：「起事者誰？」
entries.en: The Prince of Liang Sima Rong was also in the plot; she asked Jiong: "Who raised this?"
entries.literal: At that time the Prince of Liang Sima Rong also took part in the plot; the empress asked Jiong: "Who raised the affair?"

entries.zh: 冏曰：「梁、趙。」
entries.en: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."
entries.literal: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."

entries.zh: 后曰：「系狗當繫頸，反系其尾，何得不然！」
entries.en: She said: "Tie a dog by the neck, not the tail—was this not inevitable!"
entries.literal: The empress said: "When tying a dog one should tie the neck—instead they tied the tail; how could it not turn out thus!"

entries.zh: 遂廢后為庶人，幽之於建始殿，收趙粲、賈午等付暴室考竟。
entries.en: She was deposed as a commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were sent to the Severe Chamber for interrogation unto death.
entries.literal: She was thereupon deposed as commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were taken to the Severe Chamber for interrogation to the death.

entries.zh: 詔尚書收捕賈氏親黨，召中書監、侍中、黃門侍郎、八座皆夜入殿。
entries.en: An edict ordered arrest of the Jia clan; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and Eight Seats were summoned at night.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the Masters of Writing to arrest the Jia kin; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and the Eight Seats were all summoned into the hall at night.

entries.zh: 尚書始疑詔有詐，郎師景露版奏請手詔，倫等斬之以徇。
entries.en: The Masters of Writing doubted the edict; Gentleman Shi Jing asked for the emperor's own hand; Lun beheaded him as warning.
entries.literal: The Masters of Writing at first doubted the edict was false; Gentleman Shi Jing displayed the tablet and asked for a handwritten edict; Lun and the rest beheaded him as a warning.

entries.zh: 三月，尉氏雨血，妖星見南方，太白晝見，中台星拆。
entries.en: In the third month blood rained at Weishi, an ominous star appeared in the south, Venus was seen by day, and the Central Terrace star split.
entries.literal: In the third month blood rained at Weishi, an ominous star appeared in the south, the Great White was seen by day, and the Central Terrace star split.

entries.zh: 張華少子韙勸華遜位，華不從，曰：「天道幽遠，不如靜以待之。」
entries.en: Hua's younger son Wei urged him to resign; Hua refused, saying: "Heaven's way is obscure. Better to wait quietly."
entries.literal: Zhang Hua's younger son Wei urged Hua to yield his post; Hua would not, saying: "The Way of Heaven is remote and obscure—better to wait quietly."

entries.zh: 事將起，孫秀言於倫曰：「太子聰明剛猛，若還東宮，必不受制於人。
entries.en: Before the coup Sun Xiu told Lun: "The heir apparent is clever and fierce. Restored to the Eastern Palace he will not submit to anyone.
entries.literal: As the affair was about to begin, Sun Xiu said to Lun: "The Heir Apparent is intelligent, stern, and fierce; if restored to the Eastern Palace he will surely not be controlled by others.

entries.zh: 明公素黨於賈后，道路皆知之，今雖建大功於太子，太子謂公特逼於百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳，雖含忍宿忿，必不能深德明公，若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。
entries.en: You have always sided with the empress—everyone knows it. Even if you now save him, he will think you acted only under public pressure and may turn on you to clear himself. Old grudges will not become deep gratitude; the slightest fault could still cost your life.
entries.literal: Your Excellency has always been of the empress's party—the roads all know it. Though you now perform a great service for the Heir Apparent, he will say you acted only under the people's pressure and may turn to escape guilt; though he swallow old resentment he cannot deeply reward you, and if there be a flaw you still cannot escape execution.

entries.zh: 不若遷延緩期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，豈徒免禍而已，乃更可以得志！」
entries.en: Delay instead. The empress will kill him. Then depose her and avenge him—not merely escaping harm but winning your ambition!"
entries.literal: Better to delay and wait: the empress will surely harm the Heir Apparent; then depose the empress and avenge the Heir Apparent—not only escaping disaster but gaining your ambition!"

entries.zh: 倫然之。
entries.en: Lun agreed.
entries.literal: Lun agreed.

entries.zh: 於是趙王倫稱詔赦天下，自為使持節、都督中外諸軍事、相國、侍中，一依宣、文輔魏故事。
entries.en: Lun proclaimed amnesty, made himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief, Chancellor, and Attendant, following the precedents of the Sima regents of Wei.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Zhao Lun proclaimed an edict amnestying the realm, made himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs, Chancellor, and Attendant, following the precedents of Xuan and Wen in assisting Wei.

entries.zh: 置府兵萬人，以其世子散騎常侍荂領冗從僕射，子馥為前將軍，封濟陽王；
entries.en: He stationed ten thousand household troops; his heir Fu, Regular Attendant, held redundant Follower posts; son Fu was Forward General, Prince of Jiyang;
entries.literal: He stationed ten thousand troops at his headquarters; his heir, Regular Attendant Within the Encampment Fu, held redundant Followers as Vice-Director; his son Fu was Forward General and Prince of Jiyang;

entries.zh: 虔為黃門朗，封汝陰王；
entries.en: Qian was Yellow Gate Gentleman, Prince of Runan;
entries.literal: Qian was Yellow Gate Gentleman, Prince of Runan;

entries.zh: 詡為散騎侍郎，封霸城侯。
entries.en: Xu was Gentleman of the Encampment, Marquis of Bacheng.
entries.literal: Xu was Gentleman of the Encampment, Marquis of Bacheng.

entries.zh: 孫秀等皆封大郡，並據兵權，文武官封侯者數千人，百官總己以聽於倫。
entries.en: Sun Xiu and others received great fiefs and military power; thousands of officials were enfeoffed; all offices reported to Lun.
entries.literal: Sun Xiu and the rest were all enfeoffed in great commanderies and held military power; civil and military officials enfeoffed as marquis numbered in the thousands; the hundred offices all reported to Lun.

entries.zh: 倫素庸愚，復受制於孫秀。
entries.en: Lun was mediocre and foolish and controlled by Sun Xiu.
entries.literal: Lun was by nature mediocre and foolish and again controlled by Sun Xiu.

entries.zh: 秀為中書令，威權振朝廷，天下皆事秀而無求於倫。
entries.en: Xiu became Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; power radiated from him; the realm served Xiu, not Lun.
entries.literal: Xiu was Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; his authority shook the court; the realm served Xiu and sought nothing from Lun.

entries.zh: 相國倫欲收入望，選用海內名德之士，以前平陽太守李重、滎陽太守荀組為左、右長史，東平王堪、沛國劉謨為左、右司馬，尚書郎陽平束皙為記室，淮南王文學荀嵩、殿中郎陸機為參軍。
entries.en: Lun sought esteem and recruited renowned men: Li Chong and Xun Zu as chief clerks; Kan, Prince of Dongping, and Liu Mo as majors; Shuxi as recorder; Xun Song and Lu Ji on staff.
entries.literal: Chancellor Lun wished to win esteem and selected men of virtue throughout the realm: the former Administrator of Pingyang Li Chong and Administrator of Xingyang Xun Zu as Left and Right Chief Clerks; the Prince of Dongping Kan and Liu Mo of Peiguo as Left and Right Majors; Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Shuxi of Yangping as Recorder; the Literary Scholar of Huainan Xun Song and Palace Gentleman Lu Ji as Staff.

entries.zh: 組，勖之子；
entries.en: Zu was the son of Xun Xu;
entries.literal: Zu was the son of Xun Xu;

entries.zh: 嵩，彧之玄孫也。
entries.en: Song was the great-great-grandson of Xun Yu.
entries.literal: Song was the great-great-grandson of Xun Yu.

entries.zh: 李重知倫有異志，辭疾不就，倫逼之不已，憂憤成疾，扶曳受拜，數日而卒。
entries.en: Li Chong saw Lun's rebellious intent, pleaded illness, was forced to accept office, and died within days of grief.
entries.literal: Li Chong knew Lun harbored rebellious intent, declined illness and would not come; Lun pressed him without cease; he fell ill from grief and anger, was carried in to accept appointment, and died within days.

entries.zh: 太子遹之廢也，將立淮南王允為太弟，議者不合。
entries.en: When Yu was deposed they considered making Yun, Prince of Huainan, heir younger brother; deliberators disagreed.
entries.literal: When the Heir Apparent Yu was deposed, they were about to establish the Prince of Huainan Yun as heir younger brother; deliberators did not agree.

entries.zh: 會趙王倫廢賈后，乃以允為驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，領中護軍。
entries.en: When Lun deposed the empress, Yun was made General of Agile Cavalry with Three Excellencies privilege and Central Protector.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Zhao Lun deposed Empress Jia, Yun was made General of Agile Cavalry with privilege as the Three Excellencies and Commander of the Central Protector of the Army.

entries.zh: 己亥，相國倫矯詔遣尚書劉弘繼金屑酒，賜賈后死於金墉城。
entries.en: On jihai Lun forged an edict sending Liu Hong with golden crumbs wine to kill the deposed empress at Jinyong.
entries.literal: On the day jihai Chancellor Lun forged an edict sending the Masters of Writing Liu Hong with golden crumbs wine to grant the deposed Jia empress death at Jinyong.

entries.zh: 五月，己巳，詔立臨淮王臧為皇太孫，還妃王氏以母之；
entries.en: In the fifth month, on jisi, Zang, Prince of Linhuai, was made Imperial Grandson and Lady Wang restored as his mother;
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on the day jisi, an edict established the Prince of Linhuai Zang as Imperial Grandson and returned Consort Lady Wang as his mother;

entries.zh: 太子官屬即轉為太孫官屬，相國倫行太孫太傅。
entries.en: Eastern Palace staff became the Grandson's staff, and Lun acted as Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: Eastern Palace officials became Grandson's officials, and Chancellor Lun acted as Grandson's Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 詔追復故太子遹位號，使尚書和郁帥東宮官屬迎太子喪於許昌，追封遹子虨為南陽王，封虨弟臧為臨淮王，尚為襄陽王。
entries.en: An edict restored Yu's title, sent He Yu to bring the coffin from Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Xian as Prince of Nanyang and brothers Zang and Shang as princes.
entries.literal: An edict restored the former Heir Apparent Yu's title and rank, sent the Masters of Writing He Yu leading Eastern Palace officials to meet the Heir Apparent's coffin at Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Yu's son Xian as Prince of Nanyang, and enfeoffed Xian's brothers Zang as Prince of Linhuai and Shang as Prince of Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 己卯，謚故太子曰愍懷；
entries.en: On jimao the former heir apparent received the posthumous title Minhuai;
entries.literal: On the day jimao the former Heir Apparent was given the posthumous title Minhuai;

entries.zh: 六月，壬寅，葬於顯平陵。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on renyin, he was buried at Xianping Tomb.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on the day renyin, he was buried at Xianping Tomb.

entries.zh: 有司奏：「尚書令王衍備位大臣，太子被誣，志在苟免，請禁錮終身。」
entries.en: Authorities memorialized: "Wang Yan, having held high office, sought only to save himself when the heir apparent was framed, and asked lifelong ban from office."
entries.literal: The authorities memorialized: "Wang Yan, Director of the Masters of Writing, occupied a minister's post; when the Heir Apparent was falsely accused his aim was only to escape harm—request lifelong prohibition from office."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Granted.
entries.literal: It was granted.

entries.zh: 丁酉，以梁王肜為太宰，左光祿大夫何劭為司徒，右光祿大夫劉寔為司空。
entries.en: On dingyou Sima Rong was made Grand Preceptor, He Shao Minister over the Masses, Liu Shi Minister of Works.
entries.literal: On the day dingyou the Prince of Liang Sima Rong was made Grand Preceptor, He Shao was made Minister over the Masses, and Liu Shi was made Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 中護軍淮南王允，性沉毅，宿衛將士皆畏服之。
entries.en: Yun, Prince of Huainan, Central Protector of the Army, was deep and resolute by nature, and the palace guards all feared him.
entries.literal: The Central Protector of the Army, the Prince of Huainan Yun, was by nature deep and resolute; the garrison soldiers all feared and submitted to him.

entries.zh: 允知相國倫及孫秀有異志，陰養死士，謀討之；
entries.en: Knowing Lun and Xiu meant to rebel, he secretly gathered men willing to die and plotted against them;
entries.literal: Yun knew Chancellor Lun and Sun Xiu harbored rebellious intent and secretly nurtured men willing to die, plotting to attack them;

entries.zh: 倫、秀深憚之。
entries.en: Lun and Xiu feared him deeply.
entries.literal: Lun and Xiu deeply dreaded him.

entries.zh: 秋，八月，轉允為太尉，外示優崇，實奪其兵權。
entries.en: In autumn, the eighth month, he was transferred to Grand Commandant, an outward honor that in fact stripped him of military command.
entries.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Yun was transferred to Grand Commandant—outwardly a mark of honor, in reality his military power was taken away.

entries.zh: 允稱疾不拜。
entries.en: He pleaded illness and refused the appointment.
entries.literal: Yun pleaded illness and would not accept the appointment.

entries.zh: 秀遣御史劉機逼允，收其官屬以下，劾以拒詔，大逆不敬。
entries.en: Xiu sent Censor Liu Ji to coerce him, arrested his staff, and charged him with resisting an edict and great impiety.
entries.literal: Xiu sent the Censor Liu Ji to press Yun, seized his officials and subordinates, and impeached him for resisting an edict, great irreverence and impiety.

entries.zh: 允視詔，乃秀手書也，大怒，收御史，將斬之，御史走免，斬其令史二人。
entries.en: Yun saw the edict was in Xiu's own hand, flew into a rage, seized the censor and nearly executed him; the censor fled, and two clerks were beheaded.
entries.literal: Yun looked at the edict—it was in Xiu's own hand—and grew greatly angry, seized the censor, and was about to behead him; the censor fled and escaped, and two clerks were beheaded.

entries.zh: 厲色謂左右曰：「趙王欲破我家！」
entries.en: He said grimly to his attendants: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"
entries.literal: With stern countenance he said to those at his side: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"

entries.zh: 遂帥國兵及帳下七百人直出，大呼曰：「趙王反，我將討之，從我者左袒。」
entries.en: He led his state troops and seven hundred household guards straight out, shouting: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled! I shall punish him. Follow me and bare your left shoulder."
entries.literal: He thereupon led his state troops and seven hundred men of his personal guard straight out, shouting loudly: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled—I shall punish him; those who follow me, bare your left shoulder."

entries.zh: 於是歸之者甚眾。
entries.en: Many rallied to him.
entries.literal: At this very many came over to him.

entries.zh: 允將赴宮，尚書左丞王輿閉掖門，允不得入，遂圍相府。
entries.en: Yun marched on the palace, but Wang Yu, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, shut the side gate and blocked him; he then besieged the chancellor's residence.
entries.literal: Yun was about to go to the palace; the Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yu closed the side gate, and Yun could not enter; he thereupon besieged the chancellor's mansion.

entries.zh: 允所將兵皆精銳，倫與戰，屢敗，死者千餘人。
entries.en: Yun's troops were elite. Lun fought him repeatedly and lost, with more than a thousand dead.
entries.literal: The troops Yun led were all elite; Lun fought him and was repeatedly defeated, more than a thousand dead.

entries.zh: 太子左率陳徽勒東宮兵，鼓噪於內以應允。
entries.en: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, stirred Eastern Palace troops to cheer within in support of Yun.
entries.literal: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, roused Eastern Palace troops and clamored within in support of Yun.

entries.zh: 允結陳於承華門前，弓弩齊發，射倫，飛矢雨下。
entries.en: Yun formed battle lines before the Chenghua Gate. Bows and crossbows volleyed at Lun until arrows fell like rain.
entries.literal: Yun drew up his array before the Chenghua Gate; bows and crossbows fired together, shooting at Lun—arrows fell like rain.

entries.zh: 主書司馬眭秘以身蔽倫，箭中其背而死。
entries.en: Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body and was killed by an arrow in the back.
entries.literal: The Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body; an arrow struck his back and he died.

entries.zh: 倫官屬皆隱樹而立，每樹輒中數百箭，自辰至未，中書令陳淮，徽之兄也，欲應允，言於帝曰：「宜遣白虎幡以解鬥。」
entries.en: Lun's staff hid behind trees, each tree studded with hundreds of arrows. From chen to wei, Chen Huai, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Hui's elder brother, wished to aid Yun and told the emperor: "Send the white tiger banner to stop the fighting."
entries.literal: Lun's staff all hid behind trees to stand; each tree received hundreds of arrows. From the hour chen to wei, the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Chen Huai—Hui's elder brother—wished to support Yun and said to the emperor: "The white tiger banner should be sent to halt the fighting."

entries.zh: 乃使司馬督護伏胤將騎四百持幡從宮中出。
entries.en: The Major of the Protectorate Fu Yin was sent with four hundred horsemen bearing the banner from the palace.
entries.literal: He then had the Major Fu Yin of the Protectorate lead four hundred horsemen bearing the banner out from within the palace.

entries.zh: 侍中汝陰王虔在門下省，陰與胤誓曰：「富貴當與卿共之。」
entries.en: The Attendant, Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department and secretly swore to Yin: "We shall share wealth and honor."
entries.literal: The Attendant, the Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department; he secretly swore with Yin: "Wealth and honor shall be shared with you."

entries.zh: 胤乃懷空板出，詐言有詔助淮南王。
entries.en: Yin carried out a blank tablet and falsely claimed an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.
entries.literal: Yin then carried a blank tablet out and falsely said there was an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.

entries.zh: 允不之覺，開陣內之，下車受詔；
entries.en: Yun did not detect the fraud and opened his ranks. Yin dismounted to receive the edict;
entries.literal: Yun did not perceive the deception and opened his ranks to admit him; Yin dismounted to receive the edict;

entries.zh: 胤因殺之，並殺允子秦王郁、漢王迪，坐允夷滅者數千人。
entries.en: Yin then killed him, along with Yun's sons Yu, Prince of Qin, and Di, Prince of Han. Several thousand connected with Yun were exterminated.
entries.literal: Yin thereupon killed him, and also killed Yun's sons, the Prince of Qin Yu and the Prince of Han Di; those implicated with Yun and exterminated numbered several thousand.

entries.zh: 曲赦洛陽。
entries.en: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.
entries.literal: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 初，孫秀嘗為小吏，事黃門郎潘岳，岳屢撻之。
entries.en: Earlier Xiu had served as a petty clerk under Pan Yue, Yellow Gate Gentleman, whom he had often flogged.
entries.literal: Earlier Sun Xiu had once been a petty clerk serving the Yellow Gate Gentleman Pan Yue; Yue often flogged him.

entries.zh: 衛尉石崇之甥歐陽建素與相國倫有隙，崇有愛妾曰綠珠，孫秀便求之，崇不與。
entries.en: Ouyang Jian, nephew of Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, was estranged from Lun. Chong had a beloved concubine, Green Pearl, whom Xiu demanded and Chong refused.
entries.literal: Ouyang Jian, nephew of the Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, had long been at odds with Chancellor Lun; Chong had a beloved concubine named Green Pearl whom Sun Xiu asked for, but Chong would not give her.

entries.zh: 及淮南王允敗，秀因稱石崇、潘岳、歐陽建奉允為亂，收之。
entries.en: When Yun fell, Xiu accused Chong, Yue, and Jian of supporting his rebellion and arrested them.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Huainan Yun was defeated, Xiu thereupon claimed that Shi Chong, Pan Yue, and Ouyang Jian supported Yun in rebellion and arrested them.

entries.zh: 崇歎曰：「奴輩利吾財爾！」
entries.en: Chong sighed: "These slaves want my wealth!"
entries.literal: Chong sighed: "These slaves covet my wealth!"

entries.zh: 收者曰：「知財為禍，何不早散之？」
entries.en: The arresters said: "If wealth brings disaster, why not have given it away?"
entries.literal: The arresters said: "Knowing wealth brings disaster, why not have dispersed it early?"

entries.zh: 崇不能答。
entries.en: Chong had no answer.
entries.literal: Chong could not answer.

entries.zh: 初，潘岳母常誚責岳曰：「汝當知足，而乾沒不已乎！」
entries.en: Earlier Yue's mother had often scolded him: "Know when you have enough—why keep grasping for more?"
entries.literal: Earlier Pan Yue's mother often reproached Yue, saying: "You ought to know sufficiency—why seize and scrape without end!"

entries.zh: 及敗，岳謝母曰：「負阿母。」
entries.en: When ruin came Yue told his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."
entries.literal: When disaster came Yue apologized to his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."

entries.zh: 遂與崇，建皆族誅，籍沒崇家。
entries.en: Yue, Chong, and Jian were executed to the clan, and Chong's estate was confiscated.
entries.literal: Thereupon Yue, Chong, and Jian were all executed to the clan, and Chong's property was confiscated.

entries.zh: 相國倫收淮南王母弟吳王晏，欲殺之。
entries.en: Lun arrested Yan, Prince of Wu, younger brother of Yun's mother, intending to kill him.
entries.literal: Chancellor Lun arrested the Prince of Wu Yan, younger brother of the Prince of Huainan's mother, intending to kill him.

entries.zh: 光祿大夫傅祗爭之於朝堂，眾皆諫止倫，倫乃貶晏為賓徒縣王。
entries.en: Household Grandee Fu Zhi argued for him in court; all remonstrated, and Lun degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu.
entries.literal: The Household Grandee Fu Zhi contended for him in the court hall; all remonstrated and stopped Lun, and Lun thereupon degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu county.

entries.zh: 孫秀議加相國倫九錫，百官莫敢異議。
entries.en: Xiu proposed granting Lun the Nine Bestowals; no official dared object.
entries.literal: Sun Xiu proposed granting Chancellor Lun the Nine Bestowals; the hundred officials dared not dissent.

entries.zh: 吏部尚書劉頌曰：「昔漢之錫魏，魏之錫晉，皆一時之用，非可通行。
entries.en: Liu Song, Director of Personnel, said: "When Han bestowed them on Wei and Wei on Jin, those were expedients of the moment, not universal precedent.
entries.literal: Liu Song, Director of Personnel, said: "In the past Han bestowed them on Wei and Wei on Jin—all were expedients of the moment and cannot be made universal practice.

entries.zh: 周勃、霍光，其功至大，皆不聞有九錫之命也。」
entries.en: Zhou Bo and Huo Guang achieved the greatest merit, yet never received the Nine Bestowals."
entries.literal: Zhou Bo and Huo Guang achieved the greatest merit, yet one never hears of commands granting the Nine Bestowals."

entries.zh: 張林積忿不已，以頌為張華之黨，將殺之。
entries.en: Zhang Lin, still furious, treated Song as Zhang Hua's partisan and meant to kill him.
entries.literal: Zhang Lin, nursing his wrath, took Song for a partisan of Zhang Hua and was about to kill him.

entries.zh: 孫秀曰：「殺張、裴已傷時望，不可復殺頌。」
entries.en: Xiu said: "Killing Zhang and Pei has already harmed public esteem. We cannot kill Song too."
entries.literal: Sun Xiu said: "Killing Zhang and Pei has already harmed the age's esteem—we cannot kill Song again."

entries.zh: 林乃止。
entries.en: Lin desisted.
entries.literal: Lin thereupon stopped.

entries.zh: 以頌為光祿大夫。
entries.en: Song was made Household Grandee.
entries.literal: Song was made Household Grandee.

entries.zh: 遂下詔加倫九錫，復加其子荂撫軍將軍，虔中軍將軍，詡為侍中。
entries.en: An edict granted Lun the Nine Bestowals and further made Fu General of the Guards, Qian Central Commander, and Xu Attendant.
entries.literal: An edict was then issued granting Lun the Nine Bestowals; his son Fu was further made General of the Guards, Qian Central Commander of the Army, and Xu Attendant.

entries.zh: 又加孫秀侍中、輔國將軍，相國司馬、右率如故。
entries.en: Xiu was made Attendant and General Who Assists the State, retaining his posts as Chancellor's Major and Colonel of the Right.
entries.literal: Sun Xiu was further made Attendant and General Who Assists the State, retaining his posts as Chancellor's Major and Colonel of the Right.

entries.zh: 張林等並居顯要。
entries.en: Zhang Lin and others all held prominent posts.
entries.literal: Zhang Lin and the rest all held prominent posts.

entries.zh: 增相府兵為二萬人，與宿衛同，並所隱匿之兵，數逾三萬。
entries.en: Chancellor household troops were raised to twenty thousand, equal to the palace guard; with hidden forces the total exceeded thirty thousand.
entries.literal: The chancellor's household troops were increased to twenty thousand, equal to the palace guard, and with hidden troops as well the number exceeded thirty thousand.

entries.zh: 倫及諸子皆頑鄙無識，秀狡黠貪淫，所與共事者，皆邪佞之士，惟競榮利，無深謀遠略，志趣乖異，互相憎嫉。
entries.en: Lun and his sons were dull and vulgar; Xiu was cunning, greedy, and lewd. Their associates were corrupt men who sought only profit, without foresight, mutually hostile.
entries.literal: Lun and his sons were all obtuse and vulgar without understanding; Xiu was cunning, greedy, and licentious; those who worked with them were all depraved men who competed only for glory and profit, without deep plans or far sight, their aims divergent and mutually hateful.

entries.zh: 秀子會為射聲校尉，形貌短陋，如奴僕之下者，秀使尚帝女河東公主。
entries.en: Xiu's son Hui, Colonel of the Archers, was short and ugly as a menial, yet Xiu married him to the Princess of Hedong.
entries.literal: Xiu's son Hui was Colonel of the Archers; short and ugly in form, like one beneath a slave—yet Xiu had him marry the emperor's daughter, the Princess of Hedong.

entries.zh: 齊王冏以功遷游擊將軍，冏意不滿，有恨色。
entries.en: Jiong was promoted to General of the Reserves for his merit but was dissatisfied and showed resentment.
entries.literal: The Prince of Qi Jiong was transferred to General of the Reserves for his merit, but Jiong was dissatisfied and showed resentment.

entries.zh: 孫秀覺之，且憚其在內，乃出為平東將軍，鎮許昌。
entries.en: Xiu noticed and, fearing him in the capital, posted him out as General Who Pacifies the East at Xuchang.
entries.literal: Sun Xiu noticed it and, also fearing him within the capital, sent him out as General Who Pacifies the East, stationed at Xuchang.

entries.zh: 九月，改司徒為丞相，以梁王肜為之，肜固辭不受。
entries.en: In the ninth month the post of Minister over the Masses was renamed Chancellor for Rong, Prince of Liang, who firmly declined.
entries.literal: In the ninth month the Minister over the Masses was renamed Chancellor, with the Prince of Liang Rong to hold it; Rong firmly declined and would not accept.

entries.zh: 冬，十一月，甲子，立皇后羊氏，赦天下。
entries.en: In winter, the eleventh month, on jiazi, Lady Yang was made empress and the realm amnestied.
entries.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day jiazi, Lady Yang was established as empress and the realm was granted amnesty.

entries.zh: 後，尚書郎泰山羊玄之之女也。
entries.en: She was the daughter of Yang Xuanzhi, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing of Taishan.
entries.literal: The empress was the daughter of Yang Xuanzhi, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing of Taishan.

entries.zh: 外祖平南將軍樂安孫旂，與孫秀善，故秀立之。
entries.en: Her maternal grandfather was Sun Qi, General Who Pacifies the South of Le'an, friendly with Xiu, which is why Xiu made her empress.
entries.literal: Her maternal grandfather was Sun Qi, General Who Pacifies the South of Le'an, on good terms with Sun Xiu, and therefore Xiu established her.

entries.zh: 拜玄之光祿大夫、特進、散騎常侍，封興晉侯。
entries.en: Xuanzhi was made Household Grandee, Special Courtier, Gentleman of the Encampment, and Marquis of Xingjin.
entries.literal: Xuanzhi was appointed Household Grandee, Special Courtier, and Gentleman of the Encampment, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingjin.

entries.zh: 廞自稱大都督，大將軍、益州牧，署置僚屬，改易守令。
entries.en: Xin styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, and Governor of Yi, appointed staff, and replaced local officials.
entries.literal: Xin styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, and Governor of Yi Province, appointed staff, and changed the garrison commanders and magistrates.

entries.zh: 王官被召，無敢不往。
entries.en: When court officials were summoned, none dared refuse.
entries.literal: When court officials were summoned none dared not go.

entries.zh: 李庠帥妹婿李含、天水任回、上官昌、扶風李攀、始平費他、氐苻成、隗伯等四千騎歸廞。
entries.en: Li Xiu led Li Han, Ren Hui, Shangguan Chang, Li Pan, Fei Ta, Fu Cheng, Wei Bo, and four thousand horsemen to join Xin.
entries.literal: Li Xiu led his brothers-in-law Li Han of Tianshui, Ren Hui, Shangguan Chang, Li Pan of Fufeng, Fei Ta of Shiping, the Di Fu Cheng, and Wei Bo and others with four thousand horsemen to join Xin.

entries.zh: 廞以庠為威寇將軍，封陽泉亭侯，委以心膂，使招合六郡壯勇至萬餘人，以斷北道。
entries.en: Xin made Xiu General Who Subdues Bandits and Marquis of Yangquan, trusted him deeply, and had him gather more than ten thousand braves of six commanderies to block the northern road.
entries.literal: Xin made Xiu General Who Subdues Bandits and Marquis of Yangquan Pavilion, entrusted him as close confidant, and had him gather braves of the six commanderies to more than ten thousand to cut the northern road.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷
entries.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83

entries.zh: 齊高祖神武皇帝，姓高名歡，字賀六渾，渤海蓚人也。
entries.en: Gaozu Emperor Shenwu of Northern Qi bore the surname Gao; his personal name was Huan and his style Heiliuhun. He came from Tiao in Bohai.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor of Qi, Emperor Shenwu, surname Gao, taboo name Huan, style name Heiliuhun, was a native of Tiao in Bohai.

entries.zh: 六世祖隱，晉玄菟太守。
entries.en: In the sixth generation his ancestor Yin had been Administrator of Xuantu under the Jin.
entries.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Yin served as Administrator of Xuantu under Jin.

entries.zh: 隱生慶，慶生泰，泰生湖，三世仕慕容氏。
entries.en: Yin fathered Qing, Qing fathered Tai, and Tai fathered Hu; all three generations entered the service of the Murong clan.
entries.literal: Yin begot Qing; Qing begot Tai; Tai begot Hu — three generations served the Murong house.

entries.zh: 及慕容寶敗，國亂，湖率衆歸魏，為右將軍。
entries.en: When Murong Bao suffered defeat and the state collapsed into disorder, Hu brought his band over to the Northern Wei and was appointed Right General.
entries.literal: When Murong Bao was defeated and the realm fell into chaos, Hu led his followers to submit to Wei and was made Right General.

entries.zh: 湖生四子，第三子謐，仕魏，位至侍御史，坐法徙居懷朔鎮。
entries.en: Hu had four sons. The third, Mi, served the Wei court and rose to Attending Censor, but after a legal infraction was banished to live at Huaishuo garrison.
entries.literal: Hu had four sons; the third, Mi, served Wei, rose to Attending Censor, and for violating the law was exiled to garrison at Huaishuo.

entries.zh: 謐生皇考樹，性通率，不事家業。
entries.en: Mi fathered Gao Huan's father Shu, a man frank and easy in temperament who cared little for the family trade.
entries.literal: Mi begot the late father Shu, who by nature was frank and unassuming and did not attend to the family occupation.

entries.zh: 住居白道南，數有赤光紫氣之異，鄰人以為怪，勸徙居以避之。
entries.en: He lived south of the White Road, where red light and purple vapors appeared again and again. The neighbors took this for uncanny and urged him to move elsewhere to escape it.
entries.literal: He lived south of the White Road; repeatedly there were portents of red light and purple vapor, and neighbors, deeming it strange, urged him to move away to avoid them.

entries.zh: 皇考曰：「安知非吉？」
entries.en: Gao Huan's father replied, "How do you know it is not a blessing?"
entries.literal: The late father said: "Who is to say it is not auspicious?"

entries.zh: 居之自若。
entries.en: And he stayed on as before, unperturbed.
entries.literal: He remained there as before.

entries.zh: 及神武生而皇妣韓氏殂，養於同產姊婿鎮獄隊尉景家。
entries.en: When Gao Huan was born his mother Lady Han died, and he was reared in the household of his full elder sister's husband Wei Jing, captain of the garrison prison guard.
entries.literal: When Shenwu was born the late mother Lady Han died, and he was raised in the home of his uterine elder sister's husband, Jing, captain of the garrison prison guard.

entries.zh: 神武上
entries.en: Emperor Shenwu, Part One
entries.literal: Emperor Shenwu, Part One

entries.zh: 神武旣累世北邊，故習其俗，遂同鮮卑。
entries.en: For generations his family had lived on the northern marches, so Gao Huan grew up in frontier ways and lived much like the Xianbei.
entries.literal: As for generations his family had been on the northern frontier, Shenwu was accustomed to its customs and came to be as the Xianbei.

entries.zh: 長而深沉有大度，輕財重士，為豪俠所宗。
entries.en: As a man he was reserved and far-sighted, generous with money and devoted to worthy companions, and the local men of daring looked to him as their leader.
entries.literal: When grown he was deep and reserved, possessed of great breadth of mind, lightly regarded wealth and valued men of talent, and was looked to by bold heroes.

entries.zh: 目有精光，長頭高顴，齒白如玉，少有人傑表。
entries.en: His eyes gleamed, his head was long and his cheekbones high, his teeth white as jade; even in youth he wore the bearing of a man marked for greatness.
entries.literal: His eyes had a sharp brilliance; his head was long and cheeks high; his teeth white as jade — in youth he had the countenance of an uncommon man.

entries.zh: 家貧，及聘武明皇后，始有馬，得給鎮為隊主。
entries.en: The family was poor, and only after he betrothed Lady Wuming did he acquire a horse and win appointment as squad chief at the garrison.
entries.literal: His family was poor; only when he betrothed Empress Wuming did he first have a horse and was able to serve the garrison as squad chief.

entries.zh: 鎮將遼西段長常奇神武貌，謂曰：「君有康濟才，終不徒然。」
entries.en: Duan Chang of Liaoxi, the garrison commander, often admired Gao Huan's looks and told him, "You have the talent to heal the realm; you will not end your days obscurely."
entries.literal: Duan Chang of Liaoxi, commander of the garrison, often marveled at Shenwu's appearance and said to him: "You possess talent for bringing order and succor; you will not in the end come to nothing."

entries.zh: 便以子孫為托。
entries.en: And he entrusted his descendants to Gao Huan's care.
entries.literal: He thereupon entrusted him with his descendants.

entries.zh: 及貴，追贈長司空，擢其子寧用之。
entries.en: After Gao Huan rose to power he posthumously honored Duan Chang with the title Minister of Works and brought his son Ning into office.
entries.literal: When Shenwu rose high, he posthumously enfeoffed Chang as Minister of Works and promoted his son Ning to employment.

entries.zh: 神武自隊主轉為函使。
entries.en: Gao Huan moved from squad chief to garrison courier.
entries.literal: Shenwu advanced from squad chief to courier.

entries.zh: 嘗乘驛過建興，雲霧晝晦，雷聲隨之，半日乃絕，若有神應者。
entries.en: Once while riding post through Jianxing, clouds and mist darkened the day and thunder rolled after him for half a day, as though heaven itself were answering his passage.
entries.literal: Once riding post through Jianxing, clouds and mist darkened the day, thunder followed along, and for half a day it did not cease — as if there were a divine response.

entries.zh: 每行道路，往來無風塵之色。
entries.en: Whenever he traveled the roads he seemed untouched by wind and dust.
entries.literal: Whenever he traveled the roads, there was no look of wind and dust about his coming and going.

entries.zh: 又嘗夢履衆星而行，覺而內喜。
entries.en: He also dreamed once that he walked treading upon the stars; when he woke he was secretly elated.
entries.literal: Again he once dreamed of treading among the stars as he walked; waking, he rejoiced inwardly.

entries.zh: 為函使六年，每至洛陽，給令史麻祥使。
entries.en: For six years as courier he went each time to Luoyang, where he was assigned to the clerk Ma Xiang.
entries.literal: For six years as courier, whenever he reached Luoyang he was detailed to the clerk Ma Xiang.

entries.zh: 詳嘗以肉啖神武，神武性不立食，坐而進之。
entries.en: Xiang once fed him meat; Gao Huan, who never ate standing, sat down to accept it.
entries.literal: Xiang once offered meat to Shenwu to eat; Shenwu by nature would not eat standing, and so sat to receive it.

entries.zh: 祥以為慢己，笞神武四十。
entries.en: Xiang took this as an insult and had Gao Huan beaten forty strokes.
entries.literal: Xiang took this as disrespect toward himself and had Shenwu flogged forty strokes.
