entries.zh: 欽請贖之，王不許。
entries.en: Lan Qin asked to ransom him; Gao Cheng refused.
entries.literal: Lan Qin asked to ransom him; the Prince refused.

entries.zh: 京再訴，王使監廚蒼頭薛豐洛杖之，曰：「更訴當殺爾。」
entries.en: Jing appealed again; Gao Cheng had the kitchen-overseer bondman Xue Fengluo beat him and said, "Complain again and you will be killed."
entries.literal: Jing appealed again; the Prince had kitchen-overseer bondman Xue Fengluo beat him and said: "Complain again and you will be killed."

entries.zh: 京與其黨六人謀作亂。
entries.en: Jing and six of his cohort plotted mutiny.
entries.literal: Jing and six of his cohort plotted mutiny.

entries.zh: 時王居北城東柏堂蒞政，以寵琅邪公主，欲其來往無所避忌，所有侍衛，皆出於外。
entries.en: At the time Gao Cheng held court at the East Cypress Hall in the North City; favoring the Princess of Langye, he wished her comings and goings to be without restraint, and had all guards posted outside.
entries.literal: At the time the Prince held court at the East Cypress Hall in the North City; favoring the Princess of Langye, he wished her comings and goings to be without restraint, and had all guards posted outside.

entries.zh: 太史啟言宰輔星甚微，變不出一月。
entries.en: The court astronomer reported that the minister-and-councilor star was very faint and that change would come within a month.
entries.literal: The court astronomer reported that the minister-and-councilor star was very faint; change would come within a month.

entries.zh: 王曰：「小人新杖之，故嚇我耳。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng said, "That wretch was just flogged—he only wants to frighten me."
entries.literal: The Prince said: "That wretch was just flogged—he only wants to frighten me."

entries.zh: 將欲受禪，與陳元康、崔季舒等屏斥左右，署擬百官。
entries.en: About to receive the abdication, he with Chen Yuankang, Cui Jishu, and others dismissed attendants and drafted appointments for the hundred offices.
entries.literal: About to receive the abdication, he with Chen Yuankang, Cui Jishu, and others dismissed attendants and drafted appointments for the hundred offices.

entries.zh: 京將進食，王却，謂諸人曰：「昨夜夢此奴斫我，宜殺却。」
entries.en: When Jing was about to bring food, Gao Cheng held back and told the others, "Last night I dreamed this slave hacked at me—I ought to kill him."
entries.literal: When Jing was about to bring food, the Prince held back and told the others: "Last night I dreamed this slave hacked at me—I ought to kill him."

entries.zh: 京聞之，置刀於盤，冒言進食。
entries.en: Jing heard this, hid a knife in the serving tray, and came forward as if to bring food.
entries.literal: Jing heard this, hid a knife in the serving tray, and came forward as if to bring food.

entries.zh: 王怒曰：「我未索食，爾何據來！」
entries.en: Gao Cheng raged, "I did not ask for food—why do you press in!"
entries.literal: The Prince raged: "I did not ask for food—why do you press in!"

entries.zh: 京揮刀曰：「來將殺汝！」
entries.en: Jing swung the knife and said, "I have come to kill you!"
entries.literal: Jing swung the knife and said: "I have come to kill you!"

entries.zh: 王自投傷足，入于床下。
entries.en: Gao Cheng threw himself aside, wounded in the foot, and crawled under the bed.
entries.literal: The Prince threw himself aside, wounded in the foot, and crawled under the bed.

entries.zh: 賊黨去床，因而見殺。
entries.en: The assassins dragged him from the bed and killed him.
entries.literal: The assassins dragged him from the bed and so he was killed.

entries.zh: 先是訛言曰：「軟脫帽，床底喘」，其言應矣。
entries.en: Before this a rumor ran, "Soft hat off, gasping under the bed"—and the words came true.
entries.literal: Before this a rumor ran: "Soft hat off, gasping under the bed"—and the words came true.

entries.zh: 時太原公洋在城東雙堂，入而討賊，臠割京等，皆漆其頭。
entries.en: At the time Duke of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.
entries.literal: At the time Prince of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.

entries.zh: 秘不發喪，徐出言曰：「奴反，大將軍被傷，無大苦也。」
entries.en: They kept the death secret, then slowly announced, "The slave rebelled; the Grand General was wounded—nothing grave."
entries.literal: They kept the death secret, then slowly announced: "The slave rebelled; the Grand General was wounded—nothing grave."

entries.zh: 武定四年十一月，神武西討，不豫班師，文襄馳赴軍所，侍衛還晉陽。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of Wuding 4 (546), Gao Huan marched west, fell ill, and withdrew; Gao Cheng raced to the army, attended him, and escorted him back to Jinyang.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Wuding, Shenwu campaigned west and, falling ill, withdrew the army; Wenxiang raced to the army's camp, attended him, and escorted him back to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 五年正月丙午，神武崩，秘不發喪。
entries.en: In the first month of Wuding 5 (547), on bingwu day, Gao Huan died; the death was kept secret.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, on bingwu, Shenwu died; the death was kept secret.

entries.zh: 辛亥，司徒侯景據河南反，潁州刺史司馬世雲以城應之。
entries.en: On xinhai day Minister of Works Hou Jing rebelled and held Henan, and Ying Inspector Sima Shiyun opened the city to him.
entries.literal: On xinhai, Minister of Works Hou Jing held Henan in rebellion, and Sima Shiyun, Inspector of Ying Province, opened the city to him.

entries.zh: 景誘執豫州刺史高元成、襄州刺史李密、廣州刺史暴顯等。
entries.en: Hou Jing lured and seized Yuzhou Inspector Gao Yuancheng, Xiangzhou Inspector Li Mi, Guangzhou Inspector Bao Xian, and others.
entries.literal: Jing lured and seized Yuzhou Inspector Gao Yuancheng, Xiangzhou Inspector Li Mi, Guangzhou Inspector Bao Xian, and others.

entries.zh: 遣司空韓軌率衆討之。
entries.en: Gao Cheng sent Minister of Works Han Gui at the head of an army to attack him.
entries.literal: He sent Minister of Works Han Gui at the head of an army to attack him.

entries.zh: 夏四月壬申，文襄朝於鄴。
entries.en: In the fourth month, on renshen day, Gao Cheng attended court at Ye.
entries.literal: In the fourth month, on renshen, Wenxiang attended court at Ye.

entries.zh: 六月己巳，韓軌等自潁州班師。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on jisi day, Han Gui and the others withdrew from Ying Province.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on jisi, Han Gui and the others withdrew the army from Ying Province.

entries.zh: 丁丑，文襄還晉陽，乃發喪，告喻文武，陳神武遺志。
entries.en: On dingchou day Gao Cheng returned to Jinyang, announced the death, informed civil and military officials, and set forth Gao Huan's final wishes.
entries.literal: On dingchou Wenxiang returned to Jinyang, then announced the death, informed civil and military officials, and set forth Shenwu's final wishes.

entries.zh: 七月戊戌，魏帝詔以文襄為使持節、大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事、大行臺、渤海王。
entries.en: In the seventh month, on wuxu day, the Eastern Wei emperor issued an edict that Gao Cheng be Bearer of Credentials, Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies at Home and Abroad, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Prince of Bohai.
entries.literal: In the seventh month, on wuxu, the Wei Emperor issued an edict that Wenxiang be Bearer of Credentials, Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies at Home and Abroad, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Prince of Bohai.

entries.zh: 文襄啟辭位，願停王爵。
entries.en: Gao Cheng memorialized to decline and wished to relinquish the princely rank.
entries.literal: Wenxiang memorialized to decline the post and wished to relinquish the princely rank.

entries.zh: 壬寅，魏帝詔太原公洋攝理軍國，遣中使敦喻。
entries.en: On renyin day the emperor issued an edict that Duke of Taiyuan Gao Yang administer military and state affairs and sent a palace envoy to urge him earnestly.
entries.literal: On renyin the Wei Emperor issued an edict that Duke of Taiyuan Yang administer military and state affairs, and sent a palace envoy to urge him earnestly.

entries.zh: 八月戊辰，文襄啟申神武遺令，請減國邑分封將督，各有差。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on wuchen day, Gao Cheng memorialized to carry out Gao Huan's final command, asking to reduce the royal fief and enfeoff generals and commanders, each according to rank.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on wuchen, Wenxiang memorialized to carry out Shenwu's final command, asking to reduce the fiefs of the realm and enfeoff generals and commanders, each according to rank.

entries.zh: 辛未，朝鄴，固辭丞相。
entries.en: On xinwei day he attended court at Ye and firmly declined the chancellorship.
entries.literal: On xinwei he attended court at Ye and firmly declined the chancellorship.

entries.zh: 魏帝詔曰：「旣朝野攸憑，安危所系，不得令遂本懷，須有權奪，可復前大將軍，餘如故。」
entries.en: The emperor issued an edict, "Since court and countryside rely on you and safety hangs upon you, I cannot let you follow your wish; authority must be taken by necessity. You may resume your former rank of Grand General; the rest remains as before."
entries.literal: The Wei Emperor issued an edict: "Since court and countryside rely on you and safety hangs upon you, I cannot let you follow your original wish; there must be a taking of authority by necessity. You may resume your former rank of Grand General; the rest remains as before."

entries.zh: 天平元年，加使持節、尚書令、大行臺、幷州刺史。
entries.en: In Tianping 1 (534) he received Bearer of Credentials, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and the inspectorship of Bing Province.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianping he was given Bearer of Credentials, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Inspector of Bing Province.

entries.zh: 三年，入輔朝政，加領左右、京畿大都督。
entries.en: In the third year he entered the capital to assist in governance and was given charge of the Left and Right and made Grand Commander of the Capital Region.
entries.literal: In the third year he entered to assist court governance and was given charge of the Left and Right and Grand Commander of the Capital Region.

entries.zh: 時人雖聞器識，猶以少年期之，而機略嚴明，事無凝滯，於是朝野振肅。
entries.en: Though men had heard of his talent, they still treated him as a youth; yet his plans were strict and clear, nothing hung fire, and court and countryside alike were stirred to order.
entries.literal: Though people had heard of his talent and judgment, they still looked on him as a youth; yet his strategy was strict and clear, affairs never stalled, and court and countryside were stirred to solemn order.

entries.zh: 元象元年，攝吏部尚書。
entries.en: In Yuanxiang 1 (538) he served as acting Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang he acted as Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 魏自崔亮以後。
entries.en: In Northern Wei, since the time of Cui Liang,
entries.literal: In Wei, since Cui Liang's time.

entries.zh: 選人常以年勞為制，文襄乃釐改前式，銓擢唯在得人。
entries.en: appointments had been governed by seniority; Gao Cheng reformed the old practice so that selection rested only on finding the right men.
entries.literal: appointments had been governed by years of service; Wenxiang then reformed the former practice, and selection and promotion rested only on getting the right men.

entries.zh: 又沙汰尚書郎，妙選人地以充之。
entries.en: He also sifted the clerks of the Masters of Writing and chose men of talent and standing to fill the posts.
entries.literal: He also sifted the clerks of the Masters of Writing and finely chose men of talent and standing to fill the posts.

entries.zh: 至于才名之士，咸被薦擢，假有未居顯位者，皆致之門下，以為賓客，每山園游燕，必見招攜，執射賦詩，各盡其所長，以為娛適。
entries.en: Men of talent and reputation he recommended and promoted; those not yet in high office he took into his household as retainers. Whenever he toured gardens and hills he summoned them; they shot arrows, composed verse, and each showed his gift — all for pleasure.
entries.literal: As for men of talent and name, all were recommended and promoted; even those not yet in high office he brought into his household as retainers. Whenever he toured gardens and hills he always summoned them; they shot arrows, composed verse, and each displayed his strength — all for pleasure.

entries.zh: 興和二年，加大將軍，領中書監，仍攝吏部尚書。
entries.en: In Xinghe 2 (540) he was made Grand General and Director of the Secretariat Supervisor while still serving as acting Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xinghe he was given Grand General, Director of the Secretariat Supervisor, and still acted as Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 自正光已後，天下多事，在任羣官，廉潔者寡。
entries.en: Since the Zhenguang era the realm had been in turmoil, and among officials in office few were honest.
entries.literal: From after Zhenguang the realm had been in turmoil, and among officials in office few were honest.

entries.zh: 文襄乃奏吏部郎崔暹為御史中尉，糾劾權豪，無所縱捨，於是風俗更始，私枉路絕。
entries.en: Gao Cheng then had Cui Xian of the Ministry of Personnel appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful without sparing any, custom was renewed, and private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.
entries.literal: Wenxiang then memorialized to make Cui Xuan of the Ministry of Personnel Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful and wealthy without sparing any, and custom was renewed — private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.

entries.zh: 乃牓於街衢，具論經國政術，仍開直言之路，有論事上書苦言切至者，皆優容之。
entries.en: He posted notices in the streets setting forth the arts of governing the state and opened a path for blunt speech; those who submitted memorials or letters with bitter and penetrating words he all received with favor.
entries.literal: He posted notices in the streets setting forth the arts of governing the state, and opened a path for blunt speech; those who submitted memorials or letters with bitter and penetrating words he all received with favor.

entries.zh: 議者咸云侯景猶有北望之心，但信命不至耳。
entries.en: Those who debated the matter all said Hou Jing still looked northward, but only the command had not reached him.
entries.literal: Discussants all said Hou Jing still had a mind to look north, but only the command had not reached him.

entries.zh: 又景將蔡遵道北歸，稱景有悔過之心。
entries.en: Again Hou Jing's officer Cai Zundao returned north and said Hou Jing wished to repent.
entries.literal: Again Jing's officer Cai Zundao returned north and said Jing had a mind to repent.

entries.zh: 王以為信然，謂可誘而致，乃遺景書曰：
entries.en: Gao Cheng believed it and thought he could be lured back; he sent Hou Jing a letter saying,
entries.literal: The Prince believed it true and thought he could be lured back; he sent Jing a letter saying:

entries.zh: 先王與司徒契闊夷險，孤子相依，偏所眷屬，義貫終始，情存歲寒。
entries.en: The late king and the Minister of Works shared hardship through peril and isolation; I, his orphan, depended on you—you were his special charge. Righteousness ran from first to last; affection endured through the cold years.
entries.literal: The late king and the Minister of Works shared hardship through peril and isolation; I, his orphan, depended on you — you were his special charge. Righteousness ran from first to last; affection endured through the cold years.

entries.zh: 待為國士者乃立漆身之節，饋以一餐者便致扶輪之效，況其重於此乎？
entries.en: Those treated as men of the state would lay down their lives; one who was fed a single meal would repay with the deed of bracing the wheel—how much more when the bond was weightier than this?
entries.literal: Those treated as men of the state would lay down their lives; one who was fed a single meal would repay with the deed of bracing the wheel — how much more when the bond was weightier than this?

entries.zh: 常以故舊之義，欲將子孫相托，方為秦晉之匹，共成劉、范之親。
entries.en: By the old friendship I ever meant to entrust my descendants to you and make a match like Qin and Jin, forming a kinship like Liu and Fan.
entries.literal: By the old friendship I ever meant to entrust my descendants to you and make a match like Qin and Jin, forming a kinship like Liu and Fan.

entries.zh: 況聞負杖行歌，便以狼顧反噬，不蹈忠臣之路，便陷叛人之地。
entries.en: Yet I hear that leaning on your staff and singing in the lanes, you turned like a wolf to bite in return, forsook the path of the loyal minister, and fell into the land of the rebel.
entries.literal: Yet I hear that leaning on your staff and singing in the lanes, you turned like a wolf to bite in return, forsook the path of the loyal minister, and fell into the land of the rebel.

entries.zh: 力不足以自強，勢不足以自保，率烏合之衆，為累卵之危。
entries.en: Your strength is not enough to strengthen yourself; your power is not enough to protect yourself; you lead a rabble host and stand in peril like a pile of eggs.
entries.literal: Your strength is not enough to strengthen yourself; your power is not enough to protect yourself; you lead a rabble host and stand in peril like a pile of eggs.

entries.zh: 西取救於宇文，南請援於蕭氏，以狐疑之心，為首鼠之事。
entries.en: West you seek rescue from Yuwen; south you ask aid from the Xiao house—with a doubting heart you do the deed of a wavering rat.
entries.literal: West you seek rescue from Yuwen; south you ask aid from the Xiao house — with a doubting heart you do the deed of a wavering rat.

entries.zh: 入秦則秦人不容，歸吳則吳人不信。
entries.en: Enter Qin and the men of Qin will not receive you; return to Wu and the men of Wu will not trust you.
entries.literal: Enter Qin and the men of Qin will not receive you; return to Wu and the men of Wu will not trust you.

entries.zh: 當是不逞之人，曲為無端之說，遂懷市虎之疑，乃致投杼之惑。
entries.en: Surely it was men of disorder who twisted groundless words, so that you harbored the suspicion of the tiger in the market and fell into the confusion of the thrown shuttle.
entries.literal: Surely it was men of disorder who twisted groundless words, so that you harbored the suspicion of the tiger in the market and fell into the confusion of the thrown shuttle.

entries.zh: 比來舉止，事已可見，人相疑誤，想自覺知。
entries.en: Your conduct of late is already plain to see; men suspect and err, and I think you know it yourself.
entries.literal: Your conduct of late is already plain to see; men suspect and err, and I think you know it yourself.

entries.zh: 闔門大小，悉在司寇，意謂李氏未滅，猶言少卿可反。
entries.en: Your whole household, great and small, is in the hands of the Minister of Justice; I thought that since the Li clan was not yet destroyed, one might still say the Lesser Minister could return.
entries.literal: Your whole household, great and small, is in the hands of the Minister of Justice; I thought that since the Li clan was not yet destroyed, one might still say the Lesser Minister could return.

entries.zh: 孤子無狀招禍，丁天酷罰，但禮由權奪，志在忘私，聊遣偏裨，前驅致討，南兗、揚州，應時剋復。
entries.en: I, the orphan, unworthy, have drawn calamity; heaven has dealt a cruel punishment—yet ritual allows taking authority by necessity, and my aim is to forget private feeling. I have sent only a partial force as vanguard to attack; southern Yanzhou and Yangzhou were recovered at once.
entries.literal: I, the orphan, unworthy, have drawn calamity; heaven has dealt a cruel punishment — yet ritual allows taking authority by necessity, and my aim is to forget private feeling. I have sent only a partial force as vanguard to attack; southern Yanzhou and Yangzhou were recovered at once.

entries.zh: 即欲乘機，席捲縣瓠，屬以炎暑，欲為後圖，且令還師，待時更舉。
entries.en: I meant to seize the moment and sweep up Xiangcheng, but because of the heat I planned for later and for now ordered withdrawal, to strike again when the time comes.
entries.literal: I meant to seize the moment, sweep up Xiangcheng, but because of the heat I planned for later and for now ordered withdrawal, to strike again when the time comes.

entries.zh: 今寒膠向折，白露將團，方憑國靈，龔行天罰。
entries.en: Now the cold glue is about to break and white dew will soon gather; relying on the state's numen, I march to execute heaven's punishment.
entries.literal: Now the cold glue is about to break and white dew will soon gather; relying on the state's numen, I march to execute heaven's punishment.

entries.zh: 器械精新，士馬強盛，內外感恩，上下戮力，三令五申，可赴湯火。
entries.en: Weapons are sharp and new, soldiers and horses strong; within and without men are grateful, above and below strive together; thrice and five times commanded, they would walk into boiling water.
entries.literal: Weapons are sharp and new, soldiers and horses strong; within and without men are grateful, above and below strive together; thrice and five times commanded, they would walk into boiling water.

entries.zh: 使旗鼓相望，埃塵相接，勢如沃雪，事等注熒。
entries.en: Banners and drums face each other, dust and smoke meet; the force is like pouring water on snow, the affair like pouring oil on flame.
entries.literal: Banners and drums face each other, dust and smoke meet; the force is like pouring water on snow, the affair like pouring oil on flame.

entries.zh: 夫明者去危就安，智者轉禍為福，甯人負我，不我負人，當開從善之途，使有改迷之路。
entries.en: The clear-sighted leave peril for safety; the wise turn calamity into blessing. Better that others wrong me than that I wrong others—open the path of accepting good, and give a road for correcting error.
entries.literal: The clear-sighted leave peril for safety; the wise turn calamity into blessing. Better that others wrong me than that I wrong others — open the path of accepting good, and give a road for correcting error.

entries.zh: 若能卷甲來朝，垂橐還闕者，即當授豫州，必使終君身世。
entries.en: If you can roll up your armor and come to court, empty your bags and return to the capital, I will at once grant you Yuzhou and see that you hold it for life.
entries.literal: If you can roll up your armor and come to court, empty your bags and return to the capital, I will at once grant you Yuzhou and see that you hold it for life.

entries.zh: 所部文武更不追攝，進得保其祿位，退則不喪功名。
entries.en: Your civil and military subordinates will not be pursued; advance and you keep rank and salary, retreat and you lose neither merit nor fame.
entries.literal: Your civil and military subordinates will not be pursued; advance and you keep rank and salary, retreat and you lose neither merit nor fame.

entries.zh: 今王思政等皆孤軍偏將，遠來深入，然其性命在君掌握，脫能刺之，想有餘力。
entries.en: Now Wang Sizheng and the rest are isolated generals who came from afar and marched deep; yet their lives are in your hand—if you can stab them, I think you still have strength enough.
entries.literal: Now Wang Sizheng and the rest are isolated generals who came from afar and marched deep; yet their lives are in your hand — if you can stab them, I think you still have strength enough.

entries.zh: 節相加授，永保疆埸。
entries.en: I will add the seal of minister and forever secure the frontier.
entries.literal: I will add the seal of minister and forever secure the frontier.

entries.zh: 君門眷屬，可以無患，寵妻愛子，亦送相還，仍為通家，共成親好。
entries.en: Your household kin need not fear; your cherished wife and beloved sons I will also send back—we shall again be allied houses and form a close bond.
entries.literal: Your household kin need not fear; your cherished wife and beloved sons I will also send back — we shall again be allied houses and form a close bond.

entries.zh: 君今不能東封函谷，南面稱孤，受制於人，威名頓盡。
entries.en: If you cannot now seal Hangu Pass in the east and call yourself king facing south, but must be controlled by others, your renown will at once be spent.
entries.literal: If you cannot now seal Hangu Pass in the east and call yourself king facing south, but must be controlled by others, your renown will at once be spent.

entries.zh: 得地不欲自守，聚衆不以為強，空使身有背叛之名，家有惡逆之禍，覆宗絕嗣，自貽伊戚。
entries.en: You gain land yet will not hold it yourself; you gather a host yet do not count it strong—in vain you bear the name of rebel and your house the calamity of treason; clan extinguished, line cut off, you bring sorrow on yourself.
entries.literal: You gain land yet will not hold it yourself; you gather a host yet do not count it strong — in vain you bear the name of rebel and your house the calamity of treason; clan extinguished, line cut off, you bring sorrow on yourself.

entries.zh: 戴天履地，能無愧乎！
entries.en: Wearing heaven on your head and treading earth underfoot—can you be without shame!
entries.literal: Wearing heaven on your head and treading earth underfoot — can you be without shame!

entries.zh: 孤子今日不應遣此，但見蔡遵道云：「司徒本無西歸之心，深有悔過之意」，未知此語為虛為實。
entries.en: I, the orphan, ought not to send this today, but I saw Cai Zundao say, "The Minister of Works originally had no mind to go west and deeply wished to repent"—I do not know whether these words are empty or real.
entries.literal: I, the orphan, ought not to send this today, but I saw Cai Zundao say: "The Minister of Works originally had no mind to go west and deeply wished to repent" — I do not know whether these words are empty or real.

entries.zh: 吉凶之理，想自圖之。
entries.en: The logic of fortune and calamity—I think you will weigh it yourself.
entries.literal: The logic of fortune and calamity — I think you will weigh it yourself.

entries.zh: 論曰：文襄嗣膺霸道，威略昭著。
entries.en: The appraisal says: Wenxiang inherited the hegemonic enterprise, and his power and strategy were unmistakable.
entries.literal: The appraisal says: Wenxiang succeeded to the hegemonic enterprise, and his martial strategy was plainly displayed.

entries.zh: 內除奸逆，外拓淮夷，擯斥貪殘，存情人物。
entries.en: At home he eliminated treacherous rebels; abroad he pushed back the Huai peoples. He drove out the greedy and cruel, and showed concern for capable men.
entries.literal: Within he removed traitors and rebels; without he expanded against the Huai barbarians; he cast out the greedy and cruel, and kept concern for men of worth.

entries.zh: 而志在峻法，急於禦下，於前王之德，有所未同。
entries.en: Yet he set his mind on harsh law and was impatient in ruling those below him; in this he fell short of the former king's virtue.
entries.literal: Yet his intent lay in severe laws and he was harsh in governing subordinates; in the virtue of the former king, there was something with which he did not accord.

entries.zh: 蓋天意人心，好生惡殺，雖吉凶報應，未皆影響。
entries.en: Heaven's will and human feeling cherish life and abhor killing. Although fortune and disaster answer conduct, they do not always follow as swiftly as echo and shadow.
entries.literal: For Heaven's intent and human feeling love life and hate killing; although good and ill fortune answer deeds, they do not always follow like echo and shadow.

entries.zh: 總而論之，積善多慶。
entries.en: In sum, accumulated goodness brings abundant blessing.
entries.literal: To sum it up, accumulated goodness brings many blessings.

entries.zh: 然文襄之禍生所忽，蓋有由焉。
entries.en: Yet Wenxiang's disaster grew out of what he neglected; it had its cause.
entries.literal: Yet Wenxiang's disaster arose from what he neglected; there was surely a cause for it.

entries.zh: 王尋覽書，問誰為作。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng had read the letter, he asked who had written it.
entries.literal: When the Prince had read the letter, he asked who had written it.

entries.zh: 或曰：「其行臺郎王偉。」
entries.en: Someone said, "It was his mobile-court gentleman Wang Wei."
entries.literal: Someone said: "It was his Mobile Court Gentleman Wang Wei."

entries.zh: 王曰：「偉才如此，何因不使我知？」
entries.en: Gao Cheng said, "With talent like this, why was I not told?"
entries.literal: The Prince said: "With talent like this, why was I not told?"

entries.zh: 王欲間景於梁，又與景書而謬其辭，云本使景陽叛，欲與圖西，西人知之，故景更與圖南為事。
entries.en: Gao Cheng wished to drive a wedge between Hou Jing and Liang, and wrote to Jing with falsified wording, saying he had originally sent Jing to stir rebellion at Jingyang and meant to plot the west together; when Western Wei learned of it, Jing turned instead to plotting with the south.
entries.literal: The Prince wished to drive a wedge between Jing and Liang, and wrote to Jing with falsified wording, saying he had originally had Jing stir rebellion at Jingyang and planned with him to strike west; when Western Wei learned this, Jing turned instead to scheming with the south.

entries.zh: 漏其書於梁，梁人亦不之信。
entries.en: He leaked the letter to Liang, but the Liang court did not believe it either.
entries.literal: He leaked the letter to Liang, but the Liang people also did not believe it.

entries.zh: 三月辛亥，王南臨黎陽，濟於虎牢，自洛陽從太行而反晉陽。
entries.en: On xinhai of the third month Gao Cheng went south to Liyang, crossed at Hulao, and returned to Jinyang from Luoyang by way of the Taihang.
entries.literal: On xinhai of the third month, the Prince went south to Liyang, crossed at Hulao, and returned to Jinyang by way of Taihang from Luoyang.

entries.zh: 於路遺書百僚，以相戒勵。
entries.en: On the road he left letters to the hundred officials, admonishing and encouraging them.
entries.literal: On the road he left letters to the hundred officials as mutual admonition and encouragement.

entries.zh: 朝野承風，莫不震肅。
entries.en: Court and countryside caught the wind of it; none failed to be shaken into awe.
entries.literal: Court and countryside caught the wind of it; none failed to be shaken into awe.

entries.zh: 又令朝臣牧宰各舉賢良及驍武膽略堪守邊城，務得其才，不拘職業。
entries.en: He also ordered court ministers and district governors each to recommend the worthy and the brave with the boldness and strategy to hold border towns, seeking talent alone and not binding themselves to rank or trade.
entries.literal: He also ordered court ministers and district governors each to recommend the worthy and brave with the boldness and strategy to hold border towns, seeking only talent regardless of occupation.

entries.zh: 六月，王巡北邊城戍，賑賜有差。
entries.en: In the sixth month Gao Cheng toured the northern border forts and gave relief in varying measure.
entries.literal: In the sixth month the Prince toured northern border forts and gave relief in varying measure.

entries.zh: 僕鄉曲布衣，本乖藝用，出身為國，綿曆二紀，犯危履難，豈避風霜，遂得富貴當年，榮華身世。
entries.en: I, a humble man of the village lanes, by nature unfit for arts and use, entered service for the state and have passed two decades, braving peril and treading hardship without shunning wind and frost—thus I gained wealth in those years and glory in this life.
entries.literal: I, a humble man of the village lanes, by nature unfit for arts and use, entered service for the state and have passed two decades, braving peril and treading hardship without shunning wind and frost — thus I gained wealth in those years and glory in this life.

entries.zh: 一旦舉旗掞，援鼓枹，北面相抗者何哉？
entries.en: Why did I once raise the banner and beat the drum and face north in resistance?
entries.literal: Why did I once raise the banner and beat the drum and face north in resistance?

entries.zh: 寔以畏懼危亡，恐招禍害故耳。
entries.en: Truly because I feared peril and death and dreaded drawing calamity.
entries.literal: Truly because I feared peril and death and dreaded drawing calamity.

entries.zh: 往年之暮，尊王遘疾，神不祐善，祈禱莫瘳。
entries.en: In the late months of the year before, the honored king fell ill; the spirits did not bless the good, and prayers brought no cure.
entries.literal: In the late months of the year before, the honored king fell ill; the spirits did not bless the good, and prayers brought no cure.

entries.zh: 遂使嬖幸弄權，心腹離貳，妻子在宅，無事見圍。
entries.en: Thus favorites played with power, trusted hearts were divided, and though wife and children were at home they were besieged without cause.
entries.literal: Thus favorites played with power, trusted hearts were divided, and though wife and children were at home they were besieged without cause.

entries.zh: 及廻歸長社，希自陳狀，簡書未遣，斧鉞已臨。
entries.en: When I returned to Changshe and hoped to state my case, the summons had not yet been sent and the axe was already at hand.
entries.literal: When I returned to Changshe and hoped to state my case, the summons had not yet been sent and the axe was already at hand.

entries.zh: 旣旌旗相對，咫尺不遠，飛書每奏，冀申鄙情。
entries.en: Though banners faced each other and we were not a bowshot apart, I sent letters again and again, hoping to make my humble feeling plain.
entries.literal: Though banners faced each other and we were not a bowshot apart, I sent letters again and again, hoping to make my humble feeling plain.

entries.zh: 而群帥恃雄，眇然弗顧，連戰推鋒，專欲屠滅。
entries.en: Yet the commanders relied on their strength and looked down on me; battle followed battle, thrust on thrust, and they sought only to slaughter and destroy.
entries.literal: Yet the commanders relied on their strength and looked down on me; battle followed battle, thrust on thrust, and they sought only to slaughter and destroy.

entries.zh: 掘圍堰水，僅存三版，舉目相看，命縣漏刻。
entries.en: They dug ditches and dammed water until only three boards of wall remained; we looked at each other, lives hanging by the dripping clepsydra.
entries.literal: They dug ditches and dammed water until only three boards of wall remained; we looked at each other, lives hanging by the dripping clepsydra.

entries.zh: 不忍死亡，出戰城下，拘秦送地，豈樂為之？
entries.en: Unable to bear death, I went out to fight below the wall and was seized and sent to Qin—would I do that for pleasure?
entries.literal: Unable to bear death, I went out to fight below the wall and was seized and sent to Qin — would I do that for pleasure?

entries.zh: 禽獸惡死，人倫好生，僕實不辜，桓、莊何罪。
entries.en: Beasts hate death; human relations love life—I am truly guiltless; what crime had Huan and Zhuang?
entries.literal: Beasts hate death; human relations love life — I am truly guiltless; what crime had Huan and Zhuang?

entries.zh: 且尊王平昔見與比肩，戮力同心，共獎帝室，雖復權勢參差，寒暑小異，丞相司徒，雁行而已。
entries.en: Moreover the honored king in former days treated me as an equal; we strove together with one heart and jointly upheld the imperial house—though power was unequal and cold and heat differed slightly, Chancellor and Minister of Works were only like geese in flight.
entries.literal: Moreover the honored king in former days treated me as an equal; we strove together with one heart and jointly upheld the imperial house — though power was unequal and cold and heat differed slightly, Chancellor and Minister of Works were only like geese in flight.

entries.zh: 福祿官榮，自是天爵，勞而後授，理不相干，欲求吞炭，何其謬也！
entries.en: Fortune, salary, office, and glory are heaven's rank; granted after labor—reason does not connect with seeking to swallow charcoal; how absurd!
entries.literal: Fortune, salary, office, and glory are heaven's rank; granted after labor — reason does not connect with seeking to swallow charcoal; how absurd!

entries.zh: 然竊人之財，猶謂之盜。
entries.en: Yet to steal another's goods is still called theft.
entries.literal: Yet to steal another's goods is still called theft.

entries.zh: 祿去公室，抑謂不取。
entries.en: Salary taken from the public house—can one say it was not taken?
entries.literal: Salary taken from the public house — can one say it was not taken?

entries.zh: 今魏德雖衰，天命未改，拜恩私第，何足關言。
entries.en: Now Wei's virtue though declined, heaven's mandate is not yet changed; to receive favor in a private residence—what need to speak of it?
entries.literal: Now Wei's virtue though declined, heaven's mandate is not yet changed; to receive favor in a private residence — what need to speak of it?

entries.zh: 景報書曰：
entries.en: Hou Jing replied in a letter:
entries.literal: Jing replied in a letter:

entries.zh: 賜嗤不能東封函谷，受制於人，當似教僕賢祭仲而褒季氏。
entries.en: You mock me for being unable to seal Hangu Pass in the east and for being controlled by others—it is as if you praised Jizhong and commended the Ji clan.
entries.literal: You mock me for being unable to seal Hangu Pass in the east and for being controlled by others — it is as if you praised Jizhong and commended the Ji clan.

entries.zh: 無主之國，在禮未聞，動而不法，將何以訓？
entries.en: A realm without a lord—in ritual I have not heard of it; to act without law—with what will you instruct?
entries.literal: A realm without a lord — in ritual I have not heard of it; to act without law — with what will you instruct?

entries.zh: 竊以分財養幼，事歸令終，舍宅存孤，誰雲隙末？
entries.en: I hold that dividing wealth to nurture the young is a matter of proper ending; leaving a house to preserve the orphan—who would call that a petty grudge?
entries.literal: I hold that dividing wealth to nurture the young is a matter of proper ending; leaving a house to preserve the orphan — who would call that a petty grudge?

entries.zh: 復言僕衆不足以自強，身危如累卵。
entries.en: Again you say my host is not enough to strengthen myself and my person is in peril like a pile of eggs.
entries.literal: Again you say my host is not enough to strengthen myself and my person is in peril like a pile of eggs.

entries.zh: 然億兆夷人，卒降十亂，紂之百克，終自無後，潁川之戰，即是殷監。
entries.en: Yet when the hundred millions of the Yi people submitted, Zhou's ten capable ministers prevailed; King Zhou's hundred victories in the end left him without heirs—the battle at Yingchuan is the warning of Yin.
entries.literal: Yet when the hundred millions of the Yi people submitted, the ten rebels of Zhou fell; Zhou's hundred victories in the end left him without heirs — the battle at Yingchuan is the warning of Yin.

entries.zh: 輕重由人，非鼎在德，苟能忠信，雖弱必強，殷憂啟聖，處危何苦。
entries.en: Weight and light depend on the man, not the tripod on virtue; if one can be loyal and faithful, though weak one must become strong; deep sorrow opens the sage, and dwelling in peril—what hardship is there?
entries.literal: Weight and light depend on the man, not the tripod on virtue; if one can be loyal and faithful, though weak one must become strong; deep sorrow opens the sage, and dwelling in peril — what hardship is there?

entries.zh: 況今梁道邕熙，招攜以禮，被我虎文，縻之好爵，方欲苑五岳而池四海，掃氛穢以拯黎元。
entries.en: Moreover now Liang's way is harmonious and bright; it gathers men by ritual, covers them with tiger-pattern robes, and ties them with noble ranks—it intends to park the five peaks as a garden and pool the four seas, sweep foul vapors and save the black-haired people.
entries.literal: Moreover now Liang's way is harmonious and bright; it gathers men by ritual, covers them with tiger-pattern robes, and ties them with noble ranks — it intends to park the five peaks as a garden and pool the four seas, sweep foul vapors and save the black-haired people.

entries.zh: 東羈甌越，西道汧隴，吳越悍勁，帶甲千羣，秦兵冀馬，控弦十萬，大風一振，枯幹必摧，凝霜暫落，秋帶自殞，此而為弱，誰足稱雄？
entries.en: East it bridles Ou and Yue; west it opens the road to Qian and Long; Wu and Yue are fierce and strong, girded with armor in thousands; Qin troops and Ji horses, bows drawn in tens of thousands—one blast of great wind and dry trunks must break; frost gathers for a moment and autumn girdles fall of themselves—if this is called weak, who is fit to be called strong?
entries.literal: East it bridles Ou and Yue; west it opens the road to Qian and Long; Wu and Yue are fierce and strong, girded with armor in thousands; Qin troops and Ji horses, bows drawn in tens of thousands — one blast of great wind and dry trunks must break; frost gathers for a moment and autumn girdles fall of themselves — if this is called weak, who is fit to be called strong?

entries.zh: 又見誣兩端，受疑二國，斟酌物情，一何太甚！
entries.en: Again I see slander of wavering between two sides and suspicion from two states—weighing human feeling, how excessively!
entries.literal: Again I see slander of wavering between two sides and suspicion from two states — weighing human feeling, how excessively!

entries.zh: 昔陳平背楚，歸漢則強，百里出虞，入秦斯霸。
entries.en: Formerly Chen Ping turned from Chu; returning to Han he became strong. Baili left Yu; entering Qin he became hegemon.
entries.literal: Formerly Chen Ping turned from Chu; returning to Han he became strong. Baili left Yu; entering Qin he became hegemon.

entries.zh: 蓋昏明由主，用舍在人，奉禮而行，神其吐邪！
entries.en: Dark and bright depend on the lord; use and discard depend on the man—follow ritual in action, and the spirits will reject evil!
entries.literal: Dark and bright depend on the lord; use and discard depend on the man — follow ritual in action, and the spirits will reject evil!

entries.zh: 書稱士馬精新，剋日齊舉，誇張形勢，必欲相滅。
entries.en: Your letter speaks of sharp soldiers and horses and fixing a day for joint advance, exaggerating the situation and surely wishing mutual destruction.
entries.literal: Your letter speaks of sharp soldiers and horses and fixing a day for joint advance, exaggerating the situation and surely wishing mutual destruction.

entries.zh: 切以寒膠白露，節候乃同，秋風揚塵，馬首何異。
entries.en: Truly cold glue and white dew—the season is the same; wind raises dust and the horses' heads—what difference is there?
entries.literal: Truly cold glue and white dew — the season is the same; wind raises dust and the horses' heads — what difference is there?

entries.zh: 徒知北方之力爭，未識西南之合從，苟欲狥意於前途，不覺坑穽在其側。
entries.en: You know only the north's struggle for strength and do not see the southwest's alliance—if you wish to follow your whim on the road ahead, you do not notice the pitfall at your side.
entries.literal: You know only the north's struggle for strength and do not see the southwest's alliance — if you wish to follow your whim on the road ahead, you do not notice the pitfall at your side.

entries.zh: 去危就安，今歸正朔；
entries.en: Leave peril for safety—now return to the orthodox calendar;
entries.literal: Leave peril for safety — now return to the orthodox calendar;

entries.zh: 轉禍為福，已脫網羅。
entries.en: turn calamity into blessing—already escaped the net.
entries.literal: turn calamity into blessing — already escaped the net.

entries.zh: 彼當嗤僕之過迷，此亦笑君之晦昧。
entries.en: They will mock my past confusion; this too laughs at your obscurity.
entries.literal: They will mock my past confusion; this too laughs at your obscurity.

entries.zh: 今引二邦，揚旌北討，熊虎齊奮，克復中原，荊、襄、廣、潁，已屬關右，項城、縣瓠，亦奉江南，幸自取之，何勞見援。
entries.en: Now I lead two states, raise banners and march north to attack; bears and tigers strive together, recover the central plains—Jing, Xiang, Guang, and Ying already belong to the Guanxi; Xiangcheng and Xianhu already submit to the Jiangnan—take them yourself; what need to ask aid?
entries.literal: Now I lead two states, raise banners and march north to attack; bears and tigers strive together, recover the central plains — Jing, Xiang, Guang, and Ying already belong to the Guanxi; Xiangcheng and Xianhu already submit to the Jiangnan — take them yourself; what need to ask aid?

entries.zh: 然權變非一，理有萬途，為君計者，莫若割地兩和，三分鼎峙，燕、衛、趙、晉，足相俸祿，齊、曹、宋、魯，悉歸大樑。
entries.en: Yet expedients are not one; reason has ten thousand paths. For your plan, nothing surpasses ceding land and making peace in two parts, three shares standing like the tripod—Yan, Wei, Zhao, and Jin enough for salary; Qi, Cao, Song, and Lu all return to Great Liang.
entries.literal: Yet expedients are not one; reason has ten thousand paths. For your plan, nothing surpasses ceding land and making peace in two parts, three shares standing like the tripod — Yan, Wei, Zhao, and Jin enough for salary; Qi, Cao, Song, and Lu all return to Great Liang.

entries.zh: 使僕得輸力南朝，北敦姻好，束帛自行，戎車不駕，僕立當世之功，君卒父禰之業，各保疆壘，聽享歲時，百姓乂寧，四人安堵。
entries.en: Let me lend strength to the southern court, north I honor kinship by marriage; silks go of themselves, war chariots need not be driven—I stand and achieve merit for the age, you finish your fathers' and grandfathers' enterprise; each keeps his frontier, each enjoys the seasons; the hundred surnames are at peace, the four classes dwell secure.
entries.literal: Let me lend strength to the southern court, north I honor kinship by marriage; silks go of themselves, war chariots need not be driven — I stand and achieve merit for the age, you finish your fathers' and grandfathers' enterprise; each keeps his frontier, each enjoys the seasons; the hundred surnames are at peace, the four classes dwell secure.

entries.zh: 孰若驅農夫於壟畝，抗勁敵於三方，避干戈於首尾，當鋒鏑於心腹。
entries.en: How does that compare with driving farmers from the fields, facing fierce enemies on three sides, avoiding weapons at head and tail, and meeting blades and arrows at the heart?
entries.literal: How does that compare with driving farmers from the fields, facing fierce enemies on three sides, avoiding weapons at head and tail, and meeting blades and arrows at the heart?

entries.zh: 縱太公為將，不能獲存，歸之高明，何以克濟。
entries.en: Even if the Grand Duke were general, he could not survive; return to the high and bright—how could success be achieved?
entries.literal: Even if the Grand Duke were general, he could not survive; return to the high and bright — how could success be achieved?

entries.zh: 來書曰，妻子老幼悉在司寇，以此見要，庶其可反。
entries.en: Your letter says my wife, children, and elders are all held by the Ministry of Justice, and that you mean to use them to force my return.
entries.literal: Your letter says that wife, children, and elders are all in the Ministry of Justice, and you use this to coerce me, hoping I might return.

entries.zh: 當是見疑褊心，未識大趣。
entries.en: This can only be the work of a suspicious and petty mind that does not grasp the larger design.
entries.literal: Surely this shows a suspicious and narrow mind, not understanding the larger design.

entries.zh: 昔王陵附漢，母在不歸；
entries.en: Long ago Wang Ling sided with Han while his mother was alive in Chu and would not return;
entries.literal: Long ago Wang Ling sided with Han while his mother lived and did not return;

entries.zh: 太上囚楚，乞羹自若。
entries.en: the Grand Emperor was held prisoner in Chu yet asked for soup as calmly as ever.
entries.literal: the Dowager Empress was imprisoned in Chu yet begged for soup as calmly as ever.

entries.zh: 矧伊妻子，而可介意。
entries.en: How much less, then, should one make a fuss over wife and children!
entries.literal: How much less should one fuss over wife and children!

entries.zh: 脫謂誅之有益，欲止不能，殺之無損，復加阬戮，家累在君，何關僕也。
entries.en: If you think killing them would serve some purpose, you cannot restrain yourself; if it would do you no good, you would still butcher them anyway. Your hostages are in your hands—what is that to me?
entries.literal: If you say killing them would help, you cannot stop wanting to; killing them would do you no good, yet you would still slaughter them. Your hostages are in your hands—what concern are they of mine?

entries.zh: 遵道所說，頗亦非虛，故重陳辭，更論款曲。
entries.en: What Zundao reported was not wholly empty, and so I restate my case and speak again in earnest.
entries.literal: What Zundao said was not entirely empty, so I restate my case and speak again of heartfelt matters.

entries.zh: 昔與盟主，事等琴瑟，讒人間之，翻為讐敵。
entries.en: Once the alliance leader and I were as harmonious as lute and zither; slanderers came between us, and we became enemies.
entries.literal: Once I and the alliance leader were harmonious as lute and zither; slanderers set us apart, and we became enemies.

entries.zh: 撫弦搦矢，不覺傷懷，裂帛還書，其何能述。
entries.en: To touch the strings or grasp the arrow is to feel grief anew; to tear silk and send it back in reply—how can words say enough?
entries.literal: Touching the strings, grasping the arrow—I cannot but feel grief; torn silk returned in reply—how can words express it?

entries.zh: 廢帝殷，字正道，文宣帝之長子也，母曰李皇后。
entries.en: Emperor Fei, whose personal name was Yin and style name Zhengdao, was the eldest son of Emperor Wenxuan. His mother was Empress Li.
entries.literal: Emperor Fei, Yin, style name Zhengdao, was the eldest son of Emperor Wenxuan; his mother was Empress Li.

entries.zh: 天保元年，立爲皇太子，時年六歲。
entries.en: In the first year of the Tianbao era he was made crown prince, at the age of six.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, he was installed as crown prince, aged six at the time.

entries.zh: 性敏慧。
entries.en: He was quick-witted by nature.
entries.literal: His nature was keen and clever.

entries.zh: 初學反語，於「跡」字下注云自反。
entries.en: When he first studied fanqie phonetic glosses, he annotated the character "trace" as self-referential.
entries.literal: When he first studied fanqie glosses, beside the character "trace" he wrote a note saying that it glossed itself.

entries.zh: 時侍者未達其故，太子曰：「跡字足傍亦爲跡，豈非自反耶？」
entries.en: The attendants did not understand what he meant, so the crown prince said, "The character for 'trace' has the 'foot' radical on one side and still forms 'trace'—is that not glossing itself by fanqie?"
entries.literal: At the time the attendants did not understand his reason; the crown prince said, "The character for trace—with the 'foot' radical beside it—is also trace; is that not a self-gloss?"

entries.zh: 常宴北宮，獨令河間王勿入。
entries.en: He often gave banquets in the Northern Palace and specifically barred the Prince of Hejian from attending.
entries.literal: He often held banquets in the Northern Palace and ordered the Prince of Hejian alone not to enter.

entries.zh: 左右問其故，太子曰：「世宗遇賊處，河間王復何宜在此。」
entries.en: When his attendants asked why, the crown prince said, "This is where Shizong met the assassins; why should the Prince of Hejian be here again?"
entries.literal: Those at his side asked the reason; the crown prince said, "This is where Shizong met the assassins; the Prince of Hejian has no business being here again."

entries.zh: 文宣每言太子得漢家性質，不似我，欲廢之，立太原王。
entries.en: Emperor Wenxuan often said the crown prince had inherited Han Chinese ways and was nothing like himself; he wanted to depose him and set up the Prince of Taiyuan instead.
entries.literal: Wenxuan often said the crown prince had taken on Han Chinese temperament and was not like him; he wished to depose him and install the Prince of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 初詔國子博士李寶鼎傅之，寶鼎卒，復詔國子博士邢峙侍講。
entries.en: At first an edict appointed Li Baoding, erudite of the National University, as his tutor. After Baoding died, Xing Zhi, also an erudite of the National University, was ordered to serve as his lecturer.
entries.literal: At first an edict appointed National University erudite Li Baoding to tutor him; when Baoding died, another edict appointed National University erudite Xing Zhi to attend and lecture.

entries.zh: 太子雖富於春秋，而溫裕開朗，有人君之度，貫綜經業，省覽時政，甚有美名。
entries.en: Though still young, the crown prince was gentle, magnanimous, and open in bearing, with the bearing of a true sovereign. He had mastered the classics, kept abreast of current policy, and enjoyed an excellent reputation.
entries.literal: Although the crown prince was still young in years, he was mild, generous, and open in manner, with the measure of a ruler; he mastered the classics and reviewed current affairs, and enjoyed a very fine reputation.

entries.zh: 七年冬，文宣召朝臣文學者及禮學官於宮宴會，令以經義相質，親自臨聽。
entries.en: In the winter of the seventh year, Emperor Wenxuan summoned literary officials and ritual specialists to a palace banquet, had them debate passages from the classics, and listened in person.
entries.literal: In the winter of the seventh year, Wenxuan summoned court officials versed in letters and officers of ritual learning to a palace banquet, ordered them to examine one another on the meaning of the classics, and personally attended to listen.

entries.zh: 太子手筆措問，在坐莫不歎美。
entries.en: The crown prince wrote out questions himself, and everyone present marveled.
entries.literal: The crown prince set questions in his own hand; none of those seated failed to sigh in admiration.

entries.zh: 九年，文宣在晉陽，太子監國，集諸儒講《孝經》。
entries.en: In the ninth year, while Emperor Wenxuan was at Jinyang, the crown prince acted as regent, gathered the scholars, and expounded the Classic of Filial Piety.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, Wenxuan was at Jinyang; the crown prince supervised the state, gathered the Confucian scholars, and lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety.

entries.zh: 令楊愔傳旨，謂國子助教許散愁曰：「先生在世何以自資？」
entries.en: He had Yang Yin deliver his message to Xu Sanchou, assistant instructor at the National University: "Sir, how do you occupy yourself in this life?"
entries.literal: He had Yang Yin convey the imperial message and say to National University assistant instructor Xu Sanchou, "Sir, in this life by what do you support yourself?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「散愁自少以來，不登孌童之床，不入季女之室，服膺簡策，不知老之將至。
entries.en: Xu replied, "From my youth I have never shared a bed with a pretty boy or entered a maiden's room. I have devoted myself to my books and scarcely noticed that old age was upon me.
entries.literal: He replied, "Sanchou from youth onward has not mounted the couch of a catamite, has not entered the chamber of a young woman; he clings to his books and scrolls and does not know that old age is coming.

entries.zh: 平生素懷，若斯而已。」
entries.en: That has been the whole of my life's ambition."
entries.literal: His lifelong plain intent was no more than this."

entries.zh: 太子曰：「顏子縮屋稱貞，柳下嫗而不亂，未若此翁白首不娶者也。」
entries.en: The crown prince said, "Yan Hui was praised for chastity though he lived in a hovel, and Liu Xiahui kept his integrity though he shared a blanket with a woman—but neither can match this old man who has never married even to white hair."
entries.literal: The crown prince said, "Yan Hui, who shrank in his hut, was called chaste; Liu Xiahui, who shared a blanket with a woman, was not corrupted—yet neither equals this old man, white-haired and never married."

entries.zh: 乃賚絹百匹。
entries.en: He then rewarded him with a hundred bolts of silk.
entries.literal: Thereupon he bestowed a hundred bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 後文宣登金鳳台，召太子使手刃囚。
entries.en: Later Emperor Wenxuan went up to the Golden Phoenix Terrace, called the crown prince, and ordered him to execute a prisoner with his own blade.
entries.literal: Later Wenxuan ascended the Golden Phoenix Terrace, summoned the crown prince, and ordered him to kill a prisoner with his own hand.

entries.zh: 太子惻然有難色，再三不斷其首。
entries.en: The crown prince looked stricken and hesitated; several times he failed to strike off the man's head.
entries.literal: The crown prince looked pained and showed reluctance; again and again he could not sever the man's head.

entries.zh: 文宣怒，親以馬鞭撞太子三下，由是氣悸語吃，精神時復昏擾。
entries.en: Emperor Wenxuan flew into a rage and personally struck the crown prince three times with his riding crop. From that time on the prince suffered heart palpitations and a stammer, and his mind would sometimes grow confused.
entries.literal: Wenxuan grew angry and personally struck the crown prince three blows with a horsewhip; from this he suffered palpitations and stammered in speech, and his spirit was at times again clouded and disturbed.

entries.zh: 三月甲寅，詔軍國事皆申晉陽，稟大丞相常山王規算。
entries.en: In the third month, on the jiayin day, an edict declared that all military and civil affairs were to be referred to Jinyang for decision by the grand chief minister, Prince Yan of Changshan.
entries.literal: In the third month, on the jiayin day, an edict ordered that all military and state affairs be reported to Jinyang and decided according to the plans of the grand chief minister, Prince of Changshan.

entries.zh: 壬申，封文襄第二子孝珩爲廣甯王，第三子長恭爲蘭陵王。
entries.en: On renshen, Xiaoheng, Wenxiang's second son, was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangning, and Changgong, his third son, as Prince of Lanling.
entries.literal: On renshen, Wenxiang's second son Xiaoheng was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangning, and his third son Changgong as Prince of Lanling.

entries.zh: 十一月乙卯，以右丞相、咸陽王斛律金爲左丞相，以錄尚書事、常山王演爲太傅，以司徒、長廣王湛爲太尉，以司空段韶爲司徒，以平陽王淹爲司空，高陽王湜爲尚書左僕射，河間王孝琬爲司州牧，侍中燕子獻爲右僕射。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, on the yimao day, Hulu Jin, Prince of Xianyang and right chief minister, was appointed left chief minister; Prince Yan of Changshan, recorder of the Masters of Writing, became grand tutor; Prince Zhan of Changguang, minister over the masses, became grand commandant; Duan Shao, minister of works, became minister over the masses; Prince Yan of Pingyang became minister of works; Prince Shi of Gaoyang became left vice-director of the Masters of Writing; Prince Xiaowan of Hejian became governor of Sizhou; and Yanzi Xian, palace attendant, became right vice-director.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on the yimao day, the right chief minister, Prince of Xianyang Hulu Jin, was made left chief minister; Prince Yan of Changshan, recorder of the affairs of the Masters of Writing, was made grand tutor; Prince Zhan of Changguang, minister over the masses, was made grand commandant; Duan Shao, minister of works, was made minister over the masses; Prince Yan of Pingyang was made minister of works; Prince Shi of Gaoyang was made left vice-director of the Masters of Writing; Prince Xiaowan of Hejian was made governor of Sizhou; and Yanzi Xian, attendant at the palace, was made right vice-director.

entries.zh: 戊午，分命使者巡省四方，求政得失，省察風俗，問人疾苦。
entries.en: On the wuwu day the court sent envoys throughout the realm to inspect government, review local customs, and learn of the people's hardships.
entries.literal: On the wuwu day envoys were dispatched in separate directions to tour the four quarters, seek out the gains and losses of government, examine local customs, and inquire into the people's hardships.

entries.zh: 乾明元年庚辰，春正月癸丑朔，改元。
entries.en: In Qianming 1, the gengchen year, on guichou, the first day of the first month in spring, the reign era was changed.
entries.literal: In the gengchen year, the first year of Qianming, in spring, on guichou, the first day of the first month, the era name was changed.

entries.zh: 己未，詔寬徭賦。
entries.en: On jiwei, an edict lightened corvee obligations and taxes.
entries.literal: On jiwei, an edict relaxed labor services and taxes.

entries.zh: 癸亥，高陽王湜薨。
entries.en: On guihai, Prince Shi of Gaoyang died.
entries.literal: On guihai, Prince Shi of Gaoyang died.

entries.zh: 是月，車駕至自晉陽。
entries.en: That month the emperor returned from Jinyang.
entries.literal: That month, the imperial carriage arrived from Jinyang.

entries.zh: 二月己亥，以太傅、常山王演爲太師、錄尚書事，以太尉、長廣王湛爲大司馬、幷省錄尚書事，以尚書左僕射、平秦王歸彥爲司空，趙郡王叡爲尚書左僕射。
entries.en: In the second month, on jihai, Prince Yan of Changshan, then grand tutor, was appointed grand preceptor and recorder of the Masters of Writing. Prince Zhan of Changguang, then grand commandant, became grand marshal and recorder of the Masters of Writing in the Bingzhou administration. Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, became minister of works, and Prince Rui of Zhaojun became left vice director.
entries.literal: In the second month, on jihai, the Grand Tutor, Prince Yan of Changshan, was made Grand Preceptor and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing; the Grand Commandant, Prince Zhan of Changguang, was made Grand Marshal and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing in Bing Province; the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, was made Minister of Works; and Prince Rui of Zhaojun was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 詔諸元良口配沒宮內及賜人者，並放免。
entries.en: An edict released all free members of the Yuan clan who had been confiscated into palace service or granted to others.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that all free persons of the Yuan clan who had been assigned and confiscated into the palace or bestowed on others should all be released and exempted.

entries.zh: 甲辰，帝幸芳林園，親錄囚徒，死罪以下降免各有差。
entries.en: On jiachen, the emperor visited Fanglin Garden and personally reviewed the prisoners. Sentences at the death penalty and below were reduced or remitted by graded degrees.
entries.literal: On jiachen, the emperor visited Fanglin Garden and personally reviewed the prisoners; those sentenced to death and below received reductions or exemptions, each by degree.

entries.zh: 乙巳，太師、常山王演矯詔誅尚書令楊愔、尚書右僕射燕子獻、領軍大將軍可朱渾天和、侍中宋欽道、散騎常侍鄭子默。
entries.en: On the yisi day Prince Yan of Changshan, grand preceptor, forged an edict and had executed Yang Yin, director of the Masters of Writing; Yanzi Xian, right vice-director; Kezhuhun Tianhe, commanding general of the palace guards; Song Qindao, palace attendant; and Zheng Zimo, attendant of the scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: On the yisi day the grand preceptor, Prince of Changshan Yan, forged an edict and executed Yang Yin, director of the Masters of Writing; Yanzi Xian, right vice-director of the Masters of Writing; Kezhuhun Tianhe, general-in-chief commanding the guards; Song Qindao, attendant at the palace; and Zheng Zimo, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

entries.zh: 戊申，以常山王演爲大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，以大司馬、長廣王湛爲太傅、京畿大都督，以司徒段韶爲大將軍，以前司空、平陽王淹爲太尉，以司空、平秦王歸彥爲司徒，彭城王浟爲尚書令。
entries.en: On the wushen day, Prince Yan of Changshan was appointed grand chief minister, commander of all armies, and recorder of the Masters of Writing. Prince Zhan of Changguang, grand marshal, became grand tutor and metropolitan commander of the capital region. Duan Shao, minister over the masses, became great general; Prince Yan of Pingyang, formerly minister of works, became grand commandant; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, minister of works, became minister over the masses; and Prince You of Pengcheng became director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: On the wushen day, Prince Yan of Changshan was made grand chief minister, commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad, and recorder of the affairs of the Masters of Writing; Prince Zhan of Changguang, grand marshal, was made grand tutor and metropolitan commander of the capital region; Duan Shao, minister over the masses, was made great general; the former minister of works, Prince Yan of Pingyang, was made grand commandant; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, minister of works, was made minister over the masses; and Prince You of Pengcheng was made director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 又以高麗王世子湯爲使持節、領東夷校尉、遼東郡公、高麗王。
entries.en: Tang, crown prince of Goguryeo, was also appointed bearer of the imperial staff, colonel of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong commandery, and King of Goguryeo.
entries.literal: The heir of the king of Goguryeo, Tang, was also appointed bearer of the staff of authority, colonel of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong commandery, and King of Goguryeo.

entries.zh: 是月，王琳爲陳所敗，蕭莊自拔至和州。
entries.en: That month Wang Lin was defeated by Chen forces, and Xiao Zhuang fled on his own to Hezhou.
entries.literal: That month Wang Lin was defeated by Chen; Xiao Zhuang escaped on his own to Hezhou.

entries.zh: 夏四月癸亥，詔河南、定、冀、趙、瀛、滄、南膠、光、青九州，往因螽水，頗傷時稼，遣使分途贍恤。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on the guihai day, an edict to the nine provinces of Henan, Ding, Ji, Zhao, Ying, Cang, Nanjiao, Guang, and Qing noted that locusts and floods had lately damaged the harvest, and dispatched envoys along separate routes to provide relief.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the guihai day, an edict addressed the nine provinces Henan, Ding, Ji, Zhao, Ying, Cang, Nanjiao, Guang, and Qing: in the past locusts and floods had greatly harmed the season's crops, and envoys were sent by separate routes to provide relief.

entries.zh: 是月，周明帝崩。
entries.en: That month Emperor Ming of Northern Zhou died.
entries.literal: That month Emperor Ming of Zhou died.

entries.zh: 孝昭皇帝演，字延安，神武皇帝第六子，文宣皇帝之母弟也。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaozhao, whose personal name was Yan and style name Yan'an, was the sixth son of Emperor Shenwu and the full younger brother of Emperor Wenxuan.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaozhao Yan, styled Yan'an, was the sixth son of Emperor Shenwu and the younger brother of Emperor Wenxuan by the same mother.

entries.zh: 幼而英特，早有大成之量，武明皇太后早所愛重。
entries.en: Even as a boy he was remarkable, showing early promise of greatness, and Empress Dowager Wuming had cherished him from the start.
entries.literal: From childhood he was outstanding; early on he showed the measure of great accomplishment, and Empress Dowager Wuming had loved and esteemed him from the first.

entries.zh: 魏元象元年，封常山郡公。
entries.en: In the first year of the Yuanxiang era of Wei, he was made Duke of Changshan Commandery.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang of Wei, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan Commandery.

entries.zh: 及文襄執政，遣中書侍郎李同軌就霸府為諸弟師。
entries.en: Once Wenxiang took charge of the government, he dispatched Li Tonggui, Gentleman of the Secretariat, to the Overlord's residence to instruct his younger brothers.
entries.literal: When Wenxiang came to hold power, he sent Secretariat Gentleman Li Tonggui to the Overlord's residence to serve as tutor to the younger brothers.

entries.zh: 帝所覽文籍，源其指歸而不好辭彩。
entries.en: In whatever he read, he sought the root meaning and cared nothing for fine phrasing.
entries.literal: In the texts the Emperor read, he traced them to their underlying intent and did not care for ornamental language.

entries.zh: 每歎云：「雖盟津之師，左驂震而不衄。」
entries.en: He often sighed and said, "Even when the army stood at Mengjin and the left outer horse shied, they did not break and flee."
entries.literal: He would often sigh and say: "Even at the army at Mengjin, though the left outer horse was startled, they did not retreat in defeat."

entries.zh: 以為能。
entries.en: That, he thought, was real courage.
entries.literal: He regarded this as true ability.

entries.zh: 遂篤志讀《漢書》，至《李陵傳》，恒壯其所為焉。
entries.en: He then applied himself to the Book of Han; when he came to the biography of Li Ling, he always took fierce pride in Li Ling's conduct.
entries.literal: Thereupon he devoted himself to reading the Book of Han, and when he reached the "Biography of Li Ling," he always admired what Li Ling had done.

entries.zh: 聰敏過人，所與遊處，一知其家諱，終身未嘗誤犯。
entries.en: Quick beyond ordinary men, he learned the taboo names of everyone he kept company with and never once, in all his life, gave accidental offense.
entries.literal: His intelligence surpassed others'; those with whom he associated—he would at once learn their family taboo names, and throughout his life he never once mistakenly violated them.

entries.zh: 同軌病卒，又命開府長流參軍刁柔代之，性嚴褊，不適誘訓之宜，中被遣出。
entries.en: After Tonggui died of illness, Diao Rou, a senior staff officer in the chief's office, was appointed in his place—but Diao was harsh and rigid, ill suited to teaching, and before long was dismissed.
entries.literal: When Tonggui died of illness, he again ordered Diao Rou, Staff Supervisor of the Chief's Office, to replace him; Diao's nature was stern and narrow, unsuited to guidance and instruction, and midway through he was dismissed and sent away.

entries.zh: 帝送出閤，慘然斂容，淚數行下，左右莫不歔欷。
entries.en: The prince walked him out through the gate, his face drawn and still, tears running freely; everyone around him wept.
entries.literal: The Emperor escorted him out through the gate, his face grave and composed, tears streaming down in several courses; those at his side all sobbed and sighed.

entries.zh: 其敬業重舊也如此。
entries.en: Such was his devotion to his teachers and his loyalty to old ties.
entries.literal: In his respect for his calling and esteem for old associates, he was like this.

entries.zh: 皇建元年八月壬午，皇帝即位於晉陽宣德殿，大赦，改乾明元年為皇建。
entries.en: On the renwu day of the eighth month of the first year of Huangjian, the emperor ascended the throne in the Xuande Hall at Jinyang, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name from Qianming to Huangjian.
entries.literal: On the renwu day of the eighth month of Huangjian year 1, the emperor ascended the throne in the Xuande Hall at Jinyang, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name from Qianming year 1 to Huangjian.

entries.zh: 詔奉太皇太后還稱皇太后，皇太后稱文宣皇后，宮曰昭信。
entries.en: An edict restored the Grand Empress Dowager to the title of Empress Dowager, gave the former empress dowager the title Empress Wenxuan, and named her residence Zhaoxin Palace.
entries.literal: An edict restored the Grand Empress Dowager to the title of Empress Dowager; the Empress Dowager was given the title Empress Wenxuan, and her palace was named Zhaoxin.

entries.zh: 乙酉，詔自太祖創業已來，諸有佐命功臣子孫絕滅，國統不傳者，有司搜訪近親，以名聞，當量為立後；
entries.en: On the yiyou day, an edict declared that since the Founding Emperor's rise to power, wherever the descendants of founding ministers had died out and their lines of succession were broken, officials should search for close relatives, report their names, and appoint successors as appropriate.
entries.literal: On the yiyou day, an edict stated that from the time the Founding Emperor established the enterprise, wherever meritorious founding ministers' descendants had died out and the line of succession was broken, the responsible offices should search out close relatives, report their names, and appoint successors as appropriate.

entries.zh: 諸郡國老人各授版職，賜黃帽鳩杖。
entries.en: Elderly men throughout the commanderies and principalities were granted honorary appointments and presented with yellow caps and dove staffs.
entries.literal: Elderly persons in all commanderies and principalities were granted honorary rank plaques and given yellow caps and dove staffs.

entries.zh: 又詔謇正之士並聽進見陳事；
entries.en: Another edict permitted upright and outspoken men to come forward and address the throne directly.
entries.literal: Another edict also allowed upright and forthright men to come forward and present matters to the throne.

entries.zh: 軍人戰亡死王事者，以時申聞，當加榮贈；
entries.en: Soldiers who fell in battle or died in the ruler's service were to be reported promptly and granted posthumous honors.
entries.literal: Soldiers who died in battle or in service to the ruler were to be reported in timely fashion and honored with posthumous awards.

entries.zh: 督將、朝士名望素高，位歷通顯，天保以來未蒙追贈者，亦皆錄奏；
entries.en: Military governors and court officials of high standing who had held prominent posts but had not received posthumous honors since the Tianbao era were also to be recorded and memorialized.
entries.literal: Military governors and court officials of longstanding high reputation who had held prominent posts but since Tianbao had not received posthumous honors—all these were also to be recorded and memorialized.

entries.zh: 又以廷尉、中丞，執法所在，繩違按罪，不得舞文弄法；
entries.en: It further ordered the Court of Judicial Review and the Censorate, as the organs charged with enforcing the law, to investigate violations and assign guilt strictly according to statute, without twisting the law for their own purposes.
entries.literal: It further ordered that the Court of Judicial Review and the Censorate, as the organs of law enforcement, must investigate violations and assign guilt according to the law, and must not distort the law through verbal manipulation.

entries.zh: 其官奴婢年六十已上免為庶人。
entries.en: Official slaves aged sixty or older were freed and made commoners.
entries.literal: Official slave servants aged sixty and above were freed to become commoners.

entries.zh: 戊子，以太傅、長廣王湛為右丞相，以太尉、平陽王淹為太傅，以尚書令、彭城王浟為大司馬。
entries.en: On wuzi, Prince Zhan of Changguang, then grand tutor, became right chancellor; Prince Yan of Pingyang, then grand commandant, became grand tutor; and Prince You of Pengcheng, director of the Masters of Writing, became grand marshal.
entries.literal: On wuzi, the Grand Tutor, Prince Zhan of Changguang, was appointed Right Chancellor; the Grand Commandant, Prince Yan of Pingyang, was appointed Grand Tutor; and the Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince You of Pengcheng, was appointed Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 壬辰，詔分遣大使巡省四方，觀察風俗，問人疾苦，考求得失，搜訪賢良。
entries.en: On the renchen day, an edict ordered envoys to be sent throughout the realm to inspect local conditions, inquire into the people's hardships, assess what had succeeded or failed, and seek out worthy and able men.
entries.literal: On the renchen day, an edict ordered envoys to be dispatched in all directions to tour and inspect the realm, observe local customs, inquire into the people's hardships, examine gains and losses, and search out the worthy and able.

entries.zh: 甲午，詔曰：「昔武王克殷，先封兩代，漢、魏、二晉，無廢茲典。
entries.en: On the jiawu day, an edict stated: "When King Wu of Zhou conquered the Shang, he first enfeoffed descendants of the two preceding dynasties. The Han, Wei, and two Jin dynasties likewise never abandoned this precedent.
entries.literal: On the jiawu day, an edict said: "In antiquity, when King Wu conquered Yin, he first enfeoffed the two former dynasties; Han, Wei, and the two Jin dynasties did not abandon this precedent.

entries.zh: 及元氏統歷，不率舊章。
entries.en: But when the Northern Wei held power, they ceased to follow the old rites.
entries.literal: When the Yuan clan held the succession, they did not follow the old statutes.

entries.zh: 朕纂承大業，思弘古典，但二王三恪，舊說不同，可議定是非，列名條奏。
entries.en: We have inherited the imperial enterprise and wish to restore the ancient practice, but scholars disagree on the rites for enfeoffing descendants of prior dynasties; let the matter be debated, the correct view determined, and the names submitted in memorial.
entries.literal: We have inherited the great enterprise and wish to restore the ancient model, but the old accounts differ on the two kings and three classes of former dynasties; the right and wrong should be debated and determined, and the names listed in a memorial.

entries.zh: 其禮義體式亦仰議之。」
entries.en: The ritual forms and ceremonial standards should likewise be submitted for deliberation."
entries.literal: The ritual forms and ceremonial standards should also be submitted for deliberation."

entries.zh: 又詔國子寺可備立官屬，依舊置生，請習經典，歲時考試。
entries.en: Another edict ordered the Directorate of the National University to restore its full staff, enroll students as before, have them study the classics, and hold seasonal examinations.
entries.literal: Another edict stated that the Directorate of the National University should fully establish its official staff, enroll students as before, have them study the classics, and hold examinations at the proper seasons.

entries.zh: 其文襄帝所運石經，宜即施列於學館。
entries.en: The stone classics commissioned by Emperor Wenxiang should immediately be set up and displayed in the academy.
entries.literal: The stone classics transported by Emperor Wenxiang should immediately be set up and displayed in the academy halls.

entries.zh: 外州大學亦仰典司勤加督課。
entries.en: The provincial universities should likewise be diligently supervised and examined by the responsible offices.
entries.literal: The provincial universities should also be diligently supervised and examined by the responsible offices.

entries.zh: 丙申，詔九州勳人有重封者，聽分授子弟，以廣骨肉之恩。
entries.en: On the bingshen day, an edict declared that meritorious men of the nine provinces who held multiple enfeoffments might divide and grant them to sons and younger brothers, so as to extend the bonds of kinship.
entries.literal: On the bingshen day, an edict stated that meritorious men of the nine provinces who held double enfeoffments might divide and grant them to their sons and younger brothers, to broaden the ties of kinship.

entries.zh: 冬十一月辛亥，立妃元氏為皇后，世子百年為皇太子。
entries.en: On the xinhai day of the eleventh month, Consort Yuan was installed as empress and the heir apparent Gao Bainian as crown prince.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, on the xinhai day, Consort Yuan was installed as empress and the heir apparent Bainian as crown prince.

entries.zh: 賜天下為父後者爵一級。
entries.en: All men throughout the realm who were heirs to their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.
entries.literal: All who served as heirs to their fathers throughout the realm were granted one rank of nobility.

entries.zh: 癸丑，有司奏太祖獻武皇帝廟宜奏《武德》之樂，舞《昭烈》之舞；
entries.en: On the guichou day, officials memorialized that the temple of the Founding Emperor, Emperor Xianwu, should use the hymn "Martial Virtue" and the dance "Illustrious Fierceness."
entries.literal: On the guichou day, the responsible offices memorialized that the temple of the Founding Emperor, Emperor Xianwu, should use the music "Wude" and the dance "Zhaolie."

entries.zh: 世宗文襄皇帝廟宜奏《文德》之樂，舞《宣政》之舞；
entries.en: The temple of Emperor Wenxiang should use the hymn "Civil Virtue" and the dance "Proclaiming Governance."
entries.literal: The temple of Emperor Wenxiang should use the music "Wende" and the dance "Xuanzheng."

entries.zh: 顯祖文宣皇帝廟宜奏《文正》之樂，舞《光大》之舞。
entries.en: The temple of Emperor Wenxuan should use the hymn "Correct Civil Virtue" and the dance "Great Radiance."
entries.literal: The temple of Emperor Wenxuan should use the music "Wenzheng" and the dance "Guangda."

entries.zh: 詔曰可。
entries.en: The edict approved the proposal.
entries.literal: An edict said it was approved.

entries.zh: 庚申，詔以故太師尉景、故太師竇泰、故太師太原王婁昭、故太宰章武王厙狄幹、故太尉段榮、故太師万俟普、故司徒蔡儁、故太師高乾、故司徒莫多婁貸文、故太保劉貴、故太保封祖裔、故廣州刺史王懷十二人配饗太祖廟庭，故太師清河王岳、故太宰安德王韓軌、故太宰扶風王可朱渾道元、故太師高昂、故大司馬劉豐、故太師万俟受洛干、故太尉慕容紹宗七人配饗世宗廟庭，故太尉河東王潘相樂、故司空薛脩義、故太傅破六韓常三人配饗顯祖廟庭。
entries.en: On the gengshen day, an edict ordered twelve deceased ministers to receive associated sacrifice in the Founding Emperor's temple, including Wei Jing, Dou Tai, Lou Zhao, She Digan, Duan Rong, Wan Sipo, Cai Jun, Gao Gan, Moduo Lou Daiwen, Liu Gui, Feng Zuyi, and Wang Huai; seven others in Emperor Wenxiang's temple, including Princes Yue, Han Gui, and Kezhuhun Daoyuan, Liu Feng, Wan Sipo Shouluogan, and Murong Shaozong; and three more in Emperor Wenxuan's temple—Pan Xiangle, Xue Xiuyi, and Poliuhan Chang.
entries.literal: On the gengshen day, an edict ordered that the late Grand Preceptor Wei Jing, Grand Preceptor Dou Tai, Grand Preceptor Prince of Taiyuan Lou Zhao, Grand Minister Prince of Zhangwu She Digan, Grand Commander Duan Rong, Grand Preceptor Wan Sipo, Minister of Education Cai Jun, Grand Preceptor Gao Gan, Minister of Education Moduo Lou Daiwen, Grand Guardian Liu Gui, Grand Guardian Feng Zuyi, and Inspector of Guang Province Wang Huai—twelve men in all—be given associated sacrifice in the Founding Emperor's temple court; that Grand Preceptor Prince of Qinghe Yue, Grand Minister Prince of Ande Han Gui, Grand Minister Prince of Fufeng Kezhuhun Daoyuan, Grand Preceptor Gao Ao, Grand Marshal Liu Feng, Grand Preceptor Wan Sipo Shouluogan, and Grand Commander Murong Shaozong—seven men—be given associated sacrifice in Emperor Wenxiang's temple court; and that Grand Commander Prince of Hedong Pan Xiangle, Minister of Works Xue Xiuyi, and Grand Tutor Poliuhan Chang—three men—be given associated sacrifice in Emperor Wenxuan's temple court.

entries.zh: 是月，帝親戎北討庫莫奚，出長城，虜奔遁，分兵致討，大獲牛馬，括總入晉陽宮。
entries.en: That month the emperor personally led a campaign north against the Kumo Xi. He passed beyond the Great Wall; the enemy fled in rout; he sent columns in pursuit and captured large herds of cattle and horses, which were tallied and brought into Jinyang Palace.
entries.literal: That month, the emperor personally took the field and marched north to attack the Kumo Xi; he passed beyond the Great Wall, the enemy fled in rout, he sent troops in separate columns to pursue them, captured large numbers of cattle and horses, and tallied the whole and brought it into Jinyang Palace.

entries.zh: 帝聰敏有識度，深沉能斷，不可窺測。
entries.en: The emperor was quick-witted and far-sighted, deep and decisive—his inner thoughts could not be read.
entries.literal: The emperor was keen and perceptive, with breadth of judgment; deep and resolute, he could not be fathomed.

entries.zh: 身長八尺，腰帶十圍，儀望風表，迥然獨秀。
entries.en: He stood eight feet tall, with a waist ten spans around; in bearing and presence he stood apart, towering above all others.
entries.literal: He stood eight feet tall, with a waist ten spans around; in bearing and appearance he stood alone, towering above others.

entries.zh: 自居臺省，留心政術，閑明簿領，吏所不逮。
entries.en: From his years in the central administration he devoted himself to governance and mastered records and accounts with a clarity clerks could not match.
entries.literal: From the time he held office in the central administration, he devoted himself to the art of governance and was clear and skilled in records and registers, beyond what clerks could match.

entries.zh: 及正位宸居，彌所剋勵。
entries.en: Once he ascended the throne, he applied himself all the more vigorously.
entries.literal: Once he took the imperial throne, he applied himself all the more vigorously.

entries.zh: 輕徭薄賦，勤恤人隱。
entries.en: He lightened corvée labor and reduced taxes, and diligently attended to the people's hidden hardships.
entries.literal: He lightened corvée labor and reduced taxes, and diligently cared for the people's hidden hardships.

entries.zh: 內無私寵，外收人物，雖后父位亦特進無別。
entries.en: He showed no private favoritism within the palace and gathered talented men from without; even the empress's father, for all his honors, received no special treatment beyond his nominal rank.
entries.literal: Within the palace he showed no private favoritism; outside he gathered men of talent, and even the empress's father, though honored, received no special treatment beyond his nominal rank.

entries.zh: 日昃臨朝，務知人之善惡，每訪問左右，冀獲直言。
entries.en: He held court until the sun was low in the west, striving to discern men's strengths and failings; he constantly questioned those around him, hoping to hear frank counsel.
entries.literal: He held court until the sun slanted westward, striving to know men's good and bad qualities; he constantly questioned those around him, hoping to obtain frank speech.

entries.zh: 曾問舍人裴澤在外議論得失。
