entries.en: He once asked Attendant Gentleman Pei Ze what people were saying about his policies when he was away from court.
entries.literal: He once asked the Attendant Gentleman Pei Ze what was said about gains and losses when he was abroad.

entries.zh: 澤率爾對曰：「陛下聰明至公，自可遠侔古昔，而有識之士，咸言傷細，帝王之度，頗為未弘。」
entries.en: Pei Ze answered without hesitation: "Your Majesty is intelligent and utterly fair and could indeed rival the sages of antiquity, but men of discernment all say you are too exacting in small matters—the magnanimity proper to an emperor is still somewhat lacking."
entries.literal: Ze answered straight off: "Your Majesty is intelligent and utterly fair and could indeed rival the ancients of old, but men of discernment all say you are too exacting in small matters; the magnanimity proper to an emperor is still somewhat lacking."

entries.zh: 帝笑曰：「誠如卿言。
entries.en: The emperor smiled and said, "You are quite right.
entries.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "It is truly as you say.

entries.zh: 朕初臨萬機，慮不周悉，故致爾耳。
entries.en: When I first assumed the throne, I had not yet grasped every detail of governance, and that is why this happened.
entries.literal: When I first took charge of the myriad affairs of state, my concerns were not thorough and complete; that is why this came about.

entries.zh: 此事安可久行，恐後又嫌疏漏。」
entries.en: This cannot go on indefinitely—I am afraid you will later find me negligent again."
entries.literal: How can this matter be carried on for long? I fear that afterward you will again find omissions.

entries.zh: 澤因被寵遇。
entries.en: Pei Ze was thereupon showered with imperial favor.
entries.literal: Thereupon Pei Ze received favored treatment.

entries.zh: 其樂聞過也如此。
entries.en: Such was his pleasure in being told of his faults.
entries.literal: His delight in hearing of his faults was like this.

entries.zh: 趙郡王叡與厙狄顯安侍坐，帝曰：「須拔我同堂弟，顯安我親姑子，今序家人禮，除君臣之敬，可言我之不逮。」
entries.en: Prince of Zhao Gao Rui and Kudi Xian'an were seated in attendance. The emperor said, "Xu Ba is my cousin; Xian'an is my aunt's son. Today we observe family etiquette and put aside the formalities of ruler and subject—you may tell me where I fall short."
entries.literal: Prince of Zhao Rui and Kudi Xian'an were in attendance seated beside him. The Emperor said: "Xu Ba is my paternal cousin; Xian'an is the son of my paternal aunt. Today let us observe family rites and set aside the respect due between ruler and minister—you may speak of where I fall short.

entries.zh: 顯安曰：「陛下多妄言。」
entries.en: Xian'an said, "Your Majesty says many things that are not true."
entries.literal: Xian'an said: "Your Majesty speaks many reckless words.

entries.zh: 曰：「若何？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "How so?"
entries.literal: He said: "How so?

entries.zh: 對曰：「陛下昔見文宣以馬鞭撻人，常以為非，而今行之，非妄言耶？」
entries.en: He replied, "Your Majesty once saw Emperor Wenxuan lash people with a riding crop and always condemned it; yet now you do the same—is that not saying one thing and doing another?"
entries.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty once saw Emperor Wenxuan beat people with a horsewhip and always regarded it as wrong; yet now you do the same—is this not reckless speech?

entries.zh: 帝握其手謝之。
entries.en: The emperor took his hand and thanked him.
entries.literal: The Emperor grasped his hand and apologized to him.

entries.zh: 又使直言。
entries.en: He again asked them to speak plainly.
entries.literal: He again had them speak frankly.

entries.zh: 對曰：「陛下太細，天子乃更似吏。」
entries.en: They replied, "Your Majesty is too detail-minded—the Son of Heaven ends up acting more like a petty official."
entries.literal: They replied: "Your Majesty is too meticulous; the Son of Heaven ends up seeming more like a clerk.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「朕甚知之，然無法來久，將整之以至無為耳。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "I am well aware of that, but things cannot stay this way forever. I mean to set affairs in order until governance can proceed effortlessly on its own."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "I know this very well; yet it cannot go on like this for long. I intend to put things in order so as ultimately to achieve non-action.

entries.zh: 又問王晞，晞答如顯安，皆從容受納。
entries.en: He then questioned Wang Xi, who answered as Xian'an had; the emperor received all their remarks with composure.
entries.literal: He again asked Wang Xi; Xi answered as Xian'an had, and all were calmly accepted.

entries.zh: 性至孝，太后不豫，出居南宮，帝行不正履，容色貶悴，衣不解帶，殆將四旬。
entries.en: He was deeply filial. When the empress dowager fell ill and moved to the Southern Palace, the emperor walked unsteadily, his face gaunt and drawn; he slept in his clothes without removing his belt for nearly forty days.
entries.literal: By nature he was extremely filial. When the Empress Dowager fell ill and moved to the Southern Palace, the Emperor did not walk with proper gait, his countenance was haggard and worn, he did not remove his belt, for nearly forty days.

entries.zh: 殿去南宮五百餘步，雞鳴而去，辰時方還，來去徒行，不乘輿輦。
entries.en: The palace hall was over five hundred paces from the Southern Palace. He rose at cockcrow and did not return until mid-morning, walking the whole way on foot without taking a carriage or palanquin.
entries.literal: The hall was more than five hundred paces from the Southern Palace. He rose at cockcrow and returned only at the chen hour; coming and going he walked on foot and did not ride in carriage or palanquin.

entries.zh: 太后所苦小增，便即寢伏閤外，食飲藥物盡皆躬親。
entries.en: Whenever the empress dowager's illness worsened even slightly, he would immediately bed down outside her chamber and personally attend to all her food, drink, and medicine.
entries.literal: Whenever the Empress Dowager's affliction increased even slightly, he at once lay down to sleep outside her chamber door; food, drink, and medicines he attended to entirely in person.

entries.zh: 太后常心痛不自堪忍，帝立侍帷前，以爪掐手心，血流出袖。
entries.en: When the empress dowager was often racked with unbearable heart pain, the emperor would stand in attendance before her curtain, digging his nails into his palms until blood ran down his sleeves.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager often suffered heart pain she could not bear. The Emperor stood attending before the curtain, digging his fingernails into his palms until blood flowed down his sleeves.

entries.zh: 友愛諸弟，無君臣之隔。
entries.en: He was loving toward his younger brothers, with none of the distance that normally separates ruler from subject.
entries.literal: He was affectionate toward his younger brothers, with no barrier of ruler and minister between them.

entries.zh: 雄斷有謀，于時國富兵強，將雪神武遺恨，意在頓駕平陽，為進取之策。
entries.en: Bold and decisive, he was also a man of strategy. The realm was then rich and its armies strong, and he meant to avenge the grievances left by Emperor Shenwu, planning to establish his headquarters at Pingyang as a base for conquest.
entries.literal: Bold in decision and possessed of strategy, at that time the state was rich and the army strong; he wished to avenge Emperor Shenwu's lingering resentment and intended to encamp at Pingyang as a strategy for advance.

entries.zh: 遠圖不遂，惜哉！
entries.en: His grand designs were never realized—what a pity!
entries.literal: His distant designs were not fulfilled—alas!

entries.zh: 論曰：神武平定四方，威權在己，遷鄴之後，雖主器有人，號令所加，政皆自出。
entries.en: Commentary: Emperor Shenwu pacified the realm and kept power firmly in his own hands. After the capital was moved to Ye, though a sovereign sat on the throne, every command and every policy issued from him alone.
entries.literal: The commentary says: Emperor Shenwu pacified the four quarters; authority and power were in his own hands. After moving the capital to Ye, although the heir held the vessel of state, every order issued and every policy enacted came from himself.

entries.zh: 文宣因循鴻業，內外葉從，自朝及野，群心屬望，東魏之地，舉國樂推，曾未期月，遂登宸極。
entries.en: Emperor Wenxuan inherited this great enterprise; court and country fell into step, and from the capital to the provinces all looked to him. Throughout Eastern Wei the people rallied to his cause, and within a month he had taken the throne.
entries.literal: Wenxuan followed the great enterprise; inside and outside were in harmony; from court to countryside all hearts looked to him; throughout the lands of Eastern Wei the whole nation gladly supported him, and within less than a month he ascended the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 始則存心政事，風化肅然，數年之間，朝野安出。
entries.en: At first he applied himself diligently to governance, and discipline prevailed; within a few years the realm was at peace.
entries.literal: At first he devoted his heart to affairs of government and customs were sternly ordered; within a few years court and countryside were secure and at ease.

entries.zh: 其後縱酒肆欲，事極倡狂，昏邪殘暴，近代未有，饗國不永，實由斯疾。
entries.en: Later he gave himself over to wine and licentiousness to the point of madness—confused, wicked, cruel, and violent as few rulers in memory had been. His reign was brief, and the fault lay in this very failing.
entries.literal: Afterward he indulged in wine and unrestrained desire, affairs reaching the extreme of reckless abandon; muddled, depraved, cruel, and violent—unmatched in recent times—his enjoyment of the state was not long; this was truly due to this malady.

entries.zh: 濟南繼業，大革其弊，風教粲然，搢紳稱幸。
entries.en: The Prince of Jinan succeeded him and vigorously reformed these abuses; culture and morals flourished anew, and the gentry spoke of their good fortune.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jinan succeeded to the enterprise and greatly reformed its abuses; customs and teaching shone brightly, and officials and gentry spoke of their good fortune.

entries.zh: 股肱輔弼，雖懷厥誠，旣不能贊弘道德，和睦親懿，又不能遠慮防身，深謀衛主，應斷不斷，自取其咎。
entries.en: His chief ministers, for all their loyalty, could neither promote virtue and harmony among the imperial kin, nor forestall danger or counsel their lord with far-sighted care. Where decisive action was needed, they failed to act—and brought disaster on themselves.
entries.literal: His chief ministers and assistants, though cherishing their loyalty, were neither able to help expand virtue and morality and harmonize kin and in-laws, nor able to plan far ahead to protect themselves and deeply counsel to guard their lord; where they should have acted decisively they did not, and brought ruin upon themselves.

entries.zh: 臣旣誅夷，君壽廢辱，皆任非其器之所致爾。
entries.en: Ministers were put to death and the sovereign's life ended in humiliation—all because the wrong men had been placed in office.
entries.literal: Ministers were executed and the ruler's life cut short in disgrace—all caused by appointing men unfit for their posts.

entries.zh: 孝昭早居臺閤，故事通明，人吏之間，無所不委。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaozhao had long served in the imperial secretariat, knew its precedents inside out, and was entrusted with every matter great and small.
entries.literal: Xiaozhao early occupied the Terrace Pavilion; he was thoroughly versed in precedent; between men and officials nothing was not entrusted to him.

entries.zh: 文宣崩後，大革前弊。
entries.en: After Emperor Wenxuan's death he undertook sweeping reforms of earlier abuses.
entries.literal: After Wenxuan's death he greatly reformed previous abuses.

entries.zh: 及臨尊極，留心更深，時人服其明而識其細也。
entries.en: Once he ascended the throne his attentiveness only deepened; contemporaries admired his clarity of mind and noted his eye for detail.
entries.literal: When he reached the supreme dignity his attention went deeper still; men of the time admired his clarity and recognized his meticulousness.

entries.zh: 情好稽古，率由禮度，將封先代之胤，且敦學校之風，徵召英賢，文武畢集。
entries.en: He cherished antiquity and governed by ritual propriety; he planned to ennoble descendants of earlier dynasties, revive the culture of learning, and summon men of talent until scholars and soldiers alike had gathered at court.
entries.literal: In sentiment he loved antiquity and followed ritual norms; he was about to enfeoff descendants of former dynasties and also promote the spirit of schools, summoning worthy talents until civil and military men were all gathered.

entries.zh: 于時周氏朝政移於宰臣，主將相猜，不無危殆。
entries.en: At that time power in the Northern Zhou court had passed to its chief ministers; ruler and generals eyed one another with suspicion, and peril was never far away.
entries.literal: At that time the Zhou court's governance had shifted to its chief ministers; lord and generals were mutually suspicious, and danger was not absent.

entries.zh: 乃眷關右，實懷兼併之志，經謀宏遠，實當代之明主，而降年不永，其故何哉？
entries.en: He then looked westward beyond the Pass, harboring real designs of conquest; his plans were bold and far-reaching—he was truly a ruler of rare ability in his time—yet his life was cut short. What was the cause?
entries.literal: He then turned his gaze to the lands west of the Pass, truly harboring ambitions of annexation; his plans were far-reaching—he was truly an enlightened ruler of his age—yet his allotted years were not long; what was the reason?

entries.zh: 豈幽顯之間，實有報復，將齊之基宇止在於斯，帝欲大之，天不許也？
entries.en: Was there retribution at work between the seen and unseen worlds—and was the Northern Qi destined to rise no higher? He sought to expand its domain, but Heaven would not allow it.
entries.literal: Was it that between the hidden and the manifest there is truly retribution, and that the foundation of Qi would extend no further—he wished to enlarge it, but Heaven would not permit it?

entries.zh: 時文宣溺於遊宴，帝憂憤表於神色。
entries.en: By then Emperor Wenxuan was lost to feasting and pleasure, and the prince's distress and anger showed in his every look.
entries.literal: At that time Wenxuan was drowning himself in touring and banqueting; the Emperor's worry and indignation showed plainly in his face.

entries.zh: 文宣覺之，謂帝曰：「但令汝在，我何為不縱樂？」
entries.en: Emperor Wenxuan noticed and said to him, "With you here, why should I not enjoy myself?"
entries.literal: Wenxuan noticed it and said to the Emperor: "As long as you are here, why should I not indulge in pleasure?"

entries.zh: 帝唯啼泣拜伏，竟無所言。
entries.en: The prince could only weep and bow to the ground; in the end he said not a word.
entries.literal: The Emperor only wept and prostrated himself, and in the end said nothing.

entries.zh: 文宣亦大悲，抵杯於地曰：「汝以此嫌我，自今敢進酒者，斬之！」
entries.en: Emperor Wenxuan was stricken too. He smashed his cup on the floor and cried, "So this is how you see me! From today on, whoever dares set wine before me shall be executed!"
entries.literal: Wenxuan also became deeply grieved, dashed his cup to the ground, and said: "You resent me for this—from today, anyone who dares bring wine forward shall be executed!"

entries.zh: 因取所御杯盡皆壞棄。
entries.en: Then he took every cup at hand and smashed them all.
entries.literal: Thereupon he took all the cups he had been using and destroyed and discarded them.

entries.zh: 後益沉湎，或入諸貴賤家角力批拉，不限貴賤。
entries.en: After that he only sank deeper into drink. Sometimes he would walk into any house, high or low, and wrestle and brawl without distinction of rank.
entries.literal: Afterwards he sank deeper into drinking; sometimes he would enter the homes of nobles and commoners alike to wrestle and grapple, with no restriction as to high or low rank.

entries.zh: 唯常山王至，內外肅然。
entries.en: Only when the Prince of Changshan appeared did the palace fall silent and straighten itself.
entries.literal: Only when the Prince of Changshan arrived would inside and outside become solemn and awestruck.

entries.zh: 帝又密撰事條，將諫，其友王晞以為不可。
entries.en: The prince secretly drew up a list of grievances and prepared to remonstrate, but his friend Wang Xi urged him not to.
entries.literal: The Emperor also secretly drafted a list of matters and was about to remonstrate; his friend Wang Xi thought it inadvisable.

entries.zh: 帝不從，因間極言，遂逢大怒。
entries.en: He would not listen. Seizing a moment alone with Emperor Wenxuan, he spoke with all his force—and provoked a terrible rage.
entries.literal: The Emperor would not heed him; taking advantage of an opportune moment he spoke out to the fullest, and thereby encountered great wrath.

entries.zh: 順成后本魏朝宗室，文宣欲帝離之，陰為帝廣求淑媛，望移其寵。
entries.en: Empress Shuncheng came from the Wei imperial clan. Emperor Wenxuan wanted the prince to turn from her and secretly searched out worthy beauties for him, hoping to draw his heart elsewhere.
entries.literal: Empress Shuncheng was originally of the imperial clan of Wei; Wenxuan wanted the Emperor to distance himself from her, and secretly sought fine ladies widely for the Emperor, hoping to shift his favor.

entries.zh: 帝雖承旨有納，而情義彌重。
entries.en: The prince obeyed and took some of them in, but his devotion to the empress only grew deeper.
entries.literal: Though the Emperor followed the order and accepted some, his affection and attachment grew only stronger.

entries.zh: 帝性頗嚴，尚書郎中剖斷有失，輒加捶楚，令史姦慝，便即考竟。
entries.en: He could be severe. When a Secretariat gentleman erred in judgment, he had him beaten at once; when a clerk proved corrupt, he had him interrogated to the finish.
entries.literal: The Emperor's nature was quite stern; when Secretariat Gentlemen made errors in judgment, he would immediately add beating with the whip; when clerks were deceitful and wicked, he would immediately investigate them to the end.

entries.zh: 文宣乃立帝於前，以刀環擬脅召被帝罰者，臨以白刃，求帝之短，咸無所陳，方見解釋。
entries.en: Emperor Wenxuan made the prince stand before him, brandishing the ring of his sword as a threat. He called in those the prince had punished, put bare blades to their throats, and demanded his faults—but none had any charge to bring, and only then was the prince released.
entries.literal: Wenxuan then placed the Emperor before him, using the ring of a sword as if to threaten; summoning those whom the Emperor had punished, he confronted them with naked blades and sought the Emperor's faults—but all had nothing to report, and only then was the Emperor released and pardoned.

entries.zh: 自是不許笞箠郎中。
entries.en: After that he was forbidden to flog the Secretariat gentlemen.
entries.literal: From then on he was not permitted to flog and beat the Gentlemen of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 後賜帝魏時宮人，醒而忘之，謂帝擅取，遂以刀環亂築，因此致困。
entries.en: Later Emperor Wenxuan gave the prince palace women left from Wei times. When he sobered, he forgot the gift, accused the prince of taking them without leave, and beat him savagely with the sword ring until the prince collapsed from his injuries.
entries.literal: Later Wenxuan bestowed palace women from Wei times upon the Emperor; when he sobered up he forgot about it, thought the Emperor had taken them without permission, and thereupon beat him randomly with the sword ring, causing the Emperor to fall gravely ill as a result.

entries.zh: 皇太后日夜啼泣，文宣不知所為。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager wept day and night, and Emperor Wenxuan did not know what to do.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager wept day and night; Wenxuan did not know what to do.

entries.zh: 先是禁友王晞，乃捨之，令侍帝。
entries.en: Wang Xi, his friend, had earlier been placed under restriction; now Emperor Wenxuan freed him and set him to wait on the prince.
entries.literal: Earlier Wang Xi, his friend, had been confined; now he released him and ordered him to attend the Emperor.

entries.zh: 帝月餘漸瘳，不敢復諫。
entries.en: After a month and more the prince slowly mended, but he never dared remonstrate again.
entries.literal: After more than a month the Emperor gradually recovered, but dared not remonstrate again.

entries.zh: 初，帝與濟南約不相害。
entries.en: At first the emperor and the Prince of Jinan had pledged not to harm each other.
entries.literal: Initially the Emperor and the Prince of Jinan agreed not to harm each other.

entries.zh: 及輿駕在晉陽，武成鎮鄴，望氣者云鄴城有天子氣。
entries.en: When the emperor was at Jinyang and Wucheng (Gao Zhan) held Ye, geomancers declared that Ye possessed the aura of imperial destiny.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Jinyang and Wucheng was stationed at Ye, practitioners of qi-reading said Ye city had the aura of a Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 帝常恐濟南復興，乃密行鳩毒，濟南不從，乃扼而殺之。
entries.en: The emperor, fearing that the Prince of Jinan might regain power, secretly sent poison; when the prince refused to take it, he was strangled to death.
entries.literal: The Emperor often feared the Prince of Jinan would rise again, and so secretly administered poison; when the Prince of Jinan refused, he strangled him to death.

entries.zh: 後頗愧悔。
entries.en: Afterward he was deeply remorseful.
entries.literal: Afterward he felt considerable remorse.

entries.zh: 初苦內熱，頻進湯散。
entries.en: At first he was troubled by internal fever and took medicinal broths and powders repeatedly.
entries.literal: At first he suffered from internal heat and frequently took decoctions and powders.

entries.zh: 時有尚書令史姓趙，於鄴見文宣從楊愔、燕子獻等西行，言相與復讐。
entries.en: A clerk in the Secretariat surnamed Zhao, while at Ye, saw a vision of Emperor Wenxuan leading Yang Yin, Yan Zixian, and others westward, saying they had come to take revenge.
entries.literal: At that time there was a Secretariat clerk surnamed Zhao who, at Ye, saw Wenxuan leading Yang Yin, Yan Zixian, and others heading west, saying they were coming together to take revenge.

entries.zh: 帝在晉陽宮，與毛夫人亦見焉。
entries.en: The emperor, in the Jinyang Palace, saw the same vision, as did Lady Mao.
entries.literal: The Emperor, at Jinyang Palace, along with Lady Mao, also saw it.

entries.zh: 遂漸危篤。
entries.en: His illness thereupon grew steadily worse.
entries.literal: Thereupon his condition gradually became critical.

entries.zh: 備禳厭之事，或煮油四灑，或持炬燒逐。
entries.en: Every sort of exorcism was performed—oil was boiled and splashed in all directions, or torches were carried to burn and drive spirits away.
entries.literal: He prepared exorcistic and apotropaic rites: sometimes boiling oil and sprinkling it in all directions, sometimes holding torches to burn and drive away spirits.

entries.zh: 諸厲方出殿梁，騎棟上，歌呼自若，了無懼容。
entries.en: When evil spirits seemed to emerge from the palace beams, he climbed onto the rafters, singing and shouting as if unperturbed, showing not the slightest fear.
entries.literal: Just as various apparitions were emerging from the hall beams, he mounted the ridgepole, singing and shouting as if at ease, utterly without fear.

entries.zh: 時有天狗下，乃於其所講武以厭之。
entries.en: When a celestial portent appeared, he held military exercises at the spot to ward it off.
entries.literal: When the Celestial Dog descended, he performed military drills at that place to counter it.

entries.zh: 有兔驚馬，帝墜而絕肋。
entries.en: A rabbit startled his horse, and the emperor fell, breaking his ribs.
entries.literal: A rabbit startled the horse; the Emperor fell and broke his ribs.

entries.zh: 太后視疾，問濟南所在者三，帝不對。
entries.en: The empress dowager came to see him in his illness and three times asked where the Prince of Jinan was; the emperor did not reply.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager came to visit him in his illness and three times asked where the Prince of Jinan was; the Emperor did not answer.

entries.zh: 太后怒曰：「殺之耶？
entries.en: The empress dowager said angrily, "Did you kill him?
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager angrily said: "You killed him, did you?

entries.zh: 不用吾言，死其宜矣！」
entries.en: You refused to listen to me—you deserve to die!"
entries.literal: You did not heed my words—death is what you deserve!

entries.zh: 臨終之際，唯扶服床枕，叩頭求哀。
entries.en: On his deathbed he could only cling to his bed and pillow, kowtowing and pleading for his life.
entries.literal: At the point of death he only clung to the bed and pillow, kowtowing and begging for mercy.

entries.zh: 遣使詔追長廣王入纂大統，手書云：「宜將吾妻子置一好處，勿學前人也。」
entries.en: He dispatched envoys with an edict summoning the Prince of Changguang to succeed him, writing in his own hand: "See that my wife and children are placed somewhere safe; do not do as those before you did."
entries.literal: He sent envoys with an edict summoning the Prince of Changguang to succeed to the great succession, writing in his own hand: "You should place my wife and children in a good place; do not imitate those before you."

entries.zh: 及文宣崩，帝居禁中護喪事，幼主即位，乃即朝班。
entries.en: When Emperor Wenxuan died, Xiaozhao remained in the palace to oversee the funeral. Once the young ruler took the throne, he entered the court ranks.
entries.literal: When Wenxuan died, the emperor remained inside the palace to oversee the funeral arrangements; after the young ruler ascended the throne, he then took his place in the court ranks.

entries.zh: 除太傅、錄尚書，朝政皆決於帝。
entries.en: He was appointed grand tutor and recorder of the Masters of Writing, and all court affairs were decided by him.
entries.literal: He was appointed Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and all court government was decided by the emperor.

entries.zh: 月餘，乃居藩邸，自是詔勑多不關帝。
entries.en: After a little over a month he withdrew to his princely residence, and from then on many edicts no longer passed through him.
entries.literal: After more than a month he went to live in his princely residence, and from then on edicts and commands often did not involve the emperor.

entries.zh: 客或言於帝曰：「鷙烏舍巢，必有探卵之患，今日之地，何宜屢出。」
entries.en: One guest warned him, "When a bird of prey leaves the nest, someone is bound to reach for its eggs. In your present position, you should not be going out so often."
entries.literal: A guest once said to the emperor, "When a fierce bird leaves its nest, there is sure to be the danger of someone probing its eggs; in your present position, you should not go out repeatedly."

entries.zh: 乾明元年，從廢帝赴鄴，居於領軍府。
entries.en: In Qianming 1 he accompanied Emperor Fei to Ye and resided at the headquarters of the Commanding General.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianming, he followed Emperor Fei to Ye and lived at the headquarters of the Commanding General.

entries.zh: 時楊愔、燕子獻、可朱渾天和、宋欽道、鄭子默等以帝威望旣重，內懼權逼，請以帝為太師、司州牧、錄尚書事；
entries.en: At the time Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Kezhuhun Tianhe, Song Qindao, Zheng Zimo, and the others saw how great his prestige had become and secretly feared the pressure of his authority. They asked that he be made grand preceptor, governor of Sizhou, and recorder of the Masters of Writing;
entries.literal: At the time Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Kezhuhun Tianhe, Song Qindao, Zheng Zimo, and others, because the emperor’s prestige had become weighty and they inwardly feared the pressure of his power, requested that he be made Grand Preceptor, governor of Sizhou, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing;

entries.zh: 長廣王湛為大司馬、錄幷省尚書事，解京畿大都督。
entries.en: Prince Zhan of Changguang was appointed grand marshal and recorder of the Masters of Writing in the Bingzhou administration, and was relieved of the capital-region command.
entries.literal: Prince Zhan of Changguang was made Grand Marshal and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing in Bing Province, and was relieved as metropolitan commander of the capital region.

entries.zh: 帝時以尊親而見猜斥，乃與長廣王期獵，謀之於野。
entries.en: Because his rank and kinship made him suspect, Xiaozhao was being pushed aside. He therefore arranged a hunt with Prince Zhan of Changguang and plotted with him in the field.
entries.literal: The emperor at that time, because he was an honored kinsman, was regarded with suspicion and pushed aside; he therefore arranged to hunt with the Prince of Changguang and plotted with him in the countryside.

entries.zh: 十一月甲辰，詔曰：「朕嬰此暴疾，奄忽無逮。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, on jiachen, an edict declared, "I have been struck by a sudden grave illness and can no longer attend to affairs.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiachen, an edict said: "I have been stricken by this violent illness and suddenly can no longer reach affairs.

entries.zh: 今嗣子沖眇，未閑政術，社稷業重，理歸上德。
entries.en: The heir is young and slight, not yet versed in statecraft. The charge of the dynasty is heavy, and by rights it should pass to one of highest virtue.
entries.literal: Now the heir is young and slight, not yet practiced in the arts of government; the work of the altars of soil and grain is weighty, and by principle it returns to one of highest virtue.

entries.zh: 右丞相、長廣王湛研機測化，體道居宗，人雄之望，海內瞻仰，同胞共氣，家國所憑，可遣尚書左僕射、趙郡王叡喻旨，征王統茲大寶。
entries.en: Prince Zhan of Changguang, right chancellor, understands hidden workings and change, embodies the Way, and stands foremost among the clan. The whole realm looks to him as a hero among men. Born of the same mother and sharing the same breath, he is the support of house and state. Send Prince Rui of Zhaojun, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, to convey my intent and summon him to take charge of the throne.
entries.literal: The Right Chancellor, Prince Zhan of Changguang, studies subtle workings and fathoms transformation, embodies the Way and stands within the clan; as a hero among men, he is looked up to within the seas. Of the same womb and shared breath, he is one on whom house and state rely. The Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince Rui of Zhaojun, may be sent to explain the intent and summon the prince to govern this great treasure.

entries.zh: 其喪紀之禮一同漢文，三十六日悉從公除，山陵施用，務從儉約。」
entries.en: As for mourning rites, follow entirely the precedent of Emperor Wen of Han. After thirty-six days all mourning shall be removed according to public rule, and the mausoleum expenses must be kept frugal."
entries.literal: As for the rites of mourning, let all be the same as under Emperor Wen of Han; after thirty-six days, all shall follow public removal of mourning, and the expenditures for the mountain mausoleum must follow frugality."

entries.zh: 先是帝不豫而無闕聽覽，是月，崩於晉陽宮，時年二十七。
entries.en: Before this the emperor had been ill, yet he had not neglected audiences or reviews of affairs. That month he died in Jinyang Palace at the age of twenty-seven.
entries.literal: Before this, the emperor had been ill but had not neglected hearings and review; that month he died in Jinyang Palace, aged twenty-seven.

entries.zh: 大寧元年閏十二月癸卯，梓宮還鄴，上諡曰孝昭皇帝。
entries.en: In the intercalary twelfth month of Daning 1, on guimao, his coffin was returned to Ye, and he was given the posthumous title Emperor Xiaozhao.
entries.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month of the first year of Daning, on guimao, the imperial coffin returned to Ye, and the posthumous title Emperor Xiaozhao was presented.

entries.zh: 庚午，葬於文靖陵。
entries.en: On gengwu he was buried in Wenjing Mausoleum.
entries.literal: On gengwu, he was buried in Wenjing Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 世祖武成皇帝，諱湛，神武皇帝第九子，孝昭皇帝之母弟也。
entries.en: Emperor Wucheng, Gao Zhan, posthumous title Shizu, was the ninth son of Emperor Shenwu and the full younger brother of Emperor Xiaozhao.
entries.literal: Emperor Wucheng, posthumous title Shizu, taboo name Zhan, was the ninth son of Emperor Shenwu and the younger brother of Emperor Xiaozhao by the same mother.

entries.zh: 儀錶瑰傑，神武尤所鍾愛。
entries.en: Handsome in bearing and striking in appearance, he was especially beloved by Emperor Shenwu.
entries.literal: His bearing and appearance were magnificent and outstanding; Shenwu especially cherished him.

entries.zh: 神武方招懷荒遠，乃為帝聘蠕蠕太子庵羅辰女，號「鄰和公主」。
entries.en: While Emperor Shenwu was working to bring distant peoples into allegiance, he betrothed the prince to the daughter of Anluochen, the Rouran crown prince, who was given the title "Princess Linhe."
entries.literal: When Shenwu was seeking to win over distant frontier peoples, he arranged a marriage for the Emperor with the daughter of Anluochen, heir of the Rouran crown prince, titled "Princess Linhe."

entries.zh: 帝時年八歲，冠服端嚴，神情閑遠，華戎歎異。
entries.en: The prince was then eight years old. His dress was dignified and his manner calm and composed, and both Chinese and foreigners alike expressed admiration.
entries.literal: At the time the Emperor was eight years old; his cap and robes were dignified, his expression serene and distant, and both Chinese and barbarians marveled.

entries.zh: 元象中，封長廣郡公。
entries.en: During the Yuanxiang era, he was made Duke of Changguang Commandery.
entries.literal: During the Yuanxiang era, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Changguang Commandery.

entries.zh: 天保初，進爵為王，拜尚書令，尋兼司徒，遷太尉。
entries.en: At the opening of the Tianbao era, he was raised to princely rank, made Chief Minister of the Secretariat, soon also given concurrent appointment as Minister over the Masses, and then transferred to Grand Commander.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, his rank was advanced to prince; he was appointed Chief Minister of the Secretariat, soon also served concurrently as Minister over the Masses, and was transferred to Grand Commander.

entries.zh: 乾明初，楊愔等密相疏忌，以帝為大司馬，領幷州刺史。
entries.en: At the start of the Qianming era, Yang Yin and his faction secretly kept their distance and were wary of him, but nevertheless made him Grand Marshal and Inspector of Bing Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianming, Yang Yin and others secretly kept their distance and were wary of him, and appointed the Emperor Grand Marshal with concurrent duty as Inspector of Bing Province.

entries.zh: 帝旣與孝昭謀誅諸執政，遷太傅、錄尚書事、領京畿大都督。
entries.en: After he and Emperor Xiaozhao plotted to execute the ruling ministers, he was made Grand Tutor, Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat, and Metropolitan Commander of the Capital Region.
entries.literal: Once the Emperor had joined with Xiaozhao in plotting to execute the ruling ministers, he was transferred to Grand Tutor, Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat, and Metropolitan Commander of the Capital Region.

entries.zh: 皇建初，進位右丞相。
entries.en: At the opening of the Huangjian era, he was promoted to Right Chancellor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was promoted to Right Chancellor.

entries.zh: 孝昭幸晉陽，帝以懿親居守鄴，政事咸見委託。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaozhao went to Jinyang, the prince remained at Ye as a trusted kinsman, and all government affairs were entrusted to him.
entries.literal: When Xiaozhao went to Jinyang, the Emperor, as a close kinsman, remained to guard Ye, and all government affairs were entrusted to him.

entries.zh: 二年，孝昭崩，遺詔徵帝入統大位。
entries.en: In the second year, Emperor Xiaozhao died. His testamentary edict summoned the prince to succeed to the throne.
entries.literal: In the second year, Xiaozhao died; his testamentary edict summoned the Emperor to enter and succeed to the great throne.

entries.zh: 及晉陽宮，發喪於崇德殿。
entries.en: Upon reaching Jinyang Palace, mourning rites were begun at Chungde Hall.
entries.literal: Upon reaching Jinyang Palace, the mourning was begun at Chungde Hall.

entries.zh: 皇太后令所司宣遺詔，左丞相斛律金率百僚敦勸，三奏，乃許之。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager ordered the responsible offices to proclaim the testamentary edict. Left Chancellor Hulu Jin led the hundred officials in earnest urging, and after three presentations the prince consented.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered the responsible offices to proclaim the testamentary edict; Left Chancellor Hulu Jin led the hundred officials in earnest urging; after three presentations, he consented.

entries.zh: 夏四月戊午，大將軍、東安王婁叡坐事免。
entries.en: In summer, in the fourth month, on wuwu, Lou Rui, Grand General and Prince of Dong'an, was dismissed over an affair.
entries.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the wuwu day, Grand General and Prince Rui of Dong'an, Lou Rui, was dismissed for involvement in a case.

entries.zh: 乙亥，陳人來聘。
entries.en: On yihai, envoys from Chen came to court.
entries.literal: On the yihai day, people from Chen came on a diplomatic mission.

entries.zh: 太史奏天文有變，其占當有易王。
entries.en: The Grand Astrologer reported a celestial anomaly whose omen pointed to a change of ruler.
entries.literal: The Grand Astrologer memorialized that there had been a change in the celestial patterns, and the prognostication indicated that there should be a change of ruler.

entries.zh: 丙子，乃使太宰段韶兼太尉，持節奉皇帝璽綬傳位於皇太子，大赦，改元為天統元年，百官進級降罪各有差。
entries.en: On bingzi, Grand Minister Duan Shao, concurrently Grand Commandant, was sent with the credentials to convey the imperial seals and ribbons and transfer the throne to the crown prince. A general amnesty was proclaimed, the era was changed to Tiantong, and officials were advanced and punishments reduced by graded degrees.
entries.literal: On the bingzi day, he then had the Grand Minister Duan Shao concurrently serve as Grand Commandant and, bearing the credentials, present the imperial seals and ribbons to transmit the throne to the crown prince; a general amnesty was proclaimed, the era name was changed to the first year of Tiantong, and the hundred officials were advanced in grade and punishments reduced, each by rank.

entries.zh: 又詔皇太子妃斛律氏為皇后。
entries.en: A further edict made the crown prince's consort, Lady Hulu, empress.
entries.literal: Another edict made the crown prince's consort, Lady Hulu, empress.

entries.zh: 於是群公上尊號為太上皇帝，軍國大事咸以奏聞。
entries.en: The lords then offered him the title Retired Emperor, and all major military and state affairs continued to be submitted to him.
entries.literal: Thereupon the assembled lords presented him with the honorific title Retired Emperor, and all great affairs of the army and state were reported to him.

entries.zh: 始將傳政，使內參乘子尚乘驛送詔書於鄴。
entries.en: When he first prepared to hand over the government, he sent Zishang, an Inner Cansheng, by relay post to carry the edict to Ye.
entries.literal: At first, when he was about to transfer the government, he sent the Inner Cansheng Zishang by relay post to deliver the edict to Ye.

entries.zh: 子尚出晉陽城，見人騎隨後，忽失之，尚未至鄴而其言已布矣。
entries.en: As Zishang left Jinyang, he saw a rider following him who suddenly vanished; before Zishang reached Ye, the news had already spread.
entries.literal: When Zishang left Jinyang city, he saw a mounted man following behind him, who suddenly disappeared; before Zishang had reached Ye, the news had already spread.

entries.zh: 天統四年十二月辛未，太上皇帝崩於鄴宮乾壽堂，時年三十二，諡曰武成皇帝，廟號世祖。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of the Tiantong era, on the xinwei day, the retired emperor died in the Qianshou Hall of the Ye Palace. He was thirty-two years old. He was posthumously titled Emperor Wucheng, with the temple name Shizu.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Tiantong, on the xinwei day, the retired emperor died in the Qianshou Hall of the Ye Palace. He was thirty-two years old. His posthumous title was Emperor Wucheng, and his temple name was Shizu.

entries.zh: 五年二月甲申，葬於永平陵。
entries.en: In the second month of the fifth year, on the jiashen day, he was buried at Yongping Mausoleum.
entries.literal: In the second month of the fifth year, on the jiashen day, he was buried at Yongping Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 大寧元年冬十一月癸丑，皇帝即位於南宮，大赦，改皇建二年為大寧。
entries.en: In winter, in the eleventh month of the first year of Daning, on guichou, the emperor took the throne in the Southern Palace, proclaimed a general amnesty, and renamed the second year of Huangjian as Daning.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daning, in winter, in the eleventh month, on the guichou day, the emperor ascended the throne in the Southern Palace, issued a general amnesty, and changed the second year of Huangjian to Daning.

entries.zh: 乙卯，以司徒、平秦王歸彥為太傅，以尚書右僕射、趙郡王叡為尚書令，以太尉尉粲為太保，以尚書令段韶為大司馬，以豐州刺史婁叡為司空，乙太傅、平陽王淹為太宰，以太保、彭城王浟為太師、錄尚書事，以冀州刺史、博陵王濟為太尉，以中書監、任城王潛為尚書左僕射，以幷州刺史斛律光為右僕射，封孝昭皇帝太子百年為樂陵郡王。
entries.en: On the yimao day, the emperor reshuffled the highest offices: Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, Minister over the Masses, became Grand Tutor; Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, became Chief Minister of the Secretariat; Grand Commandant Wei Can became Grand Guardian; Duan Shao became Grand Marshal; Lou Rui became Minister of Works; Prince Yan of Pingyang became Grand Minister; Prince You of Pengcheng became Grand Preceptor and Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat; Prince Ji of Boling became Grand Commandant; Prince Qian of Rencheng became Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; Hulu Guang became Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Emperor Xiaozhao's crown prince Bainian was made Prince of Leling Commandery.
entries.literal: On the yimao day, Minister over the Masses and Prince Guiyan of Pingqin was made Grand Tutor; Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery was made Chief Minister of the Secretariat; Grand Commandant Wei Can was made Grand Guardian; Chief Minister of the Secretariat Duan Shao was made Grand Marshal; Inspector of Feng Province Lou Rui was made Minister of Works; Grand Tutor and Prince Yan of Pingyang was made Grand Minister; Grand Guardian and Prince You of Pengcheng was made Grand Preceptor and Recorder of the Affairs of the Secretariat; Inspector of Ji Province and Prince Ji of Boling was made Grand Commandant; Director of the Secretariat and Prince Qian of Rencheng was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; Inspector of Bing Province Hulu Guang was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Emperor Xiaozhao's crown prince Bainian was enfeoffed as Prince of Leling Commandery.

entries.zh: 庚申，詔大使巡行天下，求政善惡，問人疾苦，擢進賢良。
entries.en: On gengshen, senior envoys were ordered to tour the realm, investigate good and bad government, ask after the people's suffering, and promote worthy talent.
entries.literal: On the gengshen day, an edict sent senior envoys to tour the realm, seek out what was good and bad in government, ask after the people's hardships, and promote the worthy and capable.

entries.zh: 是歲，周武帝保定元年。
entries.en: That year corresponded to the first year of Baoding under Emperor Wu of Zhou.
entries.literal: That year was the first year of Baoding under Emperor Wu of Zhou.

entries.zh: 河清元年春正月乙亥，車駕至自晉陽。
entries.en: In spring, in the first month of the first year of Heqing, on yihai, the emperor returned from Jinyang.
entries.literal: In spring, in the first month of the first year of Heqing, on the yihai day, the imperial carriage arrived back from Jinyang.

entries.zh: 辛巳，祀南郊。
entries.en: On xinsi, he performed the sacrifice at the Southern Suburb.
entries.literal: On the xinsi day, he sacrificed at the Southern Suburb.

entries.zh: 壬午，享太廟。
entries.en: On renwu, he offered sacrifice in the Grand Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: On the renwu day, he made offerings in the Grand Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 丙戌，立妃胡氏為皇后，子緯為皇太子。
entries.en: On bingxu, Consort Hu was made empress and his son Wei was made crown prince.
entries.literal: On the bingxu day, he established Consort Hu as empress and his son Wei as crown prince.

entries.zh: 大赦，內外百官普加汎級，諸為父後者賜爵一級。
entries.en: A general amnesty was proclaimed. Officials throughout the government were advanced in rank, and heirs carrying on their fathers' lines received one noble grade.
entries.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed; all officials inside and outside the court were broadly advanced in rank, and those serving as their fathers' successors were granted one noble grade.

entries.zh: 己亥，以前定州刺史、馮翊王潤為尚書左僕射。
entries.en: On jihai, Prince Run of Fengyi, formerly Inspector of Ding Province, was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: On the jihai day, the former Inspector of Ding Province, Prince Run of Fengyi, was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 詔斷屠殺以順春令。
entries.en: An edict forbade slaughter, in keeping with the spring ordinances.
entries.literal: An edict prohibited slaughter in order to accord with the ordinances of spring.

entries.zh: 秋九月乙丑，封皇子綽為南陽王，儼為東平王。
entries.en: In the ninth month of autumn, on the yichou day, the princes Chuo and Yan were enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang and Prince of Dongping, respectively.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of autumn, on the yichou day, the emperor's sons Chuo and Yan were enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang and Prince of Dongping, respectively.

entries.zh: 是月，歸閻媼于周。
entries.en: That month Lady Yan was returned to Northern Zhou.
entries.literal: That month, Lady Yan was sent back to Northern Zhou.

entries.zh: 陳人來聘。
entries.en: Envoys from Chen came on a diplomatic visit.
entries.literal: Envoys from Chen came on a mission of friendly inquiry.

entries.zh: 突厥寇幽州，入長城，虜掠而還。
entries.en: The Turks raided You Province, crossed the Great Wall, carried off plunder, and withdrew.
entries.literal: The Turks raided You Province, entered the Great Wall, plundered, and withdrew.

entries.zh: 十二月乙卯，豫州刺史王士良以城降周將權景宣。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Wang Shiliang, Inspector of Yu Province, surrendered his city to the Zhou general Quan Jingxuan.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on the yimao day, Wang Shiliang, Inspector of Yu Province, surrendered the city to the Zhou general Quan Jingxuan.

entries.zh: 丁巳，帝自晉陽南討。
entries.en: On dingsi, the emperor set out south from Jinyang on campaign.
entries.literal: On the dingsi day, the emperor went south from Jinyang to campaign.

entries.zh: 己未，太宰、平陽王淹薨。
entries.en: On jiwei, Prince Yan of Pingyang, the Grand Minister, died.
entries.literal: On the jiwei day, the Grand Minister, Prince Yan of Pingyang, died.

entries.zh: 壬戌，太師段韶大破尉遲迥等，解洛陽圍。
entries.en: On renxu, Grand Preceptor Duan Shao routed Yuchi Jiong and the others, relieving the siege of Luoyang.
entries.literal: On the renxu day, Grand Preceptor Duan Shao badly defeated Yuchi Jiong and the others, lifting the siege of Luoyang.

entries.zh: 丁卯，帝至洛陽，免洛州經周軍處一年租賦，赦州城內死罪已下囚。
entries.en: On dingmao, the emperor reached Luoyang. He remitted a year of taxes for the parts of Luo Province traversed by the Zhou army and pardoned prisoners in the provincial seat whose sentences were death or less.
entries.literal: On the dingmao day, the emperor arrived at Luoyang, remitted one year of rents and taxes for the places in Luo Province through which the Zhou army had passed, and pardoned prisoners in the provincial city sentenced to death or below.

entries.zh: 己巳，乙太師段韶為太宰，以司徒斛律光為太尉，幷州刺史蘭陵王長恭為尚書令。
entries.en: On jisi, Duan Shao was made Grand Minister, Hulu Guang was made Grand Commandant, and Prince Changgong of Lanling, Inspector of Bing Province, was made Chief Minister of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: On the jisi day, Grand Preceptor Duan Shao was made Grand Minister, Minister over the Masses Hulu Guang was made Grand Commandant, and Prince Changgong of Lanling, Inspector of Bing Province, was made Chief Minister of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 壬申，帝至武牢，經滑臺，次於黎陽，所經減降罪人。
entries.en: On renshen, the emperor reached Wulao, passed through Huatai, and stopped at Liyang, reducing punishments for offenders along his route.
entries.literal: On the renshen day, the emperor reached Wulao, passed through Huatai, and halted at Liyang; in the places he passed, he reduced the punishments of offenders.

entries.zh: 丙子，車駕至自洛陽。
entries.en: On bingzi, the emperor returned from Luoyang.
entries.literal: On the bingzi day, the imperial carriage arrived back from Luoyang.

entries.zh: 論曰：武成風度高爽，經算弘長，文武之官，俱盡其力，有帝王之量矣。
entries.en: The appraisal says: Wucheng had an elevated bearing and far-reaching strategic judgment. Civil and military officials alike gave him their full efforts, and he possessed the measure of an emperor.
entries.literal: The appraisal says: Wucheng's bearing was lofty and expansive, and his plans and calculations were broad and far-reaching; civil and military officials all exerted their full efforts for him, and he had the capacity of an emperor.

entries.zh: 但愛狎庸豎，委以朝權，帷薄之間，淫侈過度，滅亡之兆，其在斯乎？
entries.en: Yet he was intimate with base underlings and entrusted them with court power, while within the palace chambers his licentious extravagance exceeded all bounds. The signs of ruin lay precisely there, did they not?
entries.literal: Yet he loved and kept close company with mediocre underlings, entrusted them with power at court, and in the inner chambers indulged in licentious extravagance beyond measure; were the signs of destruction not here?

entries.zh: 玄象告變，傳位元子，名號雖殊，政猶己出，跡有虛飾，事非憲典，聰明臨下，何易可誣。
entries.en: Celestial signs announced change, so he passed the throne to his eldest son. The title changed, but government still came from him; the act was empty ornament, not proper precedent. With Heaven watching clearly from above, it could hardly be deceived.
entries.literal: The dark celestial signs announced change, and he transmitted the throne to his eldest son; although the title and name were different, government still issued from himself. The act had empty ornament and was not in accord with constitutional precedent; with Heaven's clear intelligence looking down below, it could hardly be deceived.

entries.zh: 又河南、河間、樂陵等諸王，或以時嫌，或以猜忌，皆無罪而殞，非所謂知命任天道之義也。
entries.en: Moreover, the princes of Henan, Hejian, Leling, and others all died guiltless, some from the suspicions of the moment and some from jealous fear. This was hardly the meaning of knowing the mandate and yielding to the Way of Heaven.
entries.literal: Moreover, the princes of Henan, Hejian, Leling, and the others, some because of suspicion at the time and others because of jealous mistrust, all died without guilt; this was not what is meant by knowing the mandate and entrusting oneself to the Way of Heaven.

entries.zh: 二年春正月乙亥，帝詔臨朝堂策試秀才。
entries.en: In the second year, on the yihai day of the first month of spring, the emperor issued an edict for a court examination of xiucai scholars in the hall of audience.
entries.literal: In the second year, in the first month of spring, on the yihai day, the Emperor issued an edict for a court examination of xiucai scholars in the hall of audience.

entries.zh: 以太子少傅魏收為兼尚書右僕射。
entries.en: Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Wei Shou was made Concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince Wei Shou was appointed Concurrent Right Deputy Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 己卯，兼右僕射魏收以阿縱除名。
entries.en: On the jimao day, Concurrent Right Vice Director Wei Shou was dismissed from office for fawning and indulgence.
entries.literal: On the jimao day, Concurrent Right Deputy Director Wei Shou was dismissed from office for fawning and indulgence.

entries.zh: 丁丑，以武明皇后配祭北郊。
entries.en: On the dingchou day, Empress Wuming was given paired sacrifice at the Northern Suburban Altar.
entries.literal: On the dingchou day, Empress Wuming was given paired sacrifice at the Northern Suburban Altar.

entries.zh: 辛卯，帝臨都亭錄見囚，降在京罪人各有差。
entries.en: On the xinmao day, the emperor went to the Capital Pavilion to review prisoners and reduced the sentences of criminals in the capital, each according to the circumstances of his case.
entries.literal: On the xinmao day, the Emperor went to the Capital Pavilion to review prisoners brought before him, and reduced the sentences of criminals in the capital, each according to his case.

entries.zh: 三年春正月庚申朔，周軍至城下而陳，戰於城西。
entries.en: In spring of the third year, on the gengshen day—the first of the month—the Northern Zhou army reached the walls, drew up in battle order, and fought west of the city.
entries.literal: In spring of the third year, on the gengshen day, the new moon, the Northern Zhou army reached below the city walls and deployed in battle order; they fought west of the city.

entries.zh: 周軍及突厥大敗，人畜死者相枕，數百里不絕。
entries.en: The Northern Zhou army and the Turks were routed; the dead, both men and livestock, lay heaped together for hundreds of li without a break.
entries.literal: The Northern Zhou army and the Turks were utterly defeated; dead men and livestock lay piled one upon another for hundreds of li without end.

entries.zh: 詔平原王段韶追出塞而還。
entries.en: An edict ordered Prince Duan Shao of Pingyuan to pursue the enemy beyond the border and then withdraw.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Prince Duan Shao of Pingyuan to pursue them beyond the frontier and then return.

entries.zh: 四年春正月癸卯，以大將軍、任城王湝為大司馬。
entries.en: In spring of the fourth year, on the guimao day of the first month, Grand General Prince Jun of Rencheng was appointed grand marshal.
entries.literal: In spring of the fourth year, on the guimao day of the first month, Grand General Prince Cheng of Rencheng was made grand marshal.

entries.zh: 辛未，幸晉陽。
entries.en: On the xinwei day, the emperor went on an imperial progress to Jinyang.
entries.literal: On the xinwei day, the emperor went on an imperial progress to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 夏四月辛丑，皇太后婁氏崩。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on the xinchou day, Empress Dowager Lou died.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the xinchou day, Empress Dowager Lou died.

entries.zh: 乙巳，青州刺史上言，今月庚寅河、濟清。
entries.en: On the yisi day, the Inspector of Qing Province reported that on the gengyin day of that month the Yellow and Ji Rivers had run clear.
entries.literal: On the yisi day, the Inspector of Qing Province memorialized that on the gengyin day of this month the Yellow and Ji Rivers had cleared.

entries.zh: 以河、濟清，改大寧二年為河清，降罪人各有差。
entries.en: Because the Yellow and Ji Rivers had cleared, the second year of Daning was renamed Heqing, and sentences of criminals were reduced, each according to the circumstances of his case.
entries.literal: Because the Yellow and Ji Rivers had cleared, the second year of Daning was renamed Heqing, and criminals' sentences were reduced, each according to his case.

entries.zh: 五月甲申，祔葬武明皇后於義平陵。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on the jiashen day, Empress Wuming was jointly entombed at Yiping Mausoleum.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on the jiashen day, Empress Wuming was jointly entombed at Yiping Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 己丑，以尚書右僕射斛律光為尚書令。
entries.en: On the jichou day, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Hulu Guang was made Chief Minister of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: On the jichou day, Right Deputy Director of the Secretariat Hulu Guang was appointed Chief Minister of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 神武明皇后婁氏，諱昭君，贈司徒內干之女也。
entries.en: Empress Ming, née Lou, whose personal name was Zhaojun, was the daughter of Neigan, posthumously appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Empress Ming, Lady Lou, taboo name Zhaojun, was the daughter of Neigan, posthumously appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 少明悟，強族多聘之，並不肯行。
entries.en: From girlhood she was bright and perceptive. Powerful clans sought her hand again and again, yet she would not consent.
entries.literal: From youth she was bright and perceptive; powerful clans sought her in marriage many times, yet she would not go.

entries.zh: 及見神武於城上執役，驚曰：「此真吾夫也。」
entries.en: When she saw Gao Huan laboring on the city wall, she started and said, "This is truly my husband."
entries.literal: When she saw Shenwu performing labor on the city wall, she was startled and said: "This is truly my husband."

entries.zh: 乃使婢通意，又數致私財，使以聘己，父母不得已而許焉。
entries.en: She sent a maid to convey her feelings and repeatedly sent private funds so that he might betroth her; her parents, having no choice, consented.
entries.literal: She then sent a maid to convey her feelings, and repeatedly sent private funds so that he might betroth her; her parents, having no choice, consented.

entries.zh: 神武既有澄清之志，傾產以結英豪，密謀秘策，后恒參預。
entries.en: Once Gao Huan resolved to restore order, he spent his estate to win over heroes; in secret plots and hidden stratagems Empress Lou always took part.
entries.literal: Once Shenwu had the will to restore order, he spent his estate to win over heroes; in secret plots and hidden stratagems the empress always took part.

entries.zh: 及拜渤海王妃，閫闈之事悉決焉。
entries.en: When she was enfeoffed Princess Consort of Bohai, all affairs of the inner quarters were decided by her.
entries.literal: When he was enfeoffed Princess Consort of Bohai, all affairs of the inner quarters were decided by her.

entries.zh: 神武婁后
entries.en: Empress Lou of Shenwu
entries.literal: Empress Lou of Shenwu

entries.zh: 后高明嚴斷，雅遵儉約，往來外舍，侍從不過十人。
entries.en: The empress was lofty in judgment, clear-minded, and stern; she always observed thrift, and when she went out to external residences her attendants never exceeded ten.
entries.literal: The empress was lofty, clear, and stern in judgment; she always observed thrift; when going out to external residences, her attendants never exceeded ten.

entries.zh: 性寬厚，不妒忌，神武姬侍，咸加恩待。
entries.en: Her nature was generous and free of jealousy; Gao Huan's concubines and attendants she treated with equal favor.
entries.literal: Her nature was generous and she was not jealous; Shenwu's concubines and attendants she all treated with favor.

entries.zh: 神武嘗將西討出師，後夜孿生一男一女，左右以危急，請追告神武。
entries.en: Once, as Gao Huan was about to march west on campaign, the empress gave birth at night to twins, a boy and a girl. Those beside her, finding the situation perilous, asked to send word after him.
entries.literal: Once when Shenwu was about to march west on campaign, the empress at night bore twins, a boy and a girl; those beside her, finding the situation perilous, asked to send word after Shenwu.

entries.zh: 后弗聽曰：「王出統大兵，何得以我故輕離軍幕。
entries.en: The empress would not hear of it. "The king has gone forth to command a great army," she said. "He cannot lightly leave the command tent on my account.
entries.literal: The empress would not listen and said: "The king has gone forth to command a great army — how can he lightly leave the command tent on my account.

entries.zh: 死生命也，來復何為！」
entries.en: Life and death are fate — what use is it if he comes back!"
entries.literal: Life and death are fate — what use is it if he comes back!"

entries.zh: 神武聞之，嗟歎良久。
entries.en: When Gao Huan heard of it, he sighed in admiration for a long while.
entries.literal: When Shenwu heard of it, he sighed in admiration for a long while.

entries.zh: 沙苑敗後，侯景屢言請精騎二萬，必能取之。
entries.en: After the defeat at Shaya, Hou Jing repeatedly asked for twenty thousand picked cavalry, saying he could certainly recover the lost ground.
entries.literal: After the defeat at Shaya, Hou Jing repeatedly asked for twenty thousand picked cavalry, saying he could certainly recover it.

entries.zh: 神武悅，以告于后。
entries.en: Gao Huan was pleased and told the empress.
entries.literal: Shenwu was pleased and told the empress.

entries.zh: 后曰：「若如其言，豈有還理，得獺失景，亦有何利。」
entries.en: The empress said, "If things go as he promises, there would be no reason for him to return. You would gain some paltry conquest and lose Hou Jing; there would be no profit in that."
entries.literal: The empress said: "If it comes about as he says, could there be any coming back — gain the otter, lose Jing; what profit is there."

entries.zh: 乃止。
entries.en: Thereupon he desisted.
entries.literal: Thereupon he desisted.

entries.zh: 神武逼於茹茹，欲娶其女而未決。
entries.en: Gao Huan, pressed by the Rouran, wished to marry their princess but had not yet decided.
entries.literal: Shenwu, pressed by the Rouran, wished to marry their princess but had not yet decided.

entries.zh: 后曰：「國家大計，願不疑也。」
entries.en: The empress said, "This is a great plan for the state — do not hesitate."
entries.literal: The empress said: "This is a great plan for the state — do not hesitate."

entries.zh: 及茹茹公主至，后避正室處之。
entries.en: When the Rouran princess arrived, the empress vacated the main chamber to lodge her.
entries.literal: When the Rouran princess arrived, the empress vacated the main chamber to lodge her.

entries.zh: 神武愧而拜謝焉，曰：「彼將有覺，願絕勿顧。」
entries.en: Gao Huan, ashamed, bowed and apologized to her, saying, "She will notice — please sever all ties and do not look back."
entries.literal: Shenwu, ashamed, bowed and apologized to her, saying: "She will notice — please sever all ties and do not look back."

entries.zh: 慈愛諸子，不異己出，躬自紡績，人賜一袍一袴。
entries.en: She loved all the sons as if they were her own; she personally spun and wove, giving each man one robe and one pair of trousers.
entries.literal: She loved all the sons as if they were her own; she personally spun and wove, giving each man one robe and one pair of trousers.

entries.zh: 手縫戎服，以帥左右。
entries.en: With her own hands she sewed military garments to set an example for those beside her.
entries.literal: With her own hands she sewed military garments to lead those beside her.

entries.zh: 弟昭，以功名自達，其餘親屬，未嘗為請爵位。
entries.en: Her younger brother Zhao attained distinction through merit; as for the rest of her kin, she never once asked for noble rank on their behalf.
entries.literal: Her younger brother Zhao attained distinction through merit; as for the rest of her kin, she never once asked for noble rank on their behalf.

entries.zh: 每言有材當用，義不以私亂公。
entries.en: She always said that talent should be employed when found, and that righteousness must not let private feeling disorder public duty.
entries.literal: She always said that talent should be employed when found, and that righteousness must not let private feeling disorder public duty.

entries.zh: 文襄嗣位，進為太妃。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng succeeded to the throne, she was advanced to Grand Consort.
entries.literal: When Wenxiang succeeded to the throne, she was advanced to Grand Consort.

entries.zh: 文宣將受魏禪，后固執不許，帝所以中止。
entries.en: When Gao Yang was about to receive the Wei abdication, the empress firmly refused to permit it, and the emperor therefore desisted.
entries.literal: When Wenxuan was about to receive the Wei abdication, the empress firmly refused to permit it, and the emperor therefore desisted.

entries.zh: 天保初，尊為皇太后，宮曰宣訓。
entries.en: At the opening of the Tianbao era, she was honored as Empress Dowager; her palace was named Xuanxun.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, she was honored as Empress Dowager; her palace was named Xuanxun.

entries.zh: 濟南即位，尊為太皇太后。
entries.en: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 尚書令楊愔等受遺詔輔政，疏忌諸王。
entries.en: Chief Minister Yang Yin and others received the testamentary edict to assist in government and kept the princes at a distance in suspicion.
entries.literal: Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing Yang Yin and others received the testamentary edict to assist in government and kept the princes at a distance in suspicion.

entries.zh: 太皇太后密與孝昭及諸大將定策誅之，下令廢立。
entries.en: The Grand Empress Dowager secretly joined Gao Yan and the great generals in fixing a plan to execute them, and issued an edict deposing one ruler and enthroning another.
entries.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager secretly joined Xiaozhao and the great generals in fixing a plan to execute them, and issued an edict deposing and enthroning.

entries.zh: 孝昭即位，復為皇太后。
entries.en: When Gao Yan succeeded, she again became Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: When Xiaozhao succeeded, she again became Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 孝昭帝崩，太后又下詔立武成帝。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, the empress dowager again issued an edict enthroning Emperor Wucheng.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, the empress dowager again issued an edict enthroning Emperor Wucheng.

entries.zh: 大寧二年春，太后寢疾，衣忽自舉，用巫媼言改姓石氏。
entries.en: In the spring of the second year of Daning, the empress dowager fell ill; her garments suddenly lifted of themselves, and following a sorceress's words she changed her surname to Shi.
entries.literal: In the spring of the second year of Daning, the empress dowager fell ill; her garments suddenly lifted of themselves, and following a sorceress's words she changed her surname to Shi.

entries.zh: 四月辛丑，崩於北宮，時年六十二。
entries.en: On the xinchou day of the fourth month she died at the Northern Palace, aged sixty-two.
entries.literal: On the xinchou day of the fourth month she died at the Northern Palace, aged sixty-two.

entries.zh: 五月甲申，合葬義平陵。
entries.en: On the jiashen day of the fifth month she was interred with Gao Huan at Yiping Tomb.
entries.literal: On the jiashen day of the fifth month she was interred with Shenwu at Yiping Tomb.

entries.zh: 太后凡孕六男二女，皆感夢：孕文襄則夢一斷龍；
entries.en: The empress dowager in all bore six sons and two daughters, each pregnancy attended by a dream: when she conceived Gao Cheng she dreamed of a severed dragon;
entries.literal: The empress dowager in all bore six sons and two daughters, each pregnancy attended by a dream: when she conceived Wenxiang she dreamed of a severed dragon;

entries.zh: 孕文宣則夢大龍，首尾屬天地，張口動目，勢狀驚人；
entries.en: when she conceived Gao Yang she dreamed of a great dragon whose head and tail joined heaven and earth, mouth open and eyes moving, its aspect terrifying;
entries.literal: when she conceived Wenxuan she dreamed of a great dragon whose head and tail joined heaven and earth, mouth open and eyes moving, its aspect terrifying;

entries.zh: 孕孝昭則夢蠕龍於地；
entries.en: when she conceived Gao Yan she dreamed of a writhing dragon upon the ground;
entries.literal: when she conceived Xiaozhao she dreamed of a writhing dragon upon the ground;

entries.zh: 孕武成則夢龍浴於海；
entries.en: when she conceived Gao Zhan she dreamed of a dragon bathing in the sea;
entries.literal: when she conceived Wucheng she dreamed of a dragon bathing in the sea;

entries.zh: 孕魏二后並夢月入懷；
entries.en: when she conceived the two Wei empresses she both dreamed of the moon entering the bosom;
entries.literal: when she conceived the two Wei empresses she both dreamed of the moon entering the bosom;

entries.zh: 孕襄城、博陵二王夢鼠入衣下。
entries.en: when she conceived the Princes of Xiangcheng and Boling she dreamed of rats entering beneath the garments.
entries.literal: when she conceived the Princes of Xiangcheng and Boling she dreamed of rats entering beneath the garments.

entries.zh: 后未崩，有童謠曰「九龍母死不作孝」。
entries.en: Before the empress dowager died, a children's rhyme ran: "Nine dragons — when the mother dies, no mourning."
entries.literal: Before the empress dowager died, a children's rhyme said: "Nine dragons — when the mother dies, no mourning."

entries.zh: 及后崩，武成不改服，緋袍如故。
entries.en: When the empress dowager died, Wucheng did not change his garments and kept his crimson robe as before.
entries.literal: When the empress dowager died, Wucheng did not change his garments and kept his crimson robe as before.

entries.zh: 未幾，登三臺，置酒作樂。
entries.en: Before long he ascended the Three Towers, set out wine, and made music.
entries.literal: Before long he ascended the Three Towers, set out wine, and made music.

entries.zh: 帝女進白袍，帝怒，投諸臺下。
entries.en: The emperor's daughter brought a white robe; the emperor was angry and cast it down from the tower.
entries.literal: The emperor's daughter brought a white robe; the emperor was angry and cast it down from the tower.

entries.zh: 和士開請止樂，帝大怒，撻之。
entries.en: He Shikai asked that the music be stopped; the emperor was greatly angered and beat him.
entries.literal: He Shikai asked that the music be stopped; the emperor was greatly angered and beat him.

entries.zh: 帝於昆季次實九，蓋其徵驗也。
entries.en: The emperor among his brothers by birth was actually ninth — surely this was the omen's fulfillment.
entries.literal: The emperor among his brothers by birth was actually ninth — surely this was the omen's fulfillment.

entries.zh: 論曰：神武肇興齊業，武明追蹤周亂。
entries.en: The appraisal says: Shenwu founded Qi's enterprise, but Wuming followed the path of Zhou's disorder.
entries.literal: The appraisal says: Shenwu first raised the enterprise of Qi, but Wuming followed the track of Zhou's disorder.

entries.zh: 溫公之敗邦家，馮妃比跡褒後。
entries.en: Duke Wen's ruin of state and family, and Consort Feng's likeness to Empress Bao, show the pattern.
entries.literal: Duke Wen's ruin of state and house, and Consort Feng matching the traces of Empress Bao, show the pattern.

entries.zh: 然則汙隆之義，蓋有系焉。
entries.en: Thus rise and decline surely have their causes.
entries.literal: Thus the principle of decline and flourishing surely has something on which it depends.

entries.zh: 其餘作孽為眚，外平內蠹，鑒之近代，于齊為甚。
entries.en: As for the rest, their wrongdoing became disaster: outward peace, inward rot. Among recent dynasties, Qi was the worst example.
entries.literal: As for the rest, they made evil and became calamity; outwardly there was peace, inwardly decay. Looking at recent ages, in Qi this was most extreme.

entries.zh: 文襄元后
entries.en: Empress Yuan of Wenxiang
entries.literal: Empress Yuan of Wenxiang

entries.zh: 文襄敬皇后元氏，魏孝靜帝之姊也。
entries.en: Reverent Empress Yuan of Wenxiang was the elder sister of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei.
entries.literal: Reverent Empress Yuan of Wenxiang was the elder sister of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei.

entries.zh: 孝武帝時，封馮翊公主而歸於文襄。
entries.en: In the time of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei she was enfeoffed Princess of Fengyi and given in marriage to Gao Cheng.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei she was enfeoffed Princess of Fengyi and given in marriage to Wenxiang.

entries.zh: 容德兼美，曲盡和敬。
entries.en: Her bearing and virtue were both beautiful; in harmony and reverence she exhausted every measure.
entries.literal: Her bearing and virtue were both beautiful; in harmony and reverence she exhausted every measure.

entries.zh: 初生河間王孝琬，時文襄為世子，三日而孝靜帝幸世子第，贈錦彩及布帛萬匹。
entries.en: When she first bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian, Gao Cheng was then heir; on the third day Emperor Xiaojing visited the heir's residence and bestowed brocades, silks, and cloth in ten thousand bolts.
entries.literal: When she first bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian, Wenxiang was then heir; on the third day Emperor Xiaojing visited the heir's residence and bestowed brocades, silks, and cloth in ten thousand bolts.

entries.zh: 世子辭，求通受諸貴禮遺，於是十屋皆滿。
entries.en: The heir declined and asked instead to receive the gifts and presents of the nobles; thereupon ten rooms were filled.
entries.literal: The heir declined and asked instead to receive the gifts and presents of the nobles; thereupon ten rooms were filled.

entries.zh: 次生兩公主。
entries.en: Next she bore two princesses.
entries.literal: Next she bore two princesses.

entries.zh: 文宣受禪，尊為文襄皇后，居靜德宮。
entries.en: When Gao Yang received the abdication, she was honored as Empress of Wenxiang and dwelt in Jingde Palace.
entries.literal: When Wenxuan received the abdication, she was honored as Empress of Wenxiang and dwelt in Jingde Palace.

entries.zh: 及天保六年，文宣漸致昏狂，乃移居于高陽之宅，而取其府庫，曰：「吾兄昔奸我婦，我今須報。」
entries.en: By the sixth year of Tianbao, Gao Yang gradually fell into madness; he then moved her to a residence at Gaoyang and seized her storehouses, saying, "My elder brother once violated my wife — now I must repay him."
entries.literal: By the sixth year of Tianbao, Wenxuan gradually fell into madness; he then moved her to a residence at Gaoyang and took her storehouses, saying: "My elder brother once violated my wife — now I must repay him."

entries.zh: 乃淫於后。
entries.en: Thereupon he violated the empress.
entries.literal: Thereupon he violated the empress.

entries.zh: 其高氏女婦無親疏，皆使左右亂交之於前。
entries.en: Every woman of the Gao clan, close or distant in kinship, he had those beside him violate in turn before her.
entries.literal: Every woman of the Gao clan, close or distant in kinship, he had those beside him violate in turn before her.

entries.zh: 以葛為絙，令魏安德主騎上，使人推引之，又命胡人苦辱之。
entries.en: He made a rope of hemp and had Princess Andrade of Wei mount it, with men pushing and pulling her; he also ordered barbarians to humiliate her cruelly.
entries.literal: He made a rope of hemp and had Princess Andrade of Wei mount it, with men pushing and pulling her; he also ordered barbarians to humiliate her cruelly.

entries.zh: 帝又自呈露，以示群下。
entries.en: The emperor also exposed himself and displayed his nakedness before the assembled officials.
entries.literal: The emperor also exposed himself and showed himself to the assembled officials.

entries.zh: 武平中，后崩，祔葬義平陵。
entries.en: In the Wuping era the empress died and was given joint burial at Yiping Tomb.
entries.literal: In the Wuping era the empress died and was given joint burial at Yiping Tomb.

entries.zh: 武成皇后胡氏，安定胡延之女。
entries.en: Empress Hu of Wucheng was the daughter of Hu Yan of Anding.
entries.literal: Empress Hu of Wucheng was the daughter of Hu Yan of Anding.

entries.zh: 其母范陽盧道約女，初懷孕，有胡僧詣門曰：「此宅瓠蘆中有月」，既而生后。
entries.en: Her mother was a daughter of Lu Daoyue of Fanyang; when she first conceived, a barbarian monk came to the gate and said, "In this house's gourd-reeds there is a moon"; thereupon the empress was born.
entries.literal: Her mother was a daughter of Lu Daoyue of Fanyang; when she first conceived, a barbarian monk came to the gate and said: "In this house's gourd-reeds there is a moon"; thereupon the empress was born.

entries.zh: 天保初，選為長廣王妃。
entries.en: At the opening of the Tianbao era she was selected as Princess Consort of Changguang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao she was selected as Princess Consort of Changguang.

entries.zh: 產後主日，號鳴於產帳上。
entries.en: On the day she bore the Last Emperor, a bird cried above the birthing pavilion.
entries.literal: On the day she bore the Last Emperor, a bird cried above the birthing pavilion.

entries.zh: 武成崩，尊為皇太后，陸媼及和士開密謀殺趙郡王叡，出婁定遠、高文遙為刺史。
entries.en: When Wucheng died she was honored as Empress Dowager; Nurse Lu and He Shikai secretly plotted to kill Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery and sent out Lou Dingyuan and Gao Wenyao as governors.
entries.literal: When Wucheng died she was honored as Empress Dowager; Nurse Lu and He Shikai secretly plotted to kill Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery and sent out Lou Dingyuan and Gao Wenyao as governors.

entries.zh: 和、陸諂事太后，無所不至。
entries.en: He and Lu fawned upon the empress dowager to every extreme.
entries.literal: He and Lu fawned upon the empress dowager to every extreme.

entries.zh: 初武成時，後與諸閹人褻狎。
entries.en: In Wucheng's time the empress had been familiar with the eunuchs.
entries.literal: In Wucheng's time the empress had been familiar with the eunuchs.

entries.zh: 武成寵倖和士開，每與后握槊，因此與后姦通。
entries.en: Wucheng favored He Shikai; he often played polo with the empress, and through this came to commit adultery with her.
entries.literal: Wucheng favored He Shikai; he often played polo with the empress, and through this came to commit adultery with her.

entries.zh: 自武成崩後，數出詣佛寺，又與沙門曇獻通。
entries.en: After Wucheng's death she often went out to Buddhist temples, and again had relations with the monk Tanxian.
entries.literal: After Wucheng's death she often went out to Buddhist temples, and again had relations with the monk Tanxian.

entries.zh: 布金錢於獻席下，又挂寶裝胡床於獻屋壁，武成平生之所御也。
entries.en: She spread gold coins beneath Tanxian's mat and hung upon the wall of Tanxian's room a precious decorated barbarian couch that Wucheng had used in life.
entries.literal: She spread gold coins beneath Tanxian's mat and hung upon the wall of Tanxian's room a precious decorated barbarian couch that Wucheng had used in life.

entries.zh: 乃置百僧於內殿，托以聽講，日夜與曇獻寢處。
entries.en: She then placed a hundred monks in the inner hall, using the pretext of listening to lectures, and day and night shared Tanxian's bed.
entries.literal: She then placed a hundred monks in the inner hall, using the pretext of listening to lectures, and day and night shared Tanxian's bed.

entries.zh: 以獻為昭玄統。
entries.en: She made Tanxian Director of Buddhist Affairs.
entries.literal: She made Tanxian Director of Buddhist Affairs.

entries.zh: 僧徒遙指太后以弄曇獻，乃至謂之為太上者。
entries.en: Monks from afar pointed at the empress dowager while jesting with Tanxian, even calling her the Grand Sovereign.
entries.literal: Monks from afar pointed at the empress dowager while jesting with Tanxian, even calling her the Grand Sovereign.

entries.zh: 帝聞太后不謹而未之信，後朝太后，見二少尼，悅而召之，乃男子也，於是曇獻事亦發，皆伏法，並殺元、山、王三郡君，皆太后之所昵也。
entries.en: The emperor heard that the empress dowager was unrestrained but did not yet believe it; later, attending upon the empress dowager at court, he saw two young nuns, was pleased and summoned them — they were men; thereupon Tanxian's affair also came to light; all were executed by law, and the three Ladies of Yuan, Shan, and Wang were also killed — all were favorites of the empress dowager.
entries.literal: The emperor heard that the empress dowager was unrestrained but did not yet believe it; later, attending upon the empress dowager at court, he saw two young nuns, was pleased and summoned them — they were men; thereupon Tanxian's affair also came to light; all were executed by law, and the three Ladies of Yuan, Shan, and Wang were also killed — all were favorites of the empress dowager.

entries.zh: 帝自晉陽奉太后還鄴，至紫陌，卒遇大風。
entries.en: The emperor himself escorted the empress dowager from Jinyang back to Ye; at Zimo they suddenly encountered a great wind.
entries.literal: The emperor himself escorted the empress dowager from Jinyang back to Ye; at Zimo they suddenly encountered a great wind.

entries.zh: 舍人魏僧伽明風角，奏言即時當有暴逆事。
entries.en: Attendant Wei Sengqie, skilled in wind augury, reported that treason was imminent.
entries.literal: Attendant Wei Sengqie understood wind augury and memorialized that an act of violent treason was about to occur at once.

entries.zh: 帝詐云鄴中有急，彎弓緾槊，馳入南城，令鄧長顒幽太后北宮，仍有敕內外諸親一不得與太后相見。
entries.en: The emperor feigned an emergency in Ye, strung his bow and wrapped his spear, galloped into the southern city, and ordered Deng Changyang to confine the Empress Dowager in the Northern Palace, with an edict forbidding all kin, near or distant, from seeing her.
entries.literal: The emperor pretended there was an emergency in Ye, strung his bow and wrapped his spear-shaft, galloped into the southern city, ordered Deng Changyang to confine the Empress Dowager in the Northern Palace, and issued an edict that none of the inner or outer kin might see the Empress Dowager on any account.

entries.zh: 久之，帝復迎太后。
entries.en: After some time the emperor welcomed the Empress Dowager back.
entries.literal: After some time, the emperor welcomed the Empress Dowager back.

entries.zh: 太后初聞使者至，大驚，慮有不測。
entries.en: When the Empress Dowager first heard that an envoy had come, she was terrified, fearing the worst.
entries.literal: When the Empress Dowager first heard that an envoy had arrived, she was greatly alarmed, fearing something unforeseen.

entries.zh: 每太后設食，帝亦不敢嘗。
entries.en: Whenever the Empress Dowager set out a meal, the emperor dared not taste it.
entries.literal: Whenever the Empress Dowager set out food, the emperor would not dare to taste it.

entries.zh: 周使元偉來聘，作《述行賦》，敘鄭莊公克段而遷姜氏，文雖不工，當時深以為愧。
entries.en: Yuan Wei, an envoy from Zhou, came on a diplomatic visit and composed the "Rhapsody on a Journey," recounting how Duke Zhuang of Zheng crushed his brother Duan and banished their mother Lady Jiang; though the prose was crude, the court felt deeply shamed.
entries.literal: An envoy from Zhou, Yuan Wei, came on a diplomatic mission and composed the "Rhapsody on a Journey," recounting Duke Zhuang of Zheng's suppression of Duan and removal of Lady Jiang; though the writing was not polished, people at the time felt deeply shamed by it.

entries.zh: 齊亡入周，恣行姦穢。
entries.en: When Qi fell she entered Zhou and gave herself over to debauchery.
entries.literal: When Qi fell, she entered Zhou and gave free rein to lewd conduct.

entries.zh: 隋開皇中殂。
entries.en: She died during the Kaihuang era of Sui.
entries.literal: She died during the Kaihuang era of Sui.

entries.zh: 文宣皇后李氏，諱祖娥，趙郡李希宗女也。
entries.en: Empress Li of Wenxuan, whose personal name was Zu'e, was the daughter of Li Xizong of Zhao Commandery.
entries.literal: Empress Li of Wenxuan, taboo name Zu'e, was the daughter of Li Xizong of Zhao Commandery.

entries.zh: 容德甚美。
entries.en: Her bearing and virtue were exceedingly beautiful.
entries.literal: Her bearing and virtue were exceedingly beautiful.

entries.zh: 初為太原公夫人。
entries.en: At first she was Lady of the Duke of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: At first she was Lady of the Duke of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 及帝將建中宮，高隆之、高德正言漢婦人不可為天下母，宜更擇美配。
entries.en: When the emperor was about to establish the central palace, Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng said a Han woman could not be mother to the realm and that a more beautiful match should be chosen.
entries.literal: When the emperor was about to establish the central palace, Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng said a Han woman could not be mother to the realm and that a more beautiful match should be chosen.

entries.zh: 楊愔固請依漢、魏故事，不改元妃。
