entries.en: Yang Yin firmly requested following the Han and Wei precedents and not changing the original consort.
entries.literal: Yang Yin firmly requested following the Han and Wei precedents and not changing the original consort.

entries.zh: 而德正猶固請廢后而立段昭儀，欲以結勳貴之援，帝竟不從而立后焉。
entries.en: Yet Dezheng still firmly asked to depose the empress and install Lady Duan as Honored Consort, wishing thereby to win the support of meritorious nobles; the emperor in the end did not follow him and established the empress.
entries.literal: Yet Dezheng still firmly asked to depose the empress and install Lady Duan as Honored Consort, wishing thereby to win the support of meritorious nobles; the emperor in the end did not follow him and established the empress.

entries.zh: 帝好捶撻嬪御，乃至有殺戮者，唯後后蒙禮敬。
entries.en: The emperor loved to beat and flog the palace women, even to the point of killing some; only toward Empress Li did he show ritual respect.
entries.literal: The emperor loved to beat and flog the palace women, even to the point of killing some; only toward Empress Li did he show ritual respect.

entries.zh: 天保十年，改為可賀敦皇后。
entries.en: In the tenth year of Tianbao she was renamed Khedun Empress.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao she was renamed Khedun Empress.

entries.zh: 孝昭即位，降居昭信宮，號昭信皇后。
entries.en: When Gao Yan succeeded, she was reduced to Zhaoxin Palace and styled Empress of Zhaoxin.
entries.literal: When Xiaozhao succeeded, she was reduced to Zhaoxin Palace and styled Empress of Zhaoxin.

entries.zh: 武成踐祚，逼后淫亂，云：「若不許，我當殺爾兒。」
entries.en: When Wucheng took the throne, he forced the empress into illicit relations, saying, "If you do not consent, I shall kill your son."
entries.literal: When Wucheng took the throne, he forced the empress into illicit relations, saying: "If you do not consent, I shall kill your son."

entries.zh: 后懼，從之。
entries.en: The empress, in fear, complied.
entries.literal: The empress, in fear, complied.

entries.zh: 後有娠，太原王紹德至閣，不得見，慍曰：「兒豈不知耶，姊姊腹大，故不見兒。」
entries.en: Later she became pregnant; Prince Shao of Taiyuan came to her gate but could not see her, and angrily said, "Does the boy not know? Mother's belly is great — that is why she will not see the boy."
entries.literal: Later she became pregnant; Prince Shao of Taiyuan came to her gate but could not see her, and angrily said: "Does the boy not know? My elder sister's belly is great — that is why she will not see the boy."

entries.zh: 後聞之，大慚，由是生女不舉。
entries.en: When the empress heard it, she was deeply ashamed; from this she bore daughters and did not rear them.
entries.literal: When the empress heard it, she was deeply ashamed; from this she bore daughters and did not rear them.

entries.zh: 帝橫刀詬曰：「爾殺我女，我何不殺爾兒！」
entries.en: The emperor drew his blade and cursed, saying, "You killed my daughter — why should I not kill your son!"
entries.literal: The emperor drew his blade and cursed, saying: "You killed my daughter — why should I not kill your son!"

entries.zh: 對后前築殺紹德。
entries.en: Before the empress he beat Shao to death.
entries.literal: Before the empress he beat Shao to death.

entries.zh: 后大哭，帝愈怒，裸后亂撾撻之，號天不已。
entries.en: The empress wept greatly; the emperor grew angrier still, stripped her naked, and beat her at random; she cried to heaven without cease.
entries.literal: The empress wept greatly; the emperor grew angrier still, stripped her naked, and beat her at random; she cried to heaven without cease.

entries.zh: 盛以絹囊，流血淋漉，投諸渠水，良久乃蘇，犢車載送妙勝尼寺。
entries.en: She was placed in a silk sack; blood dripped and soaked through; she was cast into the canal water; only after a long while did she revive, and an ox-cart carried her to Miaosheng Nunnery.
entries.literal: She was placed in a silk sack; blood dripped and soaked through; she was cast into the canal water; only after a long while did she revive, and an ox-cart carried her to Miaosheng Nunnery.

entries.zh: 后性愛佛法，因此為尼。
entries.en: The empress by nature loved the Buddhist Law; on this account she became a nun.
entries.literal: The empress by nature loved the Buddhist Law; on this account she became a nun.

entries.zh: 齊亡入關。
entries.en: When Qi fell she entered the Pass.
entries.literal: When Qi fell she entered the Pass.

entries.zh: 隋時得還趙郡。
entries.en: In the Sui era she was able to return to Zhao Commandery.
entries.literal: In the Sui era she was able to return to Zhao Commandery.

entries.zh: 孝昭皇后元氏，開府元蠻女也。
entries.en: Empress Yuan of Xiaozhao was the daughter of Yuan Man, a Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: Empress Yuan of Xiaozhao was the daughter of Yuan Man, a Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 初為常山王妃。
entries.en: At first she was Princess Consort of Changshan.
entries.literal: At first she was Princess Consort of Changshan.

entries.zh: 天保末，賜姓步六孤。
entries.en: At the end of the Tianbao era, she was granted the surname Buliugu.
entries.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, she was bestowed the surname Buliugu.

entries.zh: 孝昭即位，立為皇后。
entries.en: When Xiaozhao took the throne, she was installed as empress.
entries.literal: When Xiaozhao ascended the throne, she was installed as empress.

entries.zh: 帝崩，梓宮之鄴。
entries.en: When the emperor died, his coffin was taken to Ye.
entries.literal: When the emperor died, his coffin proceeded to Ye.

entries.zh: 始渡汾橋，武成聞后有奇藥，追索之不得，使閹人就車頓辱。
entries.en: As the procession first crossed the Fen Bridge, Wucheng heard that the empress possessed a wondrous medicine. When his pursuit failed to obtain it, he sent eunuchs to her carriage to subject her to gross humiliation.
entries.literal: When it first crossed the Fen Bridge, Wucheng heard that the empress had a wondrous medicine; he pursued and demanded it, but did not get it, and sent eunuchs to her carriage to humiliate her harshly.

entries.zh: 降居順成宮。
entries.en: She was demoted and made to live in Shuncheng Palace.
entries.literal: She was demoted to live in Shuncheng Palace.

entries.zh: 武成既殺樂陵王，元被閟隔，不得與家相知。
entries.en: After Wucheng killed the Prince of Leling, Empress Yuan was shut away in isolation and could no longer communicate with her family.
entries.literal: After Wucheng killed the Prince of Leling, Yuan was shut away and isolated, unable to communicate with her family.

entries.zh: 宮闈內忽有飛語，帝令檢推，得后父兄書信，元蠻由是坐免官。
entries.en: When rumors suddenly circulated inside the palace, the emperor ordered an investigation. Letters from the empress's father and brothers were found, and Yuan Man was dismissed from office for it.
entries.literal: Suddenly there was a rumor within the palace; the emperor ordered an investigation and obtained letters from the empress's father and brothers, and Yuan Man was implicated by this and dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 後以齊亡入周氏宮中。
entries.en: Later, after Qi fell, she entered the palace of the Zhou dynasty.
entries.literal: Later, when Qi fell, she entered the palace of the Zhou house.

entries.zh: 隋文帝作相，放還山東。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen of Sui was serving as chancellor, she was released and allowed to return east of the mountains.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as chancellor, she was released to return east of the mountains.

entries.zh: 後主皇后穆氏，名邪利，本斛律後從婢也。
entries.en: Empress Mu of Houzhu, named Yeli, had originally been an attendant in Empress Hulu's household.
entries.literal: Empress Mu of Houzhu, named Yeli, had originally been an attendant of Empress Hulu's household.

entries.zh: 母名輕霄，本穆子倫婢也，轉入侍中宋欽道家，姦私而生后，莫知氏族，或云后即欽道女子也。
entries.en: Her mother Qingxiao had been a maid to Muzilun, then entered the household of Attendant-in-Ordinary Song Qindao, where an illicit affair produced the future empress; her lineage was unknown, though some said she was Song Qindao's own daughter.
entries.literal: Her mother Qingxiao had been a maid to Muzilun, then entered the household of Attendant-in-Ordinary Song Qindao, where an illicit affair produced the future empress; her lineage was unknown, though some said the empress was Song Qindao's own daughter.

entries.zh: 小字黃花，後字舍利。
entries.en: Her pet name was Huanghua; later she was styled Sheli.
entries.literal: She was called Huanghua as a pet name and later styled Sheli.

entries.zh: 欽道婦妬，黥輕霄面為「宋 」字。
entries.en: Song Qindao's wife, in jealousy, branded Qingxiao's face with the character "Song."
entries.literal: Song Qindao's wife, jealous, branded Qingxiao's face with the character "Song."

entries.zh: 欽道伏誅，黃花因此入宮，有幸於後主，宮內稱為舍利太監。
entries.en: After Song was executed, Huanghua entered the palace by that connection, won Houzhu's favor, and was known within the inner quarters as Director Sheli.
entries.literal: After Song was executed, Huanghua entered the palace through that connection, won the Last Emperor's favor, and was known within the inner quarters as Director Sheli.

entries.zh: 女侍中陸太姬知其寵，養以為女，薦為弘德夫人。
entries.en: Lady Attendant Lu Taiji, knowing of her favor, adopted her as a daughter and recommended her as Lady of Hongde.
entries.literal: Lady Attendant Lu Taiji, aware of her favor, adopted her as a daughter and recommended her as Lady of Hongde.

entries.zh: 武平元年六月，生皇子恒。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the first year of the Wuping era she bore Prince Heng.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Wuping she gave birth to the prince Heng.

entries.zh: 於時後主未有儲嗣，陸陰結待，以監撫之任不可無主，時皇后斛律氏，丞相光之女也，慮其懷恨，先令母養之，立為皇太子。
entries.en: The emperor still had no heir; Lu maneuvered in secret, arguing that the regency could not stand empty—the reigning empress, Guang's daughter, might resent it—so she had the child raised by the empress and established as crown prince.
entries.literal: The emperor still had no heir; Lu maneuvered privately, arguing that the role of regent for the heir could not remain vacant—the reigning empress, Guang's daughter, might resent this—so she had the child raised by the empress and established as crown prince.

entries.zh: 陸以國姓之重，穆、陸相對，又奏賜姓穆氏。
entries.en: Lu cited the weight of the dynastic surname—Mu paired with Lu—and petitioned that she be granted the surname Mu.
entries.literal: Lu cited the weight of the dynastic surname: Mu paired with Lu, and petitioned that she be granted the surname Mu.

entries.zh: 胡庶人之廢也，陸有助焉，胡遂立為皇后，大赦。
entries.en: When Lady Hu was deposed, Lu had helped; Hu was then raised to empress and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: When the deposed Lady Hu was removed, Lu had helped; Hu was then raised to empress and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

entries.zh: 初，有折衝將軍元正烈於鄴城東水中得璽以獻，文曰「天王后璽」，蓋石氏所作。
entries.en: Earlier, Breakthrough General Yuan Zhenglie had retrieved a seal from the waters east of Ye inscribed "Seal of the Heaven-King's Consort"—said to be a relic of the Shi clan.
entries.literal: Earlier, Breakthrough General Yuan Zhenglie had retrieved a seal from the waters east of Ye bearing the inscription "Seal of the Heaven-King's Consort"—a Shi-clan artifact.

entries.zh: 詔書頒告，以為穆后之瑞焉。
entries.en: An edict proclaimed the find far and wide as an auspicious portent for Empress Mu.
entries.literal: An edict proclaimed this far and wide as an auspicious portent for Empress Mu.

entries.zh: 武成時，為胡后造真珠裙袴，所費不可稱計，被火所燒。
entries.en: Under Wucheng a pearl-embroidered skirt and trousers had been made for Empress Hu at immeasurable cost, only to be consumed by fire.
entries.literal: Under Wucheng a pearl-embroidered skirt and trousers had been made for Empress Hu at immeasurable cost; fire consumed them.

entries.zh: 後主既立穆皇后，復為營之。
entries.en: After Houzhu installed Empress Mu, such garments were commissioned again.
entries.literal: After Houzhu installed Empress Mu, such garments were commissioned again.

entries.zh: 屬周武遭太后喪，詔侍中薛孤、康買等為弔使，又遣商胡齎錦彩三萬疋與使同往，欲市真珠為皇后造七寶車，周人不與交易，然而竟造焉。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu of Zhou was in mourning for his mother, envoys Xue Gu and Kang Mai were sent as condolence missions; merchant envoys carried thirty thousand bolts of brocade to buy pearls for a seven-treasure carriage for the empress—the Zhou people refused to trade, yet the carriage was built anyway.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou was mourning his mother, envoys Xue Gu and Kang Mai were sent as condolence missions; merchant envoys carried thirty thousand bolts of brocade to buy pearls for a seven-treasure carriage for the empress—the Zhou people refused trade, yet the carriage was built anyway.

entries.zh: 先是童謠曰：「黃華勢欲落，清觴滿杯酌。」
entries.en: A children's rhyme had run: "Yellow blossom's vigor will fade; brim the clear cup and pour."
entries.literal: A children's rhyme had run: "Yellow blossom's vigor will fade; brim the clear cup and pour."

entries.zh: 言黃花不久也，後主自立穆后以後，昏飲無度，故云清觴滿杯酌。
entries.en: It meant Huanghua would not endure; after Houzhu made Mu empress, he drank without measure—hence "brim the clear cup and pour."
entries.literal: It meant Huanghua would not last long; after Houzhu made Mu empress, he drank without measure—hence "brim the clear cup and pour."

entries.zh: 陸息駱提婆詔改姓為穆，陸。
entries.en: Lu ordered Mu Tipo by edict to take the surnames Mu and Lu.
entries.literal: Lu ordered Mu Tipo by edict to change his surname to Mu, Lu.

entries.zh: 太姬，皆以皇后故也。
entries.en: Taiji too—all on account of the empress.
entries.literal: Taiji—all on account of the empress.

entries.zh: 后既以陸為母，提婆為家，更不采輕霄。
entries.en: Having taken Lu as her mother and Tipo as her kin, the empress no longer acknowledged Qingxiao.
entries.literal: Having taken Lu as her mother and Tipo as her family, the empress no longer acknowledged Qingxiao.

entries.zh: 輕霄後自療面，欲求見，太后、陸媼使禁掌之，竟不得見。
entries.en: Qingxiao later healed her face and sought to see her daughter; the Empress Dowager and Lu Aun had her imprisoned, and she never gained an audience.
entries.literal: Qingxiao later healed her face and sought to see her daughter; the Empress Dowager and Lu Aun had her imprisoned and she never gained an audience.

entries.zh: 孝昭元后
entries.en: Empress Yuan of Xiaozhao
entries.literal: Empress Yuan of Xiaozhao

entries.zh: 高祖十一王
entries.en: The Eleven Princes of Shenwu
entries.literal: The Eleven Princes of Gaozu

entries.zh: 神武皇帝十五男：武明婁皇后生文襄皇帝、文宣皇帝、孝昭皇帝、襄城景王淯、武成皇帝、博陵文簡王濟，王氏生永安簡平王浚，穆氏生平陽靖翼王淹，大尒朱氏生彭城景思王浟、華山王凝，韓氏生上党剛肅王渙，小尒朱氏生任城王湝，游氏生高陽康穆王湜，鄭氏生馮翊王潤，馮氏生漢陽敬懷王洽。
entries.en: Gao Huan, the Shenwu Emperor, had fifteen sons: Empress Wuming née Lou bore Gao Cheng, Gao Yang, Gao Yan, Prince Jing of Xiangcheng Yu, Gao Zhan, and Prince Wenjian of Boling Ji; Lady Wang bore Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun; Lady Mu bore Prince Jingyi of Pingyang Yan; the Grand Lady Erzhu bore Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng You and Prince of Huashan Ning; Lady Han bore Prince Gangsu of Shangdang Huan; the Lesser Lady Erzhu bore Prince of Rencheng Jie; Lady You bore Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang Shi; Lady Zheng bore Prince of Fengyi Run; Lady Feng bore Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang Qia.
entries.literal: The Shenwu Emperor had fifteen sons: Empress Wuming née Lou bore Emperor Wenxiang, Emperor Wenxuan, Emperor Xiaozhao, Prince Jing of Xiangcheng Yu, Emperor Wucheng, and Prince Wenjian of Boling Ji; Lady Wang bore Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun; Lady Mu bore Prince Jingyi of Pingyang Yan; the Grand Lady Erzhu bore Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng You and Prince of Huashan Ning; Lady Han bore Prince Gangsu of Shangdang Huan; the Lesser Lady Erzhu bore Prince of Rencheng Jie; Lady You bore Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang Shi; Lady Zheng bore Prince of Fengyi Run; Lady Feng bore Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang Qia.

entries.zh: 永安簡平王浚，字定樂，神武第三子也。
entries.en: Prince Jianping of Yong'an, Jun, whose style name was Dingyue, was the third son of Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Prince Jianping of Yong'an, Jun, style name Dingyue, was the third son of Shenwu.

entries.zh: 初，神武納浚母，當月而有孕，及產浚，疑非己類，不甚愛之。
entries.en: When Gao Huan first took Jun's mother into his household, she conceived that same month; when Jun was born he doubted the child was truly his and showed little affection.
entries.literal: At first, when Shenwu took Jun's mother into his household, she conceived that same month; when Jun was born, he suspected the child was not of his kind and did not love him greatly.

entries.zh: 而浚早慧，後更被寵。
entries.en: Yet Jun was precocious, and in time he came to be favored.
entries.literal: Yet Jun was precocious, and afterward came to be favored.

entries.zh: 年八歲時，問于博士盧景裕曰：「『祭神如神在。』
entries.en: At eight years of age he asked the Erudite Lu Jingyu, saying, " 'One sacrifices to the spirits as though the spirits were present.
entries.literal: At eight years of age he asked the Erudite Lu Jingyu, saying, " 'One sacrifices to the spirits as though the spirits were present.

entries.zh: 為有神邪，無神邪？」
entries.en: Is there a spirit, or is there not?"
entries.literal: Is there a spirit, or is there not?"

entries.zh: 對曰；
entries.en: He replied:
entries.literal: He replied:

entries.en: "There is."
entries.literal: "There is."

entries.zh: 浚曰：「有神當雲祭神神在，何煩『如』字？」
entries.en: Jun said, "If there is a spirit, one ought simply to say 'One sacrifices to the spirits; the spirits are present' — why bother with the word 'as though'?"
entries.literal: Jun said, "If there is a spirit, one ought simply to say 'One sacrifices to the spirits; the spirits are present' — why bother with the word 'as though'?"

entries.zh: 景裕不能答。
entries.en: Jingyu could not answer.
entries.literal: Jingyu could not answer.

entries.zh: 及長，嬉戲不節，曾以屬請受納，大見杖罰，拘禁府獄，旣而見原。
entries.en: When he grew up he played without restraint; once he used his influence to solicit bribes and was severely beaten and cane-punished, confined in the princely prison, and afterward pardoned.
entries.literal: When he grew up, he played without restraint; once he used his influence to solicit bribes and was heavily beaten and cane-punished, confined in the princely prison, and afterward pardoned.

entries.zh: 後稍折節，頗以讀書為務。
entries.en: Later he somewhat reformed his conduct and devoted himself to study.
entries.literal: Later he somewhat reformed his ways and took reading as his occupation.

entries.zh: 平陽靖翼王淹，字子邃，神武第四子也。
entries.en: Prince Jingyi of Pingyang, Yan, whose style name was Zisui, was the fourth son of Shenwu.
entries.literal: Prince Jingyi of Pingyang, Yan, style name Zisui, was the fourth son of Shenwu.

entries.zh: 元象中，封平陽郡公，累遷尚書左僕射。
entries.en: During the Yuanxiang era he was made Duke of Pingyang Commandery and rose through successive offices to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: During the Yuanxiang era, he was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyang Commandery and was repeatedly promoted, reaching Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 天保初，進爵為王，歷位尚書令、開府儀同三司、司空、太尉。
entries.en: At the opening of Tianbao he was raised to princely rank and went on to serve as Chief Minister of the Secretariat, Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, Minister of Works, and Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, his title was advanced to prince, and he successively held the offices of Chief Minister of the Secretariat, Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, Minister of Works, and Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 皇建初，為太傅，與彭城、河間王並給仗衛、羽林百人。
entries.en: At the beginning of Huangjian he was made Grand Tutor; he, the Prince of Pengcheng, and the Prince of Hejian were each assigned armed guards and one hundred Yulin troops.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, he became Grand Tutor, and he, the Prince of Pengcheng, and the Prince of Hejian were all given armed guards and one hundred Yulin troops.

entries.zh: 大寧元年，遷太宰。
entries.en: In the first year of Daning he was moved to Grand Minister.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daning, he was transferred to Grand Minister.

entries.zh: 性沉謹，以寬厚稱。
entries.en: He was reserved and careful by temperament, and was known for breadth and kindness.
entries.literal: By nature he was deep and careful, and was known for generosity and kindness.

entries.zh: 河清三年，薨於晉陽，或云酖終。
entries.en: In the third year of Heqing he died at Jinyang; some said he died by poisoning.
entries.literal: In the third year of Heqing, he died at Jinyang; some say he ended by poison.

entries.zh: 還葬鄴，贈假黃鉞、太宰、錄尚書事。
entries.en: His body was returned for burial at Ye, and he was posthumously granted the acting yellow battle-axe, Grand Minister, and Recorder of Affairs of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was returned and buried at Ye, and was posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Minister, and Recorder of Affairs of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 子德素嗣。
entries.en: His son Desu succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Desu inherited.

entries.zh: 彭城景思王浟，字子深，神武第五子也。
entries.en: Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng, You, whose style name was Zishen, was the fifth son of Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng, You, style name Zishen, was the fifth son of Shenwu.

entries.zh: 元象二年，拜通直散騎常侍，封長樂郡公。
entries.en: In the second year of the Yuanxiang era he was appointed Regular Attendant and enfeoffed Duke of Changle Commandery.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yuanxiang he was appointed Regular Attendant and enfeoffed Duke of Changle Commandery.

entries.zh: 博士韓毅教浟書，見浟筆跡未工，戲浟曰：「五郎書畫如此，忽為常侍開國，今日後宜更用心。」
entries.en: The Erudite Han Yi taught You to write; seeing that You's handwriting was not yet skilled, he joked with You, saying, "Fifth Lord's writing and drawing are like this — suddenly to become Regular Attendant and establish a state, from today onward you ought to apply yourself more diligently."
entries.literal: The Erudite Han Yi taught You to write; seeing that You's handwriting was not yet skilled, he joked with You, saying, "Fifth Lord's writing and drawing are like this — suddenly to become Regular Attendant and establish a state, from today onward you ought to apply yourself more diligently."

entries.zh: 浟正色答曰：「昔甘羅幼為秦相，未聞能書。
entries.en: You replied with a stern countenance, "In former times Gan Luo in youth became Chancellor of Qin — one never heard that he could write.
entries.literal: You replied with a stern countenance, "In former times Gan Luo in youth became Chancellor of Qin — one never heard that he could write.

entries.zh: 凡人唯論才具何如，豈必動誇筆跡。
entries.en: For a man one considers only what his talents and capacity are like; there is no need to constantly boast of one's handwriting.
entries.literal: For a man one considers only what his talents and capacity are like; there is no need to constantly boast of one's handwriting.

entries.zh: 博士當今能者，何為不作三公？」
entries.en: If the Erudite is so capable today, why does he not become one of the Three Excellencies?"
entries.literal: If the Erudite is so capable today, why does he not become one of the Three Excellencies?"

entries.zh: 時年蓋八歲矣。
entries.en: He was then about eight years old.
entries.literal: He was then about eight years old.

entries.zh: 毅甚慚。
entries.en: Yi was deeply ashamed.
entries.literal: Yi was deeply ashamed.

entries.zh: 元象中，封永安郡公。
entries.en: In the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed Duke of Yong'an Commandery.
entries.literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed Duke of Yong'an Commandery.

entries.zh: 豪爽有氣力，善騎射，為文襄所愛。
entries.en: Bold and open, possessed of strength, skilled at riding and archery — he was loved by Gao Cheng.
entries.literal: Bold and open, possessed of strength, skilled at riding and archery — he was loved by Wenxiang.

entries.zh: 文宣性雌懦，每參文襄，有時涕出。
entries.en: Gao Yang was by nature timid and effeminate; whenever he attended upon Gao Cheng, tears would sometimes fall.
entries.literal: Wenxuan's nature was timid and weak; whenever he attended upon Wenxiang, tears sometimes fell.

entries.zh: 浚常責帝左右，何因不為二兄拭鼻，由是見銜。
entries.en: Jun often rebuked those at the emperor's side, asking why they did not wipe Second Elder Brother's nose for him — on this account he came to be resented.
entries.literal: Jun often rebuked those at the Emperor's side, asking why they did not wipe Second Elder Brother's nose for him — on this account he came to be resented.

entries.zh: 累遷中書監、兼侍中。
entries.en: He was promoted in succession to Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Concurrent Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 出為青州刺史，頗好畋獵，聰明矜恕，上下畏悅之。
entries.en: He went out as Governor of Qing Province; he was rather fond of hunting, yet intelligent, stern yet forgiving — high and low both feared and delighted in him.
entries.literal: He went out as Governor of Qing Province; he was rather fond of hunting; intelligent, stern yet forgiving — high and low both feared and delighted in him.

entries.zh: 天保初，進爵為王。
entries.en: At the opening of the Tianbao era he was advanced to princely rank.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was advanced to princely rank.

entries.zh: 文宣末年多酒，浚謂親近曰：「二兄舊來不甚了了，自登祚已後，識解頓進。
entries.en: In the last years of Gao Yang's reign he drank heavily; Jun said to those close to him, "Second Elder Brother was never very clear-minded before; since ascending the throne his understanding has suddenly advanced.
entries.literal: In the last years of Wenxuan's reign he drank heavily; Jun said to those close to him, "Second Elder Brother was never very clear-minded before; since ascending the throne his understanding has suddenly advanced.

entries.zh: 今因酒敗德，朝臣無敢諫者，大敵未滅，吾甚以為憂，欲乘驛至鄴面諫，不知用吾不。」
entries.en: Now through wine he ruins his virtue, yet none of the court ministers dare remonstrate. The great enemy is not yet destroyed — I am deeply troubled; I wish to take post-horses to Ye and remonstrate face to face — I do not know whether they will heed me."
entries.literal: Now through wine he ruins his virtue, yet none of the court ministers dare remonstrate. The great enemy is not yet destroyed — I am deeply troubled; I wish to take post-horses to Ye and remonstrate face to face — I do not know whether they will use me."

entries.zh: 人有知，密以白帝，又見銜。
entries.en: Someone who knew of it secretly reported to the emperor, and again he came to be resented.
entries.literal: Someone who knew of it secretly reported to the Emperor, and again he came to be resented.

entries.zh: 八年來朝，從幸東山。
entries.en: In the eighth year he came to court and accompanied the emperor on an excursion to Eastern Mountain.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he came to court and accompanied the Emperor on an excursion to Eastern Mountain.

entries.zh: 帝裸裎為樂，雜以婦女，又作狐掉尾戲。
entries.en: The emperor stripped naked for amusement, mingling with women, and also performed the fox-tail dance.
entries.literal: The Emperor stripped naked for amusement, mingling with women, and also performed the fox-tail dance.

entries.zh: 浚進言此非人主所宜。
entries.en: Jun remonstrated that this was not fitting for a ruler.
entries.literal: Jun remonstrated that this was not fitting for a ruler.

entries.zh: 帝甚不悅。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly displeased.
entries.literal: The Emperor was greatly displeased.

entries.zh: 浚又于屏處召楊遵彥，譏其不諫。
entries.en: Jun also summoned Yang Zunyan in a secluded place and mocked him for not remonstrating.
entries.literal: Jun also summoned Yang Zunyan in a secluded place and mocked him for not remonstrating.

entries.zh: 帝時不欲大臣與諸王交通，遵彥懼以奏。
entries.en: The emperor at that time did not wish great ministers to have dealings with the princes; Zunyan, in fear, reported it.
entries.literal: The Emperor at that time did not wish great ministers to have dealings with the princes; Zunyan, in fear, reported it.

entries.zh: 帝大怒曰：「小人由來難忍！」
entries.en: The emperor flew into a rage and said, "Such petty men have always been intolerable!"
entries.literal: The Emperor flew into a rage and said, "Such petty men have always been intolerable!"

entries.zh: 遂罷酒還宮。
entries.en: Thereupon he ended the feast and returned to the palace.
entries.literal: Thereupon he ended the feast and returned to the palace.

entries.zh: 浚尋還州，又上書切諫。
entries.en: Jun soon returned to his province and again submitted a memorial of stern remonstrance.
entries.literal: Jun soon returned to his province and again submitted a memorial of stern remonstrance.

entries.zh: 詔令徵浚，浚懼禍，謝疾不至。
entries.en: An edict summoned Jun; Jun, fearing disaster, pleaded illness and did not come.
entries.literal: An edict summoned Jun; Jun, fearing disaster, pleaded illness and did not come.

entries.zh: 上怒，馳驛收浚，老幼泣送者數千人。
entries.en: The emperor was enraged and sent post-horses to seize Jun; old and young wept as they saw him off — several thousand in number.
entries.literal: The Emperor was enraged and sent post-horses to seize Jun; old and young wept as they saw him off — several thousand in number.

entries.zh: 至，盛以鐵籠，與上黨王渙俱置北城地牢下，飲食溲穢共在一所。
entries.en: When he arrived, he was placed in an iron cage and, together with Prince Gangsu of Shangdang Huan, was put in an underground dungeon beneath the northern city wall; food, drink, urine, and filth were all in one place.
entries.literal: When he arrived, he was placed in an iron cage and, together with Prince of Shangdang Huan, was put in an underground dungeon beneath the northern city wall; food, drink, urine, and filth were all in one place.

entries.zh: 明年，帝親將左右臨穴歌謳，令浚和之。
entries.en: The next year the emperor personally led his attendants to the pit to sing and chant, ordering Jun to harmonize with him.
entries.literal: The next year the Emperor personally led his attendants to the pit to sing and chant, ordering Jun to harmonize with him.

entries.zh: 浚等惶怖且悲，不覺聲戰。
entries.en: Jun and the others were terrified and grief-stricken; without knowing it their voices trembled.
entries.literal: Jun and the others were terrified and grief-stricken; without knowing it their voices trembled.

entries.zh: 帝為愴然，因泣，將赦之。
entries.en: The emperor was moved to sorrow and wept, intending to pardon them.
entries.literal: The Emperor was moved to sorrow and wept, intending to pardon them.

entries.zh: 長廣王湛先與浚不睦，進曰：「猛獸安可出穴。」
entries.en: Prince Changguang Gao Zhan, who had long been on bad terms with Jun, stepped forward and said, "A fierce beast cannot safely be let out of its den."
entries.literal: Prince Changguang Zhan, who had long been on bad terms with Jun, stepped forward and said, "A fierce beast cannot safely be let out of its den."

entries.zh: 帝默然。
entries.en: The emperor fell silent.
entries.literal: The Emperor fell silent.

entries.zh: 浚等聞之，呼長廣小字曰：「步落稽，皇天見汝！」
entries.en: When Jun and the others heard it, they cried out Changguang's childhood name: "Buluoji — Heaven sees you!"
entries.literal: When Jun and the others heard it, they cried out Changguang's childhood name: "Buluoji — Heaven sees you!"

entries.zh: 左右聞者，莫不悲傷。
entries.en: Those among the attendants who heard it — none was not grief-stricken.
entries.literal: Those among the attendants who heard it — none was not grief-stricken.

entries.zh: 浚與渙皆有雄略，為諸王所傾服，帝恐為害，乃自刺渙，又使壯土劉桃枝就籠亂刺。
entries.en: Jun and Huan both possessed bold strategy and were admired and submitted to by the princes; the emperor feared they would do harm and therefore personally stabbed Huan, then had the strong man Liu Taozhi enter the cage and stab wildly.
entries.literal: Jun and Huan both possessed bold strategy and were admired and submitted to by the princes; the Emperor feared they would do harm and therefore personally stabbed Huan, then had the strong man Liu Taozhi enter the cage and stab wildly.

entries.zh: 槊每下，浚、渙輒以手拉折之，號哭呼天。
entries.en: Each time the spear descended, Jun and Huan would grasp it and break it off with their hands, crying out and calling to Heaven.
entries.literal: Each time the spear descended, Jun and Huan would grasp it and break it off with their hands, crying out and calling to Heaven.

entries.zh: 於是薪火亂投，燒殺之，填以石土。
entries.en: Thereupon firewood was thrown in confusion and they were burned to death, then covered with stone and earth.
entries.literal: Thereupon firewood was thrown in confusion and they were burned to death, then covered with stone and earth.

entries.zh: 後出，皮髮皆盡，屍色如炭，天下為之痛心。
entries.en: When they were later dug out, skin and hair were entirely gone and the corpses were black as charcoal; the realm was heart-stricken on their account.
entries.literal: When they were later dug out, skin and hair were entirely gone and the corpses were black as charcoal; the realm was heart-stricken on their account.

entries.zh: 武定六年，出為滄州刺史，為政嚴察，部內肅然。
entries.en: In the sixth year of the Wuding era he went out as Governor of Cang Prefecture; his governance was strict and searching, and within his jurisdiction all was orderly.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Wuding he went out as Governor of Cang Prefecture; his governance was strict and searching, and within his jurisdiction all was orderly.

entries.zh: 守令參佐，下及胥吏，行遊往來，皆自賚糧食。
entries.en: Prefects, magistrates, aides, and subordinates, down to clerks and petty officials — all who traveled on business brought their own provisions.
entries.literal: Prefects, magistrates, aides, and subordinates, down to clerks and petty officials — all who traveled on business brought their own provisions.

entries.zh: 浟纖介知人間事。
entries.en: You knew of the smallest matters among the people.
entries.literal: You knew of the smallest matters among the people.

entries.zh: 有濕沃縣主簿張達嘗詣州，夜投人舍，食雞羹，浟察知之。
entries.en: The chief clerk of Shiwo County, Zhang Da, once came to the province; at night he lodged in a private house and ate chicken broth — You detected it.
entries.literal: The chief clerk of Shiwo County, Zhang Da, once came to the province; at night he lodged in a private house and ate chicken broth — You detected it.

entries.zh: 守令畢集，浟對衆曰：「食雞羹何不還價直也？」
entries.en: When the prefects and magistrates had all assembled, You said before the crowd, "You ate chicken broth — why did you not pay the price?"
entries.literal: When the prefects and magistrates had all assembled, You said before the crowd, "You ate chicken broth — why did you not pay the price?"

entries.zh: 達卽伏罪。
entries.en: Da immediately confessed his guilt.
entries.literal: Da immediately confessed his guilt.

entries.zh: 合境號為神明。
entries.en: The entire jurisdiction called him divine in judgment.
entries.literal: The entire jurisdiction called him divine in judgment.

entries.zh: 又有一人從幽州來，驢馱鹿脯。
entries.en: There was also a man who came from You Province, his donkey laden with dried venison.
entries.literal: There was also a man who came from You Province, his donkey laden with dried venison.

entries.zh: 至滄州界，腳痛行遲，偶會一人為伴，遂盜驢及脯去。
entries.en: When he reached the border of Cang Prefecture his foot ached and he walked slowly; by chance he met a man who became his traveling companion, and that man stole the donkey and the venison and fled.
entries.literal: When he reached the border of Cang Prefecture his foot ached and he walked slowly; by chance he met a man who became his traveling companion, and that man stole the donkey and the venison and fled.

entries.zh: 明旦，告州。
entries.en: The next morning he reported it to the province.
entries.literal: The next morning he reported it to the province.

entries.zh: 浟乃令左右及府僚吏分市鹿脯，不限其價。
entries.en: You then ordered his attendants and provincial staff to buy dried venison in the markets, without limiting the price.
entries.literal: You then ordered his attendants and provincial staff to buy dried venison in the markets, without limiting the price.

entries.zh: 其主見脯識之，推獲盜者。
entries.en: The owner saw the venison and recognized it; pursuing it, he captured the thief.
entries.literal: The owner saw the venison and recognized it; pursuing it, he captured the thief.

entries.zh: 轉都督、定州刺史。
entries.en: He was transferred to be Area Commander and Governor of Ding Province.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be Area Commander and Governor of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 時有人被盜黑牛，背上有白毛。
entries.en: At that time a man had a black ox stolen; on its back there was white hair.
entries.literal: At that time a man had a black ox stolen; on its back there was white hair.

entries.zh: 長史韋道建謂中從事魏道勝曰：「使君在滄州日，擒姦如神，若捉得此賊，定神矣。」
entries.en: Chief Clerk Wei Daojian said to Senior Clerk Wei Daosheng, "When the lord was in Cang Prefecture he captured wrongdoers like a spirit; if he catches this thief, he will surely be divine."
entries.literal: Chief Clerk Wei Daojian said to Senior Clerk Wei Daosheng, "When the lord was in Cang Prefecture he captured wrongdoers like a spirit; if he catches this thief, he will surely be divine."

entries.zh: 浟乃詐為上府市牛皮，倍酬價直，使牛主認之，因獲其盜。
entries.en: You then falsely announced that the superior office was buying ox hides in the market, paying double the price, and had the ox's owner identify them — thereby capturing the thief.
entries.literal: You then falsely announced that the superior office was buying ox hides in the market, paying double the price, and had the ox's owner identify them — thereby capturing the thief.

entries.zh: 建等歎服。
entries.en: Daojian and the others sighed in admiration.
entries.literal: Daojian and the others sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 又有老母姓王，孤獨，種菜三畝，數被偷。
entries.en: There was also an old woman surnamed Wang, alone and without support, who planted vegetables on three mu; they were stolen repeatedly.
entries.literal: There was also an old woman surnamed Wang, alone and without support, who planted vegetables on three mu; they were stolen repeatedly.

entries.zh: 浟乃令人密往書菜葉為字，明日市中看菜葉有字，獲賊。
entries.en: You then had men secretly go and write characters on the vegetable leaves; the next day, seeing characters on the leaves in the market, they captured the thief.
entries.literal: You then had men secretly go and write characters on the vegetable leaves; the next day, seeing characters on the leaves in the market, they captured the thief.

entries.zh: 爾後境內無盜，政化為當時第一。
entries.en: After that there were no thieves within the borders, and his governance and transformation ranked first in the age.
entries.literal: After that there were no thieves within the borders, and his governance and transformation ranked first in the age.

entries.zh: 天保初，封彭城王。
entries.en: At the opening of the Tianbao era he was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 四年，徵為侍中，人吏送別悲號。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was summoned as Palace Attendant; officials and commoners saw him off with wailing lament.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as Palace Attendant; officials and commoners saw him off with wailing lament.

entries.zh: 有老公數百人相率具饌曰：「自殿下至來五載，人不識吏，吏不欺人，百姓有識已來，始逢今化。
entries.en: Several hundred old men together prepared provisions and said, "From the time Your Highness arrived until now, five years — the people do not know officials, and officials do not deceive the people; from the time the common people have had understanding until now, they have only now encountered such transformation.
entries.literal: Several hundred old men together prepared provisions and said, "From the time Your Highness arrived until now, five years — the people do not know officials, and officials do not deceive the people; from the time the common people have had understanding until now, they have only now encountered such transformation.

entries.zh: 殿下唯飲此鄉水，未食此鄉食，聊獻疏薄。」
entries.en: Your Highness has only drunk this district's water and has not yet eaten this district's food — we humbly offer this poor fare."
entries.literal: Your Highness has only drunk this district's water and has not yet eaten this district's food — we humbly offer this poor fare."

entries.zh: 浟重其意，為食一口。
entries.en: You, honoring their intent, ate one mouthful.
entries.literal: You, honoring their intent, ate one mouthful.

entries.zh: 七年，轉司州牧，選從事皆取文才士明剖斷者，當時稱為美選。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was transferred to Governor of Si Province; in selecting aides he took only men of literary talent skilled in clear judgment — at the time this was called a fine selection.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Governor of Si Province; in selecting aides he took only men of literary talent skilled in clear judgment — at the time this was called a fine selection.

entries.zh: 州舊案五百餘，浟未期悉斷盡。
entries.en: The province had more than five hundred old cases; before the term was out You had judged them all.
entries.literal: The province had more than five hundred old cases; before the term was out You had judged them all.

entries.zh: 別駕羊脩等恐犯權戚，乃詣閤諮陳。
entries.en: Vice Prefect Yang Xiu and others, fearing they might offend powerful kin, therefore came to the gate to consult and report.
entries.literal: Vice Prefect Yang Xiu and others, fearing they might offend powerful kin, therefore came to the gate to consult and report.

entries.zh: 浟使告曰：「吾直道而行，何憚權戚，卿等當成人之美，反以權戚為言。」
entries.en: You sent word saying, "I walk the straight path — why should I fear powerful kin? You ought to help others achieve excellence; instead you speak of powerful kin."
entries.literal: You sent word saying, "I walk the straight path — why should I fear powerful kin? You ought to help others achieve excellence; instead you speak of powerful kin."

entries.zh: 脩等慚悚而退。
entries.en: Xiu and the others withdrew in shame and fear.
entries.literal: Xiu and the others withdrew in shame and fear.

entries.zh: 後加特進，兼司空、太尉，州牧如故。
entries.en: Later he was additionally appointed Special Advancement, Concurrent Minister of Works and Grand Commandant, his governorship unchanged.
entries.literal: Later he was additionally appointed Special Advancement, Concurrent Minister of Works and Grand Commandant, his governorship unchanged.

entries.zh: 太妃薨，解任，尋詔復本官。
entries.en: When the Princess Consort died he was relieved of office; soon an edict restored him to his original post.
entries.literal: When the Princess Consort died he was relieved of office; soon an edict restored him to his original post.

entries.zh: 俄拜司空，兼尚書令。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed Minister of Works and Concurrent Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Works and Concurrent Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 濟南嗣位，除開府儀同三司、尚書令、領大宗正卿。
entries.en: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, he was removed to Opener of the Way Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Director of the Imperial Clan.
entries.literal: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, he was removed to Opener of the Way Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Director of the Imperial Clan.

entries.zh: 皇建初，拜大司馬，兼尚書令，轉太保。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Huangjian era he was appointed Grand Marshal and Concurrent Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he was appointed Grand Marshal and Concurrent Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 武成入承大業，遷太師、錄尚書事。
entries.en: When Gao Zhan succeeded to the great enterprise, he was transferred to Grand Preceptor and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: When Wucheng succeeded to the great enterprise, he was transferred to Grand Preceptor and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 浟明練世務，果於斷決，事無大小，咸悉以情。
entries.en: You was clear and practiced in affairs of the age, decisive in judgment; matters great and small he handled entirely according to the merits of each case.
entries.literal: You was clear and practiced in affairs of the age, decisive in judgment; matters great and small he handled entirely according to the merits of each case.

entries.zh: 趙郡李公統預高歸彥之逆，其母崔氏卽御史中丞崔昂從父子，兼右僕射魏收之內妹也。
entries.en: Li Gongtong of Zhao Commandery took part in Gao Guiyan's rebellion; his mother Lady Cui was the daughter of a younger cousin of Censor-in-Chief Cui Ang, and also the younger sister by marriage of Right Vice Director Wei Shou.
entries.literal: Li Gongtong of Zhao Commandery took part in Gao Guiyan's rebellion; his mother Lady Cui was the daughter of a younger cousin of Censor-in-Chief Cui Ang, and also the younger sister by marriage of Right Vice Director Wei Shou.

entries.zh: 依令，年出六十，例免入官。
entries.en: According to the statute, those over sixty years of age were by rule exempt from being taken into official service.
entries.literal: According to the statute, those over sixty years of age were by rule exempt from being taken into official service.

entries.zh: 崔增年陳訴，所司以昂、收故，崔遂獲免。
entries.en: Cui added years to her age and submitted a petition; the responsible office, because of Ang and Shou, therefore exempted Cui.
entries.literal: Cui added years to her age and submitted a petition; the responsible office, because of Ang and Shou, therefore exempted Cui.

entries.zh: 浟摘發其事，昂等以罪除名。
entries.en: You exposed the matter; Ang and the others were stripped of their names and offices on account of the crime.
entries.literal: You exposed the matter; Ang and the others were stripped of their names and offices on account of the crime.

entries.zh: 上黨剛肅王渙，字敬壽，神武第七子也。
entries.en: Prince Gangsu of Shangdang, Huan, whose style name was Jingshou, was the seventh son of Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Prince Gangsu of Shangdang, Huan, style name Jingshou, was the seventh son of Shenwu.

entries.zh: 天姿雄傑，俶儻不群，雖在童幼，恒以將略自許。
entries.en: Naturally heroic and bold, unmatched even in boyhood, he always counted himself born for command.
entries.literal: By nature he was heroic and outstanding, daring and unlike others; even in childhood he always reckoned himself destined for generalship.

entries.zh: 神武壯而愛之，曰：「此兒似我。」
entries.en: Gao Huan admired him and said, "This boy is my image."
entries.literal: Shenwu, impressed, loved him and said, "This boy is like me."

entries.zh: 及長，力能扛鼎，材武絕倫。
entries.en: Grown to manhood he could lift a bronze tripod; in arms and valor none could match him.
entries.literal: When he grew up he could lift a tripod; in talent and martial prowess he was without peer.

entries.zh: 每謂左右曰：「人不可無學，但要不為博士耳。」
entries.en: He often told his attendants, "A man must have learning — he need only avoid becoming a pedant."
entries.literal: He often told those at his side, "A man must not be without learning — only he need not become an Erudite."

entries.zh: 故讀書頗知梗概，而不甚耽習。
entries.en: He read enough to grasp the main points, but never lost himself in books.
entries.literal: Therefore he read books and knew the outlines of things, but was not deeply devoted to study.

entries.zh: 初，術士言亡高者黑衣，由是自神武后，每出行，不欲見沙門，為黑衣故也。
entries.en: Diviners had once said the destroyer of the Gao would wear black; after Gao Huan's death the court on its travels avoided Buddhist monks for that reason.
entries.literal: At first diviners had said that the destroyer of the Gao would wear black; hence after Shenwu, whenever they went abroad they did not wish to meet Buddhist monks, because monks wore black.

entries.zh: 是時文宣幸晉陽，以所忌問左右曰：「何物最黑？」
entries.en: Gao Yang was then at Jinyang; acting on this fear he asked his attendants, "What is blackest of all?"
entries.literal: At that time Wenxuan was at Jinyang; following his superstition he asked those at his side, "What thing is blackest?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「莫過漆。」
entries.en: They answered, "Nothing surpasses lacquer."
entries.literal: They answered, "Nothing blacker than lacquer."

entries.zh: 帝以渙第七子為當之，乃使庫真都督破六韓伯昇之鄴徵渙。
entries.en: The emperor decided Huan, as the seventh son, must be the omen, and sent storehouse commissioner Poliuhan Bosheng to Ye to summon him.
entries.literal: The Emperor decided that Huan as the seventh son must be the omen, and sent Storehouse Commissioner Poliuhan Bosheng to Ye to summon Huan.

entries.zh: 渙至紫陌橋，殺伯昇以逃，憑河而度，土人執以送帝。
entries.en: At Zimo Bridge Huan killed Bosheng and fled; he forded a river, but local men seized him and delivered him to the emperor.
entries.literal: When Huan reached Zimo Bridge he killed Bosheng and fled; he forded a river, but local men seized him and delivered him to the Emperor.

entries.zh: 鐵籠盛之，與永安王浚同置地牢下。
entries.en: He was caged in iron and shut in the underground dungeon with Jun, Prince of Yong'an.
entries.literal: He was placed in an iron cage and, together with Jun, Prince of Yong'an, was put in an underground dungeon.

entries.zh: 歲餘，與浚同見殺，時年二十六。
entries.en: After more than a year he was killed together with Jun. He was twenty-six.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was killed together with Jun. He was twenty-six years of age.

entries.zh: 以其妃李氏配馮文洛，是帝家舊奴，積勞位至刺史，帝令文洛等殺渙，故以其妻妻焉。
entries.en: His consort Lady Li was given to Feng Wenluo — an old household slave of the imperial clan who through long service had risen to provincial governor; the emperor had ordered Wenluo and others to kill Huan, and so gave him Huan's wife.
entries.literal: His consort Lady Li was given in marriage to Feng Wenluo — an old household slave of the imperial clan who through long service had risen to governor; the Emperor had ordered Wenluo and others to kill Huan, and therefore gave him Huan's wife.

entries.zh: 襄城景王淯，神武第八子也。
entries.en: Prince Jing of Xiangcheng, Yu, was the eighth son of Shenwu.
entries.literal: Prince Jing of Xiangcheng, Yu, was the eighth son of Shenwu.

entries.zh: 容貌甚美，弱年有器望。
entries.en: He was very handsome and, while still young, showed promise and distinction.
entries.literal: His appearance was very handsome, and while still young he had capacity and reputation.

entries.zh: 元象中，封章武郡公。
entries.en: During the Yuanxiang era he was made Duke of Zhangwu Commandery.
entries.literal: During the Yuanxiang era, he was enfeoffed Duke of Zhangwu Commandery.

entries.zh: 天保初，封襄城郡王。
entries.en: At the opening of Tianbao he was made Prince of Xiangcheng Commandery.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiangcheng Commandery.

entries.zh: 二年春，薨。
entries.en: In spring of the second year he died.
entries.literal: In spring of the second year, he died.

entries.zh: 齊氏諸王選國臣府佐，多取富商群小、鷹犬少年，唯襄城、廣甯、蘭陵王等頗引文藝清識之士，當時以此稱之。
entries.en: When the princes of the Qi house chose state ministers and office staff, most selected wealthy merchants, petty men, and sporting youths. Only the princes of Xiangcheng, Guangning, Lanling, and a few others drew in cultivated and perceptive men, and they were praised for it at the time.
entries.literal: When the princes of the Qi house selected ministers for their states and assistants for their offices, they mostly took wealthy merchants, petty men, and youths who kept hawks and dogs; only the princes of Xiangcheng, Guangning, Lanling, and the like rather drew in men of letters and clear discernment, and for this they were praised at the time.

entries.zh: 乾明元年二月，贈假黃鋮、太師、太尉、錄尚書事。
entries.en: In the second month of the first year of Qianming, he was posthumously granted the acting yellow battle-axe, Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the second month of the first year of Qianming, he was posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 無子，詔以常山王演第二子亮嗣。
entries.en: Because he had no son, an edict made Liang, the second son of Prince Yan of Changshan, his heir.
entries.literal: Having no sons, an edict appointed Liang, the second son of Prince Yan of Changshan, to succeed him.

entries.zh: 任城王湝，神武第十子也，少明慧。
entries.en: Prince Jie of Rencheng was the tenth son of Shenwu and was bright and perceptive from youth.
entries.literal: Prince of Rencheng, Jie, was the tenth son of Shenwu and was intelligent and perceptive from youth.

entries.zh: 天保初封。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed at the opening of Tianbao.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed at the beginning of Tianbao.

entries.zh: 自孝昭、武成時，車駕還鄴，常令湝鎮晉陽，總幷省事，歷司徒、太尉、幷省錄尚書事。
entries.en: In the reigns of Xiaozhao and Wucheng, whenever the emperor returned to Ye, Jie was usually left to garrison Jinyang and supervise Bing Province. He served successively as Minister over the Masses, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Secretariat in Bing Province.
entries.literal: From the times of Xiaozhao and Wucheng, whenever the imperial carriage returned to Ye, Jie was regularly ordered to garrison Jinyang and oversee the affairs of Bing Province; he successively served as Minister over the Masses, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Secretariat in Bing Province.

entries.zh: 天統三年，拜太保、幷州刺史，別封正平郡公。
entries.en: In the third year of Tiantong he was appointed Grand Guardian and Inspector of Bing Province, and separately made Duke of Zhengping Commandery.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tiantong, he was appointed Grand Guardian and Inspector of Bing Province, and was separately enfeoffed Duke of Zhengping Commandery.

entries.zh: 時有婦人臨汾水浣衣，有乘馬人換其新靴馳而去者，婦人持故靴，詣州言之。
entries.en: At the time a woman washing clothes by the Fen River had her new boots swapped by a mounted man who then rode off. She took the old boots to the provincial office and reported it.
entries.literal: At the time, a woman was washing clothes by the Fen River when a mounted man exchanged her new boots and rode away; the woman took the old boots and went to the provincial office to report it.

entries.zh: 湝召城外諸嫗，以靴示之，紿曰：「有乘馬人在路被賊劫害，遺此靴焉，得無親屬乎？」
entries.en: Jie summoned the old women outside the city, showed them the boots, and said deceptively, "A rider was robbed and killed on the road and left these boots behind. Could he be a relative of yours?"
entries.literal: Jie summoned the old women outside the city, showed them the boots, and deceived them, saying, "A mounted man was robbed and killed by bandits on the road, leaving these boots behind. Might he have any kin among you?"

entries.zh: 一嫗撫膺哭曰：「兒昨著此靴向妻家。」
entries.en: One old woman beat her breast and cried, "My son wore these boots yesterday when he went to his wife's family."
entries.literal: One old woman beat her breast and cried, saying, "My son wore these boots yesterday when he went to his wife's family."

entries.zh: 如其語，捕獲之。
entries.en: Following her statement, they caught him.
entries.literal: Following her words, they arrested and captured him.

entries.zh: 時稱明察。
entries.en: People at the time praised his keen discernment.
entries.literal: At the time, people praised him as discerning in investigation.

entries.zh: 武平初，遷太師、司州牧，出為冀州刺史，加太宰，遷右丞相、都督、青州刺史。
entries.en: At the opening of Wuping he became Grand Preceptor and Governor of Si Province, was then sent out as Inspector of Ji Province, additionally made Grand Minister, and later transferred to Right Chancellor, Area Commander, and Inspector of Qing Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wuping, he was transferred to Grand Preceptor and Governor of Si Province, then sent out as Inspector of Ji Province, additionally made Grand Minister, and transferred to Right Chancellor, Area Commander, and Inspector of Qing Province.

entries.zh: 湝頻牧大藩，雖不潔己，然寬恕為吏人所懷。
entries.en: Jie often governed major provinces. Though he was not personally incorrupt, his generosity and leniency endeared him to officials and commoners.
entries.literal: Jie repeatedly governed great provinces; although he did not keep himself pure, his generosity and forbearance won the attachment of officials and people.

entries.zh: 五年，青州崔蔚波等夜襲州城，湝部分倉卒之際，咸得齊整，擊賊，大破之。
entries.en: In the fifth year, Cui Weibo and others in Qing Province launched a night attack on the provincial city. In the emergency Jie organized his divisions in good order, struck the attackers, and routed them.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, Cui Weibo and others of Qing Province attacked the provincial city by night; in the sudden emergency, Jie deployed his forces and all were orderly, struck the bandits, and badly defeated them.

entries.zh: 拜左丞相，轉瀛州刺史。
entries.en: He was appointed Left Chancellor and then transferred to Inspector of Ying Province.
entries.literal: He was appointed Left Chancellor and transferred to Inspector of Ying Province.

entries.zh: 及後主奔鄴，加湝大丞相。
entries.en: When Houzhu fled to Ye, Jie was made Grand Chancellor.
entries.literal: When Houzhu fled to Ye, Jie was additionally made Grand Chancellor.

entries.zh: 元象中，封平原郡公。
entries.en: In the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.
entries.literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.

entries.zh: 文襄之遇賊，渙年尚幼，在西學，聞宮中嘩，驚曰：「大兄必遭難矣！」
entries.en: When Gao Cheng fell to assassins, Huan was still a boy at the Western Academy; hearing uproar in the palace, he cried, "Eldest brother has met disaster!"
entries.literal: When Wenxiang met with assassins, Huan was still young and at the Western Academy; hearing an uproar in the palace, he started and said, "Eldest brother must have met disaster!"

entries.zh: 彎弓而出。
entries.en: He strung his bow and ran out.
entries.literal: He strung his bow and rushed out.

entries.zh: 武定末，除冀州刺史，在州有美政。
entries.en: At the end of the Wuding era he was appointed governor of Ji Province and governed with distinction.
entries.literal: At the end of the Wuding era he was appointed Governor of Ji Province and governed the province with distinction.

entries.zh: 天保初，封上党王，歷中書令、尚書左僕射。
entries.en: At the opening of the Tianbao era he was enfeoffed Prince of Shangdang and rose through director of the Secretariat and left vice director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Shangdang and served successively as Director of the Secretariat and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 與常山王演等築伐惡諸城。
entries.en: With Prince of Changshan Gao Yan and others he built fortified camps for punitive raids.
entries.literal: Together with Prince of Changshan Yan and others he built fortified camps to attack the enemy.

entries.zh: 遂聚鄴下輕薄，淩犯郡縣，為法司所糾。
entries.en: He then gathered ruffians from Ye who harassed the counties and were denounced by the judiciary.
entries.literal: He then gathered rowdies beneath Ye, who harassed the commanderies and counties and were reported by the judiciary.

entries.zh: 文宣戮其左右數人，渙亦被譴。
entries.en: Gao Yang executed several of his attendants and rebuked Huan himself.
entries.literal: Wenxuan executed several of his attendants and reprimanded Huan as well.

entries.zh: 六年，率衆送梁王蕭明還江南，仍破東關，斬梁特進裴之橫等，威名甚盛。
entries.en: In the sixth year he escorted Liang's Prince Xiao Ming south to Jiangnan, broke Dong Pass, and slew Liang's special advance Pei Zhiheng and others — his fame standing at its height.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he led troops escorting Liang's Prince Xiao Ming back to Jiangnan, and also broke through Dong Pass, slaying Liang's Special Advance Pei Zhiheng and others; his fame was at its height.

entries.zh: 八年，錄尚書事。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was made recorder of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was made Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 及安德王稱尊號於晉陽，使劉子昂修啟於湝：「至尊出奔，宗廟旣重，群公勸迫，權主號令，事甯終歸叔父。」
entries.en: When Prince Yanzong of Ande proclaimed himself at Jinyang, he had Liu Zi'ang draft a memorial to Jie: "The sovereign has fled, the ancestral temple hangs in the balance, the lords press us to act; we hold command only for the moment — in the end it must return to our uncle."
entries.literal: When Prince Yanzong of Ande proclaimed himself emperor at Jinyang, he had Liu Zi'ang draft a memorial to Jie, saying, "The sovereign has fled; the ancestral temple weighs heavily on us; the lords press us to act — we temporarily hold command, but in the end power must return to our uncle."

entries.zh: 湝曰：「我人臣，何容受此啟。」
entries.en: Jie said, "I am the emperor's subject; I could not accept this."
entries.literal: Jie said, "I am the emperor's subject; I could not accept such a memorial."

entries.zh: 執子昂送鄴。
entries.en: He seized Zi'ang and sent him to Ye.
entries.literal: He seized Zi'ang and sent him to Ye.

entries.zh: 帝至濟州，禪位於湝，啟竟不達。
entries.en: When the emperor reached Ji Province and abdicated in Jie's favor, the memorial never reached him.
entries.literal: When the Emperor reached Ji Province and abdicated in Jie's favor, the memorial never reached him.

entries.zh: 湝與廣甯王孝珩于冀州召募得四萬餘人，拒周軍。
entries.en: Jie and Prince Xiaogong of Guangning mustered more than forty thousand men in Ji Province to resist Zhou.
entries.literal: Jie and Prince Xiaogong of Guangning raised more than forty thousand men in Ji Province to resist the Zhou army.

entries.zh: 周齊王憲來伐，先遣送書並赦詔，湝並沉諸井。
entries.en: Zhou's Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian marched against them, first sending letters and an amnesty edict; Jie drowned them all in a well.
entries.literal: Zhou's Prince of Qi, Yuwen Xian, came to attack and first sent letters and an amnesty edict; Jie sank them all in a well.

entries.zh: 戰敗，湝、孝珩俱被擒。
entries.en: Defeated, Jie and Xiaogong were both taken.
entries.literal: Defeated in battle, Jie and Xiaogong were both captured.

entries.zh: 憲曰：「任城王何苦至此？」
entries.en: Xian said, "Prince of Rencheng — why must it end like this?"
entries.literal: Xian said, "Prince of Rencheng — why must it come to this?"

entries.zh: 湝曰：「下官神武帝子，兄弟十五人，幸而獨存，逢宗社顛覆，今日得死，無愧墳陵。」
entries.en: Jie said, "I am a son of the Shenwu Emperor; of fifteen brothers I alone survive. To see the altars overturned and die today — I need feel no shame before our tombs."
entries.literal: Jie said, "I am a subject-son of the Shenwu Emperor; of fifteen brothers I alone survived. To meet the dynasty's fall and die today — I need not blush before our tombs."

entries.zh: 憲壯之，歸其妻子。
entries.en: Xian admired his spirit and restored his wife and children.
entries.literal: Xian admired his spirit and returned his wife and children.

entries.zh: 將至鄴城，湝馬上大哭，自投於地，流血滿面。
entries.en: Approaching Ye, Jie wept on horseback and threw himself to earth, blood covering his face.
entries.literal: As they neared Ye city, Jie wept aloud on horseback and threw himself to the ground, blood streaming down his face.

entries.zh: 至長安，尋與後主同死。
entries.en: At Chang'an he soon died together with Houzhu.
entries.literal: Reaching Chang'an, he soon died together with Houzhu.

entries.zh: 高陽康穆王湜，神武第十一子也。
entries.en: Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang, Shi, was the eleventh son of Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang, Shi, was the eleventh son of Shenwu.

entries.zh: 天保元年封。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed in the first year of the Tianbao era.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianbao.

entries.zh: 十年，稍遷尚書令。
entries.en: In the tenth year he rose to chief minister of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was gradually promoted to Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 以滑稽便辟，有寵于文宣，常在左右，行杖以撻諸王。
entries.en: Glib, amusing, and adept at flattery, he won Gao Yang's favor, kept always at his side, and carried a staff with which he beat the other princes.
entries.literal: Because he was glib, amusing, and adept at flattery, he won Wenxuan's favor, always attended him, and walked about beating the other princes with a staff.

entries.zh: 太后深銜之。
entries.en: The empress dowager bitterly resented him.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager deeply resented him.

entries.zh: 其妃父護軍長史張晏之嘗要道拜湜，湜不禮焉。
entries.en: His consort's father, chief commandant's senior aide Zhang Yanzi, once intercepted the road to pay respects; Shi did not return them.
entries.literal: His consort's father, Chief Commandant's Senior Aide Zhang Yanzi, once stopped the road to pay respects to Shi; Shi did not return the courtesy.

entries.zh: 帝問其故，對曰：「無官職漢，何須禮。」
entries.en: Asked why, Shi said, "A Han man without office needs no bow."
entries.literal: When the Emperor asked why, Shi answered, "A Han man with no office needs no courtesy."

entries.zh: 帝於是擢拜晏之為徐州刺史。
entries.en: The emperor promptly made Yanzi governor of Xu Province.
entries.literal: The Emperor thereupon promoted Yanzi to Governor of Xu Province.

entries.zh: 文宣崩，兼司徒，導引梓宮，吹笛，云「至尊頗知臣不」，又擊胡鼓為樂。
entries.en: When Gao Yang died Shi served as minister of works, led the coffin procession, played the flute saying "The sovereign knew me well," and beat the Hu drum for sport.
entries.literal: When Wenxuan died Shi served concurrently as Minister of Works, led the imperial coffin, played the flute, and said, "The sovereign surely knew his servant," also beating the Hu drum for amusement.

entries.zh: 太后杖湜百餘，未幾薨。
entries.en: The empress dowager had him beaten more than a hundred strokes; he died shortly after.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager had Shi beaten more than a hundred strokes; before long he died.

entries.zh: 太后哭之哀，曰：「我恐其不成就，與杖，何期帶創死也！」
entries.en: The empress dowager wept bitterly: "I feared he would never amount to anything and struck him — who dreamed the blows would kill him!"
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager wept bitterly and said, "I feared he would never amount to anything and beat him — who dreamed he would die of his wounds!"

entries.zh: 乾明初，贈假黃鉞、太師、司徒、錄尚書事。
entries.en: At the opening of the Qianming era he was posthumously granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand preceptor, minister of works, and recorder of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianming he was posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Preceptor, Minister of Works, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 子士義襲爵。
entries.en: His son Shiyi inherited.
entries.literal: His son Shiyi inherited the title.

entries.zh: 博陵文簡王濟，神武第十二子也。
entries.en: Prince Wenjian of Boling, Ji, was the twelfth son of Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Prince Wenjian of Boling, Ji, was the twelfth son of Shenwu.

entries.zh: 天保元年封。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed in the first year of the Tianbao era.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianbao.

entries.zh: 濟嘗從文宣巡幸，在路忽憶太后，遂逃歸。
entries.en: Ji once accompanied Gao Yang on tour; on the road he suddenly missed the empress dowager and fled home.
entries.literal: Ji once accompanied Wenxuan on tour; on the road he suddenly remembered the Empress Dowager and fled back home.

entries.zh: 帝怒，臨以白刃，因此驚恍。
entries.en: The emperor threatened him with naked steel; from that shock Ji was never right again.
entries.literal: The Emperor in rage threatened him with naked blades, and from this Ji was seized with terror and confusion.

entries.zh: 歷位太尉。
entries.en: He served through the rank of grand commandant.
entries.literal: He held office through the rank of Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 河清初，出為定州刺史。
entries.en: At the opening of the Heqing era he was made governor of Ding Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Heqing he was sent out as Governor of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 天統五年，在州語人云：「計次第亦應到我。」
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Tiantong era he told people at his post, "By order of succession it should be my turn next."
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Tiantong, at his post he told people, "By the count of succession my turn ought to come."

entries.zh: 後主聞之，陰使人殺之。
entries.en: Houzhu heard and secretly had him killed.
entries.literal: Houzhu heard of it and secretly had him killed.

entries.zh: 贈假黃鉞、太尉、錄尚書事。
entries.en: Posthumously granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand commandant, and recorder of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 子智襲爵。
entries.en: His son Zhi inherited.
entries.literal: His son Zhi inherited the title.

entries.zh: 華山王凝，神武第十三子也。
entries.en: Prince Ning of Huashan was the thirteenth son of Shenwu.
entries.literal: Prince of Huashan, Ning, was the thirteenth son of Shenwu.

entries.zh: 天保元年，封新平郡王；九年，改封安定；十年，封華山。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianbao he was made Prince of Xinping Commandery; in the ninth year his fief was changed to Anding; in the tenth year he was enfeoffed at Huashan.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Xinping Commandery; in the ninth year, his fief was changed to Anding; in the tenth year, he was enfeoffed at Huashan.

entries.zh: 歷位中書令、齊州刺史，就加太傅。
entries.en: He served as Director of the Secretariat and Inspector of Qi Province, and while in that post was additionally made Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: He successively held the posts of Director of the Secretariat and Inspector of Qi Province, and while there was additionally made Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 薨於州，贈左丞相、太師、錄尚書。
entries.en: He died in the province and was posthumously granted Left Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, and Recorder of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He died in the province and was posthumously granted Left Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, and Recorder of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 凝諸王中最為孱弱，妃王氏，太子洗馬王洽女也，與倉頭姦，凝知而不能限禁。
entries.en: Ning was the weakest of the princes. His consort Lady Wang, daughter of Wang Qia, Groom of the Crown Prince, had an affair with a household slave; Ning knew but could not stop her.
entries.literal: Among the princes, Ning was the weakest; his consort Lady Wang, daughter of the Crown Prince's Groom Wang Xia, committed adultery with a household slave, and though Ning knew of it, he could not restrain or forbid her.

entries.zh: 後事發，王氏賜死，詔杖凝一百。
entries.en: When the affair later came to light, Lady Wang was ordered to commit suicide, and an edict had Ning beaten one hundred strokes.
entries.literal: Later, when the affair was exposed, Lady Wang was ordered to die, and an edict had Ning beaten one hundred strokes.

entries.zh: 其愚如此。
entries.en: Such was his foolishness.
entries.literal: His foolishness was like this.

entries.zh: 馮翊王潤，字子澤，神武第十四子也。
entries.en: Prince of Fengyi, Run, whose style name was Zize, was the fourteenth son of Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Prince of Fengyi, Run, style name Zize, was the fourteenth son of Shenwu.

entries.zh: 幼時，神武稱曰：「此吾家千里駒也。」
entries.en: In boyhood Gao Huan called him "the thousand-li colt of our house."
entries.literal: In youth Shenwu called him "the thousand-li colt of our house."

entries.zh: 天保初封。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed at the opening of the Tianbao era.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed at the beginning of Tianbao.

entries.zh: 歷位東北道大行臺、右僕射、都督、定州刺史。
entries.en: He served as northeast-route grand mobile headquarters, right vice director of the Masters of Writing, area commander, and governor of Ding Province.
entries.literal: He held office successively as Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Northeast Road, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Area Commander, and Governor of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 潤美姿儀，年十四五，母鄭妃與之同寢，有穢雜之聲。
entries.en: Run was handsome; at fourteen or fifteen he shared a bed with his mother Consort Zheng, and lewd sounds were heard.
entries.literal: Run had handsome looks; at fourteen or fifteen his mother Consort Zheng slept with him in the same bed, and obscene sounds were heard.

entries.zh: 及長，廉慎方雅，習於吏職，至摘發隱偽，姦吏無所匿其情。
entries.en: Grown, he was upright, cautious, and skilled in office; in exposing hidden fraud no clerk could hide from him.
entries.literal: When grown he was upright, cautious, and refined, skilled in official business; even in exposing hidden fraud no corrupt clerk could conceal the facts from him.

entries.zh: 開府王迴洛與六州大都督獨孤枝侵竊官田，受納賄賂，潤按舉其事。
entries.en: Opener of the way Wang Huiluo and six-province commander-in-chief Dugu Zhi had encroached on public land and taken bribes; Run investigated and impeached them.
entries.literal: Opener of the Way Wang Huiluo and Six-Province Commander-in-Chief Dugu Zhi encroached on public land and accepted bribes; Run investigated and reported them.

entries.zh: 二人表言，王出送臺使，登魏文舊壇，南望歎息，不測其意。
entries.en: The two memorialized that when Run saw off a capital envoy he climbed Cao Pi's old platform, gazed south, and sighed — no one could read his mind.
entries.literal: The two submitted a memorial saying that when the prince saw off a capital envoy he climbed the old platform of Emperor Wen of Wei, looked south, and sighed — none could fathom his intent.

entries.zh: 武成使元文遙就州宣勑曰：「馮翊王少小謹慎，在州不為非法，朕信之熟矣。
entries.en: Gao Zhan sent Yuan Wenyao with an edict: "Prince Run has been careful from youth and committed no crime in office — I know him thoroughly.
entries.literal: Wucheng sent Yuan Wenyao to the province with an edict, saying, "Prince of Fengyi Run has been careful from youth; at his post he has committed no wrong — I know him well.

entries.zh: 登高遠望，人之常情，鼠輩欲橫相間構，曲生眉目。」
entries.en: To climb high and look far is only human; these vermin would invent treason out of thin air."
entries.literal: To climb high and gaze far is human nature; vermin trying to invent slander and twist facts out of nothing."

entries.zh: 於是回洛決鞭二百，獨孤枝決杖一百。
entries.en: Huiluo received two hundred lashes; Dugu Zhi one hundred strokes of the staff.
entries.literal: Huiluo was sentenced to two hundred lashes; Dugu Zhi to one hundred strokes with the staff.

entries.zh: 尋為尚書令，領太子少師，歷司徒、太尉、大司馬、司州牧、太保、河南道行台、領錄尚書，別封文成郡公、太師、太宰，復為定州刺史。
entries.en: He became chief minister of the Masters of Writing and junior tutor of the crown prince, then minister of works, grand commandant, grand marshal, governor of Si Province, grand tutor, Henan-route grand mobile headquarters, and recorder of the Masters of Writing; he was separately enfeoffed duke of Wencheng, grand preceptor, and grand steward — and again made governor of Ding Province.
entries.literal: He soon became Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing and Concurrent Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, and successively Minister of Works, Grand Commandant, Grand Marshal, Governor of Si Province, Grand Tutor, Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Henan Road, and Concurrent Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing; he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Wencheng Commandery, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Steward — and again made Governor of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 薨，贈假黃鉞、左丞相。
entries.en: At his death he was posthumously granted the acting yellow battle-axe and left chancellor.
entries.literal: At his death he was posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe and Left Chancellor.

entries.zh: 子茂德嗣。
entries.en: His son Maode succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Maode succeeded.

entries.zh: 漢陽敬懷王洽，字敬延，神武第十五子也。
entries.en: Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang, Qia, whose style name was Jingyan, was the fifteenth son of Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang, Qia, style name Jingyan, was the fifteenth son of Shenwu.

entries.zh: 天保元年封。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed in the first year of the Tianbao era.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianbao.

entries.zh: 五年，薨，年十三。
entries.en: In the fifth year he died, aged thirteen.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged thirteen.

entries.zh: 乾明元年，贈太保、司空。
entries.en: In the first year of the Qianming era he was posthumously made grand tutor and minister of works.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianming he was posthumously made Grand Tutor and Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 無子，以任城王第二子建德為後。
entries.en: Having no son, Jiande, second son of the Prince of Rencheng, was made his heir.
entries.literal: Having no sons, the second son of the Prince of Rencheng, Jiande, was made his heir.

entries.zh: 文襄六男：文敬元皇后生河間王孝琬，宋氏生河南王孝瑜，王氏生廣寧王孝珩，蘭陵王長恭不得母氏姓，陳氏生安德王延宗，燕氏生漁陽王紹信。
entries.en: Gao Cheng had six sons: Empress Yuan of Wenjing bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian; Lady Song bore Prince Xiaoyu of Henan; Lady Wang bore Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning; Prince Changgong of Lanling never learned his mother's surname; Lady Chen bore Prince Yanzong of Ande; Lady Yan bore Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang.
entries.literal: Wenxiang had six sons: Empress Yuan of Wenjing bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian; Lady Song bore Prince Xiaoyu of Henan; Lady Wang bore Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning; Prince Changgong of Lanling’s mother’s surname could not be learned; Lady Chen bore Prince Yanzong of Ande; Lady Yan bore Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang.

entries.zh: 廣寧王孝珩，文襄第二子也。
entries.en: Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning was Gao Cheng's second son.
entries.literal: Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning was Wenxiang's second son.

entries.zh: 歷位司州牧、尚書令、司空、司徒、錄尚書、大將軍、大司馬。
entries.en: He rose in succession to Governor of Si Province, Chief Minister of the Secretariat, Minister of Works, Minister over the Masses, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand General, and Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: He rose in succession to Governor of Si Province, Chief Minister of the Secretariat, Minister of Works, Minister over the Masses, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand General, and Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 孝珩愛賞人物，學涉經史，好綴文，有伎藝。
entries.en: Xiaoheng loved and appreciated men of talent; he studied the classics and histories, enjoyed composing literary pieces, and possessed artistic skill.
entries.literal: Xiaoheng loved and appreciated men of talent; he studied the classics and histories, enjoyed composing literary pieces, and possessed artistic skill.

entries.zh: 嘗於廳事壁自畫一蒼鷹，見者皆以為真，又作朝士圖，亦當時之妙絕。
entries.en: Once on the wall of his reception hall he painted an azure hawk himself; viewers all took it for real. He also made a painting of court gentlemen — both were marvels of the age.
entries.literal: Once on the wall of his reception hall he painted an azure hawk himself; viewers all took it for real; he also made a painting of court gentlemen — both were marvels of the age.

entries.zh: 文襄六王
entries.en: The Six Princes of Wenxiang
entries.literal: The Six Princes of Wenxiang

entries.zh: 河南康獻王孝瑜，字正德，文襄長子也。
entries.en: Prince Xiaoyu of Henan, posthumously Prince Kangxian, style name Zhengde, was Wenxiang's eldest son.
entries.literal: Prince Kangxian of Henan, Xiaoyu, style name Zhengde, was Wenxiang's eldest son.

entries.zh: 初封河南郡公，齊受禪，進爵為王。
entries.en: He was first made Duke of Henan Commandery. When Qi received the abdication, he was promoted to prince.
entries.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Duke of Henan Commandery; when Qi received the abdication, his title was advanced to prince.

entries.zh: 歷位中書令、司州牧。
entries.en: He later served as Director of the Secretariat and Governor of Si Province.
entries.literal: He successively held the posts of Director of the Secretariat and Governor of Si Province.

entries.zh: 初，孝瑜養於神武宮中，與武成同年相愛。
entries.en: Xiaoyu was initially raised in Shenwu's palace. He and Wucheng were the same age and were deeply attached to one another.
entries.literal: At first Xiaoyu was raised in Shenwu's palace; he and Wucheng were the same age and loved each other.

entries.zh: 將誅楊愔等，孝瑜預其謀。
entries.en: When the plot was made to kill Yang Yin and the others, Xiaoyu was involved in it.
entries.literal: When Yang Yin and the others were about to be executed, Xiaoyu took part in the plot.

entries.zh: 及武成即位，禮遇特隆。
entries.en: After Wucheng ascended the throne, he treated Xiaoyu with exceptional honor.
entries.literal: When Wucheng came to the throne, the courtesy and treatment he gave Xiaoyu were especially generous.

entries.zh: 帝在晉陽，手勑之曰：「吾飲汾清二盃，勸汝於鄴酌兩盃。」
entries.en: While in Jinyang, the emperor sent him a handwritten edict: "I have drunk two cups of Fenqing; you should pour two cups in Ye as well."
entries.literal: While the emperor was at Jinyang, he wrote him an edict in his own hand, saying, "I have drunk two cups of Fenqing; I urge you in Ye to pour two cups too."

entries.zh: 其親愛如此。
entries.en: Such was the affection between them.
entries.literal: Their intimacy and affection were like this.

entries.zh: 孝瑜容貌魁偉，精彩雄毅，謙慎寬厚，兼愛文學，讀書敏速，十行俱下，覆棋不失一道。
entries.en: Xiaoyu was tall and imposing, with a bold, spirited bearing. Modest, cautious, and generous, he loved literature, read with exceptional speed, taking in ten lines at a glance, and when replaying a game never lost track of a single move.
entries.literal: Xiaoyu's appearance was imposing and tall, his spirit bold and resolute; he was modest, cautious, generous, and also loved literature. He read swiftly, taking in ten lines at once, and when replaying a game never missed a single move.

entries.zh: 初，文襄於鄴東起山池遊觀，時俗眩之。
