entries.en: When Wenxiang first built ornamental hills and pools for recreation east of Ye, the fashion dazzled the age.
entries.literal: At first Wenxiang built hills, pools, and pleasure grounds east of Ye, and the fashion dazzled people at the time.

entries.zh: 孝瑜遂於第作水堂、龍舟，植幡矟於舟上，數集諸弟宴射為樂。
entries.en: Xiaoyu followed by building a water hall and dragon boat at his mansion, fitting the vessel with banners and spears and often gathering his brothers there for feasts and archery.
entries.literal: Xiaoyu thereupon built a water hall and dragon boat at his residence, planted banners and spears on the boat, and several times gathered his younger brothers for feasting and archery as amusement.

entries.zh: 武成幸其第，見而悅之，故盛興後園之玩，於是貴賤慕斅，處處營造。
entries.en: When Wucheng visited Xiaoyu's mansion and liked what he saw, rear-garden amusements became all the rage. High and low alike rushed to imitate them, building such displays everywhere.
entries.literal: Wucheng visited his residence, saw it, and was pleased by it; therefore amusements in rear gardens flourished greatly, and high and low alike emulated them, constructing them everywhere.

entries.zh: 孝瑜母，魏吏部尚書宋弁孫也，本魏潁川王斌之妃，為文襄所納，生孝瑜，孝瑜還第，為太妃。
entries.en: Xiaoyu's mother was a granddaughter of Song Bian, Wei's Minister of Personnel. She had originally been consort to Prince Bin of Yingchuan in Wei, but Wenxiang took her into his household and she bore Xiaoyu. When Xiaoyu took up residence in his own mansion, she became Grand Consort.
entries.literal: Xiaoyu's mother was the granddaughter of Song Bian, Minister of Personnel under Wei. She had originally been the consort of Prince Bin of Yingchuan in Wei; Wenxiang took her into his household, and she bore Xiaoyu. When Xiaoyu returned to his residence, she became Grand Consort.

entries.zh: 孝瑜妃，盧正山女，武成胡后之內姊也。
entries.en: Xiaoyu's consort was a daughter of Lu Zhengshan and an elder sister of Emperor Wucheng's Empress Hu.
entries.literal: Xiaoyu's consort was the daughter of Lu Zhengshan and was the elder sister of Wucheng's Empress Hu.

entries.zh: 孝瑜薨後，宋太妃為盧妃所譖訴，武成殺之。
entries.en: After Xiaoyu died, Consort Lu brought slanderous accusations against Grand Consort Song, and Wucheng had Song killed.
entries.literal: After Xiaoyu died, Grand Consort Song was slanderously accused by Consort Lu, and Wucheng killed her.

entries.zh: 武成常使和士開與胡后對坐握槊，孝瑜諫曰：「皇后天下之母，不可與臣下接手。」
entries.en: Gao Zhan often had He Shikai and Empress Hu sit facing each other playing shuo; Xiaoyu remonstrated, saying, "The empress is mother to all under Heaven — she must not touch hands with a subordinate minister."
entries.literal: Wucheng often had He Shikai and Empress Hu sit facing each other playing shuo; Xiaoyu remonstrated, saying, "The empress is mother to all under Heaven — she must not touch hands with a subordinate minister."

entries.zh: 帝深納之。
entries.en: The emperor took this deeply to heart.
entries.literal: The emperor took this deeply to heart.

entries.zh: 後又言趙郡王父死非命，不可親。
entries.en: Later he also said that the Prince of Zhao Commandery, whose father had died by violence, should not be kept close.
entries.literal: Later he also said that the Prince of Zhao Commandery's father had died by violence and should not be kept close.

entries.zh: 由是叡及士開皆側目。
entries.en: On this account both Gao Rui and He Shikai looked askance at him.
entries.literal: On this account both Rui and Shikai looked askance at him.

entries.zh: 士開密告其奢僭，叡又言山東唯聞河南王，不聞有陛下。
entries.en: He Shikai secretly reported his extravagance and presumption; Gao Rui also said that east of the mountains one heard only of the Prince of Henan, and never of the emperor.
entries.literal: Shikai secretly reported his extravagance and presumption; Rui also said that east of the mountains one heard only of the Prince of Henan, and never of Your Majesty.

entries.zh: 帝由是忌之。
entries.en: The emperor on this account came to resent him.
entries.literal: The emperor on this account came to resent him.

entries.zh: 尒朱御女名摩女，本事太后，孝瑜先與之通，後因太子婚夜，孝瑜竊與之言。
entries.en: An Erzhu palace woman named Monü had originally served the empress dowager; Xiaoyu had first had relations with her, and later, on the night of the crown prince's wedding, stole away to speak with her.
entries.literal: An Erzhu palace woman named Monü had originally served the empress dowager; Xiaoyu had first had relations with her, and later, on the night of the crown prince's wedding, Xiaoyu stole away to speak with her.

entries.zh: 武成大怒，頓飲其酒三十七盃。
entries.en: Gao Zhan was greatly enraged and made him drink thirty-seven cups of wine in succession.
entries.literal: Wucheng was greatly enraged and made him drink thirty-seven cups of wine in succession.

entries.zh: 體至肥大，腰帶十圍。
entries.en: His body was extremely corpulent, his waist ten arm-spans around.
entries.literal: His body was extremely corpulent, his waistband ten arm-spans around.

entries.zh: 使婁子彥載以出，酖之於車。
entries.en: He had Lou Ziyan carry him out and poison him in the carriage.
entries.literal: He had Lou Ziyan carry him out and poison him in the carriage.

entries.zh: 至西華門，煩熱躁悶，投水而絕。
entries.en: At the West Flowery Gate he grew feverish and stifled with distress, threw himself into the water, and died.
entries.literal: At the West Flowery Gate he grew feverish and stifled with distress, threw himself into the water, and died.

entries.zh: 贈太尉、錄尚書事。
entries.en: He was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: He was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 子弘節嗣。
entries.en: His son Hongjie succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Hongjie succeeded.

entries.zh: 後主自晉州敗奔鄴，詔王公議於含光殿。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor fled in defeat from Jinzhou to Ye, an edict summoned the princes and dukes to deliberate in the Hall of Contained Light.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor fled in defeat from Jinzhou to Ye, an edict summoned the princes and dukes to deliberate in the Hall of Contained Light.

entries.zh: 孝珩以大敵既深，事藉機變。
entries.en: Xiaoheng said that with the great enemy already pressing deep, affairs must rely on swift adaptation.
entries.literal: Xiaoheng said that with the great enemy already pressing deep, affairs must rely on swift adaptation.

entries.zh: 宜使任城王領幽州道兵入土門，揚聲趣并州；
entries.en: The Prince of Rencheng should be sent to lead the Youzhou-route troops through Tumen Pass, proclaiming that he was marching on Bing Province;
entries.literal: The Prince of Rencheng should be sent to lead the Youzhou-route troops through Tumen Pass, proclaiming that he was marching on Bing Province;

entries.zh: 獨孤永業領洛州兵趣潼關，揚聲趣長安；
entries.en: Dugu Yongye should lead the Luozhou troops toward Tong Pass, proclaiming that he was marching on Chang'an;
entries.literal: Dugu Yongye should lead the Luozhou troops toward Tong Pass, proclaiming that he was marching on Chang'an;

entries.zh: 臣請領京畿兵出滏口，鼓行逆戰。
entries.en: your servant asks to lead the capital-region troops out through Fukou and advance with drums beating to meet the enemy.
entries.literal: your servant asks to lead the capital-region troops out through Fukou and advance with drums beating to meet the enemy.

entries.zh: 敵聞南北有兵，自然潰散。
entries.en: When the enemy heard that there were armies north and south, they would naturally scatter in rout.
entries.literal: When the enemy heard that there were armies north and south, they would naturally scatter in rout.

entries.zh: 又請出宮人珍寶賜將士，帝不能用。
entries.en: He also asked that palace women and precious objects be brought out to reward the officers and soldiers; the emperor would not adopt this.
entries.literal: He also asked that palace women and precious objects be brought out to reward the officers and soldiers; the emperor would not adopt this.

entries.zh: 承光即位，以孝珩為太宰。
entries.en: When Chengguang succeeded to the throne, Xiaoheng was made Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: When Chengguang succeeded to the throne, Xiaoheng was made Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 與呼延族、莫多婁敬顯、尉相願同謀，期正月五日，孝珩於千秋門斬高阿那肱，相願在內以禁兵應之，族與敬顯自遊豫園勒兵出。
entries.en: He joined with Huyan Zu, Moduolou Jingxian, and Wei Xiangyuan in a common plot, fixing the fifth day of the first month: Xiaoheng was to behead Gao Anaogong at the Gate of a Thousand Autumns; Xiangyuan inside would respond with the forbidden guard; Zu and Jingxian would lead troops out from the Pleasure Garden.
entries.literal: He joined with Huyan Zu, Moduolou Jingxian, and Wei Xiangyuan in a common plot, fixing the fifth day of the first month: Xiaoheng was to behead Gao Anaogong at the Gate of a Thousand Autumns; Xiangyuan inside would respond with the forbidden guard; Zu and Jingxian would lead troops out from the Pleasure Garden.

entries.zh: 既而阿那肱從別宅取便路入宮，事不果。
entries.en: Before long Anaogong took a shortcut from another residence into the palace, and the affair did not succeed.
entries.literal: Before long Anaogong took a shortcut from another residence into the palace, and the affair did not succeed.

entries.zh: 乃求出拒西軍，謂阿那肱、韓長鸞、陳德信等云：「朝廷不賜遣擊賊，豈不畏孝珩反耶？
entries.en: He then asked to go out to resist the western army, saying to Anaogong, Han Changluan, Chen Dexin, and the others, "The court will not grant permission to go out and strike the enemy — are you not afraid Xiaoheng will rebel?
entries.literal: He then asked to go out to resist the western army, saying to Anaogong, Han Changluan, Chen Dexin, and the others, "The court will not grant permission to go out and strike the enemy — are you not afraid Xiaoheng will rebel?

entries.zh: 孝珩破宇文邕，遂至長安，反時何與國家事。
entries.en: If Xiaoheng defeats Yuwen Yong and then reaches Chang'an, what will rebellion have to do with the affairs of the state?
entries.literal: If Xiaoheng defeats Yuwen Yong and then reaches Chang'an, what will rebellion have to do with the affairs of the state?

entries.zh: 以今日之急，猶作如此猜疑。」
entries.en: At today's urgent pass you still harbor such suspicions."
entries.literal: At today's urgent pass you still harbor such suspicions."

entries.zh: 高、韓恐其變，出孝珩為滄州刺史。
entries.en: Gao and Han, fearing he might change, sent Xiaoheng out as Governor of Cang Province.
entries.literal: Gao and Han, fearing he might change, sent Xiaoheng out as Governor of Cang Province.

entries.zh: 至州，以五千人會任城王於信都，共為匡復計。
entries.en: When he reached the province, he joined the Prince of Rencheng at Xindu with five thousand men to plan together for restoration.
entries.literal: When he reached the province, he joined the Prince of Rencheng at Xindu with five thousand men to plan together for restoration.

entries.zh: 周齊王憲來伐，兵弱不能敵。
entries.en: Prince Xian of Zhou came to attack; their forces were weak and could not resist.
entries.literal: Prince Xian of Zhou came to attack; their forces were weak and could not resist.

entries.zh: 怒曰：「由高阿那肱小人，吾道窮矣！」
entries.en: In anger he said, "Because of the petty man Gao Anaogong, my road is at an end!"
entries.literal: In anger he said, "Because of the petty man Gao Anaogong, my road is at an end!"

entries.zh: 齊叛臣乞扶令和以矟刺孝珩墜馬，奴白澤以身扞之，孝珩猶傷數處，遂見虜。
entries.en: A Qi turncoat, Qifu Linghe, stabbed Xiaoheng with a spear and knocked him from his horse; the slave Baize shielded him with his body; Xiaoheng still suffered wounds in several places and was then taken captive.
entries.literal: A Qi turncoat, Qifu Linghe, stabbed Xiaoheng with a spear and knocked him from his horse; the slave Baize shielded him with his body; Xiaoheng still suffered wounds in several places and was then taken captive.

entries.zh: 齊王憲問孝珩齊亡所由，孝珩自陳國難，辭淚俱下，俯仰有節。
entries.en: Prince Xian of Zhou asked Xiaoheng the reason for Qi's fall; Xiaoheng himself explained the state's calamity, words and tears together falling, his bearing composed in every movement.
entries.literal: Prince Xian of Zhou asked Xiaoheng the reason for Qi's fall; Xiaoheng himself explained the state's calamity, words and tears together falling, his bearing composed in every movement.

entries.zh: 憲為之改容，親為洗創傅藥，禮遇甚厚。
entries.en: Xian changed countenance on his account, personally washed his wounds and applied medicine, and treated him with great courtesy.
entries.literal: Xian changed countenance on his account, personally washed his wounds and applied medicine, and treated him with great courtesy.

entries.zh: 孝珩獨歎曰：「李穆叔言齊氏二十八年，今果然矣。
entries.en: Xiaoheng sighed alone and said, "Li Mushu said the Qi house would last twenty-eight years — today it has indeed come to pass.
entries.literal: Xiaoheng sighed alone and said, "Li Mushu said the Qi house would last twenty-eight years — today it has indeed come to pass.

entries.zh: 自神武皇帝以外，吾諸父兄弟無一人得至四十者，命也。
entries.en: Apart from Gao Huan, not one of my fathers and brothers among the clan reached forty — such is fate.
entries.literal: Apart from the Shenwu Emperor, not one of my fathers and brothers among the clan reached forty — such is fate.

entries.zh: 嗣君無獨見之明，宰相非柱石之寄，恨不得握兵符，受廟算，展我心力耳。」
entries.en: The succeeding ruler lacked independent insight; the chief ministers were no pillars to rely upon — I only regret that I could not grasp the tally of command, receive the plans of the temple, and give full play to the strength of my heart."
entries.literal: The succeeding ruler lacked independent insight; the chief ministers were no pillars to rely upon — I only regret that I could not grasp the tally of command, receive the plans of the temple, and give full play to the strength of my heart."

entries.zh: 至長安，依例授開府、縣侯。
entries.en: When he reached Chang'an, by precedent he was appointed Opener of an Office (kaifu) and Marquis of a county.
entries.literal: When he reached Chang'an, by precedent he was appointed Opener of an Office (kaifu) and Marquis of a county.

entries.zh: 後周武帝在雲陽，宴齊君臣，自彈胡琵琶，命孝珩吹笛。
entries.en: Later, when Emperor Wu of Zhou was at Yunyang, he feasted the Qi ruler and ministers, himself playing the barbarian pipa and ordering Xiaoheng to play the flute.
entries.literal: Later, when Emperor Wu of Zhou was at Yunyang, he feasted the Qi ruler and ministers, himself playing the barbarian pipa and ordering Xiaoheng to play the flute.

entries.zh: 辭曰：「亡國之音，不足聽也。」
entries.en: He declined, saying, "The music of a fallen state is not worth hearing."
entries.literal: He declined, saying, "The music of a fallen state is not worth hearing."

entries.zh: 固命之，舉笛裁至口，淚下嗚咽，武帝乃止。
entries.en: Though pressed he obeyed; he raised the flute barely to his lips, tears falling in sobs, and Emperor Wu then stopped.
entries.literal: Though pressed he obeyed; he raised the flute barely to his lips, tears falling in sobs, and Emperor Wu then stopped.

entries.zh: 其年十月，疾甚，啟歸葬山東，從之。
entries.en: In the tenth month of that year his illness grew severe; he petitioned to be buried back in Shandong, and permission was granted.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of that year his illness grew severe; he petitioned to be buried back in Shandong, and permission was granted.

entries.zh: 尋卒，令還葬鄴。
entries.en: Before long he died; an order was issued to return his body for burial at Ye.
entries.literal: Before long he died; an order was issued to return his body for burial at Ye.

entries.zh: 孝琬以文襄世嫡，驕矜自負。
entries.en: Xiaowan, as Gao Cheng's legitimate heir of the generation, was proud and self-important.
entries.literal: Xiaowan, as Wenxiang's legitimate heir of the generation, was proud and self-important.

entries.zh: 河南王之死，諸王在宮內莫敢舉聲，唯孝琬大哭而出。
entries.en: At Prince Xiaoyu of Henan's death, the princes within the palace did not dare raise a sound; only Xiaowan wept loudly and went out.
entries.literal: At the Prince of Henan's death, the princes within the palace did not dare raise a sound; only Xiaowan wept loudly and went out.

entries.zh: 又怨執政，為草人而射之。
entries.en: He also resented those in power and made a straw effigy which he shot at.
entries.literal: He also resented those in power and made a straw effigy which he shot at.

entries.zh: 和士開與祖珽譖之，云：「草人擬聖躬也。
entries.en: He Shikai and Zu Ting slandered him, saying, "The straw effigy was modeled on the sacred person.
entries.literal: He Shikai and Zu Ting slandered him, saying, "The straw effigy was modeled on the sacred person.

entries.zh: 又前突厥至州，孝琬脫兜鍪抵地，云『豈是老嫗，須著此』。
entries.en: Moreover, when the Turks earlier came to the province, Xiaowan took off his helmet and cast it to the ground, saying, 'Am I an old woman that I must wear this?'
entries.literal: Moreover, when the Turks earlier came to the province, Xiaowan took off his helmet and cast it to the ground, saying, 'Am I an old woman that I must wear this?'

entries.zh: 此言屬大家也。」
entries.en: These words were directed at Your Majesty."
entries.literal: These words were directed at Your Majesty."

entries.zh: 初，魏世謠言：「河南種穀河北生，白楊樹頭金雞鳴。」
entries.en: Earlier, in Wei times there was a rhyme: "Henan plants grain, Hebei gives birth; on the white poplar's crown a golden cock crows."
entries.literal: Earlier, in Wei times there was a rhyme: "Henan plants grain, Hebei gives birth; on the white poplar's crown a golden cock crows."

entries.zh: 珽以說曰：「河南、河北，河間也。
entries.en: Ting used this to explain, saying, "Henan and Hebei mean Hejian.
entries.literal: Ting used this to explain, saying, "Henan and Hebei mean Hejian.

entries.zh: 金雞鳴，孝琬將建金雞而大赦。」
entries.en: The golden cock's crow means Xiaowan will build a golden cock and proclaim a great amnesty."
entries.literal: The golden cock's crow means Xiaowan will build a golden cock and proclaim a great amnesty."

entries.zh: 帝頗惑之。
entries.en: The emperor was quite swayed.
entries.literal: The emperor was quite swayed.

entries.zh: 時孝琬得佛牙，置於第內，夜有神光。
entries.en: At the time Xiaowan had obtained a Buddha tooth and placed it in his residence; at night there was divine light.
entries.literal: At the time Xiaowan had obtained a Buddha tooth and placed it in his residence; at night there was divine light.

entries.zh: 昭玄都法順請以奏聞，不從。
entries.en: Fashun of Zhaoxuan Abbey asked to report it to the throne; he would not consent.
entries.literal: Fashun of Zhaoxuan Abbey asked to report it to the throne; he would not consent.

entries.zh: 帝聞，使搜之，得鎮庫矟幡數百。
entries.en: When the emperor heard of it, he sent men to search the residence and found several hundred spears and banners from the arsenal.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he sent men to search the residence and found several hundred spears and banners from the arsenal.

entries.zh: 帝聞之，以為反。
entries.en: When the emperor heard of this, he took it for rebellion.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard of this, he took it for rebellion.

entries.zh: 訊其諸姬，有陳氏者無寵，誣對曰「孝琬畫作陛下形哭之」，然實是文襄像，孝琬時時對之泣。
entries.en: His concubines were interrogated; one surnamed Chen, who had no favor, falsely answered that "Xiaowan painted the emperor's likeness and wept before it" — but in truth it was a portrait of Gao Cheng, before which Xiaowan often wept.
entries.literal: His concubines were interrogated; one surnamed Chen, who had no favor, falsely answered that "Xiaowan painted the emperor's likeness and wept before it" — but in truth it was a portrait of Wenxiang, before which Xiaowan often wept.

entries.zh: 帝怒，使武纫赫連輔玄倒鞭撾之。
entries.en: The emperor was enraged and ordered the guard Helian Fuxuan to beat him with an inverted whip.
entries.literal: The emperor was enraged and ordered the guard Helian Fuxuan to beat him with an inverted whip.

entries.zh: 孝琬呼阿叔，帝怒曰：「誰是爾叔？
entries.en: Xiaowan cried out "Uncle!" The emperor in anger said, "Who is your uncle?
entries.literal: Xiaowan cried out "Uncle!" The emperor in anger said, "Who is your uncle?

entries.zh: 敢喚我作叔！」
entries.en: You dare call me uncle!"
entries.literal: You dare call me uncle!"

entries.zh: 孝琬曰：「神武皇帝嫡孫，文襄皇帝嫡子，魏孝靜皇帝外甥，何為不得喚作叔也？」
entries.en: Xiaowan said, "Grandson of Gao Huan, son of Gao Cheng, nephew of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei — why may I not call you uncle?"
entries.literal: Xiaowan said, "Grandson of Emperor Shenwu, son of Emperor Wenxiang, nephew of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei — why may I not call you uncle?"

entries.zh: 帝愈怒，折其兩脛而死。
entries.en: The emperor grew still more enraged and broke both his shins, and he died.
entries.literal: The emperor grew still more enraged and broke both his shins, and he died.

entries.zh: 瘞諸西山，帝崩後，乃改葬。
entries.en: He was buried on the western hills; after the emperor's death he was reinterred.
entries.literal: He was buried on the western hills; after the emperor's death he was reinterred.

entries.zh: 子正禮嗣，幼聰穎，能誦左氏春秋。
entries.en: His son Zhengli succeeded; in youth he was clever and sharp, and could recite the Zuo Tradition.
entries.literal: His son Zhengli succeeded; in youth he was clever and sharp, and could recite the Zuo Tradition.

entries.zh: 齊亡，遷綿州卒。
entries.en: When Qi fell he was transferred to Mian Prefecture, where he died.
entries.literal: When Qi fell he was transferred to Mian Prefecture, where he died.

entries.zh: 蘭陵武王長恭，一名孝瓘，文襄第四子也。
entries.en: Prince Wu of Lanling, Changgong — also named Xiaoguan — was Gao Cheng's fourth son.
entries.literal: Prince Wu of Lanling, Changgong — also named Xiaoguan — was Wenxiang's fourth son.

entries.zh: 累遷并州刺史。
entries.en: He was promoted in succession to Governor of Bing Province.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Governor of Bing Province.

entries.zh: 突厥入晉陽，長恭盡力擊之。
entries.en: When the Turks entered Jinyang, Changgong exerted himself to the utmost in striking them.
entries.literal: When the Turks entered Jinyang, Changgong exerted himself to the utmost in striking them.

entries.zh: 芒山之敗，長恭為中軍，率五百騎再入周軍，遂至金墉之下，被圍甚急，城上人弗識，長恭免冑示之面，乃下弩手救之，於是大捷。
entries.en: At the defeat at Mang Mountain, Changgong served as central army commander; leading five hundred horsemen he entered the Zhou army a second time and reached beneath the walls of Jinyong; besieged in extreme peril, those on the walls did not recognize him; Changgong removed his helmet to show his face, and only then did they lower crossbowmen to rescue him — whereupon there was a great victory.
entries.literal: At the defeat at Mang Mountain, Changgong served as central army commander; leading five hundred horsemen he entered the Zhou army a second time and reached beneath the walls of Jinyong; besieged in extreme peril, those on the walls did not recognize him; Changgong removed his helmet to show his face, and only then did they lower crossbowmen to rescue him — whereupon there was a great victory.

entries.zh: 武士共歌謠之，為蘭陵王入陣曲是也。
entries.en: The warriors together sang ballads of it — this is the Entry of the Prince of Lanling into Battle.
entries.literal: The warriors together sang ballads of it — this is the Entry of the Prince of Lanling into Battle.

entries.zh: 歷司州牧、青瀛二州，頗受財貨。
entries.en: He served in succession as Governor of Si Province and of Qing and Ying provinces, and rather accepted goods and wealth.
entries.literal: He served in succession as Governor of Si Province and of Qing and Ying provinces, and rather accepted goods and wealth.

entries.zh: 後為太尉，與段韶討栢谷，又攻定陽。
entries.en: Later he became Grand Commandant; with Duan Shao he attacked Baigu, and again attacked Dingyang.
entries.literal: Later he became Grand Commandant; with Duan Shao he attacked Baigu, and again attacked Dingyang.

entries.zh: 韶病，長恭總其衆。
entries.en: Shao fell ill; Changgong took overall command of his forces.
entries.literal: Shao fell ill; Changgong took overall command of his forces.

entries.zh: 前後以戰功別封鉅鹿、長樂、樂平、高陽等郡公。
entries.en: Before and after, for military merit he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Julu, Changle, Leping, Gaoyang, and other commanderies.
entries.literal: Before and after, for military merit he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Julu, Changle, Leping, Gaoyang, and other commanderies.

entries.zh: 安德王延宗，文襄第五子也。
entries.en: Prince Yanzong of Ande was the fifth son of Gao Cheng.
entries.literal: Prince Yanzong of Ande was the fifth son of Wenxiang.

entries.zh: 母陳氏，廣陽王妓也。
entries.en: His mother was Lady Chen, a courtesan of the Prince of Guangyang.
entries.literal: His mother was Lady Chen, a courtesan of the Prince of Guangyang.

entries.zh: 延宗幼為文宣所養，年十二，猶騎置腹上，令溺己臍中，抱之曰：「可憐止有此一箇。」
entries.en: Yanzong was raised from childhood by Gao Yang; even at twelve the emperor would set him astride his belly, make him urinate into his navel, hold him close and say, "Poor child — I have only this one."
entries.literal: Yanzong was raised from childhood by Wenxuan; even at twelve Wenxuan would set him astride his belly, make him urinate into his navel, hold him close and say, "Pitiful — I have only this one."

entries.zh: 問欲作何王，對曰：「欲作衝天王。」
entries.en: He asked what title the boy wanted; Yanzong answered, "I want to be Prince Heaven-Storm."
entries.literal: He asked what prince Yanzong wished to be; the boy answered, "I wish to be Prince Storm-the-Heavens."

entries.zh: 文宣問楊愔，愔曰：「天下無此郡名，願使安於德。」
entries.en: Gao Yang asked Yang Yin; Yang said, "No such commandery exists in the realm — let him dwell secure in virtue instead."
entries.literal: Wenxuan asked Yang Yin; Yang said, "There is no such commandery in the realm — I wish he may dwell secure in virtue."

entries.zh: 於是封安德焉。
entries.en: And so he was enfeoffed Prince of Ande.
entries.literal: And so he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ande.

entries.zh: 為定州刺史，於樓上大便，使人在下張口承之。
entries.en: As governor of Ding Province he would defecate from an upper story while men below opened their mouths to receive it.
entries.literal: As governor of Ding Province, he would defecate from an upper story, having men below open their mouths to catch it.

entries.zh: 以蒸嚢糝和人糞以飼左右，有難色者鞭之。
entries.en: He mixed steamed grain with human dung to feed his attendants and whipped any who looked disgusted.
entries.literal: He mixed steamed grain with human dung to feed his attendants, and whipped any who showed revulsion.

entries.zh: 孝昭帝聞之，使趙道德就州杖之一百。
entries.en: Emperor Gao Yan heard and sent Zhao Daode to the province to beat him a hundred strokes.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaozhao heard of it and sent Zhao Daode to the province to beat him a hundred strokes.

entries.zh: 道德以延宗受杖不謹，又加三十。
entries.en: Daode, finding Yanzong insufficiently deferential under the rod, added thirty strokes.
entries.literal: Daode, seeing that Yanzong did not take the beating with proper deference, added thirty more.

entries.zh: 又以囚試刀，驗其利鈍。
entries.en: He also tested blades on prisoners to see whether they were sharp or dull.
entries.literal: He also tested blades on prisoners to see whether they were sharp or dull.

entries.zh: 驕縱多不法。
entries.en: Arrogant and unrestrained, he broke the law in many ways.
entries.literal: Arrogant and unrestrained, he committed many unlawful acts.

entries.zh: 武成使撻之，殺其昵近九人，從是深自改悔。
entries.en: Gao Zhan had him flogged and killed nine of his closest intimates; from that Yanzong deeply repented.
entries.literal: Wucheng had him flogged and killed nine of his closest intimates; from this Yanzong deeply repented.

entries.zh: 蘭陵王芒山凱捷，自陳兵勢，諸兄弟咸壯之。
entries.en: When Prince Changgong of Lanling reported his victory at Mangshan and described his forces, all his brothers praised him.
entries.literal: When Prince Changgong of Lanling reported his victory at Mangshan and described his military strength, all the brothers praised him.

entries.zh: 延宗獨曰：「四兄非大丈夫，何不乘勝徑入？
entries.en: Yanzong alone said, "Fourth brother is no true man — why not press the victory and march straight in?
entries.literal: Yanzong alone said, "Fourth brother is no true man — why did he not press the advantage and march straight in?

entries.zh: 使延宗當此勢，關西豈得復存。」
entries.en: Had Yanzong held that position, how could the lands west of the passes still stand?"
entries.literal: If Yanzong were in that position, how could the lands west of the passes still stand?"

entries.zh: 及蘭陵死，妃鄭氏以頸珠施佛。
entries.en: When Changgong of Lanling died, his consort Lady Zheng offered her neck-pearl to the Buddha.
entries.literal: When Changgong of Lanling died, his consort Lady Zheng offered her neck-pearl to the Buddha.

entries.zh: 廣寧王使贖之。
entries.en: The Prince of Guangning sent men to redeem it.
entries.literal: The Prince of Guangning sent men to redeem it.

entries.zh: 延宗手書以諫，而淚滿紙。
entries.en: Yanzong wrote a letter of remonstrance by hand, the page soaked with tears.
entries.literal: Yanzong wrote a letter of remonstrance by hand, tears flooding the page.

entries.zh: 河間死，延宗哭之淚亦甚。
entries.en: When the Prince of Hejian died, Yanzong wept for him with equal grief.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Hejian died, Yanzong wept for him with equal grief.

entries.zh: 又為草人以像武成，鞭而訊之曰：「何故殺我兄！」
entries.en: He also made a straw effigy in Gao Zhan's likeness, whipped it and demanded, "Why did you kill my brother!"
entries.literal: He also made a straw effigy in Wucheng's likeness, whipped it and interrogated it: "Why did you kill my brother!"

entries.zh: 奴告之，武成覆臥延宗於地，馬鞭撾之二百，幾死。
entries.en: A servant reported it; Gao Zhan had Yanzong thrown face-down and lashed two hundred strokes with a horsewhip, nearly killing him.
entries.literal: A servant reported it; Wucheng had Yanzong thrown face-down to the ground and lashed two hundred strokes with a horsewhip, nearly killing him.

entries.zh: 後歷司徒、太尉。
entries.en: Later he served as minister over the masses and grand commandant.
entries.literal: Later he served successively as Minister over the Masses and Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 長恭貌柔心壯，音容兼美。
entries.en: Changgong looked gentle but his heart was bold; in voice and bearing alike he was beautiful.
entries.literal: Changgong's face was gentle but his heart was bold; voice and bearing alike were beautiful.

entries.zh: 為將躬勤細事，每得甘美，雖一瓜數果，必與將士共之。
entries.en: As a general he personally saw to the smallest things; whenever he had anything sweet or fine — even a melon or a few fruits — he shared it with his officers and men.
entries.literal: As a general he personally attended to the smallest matters; whenever he obtained anything sweet or fine, even a single melon or a few fruits, he always shared them with his officers and men.

entries.zh: 初在瀛州，行參軍陽士深表列其贓，免官。
entries.en: While governor of Ying Province, the acting adjutant Yang Shishen submitted a detailed list of his corruption, and he was dismissed.
entries.literal: At first, while in Ying Province, the acting adjutant Yang Shishen submitted a detailed list of his corrupt acts, and he was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 及討定陽，士深在軍，恐禍及。
entries.en: During the campaign against Dingyang, Shishen was with the army and feared retribution.
entries.literal: When they campaigned against Dingyang, Shishen was with the army, fearing that retribution would reach him.

entries.zh: 長恭聞之曰：「吾本無此意。」
entries.en: Changgong heard and said, "That was never my intent."
entries.literal: Changgong heard of it and said, "I never had such an intention."

entries.zh: 乃求小失，杖士深二十以安之。
entries.en: He then found a minor fault, had Shishen beaten twenty strokes, and put the matter to rest.
entries.literal: He then found a minor fault, had Shishen beaten twenty strokes, and so reassured him.

entries.zh: 嘗入朝而僕從盡散，唯有一人，長恭獨還，無所譴罰。
entries.en: Once on his way to court his attendants all fled save one; Changgong returned alone and punished no one.
entries.literal: Once when he went to court his attendants all scattered, and only one remained; Changgong returned alone without punishing anyone.

entries.zh: 武成賞其功，命賈護為買妾二十人，唯受其一。
entries.en: Gao Zhan rewarded his service and ordered Jia Hu to buy him twenty concubines; he accepted only one.
entries.literal: Wucheng rewarded his achievements and ordered Jia Hu to buy twenty concubines for him; he accepted only one.

entries.zh: 有千金責券，臨死日，盡燔之。
entries.en: He held promissory notes worth a thousand gold; on the day of his death he burned them all.
entries.literal: He held promissory notes worth a thousand gold; on the day he died, he burned them all.

entries.zh: 及平陽之役，後主自禦之，命延宗率右軍先戰，城下擒周開府宗挺。
entries.en: At the battle of Pingyang, Houzhu personally took command, ordering Yanzong to lead the right wing in the first attack; below the walls they captured Zhou's Opening-Office General Zong Ting.
entries.literal: At the battle of Pingyang, Houzhu personally took command, ordering Yanzong to lead the right wing in the first engagement; below the walls they captured Zhou's general Zong Ting.

entries.zh: 及大戰，延宗以麾下再入周軍，莫不披靡。
entries.en: In the great battle Yanzong led his men twice into the Zhou army, and none could stand before them.
entries.literal: In the great battle, Yanzong with his troops charged twice into the Zhou army, and none could stand before them.

entries.zh: 諸軍敗，延宗獨全軍。
entries.en: The other armies broke; Yanzong alone kept his force intact.
entries.literal: The other armies were defeated; Yanzong alone kept his force intact.

entries.zh: 後主將奔晉陽，延宗言：「大家但在營莫動，以兵馬付臣，臣能破之。」
entries.en: As Houzhu prepared to flee to Jinyang, Yanzong said, "Your Majesty need only stay in camp; give me the army and I can break them."
entries.literal: As Houzhu was about to flee to Jinyang, Yanzong said, "Your Majesty need only remain in camp without moving; give me command of the cavalry and infantry and I can break them."

entries.zh: 帝不納。
entries.en: The emperor would not listen.
entries.literal: The emperor would not accept this.

entries.zh: 及至并州，又聞周軍已入雀鼠谷，乃以延宗為相國、并州刺史，總山西兵事。
entries.en: At Bing Province, hearing Zhou troops had entered Queyu Valley, he made Yanzong chancellor and governor of Bing Province, giving him overall command of military affairs west of the mountains.
entries.literal: When they reached Bing Province and heard that Zhou troops had entered Queyu Valley, he made Yanzong Chancellor and governor of Bing Province, putting him in overall charge of military affairs west of the mountains.

entries.zh: 謂曰：「并州，阿兄自取，兒今去也。」
entries.en: He told him, "Bing Province — elder brother takes it for himself; your son leaves now."
entries.literal: He said to him, "Bing Province — elder brother takes it for himself; your son departs now."

entries.zh: 延宗曰：「陛下為社稷莫動，臣為陛下出死力戰。」
entries.en: Yanzong said, "Your Majesty must not stir for the altars of state; your servant will fight to the death for you."
entries.literal: Yanzong said, "Your Majesty must not move for the sake of the altars of state; your servant will fight to the death for Your Majesty."

entries.zh: 駱提婆曰：「至尊計已成，王不得輒沮。」
entries.en: Luotipo said, "His Majesty's plan is set — the prince must not obstruct it."
entries.literal: Luotipo said, "His Majesty's plan is already set — the prince must not obstruct it."

entries.zh: 後主竟奔鄴。
entries.en: Houzhu fled to Ye after all.
entries.literal: Houzhu fled to Ye after all.

entries.zh: 在并將率咸請曰：「王若不作天子，諸人實不能出死力。」
entries.en: The commanders at Bing all petitioned: "If the prince will not become emperor, we truly cannot fight to the death."
entries.literal: The commanders at Bing all petitioned: "If the prince will not become Son of Heaven, we truly cannot fight to the death."

entries.zh: 延宗不得已，即皇帝位，下詔曰：「武平孱弱，政由宦豎，釁結蕭牆，盜起疆埸。
entries.en: Yanzong had no choice but to take the throne and issued an edict: "The Wuping reign was feeble; government lay with eunuchs; strife rose within the palace walls and invaders on the borders.
entries.literal: Yanzong had no choice but to take the imperial throne, and issued an edict: "The Wuping reign was feeble; government lay in the hands of eunuchs; strife arose within the palace walls, and invaders rose on the borders.

entries.zh: 斬關夜遁，莫知所之，則我高祖之業將墜於地。
entries.en: He who should hold the passes fled by night, none knew where — and our founder's enterprise was about to crash to earth.
entries.literal: He who should hold the passes fled by night with none knowing whither — and our Gaozu's enterprise was about to crash to earth.

entries.zh: 王公卿士，猥見推逼，今便祗承寶位。
entries.en: Lords and ministers, though unworthy, have pressed me; I now reverently take the throne.
entries.literal: Lords and ministers, though unworthy, have pressed me; I now reverently assume the sacred throne.

entries.zh: 可大赦天下，改武平七年為德昌元年。」
entries.en: Let there be a general amnesty; change the seventh year of Wuping to the first year of Dechang."
entries.literal: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm; change the seventh year of Wuping to the first year of Dechang."

entries.zh: 以晉昌王唐邕為宰輔，齊昌王莫多婁敬顯、沭陽王和阿于子、右纫大將軍段暢、武纫將軍相里僧伽、開府韓骨胡、侯莫陳洛州為爪牙。
entries.en: He made Prince Tang Yong of Jinchang chief minister; Prince Moduolou Jingxian of Qichang; Prince Ah-Yuzi of Shuyang; Right Guard General Duan Chang; Martial Guard General Xiangli Sengqie; Opening-Office General Han Guhu; and Houmochen Luozhou his strong arms.
entries.literal: He appointed Prince Tang Yong of Jinchang as chief minister; Prince Moduolou Jingxian of Qichang; Prince Ah-Yuzi of Shuyang; Right Guard General Duan Chang; Martial Guard General Xiangli Sengqie; General of Opening Gates Han Guhu; and Houmochen Luozhou as his strong arms.

entries.zh: 衆聞之，不召而至者，前後相屬。
entries.en: When word spread, men came unbidden in endless succession.
entries.literal: When the multitudes heard, those who came without being summoned followed one after another.

entries.zh: 延宗容貌充壯，坐則仰，偃則伏，人笑之，乃赫然奮發。
entries.en: Yanzong was full and sturdy of build; seated he leaned back, lying down he sprawled — people laughed until he suddenly blazed into action.
entries.literal: Yanzong was full and sturdy of build; seated he leaned back, lying down he sprawled flat — people laughed at him until he suddenly blazed into action.

entries.zh: 氣力絕異，馳騁行陣，勁捷若飛。
entries.en: His strength was beyond compare; charging through battle lines he was swift and fierce as flight.
entries.literal: His strength was beyond compare; charging through battle lines he was swift and fierce as flight itself.

entries.zh: 傾覆府藏及後宮美女，以賜將士，籍沒內參千餘家。
entries.en: He emptied the treasury and the palace women to reward the troops and confiscated the property of more than a thousand inner attendants.
entries.literal: He emptied the treasury and the palace beauties to reward the troops, and confiscated the property of more than a thousand inner attendants.

entries.zh: 後主謂近臣曰：「我寧使周得并州，不欲安德得之。」
entries.en: Houzhu told his close attendants, "I would rather Zhou take Bing Province than let Ande have it."
entries.literal: Houzhu told his close attendants, "I would rather let Zhou take Bing Province than let Ande have it."

entries.zh: 左右曰：「理然。」
entries.en: Those beside him said, "That is only reasonable."
entries.literal: Those beside him said, "That is only reasonable."

entries.zh: 延宗見士卒，皆親執手，陳辭自稱名，流涕嗚咽。
entries.en: When Yanzong met the soldiers he grasped each man's hand, spoke his own name, weeping and choking with sobs.
entries.literal: When Yanzong met the soldiers he personally grasped each man's hand, spoke his own name in clear words, weeping and choking with sobs.

entries.zh: 红皆爭為死，童兒女子亦乘屋攘袂，投蝋石以禦周軍。
entries.en: All competed to die for him; boys and girls too climbed rooftops, baring their sleeves, and hurled wax-stones at the Zhou army.
entries.literal: All competed to die for him; boys and girls too climbed rooftops, baring their sleeves, and hurled wax-stones at the Zhou army.

entries.zh: 特進、開府那盧安生守太谷，以萬兵叛。
entries.en: Special Advance and Opening-Office General Nalu Ansheng held Taigu with ten thousand men and rebelled.
entries.literal: Special Advance and General of Opening Gates Nalu Ansheng held Taigu with ten thousand men and rebelled.

entries.zh: 周軍圍晉陽，望之如黑雲四合。
entries.en: Zhou troops besieged Jinyang; seen from afar they were like black clouds closing on every side.
entries.literal: Zhou troops besieged Jinyang; seen from afar they were like black clouds closing on every side.

entries.zh: 延宗命莫多婁敬顯、韓骨胡拒城南，和阿于子、段暢拒城東。
entries.en: Yanzong ordered Moduolou Jingxian and Han Guhu to hold the south wall, and Ah-Yuzi and Duan Chang the east.
entries.literal: Yanzong ordered Moduolou Jingxian and Han Guhu to hold the south wall, and Ah-Yuzi and Duan Chang the east.

entries.zh: 延宗親當周齊王於城北，奮大矟，往來督戰，所向無前。
entries.en: Yanzong personally faced Zhou's Prince of Qi at the north wall, wielding a great spear, riding back and forth to direct the fight — nowhere could anyone stand before him.
entries.literal: Yanzong personally faced Zhou's Prince of Qi at the north wall, wielding a great spear, riding back and forth to direct the fight — nowhere was there resistance before him.

entries.zh: 尚書令史沮山亦肥大多力，捉長刀步從，殺傷甚多。
entries.en: Ju Shan, records clerk of the Masters of Writing, also fat and immensely strong, followed on foot with a long blade and killed or wounded many.
entries.literal: The Records Clerk of the Masters of Writing, Ju Shan, also fat and immensely strong, followed on foot with a long blade and killed or wounded many.

entries.zh: 武衞蘭芙蓉、綦連延長皆死於陣。
entries.en: Martial Guard Lan Furong and Qilian Yanchang both died in battle.
entries.literal: Martial Guard Lan Furong and Qilian Yanchang both died in battle.

entries.zh: 漁陽王紹信，文襄第六子也。
entries.en: Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang was the sixth son of Gao Cheng.
entries.literal: Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang was the sixth son of Wenxiang.

entries.zh: 歷特進、開府、中領軍、護軍、青州刺史。
entries.en: He rose through special eminence, opener of the government, director of the central guard, protector of the army, and governor of Qing Province.
entries.literal: He held in succession the ranks of special eminence, opener of the government, director of the central guard, protector of the army, and governor of Qing Province.

entries.zh: 行過漁陽，與大富人鍾長命同祷坐。
entries.en: On the road through Yuyang he sat at prayer with the wealthy merchant Zhong Changming.
entries.literal: Passing through Yuyang, he sat together with the great merchant Zhong Changming to pray.

entries.zh: 太守鄭道蓋謁，長命欲起，紹信不聽，曰：「此何物小人，而主人公為起。」
entries.en: When Prefect Zheng Daogai came to pay his respects, Changming started to rise; Shaoxin stopped him and said, "What sort of wretch is this, that the host should stand for him?"
entries.literal: When Prefect Zheng Daogai came to pay respects, Changming wished to rise; Shaoxin would not allow it and said, "What kind of low creature is this, that the master of the house should rise for him?"

entries.zh: 乃與長命結為義兄弟，妃與長命妻為姊妹，責其闔家幼長皆有贈賄，鍾氏因此遂貧。
entries.en: He then swore brotherhood with Changming; his consort and Changming's wife became sworn sisters. He extorted gifts from every member of the household, young and old, until the Zhong family was beggared.
entries.literal: He then made sworn brothers with Changming; his consort and Changming's wife became sworn sisters. He demanded gifts from the whole family, young and old alike, and the Zhong clan was ruined by it.

entries.zh: 齊滅，死於長安。
entries.en: When Qi fell he died at Chang'an.
entries.literal: When Qi perished he died at Chang'an.

entries.zh: 論曰：文襄諸子，咸有風骨。
entries.en: Appraisal: Wenxiang's sons all had force of character.
entries.literal: The appraisal says: Wenxiang's sons all possessed force of character.

entries.zh: 雖文雅之道，有謝間、平，然武藝英姿，多堪禦侮。
entries.en: Although they fell short of Hejian and Pingyuan in literary refinement, many had the martial skill and heroic bearing to withstand insult.
entries.literal: Although in the way of literary refinement they fell short of Jian and Ping, in martial skill and heroic bearing many were fit to repel insults.

entries.zh: 縱咸陽賜劍，殲覆有徵，若使蘭陵獲全，未可量也。
entries.en: Even with the sword granted at Xianyang and the signs of annihilation already visible, had the Prince of Lanling survived intact, what might have followed is beyond reckoning.
entries.literal: Even if the sword was bestowed at Xianyang and signs of annihilation had appeared, had Lanling been preserved whole, the outcome could not have been measured.

entries.zh: 而終見誅翦，以至土崩，可為太息者矣。
entries.en: Yet in the end they were cut down one after another until the state collapsed. It is enough to make one sigh deeply.
entries.literal: Yet in the end they were executed and cut down, until the state collapsed like crumbling earth; this is a matter for deep sighs.

entries.zh: 安德以時艱主暗，晦跡韜光；及平陽之陣，奮其忠勇，蓋以臨難見危，義深家國。
entries.en: Yanzong of Ande hid himself in dangerous times under a benighted ruler, but at Pingyang he summoned his loyal courage. Faced with crisis and danger, his devotion to house and state ran deep.
entries.literal: Ande, because the times were perilous and the ruler benighted, concealed his traces and veiled his brilliance; at the battle of Pingyang he roused his loyalty and courage, for when he faced difficulty and danger his sense of duty to house and state was deep.

entries.zh: 德昌大舉，事迫群情，理至淪亡，無所歸命。
entries.en: The Dechang rising was forced by the troops' urgent feeling. By then collapse had come, and there was nowhere else for allegiance to go.
entries.literal: The great Dechang undertaking was forced by the feelings of the multitude; when affairs had reached ruin, there was nowhere else to entrust the mandate.

entries.zh: 廣甯請出後宮，竟不獲遂，非孝珩辭致，有謝李同，自是後主心識，去平原已遠。
entries.en: Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning asked to send out the palace women, but the request was never granted. It was not that Xiaoheng lacked Li Tong's persuasiveness; the Later Lord's judgment was already far removed from Pingyuan.
entries.literal: Guangning requested to take the palace women out, but in the end this was not granted. It was not that Xiaoheng's rhetoric fell short of Li Tong; rather, from this point the Later Lord's judgment was already far removed from Pingyuan.

entries.zh: 存亡事異，安可同年而說。
entries.en: Survival and destruction are different things; how can they be spoken of in the same breath?
entries.literal: Survival and destruction are different matters; how can they be discussed as if they belonged to the same year?

entries.zh: 北齊書卷十一 按此卷原缺，後人以北史卷五二齊宗室諸王傳下文襄諸子傳補。
entries.en: Book of Northern Qi, juan 11: This juan was originally lost; later editors restored it from the account of Wenxiang's sons in Beishi, juan 52, Biographies of Princes of the Imperial Clan of Qi.
entries.literal: Book of Northern Qi, juan 11: This juan was originally missing; later hands supplemented it from the section on Wenxiang's sons in Beishi, juan 52, Biographies of Princes of the Imperial Clan of Qi.

entries.zh: 三朝本、南本卷後有宋人校語「此卷與北史同」。
entries.en: At the end of the juan, the Song-era collation note in the Three Dynasties and Southern editions reads: "This juan matches the Beishi."
entries.literal: The Song collator's note at the end of the juan in the editions of the Three Dynasties and the Southern edition reads: "This juan is identical to the Beishi."

entries.zh: 北齊書卷十一
entries.en: Book of Northern Qi, Volume 11
entries.literal: Book of Northern Qi, Volume 11

entries.zh: 趙郡王琛，字永寶，高祖之弟也。
entries.en: Prince Chen of Zhao Commandery, styled Yongbao, was a younger brother of Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Prince Chen of Zhao Commandery, styled Yongbao, was a younger brother of the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 少時便弓馬，有志氣。
entries.en: In youth he was skilled at archery and horsemanship, and possessed ambition and spirit.
entries.literal: In youth he was skilled at archery and horsemanship, and possessed ambition and spirit.

entries.zh: 高祖既匡天下，中興初，授散騎常侍、鎮西將軍、金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: After Gao Huan had set the realm right, at the beginning of the Restoration he was appointed regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, general who pacifies the west, and grand master of the golden seal and purple ribbon.
entries.literal: After the Grand Ancestor had set the realm right, at the beginning of the Restoration he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the West, and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 既居禁衛，恭勤慎密，率先左右。
entries.en: Once he held palace guard duty, he was reverent, diligent, and discreet, taking the lead among those at the emperor's side.
entries.literal: Once he held palace guard duty, he was reverent, diligent, and discreet, taking the lead among those at the emperor's side.

entries.zh: 太昌初，除車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫，封南趙郡公，食邑五千戶。
entries.en: At the beginning of Taichang, he was made general of chariots and cavalry, left grand master of the golden seal, and enfeoffed duke of Southern Zhao Commandery with a fief of five thousand households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Grand Master of the Golden Seal, enfeoffed Duke of Southern Zhao Commandery with a fief of five thousand households.

entries.zh: 尋拜驃騎大將軍、特進、開府儀同三司、散騎常侍。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was appointed grand general of the agile cavalry, special advance, opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Grand General of the Agile Cavalry, Special Advance, Opener of a Government Office Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators, and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 永熙二年，除使持節、都督定州刺史、六州大都督。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongxi, he was made bearer of the staff of authority, area commander of Ding Province, and area commander-in-chief of six provinces.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, he was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander of Ding Province, and Area Commander-in-Chief of Six Provinces.

entries.zh: 琛推誠撫納，拔用人士，甚有聲譽。
entries.en: Chen treated people with sincerity and kindness, promoted men of talent, and enjoyed a very fine reputation.
entries.literal: Chen treated people with sincerity and kindness, promoted men of talent, and enjoyed a very fine reputation.

entries.zh: 及斛斯椿等釁結。
entries.en: Conflict then arose with Husi Chun and the others.
entries.literal: Hostilities arose with Husi Chun and the others.

entries.zh: 高祖將謀內討，以晉陽根本，召琛留掌後事，以為幷、肆、汾大行臺僕射，領六州九酋長大都督，其相府政事琛悉決之。
entries.en: Gao Huan planned an internal punitive campaign; because Jinyang was the foundation of his power, he summoned Chen to remain and manage affairs in the rear, appointing him vice director of the great eastern headquarters for Bing, Xi, and Fen, and area commander-in-chief of the six provinces and nine chieftains — Chen decided all affairs of the chancellor's office.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor planned an internal punitive campaign; because Jinyang was the foundation of his power, he summoned Chen to remain and manage affairs in the rear, appointing him Vice Director of the Great Eastern Headquarters for Bing, Xi, and Fen, and Area Commander-in-Chief of the Six Provinces and Nine Chieftains — Chen decided all affairs of the chancellor's office.

entries.zh: 天平中，除御史中尉，正色糾彈，無所回避，遠近肅然。
entries.en: In the Tianping era he was made censor-in-chief; with stern countenance he investigated and impeached, never shrinking from anyone, and near and far were awed into order.
entries.literal: In the Tianping era he was made Censor-in-Chief; with stern countenance he investigated and impeached, never shrinking from anyone, and near and far were awed into order.

entries.zh: 尋亂高祖後庭，高祖責罰之，因杖而斃，時年二十三。
entries.en: Soon he violated Gao Huan's rear palaces; Gao Huan rebuked and punished him, and he was beaten to death with a staff — he was twenty-three.
entries.literal: Soon he violated the Grand Ancestor's rear palaces; the Grand Ancestor rebuked and punished him, and he was beaten to death with a staff — he was twenty-three.

entries.zh: 贈使持節、侍中、都督冀定滄瀛幽殷幷肆雲朔十州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、冀州刺史、太尉、尚書令，諡曰貞平。
entries.en: Posthumously he was appointed bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, area commander of military affairs in ten provinces — Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, You, Yin, Bing, Xi, Yun, and Shuo — grand general of the agile cavalry, governor of Ji Province, grand commandant, and director of the masters of writing; his posthumous title was Zhenping.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Area Commander of Military Affairs in ten provinces — Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, You, Yin, Bing, Xi, Yun, and Shuo — Grand General of the Agile Cavalry, Governor of Ji Province, Grand Commandant, and Director of the Masters of Writing; his posthumous title was Zhenping.

entries.zh: 天統三年，又贈假黃鉞、左丞相、太師、錄尚書事、冀州刺史，進爵為王，配饗高祖廟庭。
entries.en: In the third year of Tiantong he was further posthumously granted the yellow battle-axe, left chancellor, grand preceptor, recorder of affairs of the masters of writing, and governor of Ji Province; his rank was advanced to prince, and he was granted sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple hall.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tiantong he was further posthumously granted the Yellow Battle-Axe, Left Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Ji Province; his rank was advanced to prince, and he was granted sacrifice in the Grand Ancestor's temple hall.

entries.zh: 子叡嗣。
entries.en: His son Rui succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Rui succeeded.

entries.zh: 後主晉州敗，太后從土門道還京師，敕勱統領兵馬，侍衛太后。
entries.en: When Houzhu was defeated at Jin Province, the Empress Dowager returned to the capital by the Tumen Road; an edict put Mai in overall command of troops to escort her.
entries.literal: When Houzhu was defeated at Jin Province, the Empress Dowager returned to the capital by the Tumen Road; an edict ordered Mai to take overall command of troops and escort the Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 時佞幸閽寺，猶行暴虐，民間雞豬，悉放鷹犬搏噬取之。
entries.en: Favored eunuchs still ran riot; they loosed hawks and dogs on the people's chickens and pigs and took them by force.
entries.literal: At that time favored eunuchs still carried out wanton cruelty; throughout the common folk they set hawks and dogs to seize chickens and pigs by force.

entries.zh: 勱收儀同三司茍子溢徇軍，欲行大戮。
entries.en: Mai seized Gou Ziyi, an official of equal-in-rank third rank, paraded him before the army, and meant to execute him on the spot.
entries.literal: Mai seized Equal-in-Rank Third Rank official Gou Ziyi and paraded him through the army, intending a mass execution.

entries.zh: 太后有令，然後釋之。
entries.en: Only when the Empress Dowager sent an order was Gou released.
entries.literal: Only after the Empress Dowager issued an order was he released.

entries.zh: 劉文殊竊謂勱曰：「子溢之徒，言成禍福，何容如此，豈不慮後生毀謗耶？」
entries.en: Liu Wenshu whispered to Mai, "Men like Ziyi can make or break us with a word — how can you treat them so? Will you not fear what men will say afterward?"
entries.literal: Liu Wenshu whispered to Mai, saying, "Men like Ziyi can make or break us with a word — how can you treat them thus? Will you not fear slander afterward?"

entries.zh: 勱攘袂語文殊曰：「自獻武皇帝以來，撫養士卒，委政親賢，用武行師，未有折衂。
entries.en: Mai rolled up his sleeves and told Wenshu, "Since Gao Huan, we have nurtured soldiers, entrusted rule to kin and worthies, and taken the field — never once were we broken.
entries.literal: Mai rolled up his sleeves and said to Wenshu, "Since the Shenwu Emperor, we have nurtured soldiers, entrusted government to kin and worthies, and taken the field in war — never once were we defeated.

entries.zh: 今西寇已次幷州，達官多悉委叛，正坐此輩專政弄權，所以內外離心，衣冠解體。
entries.en: Now the western invaders stand at Bingzhou; great officials defect in droves. It is because men like these hold power and twist affairs that court and countryside have lost heart and the gentry have come undone.
entries.literal: Now the western invaders have reached Bingzhou; many high officials have already defected. It is precisely because these men monopolize power and manipulate affairs that hearts within and without have split and the gentry have fallen apart.

entries.zh: 若得今日斬此卒，明日及誅，亦無所恨。
entries.en: If I can cut off this man's head today and die for it tomorrow, I will not regret it.
entries.literal: If I can behead this one today, and die tomorrow for it, I shall have no regret.

entries.zh: 王國家姻婭，須同疾惡，返為此言，豈所望乎！」
entries.en: Our houses are joined by marriage; we ought to hate the same evil. To speak to me like this — is this what I expected of you!"
entries.literal: Your house and mine are joined by marriage — we must share the same hatred of evil. To speak thus against me — is this what I expected of you!"

entries.zh: 太后還至鄴，周軍續至，人皆恟懼，無有鬭心，朝士出降，晝夜相屬。
entries.en: When the Empress Dowager reached Ye, Zhou armies pressed on without pause; panic spread and no one would fight; court officials surrendered day and night without end.
entries.literal: When the Empress Dowager returned to Ye, Zhou armies pressed on in succession; everyone was panic-stricken, with no will to fight; court officials surrendered by day and night without cease.

entries.zh: 勱因奏後主曰：「今所翻叛，多是貴人，至於卒伍，猶未離貳。
entries.en: Mai therefore memorialized Houzhu: "Those who have turned are mostly nobles; among the common ranks many have not yet gone over.
entries.literal: Mai therefore memorialized Houzhu, saying, "Those who have defected are mostly nobles; among the common soldiers, many have not yet turned.

entries.zh: 請追五品已上家屬，置之三臺，因協之曰：『若戰不捷，即退焚臺。』
entries.en: I ask that the families of every official of fifth rank and above be gathered into the Three Platforms, and that they be told: 'If we do not win, we withdraw and burn the platforms.'
entries.literal: I ask that the families of all officials of fifth rank and above be gathered and placed in the Three Platforms, and that they be told: 'If the battle is not won, we will withdraw and burn the platforms.'

entries.zh: 此曹顧惜妻子，必當死戰。
entries.en: Those men, for wife and child, will fight to the death.
entries.literal: These men, cherishing wife and children, will surely fight to the death.

entries.zh: 且王師頻北，賊徒輕我，今背城一決，理必破之，此亦計之上者。」
entries.en: Our armies have retreated again and again; the enemy holds us cheap. One decisive battle with our backs to the wall must break them — that too is the highest plan."
entries.literal: Moreover our armies have repeatedly retreated north; the enemy despises us. If we stake everything on a single battle behind the walls, reason says we must break them — this too is the supreme stratagem."

entries.zh: 後主卒不能用。
entries.en: Houzhu in the end would not take his counsel.
entries.literal: Houzhu in the end could not adopt it.

entries.zh: 齊亡入周，依例授開府。
entries.en: When Qi fell he entered Zhou and, by precedent, was granted an opening establishment.
entries.literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou; by precedent he was given an Opening Establishment.

entries.zh: 隋朝歷楊、楚、光、洮四州刺史。
entries.en: Under the Sui he served in turn as governor of Yang, Chu, Guang, and Tao provinces.
entries.literal: Under the Sui he successively held the governorships of Yang, Chu, Guang, and Tao Provinces.

entries.zh: 開皇中卒。
entries.en: He died in the Kaihuang era.
entries.literal: He died in the Kaihuang era.

entries.zh: 清河王岳，字洪略，高祖從父弟也。
entries.en: Prince of Qinghe Gao Yue, courtesy name Honglüe, was a younger cousin of Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Prince of Qinghe Yue, courtesy name Honglüe, was a younger cousin of the High Ancestor on the father's side.

entries.zh: 父翻，字飛雀，魏朝贈太尉，諡孝宣公。
entries.en: His father Gao Fan, courtesy name Feique, was posthumously made grand commandant by Wei and given the posthumous title Duke Xiaoxuan.
entries.literal: His father Fan, courtesy name Feique, was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant by Wei and given the posthumous title Duke Xiaoxuan.

entries.zh: 岳幼時孤貧，人未之知也，長而敦直，姿貌嶷然，沈深有器量。
entries.en: Yue was orphaned and poor in youth; no one yet marked him. Grown, he was honest and upright, of striking bearing — deep, reserved, and possessed of great capacity.
entries.literal: Yue in youth was orphaned and poor; no one yet knew him. Grown, he was honest and upright, of lofty bearing, deep and reserved, with great capacity.

entries.zh: 初，岳家於洛邑，高祖每奉使入洛，必止于岳舍。
entries.en: At first Yue's household was at Luoyang; whenever Gao Huan came to the capital on business he always stayed at Yue's house.
entries.literal: At first Yue's family lived at Luoyang; whenever the High Ancestor came to Luoyang on mission he always lodged at Yue's house.

entries.zh: 岳母山氏，嘗夜起，見高祖室中有光，密往覘之，乃無燈，即移高祖於別室，如前所見。
entries.en: Yue's mother Lady Shan once rose at night and saw light in Gao Huan's room. She stole a look — no lamp burned — and moved him to another chamber; the same radiance appeared there.
entries.literal: Yue's mother, Lady Shan, once rose at night and saw light in the High Ancestor's chamber; she stole a look — there was no lamp — and moved the High Ancestor to another room; the same sight appeared as before.

entries.zh: 怪其神異，詣卜者筮之，遇《幹》之《大有》，占之曰：「吉，《易》稱『飛龍在天，大人造也』，飛龍九五大人之卦，貴不可言。」
entries.en: Struck by the omen, she consulted a diviner and obtained Qian changing to Dayou. The reading ran: "Auspicious. The Changes says, 'The flying dragon is in heaven — the great man creates.' The fifth line — the great man's hexagram; honor beyond words."
entries.literal: Marveling at the portent, she went to a diviner who cast and obtained Qian changing to Dayou; the reading said: "Auspicious. The Changes says, 'The flying dragon is in heaven — the great man creates.' Flying dragon, the fifth line — the hexagram of the great man; honor beyond words."

entries.zh: 山氏歸報高祖。
entries.en: Lady Shan went back and told Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Lady Shan returned and reported to the High Ancestor.

entries.zh: 後高祖起兵於信都，山氏聞之，大喜，謂岳曰：「赤光之瑞，今當驗矣，汝可間行從之，共圖大計。」
entries.en: When Gao Huan later raised troops at Xindu, Lady Shan heard and rejoiced. She told Yue, "The omen of red light is fulfilled — go by a secret route and join him; together you will shape the great design."
entries.literal: Later when the High Ancestor raised troops at Xindu, Lady Shan heard and rejoiced greatly; she told Yue: "The omen of red light is now fulfilled — you should go by secret route and join him; together plot the great design."

entries.zh: 岳遂往信都。
entries.en: Yue went to Xindu.
entries.literal: Yue thereupon went to Xindu.

entries.zh: 高祖見之，大悅。
entries.en: Gao Huan saw him and was greatly pleased.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor saw him and was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 及高祖崩，侯景叛，世宗徵岳還幷，共圖取景之計。
entries.en: When Gao Huan died and Hou Jing rebelled, Gao Cheng summoned Yue back to Bing to plan the campaign against Jing.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor died and Hou Jing rebelled, the Heir Apparent summoned Yue back to Bing to plan together the campaign against Jing.

entries.zh: 而武帝乘間遣其貞陽侯明率衆於寒山，擁泗水灌彭城，與景為掎角聲援。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Liang seized the moment and sent his Marquis of Zhenyang Ming with an army to Hanshan, damming the Si to flood Pengcheng and coordinating with Jing in pincer support.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang seized the moment and sent his Marquis of Zhenyang Ming at the head of an army at Hanshan, damming the Si River to flood Pengcheng, coordinating with Jing in pincer support.

entries.zh: 岳總帥諸軍南討，與行臺慕容紹宗等擊明，大破之，臨陣擒明及其大將胡貴孫，自餘俘馘數萬。
entries.en: Yue led the armies south; with field headquarters Murong Shaozong and others he attacked Ming, routed him completely, captured Ming and his great general Hu Guisun on the field, and took tens of thousands more captive.
entries.literal: Yue commanded the armies south in punitive expedition; with the field headquarters Murong Shaozong and others he attacked Ming, routed him completely, captured Ming and his great general Hu Guisun on the field, and took tens of thousands more captive.

entries.zh: 景乃擁衆於渦陽，與左衛將軍劉豐等相持。
entries.en: Jing then massed troops at Woyang, locked in stalemate with left guard general Liu Feng and others.
entries.literal: Jing then massed troops at Woyang, locked in stalemate with Left Guard General Liu Feng and others.

entries.zh: 岳回軍追討，又破之，景單騎逃竄。
entries.en: Yue wheeled to pursue and defeated him again; Jing fled alone on horseback.
entries.literal: Yue turned his army to pursue and again defeated him; Jing fled alone on horseback.

entries.zh: 六年，以功除侍中、太尉，餘如故，別封新昌縣子。
entries.en: In the sixth year, he was rewarded for his merit with appointment as palace attendant and grand commandant; his other offices remained unchanged, and he was separately enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinchang.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, for merit he was made Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant; the rest as before; separately enfeoffed Viscount of Xinchang.

entries.zh: 又拜使持節、河南總管、大都督，統慕容紹宗、劉豐等討王思政於長社。
entries.en: He was also made bearer of the staff, grand governor of Henan, and grand commander, leading Murong Shaozong, Liu Feng, and others against Wang Sizheng at Changshe.
entries.literal: He was also made Bearer of the Staff, Grand Governor of Henan, and Grand Commander, commanding Murong Shaozong, Liu Feng, and others to attack Wang Sizheng at Changshe.

entries.zh: 思政嬰城自守，岳等引洧水灌城。
entries.en: Sizheng held the city; Yue and the rest diverted the Wei River to flood it.
entries.literal: Sizheng held the city and defended; Yue and the rest diverted the Wei River to flood it.

entries.zh: 紹宗、劉豐為思政所獲，關西出兵援思政，岳內外防禦，甚有謀算。
entries.en: Shaozong and Liu Feng were captured by Sizheng; troops from west of the Pass came to aid him; Yue defended within and without with shrewd calculation.
entries.literal: Shaozong and Liu Feng were captured by Sizheng; troops from west of the Pass came to aid Sizheng; Yue defended within and without with shrewd calculation.

entries.zh: 城不沒者三板。
entries.en: Only three boards' thickness of wall stood above the flood.
entries.literal: The city was not submerged by more than three boards' thickness.

entries.zh: 會世宗親臨，數日城下，獲思政等。
entries.en: Gao Cheng came in person; within days beneath the walls Sizheng and the rest were captured.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent came in person; within days beneath the walls Sizheng and the rest were captured.

entries.zh: 以功別封真定縣男，世宗以為己功，故賞典弗弘也。
entries.en: For merit he was separately enfeoffed baron of Zhending; Gao Cheng claimed the credit, so rewards were not fully granted.
entries.literal: For merit he was separately enfeoffed Baron of Zhending; the Heir Apparent claimed the credit for himself, so rewards were not fully granted.

entries.zh: 叡小名須拔，生三旬而孤，聰慧夙成，特為高祖所愛，養於宮中，令遊娘母之，恩同諸子。
entries.en: Rui's childhood name was Xuba; he was orphaned at thirty days, precocious and clever from infancy, and was especially loved by Gao Huan; he was raised in the palace and entrusted to Youniang as foster mother, receiving favor equal to the other sons.
entries.literal: Rui's childhood name was Xuba; he was orphaned at thirty days, precocious and clever from infancy, and was especially loved by the Grand Ancestor; he was raised in the palace and entrusted to Youniang as foster mother, receiving favor equal to the other sons.

entries.zh: 魏興和中，襲爵南趙郡公。
entries.en: In the Xinghe era of Wei, he inherited the title duke of Southern Zhao Commandery.
entries.literal: In the Xinghe era of Wei, he inherited the title Duke of Southern Zhao Commandery.

entries.zh: 至四歲，未嘗識母，其母則魏華陽公主也。
entries.en: By the age of four he had never known his mother — his mother was the Princess Huayang of Wei.
entries.literal: By the age of four he had never known his mother — his mother was the Princess Huayang of Wei.

entries.zh: 有鄭氏者，叡母之從母姊妹之女，戲語叡曰：「汝是我姨兒，何因倒親遊氏。」
entries.en: There was a Lady Zheng, daughter of a maternal cousin of Rui's mother, who playfully said to Rui, "You are my cousin's child — why do you instead show affection for the You clan?"
entries.literal: There was a Lady Zheng, daughter of a maternal cousin of Rui's mother, who playfully said to Rui, "You are my cousin's child — why do you instead show affection for the You clan?"

entries.zh: 叡因問訪，遂精神不怡。
entries.en: Rui thereupon made inquiries, and his spirits grew troubled.
entries.literal: Rui thereupon made inquiries, and his spirits grew troubled.

entries.zh: 高祖甚以為怪，疑其感疾，欲命醫看之。
entries.en: Gao Huan thought it very strange, suspected he had fallen ill, and wished to summon a physician to examine him.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor thought it very strange, suspected he had fallen ill, and wished to summon a physician to examine him.

entries.zh: 叡對曰：「兒無患苦，但聞有所生，欲得暫見。」
entries.en: Rui replied, "Your son has no illness or pain — I only heard that I have a birth mother, and wish to see her for a time."
entries.literal: Rui replied, "Your son has no illness or pain — I only heard that I have a birth mother, and wish to see her for a time."

entries.zh: 高祖驚曰：「誰向汝道耶？」
entries.en: Gao Huan said in astonishment, "Who told you this?"
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor said in astonishment, "Who told you this?"

entries.zh: 叡具陳本末。
entries.en: Rui fully explained the sequence of events.
entries.literal: Rui fully explained the sequence of events.

entries.zh: 高祖命元夫人令就宮與叡相見，叡前跪拜，因抱頭大哭。
entries.en: Gao Huan ordered Lady Yuan to come to the palace and meet Rui; Rui went forward, knelt and bowed, then embraced her head and wept loudly.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor ordered Lady Yuan to come to the palace and meet Rui; Rui went forward, knelt and bowed, then embraced her head and wept loudly.

entries.zh: 高祖甚以悲傷。
entries.en: Gao Huan was deeply grieved.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor was deeply grieved.

entries.zh: 語平秦王曰：「此兒天生至孝，我兒子無有及者。」
entries.en: He said to Prince of Pingqin Guiyan, "This child is filial by nature — none of my sons can match him."
entries.literal: He said to the Prince of Pingqin, "This child is filial by nature — none of my sons can match him."

entries.zh: 遂為休務一日。
entries.en: Thereupon he suspended official business for one day.
entries.literal: Thereupon he suspended official business for one day.

entries.zh: 叡初讀《孝經》，至「資於事父」，輒流涕歔欷。
entries.en: When Rui first read the Classic of Filial Piety, upon reaching "drawing upon in serving one's father" he would weep and sigh.
entries.literal: When Rui first read the Classic of Filial Piety, upon reaching "drawing upon in serving one's father" he would weep and sigh.

entries.zh: 十歲喪母，高祖親送叡至領軍府，為叡發喪，與聲殞絕，哀感左右，三日水漿不入口。
entries.en: At ten he lost his mother; Gao Huan personally escorted Rui to the commandant's headquarters, held mourning for him, and wailed until his voice failed — his grief moved those around him, and for three days he took neither water nor food.
entries.literal: At ten he lost his mother; the Grand Ancestor personally escorted Rui to the Commandant's headquarters, held mourning for him, and wailed until his voice failed — his grief moved those around him, and for three days he took neither water nor food.

entries.zh: 高祖與武明婁皇后殷勤敦譬，方漸順旨。
entries.en: Gao Huan and Empress Lou Wuming earnestly urged and admonished him, and only then did he gradually comply.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor and Empress Wuming of the Lou clan earnestly urged and admonished him, and only then did he gradually comply.

entries.zh: 居喪盡禮，持佛像長齋，至于骨立，杖而後起。
entries.en: In mourning he observed every rite, kept a long fast before a Buddha image until he was wasted to the bone, and only rose with the aid of a staff.
entries.literal: In mourning he observed every rite, kept a long fast before a Buddha image until he was wasted to the bone, and only rose with the aid of a staff.

entries.zh: 高祖令常山王共臥起，日夜說喻之。
entries.en: Gao Huan had Prince of Changshan Gao Yan share bed and board with him, exhorting him day and night.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor had the Prince of Changshan share bed and board with him, exhorting him day and night.

entries.zh: 並敕左右不聽進水，雖絕清漱，午後輒不肯食。
entries.en: He also ordered those at his side not to allow water to be brought in; though he cut off even rinsing his mouth, after noon he still refused food.
entries.literal: He also ordered those at his side not to allow water to be brought in; though he cut off even rinsing his mouth, after noon he still refused food.

entries.zh: 由是高祖食必喚叡同案。
entries.en: From this Gao Huan always summoned Rui to share his table at meals.
entries.literal: From this the Grand Ancestor always summoned Rui to share his table at meals.

entries.zh: 其見湣惜如此。
entries.en: Such was the pity and tenderness shown him.
entries.literal: Such was the pity and tenderness shown him.

entries.zh: 高祖崩，哭泣嘔血。
entries.en: When Gao Huan died, Rui wept until he vomited blood.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor died, Rui wept until he vomited blood.

entries.zh: 及壯，將為婚娶，而貌有戚容。
entries.en: When he came of age and was to marry, his countenance still bore sorrow.
entries.literal: When he came of age and was to marry, his countenance still bore sorrow.

entries.zh: 世宗謂之曰：「我為爾娶鄭述祖女，門閥甚高，汝何所嫌而精神不樂？」
entries.en: Gao Cheng said to him, "I will marry you to the daughter of Zheng Shuzu — her family standing is very high; what do you find objectionable, that your spirits are not glad?"
entries.literal: The Imperial Founder said to him, "I will marry you to the daughter of Zheng Shuzu — her family standing is very high; what do you find objectionable, that your spirits are not glad?"

entries.zh: 叡對曰：「自痛孤遺，常深膝下之慕，方從婚冠，彌用感切。」
entries.en: Rui replied, "Since I was orphaned early, I have always deeply yearned for the warmth beneath my parents' knees; now, on the eve of cap and marriage, I feel this all the more keenly."
entries.literal: Rui replied, "Since I was orphaned early, I have always deeply yearned for the warmth beneath my parents' knees; now, on the eve of cap and marriage, I feel this all the more keenly."

entries.zh: 言未卒，嗚咽不自勝。
entries.en: Before he finished speaking, he sobbed uncontrollably.
entries.literal: Before he finished speaking, he sobbed uncontrollably.

entries.zh: 世宗為之憫默。
entries.en: Gao Cheng was moved to pity and fell silent.
entries.literal: The Imperial Founder was moved to pity and fell silent.

entries.zh: 勵己勤學，常夜久方罷。
entries.en: He disciplined himself in study, often reading late into the night before stopping.
entries.literal: He disciplined himself in study, often reading late into the night before stopping.

entries.zh: 武定末，除太子庶子。
entries.en: At the end of Wuding he was made junior tutor to the crown prince.
entries.literal: At the end of Wuding he was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 顯祖受禪，進封爵為趙郡王，邑一千二百戶，遷散騎常侍。
entries.en: When Gao Yang received the abdication, Rui's enfeoffment was advanced to prince of Zhao Commandery with a fief of twelve hundred households, and he was transferred to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: When the Manifest Ancestor received the abdication, Rui's enfeoffment was advanced to Prince of Zhao Commandery with a fief of twelve hundred households, and he was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 中興初，除散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫，領武衛將軍。
entries.en: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, general who pacifies the east, and grand master of the gold seal and purple ribbon, concurrently commanding the martial guard.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the East, and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, concurrently commanding the Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 高祖與四胡戰于韓陵，高祖將中軍，高昂將左軍，岳將右軍。
entries.en: Gao Huan fought the Four Hus at Hanling: he himself held the center, Gao Ang the left, Yue the right.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor fought the Four Hus at Hanling; the High Ancestor commanded the center, Gao Ang the left, Yue the right.

entries.zh: 中軍敗績，賊乘之，岳舉麾大呼，橫沖賊陣，高祖方得回師，表裏奮擊，因大破賊。
entries.en: The center broke; the enemy pressed in. Yue raised his banner and shouted, driving straight through their line — Gao Huan could wheel about, and front and rear together smashed the foe.
entries.literal: The center was routed; the enemy pressed in. Yue raised his banner and shouted, charging straight through the enemy line; the High Ancestor was thus able to wheel about, and front and rear struck together, breaking the enemy completely.

entries.zh: 以功除衛將軍、右光祿大夫，仍領武衛。
entries.en: For this he was made guard general and right grand master of the gold seal and purple ribbon, still commanding the martial guard.
entries.literal: For merit he was made Guard General and Right Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, still commanding the Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 太昌初，除車騎將軍、左光祿大夫，領左右衛，封清河郡公，食邑二千戶。
entries.en: At the beginning of Taichang he was made chariot-and-horse general and left grand master of the gold seal and purple ribbon, commanding the left and right guards, enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe Commandery with two thousand households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was made Chariot-and-Horse General and Left Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, commanding the Left and Right Guards, enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe Commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 母山氏，封為郡君，授女侍中，入侍皇后。
entries.en: His mother, Lady Shan, was enfeoffed as Lady of the Commandery, appointed Female Palace Attendant, and entered the palace to serve the empress.
entries.literal: His mother Lady Shan was enfeoffed as Lady of the Commandery, appointed Female Palace Attendant, and entered to serve the empress.

entries.zh: 時尒朱兆猶據幷州，高祖將討之，令岳留鎮京師，遷驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。
entries.en: Erzhu Zhao still held Bing Province; Gao Huan meant to attack him and left Yue to guard the capital, promoting him to grand general of the flying cavalry and honorary equal to the three ducal ministers.
entries.literal: At that time Erzhu Zhao still held Bing Province; the High Ancestor was about to attack him and ordered Yue to remain guarding the capital, promoting him to Grand General of the Flying Cavalry and Honorary Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

entries.zh: 天平二年，除侍中、六州軍事都督，尋加開府。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianping he was made palace attendant and military governor of six provinces; soon opening-establishment was added.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianping he was made Palace Attendant and Military Governor of Six Provinces; soon opening-establishment was added.

entries.zh: 岳辟引時賢，以為僚屬，論者以為美。
entries.en: Yue recruited the worthy of the age for his staff; commentators praised it.
entries.literal: Yue recruited men of the age and made them staff; commentators held this admirable.

entries.zh: 尋都監典書，復為侍學，除使持節、六州大都督、冀州大中正。
entries.en: Soon he was made director of the palace library, again tutor to the heir, bearer of the staff, military governor of six provinces, and chief rectifier of Ji Province.
entries.literal: Soon he was made director of the Palace Library, again tutor to the heir, and made Bearer of the Staff, Military Governor of Six Provinces, and Chief Rectifier of Ji Province.

entries.zh: 俄拜京畿大都督，其六州事悉詣京畿。
entries.en: Shortly he was made grand governor of the capital region; all six provinces' business came under the capital region.
entries.literal: Shortly he was made Grand Governor of the Capital Region; all affairs of the six provinces were referred to the capital region.

entries.zh: 時高祖統務晉陽，岳與侍中孫騰等在京師輔政。
entries.en: Gao Huan then directed affairs from Jinyang; Yue with palace attendant Sun Teng and others governed at the capital.
entries.literal: At that time the High Ancestor directed affairs from Jinyang; Yue with Palace Attendant Sun Teng and others assisted government in the capital.

entries.zh: 元象二年，遭母憂去職。
entries.en: In the second year of Yuanxiang he left office to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yuanxiang he left office on his mother's death.

entries.zh: 岳性至孝，盡力色養，母若有疾，衣不解帶，及遭喪，哀毀骨立，高祖深以憂之，每日遣人勞勉。
entries.en: Yue was utterly filial, serving her with every devotion; when she was ill he never unbelted his robe; in mourning he wasted to skin and bone. Gao Huan was deeply troubled and sent men daily to comfort him.
entries.literal: Yue was utterly filial, exerting himself in tending her with full devotion; when his mother was ill he never unbelted his robe; in mourning he wasted away to the bone. The High Ancestor was deeply troubled and daily sent men to comfort him.

entries.zh: 尋起復本任。
entries.en: Soon he was recalled to his former post.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled to his original post.

entries.zh: 二年，除兼領軍將軍。
entries.en: In the second year he was additionally made concurrent commander of the army.
entries.literal: In the second year he was additionally made Concurrent Commander of the Army.

entries.zh: 興和初，世宗入總朝政，岳出為使持節、都督、冀州刺史，侍中、驃騎、開府儀同如故。
