entries.en: At the beginning of Xinghe the heir apparent took charge of government; Yue went out as bearer of the staff, military governor, and governor of Ji Province; palace attendant, flying-cavalry general, and opening-establishment honors remained.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xinghe the Heir Apparent took overall charge of government; Yue went out as Bearer of the Staff, Military Governor, and Governor of Ji Province; palace attendant, flying-cavalry general, and opening-establishment honors remained as before.

entries.zh: 三年，轉青州刺史。
entries.en: In the third year he was transferred to governor of Qing Province.
entries.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Governor of Qing Province.

entries.zh: 岳任權日久，素為朝野畏服，及為二藩，百姓望風讋憚。
entries.en: Yue had held power long; court and countryside alike feared him. As governor of two provinces the people looked to the wind and trembled.
entries.literal: Yue had long held power and was feared by court and countryside alike; as governor of two provinces the people looked to the wind and trembled.

entries.zh: 武定元年，除晉州刺史、西南道大都督，得綏邊之稱。
entries.en: In the first year of Wuding he was made governor of Jin Province and grand governor of the southwest circuit, winning praise for pacifying the frontier.
entries.literal: In the first year of Wuding he was made Governor of Jin Province and Grand Governor of the Southwest Circuit, winning praise for pacifying the frontier.

entries.zh: 時岳遇患，高祖令還幷治療，疾瘳，復令赴職。
entries.en: When Yue fell ill Gao Huan had him return to Bing for treatment; when he recovered he was sent back to his post.
entries.literal: When Yue fell ill the High Ancestor had him return to Bing for treatment; when the illness cleared he was again ordered to his post.

entries.zh: 岳自討寒山、長社及出隨、陸，並有功績，威名彌重。
entries.en: Yue himself had merit at Hanshan, Changshe, and the campaigns through Sui and Lu; his martial name weighed ever heavier.
entries.literal: Yue himself had merit at Hanshan, Changshe, and the campaigns through Sui and Lu; his martial name weighed ever heavier.

entries.zh: 而性華侈，尤悅酒色，歌姬舞女，陳鼎擊鐘，諸王皆不及也。
entries.en: Yet by nature he was extravagant, especially fond of wine and women; singing girls, dancing women, cauldrons set and bells struck — no prince matched him.
entries.literal: Yet by nature he was extravagant, especially fond of wine and women; singing girls and dancing women, cauldrons set and bells struck — none of the princes matched him.

entries.zh: 初，高歸彥少孤，高祖令岳撫養，輕其年幼，情禮甚薄。
entries.en: Gao Guiyan was orphaned young; Gao Huan ordered Yue to raise him. Yue thought him too young and treated him with very thin courtesy.
entries.literal: At first Gao Guiyan was orphaned young; the High Ancestor ordered Yue to raise him. Yue thought him too young and treated him with very thin courtesy.

entries.zh: 歸彥內銜之而未嘗出口。
entries.en: Guiyan nursed resentment within but never spoke of it.
entries.literal: Guiyan harbored resentment within but never spoke of it.

entries.zh: 及歸彥為領軍，大被寵遇，岳謂其德己，更倚賴之。
entries.en: When Guiyan became commander of the army and was greatly favored, Yue thought he owed a debt and relied on him all the more.
entries.literal: When Guiyan became Commander of the Army and was greatly favored, Yue thought he owed Yue a debt and relied on him all the more.

entries.zh: 歸彥密構其短。
entries.en: Guiyan secretly built up his faults.
entries.literal: Guiyan secretly built up his faults.

entries.zh: 岳於城南起宅，聽事後開巷。
entries.en: Yue built a mansion south of the city; behind the audience hall he opened a lane.
entries.literal: Yue built a mansion south of the city; behind the audience hall he opened a lane.

entries.zh: 歸彥奏帝曰：「清河造宅，僭擬帝宮，制為永巷，但唯無闕耳。」
entries.en: Guiyan memorialized the emperor: "Prince of Qinghe builds his mansion in imitation of the palace, with an Eternal Lane — only the gate-towers are missing."
entries.literal: Guiyan memorialized the emperor: "Prince of Qinghe builds his mansion, presumptuously imitating the imperial palace, making an Eternal Lane — only the gate-towers are missing."

entries.zh: 顯祖聞而惡之，漸以疏岳。
entries.en: Gao Yang heard and hated it; he gradually grew distant from Yue.
entries.literal: The Manifest Ancestor heard and hated it; he gradually grew distant from Yue.

entries.zh: 仍屬顯祖召鄴下婦人薛氏入宮，而岳先嘗喚之至宅，由其姊也。
entries.en: It happened that Gao Yang summoned a woman of Ye named Xue into the palace; Yue had earlier summoned her to his house — through his elder sister.
entries.literal: It happened that the Manifest Ancestor summoned a woman of Ye named Xue into the palace; Yue had earlier summoned her to his house — through his elder sister.

entries.zh: 帝懸薛氏姊而鋸殺之，讓岳以為姦民女。
entries.en: The emperor had Xue's elder sister suspended and sawn apart, reproaching Yue for violating commoners' daughters.
entries.literal: The emperor had Xue's elder sister suspended and sawn apart, reproaching Yue for violating commoners' daughters.

entries.zh: 岳曰：「臣本欲取之，嫌其輕薄不用，非姦也。」
entries.en: Yue said, "I originally meant to take her but found her frivolous and did not — it was not violation."
entries.literal: Yue said: "Your servant originally meant to take her but found her frivolous and did not use her — it was not violation."

entries.zh: 帝益怒。
entries.en: The emperor grew angrier still.
entries.literal: The emperor grew angrier still.

entries.zh: 六年十一月，使高歸彥就宅切責之。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of the sixth year he sent Gao Guiyan to Yue's house to rebuke him sharply.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the sixth year he sent Gao Guiyan to Yue's house to rebuke him sharply.

entries.zh: 岳憂悸不知所為，數日而薨，故時論紛然，以為賜鴆也。
entries.en: Yue, anxious and fearful, knew not what to do; within days he died — contemporary talk widely held he had been given poisoned wine.
entries.literal: Yue, anxious and fearful, knew not what to do; within days he died — so contemporary talk widely held he had been given poisoned wine.

entries.zh: 朝野嘆惜之。
entries.en: Court and countryside mourned him.
entries.literal: Court and countryside mourned him.

entries.zh: 時年四十四。
entries.en: He was forty-four.
entries.literal: He was forty-four.

entries.zh: 詔大鴻臚監護喪事，贈使持節、都督冀定滄瀛趙幽濟七州諸軍、太宰、太傅、定州刺史，假黃鉞，給轀輬車，赗物二千段，諡曰昭武。
entries.en: An edict ordered the grand master of ceremonies to oversee the funeral; posthumously he was made bearer of the staff, military governor of seven provinces, grand preceptor, grand tutor, and governor of Ding Province; the yellow battle-axe was granted, an imperial carriage for the coffin provided, and two thousand bolts of burial goods; posthumous name Zhaowu.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to oversee the funeral; posthumously he was made Bearer of the Staff, Military Governor of Seven Provinces, Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Governor of Ding Province; the yellow battle-axe was granted, an imperial carriage for the coffin provided, and two thousand bolts of burial goods; posthumous name Zhaowu.

entries.zh: 初，岳與高祖經綸天下，家有私兵，並畜戎器，儲甲千餘領。
entries.en: At first Yue with Gao Huan had ordered the realm; the household kept private troops and stored weapons; more than a thousand suits of armor were hoarded.
entries.literal: At first Yue with the High Ancestor had ordered the realm; the household kept private troops and stored weapons; more than a thousand suits of armor were hoarded.

entries.zh: 世宗之末，岳以四海無事，表求納之。
entries.en: At the end of Gao Cheng's reign Yue, because the realm was at peace, memorialized asking to turn them in.
entries.literal: At the end of the Heir Apparent's reign Yue, because all under Heaven was at peace, memorialized asking to turn them in.

entries.zh: 世宗敦至親之重，推心相任，云 ：「叔屬居肺腑，職在維城，所有之甲，本資國用，叔何疑而納之。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng, honoring close kin, gave him his full trust and said, "Uncle is of our inner flesh; your charge is to guard the walls — the armor you hold is meant for the state; why doubt and turn it in?"
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent, honoring the weight of close kin, gave him his full trust and said: "Uncle is of our inner flesh; your charge is to guard the walls — the armor you hold is meant for the state's use; why doubt and turn it in?"

entries.zh: 文宣之世，亦頻請納，又固不許。
entries.en: In Gao Yang's reign he also repeatedly asked to turn them in, and again was firmly refused.
entries.literal: In the era of Wenxuan he also repeatedly asked to turn them in, and again was firmly refused.

entries.zh: 及將薨，遺表謝恩，並請上甲于武庫，至此葬畢，方許納焉。
entries.en: When about to die he left a final memorial thanking grace and again asked to submit the superior armor to the armory; only when the burial was complete was surrender permitted.
entries.literal: When about to die he left a final memorial thanking grace and again asked to submit the superior armor to the armory; only when the burial was complete was surrender permitted.

entries.zh: 皇建中，配享世宗廟庭。
entries.en: In the Huangjian era he was given paired sacrifice in Gao Cheng's temple hall.
entries.literal: In the Huangjian era he was given paired sacrifice in the Heir Apparent's temple hall.

entries.zh: 後歸彥反，世祖知其前譖，曰：「清河忠烈，盡力皇家，而歸彥毀之，間吾骨肉。」
entries.en: Later when Guiyan rebelled, Gao Zhan knew his earlier slander and said, "Prince of Qinghe was loyal and fierce, exerting himself for the royal house — yet Guiyan destroyed him and came between my flesh and bone."
entries.literal: Later when Guiyan rebelled, the Shizu Emperor knew his earlier slander and said: "Prince of Qinghe was loyal and fierce, exerting himself for the royal house — yet Guiyan destroyed him and came between my flesh and bone."

entries.zh: 籍沒歸彥，以良賤百口賜岳家。
entries.en: Guiyan's property was confiscated; a hundred mouths of good and low slaves were granted to Yue's household.
entries.literal: Guiyan's property was confiscated; a hundred mouths of good and low slaves were granted to Yue's household.

entries.zh: 後又思岳之功，重贈太師、太保，餘如故。
entries.en: Later, remembering Yue's merit, he was again posthumously made grand preceptor and grand tutor; other honors unchanged.
entries.literal: Later, remembering Yue's merit, he was again posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Grand Tutor; the rest as before.

entries.zh: 子勱嗣。
entries.en: His son Gao Mai succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Mai inherited the succession.

entries.zh: 世宗崩，顯祖出撫晉陽，令岳以本官兼尚書左僕射，留鎮京師。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng died Gao Yang went out to administer Jinyang and left Yue at his original post while additionally serving as left vice minister of the Masters of Writing, guarding the capital.
entries.literal: When the Heir Apparent died the Manifest Ancestor went out to administer Jinyang and ordered Yue to remain at his original post while additionally serving as Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, guarding the capital.

entries.zh: 天保初，進封清河郡王，尋除使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、宗師、司州牧。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianbao he was advanced to Prince of Qinghe Commandery; soon made bearer of the staff, grand general of the flying cavalry, opener with honors equal to the three ducal ministers, preceptor of the imperial clan, and governor of Si Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was advanced to Prince of Qinghe Commandery; soon made Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, Opener with Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, Preceptor of the Imperial Clan, and Governor of Si Province.

entries.zh: 五年，加太保。
entries.en: In the fifth year grand preceptor was added.
entries.literal: In the fifth year Grand Preceptor was added.

entries.zh: 梁蕭繹為周軍所逼，遣使告急，且請援。
entries.en: Xiao Yi of Liang, pressed by Zhou armies, sent envoys begging aid.
entries.literal: Xiao Yi of Liang, pressed by Zhou armies, sent envoys reporting emergency and requesting aid.

entries.zh: 冬，詔岳為西南道大行臺，統司徒潘相樂等救江陵。
entries.en: In winter an edict made Yue grand field headquarters of the southwest circuit, commanding minister of state Pan Xiangyue and others to rescue Jiangling.
entries.literal: In winter an edict made Yue Grand Field Headquarters of the Southwest Circuit, commanding Minister of State Pan Xiangyue and others to rescue Jiangling.

entries.zh: 六年正月，師次義陽，遇荊州陷，因略地南至郢州，獲梁州刺史司徒陸法和，仍剋郢州。
entries.en: In the first month of the sixth year, the army halted at Yiyang. When Jing Province fell, they raided south as far as Ying Province, captured Lu Fahe, Inspector of Liang Province and Minister of State, and then took Ying Province.
entries.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, the army halted at Yiyang. When Jing Province fell, they raided south as far as Ying Province, captured Lu Fahe, Inspector of Liang Province and Minister of State, and then took Ying Province.

entries.zh: 岳先送法和於京師，遣儀同慕容儼據郢城。
entries.en: Yue first sent Fahé to the capital and dispatched honorary equal Murong Yan to hold Ying city.
entries.literal: Yue first sent Fahé to the capital and dispatched Honorary Equal Murong Yan to hold Ying city.

entries.zh: 朝廷知江陵陷，詔岳旋師。
entries.en: When the court learned Jiangling had fallen, an edict ordered Yue to withdraw.
entries.literal: When the court learned Jiangling had fallen, an edict ordered Yue to withdraw.

entries.zh: 子整信嗣。
entries.en: His son Zhengxin succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Zhengxin succeeded him.

entries.zh: 歷散騎常侍、儀同三司。
entries.en: He rose in turn to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and honorary equal to the three ducal ministers.
entries.literal: He served in succession as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Honorary Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

entries.zh: 好學有行檢，少年時因獵墜馬，傷腰腳，卒不能行起，終於長安。
entries.en: He loved learning and kept his conduct straight. As a youth he fell from his horse on a hunt and injured waist and legs; he never walked again and died at Chang'an.
entries.literal: Fond of learning and upright in conduct, in youth he fell from a horse while hunting, injuring his waist and legs; he never walked again and died at Chang'an.

entries.zh: 琛同母弟惠寶早亡，元象初，贈侍中、尚書令、都督四州諸軍事、青州刺史。
entries.en: Chen's younger half-brother Huibao died young; in the first year of Yuanxiang he was posthumously made palace attendant, chief minister of the Masters of Writing, and military governor of four provinces and governor of Qing Province.
entries.literal: Chen's younger half-brother Huibao died young; in the first year of Yuanxiang he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Military Governor of Four Provinces, Governor of Qing Province.

entries.zh: 天統三年，重贈十州都督，封陳留王，諡曰文恭，以清河王岳第十子敬文嗣。
entries.en: In the third year of Tiantong he was again posthumously made military governor of ten provinces and enfeoffed Prince of Chenliu, posthumous name Wengong; Gao Yue's tenth son Jingwen was made his heir.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tiantong he was again posthumously made Military Governor of Ten Provinces, enfeoffed Prince of Chenliu, posthumous name Wengong; the tenth son of Prince of Qinghe Yue, Jingwen, was made heir.

entries.zh: 皇建初，行幷州事。
entries.en: At the beginning of Huangjian he acted as administrator of Bing Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he acted as Administrator of Bing Province.

entries.zh: 孝昭臨崩，預受顧托，奉迎世祖於鄴，以功拜尚書令，別封浮陽郡公，監太史，太子太傅，議律令。
entries.en: When Gao Yan faced death he received the imperial testament in advance, welcomed Gao Zhan at Ye, and for his service was appointed director of the masters of writing; he was separately enfeoffed duke of Fuyang Commandery, made supervisor of the grand astrologer, grand preceptor to the crown prince, and charged with deliberating on the code of laws.
entries.literal: When Xiaozhao faced death he received the imperial testament in advance, welcomed the Imperial Ancestor at Ye, and for his service was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing; he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Fuyang Commandery, made Supervisor of the Grand Astrologer, Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince, and charged with deliberating on the code of laws.

entries.zh: 又以討北狄之功，封潁川郡公。
entries.en: For merit in campaigning against the northern barbarians he was also enfeoffed duke of Yingchuan Commandery.
entries.literal: For merit in campaigning against the northern barbarians he was also enfeoffed Duke of Yingchuan Commandery.

entries.zh: 復拜尚書令，攝大宗正卿。
entries.en: He was again appointed director of the masters of writing and acting director of the grand clan court.
entries.literal: He was again appointed Director of the Masters of Writing and Acting Director of the Grand Clan Court.

entries.zh: 天統中，追贈叡父琛假黃鉞，母元氏贈趙郡王妃，諡曰貞昭，華陽長公主如故，有司備禮儀就墓拜授。
entries.en: In the Tiantong era Rui's father Chen was posthumously granted the yellow battle-axe; his mother the Yuan clan was posthumously made princess of Zhao Commandery with the posthumous title Zhenzhao — her title Princess Huayang remained unchanged — and the relevant offices prepared the rites and went to the tomb to invest her by proclamation.
entries.literal: In the Tiantong era Rui's father Chen was posthumously granted the Yellow Battle-Axe; his mother the Yuan clan was posthumously made Princess of Zhao Commandery with the posthumous title Zhenzhao — her title Princess Huayang remained unchanged — and the relevant offices prepared the rites and went to the tomb to invest her by proclamation.

entries.zh: 時隆冬盛寒，叡跣步號哭，面皆破裂，嘔血數升。
entries.en: It was deep winter and bitterly cold; Rui walked barefoot, wailing and crying until his face split open, and he vomited several sheng of blood.
entries.literal: It was deep winter and bitterly cold; Rui walked barefoot, wailing and crying until his face split open, and he vomited several sheng of blood.

entries.zh: 及還，不堪參謝，帝親就第看問。
entries.en: When he returned he could not bear to attend court in audience; the emperor personally visited his residence to inquire after him.
entries.literal: When he returned he could not bear to attend court in audience; the emperor personally visited his residence to inquire after him.

entries.zh: 拜司空，攝錄尚書事。
entries.en: He was appointed minister of works and acting recorder of affairs of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: He was appointed Minister of Works and Acting Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 突厥嘗侵軼至幷州，帝親禦戎，六軍進止皆令取叡節度。
entries.en: The Turks once raided as far as Bing Province; the emperor personally took the field, and the advance and halt of the six armies all followed Rui's command.
entries.literal: The Turks once raided as far as Bing Province; the emperor personally took the field, and the advance and halt of the six armies all followed Rui's command.

entries.zh: 以功復封宣城郡公。
entries.en: For his merit he was again enfeoffed duke of Xuancheng Commandery.
entries.literal: For his merit he was again enfeoffed Duke of Xuancheng Commandery.

entries.zh: 攝宗正卿，進拜太尉，監議五禮。
entries.en: Acting director of the grand clan court, he was promoted to grand commandant and made supervisor of the deliberation on the five rites.
entries.literal: Acting Director of the Grand Clan Court, he was promoted to Grand Commandant and made Supervisor of the deliberation on the Five Rites.

entries.zh: 叡久典朝政，清真自守，譽望日隆，漸被疏忌，乃撰古之忠臣義士，號曰《要言》，以致其意。
entries.en: Rui had long managed court politics, kept himself pure and upright, and his reputation rose day by day; he was gradually viewed with distant suspicion, and so he compiled ancient loyal ministers and righteous men in a work called Essential Words to express his intent.
entries.literal: Rui had long managed court politics, kept himself pure and upright, and his reputation rose day by day; he was gradually viewed with distant suspicion, and so he compiled ancient loyal ministers and righteous men in a work called Essential Words to express his intent.

entries.zh: 世祖崩，葬後數日，叡與馮翊王潤、安德王延宗及元文遙奏後主云 ：「和士開不宜仍居內任。」
entries.en: When Gao Zhan died, several days after the burial, Rui, together with Prince of Fengyi Gao Run, Prince of Ande Gao Yanzong, and Yuan Wenyao, memorialized the Last Emperor, saying, "He Shikai should not continue to hold an inner appointment."
entries.literal: When the Imperial Ancestor died, several days after the burial, Rui, together with the Prince of Fengyi Run, the Prince of Ande Yanzong, and Yuan Wenyao, memorialized the Last Emperor, saying, "He Shikai should not continue to hold an inner appointment."

entries.zh: 並入奏太后，因出士開為兗州刺史。
entries.en: They all entered to memorialize the empress dowager, and He Shikai was sent out as governor of Yan Province.
entries.literal: They all entered to memorialize the empress dowager, and He Shikai was sent out as Governor of Yan Province.

entries.zh: 太后曰：「士開舊經驅使，欲留過百日。」
entries.en: The empress dowager said, "Shikai has long served at my command — I wish to keep him for a hundred days more."
entries.literal: The empress dowager said, "Shikai has long served at my command — I wish to keep him for a hundred days more."

entries.zh: 叡正色不許。
entries.en: Rui with stern countenance would not permit it.
entries.literal: Rui with stern countenance would not permit it.

entries.zh: 數日之內，太后數以為言。
entries.en: Within a few days the empress dowager repeatedly spoke on his behalf.
entries.literal: Within a few days the empress dowager repeatedly spoke on his behalf.

entries.zh: 有中官要人知太后密旨，謂叡曰：「太后意既如此，殿下何宜苦違。」
entries.en: A favored eunuch who knew the empress dowager's secret intent said to Rui, "Since the empress dowager's wish is already thus, why should Your Highness stubbornly oppose it?"
entries.literal: A favored eunuch who knew the empress dowager's secret intent said to Rui, "Since the empress dowager's wish is already thus, why should Your Highness stubbornly oppose it?"

entries.zh: 叡曰：「吾國家事重，死且不避，若貪生茍全，令國家擾攘，非吾志也。
entries.en: Rui said, "Affairs of state and family are weighty — I would not shrink even from death; if I clung to life and sought safety, letting the state fall into turmoil, that is not my intent.
entries.literal: Rui said, "Affairs of state and family are weighty — I would not shrink even from death; if I clung to life and sought safety, letting the state fall into turmoil, that is not my intent.

entries.zh: 況受先皇遺旨，委寄不輕。
entries.en: Moreover I received the late emperor's testament — the trust placed in me is no light matter.
entries.literal: Moreover I received the late emperor's testament — the trust placed in me is no light matter.

entries.zh: 今嗣主幼沖，豈可使邪臣在側。
entries.en: The succeeding ruler is young and tender — how can an evil minister be kept at his side?
entries.literal: The succeeding ruler is young and tender — how can an evil minister be kept at his side?

entries.zh: 不守之以正，何面戴天。」
entries.en: If I do not uphold what is right, with what face can I look up to Heaven?"
entries.literal: If I do not uphold what is right, with what face can I look up to Heaven?"

entries.zh: 遂重進言，詞理懇切。
entries.en: He thereupon pressed his argument again, his words earnest and forceful.
entries.literal: He thereupon pressed his argument again, his words earnest and forceful.

entries.zh: 太后令酌酒賜叡。
entries.en: The empress dowager ordered wine poured and granted to Rui.
entries.literal: The empress dowager ordered wine poured and granted to Rui.

entries.zh: 叡正色曰：「今論國家大事，非為卮酒！」
entries.en: Rui with stern countenance said, "We are now discussing great affairs of state — this is not for a cup of wine!"
entries.literal: Rui with stern countenance said, "We are now discussing great affairs of state — this is not for a cup of wine!"

entries.zh: 言訖便出。
entries.en: When he finished speaking he went out at once.
entries.literal: When he finished speaking he went out at once.

entries.zh: 其夜，叡方寢，見一人可長丈五，臂長丈餘，當門向床，以臂壓叡，良久，遂失所在。
entries.en: That night Rui lay asleep when he saw a figure some fifteen chi tall, arms more than ten chi long, blocking the doorway and leaning over the bed. The arm pressed down on him a long while — then the apparition was gone.
entries.literal: That night Rui was asleep when he saw a man about fifteen chi tall, with arms more than ten chi long, standing in the doorway facing the bed; the man pressed Rui with his arm for a long while, then vanished.

entries.zh: 叡意甚惡之，便起坐獨嘆曰：「大丈夫命運一朝至此！」
entries.en: The omen filled Rui with dread. He sat up alone and sighed: "A great man's fate — to reach this in a single morning!"
entries.literal: Rui felt it deeply ill-omened; he rose at once and sighed alone: "A great man's fate has come to this in a single morning!"

entries.zh: 恐為太后所殺，旦欲入朝，妻子咸諫止之。
entries.en: Fearing the empress dowager meant to kill him, at dawn he would go to court; wife and children all pleaded with him to stay.
entries.literal: Fearing the empress dowager would kill him, at dawn he wished to enter court; his wife and children all remonstrated and stopped him.

entries.zh: 叡曰：「自古忠臣，皆不顧身命，社稷事重，吾當以死效之，豈容令一婦人傾危宗廟。
entries.en: Rui said, "Loyal ministers since antiquity have never counted their lives; the realm matters more than I — I should die for it. How can I let one woman overturn the altars?
entries.literal: Rui said: "Since ancient times loyal ministers have never spared their own lives; the altars weigh heavier than I — I ought to die in their service. How could I let one woman overturn the ancestral temple?

entries.zh: 且和士開何物豎子，如此縱橫，吾寧死事先皇，不忍見朝廷顛沛。」
entries.en: And what is He Shikai but a base upstart, strutting as he pleases? I would rather die serving the late emperor than watch the court come apart."
entries.literal: Besides, what sort of wretch is He Shikai, to run rampant like this? I would rather die serving the late emperor than live to see the court thrown into turmoil."

entries.zh: 至殿門，又有人曰：「願殿下勿入，慮有危變。」
entries.en: At the palace gate another voice said, "Do not go in, Highness — there may be treachery."
entries.literal: Reaching the palace gate, someone again said: "I beg Your Highness not to enter — I fear sudden danger."

entries.zh: 叡曰：「吾上不負天，死亦無恨。」
entries.en: Rui said, "I owe Heaven; if I die, I die without regret."
entries.literal: Rui said: "Above I owe Heaven; even in death I have no regret."

entries.zh: 入見太后，太后復以為言，叡執之彌固。
entries.en: He went in to the empress dowager; she argued as before, but Rui would not yield.
entries.literal: He entered and saw the empress dowager; she again spoke as before, but Rui held all the more firmly.

entries.zh: 出至永巷，遇兵被執，送華林園，於雀離佛院令劉桃枝拉而殺之，時年三十六。
entries.en: Leaving the palace he reached Eternal Lane, was seized by soldiers, and sent to Hualin Garden. At Sparrow-Departure Cloister Liu Taozhi strangled him. He was thirty-six.
entries.literal: Leaving he reached the Eternal Lane, met soldiers, was seized, and sent to Hualin Garden; at the Sparrow-Departure Buddhist cloister Liu Taozhi strangled and killed him. He was thirty-six.

entries.zh: 大霧三日，朝野冤惜之。
entries.en: Thick fog shrouded the land for three days; court and countryside grieved the injustice.
entries.literal: Heavy fog lasted three days; court and countryside mourned the injustice.

entries.zh: 期年後，詔聽以王禮葬，竟無贈諡焉。
entries.en: A year later an edict allowed princely burial — but no posthumous name was ever granted.
entries.literal: A year later an edict permitted burial with princely rites; in the end no posthumous title was granted.

entries.zh: 趙郡王琛 子叡 清河王岳 子勱
entries.en: Prince Chen of Zhao Commandery (Gao Chen); his son Rui (Gao Rui); Prince Yue of Qinghe (Gao Yue); his son Mai (Gao Mai)
entries.literal: Prince Chen of Zhao Commandery Chen; his son Rui; Prince Yue of Qinghe Yue; his son Mai

entries.zh: 廣平公盛 陽州公永樂 弟長弼 襄樂王顯國 上洛王思宗 子元海 弟思好 平秦王歸彥 武興王普 長樂太守靈山 嗣子伏護
entries.en: Duke Sheng of Guangping; Duke Yongle of Yangzhou; younger brother Changbi; Prince Xianguo of Xiangle; Prince Sizong of Shangluo; son Yuanhai; younger brother Sihao; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin; Prince Pu of Wuxing; Lingshan, Governor of Changle; successor son Fuhu
entries.literal: Duke Sheng of Guangping; Duke Yongle of Yangzhou; younger brother Changbi; Prince Xianguo of Xiangle; Prince Sizong of Shangluo; son Yuanhai; younger brother Sihao; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin; Prince Pu of Wuxing; Lingshan, Governor of Changle; successor son Fuhu

entries.zh: 廣平公盛，神武從叔祖也。
entries.en: Duke Sheng of Guangping was a great-uncle of Gao Huan on the father's side.
entries.literal: Duke Sheng of Guangping was a great-uncle of the Grand Ancestor on the father's side.

entries.zh: 寬厚有長者風。
entries.en: Generous and mild, he had the bearing of an elder of worth.
entries.literal: Generous and mild, he had the bearing of an elder of worth.

entries.zh: 神武起兵於信都，以盛為中軍大都督，封廣平郡公。
entries.en: When Gao Huan raised troops at Xindu, he made Sheng grand commander of the center army and enfeoffed him duke of Guangping Commandery.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised troops at Xindu, he made Sheng Grand Commander of the Center Army and enfeoffed him Duke of Guangping Commandery.

entries.zh: 歷位司徒、太尉。
entries.en: He rose in succession to minister of works and grand commandant.
entries.literal: He rose in succession to Minister of Works and Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 天平三年，薨於位。
entries.en: In the third year of Tianping, he died in office.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianping, he died in office.

entries.zh: 贈假黃鉞，太尉、太師、錄尚書事。
entries.en: Posthumously he was granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand commandant, grand preceptor, and recorder of affairs of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Commandant, Grand Preceptor, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 無子，以兄子子瑗嗣。
entries.en: Having no son, he made his elder brother's son Ziyuan his heir.
entries.literal: Having no son, he made his elder brother's son Ziyuan his heir.

entries.zh: 天保初，改封平昌王，卒於魏尹。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianbao, his title was changed to prince of Pingchang; he died while serving as governor of Wei.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, his title was changed to Prince of Pingchang; he died while serving as Governor of Wei.

entries.zh: 陽州公永樂，神武從祖兄子也。
entries.en: Duke Yongle of Yangzhou was the son of Gao Huan's father's elder cousin.
entries.literal: Duke Yongle of Yangzhou was the son of the Grand Ancestor's father's elder cousin.

entries.zh: 太昌初，封陽州縣伯，進爵為公。
entries.en: At the beginning of Taichang, he was enfeoffed baron of Yangzhou County and his rank was advanced to duke.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was enfeoffed Baron of Yangzhou County and his rank was advanced to duke.

entries.zh: 累遷北豫州刺史。
entries.en: He rose in succession to governor of Beiyu Province.
entries.literal: He rose in succession to Governor of Beiyu Province.

entries.zh: 河陰之戰，司徒高昂失利退。
entries.en: At the Battle of Heyin, Minister of Works Gao Ang suffered defeat and withdrew.
entries.literal: At the Battle of Heyin, Minister of Works Gao Ang suffered defeat and withdrew.

entries.zh: 永樂守河陽南城，昂走趣城，西軍追者將至，永樂不開門，昂遂為西軍所擒。
entries.en: Yongle held the southern city of Heyang; Ang fled toward the city, and as the Western army's pursuers were about to arrive, Yongle would not open the gate — Ang was thereupon captured by the Western army.
entries.literal: Yongle held the southern city of Heyang; Ang fled toward the city, and as the Western army's pursuers were about to arrive, Yongle would not open the gate — Ang was thereupon captured by the Western army.

entries.zh: 神武大怒，杖之二百。
entries.en: Gao Huan was furious and had him beaten two hundred strokes with the staff.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor was furious and had him beaten two hundred strokes with the staff.

entries.zh: 後罷豫州，家產不立。
entries.en: Later he was removed from Yu Province, and his household estate was not established.
entries.literal: Later he was removed from Yu Province, and his household estate was not established.

entries.zh: 神武問其故，對曰：「裴監為長史，辛公正為別駕，受王委寄，斗酒只雞不入。」
entries.en: Gao Huan asked the reason; he replied, "Pei Jian served as chief administrator, and Xin Gongzheng as vice director — entrusted by the prince, they would not accept so much as a cup of wine or a chicken."
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor asked the reason; he replied, "Pei Jian served as Chief Administrator, and Xin Gongzheng as Vice Director — entrusted by the prince, they would not accept so much as a cup of wine or a chicken."

entries.zh: 神武乃以永樂為濟州，仍以監、公正為長史、別駕。
entries.en: Gao Huan thereupon made Yongle governor of Ji Province and again appointed Jian and Gongzheng as chief administrator and vice director.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor thereupon made Yongle Governor of Ji Province and again appointed Jian and Gongzheng as Chief Administrator and Vice Director.

entries.zh: 謂永樂曰：「爾勿大貪，小小義取莫復畏。」
entries.en: He said to Yongle, "Do not be too greedy — take a little in propriety and need not fear again."
entries.literal: He said to Yongle, "Do not be too greedy — take a little in propriety and need not fear again."

entries.zh: 永樂至州，監、公正諫不見聽，以狀啟神武。
entries.en: When Yongle reached the province, Jian and Gongzheng remonstrated but were not heeded; they submitted a report to Gao Huan.
entries.literal: When Yongle reached the province, Jian and Gongzheng remonstrated but were not heeded; they submitted a report to the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 神武封啟以示永樂。
entries.en: Gao Huan sealed the report and showed it to Yongle.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor sealed the report and showed it to Yongle.

entries.zh: 然後知二人清直，並擢用之。
entries.en: Only then did he know the two men were upright and incorrupt; both were promoted and employed.
entries.literal: Only then did he know the two men were upright and incorrupt; both were promoted and employed.

entries.zh: 永樂卒於州。
entries.en: Yongle died in the province.
entries.literal: Yongle died in the province.

entries.zh: 贈太師、太尉、錄尚書事，諡曰武昭。
entries.en: Posthumously he was made grand preceptor, grand commandant, and recorder of affairs of the masters of writing; his posthumous title was Wuzhao.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was made Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing; his posthumous title was Wuzhao.

entries.zh: 無子，從兄思宗以第二子孝緒為後，襲爵。
entries.en: Having no son, his elder cousin Sizong made his second son Xiaoxu his successor to inherit the title.
entries.literal: Having no son, his elder cousin Sizong made his second son Xiaoxu his successor to inherit the title.

entries.zh: 天保初，改封脩城郡王。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianbao, his title was changed to prince of Xiucheng Commandery.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, his title was changed to Prince of Xiucheng Commandery.

entries.zh: 思好本浩氏子也，思宗養以為弟，遇之甚薄。
entries.en: Sihao was originally a son of the Hao clan; Sizong raised him as a younger brother but treated him very poorly.
entries.literal: Sihao was originally a son of the Hao clan; Sizong raised him as a younger brother but treated him very poorly.

entries.zh: 少以騎射事文襄。
entries.en: In youth he served Gao Cheng in horsemanship and archery.
entries.literal: In youth he served the Imperial Founder in horsemanship and archery.

entries.zh: 及文宣受命，為左衛大將軍。
entries.en: When Wenxuan took the throne, Sihao was made grand general of the Left Guard.
entries.literal: When Wenxuan received the Mandate, Sihao was made Grand General of the Left Guard.

entries.zh: 本名思孝，天保五年，討蠕蠕，文宣悅其驍勇，謂曰：「爾擊賊如鶻入鴉群，宜思好事。」
entries.en: His original name was Sixiao. In the fifth year of Tianbao, on campaign against the Rouran, Wenxuan delighted in his fierce bravery and said, "You strike the enemy like a goshawk among crows — think on deeds worthy of that gift."
entries.literal: His original name was Sixiao. In the fifth year of Tianbao, campaigning against the Rouran, Wenxuan was pleased with his fierce valor and said: "You strike the enemy like a goshawk among crows — you ought to think of good deeds."

entries.zh: 故改名焉。
entries.en: Hence his name was changed.
entries.literal: Hence he was renamed.

entries.zh: 累遷尚書令、朔州道行臺、朔州刺史、開府、南安王，甚得邊朔人心。
entries.en: He rose in turn to director of the Masters of Writing, field headquarters of the Shuozhou circuit, governor of Shuozhou, opening-establishment honors, and Prince of Nan'an — and won deep loyalty on the northern frontier.
entries.literal: He rose in succession to Director of the Masters of Writing, Field Headquarters of the Shuozhou Circuit, Governor of Shuozhou, opening-establishment, and Prince of Nan'an — and won the hearts of the northern frontier greatly.

entries.zh: 襄樂王顯國，神武從祖弟也。
entries.en: Prince Xianguo of Xiangle was a younger kinsman of Gao Huan's paternal clan.
entries.literal: Prince Xianguo of Xiangle was Shenwu's younger cousin in the ancestral line.

entries.zh: 無才伎，直以宗室謹厚，天保元年，封襄樂王，位右衛將軍。
entries.en: He had no special ability, but because he was a cautious and generous imperial clansman, he was made Prince of Xiangle in the first year of Tianbao and served as General of the Right Guard.
entries.literal: He had no talents or skills; simply because, as a member of the imperial clan, he was cautious and generous, in the first year of Tianbao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangle and held office as General of the Right Guard.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 上洛王思宗，神武從子也。
entries.en: Prince Sizong of Shangluo was a nephew of Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Prince Sizong of Shangluo was a nephew of the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 性寬和，頗有武幹。
entries.en: By nature generous and mild, he possessed considerable martial ability.
entries.literal: By nature generous and mild, he possessed considerable martial ability.

entries.zh: 天保初，封上洛郡王。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was enfeoffed prince of Shangluo Commandery.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Shangluo Commandery.

entries.zh: 歷位司空、太傅。
entries.en: He rose in succession to minister of works and grand tutor.
entries.literal: He rose in succession to Minister of Works and Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 薨於官。
entries.en: He died in office.
entries.literal: He died in office.

entries.zh: 平秦王歸彥，字仁英，神武族弟也。
entries.en: Prince of Pingqin Guiyan, courtesy name Renying, was a younger cousin of Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Prince of Pingqin Guiyan, courtesy name Renying, was a younger clansman of Shenwu on the father's side.

entries.zh: 父徽，魏末坐事當徙涼州，行至河、渭間，遇賊，以軍功得免流。
entries.en: His father Hui, at the end of Wei, was implicated in a crime and condemned to exile in Liangzhou. Between the Yellow and Wei rivers he met bandits and, through military service, won release from banishment.
entries.literal: His father Hui, at the end of Wei, was implicated in a crime and sentenced to exile in Liangzhou; traveling between the Yellow and Wei rivers he encountered bandits and, through military merit, obtained release from banishment.

entries.zh: 因於河州積年。
entries.en: He remained in Hezhou many years.
entries.literal: He therefore remained in Hezhou many years.

entries.zh: 以解胡言，為西域大使，得胡師子來獻，以功得河東守。
entries.en: Fluent in the Hu tongue, he served as ambassador to the Western Regions, obtained a Hu lion to present as tribute, and was made governor of Hedong for his merit.
entries.literal: Because he understood the Hu tongue, he served as ambassador to the Western Regions, obtained a Hu lion to present as tribute, and for merit was made Governor of Hedong.

entries.zh: 尋遂死焉。
entries.en: He died there not long after.
entries.literal: Before long he died there.

entries.zh: 徽於神武舊恩甚篤。
entries.en: Hui and Gao Huan shared a deep old bond.
entries.literal: Hui and Shenwu had been bound by deep old obligation.

entries.zh: 及神武平京洛，迎徽喪與穆同營葬。
entries.en: When Gao Huan pacified Luoyang, he brought Hui's coffin home and buried him in the same tomb compound as Lady Mu.
entries.literal: When Shenwu pacified the capital and Luoyang, he brought Hui's coffin back and buried him in the same tomb precinct as Lady Mu.

entries.zh: 贈司徒，諡曰文宣。
entries.en: He was posthumously made minister over the masses, posthumous name Wenxuan.
entries.literal: Hui was posthumously made Minister over the Masses, posthumous name Wenxuan.

entries.zh: 初徽嘗過長安市，與婦人王氏私通而生歸彥，至是年已九歲。
entries.en: Hui had once passed through the Chang'an market and had an affair with a woman of the Wang clan, who gave birth to Guiyan; by this time the boy was already nine.
entries.literal: At first Hui once passed through the Chang'an market and had illicit relations with a woman of the Wang clan, by whom Guiyan was born; by this year he was already nine years old.

entries.zh: 神武追見之，撫對悲喜。
entries.en: When Gao Huan later met him, he stroked the boy and was overcome by both grief and joy.
entries.literal: Shenwu later saw him; stroking him as they faced one another, he felt both grief and joy.

entries.zh: 稍遷徐州刺史。
entries.en: He was gradually promoted to Inspector of Xu Province.
entries.literal: He was gradually promoted to Inspector of Xu Province.

entries.zh: 歸彥少質朴，後更改節，放縱好聲色，朝夕酣歌。
entries.en: Guiyan was plain and unpolished in youth, but later changed his ways, gave himself over to sensual pleasures, and drank and sang day and night.
entries.literal: Guiyan was simple and unpolished when young, but later changed his conduct, becoming unrestrained and fond of music and women, drinking and singing from morning to night.

entries.zh: 妻魏上黨王元天穆女也，貌不美而甚驕妒，數忿爭，密啟文宣求離，事寢不報。
entries.en: His wife was a daughter of Yuan Tianmu, Prince of Shangdang of Wei. She was not beautiful and was extremely arrogant and jealous; after repeated angry quarrels, Guiyan secretly petitioned Wenxuan for a separation, but the matter was shelved without reply.
entries.literal: His wife was a daughter of Yuan Tianmu, Prince of Shangdang of Wei; she was not beautiful in appearance but was very arrogant and jealous, and after repeated angry quarrels he secretly petitioned Wenxuan seeking separation, but the matter was shelved and not reported back.

entries.zh: 天保元年，封平秦王。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianbao, he was made Prince of Pingqin.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Pingqin.

entries.zh: 嫡妃康及所生母王氏並為太妃。
entries.en: His principal consort, Lady Kang, and his birth mother, Lady Wang, were both made grand consorts.
entries.literal: His principal consort Kang and his birth mother, Lady Wang, were both made grand consorts.

entries.zh: 善事二母，以孝聞。
entries.en: He served both mothers well and was known for filial piety.
entries.literal: He served his two mothers well and was known for filial piety.

entries.zh: 徵為兼侍郎，稍被親寵。
entries.en: He was summoned to serve as acting shilang and gradually won the emperor's close favor.
entries.literal: He was summoned to serve as acting shilang and gradually received intimate favor.

entries.zh: 以討侯景功，別封長樂郡公，除領軍大將軍。
entries.en: For his service in the campaign against Hou Jing, he received a separate enfeoffment as Duke of Changle Commandery and was appointed Grand General of the Army Command.
entries.literal: For merit in the campaign against Hou Jing, he was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Changle Commandery and appointed Grand General of the Army Command.

entries.zh: 領軍加大，自歸彥始也。
entries.en: The expanded title of Grand General of the Army Command began with Guiyan.
entries.literal: The addition of 'Grand' to the Army Command began with Guiyan.

entries.zh: 文宣誅高德正，金寶財貨悉以賜之。
entries.en: When Wenxuan executed Gao Dezheng, he gave Guiyan all of Gao's gold, jewels, wealth, and property.
entries.literal: When Wenxuan executed Gao Dezheng, he bestowed all the gold, jewels, wealth, and goods on him.

entries.zh: 幹明初，拜司徒，仍總知禁衛。
entries.en: At the beginning of Ganming, he was appointed Minister over the Masses and continued to oversee the palace guards.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Ganming, he was appointed Minister over the Masses and still oversaw the palace guard as a whole.

entries.zh: 武興王普，字德廣，歸彥兄歸義之子也。
entries.en: Prince Pu of Wuxing, courtesy name Deguang, was the son of Guiyan's elder brother Guiyi.
entries.literal: Prince Pu of Wuxing, courtesy name Deguang, was the son of Guiyan's elder brother Guiyi.

entries.zh: 性寬和有度量。
entries.en: By nature he was generous, even-tempered, and possessed of measure.
entries.literal: By nature he was generous, harmonious, and possessed of measure.

entries.zh: 九歲，歸彥自河州俱入洛，神武使與諸子同遊處。
entries.en: At nine, when Guiyan came from Hezhou into Luoyang with him, Gao Huan had him lodge and roam with his own sons.
entries.literal: At nine years of age, when Guiyan came from Hezhou into Luoyang together with him, Shenwu had him lodge and roam with his own sons.

entries.zh: 天保初，封武興郡王。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Wuxing Commandery.

entries.zh: 武平二年，累遷司空。
entries.en: In the second year of Wuping he rose to minister of works.
entries.literal: In the second year of Wuping he rose in succession to Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 六年，為豫州道行臺、尚書令。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was made field headquarters of the Yuzhou circuit and director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was made Field Headquarters of the Yuzhou Circuit and Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 後主奔鄴，就加太宰。
entries.en: When the Later Lord fled to Ye, Pu was additionally made grand preceptor.
entries.literal: When the Later Lord fled to Ye, Pu was additionally made Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 周師逼，乃降。
entries.en: When the armies of Zhou closed in, he yielded.
entries.literal: When the Zhou armies pressed close, he thereupon surrendered.

entries.zh: 卒於長安。
entries.en: He died at Chang'an.
entries.literal: He died at Chang'an.

entries.zh: 贈上開府、豫州刺史。
entries.en: Posthumously he was granted an upper opening establishment and the governorship of Yu Province.
entries.literal: Posthumously granted Upper Opening Establishment and Governor of Yu Province.

entries.zh: 皇建末，孝昭幸晉陽，武成居守，元海以散騎常侍留典機密。
entries.en: At the end of the Huangjian era, Gao Yan visited Jinyang while Gao Zhan remained on guard; Yuanhai, as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, stayed behind to manage confidential affairs.
entries.literal: At the end of the Huangjian era, Xiaozhao visited Jinyang while Wucheng remained on guard; Yuanhai, as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, stayed behind to manage confidential affairs.

entries.zh: 初孝昭之誅楊愔等，謂武成云：「事成，以爾為皇太弟。」
entries.en: When Gao Yan first executed Yang Yin and the others, he had told Gao Zhan, "When the affair succeeds, I will make you imperial younger brother."
entries.literal: When Xiaozhao first executed Yang Yin and the others, he had told Wucheng, "When the affair succeeds, I will make you Imperial Younger Brother."

entries.zh: 及踐祚，乃使武成在鄴主兵，立子百年為皇太子，武成甚不平。
entries.en: When he ascended the throne, he made Gao Zhan hold troops at Ye and established his son Bainian as crown prince — Gao Zhan was very discontent.
entries.literal: When he ascended the throne, he made Wucheng hold troops at Ye and established his son Bainian as crown prince — Wucheng was very discontent.

entries.zh: 先是，恒留濟南於鄴，除領軍厙狄伏連為幽州刺史，以斛律豐樂為領軍，以分武成之權。
entries.en: Before this, the Prince of Ji'nan had always been kept at Ye; Kudi Fulian was made governor of You Province, and Hulu Fengle was made commander of the army — both to divide Gao Zhan's power.
entries.literal: Before this, the Prince of Ji'nan had always been kept at Ye; Kudi Fulian was made Governor of You Province, and Hulu Fengle was made Commander of the Army — both to divide Wucheng's power.

entries.zh: 武成留伏連而不聽豐樂視事。
entries.en: Gao Zhan kept Fulian but would not allow Fengle to assume his duties.
entries.literal: Wucheng kept Fulian but would not allow Fengle to assume his duties.

entries.zh: 乃與河南王孝瑜偽獵，謀於野，暗乃歸。
entries.en: He then joined Prince Xiaoyu of Henan in a feigned hunt, plotting in the wild, and returned only after dark.
entries.literal: He then joined Prince Xiaoyu of Henan in a feigned hunt, plotting in the wild, and returned only after dark.

entries.zh: 先是童謠云：「中興寺內白鳧翁，四方側聽聲雍雍，道人聞之夜打鐘。」
entries.en: Before this a children's rhyme said, "At Zhongxing Temple, a white duck old man — from the four quarters they listen, the sound harmonious; the Daoist hears it and at night strikes the bell."
entries.literal: Before this a children's rhyme said, "At Zhongxing Temple, a white duck old man — from the four quarters they listen, the sound harmonious; the Daoist hears it and at night strikes the bell."

entries.zh: 時丞相府在北城中，卽舊中興寺也。
entries.en: At that time the chancellor's headquarters was in the northern city — that is, the old Zhongxing Temple.
entries.literal: At that time the chancellor's headquarters was in the northern city — that is, the old Zhongxing Temple.

entries.zh: 鳧翁，謂雄雞，蓋指武成小字步落稽也。
entries.en: "Duck old man" means rooster — it pointed to Gao Zhan's childhood name Buluoqi.
entries.literal: "Duck old man" means rooster — it pointed to Wucheng's childhood name Buluoqi.

entries.zh: 道人，濟南王小名。
entries.en: "The Daoist" was the Prince of Ji'nan's childhood name.
entries.literal: "The Daoist" was the Prince of Ji'nan's childhood name.

entries.zh: 打鐘，言將被擊也。
entries.en: "Strikes the bell" meant he would be beaten.
entries.literal: "Strikes the bell" meant he would be beaten.

entries.zh: 旣而太史奏言北城有天子氣。
entries.en: Soon afterward the court astrologer memorialized that there was an emperor's aura in the northern city.
entries.literal: Soon afterward the court astrologer memorialized that there was an emperor's aura in the northern city.

entries.zh: 昭帝以為濟南應之，乃使平秦王歸彥之鄴，迎濟南赴幷州。
entries.en: Gao Yan thought the Prince of Ji'nan corresponded to it; he therefore sent Prince Guiyan of Pingqin to Ye to welcome the Prince of Ji'nan to Bing Province.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhao thought the Prince of Ji'nan corresponded to it; he therefore sent Prince Guiyan of Pingqin to Ye to welcome the Prince of Ji'nan to Bing Province.

entries.zh: 武成先咨元海，並問自安之計。
entries.en: Gao Zhan first consulted Yuanhai and also asked for a plan to secure himself.
entries.literal: Wucheng first consulted Yuanhai and also asked for a plan to secure himself.

entries.zh: 元海曰：「皇太后萬福，至尊孝性非常，殿下不須別慮。」
entries.en: Yuanhai said, "The Empress Dowager enjoys boundless fortune; the emperor's filial nature is extraordinary — Your Highness need not worry otherwise."
entries.literal: Yuanhai said, "The Empress Dowager enjoys boundless fortune; the emperor's filial nature is extraordinary — Your Highness need not worry otherwise."

entries.zh: 武成曰：「豈我推誠之意耶？」
entries.en: Gao Zhan said, "Is this truly the meaning of my open-hearted sincerity?"
entries.literal: Wucheng said, "Is this truly the meaning of my open-hearted sincerity?"

entries.zh: 元海乞還省一夜思之。
entries.en: Yuanhai asked to return to his quarters and think on it one night.
entries.literal: Yuanhai asked to return to his quarters and think on it one night.

entries.zh: 武成卽留元海後堂。
entries.en: Gao Zhan kept Yuanhai in the rear hall.
entries.literal: Wucheng kept Yuanhai in the rear hall.

entries.zh: 元海達旦不眠，唯繞床徐步。
entries.en: Yuanhai went all night without sleep, only pacing slowly around the bed.
entries.literal: Yuanhai went all night without sleep, only pacing slowly around the bed.

entries.zh: 夜漏未曙，武成遽出，曰：「神算如何？」
entries.en: Before dawn Gao Zhan hurried out and said, "What is your divine calculation?"
entries.literal: Before dawn Wucheng hurried out and said, "What is your divine calculation?"

entries.zh: 答云：「夜中得三策，恐不堪用耳。」
entries.en: He answered, "In the night I obtained three stratagems — I fear they may not be usable."
entries.literal: He answered, "In the night I obtained three stratagems — I fear they may not be usable."

entries.zh: 因說梁孝王懼誅入關事，請乘數騎入晉陽，先見太后求哀，後見主上，請去兵權，以死為限，求不干朝政，必保太山之安。
entries.en: He then spoke of Prince Xiao of Liang, who fearing execution entered the passes, and proposed that with a few horsemen he enter Jinyang, first see the Empress Dowager and beg mercy, then see the sovereign and request removal of military authority, taking death as his limit and seeking not to interfere in court governance — he would surely preserve the security of Mount Tai.
entries.literal: He then spoke of Prince Xiao of Liang, who fearing execution entered the passes, and proposed that with a few horsemen he enter Jinyang, first see the Empress Dowager and beg mercy, then see the sovereign and request removal of military authority, taking death as his limit and seeking not to interfere in court governance — he would surely preserve the security of Mount Tai.

entries.zh: 此上策也。
entries.en: This was the upper stratagem.
entries.literal: This was the upper stratagem.

entries.zh: 若不然，當具表，云「『威權大盛，恐取謗衆口』，請青、齊二州刺史。
entries.en: If not, he should submit a memorial stating, "'My authority and power are too great; I fear I will draw slander from the multitude' — and request the governorships of Qing and Qi Provinces.
entries.literal: If not, he should submit a memorial stating, "'My authority and power are too great; I fear I will draw slander from the multitude' — and request the governorships of Qing and Qi Provinces.

entries.zh: 沉靜自居，必不招物議。
entries.en: Dwelling in quiet and keeping to himself, he would surely not invite public criticism.
entries.literal: Dwelling in quiet and keeping to himself, he would surely not invite public criticism.

entries.zh: 此中策也。」
entries.en: This was the middle stratagem."
entries.literal: This was the middle stratagem."

entries.zh: 更問下策曰：「發言卽恐族誅。」
entries.en: When asked further about the lower stratagem he said, "To speak would mean immediate execution of the whole clan."
entries.literal: When asked further about the lower stratagem he said, "To speak would mean immediate execution of the whole clan."

entries.zh: 因逼之，答曰：「濟南世嫡，主上假太后令而奪之。
entries.en: Pressed, he answered, "The Prince of Ji'nan is the legitimate heir; the sovereign seized the throne through the Empress Dowager's order.
entries.literal: Pressed, he answered, "The Prince of Ji'nan is the legitimate heir; the sovereign seized the throne through the Empress Dowager's order.

entries.zh: 今集文武，示以此勑，執豐樂，斬歸彥，尊濟南，號令天下，以順討逆，此萬世一時也。」
entries.en: Now gather the civil and military officials, display this edict, seize Fengle, behead Guiyan, honor the Prince of Ji'nan, and proclaim to the realm — with righteousness to punish rebellion, this would be a once-in-ten-thousand-generations opportunity."
entries.literal: Now gather the civil and military officials, display this edict, seize Fengle, behead Guiyan, honor the Prince of Ji'nan, and proclaim to the realm — with righteousness to punish rebellion, this would be a once-in-ten-thousand-generations opportunity."

entries.zh: 武成大悅，狐疑，竟未能用。
entries.en: Gao Zhan was greatly pleased but hesitated, and in the end could not adopt it.
entries.literal: Wucheng was greatly pleased but hesitated, and in the end could not adopt it.

entries.zh: 乃使鄭道謙卜之，皆曰：「不利舉事，靜則吉。」
entries.en: He then had Zheng Daoqian perform divination; all said, "It is unfavorable to act; quiet brings good fortune."
entries.literal: He then had Zheng Daoqian perform divination; all said, "It is unfavorable to act; quiet brings good fortune."

entries.zh: 又召曹魏祖，問之國事。
entries.en: He also summoned Cao Weizu and questioned him on state affairs.
entries.literal: He also summoned Cao Weizu and questioned him on state affairs.

entries.zh: 對曰：「當有大凶。」
entries.en: He replied, "There will be great misfortune."
entries.literal: He replied, "There will be great misfortune."

entries.zh: 又時有林慮令姓潘，知占候，密謂武成曰：「宮車當晏駕，殿下為天下主。」
entries.en: At that time the Magistrate of Linlu, surnamed Pan, knew divination and omens; he secretly told Gao Zhan, "The imperial carriage will break at dusk — Your Highness will be sovereign of the realm."
entries.literal: At that time the Magistrate of Linlu, surnamed Pan, knew divination and omens; he secretly told Wucheng, "The imperial carriage will break at dusk — Your Highness will be sovereign of the realm."

entries.zh: 武成拘之於內以候之。
entries.en: Gao Zhan detained him inside to wait for the outcome.
entries.literal: Wucheng detained him inside to wait for the outcome.

entries.zh: 又令巫覡卜之，多云不須舉兵，自有大慶。
entries.en: He also had shamans perform divination; most said there was no need to raise troops — great good fortune would come of itself.
entries.literal: He also had shamans perform divination; most said there was no need to raise troops — great good fortune would come of itself.

entries.zh: 武成乃奉詔，令數百騎送濟南於晉陽。
entries.en: Gao Zhan thereupon obeyed the edict and sent several hundred horsemen to escort the Prince of Ji'nan to Jinyang.
entries.literal: Wucheng thereupon obeyed the edict and sent several hundred horsemen to escort the Prince of Ji'nan to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 孝昭崩，歸彥從晉陽迎武成於鄴。
entries.en: When Xiaozhao died, Guiyan went from Jinyang to welcome Wucheng to Ye.
entries.literal: When Xiaozhao died, Guiyan went from Jinyang to welcome Wucheng at Ye.

entries.zh: 及武成卽位，進位太傅，領司徒，常聽將私部曲三人帶刀入仗。
entries.en: When Wucheng took the throne, Guiyan was made grand tutor and minister over the masses, and was regularly allowed three armed retainers at his side in the guard of honor.
entries.literal: When Wucheng took the throne, Guiyan was advanced to Grand Tutor, held the title Minister over the Masses, and was regularly permitted to bring three private retainers, swords at belt, into the guard of honor.

entries.zh: 從武成還都，諸貴戚等競要之，其所往處，一坐盡傾。
entries.en: Returning to the capital with Wucheng, the great families vied to host him. Wherever he went, the room tilted his way.
entries.literal: Returning to the capital with Wucheng, the high nobles all vied to invite him — wherever he went, the whole gathering leaned toward him.

entries.zh: 歸彥旣地居將相，志意盈滿，發言陵侮，旁若無人。
entries.en: Having reached the summit of general and chancellor, Guiyan's ambition brimmed over. His speech turned overbearing, as though no one else were in the room.
entries.literal: Guiyan now stood among generals and chancellors; his ambition brimmed over — his words were overbearing and insulting, as if no one else were present.

entries.zh: 議者以威權震主，必為禍亂。
entries.en: Commentators warned that his power overshadowed the throne — disaster was inevitable.
entries.literal: Commentators held that his might and authority alarmed the ruler — he would surely bring calamity and chaos.

entries.zh: 上亦尋其前翻覆之跡，漸忌之。
entries.en: The emperor, recalling his earlier betrayals, grew wary.
entries.literal: The emperor also traced his earlier shifts of loyalty and gradually grew wary.

entries.zh: 高元海、畢義雲、高乾乾和等咸數言其短。
entries.en: Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, Gao Qianhe, and others repeatedly denounced him.
entries.literal: Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, Gao Qianhe, and others repeatedly spoke of his faults.

entries.zh: 上幸歸彥家，召魏收對御作詔草，欲加右丞相。
entries.en: The emperor visited Guiyan's home and summoned Wei Shou to draft an edict in his presence — intending to add the title right chancellor.
entries.literal: The emperor visited Guiyan's home, summoned Wei Shou to compose an edict in the royal presence, intending to add the title Right Chancellor.

entries.zh: 收謂元海曰：「至尊以右丞相登位，今為歸彥威名太盛，故出之，豈可復加此號。」
entries.en: Shou said to Yuanhai, "His Majesty took the throne as right chancellor. Guiyan's fame is too great — that is why he is being sent away. How can we give him that title again?"
entries.literal: Shou said to Yuanhai: "His Majesty took the throne as right chancellor — now, because Guiyan's fame and power are too great, he is being sent out; how could that title be given again?"

entries.zh: 乃拜太宰、冀州刺史，卽乾和繕寫。
entries.en: Instead he was appointed grand preceptor and governor of Ji Province — Gao Qianhe copied the edict at once.
entries.literal: He was therefore appointed Grand Preceptor and Governor of Ji Province — Gao Qianhe copied it out at once.

entries.zh: 晝日，仍勑門司不聽輒入內。
entries.en: That same day an order went to the gate office: no entry to the palace without leave.
entries.literal: That same day, an order was issued to the gate office forbidding entry into the palace without permission.

entries.zh: 時歸彥在家縱酒，經宿不知，至明欲參，至門知之，大驚而退。
entries.en: Guiyan was at home drinking through the night and knew nothing. At dawn he set out for audience — reached the gate, learned what had happened, and fled back in alarm.
entries.literal: Guiyan was at home drinking freely; he knew nothing until dawn. When he wished to attend audience and reached the gate and learned of it, he was greatly startled and withdrew.

entries.zh: 及通名謝，勑令早發，別賜錢帛、鼓吹、醫藥，事事周備。
entries.en: When he announced himself to take leave, he was told to depart at once. Money, silk, musicians, physicians — every comfort was provided.
entries.literal: When he announced himself to take leave, he was ordered to depart early; money, silk, musicians, and medicine were separately bestowed — every need provided.

entries.zh: 又勑武職督將悉送至青陽宮，拜而退，莫敢共語。
entries.en: Military officers were ordered to escort him to Qingyang Palace. They bowed and withdrew — none dared speak with him.
entries.literal: Military officers and commanders were also ordered to escort him all the way to Qingyang Palace; they bowed and withdrew, none daring to speak with him together.

entries.zh: 唯與趙郡王叡久語，時無聞者。
entries.en: Only with Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui did he speak at length — and no one heard what passed.
entries.literal: Only with Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui did he converse at length — at the time none overheard them.

entries.zh: 初濟南自晉陽之鄴，楊愔宣勑，留從駕五千兵於西中，陰備非常。
entries.en: When Prince of Jinan first traveled from Jinyang to Ye, Yang Yin read the edict leaving five thousand troops of the escort in the Western Quarter — a secret guard against surprise.
entries.literal: At first, when the Prince of Jinan went from Jinyang to Ye, Yang Yin proclaimed the edict and left five thousand troops of the imperial escort in the Western Quarter, secretly preparing against the unexpected.

entries.zh: 至鄴數日，歸彥乃知之，由是陰怨楊、燕。
entries.en: Several days after reaching Ye, Guiyan learned of it and began to nurse secret resentment against Yang and Yan.
entries.literal: Several days after reaching Ye, Guiyan learned of it — and from this nursed secret resentment against Yang and Yan.

entries.zh: 楊、燕等欲去二王，問計於歸彥。
entries.en: Yang, Yan, and their faction meant to remove the two princes and sought Guiyan's counsel.
entries.literal: Yang, Yan, and the rest wished to remove the two princes and asked Guiyan's counsel.

entries.zh: 歸彥詐喜，請共元海量之。
entries.en: Guiyan feigned enthusiasm and proposed consulting Yuanhai together.
entries.literal: Guiyan feigned delight and asked to take counsel together with Yuanhai.

entries.zh: 元海亦口許心違，馳告長廣。
entries.en: Yuanhai agreed with his lips while his heart refused, and raced to warn Prince of Changguang.
entries.literal: Yuanhai likewise assented with his mouth while his heart refused, and galloped to inform Prince of Changguang.

entries.zh: 長廣於是誅楊、燕等。
entries.en: Changguang thereupon executed Yang, Yan, and their allies.
entries.literal: Prince of Changguang thereupon put Yang, Yan, and the rest to death.

entries.zh: 孝昭將入雲龍門，都督成休寧列仗拒而不內，歸彥諭之，然後得入，進向柏閤、永巷亦如之。
entries.en: When Xiaozhao was about to enter the Cloud-Dragon Gate, commander Cheng Xiuning drew up his troops and barred the way. Guiyan talked him round — only then was entry granted. The same at Cypress Pavilion and Eternal Lane.
entries.literal: When Xiaozhao was about to enter the Cloud-Dragon Gate, Commander Cheng Xiuning drew up troops and barred him; Guiyan persuaded him, and only then was entry granted — proceeding toward the Cypress Pavilion and the Eternal Lane, the same again.

entries.zh: 孝昭踐祚，以此彌見優重，每入常在平原王段韶上。
entries.en: When Xiaozhao took the throne, Guiyan was favored all the more for this — at every audience he was seated above Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao.
entries.literal: When Xiaozhao ascended the throne, for this he was all the more favored and honored — whenever he entered audience he was always ranked above Prince of Pingyuan Duan Shao.

entries.zh: 以為司空，兼尚書令。
entries.en: He was made minister of works and concurrently director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: He was made Minister of Works and concurrently Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 齊制，宮內唯天子紗帽，臣下皆戎帽，特賜歸彥紗帽以寵之。
entries.en: Under Qi law only the emperor wore the gauze cap within the palace; all others wore military caps. Guiyan alone was granted a gauze cap — a singular mark of favor.
entries.literal: Under Qi law, within the palace only the Son of Heaven wore the gauze cap; all subjects wore military caps — Guiyan was specially granted a gauze cap as a mark of favor.

entries.zh: 及孝昭崩，武成卽位，除元海侍中、開府儀同三司、太子詹事。
entries.en: When Gao Yan died and Gao Zhan ascended the throne, Yuanhai was made palace attendant, opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators, and grand tutor to the crown prince.
entries.literal: When Xiaozhao died and Wucheng ascended the throne, Yuanhai was made Palace Attendant, Opener of a Government Office Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators, and Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 河清二年，元海為和士開所譖，被捶馬鞭六十。
entries.en: In the second year of Heqing, Yuanhai was slandered by He Shikai and was beaten sixty strokes with the horsewhip.
entries.literal: In the second year of Heqing, Yuanhai was slandered by He Shikai and was beaten sixty strokes with the horsewhip.

entries.zh: 責云：「爾在鄴城，說我以弟反兄，幾許不義！
entries.en: He was rebuked, "You at Ye told me to rebel as younger brother against elder brother — how many acts of unrighteousness were there!
entries.literal: He was rebuked, "You at Ye told me to rebel as younger brother against elder brother — how many acts of unrighteousness were there!

entries.zh: 鄴城兵馬抗幷州，幾許無智！
entries.en: Ye's troops and horses resisting Bing Province — how many acts of folly were there!
entries.literal: Ye's troops and horses resisting Bing Province — how many acts of folly were there!

entries.zh: 不義無智，若為可使？」
entries.en: Unrighteous and foolish — how could you be employed?"
entries.literal: Unrighteous and foolish — how could you be employed?"

entries.zh: 出為兗州刺史。
entries.en: He was sent out as governor of Yan Province.
entries.literal: He was sent out as Governor of Yan Province.

entries.zh: 元海後妻，陸太姬甥也，故尋被追任使。
entries.en: Yuanhai's later wife was a niece of Empress Dowager Lu; for this reason he was soon recalled and given employment again.
entries.literal: Yuanhai's later wife was a niece of Empress Dowager Lu; for this reason he was soon recalled and given employment again.

entries.zh: 武平中，與祖珽共執朝政。
entries.en: In the Wuping era he jointly held court governance with Zu Ting.
entries.literal: In the Wuping era he jointly held court governance with Zu Ting.

entries.zh: 元海多以太姬密語告珽。
entries.en: Yuanhai often reported the Empress Dowager's confidential words to Ting.
entries.literal: Yuanhai often reported the Empress Dowager's confidential words to Ting.

entries.zh: 珽求領軍，元海不可，珽乃以其所告報太姬。
entries.en: Ting sought the post of commander of the army; Yuanhai would not agree — Ting thereupon reported what Yuanhai had told him to the Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: Ting sought the post of Commander of the Army; Yuanhai would not agree — Ting thereupon reported what Yuanhai had told him to the Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 姬怒，出元海為鄭州刺史。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager was angry and sent Yuanhai out as governor of Zheng Province.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager was angry and sent Yuanhai out as Governor of Zheng Province.

entries.zh: 鄴城將敗，徵為尚書令。
entries.en: When Ye was about to fall, he was summoned and made director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: When Ye was about to fall, he was summoned and made Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 周建德七年，於鄴城謀逆，伏誅。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Jiande of Zhou, at Ye he plotted rebellion and was executed.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Jiande of Zhou, at Ye he plotted rebellion and was executed.

entries.zh: 魏時山崩，得石角二，藏在武庫。
entries.en: In Wei times a mountain collapsed and two stone horns were found and stored in the armory.
entries.literal: In Wei times a mountain collapsed and two stone horns were obtained, stored in the armory.

entries.zh: 文宣入庫，賜從臣兵器，特以二石角與歸彥。
entries.en: Wenxuan entered the armory to distribute weapons among his followers and specially gave the two stone horns to Guiyan.
entries.literal: Wenxuan entered the storehouse to distribute weapons among his followers and specially gave the two stone horns to Guiyan.

entries.zh: 謂曰：「爾事常山不得反，事長廣得反，反時，將此角嚇漢。」
entries.en: He said, "Serving Changshan you did not rebel; serving Changguang you rebelled. When you rebel, use these horns to frighten the Han."
entries.literal: He said: "Serving Changshan you did not rebel; serving Changguang you rebelled — when you rebel, use these horns to frighten the Han."

entries.zh: 歸彥額骨三道，著幘不安。
entries.en: Guiyan had three ridges on his brow; a headcloth would not sit straight on his skull.
entries.literal: Guiyan had three ridges on his forehead bone; wearing a headcloth he could not keep it in place.

entries.zh: 文宣嘗見之，怒，使以馬鞭擊其額，血被面，曰：「爾反時當以此骨嚇漢。」
entries.en: Wenxuan once saw it and grew angry. He had Guiyan struck on the brow with a horsewhip until blood covered his face, saying, "When you rebel you should use this bone to frighten the Han."
entries.literal: Wenxuan once saw it and grew angry; he had him struck on the forehead with a horsewhip until blood covered his face, saying: "When you rebel you should use this bone to frighten the Han."

entries.zh: 其言反竟驗云。
entries.en: In the end his words of rebellion came true.
entries.literal: His words of rebellion were fulfilled in the end.

entries.zh: 長樂太守靈山，字景嵩，神武族弟也。
entries.en: Lingshan, Governor of Changle, styled Jingsong, was Gao Huan's clansman and younger brother.
entries.literal: Lingshan, Governor of Changle, styled Jingsong, was a clansman younger brother of Shenwu (Gao Huan).

entries.zh: 從神武起兵信都，終於長樂太守。
entries.en: He followed Gao Huan when arms were raised at Xindu and ended his life as Governor of Changle.
entries.literal: He followed Shenwu (Gao Huan) in raising troops at Xindu, and ended as Governor of Changle.

entries.zh: 贈大將軍、司空，諡曰文宣。
entries.en: Posthumously he was made grand general and minister of works, with the posthumous title Wenxuan.
entries.literal: Posthumously granted Grand General and Minister of Works; his posthumous title was Wenxuan.

entries.zh: 子懿，卒於武平鎮將，無子，文宣帝以靈山從父兄齊州刺史建國子伏護為靈山後。
entries.en: His son Yi died as commander of the Wuping garrison without heirs; Emperor Wenxuan appointed Fuhu — son of Jianguo, Governor of Qi Province and Lingshan's elder paternal cousin — to carry on Lingshan's line.
entries.literal: His son Yi died as commander of the Wuping garrison without heirs; Emperor Wenxuan made Fuhu, son of Jianguo, Governor of Qi Province and Lingshan's elder paternal cousin, successor to Lingshan's line.

entries.zh: 竇泰，字世寧，大安捍殊人也。
entries.en: Dou Tai, courtesy name Shining, was a native of Da'an Hanshu.
entries.literal: Dou Tai, courtesy name Shining, was a native of Da'an Hanshu.

entries.zh: 本出清河觀津，曾祖羅，魏統萬鎮將，因居北邊。
entries.en: His family originally came from Guanjin in Qinghe; his great-grandfather Luo was general of the Wei garrison at Tongwan and settled on the northern frontier.
entries.literal: His family originally came from Guanjin in Qinghe; his great-grandfather Luo was general of the Wei garrison at Tongwan and settled on the northern frontier.

entries.zh: 父樂，魏末破六韓拔陵為亂，與鎮將楊鈞固守，遇害。
entries.en: His father Yue, when Poliuhan Baling rebelled at the end of Wei, held firm with the garrison general Yang Jun and was killed in action.
entries.literal: His father Yue, when Poliuhan Baling rebelled at the end of Wei, held firm with the garrison general Yang Jun and was killed in action.

entries.zh: 泰貴，追贈司徒。
entries.en: When Dou Tai rose high, his father Yue was posthumously made minister of education.
entries.literal: When Tai rose high, Yue was posthumously made minister of education.

entries.zh: 初，泰母夢風雷暴起，若有雨狀，出庭觀之，見電光奪目，駛雨霑灑，寤而驚汗，遂有娠。
entries.en: At first Dou Tai's mother dreamed that wind and thunder burst up as though rain were coming; she went out to the courtyard to watch and saw lightning dazzle her eyes and driving rain spatter down; waking in a sweat of alarm, she conceived.
entries.literal: At first Tai's mother dreamed that wind and thunder burst up as though rain were coming; she went out to the courtyard to watch and saw lightning dazzle her eyes and driving rain spatter down; waking in a sweat of alarm, she conceived.

entries.zh: 期而不產，大懼。
entries.en: When her term passed without birth, she was greatly afraid.
entries.literal: When her term passed without birth, she was greatly afraid.

entries.zh: 有巫曰：「渡河湔裙，產子必易。」
entries.en: A witch said, "Cross the river and wash your skirt, and the birth will surely come easily."
entries.literal: A witch said, "Cross the river and wash your skirt, and the birth will surely come easily."

entries.zh: 便向水所。
entries.en: She went at once toward the water.
entries.literal: She went at once toward the water.

entries.zh: 忽見一人，曰：「當生貴子，可徙而南。」
entries.en: Suddenly she saw a man who said, "You will bear a noble son; move south."
entries.literal: Suddenly she saw a man who said, "You will bear a noble son; move south."

entries.zh: 泰母從之。
entries.en: Dou Tai's mother obeyed.
entries.literal: Tai's mother obeyed.

entries.zh: 俄而生泰。
entries.en: Soon afterward Dou Tai was born.
entries.literal: Soon afterward Tai was born.

entries.zh: 及長，善騎射，有勇略。
entries.en: When he grew up, he was skilled at riding and archery and possessed courage and strategy.
entries.literal: When he grew up, he was skilled at riding and archery and possessed courage and strategy.

entries.zh: 泰父兄戰歿於鎮，泰身負骸骨歸尒朱榮。
entries.en: Dou Tai's father and elder brother died in battle at the garrison; Dou Tai personally carried their bones back to Erzhu Rong.
entries.literal: Tai's father and elder brother died in battle at the garrison; Tai personally carried their bones back to Erzhu Rong.

entries.zh: 以從討邢杲功，賜爵廣阿子。
entries.en: For following the campaign against Xing Gao and meriting success, he was granted the title viscount of Guanga.
entries.literal: For following the campaign against Xing Gao and meriting success, he was granted the title Viscount of Guanga.

entries.zh: 神武之為晉州，請泰為鎮城都督，參謀軍事。
entries.en: When Gao Huan became governor of Jin Province, he requested Dou Tai as garrison-city commander and staff officer for military affairs.
entries.literal: When Shenwu became governor of Jin Province, he requested Tai as garrison-city commander and staff officer for military affairs.

entries.zh: 累遷侍中、京畿大都督，尋領御史中尉。
entries.en: He rose in succession to palace attendant, grand commander of the capital region, and soon afterward also served as censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: He rose in succession to palace attendant, grand commander of the capital region, and soon afterward also served as censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 泰以勳戚居臺，雖無多糾舉，而百僚畏懼。
entries.en: Dou Tai, holding high office by merit and kinship, made few impeachments, yet the hundred officials feared him.
entries.literal: Tai, holding high office by merit and kinship, made few impeachments, yet the hundred officials feared him.

entries.zh: 尉景，字士真，善無人也。
entries.en: Wei Jing, styled Shizhen, was a native of Shanwu.
entries.literal: Wei Jing, styled Shizhen, was a native of Shanwu.

entries.zh: 秦、漢置尉候官，其先有居此職者，因以氏焉。
entries.en: In Qin and Han the office of frontier scout was established; an ancestor who had held that post took it as the clan surname.
entries.literal: In Qin and Han the office of frontier scout was established; an ancestor who had held that post took it as the clan surname.

entries.zh: 景性溫厚，頗有俠氣。
entries.en: Jing was warm by nature and possessed a chivalrous spirit.
entries.literal: Jing was warm by nature and possessed a chivalrous spirit.

entries.zh: 魏孝昌中，北鎮反，景與神武入杜洛周軍中，仍共歸尒朱榮。
entries.en: In the Xiaochang era of Wei, when the northern garrisons rebelled, Jing entered Du Luozhou's army together with Gao Huan and then both returned to Erzhu Rong.
entries.literal: In the Xiaochang era of Wei, when the northern garrisons rebelled, Jing entered Du Luozhou's army together with Shenwu and then both returned to Erzhu Rong.

entries.zh: 以軍功封博野縣伯。
entries.en: For military merit he was enfeoffed baron of Boye County.
entries.literal: For military merit he was enfeoffed baron of Boye County.

entries.zh: 後從神武起兵信都。
entries.en: Later he followed Gao Huan in raising troops at Xindu.
entries.literal: Later he followed Shenwu in raising troops at Xindu.

entries.zh: 韓陵之戰，唯景所統失利。
entries.en: At the Battle of Hanling, only the force Jing commanded suffered defeat.
entries.literal: At the Battle of Hanling, only the force Jing commanded suffered defeat.

entries.zh: 神武入洛，留景鎮鄴。
entries.en: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, he left Jing to garrison Ye.
entries.literal: When Shenwu entered Luoyang, he left Jing to garrison Ye.

entries.zh: 尋進封為公。
entries.en: Soon afterward his rank was advanced to duke.
entries.literal: Soon afterward his rank was advanced to duke.

entries.zh: 天平三年，神武西討，令泰自潼關入。
entries.en: In the third year of Tianping, Gao Huan campaigned west and ordered Dou Tai to enter by Tong Pass.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianping, Shenwu campaigned west and ordered Tai to enter by Tong Pass.

entries.zh: 四年，泰至小關，為周文帝所襲，衆盡沒，泰自殺。
entries.en: In the fourth year Dou Tai reached Little Pass, was ambushed by Yuwen Tai, and his whole force was destroyed; Dou Tai killed himself.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Tai reached Little Pass, was ambushed by Emperor Wen of Zhou, and his whole force was destroyed; Tai killed himself.

entries.zh: 初，泰將發鄴，鄴有惠化尼謠云：「竇行臺，去不回。」
entries.en: At first, when Dou Tai was about to set out from Ye, a ballad of the nun Huihua in Ye said, "Commandery Chief Dou goes and does not return."
entries.literal: At first, when Tai was about to set out from Ye, a ballad of the nun Huihua in Ye said, "Commandery Chief Dou goes and does not return."

entries.zh: 未行之前，夜三更，忽有朱衣冠幘數千人入臺，云「收竇中尉」，宿直兵吏皆驚，其人入數屋，俄頃而去。
entries.en: Before he marched, at the third watch of the night, suddenly several thousand men in red robes and caps entered the censorate, saying they had come "to arrest Censor Dou"; the night guards and clerks were all alarmed; the figures entered several rooms and in a moment were gone.
entries.literal: Before he marched, at the third watch of the night, suddenly several thousand men in red robes and caps entered the censorate, saying they had come "to arrest Censor Dou"; the night guards and clerks were all alarmed; the figures entered several rooms and in a moment were gone.

entries.zh: 旦視關鍵不異，方知非人。
entries.en: At dawn they looked and the locks were unchanged; only then did they know these were not human beings.
entries.literal: At dawn they looked and the locks were unchanged; only then did they know these were not human beings.

entries.zh: 皆知其必敗。
entries.en: All knew he was doomed to defeat.
entries.literal: All knew he was doomed to defeat.

entries.zh: 贈大司馬、太尉、錄尚書事，諡曰武貞。
entries.en: Posthumously he was made grand marshal, grand commandant, and recorder of affairs of the masters of writing; his posthumous title was Wuzhen.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was made grand marshal, grand commandant, and recorder of affairs of the masters of writing; his posthumous title was Wuzhen.

entries.zh: 泰妻，武明婁后妹也。
entries.en: Dou Tai's wife was the younger sister of Empress Lou Wuming.
entries.literal: Tai's wife was the younger sister of Empress Lou Wuming.

entries.zh: 泰雖以親見待，而功名自建。
entries.en: Although Dou Tai was treated as kin, his fame and achievement were his own.
entries.literal: Although Tai was treated as kin, his fame and achievement were his own.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，祭告其墓。
entries.en: When Qi received the abdication, sacrifice was announced at his tomb.
entries.literal: When Qi received the abdication, sacrifice was announced at his tomb.

entries.zh: 皇建初，配享神武廟庭。
entries.en: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given associated sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple court.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given associated sacrifice in Shenwu's temple court.

entries.zh: 子孝敬嗣。
entries.en: His son Xiaojing succeeded.
