entries.literal: His son Xiaojing succeeded.

entries.zh: 位儀同三司。
entries.en: He rose to Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes (yitong sansi).
entries.literal: He rose to Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes (yitong sansi).

entries.zh: 景妻常山君，神武之姊也。
entries.en: Jing's wife, Lady Changshan, was Gao Huan's elder sister.
entries.literal: Jing's wife, Lady Changshan, was Shenwu's elder sister.

entries.zh: 以勳戚，每有軍事，與厙狄干常被委重，而不能忘懷財利，神武每嫌責之。
entries.en: As a meritorious kinsman, whenever there was military business he and Kudie Gan were often entrusted with weighty command, yet he could not put aside profit; Gao Huan frequently reproved him for it.
entries.literal: As a meritorious kinsman, whenever there was military business he and Kudie Gan were often entrusted with weighty command, yet he could not put aside profit; Shenwu frequently reproved him for it.

entries.zh: 轉冀州刺史，又大納賄，發夫獵，死者三百人。
entries.en: Transferred to governor of Ji Province, he again took large bribes and pressed laborers into a hunt in which three hundred men died.
entries.literal: Transferred to governor of Ji Province, he again took large bribes and pressed laborers into a hunt in which three hundred men died.

entries.zh: 厙狄干與景在神武坐，請作御史中尉。
entries.en: Kudie Gan and Jing, while seated with Gao Huan, asked to serve as censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: Kudie Gan and Jing, while seated with Shenwu, asked to serve as censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 神武曰：「何意下求卑官？」
entries.en: Gao Huan said, "Why do you seek so low an office?"
entries.literal: Shenwu said, "Why do you seek so low an office?"

entries.zh: 干曰：「欲捉尉景。」
entries.en: Kudie Gan said, "To arrest Wei Jing."
entries.literal: Gan said, "To arrest Wei Jing."

entries.zh: 神武大笑，令優者石董桶戲之。
entries.en: Gao Huan laughed greatly and had the actor Shi Dongtong mock them.
entries.literal: Shenwu laughed greatly and had the actor Shi Dongtong mock them.

entries.zh: 董桶剝景衣，曰：「公剝百姓，董桶何為不剝公！」
entries.en: Dongtong stripped Jing's clothes and said, "You strip the common people — why should Dongtong not strip you!"
entries.literal: Dongtong stripped Jing's clothes and said, "You strip the common people — why should Dongtong not strip you!"

entries.zh: 神武誡景曰：「可以無貪也。」
entries.en: Gao Huan admonished Jing, "You can do without greed."
entries.literal: Shenwu admonished Jing, "You can do without greed."

entries.zh: 景曰：「與爾計生活孰多，我止人上取，爾割天子調。」
entries.en: Jing said, "When we reckon whose way of living brings in more, I only take from people; you carve off the emperor's taxes."
entries.literal: Jing said, "When we reckon whose way of living brings in more, I only take from people; you carve off the emperor's taxes."

entries.zh: 神武笑不答。
entries.en: Gao Huan smiled and did not answer.
entries.literal: Shenwu smiled and did not answer.

entries.zh: 改長樂郡公。
entries.en: His title was changed to duke of Changle Commandery.
entries.literal: His title was changed to Duke of Changle Commandery.

entries.zh: 歷位太保、太傅，坐匿亡人見禁止。
entries.en: He rose in succession to grand guardian and grand tutor, then was imprisoned for concealing a fugitive.
entries.literal: He rose in succession to grand guardian and grand tutor, then was imprisoned for concealing a fugitive.

entries.zh: 使崔暹謂文襄曰：「語阿惠兒，富貴欲殺我耶！」
entries.en: He had Cui Xian tell Gao Cheng, "Tell Ahuier — does his wealth and power mean to kill me!"
entries.literal: He had Cui Xian tell Wenshuang, "Tell Ahuier — does his wealth and power mean to kill me!"

entries.zh: 神武聞之泣，詣闕曰：「臣非尉景，無以至今日。」
entries.en: Gao Huan heard and wept; he went to the palace and said, "Were it not for Wei Jing, your subject would never have reached today."
entries.literal: Shenwu heard and wept; he went to the palace and said, "Were it not for Wei Jing, your subject would never have reached today."

entries.zh: 三請，帝乃許之。
entries.en: After three petitions the emperor granted it.
entries.literal: After three petitions the emperor granted it.

entries.zh: 於是黜為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: Thereupon he was demoted to general of the imperial horse and opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was demoted to general of the imperial horse and opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators.

entries.zh: 神武造之，景恚臥不動，叫曰：「殺我時趣耶！」
entries.en: Gao Huan visited him; Jing lay in anger and would not rise, shouting, "If you're going to kill me, hurry up!"
entries.literal: Shenwu visited him; Jing lay in anger and would not rise, shouting, "If you're going to kill me, hurry up!"

entries.zh: 常山君謂神武曰：「老人去死近，何忍煎迫至此。」
entries.en: Lady Changshan said to Gao Huan, "The old man is near death — how can you press him so cruelly?"
entries.literal: Lady Changshan said to Shenwu, "The old man is near death — how can you press him so cruelly?"

entries.zh: 又曰：「我為爾汲水胝生。」
entries.en: She also said, "I drew water for you until calluses formed on my hands."
entries.literal: She also said, "I drew water for you until calluses formed on my hands."

entries.zh: 因出其掌。
entries.en: She then showed her palms.
entries.literal: She then showed her palms.

entries.zh: 神武撫景，為之屈膝。
entries.en: Gao Huan comforted Jing and knelt before him.
entries.literal: Shenwu comforted Jing and knelt before him.

entries.zh: 先是，景有果下馬，文襄求之，景不與，曰：「土相扶為墻，人相扶為王，一馬亦不得畜而索也。」
entries.en: Before this Jing had a pony; Gao Cheng asked for it, and Jing would not give it, saying, "Earth piled together makes a wall; men supporting one another make a king — not even one horse may be kept and then demanded back."
entries.literal: Before this Jing had a pony; Wenshuang asked for it, and Jing would not give it, saying, "Earth piled together makes a wall; men supporting one another make a king — not even one horse may be kept and then demanded back."

entries.zh: 神武對景及常山君責文襄而杖之。
entries.en: Gao Huan, before Jing and Lady Changshan, rebuked Gao Cheng and had him beaten.
entries.literal: Shenwu, before Jing and Lady Changshan, rebuked Wenshuang and had him beaten.

entries.zh: 常山君泣救之。
entries.en: Lady Changshan wept and pleaded for him.
entries.literal: Lady Changshan wept and pleaded for him.

entries.zh: 景曰：「小兒慣去，放使作心腹，何須干啼濕哭不聽打耶！」
entries.en: Jing said, "The boy is used to indulgence — let him learn to be a trusted man; why all this weeping and wailing to stop a beating!"
entries.literal: Jing said, "The boy is used to indulgence — let him learn to be a trusted man; why all this weeping and wailing to stop a beating!"

entries.zh: 尋授青州刺史，操行頗改，百姓安之。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was appointed governor of Qing Province; his conduct improved greatly, and the people lived at ease.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed governor of Qing Province; his conduct improved greatly, and the people lived at ease.

entries.zh: 徵授大司馬。
entries.en: Summoned back, he was made grand marshal.
entries.literal: Summoned back, he was made grand marshal.

entries.zh: 遇疾，薨於州。
entries.en: He fell ill and died in the province.
entries.literal: He fell ill and died in the province.

entries.zh: 贈太師、尚書令。
entries.en: Posthumously he was made grand preceptor and director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was made grand preceptor and director of the masters of writing.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，以景元勳，詔祭告其墓。
entries.en: When Qi received the abdication, because Jing was an original meritorious minister, an edict ordered sacrifice announced at his tomb.
entries.literal: When Qi received the abdication, because Jing was an original meritorious minister, an edict ordered sacrifice announced at his tomb.

entries.zh: 皇建初，配享神武廟庭，追封長樂王。
entries.en: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given associated sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple court and posthumously enfeoffed prince of Changle.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given associated sacrifice in Shenwu's temple court and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Changle.

entries.zh: 神武將出信都，昭贊成大策，卽以為中軍大都督。
entries.en: When Gao Huan was about to march out from Xindu, Zhao endorsed the grand plan and was immediately made Grand Commander of the Central Army.
entries.literal: When Shenwu was about to set out from Xindu, Zhao endorsed the grand plan and was at once made Grand Commander of the Central Army.

entries.zh: 從破尒朱兆於廣阿，封安喜縣伯，改濟北公，又徙濮陽郡公，授領軍將軍。
entries.en: He took part in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, was enfeoffed as Baron of Anxi County, then made Duke of Jibei and later Duke of Puyang Commandery, and was appointed General of the Guard Army.
entries.literal: He followed in defeating Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, was enfeoffed as Baron of Anxi County, changed to Duke of Jibei, then transferred to Duke of Puyang Commandery, and was appointed General of the Guard Army.

entries.zh: 魏孝武將貳於神武，昭以疾辭還晉陽。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei was about to break with Gao Huan, Zhao pleaded illness and returned to Jinyang.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei was about to become divided from Shenwu, Zhao excused himself on grounds of illness and returned to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 從神武入洛，兗州刺史樊子鵠反，以昭為東道大都督討之。
entries.en: He followed Gao Huan into Luoyang. When Fan Zihu, Inspector of Yan Province, rebelled, Zhao was made Grand Commander of the Eastern Route and sent to suppress him.
entries.literal: He followed Shenwu into Luoyang; when Fan Zihu, Inspector of Yan Province, rebelled, Zhao was made Grand Commander of the Eastern Route to campaign against him.

entries.zh: 子鵠既死，諸將勸昭盡捕誅其黨。
entries.en: After Zihu was dead, the generals urged Zhao to arrest and execute all his followers.
entries.literal: After Zihu had died, the generals urged Zhao to arrest and execute all of his followers.

entries.zh: 昭曰：「此州無狀，橫被殘賊，其君是怨，其人何罪。」
entries.en: Zhao said, "This province was helplessly overrun by violent rebels. Their lord is the one to blame. What crime have the people committed?"
entries.literal: Zhao said, "This province was in poor condition and was violently overrun by cruel rebels; their lord is the one to blame, so what crime have the people committed?"

entries.zh: 遂皆捨焉。
entries.en: He released them all.
entries.literal: Thereupon he released them all.

entries.zh: 後轉大司馬，仍領軍。
entries.en: He was later made Grand Marshal while retaining command of the Guard Army.
entries.literal: Later he was transferred to Grand Marshal while still commanding the Guard Army.

entries.zh: 遷司徒，出為定州刺史。
entries.en: He was promoted to Minister over the Masses and sent out as Inspector of Ding Province.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Minister over the Masses and sent out as Inspector of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 昭好酒，晚得偏風，雖愈，猶不能處劇務，在州事委僚屬，昭舉其大綱而已。
entries.en: Zhao loved wine and in later life suffered a stroke. Although he recovered, he still could not manage demanding business, so in the province he left affairs to his staff and handled only the broad outlines.
entries.literal: Zhao liked wine, and in later life suffered a stroke; although he recovered, he still could not handle heavy business, so in the province he entrusted affairs to his staff and only took up the main outlines.

entries.zh: 薨於州。
entries.en: He died in the province.
entries.literal: He died in the province.

entries.zh: 贈假黃鉞、太師、太尉，諡曰武。
entries.en: Posthumously he was granted the acting yellow battle-axe and the titles Grand Preceptor and Grand Commandant; his posthumous name was Wu.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted the acting yellow battle-axe, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Commandant; his posthumous name was Wu.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，詔祭告其墓，封太原王。
entries.en: When Qi received the abdication, an edict ordered sacrifices announced at his tomb, and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: When Qi received the abdication, an edict ordered sacrifice announced at his tomb, and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 皇建初，配享神武廟庭。
entries.en: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given associated sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple court.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given associated sacrifice in Shenwu's temple court.

entries.zh: 長子仲達嗣，改封濮陽王。
entries.en: His eldest son Zhongda succeeded him, and the title was changed to Prince of Puyang.
entries.literal: His eldest son Zhongda succeeded and the title was changed to Prince of Puyang.

entries.zh: 婁昭，字菩薩，代郡平城人也，武明皇後之母弟也。
entries.en: Lou Zhao, styled Pusa, was a native of Pingcheng in Dai Commandery and the maternal younger brother of Empress Lou Wuming.
entries.literal: Lou Zhao, styled Pusa, was a native of Pingcheng in Dai Commandery and the maternal younger brother of Empress Lou Wuming.

entries.zh: 祖父提，雄傑有識度，家僮千數，牛馬以谷量。
entries.en: His grandfather Ti was bold and far-sighted; his household had a thousand servants, and cattle and horses were counted by the bushel.
entries.literal: His grandfather Ti was bold and far-sighted; his household had a thousand servants, and cattle and horses were counted by the bushel.

entries.zh: 性好周給，士多歸附之。
entries.en: By nature he delighted in giving to others; many men of worth attached themselves to him.
entries.literal: By nature he delighted in giving to others; many men of worth attached themselves to him.

entries.zh: 魏太武時，以功封真定侯。
entries.en: In the reign of Emperor Taiwu of Wei he was enfeoffed marquis of Zhending for merit.
entries.literal: In the reign of Emperor Taiwu of Wei he was enfeoffed marquis of Zhending for merit.

entries.zh: 父內干，有武力，未仕而卒。
entries.en: His father Neigan possessed martial strength but died before holding office.
entries.literal: His father Neigan possessed martial strength but died before holding office.

entries.zh: 昭貴，魏朝贈司徒。
entries.en: When Lou Zhao rose high, the Wei court posthumously made his father Neigan minister of education.
entries.literal: When Zhao rose high, the Wei court posthumously made Neigan minister of education.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，追封太原王。
entries.en: When Qi received the abdication, Lou Zhao's father Neigan was posthumously enfeoffed prince of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: When Qi received the abdication, Neigan was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 昭方雅正直，有大度深謀，腰帶八尺，弓馬冠世。
entries.en: Lou Zhao was dignified, upright, and of great bearing, with deep designs; his belt was eight feet long, and in archery and horsemanship he stood first in the age.
entries.literal: Zhao was dignified, upright, and of great bearing, with deep designs; his belt was eight feet long, and in archery and horsemanship he stood first in the age.

entries.zh: 神武少親重之。
entries.en: From youth Gao Huan treated him with close regard.
entries.literal: From youth Shenwu treated him with close regard.

entries.zh: 昭亦早識人，恒曲盡禮敬。
entries.en: Lou Zhao also recognized men early and always showed them full courtesy and respect.
entries.literal: Zhao also recognized men early and always showed them full courtesy and respect.

entries.zh: 數隨神武獵，每致請不宜乘危歷階。
entries.en: He often followed Gao Huan on hunts and each time urged that one should not ride through danger or up steep slopes.
entries.literal: He often followed Shenwu on hunts and each time urged that one should not ride through danger or up steep slopes.

entries.zh: 次子定遠，少歷顯職，外戚中偏為武成愛狎。
entries.en: The second son Dingyuan, from youth, held prominent posts; among the imperial kin he was especially favored and intimate with Gao Zhan.
entries.literal: The second son Dingyuan, from youth, held prominent posts; among the imperial kin he was especially favored and intimate with Wucheng.

entries.zh: 別封臨淮郡王。
entries.en: He was separately enfeoffed prince of Linhuai Commandery.
entries.literal: He was separately enfeoffed Prince of Linhuai Commandery.

entries.zh: 武成大漸，與趙郡王等同受顧命，位司空。
entries.en: As Wucheng grew gravely ill, Dingyuan together with the Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui and others received the final testament; Dingyuan was made minister of works.
entries.literal: As Wucheng grew gravely ill, he and Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui and others alike received the final testament; Dingyuan was made Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 趙郡王之奏黜和士開，定遠與其謀，遂納士開賄賂，成趙郡之禍，其貪鄙如此。
entries.en: When Prince of Zhao Commandery moved to dismiss He Shikai, Dingyuan joined the plot — then took He Shikai's bribe and brought ruin on the prince. Such was his greed.
entries.literal: When Prince of Zhao Commandery memorialized to dismiss He Shikai, Dingyuan joined the plot — then accepted He Shikai's bribe, bringing calamity upon the prince; such was his greed and baseness.

entries.zh: 尋除瀛州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he was made governor of Ying Province.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Ying Province.

entries.zh: 初，定遠弟季略，穆提婆求其伎妾，定遠不許。
entries.en: Earlier, Dingyuan's younger brother Jilue had a performing concubine. Mutipo demanded her; Dingyuan refused.
entries.literal: Earlier, Dingyuan's younger brother Jilue had a performing concubine; Mutipo asked for her, and Dingyuan refused.

entries.zh: 因高思好作亂，提婆令臨淮國郎中令告定遠陰與思好通。
entries.en: When Gao Sihao rose in rebellion, Mutipo had the Linhuai principality's director accuse Dingyuan of secret dealings with Sihao.
entries.literal: When Gao Sihao rebelled, Mutipo had the director of the Linhuai principality accuse Dingyuan of secretly communicating with Sihao.

entries.zh: 後主令開府段暢率三千騎掩之，令侍御史趙秀通至州，以贓貨事劾定遠。
entries.en: The Later Lord ordered Duan Chang, who held opening-establishment honors, to lead three thousand cavalry in a surprise raid, and sent attendant censor Zhao Xiutong to the province to impeach Dingyuan for embezzlement.
entries.literal: The Later Lord ordered Duan Chang, holder of opening-establishment honors, to lead three thousand cavalry in a surprise strike, and sent Attendant Censor Zhao Xiutong to the province to impeach Dingyuan on charges of embezzlement.

entries.zh: 定遠疑有變，遂縊而死。
entries.en: Dingyuan sensed a trap and hanged himself.
entries.literal: Dingyuan suspected a trap and hanged himself.

entries.zh: 昭兄子叡。
entries.en: Rui was Zhao's nephew, the son of his elder brother.
entries.literal: Zhao's elder brother's son was Rui.

entries.zh: 叡字佛仁，父拔，魏南部尚書。
entries.en: Rui, courtesy name Furen, was the son of Ba, who had served in Wei as Minister of the Southern Section.
entries.literal: Rui, courtesy name Furen, was the son of Ba, who was Wei Minister of the Southern Section.

entries.zh: 叡幼孤，被叔父昭所養。
entries.en: Rui was orphaned young and raised by his uncle Zhao.
entries.literal: Rui was orphaned when young and was raised by his uncle Zhao.

entries.zh: 為神武帳內都督，封掖縣子，累遷光州刺史。
entries.en: He served as commandant in Gao Huan's personal retinue, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Ye County, and rose in succession to Inspector of Guang Province.
entries.literal: He served as Shenwu's tent commandant, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Ye County, and rose successively to Inspector of Guang Province.

entries.zh: 在任貪縱，深為文襄所責。
entries.en: In office he was greedy and self-indulgent, and Gao Cheng sharply reprimanded him.
entries.literal: In office he was greedy and unrestrained, and was sharply reproved by Wenxiang.

entries.zh: 後改封九門縣公。
entries.en: His title was later changed to Duke of Jiumen County.
entries.literal: Later his title was changed to Duke of Jiumen County.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，得除領軍將軍，別封安定侯。
entries.en: When Qi received the abdication, he was appointed General of the Guard Army and received a separate enfeoffment as Marquis of Anding.
entries.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was appointed General of the Guard Army and separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Anding.

entries.zh: 叡無他器干，以外戚貴幸，縱情財色。
entries.en: Rui had no special ability, but as an imperial in-law he enjoyed rank and favor, and gave himself over to wealth and women.
entries.literal: Rui had no other capacity; because he was a maternal relative he was honored and favored, and he gave himself over to wealth and women.

entries.zh: 為瀛州刺史，聚斂無厭。
entries.en: As Inspector of Ying Province, he extorted endlessly.
entries.literal: As Inspector of Ying Province, he amassed exactions without satiety.

entries.zh: 皇建初，封東安王。
entries.en: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was made Prince of Dong'an.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dong'an.

entries.zh: 大寧元年，進位司空。
entries.en: In the first year of Daning, he was promoted to Minister of Works.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daning, his rank was advanced to Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 平高歸彥於冀州，還拜司徒。
entries.en: After suppressing Gao Guiyan in Ji Province, he returned and was appointed Minister over the Masses.
entries.literal: He pacified Gao Guiyan in Ji Province, and on returning was appointed Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 河清三年，濫殺人，為尚書左丞宋仲羨彈奏，經赦乃免。
entries.en: In the third year of Heqing, he killed people indiscriminately and was impeached by Song Zhongxian, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; he escaped punishment only through an amnesty.
entries.literal: In the third year of Heqing, he killed people indiscriminately and was impeached by Song Zhongxian, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; only after an amnesty was he spared.

entries.zh: 尋為太尉，以軍功進大司馬。
entries.en: Soon he was made Grand Commandant and, for military merit, promoted to Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: Soon he became Grand Commandant, and for military merit advanced to Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 武成至河陽，仍遣總偏師赴懸瓠。
entries.en: When Emperor Wucheng reached Heyang, Rui was sent to command a detached force to Xuanhu.
entries.literal: When Wucheng reached Heyang, he was then sent to command a detached force to Xuanhu.

entries.zh: 叡在豫境留停百餘日，專行非法，詔免官，以王還第。
entries.en: Rui stayed in Yu territory for more than a hundred days, acting lawlessly. An edict removed him from office, and he returned home retaining his princely title.
entries.literal: Rui lingered in Yu territory for more than a hundred days and acted entirely unlawfully; an edict removed him from office, and he returned to his residence with his princely rank.

entries.zh: 尋除太尉，薨。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed Grand Commandant, then died.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Commandant and died.

entries.zh: 贈大司馬。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 子子彥嗣，位開府儀同三司。
entries.en: His son Ziyan succeeded him and rose to Opening Office with the same honors as the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: His son Ziyan succeeded, reaching the rank of Opening Office with the same honors as the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 厙狄干，善無人也。
entries.en: Kudie Gan was from Shanwu.
entries.literal: Kudie Gan was a man of Shanwu.

entries.zh: 曾祖越豆眷，魏道武時以功割善無之西臘汙山地方百里以處之，後率部北遷，因家朔方。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Yuedoujuan was granted a hundred li of land at Xilawu Mountain west of Shanwu for his service under Emperor Daowu of Wei. He later led his people north and settled in Shuofang.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Yuedoujuan, in the time of Emperor Daowu of Wei, was allotted for his merit a hundred li of land at Xilawu Mountain west of Shanwu on which to settle; later he led his tribe northward and thus made his home in Shuofang.

entries.zh: 干梗直少言，有武藝。
entries.en: Gan was blunt and upright, sparing of speech, and skilled in arms.
entries.literal: Gan was blunt and upright, spoke little, and possessed martial skill.

entries.zh: 魏正光初，除掃逆黨，授將軍，宿衛於內。
entries.en: At the beginning of Zhengguang in Wei, he was appointed to sweep away rebel bands, made a general, and assigned to the inner palace guard.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhengguang in Wei, he was appointed to sweep away rebel bands, was granted the title of general, and served on guard inside the palace.

entries.zh: 以家在寒鄉，不宜毒暑，冬得入京師，夏歸鄉里。
entries.en: Because his home was in a cold region and he could not bear severe summer heat, he was allowed to spend winters in the capital and return home in summer.
entries.literal: Because his home was in a cold region and he was not suited to fierce summer heat, in winter he was permitted to enter the capital and in summer to return to his native place.

entries.zh: 孝昌元年，北邊擾亂，奔雲中，為刺史費穆送於尒朱榮。
entries.en: In the first year of Xiaochang, when the northern frontier fell into disorder, he fled to Yunzhong and was sent by Inspector Fei Mu to Erzhu Rong.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang, when the northern frontier fell into disorder, he fled to Yunzhong and was sent by Inspector Fei Mu to Erzhu Rong.

entries.zh: 以軍主隨榮入洛。
entries.en: As an army commander, he followed Erzhu Rong into Luoyang.
entries.literal: As an army commander, he followed Rong into Luoyang.

entries.zh: 後從神武起兵，破四胡於韓陵，封廣平縣公，尋進郡公。
entries.en: Later he followed Gao Huan in raising arms, routed the Four Hus at Hanling, was enfeoffed duke of Guangping County, and soon advanced to commandery duke.
entries.literal: Later he followed Shenwu in raising troops, defeated the Four Hus at Hanling, was enfeoffed Duke of Guangping County, and soon advanced to commandery duke.

entries.zh: 河陰之役，諸將大捷，唯干兵退。
entries.en: At Heyin the other generals won great victories — only Gan's troops fell back.
entries.literal: At the Battle of Heyin the other generals won great victories — only Gan's troops retreated.

entries.zh: 神武以其舊功，竟不責黜。
entries.en: Gao Huan, weighing his old service, did not punish or dismiss him.
entries.literal: Shenwu, considering his past merit, did not punish or dismiss him.

entries.zh: 尋轉太保、太傅。
entries.en: Soon he was made grand preceptor and grand tutor.
entries.literal: Soon he was made Grand Preceptor and Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 及高仲密以武牢叛，神武討之，以干為大都督前驅。
entries.en: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled at Wulao, Gao Huan marched against him and made Gan grand commander of the vanguard.
entries.literal: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled at Wulao, Shenwu marched against him and made Gan grand commander as vanguard.

entries.zh: 干上道不過家，見侯景不遑食，景使騎追饋之。
entries.en: Gan took the road without stopping at home. He met Hou Jing and had no time to eat — Jing sent riders racing after him with provisions.
entries.literal: Gan set out without stopping at home; he met Hou Jing and had no time to eat — Jing sent horsemen racing after him with food.

entries.zh: 時文帝自將兵至洛陽，軍容甚盛。
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Western Wei had personally led troops to Luoyang — his army's bearing was formidable.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Wen personally led troops to Luoyang; his army's appearance was very imposing.

entries.zh: 諸將未欲南度，干決計濟河。
entries.en: The generals shrank from crossing south; Gan resolved to ford the river.
entries.literal: The generals did not wish to cross south; Gan resolved to ford the river.

entries.zh: 神武大兵繼至，遂大破之。
entries.en: Gao Huan's main army came up behind, and they routed the enemy.
entries.literal: Shenwu's main force followed, and they routed the enemy.

entries.zh: 還為定州刺史。
entries.en: He returned and was made governor of Ding Province.
entries.literal: He returned and was made Governor of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 不閑吏事，事多擾煩，然清約自居，不為吏人所患。
entries.en: He was no hand at administration, and his office was often in disorder — yet he lived plainly and frugally, and neither clerks nor commoners resented him.
entries.literal: Unskilled in administration, his affairs were often chaotic — yet he kept himself frugal and simple, and the clerks and people did not resent him.

entries.zh: 遷太師。
entries.en: He was made grand preceptor.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 天保初，以天平元勳佐命，封章武郡王，轉太宰。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianbao, for his merit among the Tianping founding ministers, he was enfeoffed Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and made grand minister.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, for his merit as one of the founding ministers of the Tianping era, he was enfeoffed Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and made Grand Minister.

entries.zh: 干尚神武妹樂陵長公主，以親地見待。
entries.en: Gan married Gao Huan's sister, Princess of Leling — as kin by marriage, he was treated with singular favor.
entries.literal: Gan married Shenwu's sister, Princess of Leling — as kin by marriage, he was treated with special favor.

entries.zh: 自預勤王，常總大衆，威望之重，為諸將所伏，而最為嚴猛。
entries.en: From the first campaigns to rescue the throne he often commanded the main armies. The weight of his prestige bowed the other generals — and of them all he was the sternest, the fiercest.
entries.literal: From his first service in the rescue of the throne he often commanded the main armies; the weight of his prestige made the other generals defer to him, and he was the sternest and fiercest of them all.

entries.zh: 會詣京師，魏譙王元孝友於公門言戲過度，諸公無能面折者，干正色責之，孝友大慚，時人稱之。
entries.en: Once at the capital, Yuan Xiaoyou, Prince Qiao of Wei, carried on with excessive ribaldry at court — and none of the nobles dared rebuke him to his face. Gan sternly reproached him. Xiaoyou was deeply shamed; men praised Gan for it.
entries.literal: Once when he visited the capital, Yuan Xiaoyou, Prince Qiao of Wei, indulged in excessive ribaldry at court — none of the nobles could rebuke him to his face. Gan sternly reproached him; Xiaoyou was deeply ashamed, and contemporaries praised Gan.

entries.zh: 薨，贈假黃鉞，太宰，給轀輬車，諡曰景烈。
entries.en: He died. Posthumously he was granted the acting yellow battle-axe and grand minister rank, given an imperial carriage — posthumous name Jinglie.
entries.literal: He died. Posthumously he was granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe and Grand Minister rank, given an imperial carriage; posthumous name Jinglie.

entries.zh: 干不知書，署名為「干」字，逆上畫之，時人謂之穿錐。
entries.en: Gan could not read. To sign his name he drew the character for Gan upside down — people called it "piercing the awl."
entries.literal: Gan could not read; to sign his name he drew the character gan upside down — people called it "piercing the awl."

entries.zh: 又有武將王周者，署名先為「吉」而後成其外，二人至子孫始並知書。
entries.en: There was also the warrior Wang Zhou, who signed by writing the inner strokes of "ji" first and only then completing the character — not until their descendants did either family learn to read.
entries.literal: There was also the warrior Wang Zhou, who signed by writing the inner part ji first and then completing the outer strokes — not until their descendants did either family learn to read.

entries.zh: 干，皇建初配享神武廟庭。
entries.en: At the beginning of Huangjian, Gan was granted posthumous sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple hall.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, Gan was granted posthumous sacrifice in Shenwu's temple hall.

entries.zh: 子敬伏，位儀同三司，卒。
entries.en: His son Jingfu rose to rank equal to the three excellencies and died.
entries.literal: His son Jingfu rose to rank equal to the three excellencies and died.

entries.zh: 子士文嗣。
entries.en: His son Shiwen succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Shiwen succeeded him.

entries.zh: 韓軌，字百年，太安狄那人也。
entries.en: Han Gui, courtesy name Bainian, was a native of Dina in Tai'an.
entries.literal: Han Gui, courtesy name Bainian, was a native of Dina in Tai'an.

entries.zh: 少有志操，性深沈，喜怒不形於色。
entries.en: From youth he had resolution and integrity — deep and reserved, he never showed pleasure or anger on his face.
entries.literal: From youth he had resolution and integrity; deep and reserved, he never showed pleasure or anger on his face.

entries.zh: 神武鎮晉州，引為鎮城都督。
entries.en: When Gao Huan held Jin Province, he recruited Gui as garrison commander of the walled city.
entries.literal: When Shenwu held Jin Province, he recruited Gui as garrison commander of the walled city.

entries.zh: 及起兵於信都，軌贊成大策。
entries.en: When arms were raised at Xindu, Gui supported the great plan.
entries.literal: When troops were raised at Xindu, Gui supported the great plan.

entries.zh: 從破尒朱兆於廣阿，又從韓陵陣，封平昌縣侯。
entries.en: He followed in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and fought at Hanling — and was enfeoffed marquis of Pingchang County.
entries.literal: He followed in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and fought at Hanling; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Pingchang County.

entries.zh: 仍督中軍，從破尒朱兆於赤谼嶺。
entries.en: He continued to command the center army and followed in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Chihong Ridge.
entries.literal: He continued to command the center army and followed in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Chihong Ridge.

entries.zh: 再遷泰州刺史。
entries.en: He was made governor of Tai Province.
entries.literal: He was twice transferred and made Governor of Tai Province.

entries.zh: 甚得邊和。
entries.en: He won deep peace on the frontier.
entries.literal: He won great peace on the frontier.

entries.zh: 神武巡泰州，欲以軌還，仍賜城人戶別絹布兩匹。
entries.en: When Gao Huan inspected Tai Province and wished to transfer Gui away, he granted each household in the city two bolts of silk and cloth.
entries.literal: When Shenwu inspected Tai Province and wished to transfer Gui away, he granted each household in the city two bolts of silk and cloth apiece.

entries.zh: 州人田昭等七千戶皆辭不受，唯乞留軌。
entries.en: Seven thousand households led by Tian Zhao declined the gift and begged only that Gui remain.
entries.literal: Seven thousand households led by Tian Zhao all declined the gift and begged only that Gui remain.

entries.zh: 神武嘉嘆，乃留焉。
entries.en: Gao Huan praised and sighed with admiration — and kept him.
entries.literal: Shenwu praised and sighed with admiration — and kept him.

entries.zh: 頻以軍功，進封安德郡公。
entries.en: Again and again for military merit he was advanced to duke of Ande Commandery.
entries.literal: Repeatedly for military merit he was advanced to Duke of Ande Commandery.

entries.zh: 遷瀛州刺史，在州聚斂，為御史糾劾，削除官爵。
entries.en: Made governor of Ying Province, he amassed wealth in office — the censorate impeached him and stripped his office and rank.
entries.literal: Made Governor of Ying Province, he accumulated wealth in the province; the censorate impeached him and stripped his office and rank.

entries.zh: 未幾，復其安德郡公。
entries.en: Before long his ducal title of Ande was restored.
entries.literal: Before long his ducal title of Ande was restored.

entries.zh: 歷位中書令、司徒。
entries.en: He rose through director of the secretariat and minister of education.
entries.literal: He rose through the posts of Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，封安德郡王。
entries.en: When Qi received the abdication, he was enfeoffed Prince of Ande Commandery.
entries.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was enfeoffed Prince of Ande Commandery.

entries.zh: 軌妹為神武所納，生上黨王渙，復以勳庸，歷登臺鉉。
entries.en: Gao Huan took Gui's younger sister as consort; she bore Prince Huan of Shangdang. Again through merit Gui rose to the highest offices of state.
entries.literal: Shenwu took Gui's younger sister as consort; she bore Prince Huan of Shangdang. Again through merit Gui rose to the highest offices of state.

entries.zh: 常以謙恭自處，不以富貴驕人。
entries.en: He always conducted himself with humility — never lording his wealth and rank over others.
entries.literal: He always conducted himself with humility and deference, never lording his wealth and rank over others.

entries.zh: 後拜大司馬，從文宣征蠕蠕，在軍暴疾薨。
entries.en: Later he was made grand marshal. Campaigning against the Rouran with Wenxuan, he died suddenly of illness in camp.
entries.literal: Later he was made Grand Marshal; campaigning against the Rouran with Wenxuan, he died suddenly of illness in camp.

entries.zh: 贈假黃鉞，太宰、太師，諡曰肅武。
entries.en: Posthumously he was granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand minister and grand preceptor — posthumous name Suwu.
entries.literal: Posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Minister and Grand Preceptor; posthumous name Suwu.

entries.zh: 皇建初，配饗文襄廟庭。
entries.en: At the beginning of Huangjian he was granted posthumous sacrifice in Wenxiang's temple hall.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he was granted posthumous sacrifice in Wenxiang's temple hall.

entries.zh: 潘樂，字相貴，廣寧石門人也。
entries.en: Pan Le, courtesy name Xianggui, was a native of Shimen in Guangning.
entries.literal: Pan Le, courtesy name Xianggui, was a native of Shimen in Guangning.

entries.zh: 本廣宗大族，魏世分鎮北邊，因家焉。
entries.en: Originally a great clan of Guangzong — in Wei times they were posted to guard the northern frontier and settled there.
entries.literal: Originally a great clan of Guangzong, in Wei times they were posted to guard the northern frontier and settled there.

entries.zh: 父永，有技藝，襲爵廣宗男。
entries.en: His father Yong had technical skills and inherited the barony of Guangzong.
entries.literal: His father Yong had technical skills and inherited the barony of Guangzong.

entries.zh: 樂初生，有一雀止其母左肩，占者咸言富貴之徵，因名相貴，後始為字。
entries.en: When Le was born a sparrow alighted on his mother's left shoulder. Diviners all said it was a sign of wealth and rank — hence the name Xianggui, later adopted as his courtesy name.
entries.literal: When Le was born a sparrow alighted on his mother's left shoulder; diviners all said it was a sign of wealth and rank — hence the name Xianggui, later adopted as his courtesy name.

entries.zh: 及長，寬厚有膽略。
entries.en: When he grew up he was generous and broad-minded, possessed of courage and strategy.
entries.literal: When he grew up he was generous, broad-minded, and possessed of courage and strategy.

entries.zh: 初歸葛榮，授京兆王，時年十九。
entries.en: At first he joined Ge Rong and was made Prince of Jingzhao — he was nineteen.
entries.literal: At first he joined Ge Rong and was made Prince of Jingzhao — he was nineteen.

entries.zh: 榮敗，隨尒朱榮，為別將討元顥，以功封敷城縣男。
entries.en: When Rong was defeated he followed Erzhu Rong, served as a separate commander against Yuan Hao, and for merit was enfeoffed baron of Fucheng County.
entries.literal: When Rong was defeated he followed Erzhu Rong, served as a separate commander against Yuan Hao, and for merit was enfeoffed Baron of Fucheng County.

entries.zh: 齊神武出牧晉州，引樂為鎮城都將。
entries.en: When Gao Huan went out to hold Jin Province, he recruited Le as garrison general of the walled city.
entries.literal: When Shenwu went out to hold Jin Province, he recruited Le as garrison general of the walled city.

entries.zh: 從破尒朱兆於廣阿，進爵廣宗縣伯。
entries.en: He followed in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and was advanced to earl of Guangzong County.
entries.literal: He followed in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and was advanced to Earl of Guangzong County.

entries.zh: 累以軍功拜東雍州刺史。
entries.en: Again and again for military merit he was made governor of Eastern Yong Province.
entries.literal: Repeatedly for military merit he was made Governor of Eastern Yong Province.

entries.zh: 神武嘗議欲廢州，樂以東雍地帶山河，境連胡、蜀，形勝之會，不可棄也，遂如故。
entries.en: Gao Huan once debated abolishing the province. Le argued that Eastern Yong lay between mountains and rivers, bordered Hu and Shu, and occupied a strategically vital junction — it could not be abandoned. The province remained as before.
entries.literal: Shenwu once debated abolishing the province; Le argued that Eastern Yong lay between mountains and rivers, bordered Hu and Shu territories, and occupied a strategically vital junction — it could not be abandoned. The province remained as before.

entries.zh: 後破周師於河陰，議欲追之，令追者在西，不願者東，唯樂與劉豐居西。
entries.en: Later, after defeating Zhou troops at Heyin, there was debate over pursuit — those willing to pursue stood west, the unwilling east. Only Le and Liu Feng stood on the west.
entries.literal: Later, after defeating Zhou troops at Heyin, there was debate over pursuit — those willing to pursue stood west, the unwilling east. Only Le and Liu Feng stood on the west.

entries.zh: 神武善之，以衆議不同而止。
entries.en: Gao Huan approved — but because the council could not agree, he dropped the pursuit.
entries.literal: Shenwu approved of it; because the multitude's counsels differed, he ceased.

entries.zh: 改封金門郡公。
entries.en: He was re-enfeoffed as duke of Jinmen Commandery.
entries.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Jinmen Commandery.

entries.zh: 文宣嗣事，鎮河陽，破西將楊檦等。
entries.en: When Gao Yang succeeded to power, Le held the Heyang garrison and routed Western general Yang Piao and others.
entries.literal: When Wenxuan succeeded to affairs, Le garrisoned Heyang and defeated Western generals Yang Piao and others.

entries.zh: 時帝以懷州刺史平鑒等所築城深入敵境，欲棄之，樂以軹關要害，必須防固，乃更修理，增置兵將，而還鎮河陽，拜司空。
entries.en: The emperor wished to abandon fortifications built by Huai Province governor Ping Jian and others, because they lay deep in enemy territory. Pan Le argued that Zhiguan Pass was a vital strongpoint and had to be held; he repaired the works, posted more troops and officers, returned to garrison Heyang, and was appointed minister of works.
entries.literal: At the time the emperor, because the walled fort built by Huai Province Governor Ping Jian and others lay deep in enemy territory, wished to abandon it; Le, holding that Zhiguan Pass was a strategic strongpoint that must be defended, thereupon repaired it further, added troops and commanders, returned to garrison Heyang, and was appointed Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，樂進璽綬。
entries.en: When Qi received the abdication, Pan Le presented the imperial seal and cord.
entries.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, Le presented the seal and cord.

entries.zh: 進封河東郡王，遷司徒。
entries.en: He was advanced to Prince of Hedong Commandery and transferred to minister over the masses.
entries.literal: Advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Hedong Commandery; transferred to Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 周文東至崤、陜，遣其行臺侯莫陳崇自齊子嶺趣軹關，儀同楊檦從鼓鐘道出建州，陷孤公戍。
entries.en: Yuwen Tai marched east to Xiao and Shan, sending field headquarters Houmochen Chong from Qizi Ridge against Zhiguan Pass while yitong Yang Piao by the Guchong road into Jian Province captured the Gugong garrison.
entries.literal: Zhou Wen marched east to Xiao and Shan, dispatching his field headquarters Houmochen Chong from Qizi Ridge toward Zhiguan, while Yitong Yang Piao by the Guchong road out toward Jian Province captured Gugong garrison.

entries.zh: 詔樂總大衆禦之。
entries.en: An edict ordered Pan Le to take overall command and meet the invasion.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Le to command the great host to resist.

entries.zh: 樂晝夜兼行，至長子，遣儀同韓永興從建州西趣崇，崇遂遁。
entries.en: Pan Le forced the march day and night as far as Changzi, sent yitong Han Yongxing west from Jian Province against Houmochen Chong — and Chong fled.
entries.literal: Le marched day and night without pause; reaching Changzi, he dispatched Yitong Han Yongxing west from Jian Province toward Chong, and Chong thereupon fled.

entries.zh: 又為南道大都督，討侯景。
entries.en: He was again made grand governor of the south route and sent against Hou Jing.
entries.literal: Again made Grand Governor of the Southern Route, to campaign against Hou Jing.

entries.zh: 樂發石鱉，南度百餘里，至梁涇州。
entries.en: Pan Le marched out from Shibie, drove south more than a hundred li, and reached Jing Province in Liang territory.
entries.literal: Le set out from Shibie, marched south over a hundred li, and reached Liang's Jing Province.

entries.zh: 涇州舊在石梁，侯景改為懷州，樂獲其地，仍立涇州，又克安州。
entries.en: Jing Province had stood at Shiliang until Hou Jing renamed it Huai Province. Pan Le recovered the ground, restored Jing Province, and also took An Province.
entries.literal: Jing Province had formerly been at Shiliang; Hou Jing had changed it to Huai Province. Le recovered the territory, re-established Jing Province, and also captured An Province.

entries.zh: 除瀛州刺史，仍略淮、漢。
entries.en: He was appointed governor of Ying Province and continued to carry the war into the Huai and Han country.
entries.literal: Appointed Governor of Ying Province; still raided Huai and Han.

entries.zh: 天保六年，薨於懸瓠。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Tianbao he died at Xuanhu.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao, he died at Xuanhu.

entries.zh: 贈假黃鉞，太師、大司馬、尚書令。
entries.en: Posthumously he was granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand preceptor, grand marshal, and director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Posthumously granted Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Preceptor, Grand Marshal, and Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 竇泰 尉景 婁昭 兄子叡 厙狄干 子士文 韓軌 潘樂
entries.en: Dou Tai; Wei Jing; Lou Zhao; nephew Rui; Kudie Gan; son Shiwen; Han Gui; Pan Le
entries.literal: Dou Tai; Wei Jing; Lou Zhao; nephew Rui; Kudie Gan; son Shiwen; Han Gui; Pan Le

entries.zh: 段榮，字子茂，姑臧武威人也。
entries.en: Duan Rong, styled Zimao, was a native of Guzang in Wuwei.
entries.literal: Duan Rong, styled Zimao, was a native of Guzang in Wuwei.

entries.zh: 祖信，仕沮渠氏，後入魏，以豪族徙北邊，仍家於五原郡。
entries.en: His grandfather Xin served the Juqu clan; later he entered Wei and, as a prominent clan, was relocated to the northern frontier, settling in Wuyuan Commandery.
entries.literal: His grandfather Xin served the Juqu clan; later he entered Wei and, as a prominent clan, was relocated to the northern frontier, settling in Wuyuan Commandery.

entries.zh: 父連，安北府司馬。
entries.en: His father Lian served as military aide of the Anbei headquarters.
entries.literal: His father Lian served as military aide of the Anbei headquarters.

entries.zh: 榮少好曆術，專意星象。
entries.en: From youth Duan Rong loved calendrical arts and devoted himself to stars and portents.
entries.literal: From youth Rong loved calendrical arts and devoted himself to stars and portents.

entries.zh: 正光初，語人曰：「《易》云 『觀於天文以察時變』，又曰『天垂象，見吉兇』，今觀玄象，察人事，不及十年，當有亂矣。」
entries.en: At the beginning of Zhenguang, he told people, "The Book of Changes says, 'Observe the heavens to discern changes in the times,' and also says, 'Heaven displays signs, revealing fortune and calamity.' Now observing the dark heavens and examining human affairs, within ten years there will be turmoil."
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguang, he told people, "The Book of Changes says, 'Observe the heavens to discern changes in the times,' and also says, 'Heaven displays signs, revealing fortune and calamity.' Now observing the dark heavens and examining human affairs, within ten years there will be turmoil."

entries.zh: 或問曰：「起於何處，當可避乎？」
entries.en: Someone asked, "Where will it begin — can one avoid it?"
entries.literal: Someone asked, "Where will it begin — can one avoid it?"

entries.zh: 榮曰：「構亂之源，此地為始，恐天下因此橫流，無所避也。」
entries.en: Duan Rong said, "The source of strife will begin here; I fear the realm will be swept along in the torrent — there is nowhere to escape."
entries.literal: Rong said, "The source of strife will begin here; I fear the realm will be swept along in the torrent — there is nowhere to escape."

entries.zh: 未幾，果如言。
entries.en: Before long, it happened just as he said.
entries.literal: Before long, it happened just as he said.

entries.zh: 榮遇亂，與鄉舊攜妻子，南趣平城。
entries.en: When turmoil came, Duan Rong, with his fellow townsmen, took wife and children and hurried south toward Pingcheng.
entries.literal: When turmoil came, Rong, with his fellow townsmen, took wife and children and hurried south toward Pingcheng.

entries.zh: 屬杜洛周為亂，榮與高祖謀誅之，事不捷，共奔尒朱榮。
entries.en: Just then Du Luozhou rebelled; Duan Rong and Gao Huan plotted to kill him, but the matter failed, and together they fled to Erzhu Rong.
entries.literal: Just then Du Luozhou rebelled; Rong and the Grand Ancestor plotted to kill him, but the matter failed, and together they fled to Erzhu Rong.

entries.zh: 後高祖建義山東，榮贊成大策。
entries.en: Later, when Gao Huan raised the righteous banner in Shandong, Duan Rong helped bring the great plan to fruition.
entries.literal: Later, when the Grand Ancestor raised the righteous banner in Shandong, Rong helped bring the great plan to fruition.

entries.zh: 為行臺右丞，西北道慰喻大使，巡方曉喻，所在下之。
entries.en: He served as right deputy of the mobile office, ambassador to pacify and instruct the northwest circuit, touring the regions to enlighten and persuade; wherever he went, people submitted.
entries.literal: He served as right deputy of the mobile office, ambassador to pacify and instruct the northwest circuit, touring the regions to enlighten and persuade; wherever he went, people submitted.

entries.zh: 高祖南討鄴，留榮鎮信都，仍授鎮北將軍，定州刺史。
entries.en: When Gao Huan marched south to attack Ye, he left Duan Rong to garrison Xindu and concurrently appointed him general who pacifies the north and governor of Ding Province.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor marched south to attack Ye, he left Rong to garrison Xindu and concurrently appointed him General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 時攻鄴未克，所須軍資，榮轉輸無闕。
entries.en: At that time the attack on Ye had not yet succeeded; whatever military supplies were needed, Duan Rong transported them without shortfall.
entries.literal: At that time the attack on Ye had not yet succeeded; whatever military supplies were needed, Rong transported them without shortfall.

entries.zh: 高祖入洛，論功封姑臧縣侯，邑八百戶。
entries.en: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, for merit Duan Rong was enfeoffed marquis of Guzang County with a fief of eight hundred households.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor entered Luoyang, for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Guzang County with a fief of eight hundred households.

entries.zh: 轉授瀛州刺史。
entries.en: He was transferred to governor of Ying Province.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Ying Province.

entries.zh: 榮妻，皇后姊也，榮恐高祖招私親之議，固推諸將，竟不之州。
entries.en: Duan Rong's wife was the empress's elder sister; fearing Gao Huan would draw criticism for favoring private kin, Duan Rong firmly yielded to other generals and in the end never went to the province.
entries.literal: Rong's wife was the empress's elder sister; fearing the Grand Ancestor would draw criticism for favoring private kin, Rong firmly yielded to other generals and in the end never went to the province.

entries.zh: 尋行相州事，後為濟州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he acted as administrator of Xiang Province; later he became governor of Ji Province.
entries.literal: Soon he acted as administrator of Xiang Province; later he became Governor of Ji Province.

entries.zh: 天平三年，轉行泰州事。
entries.en: In the third year of Tianping, he was transferred to act as administrator of Tai Province.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianping, he was transferred to act as administrator of Tai Province.

entries.zh: 榮性溫和，所歷皆推仁恕，民吏愛之。
entries.en: Duan Rong was mild by nature; everywhere he served he practiced benevolence and forbearance, and officials and common people alike loved him.
entries.literal: Rong was mild by nature; everywhere he served he practiced benevolence and forbearance, and officials and common people alike loved him.

entries.zh: 初，高祖將圖關右，與榮密謀，榮盛稱未可。
entries.en: At first, when Gao Huan planned to take the Guanxi region, he secretly consulted Duan Rong, who strongly argued it was not yet feasible.
entries.literal: At first, when the Grand Ancestor planned to take the Guanxi region, he secretly consulted Rong, who strongly argued it was not yet feasible.

entries.zh: 及渭曲失利，高祖悔之，曰：「吾不用段榮之言，以至於此。」
entries.en: When they suffered defeat at Weiqu, Gao Huan regretted it and said, "I did not heed Duan Rong's counsel, and so came to this."
entries.literal: When they suffered defeat at Weiqu, the Grand Ancestor regretted it and said, "I did not heed Duan Rong's counsel, and so came to this."

entries.zh: 四年，除山東大行臺、大都督，甚得物情。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was appointed grand commissioner of Shandong and grand commander; he won the hearts of all greatly.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed grand commissioner of Shandong and grand commander; he won the hearts of all greatly.

entries.zh: 元象元年，授儀同三司。
entries.en: In the first year of Yuanxiang, he was granted Equal to the Three Dukes.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang, he was granted Equal to the Three Dukes.

entries.zh: 二年五月卒，年六十二。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the second year he died, aged sixty-two.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the second year he died, aged sixty-two.

entries.zh: 贈使持節、定冀滄瀛四州諸軍事、定州刺史、太尉、尚書左僕射，諡曰昭景。
entries.en: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the four provinces of Ding, Ji, Cang, and Ying, governor of Ding Province, grand commandant, and left vice director of the masters of writing; his posthumous title was Zhaojing.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the four provinces of Ding, Ji, Cang, and Ying, Governor of Ding Province, Grand Commandant, and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; his posthumous title was Zhaojing.

entries.zh: 皇建初，配饗高祖廟庭。
entries.en: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was given associated sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple court.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was given associated sacrifice in the Grand Ancestor's temple court.

entries.zh: 二年，重贈大司馬、尚書令、武威王。
entries.en: In the second year he was again posthumously granted grand marshal, director of the masters of writing, and prince of Wuwei.
entries.literal: In the second year he was again posthumously granted Grand Marshal, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Wuwei.

entries.zh: 長子韶嗣。
entries.en: His eldest son Shao succeeded.
entries.literal: His eldest son Shao succeeded.

entries.zh: 韶，字孝先，小名鐵伐。
entries.en: Shao, styled Xiaoxian, had the childhood name Tiefa.
entries.literal: Shao, styled Xiaoxian, had the childhood name Tiefa.

entries.zh: 少工騎射，有將領才略。
entries.en: From youth he was skilled at mounted archery and possessed the talent and strategy of a commander.
entries.literal: From youth he was skilled at mounted archery and possessed the talent and strategy of a commander.

entries.zh: 高祖以武明皇后姊子，盡器愛之，常置左右，以為心腹。
entries.en: Gao Huan, because Shao was the nephew of Empress Lou Wuming, fully treasured and loved him, kept him constantly at his side, and regarded him as a trusted confidant.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor, because he was the nephew of Empress Lou Wuming, fully treasured and loved him, kept him constantly at his side, and regarded him as a trusted confidant.

entries.zh: 建義初，領親信都督。
entries.en: At the beginning of the righteous enterprise, he commanded trusted bodyguards.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the righteous enterprise, he commanded trusted bodyguards.

entries.zh: 中興元年，從高祖拒尒朱兆，戰於廣阿。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhongxing, he followed Gao Huan in resisting Erzhu Zhao; they fought at Guang'a.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing, he followed the Grand Ancestor in resisting Erzhu Zhao; they fought at Guang'a.

entries.zh: 高祖謂韶曰：「彼衆我寡，其若之何？」
entries.en: Gao Huan said to Shao, "They are many and we are few — what is to be done?"
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor said to Shao, "They are many and we are few — what is to be done?"

entries.zh: 韶曰：「所謂衆者，得衆人之死；
entries.en: Shao said, "What is called 'many' is winning the people's willingness to die;
entries.literal: Shao said, "What is called 'many' is winning the people's willingness to die;

entries.zh: 強者，得天下之心。
entries.en: what is called 'strong' is winning the hearts of the realm.
entries.literal: what is called 'strong' is winning the hearts of the realm.

entries.zh: 尒朱狂狡，行路所見，裂冠毀冕，拔本塞源，邙山之會，搢紳何罪，兼殺主立君，不脫旬朔，天下思亂，十室而九。
entries.en: Erzhu is reckless and cunning — what everyone on the road sees: they tear off caps and destroy crowns, uproot foundations and block the source. At the assembly at Mount Mang, what crime did the gentry commit? Yet they also killed their lord and set up another — within no more than ten days and a month the realm yearns for disorder; nine of ten households.
entries.literal: Erzhu is reckless and cunning — what everyone on the road sees: they tear off caps and destroy crowns, uproot foundations and block the source. At the assembly at Mount Mang, what crime did the gentry commit? Yet they also killed their lord and set up another — within no more than ten days and a month the realm yearns for disorder; nine of ten households.

entries.zh: 王躬昭德義，除君側之惡，何往而不克哉！」
entries.en: Your Highness personally displays virtue and righteousness, removing evil at the ruler's side — where could you go without prevailing!"
entries.literal: Your Highness personally displays virtue and righteousness, removing evil at the ruler's side — where could you go without prevailing!"

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「吾雖以順討逆，奉辭伐罪，但弱小在強大之間，恐無天命，卿不聞之也？」
entries.en: Gao Huan said, "Although I take righteousness against rebellion and go forth with a mandate to punish crime, we are weak amid the strong — I fear we lack Heaven's mandate. Have you not heard of this?"
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor said, "Although I take righteousness against rebellion and go forth with a mandate to punish crime, we are weak amid the strong — I fear we lack Heaven's mandate. Have you not heard of this?"

entries.zh: 答曰：「韶聞小能敵大，小道大淫，皇天無親，唯德是輔，尒朱外賊天下，內失善人，知者不為謀，勇者不為鬭，不肖失職，賢者取之，復何疑也。」
entries.en: He answered, "Shao has heard that the small can overcome the large, and the way that is small may yet overcome one that is great and excessive; August Heaven is not partial — only virtue receives its aid. Erzhu outwardly harms the realm and inwardly loses good men; the wise will not plan for him, the brave will not fight for him. The unworthy lose their offices; the worthy take them — what doubt remains?"
entries.literal: He answered, "Shao has heard that the small can overcome the large, and the way that is small may yet overcome one that is great and excessive; August Heaven is not partial — only virtue receives its aid. Erzhu outwardly harms the realm and inwardly loses good men; the wise will not plan for him, the brave will not fight for him. The unworthy lose their offices; the worthy take them — what doubt remains?"

entries.zh: 遂與兆戰，兆軍潰。
entries.en: They then fought Zhao; Zhao's army collapsed.
entries.literal: They then fought Zhao; Zhao's army collapsed.

entries.zh: 攻劉誕於鄴。
entries.en: They attacked Liu Dan at Ye.
entries.literal: They attacked Liu Dan at Ye.

entries.zh: 及韓陵之戰，韶督率所部，先鋒陷陣。
entries.en: At the Battle of Hanling, Shao commanded and led his division as vanguard, breaking through the enemy lines.
entries.literal: At the Battle of Hanling, Shao commanded and led his division as vanguard, breaking through the enemy lines.

entries.zh: 尋從高祖出晉陽，追尒朱兆於赤谼嶺，平之。
entries.en: Soon he followed Gao Huan out of Jinyang, pursued Erzhu Zhao to Chihong Ridge, and pacified him.
entries.literal: Soon he followed the Grand Ancestor out of Jinyang, pursued Erzhu Zhao to Chihong Ridge, and pacified him.

entries.zh: 以軍功封下洛縣男。
entries.en: For military merit he was enfeoffed baron of Xialuo County.
entries.literal: For military merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Xialuo County.

entries.zh: 又從襲取夏州，擒斛律彌娥突，加龍驤將軍、諫議大夫，累遷武衛將軍。
entries.en: He also followed in the surprise capture of Xia Province, taking Hulu Mi'etuo prisoner; he was promoted to dragon-courser general and remonstrating grandee, rising in succession to general of martial guards.
entries.literal: He also followed in the surprise capture of Xia Province, taking Hulu Mi'etuo prisoner; he was promoted to Dragon-Courser General and Remonstrating Grandee, rising in succession to General of Martial Guards.

entries.zh: 後恩賜父榮姑臧縣侯，其下洛縣男啟讓繼母弟寧安。
entries.en: Later, by grace his father Duan Rong was given the title marquis of Guzang County; Shao petitioned to yield his barony of Xialuo County to his younger half-brother Ning'an.
entries.literal: Later, by grace his father Rong was given the title Marquis of Guzang County; Shao petitioned to yield his barony of Xialuo County to his younger half-brother Ning'an.

entries.zh: 興和四年，從高祖禦周文帝於邙山。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Xinghe, he followed Gao Huan in opposing Yuwen Tai at Mount Mang.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Xinghe, he followed the Grand Ancestor in opposing the Zhou Emperor Wen at Mount Mang.

entries.zh: 高祖身在行間，為西魏將賀拔勝所識，率銳來逼。
entries.en: Gao Huan was personally among the ranks; recognized by the Western Wei general Heba Sheng, Sheng led crack troops to press close.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor was personally among the ranks; recognized by the Western Wei general Heba Sheng, Sheng led crack troops to press close.

entries.zh: 韶從傍馳馬引弓反射，一箭斃其前驅，追騎懾憚，莫敢前者。
entries.en: Shao galloped up from the side, drew his bow and shot back; one arrow killed Sheng's lead rider. The pursuers were awed and dared not press forward.
entries.literal: Shao galloped up from the side, drew his bow and shot back; one arrow killed Sheng's lead rider. The pursuers were awed and dared not press forward.

entries.zh: 西軍退，賜馬並金，進爵為公。
entries.en: When the Western army withdrew, he was granted horses and gold and his rank was advanced to duke.
entries.literal: When the Western army withdrew, he was granted horses and gold and his rank was advanced to duke.

entries.zh: 武定四年，從征玉壁。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Wuding, he followed the campaign against Yubi.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Wuding, he followed the campaign against Yubi.

entries.zh: 時高祖不豫，攻城未下，召集諸將，共論進止之宜。
entries.en: At that time Gao Huan was unwell; the siege had not succeeded, and he summoned the generals to discuss together whether to advance or halt.
entries.literal: At that time the Grand Ancestor was unwell; the siege had not succeeded, and he summoned the generals to discuss together whether to advance or halt.

entries.zh: 謂大司馬斛律金、司徒韓軌、左衛將軍劉豐等曰：「吾每與段孝先論兵，殊有英略，若使比來用其謀，亦可無今日之勞矣。
entries.en: He said to grand marshal Hulu Jin, minister of education Han Gui, left guard general Liu Feng, and others, "Whenever I discuss warfare with Duan Xiaoxian, he shows remarkable strategic brilliance. Had I used his plans all along, I might have been spared today's toil.
entries.literal: He said to Grand Marshal Hulu Jin, Minister of Education Han Gui, Left Guard General Liu Feng, and others, "Whenever I discuss warfare with Duan Xiaoxian, he shows remarkable strategic brilliance. Had I used his plans all along, I might have been spared today's toil.

entries.zh: 吾患勢危篤，恐或不虞，欲委孝先以鄴下之事，何如？」
entries.en: I fear my illness is grave and dread some unforeseen turn; I wish to entrust Xiaoxian with affairs below Ye — what do you think?"
entries.literal: I fear my illness is grave and dread some unforeseen turn; I wish to entrust Xiaoxian with affairs below Ye — what do you think?"

entries.zh: 金等曰：「知臣莫若君，實無出孝先。」
entries.en: Jin and the others said, "No one knows a subject better than the lord — truly none surpasses Xiaoxian."
entries.literal: Jin and the others said, "No one knows a subject better than the lord — truly none surpasses Xiaoxian."

entries.zh: 仍謂韶曰：「吾昔與卿父冒涉險艱，同獎王室，建此大功。
entries.en: He then said to Shao, "Long ago your father and I braved danger and hardship together, jointly upheld the royal house, and built this great achievement.
entries.literal: He then said to Shao, "Long ago your father and I braved danger and hardship together, jointly upheld the royal house, and built this great achievement.

entries.zh: 今病疾如此，殆將不濟，宜善相翼佐，克茲負荷。」
entries.en: Now my illness is such that I may not recover; you should well assist each other and bear up under this burden."
entries.literal: Now my illness is such that I may not recover; you should well assist each other and bear up under this burden."

entries.zh: 即令韶從顯祖鎮鄴，召世宗赴軍。
entries.en: He thereupon ordered Shao to follow Gao Yang in garrisoning Ye and summoned Gao Cheng to the army.
entries.literal: He thereupon ordered Shao to follow the Founding Emperor in garrisoning Ye and summoned the Heir Apparent to the army.

entries.zh: 高祖疾甚，顧命世宗曰：「段孝先忠亮仁厚，智勇兼備，親戚之中，唯有此子，軍旅大事，宜共籌之。」
entries.en: When Gao Huan's illness grew severe, he entrusted Gao Cheng, saying, "Duan Xiaoxian is loyal, upright, benevolent, and generous, combining wisdom and courage. Among kinsmen, only this man — on great military matters, you should plan together."
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor's illness grew severe, he entrusted the Heir Apparent, saying, "Duan Xiaoxian is loyal, upright, benevolent, and generous, combining wisdom and courage. Among kinsmen, only this man — on great military matters, you should plan together."

entries.zh: 五年春，高祖崩於晉陽，秘不發喪。
entries.en: In the spring of the fifth year Gao Huan died at Jinyang; the death was kept secret and mourning was not announced.
entries.literal: In the spring of the fifth year the Grand Ancestor died at Jinyang; the death was kept secret and mourning was not announced.

entries.zh: 俄而侯景構亂，世宗還鄴，韶留守晉陽。
entries.en: Before long Hou Jing provoked rebellion; Gao Cheng returned to Ye and Shao remained to hold Jinyang.
entries.literal: Before long Hou Jing provoked rebellion; the Heir Apparent returned to Ye and Shao remained to hold Jinyang.

entries.zh: 世宗還，賜女樂十數人，金十斤，繒帛稱是，封長樂郡公。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng returned, he granted more than ten female musicians, ten jin of gold, and silk and brocade in corresponding measure, and enfeoffed Shao as duke of Changle Commandery.
entries.literal: When the Heir Apparent returned, he granted more than ten female musicians, ten jin of gold, and silk and brocade in corresponding measure, and enfeoffed Shao as Duke of Changle Commandery.

entries.zh: 世宗征潁川，韶留鎮晉陽。
entries.en: Gao Cheng campaigned against Yingchuan; Shao remained to garrison Jinyang.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent campaigned against Yingchuan; Shao remained to garrison Jinyang.

entries.zh: 別封真定縣男，行幷州刺史。
entries.en: Separately he was enfeoffed baron of Zhending County and acted as governor of Bing Province.
entries.literal: Separately he was enfeoffed Baron of Zhending County and acted as Governor of Bing Province.

entries.zh: 顯祖受禪，別封朝陵縣，又封霸城縣，加位特進。
entries.en: When Gao Yang received the abdication, Shao was separately enfeoffed in Chaoling County, again enfeoffed in Bacheng County, and granted special advancement.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication, Shao was separately enfeoffed in Chaoling County, again enfeoffed in Bacheng County, and granted special advancement.

entries.zh: 啟求歸朝陵公，乞封繼母梁氏為郡君。
entries.en: He petitioned to return the dignity of duke of Chaoling and begged that his stepmother Lady Liang be enfeoffed as commandery lady.
entries.literal: He petitioned to return the dignity of Duke of Chaoling and begged that his stepmother Lady Liang be enfeoffed as commandery lady.

entries.zh: 顯祖嘉之，別以梁氏為安定郡君。
entries.en: Gao Yang approved; separately Lady Liang was made lady of Anding Commandery.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor approved; separately Lady Liang was made Lady of Anding Commandery.

entries.zh: 又以霸城縣侯讓其繼母弟孝言。
entries.en: He also yielded the marquisate of Bacheng County to his younger half-brother Xiaoyan.
entries.literal: He also yielded the marquisate of Bacheng County to his younger half-brother Xiaoyan.

entries.zh: 論者美之。
entries.en: Commentators praised him.
entries.literal: Commentators praised him.

entries.zh: 天保三年，為冀州刺史、六州大都督，有惠政，得吏民之心。
entries.en: In the third year of Tianbao, he served as governor of Ji Province and grand commander of six provinces; his benevolent administration won the hearts of officials and people.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianbao, he served as Governor of Ji Province and grand commander of six provinces; his benevolent administration won the hearts of officials and people.

entries.zh: 四年十二月，梁將東方白額潛至宿預，招誘邊民，殺害長吏，淮、泗擾動。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, the Liang general Dongfang Baie secretly reached Suyu, recruited and enticed frontier people, killed local officials, and stirred turmoil along the Huai and Si rivers.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, the Liang general Dongfang Baie secretly reached Suyu, recruited and enticed frontier people, killed local officials, and stirred turmoil along the Huai and Si rivers.

entries.zh: 五年二月，詔徵韶討之。
entries.en: In the second month of the fifth year an edict summoned Shao to suppress them.
entries.literal: In the second month of the fifth year an edict summoned Shao to suppress them.

entries.zh: 既至，會梁將嚴超達等軍逼涇州；
entries.en: When he arrived, the Liang generals Yan Chaoda and others were pressing Jing Province;
entries.literal: When he arrived, the Liang generals Yan Chaoda and others were pressing Jing Province;

entries.zh: 又陳武帝率衆將攻廣陵，刺史王敬寶遣使告急；
entries.en: Chen Baxian was also leading a host of generals to attack Guangling; governor Wang Jingbao sent envoys in urgent appeal;
entries.literal: Chen Baxian was also leading a host of generals to attack Guangling; Governor Wang Jingbao sent envoys in urgent appeal;

entries.zh: 復有尹思令率衆萬餘人，謀襲盱貽。
entries.en: Yin Siling too led more than ten thousand men, plotting a surprise attack on Xuyi.
entries.literal: Yin Siling too led more than ten thousand men, plotting a surprise attack on Xuyi.

entries.zh: 三軍咸懼。
entries.en: The whole army was afraid.
entries.literal: The whole army was afraid.

entries.zh: 韶謂諸將曰：「自梁氏喪亂，國無定主，人懷去就，強者從之。
entries.en: Shao said to the generals, "Since the Liang house fell into disorder, the state has had no fixed ruler; people weigh where to go and where to stay, following whichever side seems stronger.
entries.literal: Shao said to the generals, "Since the Liang house fell into disorder, the state has had no fixed ruler; people weigh where to go and where to stay, following whichever side seems stronger.

entries.zh: 霸先等智小謀大，政令未一，外託同德，內有離心，諸君不足憂，吾揣之熟悉矣。」
entries.en: Chen Baxian and the like have small minds and large ambitions; their orders are not unified — outwardly claiming unity, inwardly divided at heart. You need not worry, gentlemen; I know them thoroughly."
entries.literal: Baxian and the like have small minds and large ambitions; their orders are not unified — outwardly claiming unity, inwardly divided at heart. You need not worry, gentlemen; I know them thoroughly."

entries.zh: 乃留儀同敬顯儁、堯難宗等圍守宿預，自將步騎數千人倍道赴涇州。
entries.en: He left Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes Jing Xianjun, Yao Nazong, and others to besiege and hold Suyu; he himself led several thousand infantry and cavalry by forced march toward Jing Province.
entries.literal: He left Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes Jing Xianjun, Yao Nazong, and others to besiege and hold Suyu; he himself led several thousand infantry and cavalry by forced march toward Jing Province.

entries.zh: 途出盱眙，思令不虞大軍卒至，望旗奔北。
entries.en: Passing through Xuyi, Yin Siling did not expect the main army to arrive so suddenly; at sight of the banners he fled north.
entries.literal: Passing through Xuyi, Yin Siling did not expect the main army to arrive so suddenly; at sight of the banners he fled north.

entries.zh: 進與超達合戰，大破之，盡獲其舟艦器械。
entries.en: Advancing, he joined battle with Chaoda and routed them utterly, capturing all their boats and equipment.
entries.literal: Advancing, he joined battle with Chaoda and routed them utterly, capturing all their boats and equipment.

entries.zh: 謂諸將士曰：「吳人輕躁，本無大謀，今破超達，霸先必走。」
entries.en: He told the officers and soldiers, "The Wu people are rash by nature and never had great plans. Now that Chaoda is broken, Chen Baxian will surely flee."
entries.literal: He told the officers and soldiers, "The Wu people are rash by nature and never had great plans. Now that Chaoda is broken, Baxian will surely flee."

entries.zh: 即回赴廣陵。
entries.en: He at once turned back toward Guangling.
entries.literal: He at once turned back toward Guangling.

entries.zh: 陳武帝果遁去。
entries.en: Chen Baxian indeed fled.
entries.literal: Chen Baxian indeed fled.

entries.zh: 追至楊子柵，望揚州城乃還，大獲其軍資器物，旋師宿預。
entries.en: Pursuing as far as Yangzi stockade, he sighted Yangzhou city and turned back; he captured a great store of military supplies and equipment, then wheeled his army back to Suyu.
entries.literal: Pursuing as far as Yangzi stockade, he sighted Yangzhou city and turned back; he captured a great store of military supplies and equipment, then wheeled his army back to Suyu.

entries.zh: 六月，韶遣辯士喻白額禍福，白額於是開門請盟。
entries.en: In the sixth month, Shao sent eloquent envoys to explain fortune and disaster to Baie; Baie thereupon opened the gates and requested an alliance.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, Shao sent eloquent envoys to explain fortune and disaster to Baie; Baie thereupon opened the gates and requested an alliance.

entries.zh: 韶與行臺辛術等議，且為受盟。
entries.en: Shao discussed with the mobile commissioner Xin Shu and others and provisionally accepted the alliance.
entries.literal: Shao discussed with the mobile commissioner Xin Shu and others and provisionally accepted the alliance.

entries.zh: 盟訖，度白額終不為用，因執而斬之，並其諸弟等並傳首京師。
entries.en: When the alliance was concluded, judging that Baie would never be useful, he seized and executed him, and together with his brothers sent their heads to the capital.
entries.literal: When the alliance was concluded, judging that Baie would never be useful, he seized and executed him, and together with his brothers sent their heads to the capital.

entries.zh: 江淮帖然，民皆安輯。
entries.en: The Huai and Yangzi regions grew calm; the people were all settled.
entries.literal: The Huai and Yangzi regions grew calm; the people were all settled.

entries.zh: 顯祖嘉其功，詔賞吳口七十人，封平原郡王。
entries.en: Gao Yang applauded his merit; an edict granted seventy Wu captives and enfeoffed him as prince of Pingyuan Commandery.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor applauded his merit; an edict granted seventy Wu captives and enfeoffed him as Prince of Pingyuan Commandery.

entries.zh: 清河王岳之克郢州，執司徒陸法和，韶亦豫行，築層城，於新蔡立郭默戍而還。
entries.en: When Prince Qinghe Yue captured Ying Province and took minister of education Lu Fazhe prisoner, Shao also took part in the expedition, built tiered fortifications, established the Guo Mo garrison at Xincai, and returned.
entries.literal: When Prince Qinghe Yue captured Ying Province and took Minister of Education Lu Fazhe prisoner, Shao also took part in the expedition, built tiered fortifications, established the Guo Mo garrison at Xincai, and returned.

entries.zh: 皇建元年，領太子太師。
entries.en: In the first year of Huangjian, he served as grand preceptor of the crown prince.
entries.literal: In the first year of Huangjian, he served as Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 十二月，周武帝遣將率羌夷與突厥合衆逼晉陽，世祖自鄴倍道兼行赴救。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou dispatched generals leading Qiang and tribal forces together with the Turks in a combined host pressing Jinyang; Emperor Wucheng hurried from Ye by forced march to the rescue.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, the Zhou Emperor Wu dispatched generals leading Qiang and tribal forces together with the Turks in a combined host pressing Jinyang; the Shizu Emperor hurried from Ye by forced march to the rescue.

entries.zh: 突厥從北結陣而前，東距汾河，西被風谷。
entries.en: The Turks advanced from the north in battle formation, touching the Fen River on the east and Wind Valley on the west.
entries.literal: The Turks advanced from the north in battle formation, touching the Fen River on the east and Wind Valley on the west.

entries.zh: 時事既倉卒，兵馬未整，世祖見如此，亦欲避之而東。
entries.en: Events had come in a rush; troops and horses were not yet in order. Seeing the field, Emperor Wucheng wished to withdraw eastward.
entries.literal: Events were sudden; troops and horses were not yet arrayed. Seeing this, the Shizu Emperor also wished to withdraw eastward.

entries.zh: 尋納河間王孝琬之請，令趙郡王盡護諸將。
entries.en: Soon he accepted Prince of Hejian Xiaowan's plea and put Prince of Zhao Commandery in overall charge of the generals.
entries.literal: Soon he accepted Prince of Hejian Xiaowan's request and ordered Prince of Zhao Commandery to take overall command of the generals.

entries.zh: 時大雪之後，周人以步卒為前鋒，從西山而下，去城二里。
entries.en: After heavy snow, the Zhou made infantry their vanguard, descending from the western hills two li from the city.
entries.literal: After heavy snow, the Zhou men made infantry their vanguard, descending from the western hills — two li from the city.

entries.zh: 諸將咸欲逆擊之。
entries.en: Every general wanted to meet them with a counterattack.
entries.literal: All the generals wished to meet them with a counterattack.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「步人氣勢自有限，今積雪既厚，逆戰非便，不如陣以待之。
entries.en: An edict ran, "Infantry can only push so far. With snow this deep, a meeting fight is ill advised — hold your lines and wait.
entries.literal: An edict said, "Infantry by nature have limited momentum. With the snow so deep, a meeting engagement is ill advised — better to hold formation and wait.

entries.zh: 彼勞我逸，破之必矣。」
entries.en: They will be weary and we rested — the victory is certain."
entries.literal: They will be weary and we rested — defeating them is certain."

entries.zh: 既而交戰，大破之，敵前鋒盡殪，無復孑遺，自餘通宵奔遁。
entries.en: Battle was joined and the enemy was routed. The vanguard was annihilated to the last man; the rest fled through the night.
entries.literal: Battle was joined and the enemy was routed. The vanguard was annihilated to the last man; the rest fled through the night.

entries.zh: 仍令韶率騎追之，出塞不及而還。
entries.en: Shao was ordered to lead cavalry in pursuit — he could not overtake them before the frontier and turned back.
entries.literal: Shao was then ordered to lead cavalry in pursuit; he could not overtake them before the frontier and returned.

entries.zh: 世祖嘉其功，別封懷州武德郡公，進位太師。
entries.en: Emperor Wucheng commended his merit, separately enfeoffed him duke of Wude Commandery in Huai Province, and advanced him to grand preceptor.
entries.literal: The Shizu Emperor commended his merit, separately enfeoffed him Duke of Wude Commandery in Huai Province, and advanced him to Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 周冢宰宇文護母閻氏先配中山宮，護聞閻尚存，乃因邊境移書，請還其母，並通鄰好。
entries.en: The mother of Zhou chancellor Yuwen Hu, Lady Yan, had first been assigned to Zhongshan Palace. Learning she still lived, Hu sent a letter through the border asking for her return and proposing neighborly peace.
entries.literal: The mother of Zhou chancellor Yuwen Hu, Lady Yan, had first been assigned to Zhongshan Palace. Learning that Yan still lived, Hu sent a letter through the border asking for his mother's return and proposing neighborly peace.

entries.zh: 時突厥屢犯邊，韶軍於塞下。
entries.en: At that time the Turks repeatedly raided the frontier; Shao encamped below the passes.
entries.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly raided the frontier; Shao encamped below the passes.

entries.zh: 世祖遣黃門徐世榮乘傳賫周書問韶。
entries.en: Emperor Wucheng sent Attendant of the Yellow Gate Xu Shirong by fast relay with the Zhou letter to consult Shao.
entries.literal: The Shizu Emperor sent Attendant of the Yellow Gate Xu Shirong by fast relay with the Zhou letter to consult Shao.

entries.zh: 韶以周人反覆，本無信義，比晉陽之役，其事可知。
entries.en: Shao said the Zhou were fickle and had never kept faith — the affair at Jinyang had already shown as much.
entries.literal: Shao said the Zhou were fickle and had never kept faith; the affair at Jinyang had already shown as much.

entries.zh: 護外托為相，其實王也，既為母請和，不遣一介之使申其情理，乃據移書即送其母，恐示之弱。
entries.en: Hu outwardly styled himself chancellor but was in truth a king. He asked peace for his mother's sake, yet sent not a single envoy to state his case — and we would return her on the strength of a letter alone. That would look like weakness.
entries.literal: Hu outwardly styled himself chancellor but was in truth a king. Having asked peace for his mother's sake, he sent not a single envoy to state his case — yet we would return her on the strength of a letter alone. That would look like weakness.

entries.zh: 如臣管見，且外許之，待後放之未晚。
entries.en: In my humble view, we should agree outwardly and release her later — that would not be too late.
entries.literal: In my humble view, we should agree outwardly and release her later — that would not be too late.

entries.zh: 不聽。
entries.en: He was not heeded.
entries.literal: He was not heeded.

entries.zh: 遂遣使以禮將送。
entries.en: An envoy was sent to escort her back with full ceremony.
entries.literal: An envoy was then sent to escort her back with full ceremony.

entries.zh: 護既得母，仍遣將尉遲迥等襲洛陽。
entries.en: Once Hu had his mother, he still sent generals Yuchi Jiong and others to strike at Luoyang.
entries.literal: Once Hu had his mother, he still sent generals Yuchi Jiong and others to strike at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 詔遣蘭陵王長恭、大將軍斛律光率衆擊之，軍於邙山之下，逗留未進。
entries.en: An edict dispatched Prince of Lanling Gao Chang Gong and Grand General Hulü Guang with troops to attack them. They encamped below Mount Mang and lingered without advancing.
