entries.literal: An edict dispatched Prince of Lanling Chang Gong and Grand General Hulü Guang with troops to attack them; they encamped below Mount Mang and lingered without advancing.

entries.zh: 世祖召謂曰：「今欲遣王赴洛陽之圍，但突厥在此，復須鎮禦，王謂如何？」
entries.en: Emperor Wucheng summoned Shao and said, "I wish to send you to the siege at Luoyang — but the Turks are here and must still be held in check. What do you think?"
entries.literal: The Shizu Emperor summoned Shao and said, "I wish to send you to the siege at Luoyang — but the Turks are here and must still be held in check. What do you think?"

entries.zh: 韶曰：「北虜侵邊，事等疥癬，今西羌窺逼，便是膏肓之病，請奉詔南行。」
entries.en: Shao said, "Northern raiders on the frontier are scabies; the Western Qiang pressing in are a disease in the vitals. I beg leave to go south as ordered."
entries.literal: Shao said, "Northern barbarians on the frontier are a matter of scabies; the Western Qiang pressing in are a disease in the vitals. I beg leave to go south as ordered."

entries.zh: 世祖曰：「朕意亦爾。」
entries.en: Emperor Wucheng said, "My mind is the same."
entries.literal: The Shizu Emperor said, "My mind is the same."

entries.zh: 乃令韶督精騎一千，發自晉陽。
entries.en: He ordered Shao to command a thousand elite cavalry and set out from Jinyang.
entries.literal: He then ordered Shao to command a thousand elite cavalry, setting out from Jinyang.

entries.zh: 五日便濟河，與大將共量進止。
entries.en: In five days he had crossed the river and joined the grand generals in weighing advance and halt.
entries.literal: In five days he had crossed the river and joined the grand generals in deliberating advance and halt.

entries.zh: 韶旦將帳下二百騎與諸軍共登邙阪，聊觀周軍形勢。
entries.en: At dawn Shao led two hundred cavalry from his personal retinue and climbed the Mang slopes with the other armies to take a brief look at the Zhou disposition.
entries.literal: At dawn Shao led two hundred cavalry from his personal retinue and climbed the Mang slopes with the other armies to take a brief look at the Zhou disposition.

entries.zh: 至大和谷，便值周軍，即遣馳告諸營，追集兵馬。
entries.en: At Dahe Valley they ran straight into the Zhou army; he at once sent riders racing to the camps to muster troops and horses.
entries.literal: At Dahe Valley they ran straight into the Zhou army; he at once sent riders racing to the camps to muster troops and horses.

entries.zh: 仍與諸將結陣以待之。
entries.en: He then formed battle lines with the generals and waited.
entries.literal: He then formed battle lines with the generals and waited.

entries.zh: 韶為左軍，蘭陵王為中軍，斛律光為右軍，與周人相對。
entries.en: Shao took the left wing, Prince of Lanling the center, and Hulü Guang the right — facing the Zhou.
entries.literal: Shao took the left wing, Prince of Lanling the center, and Hulü Guang the right — facing the Zhou.

entries.zh: 韶遙謂周人曰：「汝宇文護幸得其母，不能懷恩報德，今日之來，竟何意也？」
entries.en: Shao shouted across to the Zhou, "You, Yuwen Hu — you have just recovered your mother and cannot repay kindness with gratitude. What do you mean by coming today?"
entries.literal: Shao shouted across to the Zhou, "You, Yuwen Hu — you have just recovered your mother and cannot repay kindness with gratitude. What do you mean by coming today?"

entries.zh: 周人曰：「天遣我來，有何可問。」
entries.en: The Zhou answered, "Heaven sent us — what is there to ask?"
entries.literal: The Zhou answered, "Heaven sent us — what is there to ask?"

entries.zh: 韶曰：「天道賞善罰惡，當遣汝送死來耳。」
entries.en: Shao said, "Heaven rewards the good and punishes the evil — it has sent you here to die."
entries.literal: Shao said, "Heaven rewards the good and punishes the evil — it has sent you here to die."

entries.zh: 周軍仍以步人在前，上山逆戰。
entries.en: The Zhou army again put infantry in front and came up the hill to fight.
entries.literal: The Zhou army again put infantry in front and came up the hill to fight.

entries.zh: 韶以彼徒我騎，且却且引，待其力弊，乃遣下馬擊之。
entries.en: Shao, seeing foot soldiers against his cavalry, withdrew step by step and drew them on until their strength failed — then ordered his men to dismount and strike.
entries.literal: Shao, seeing their foot soldiers against his cavalry, withdrew step by step and drew them on until their strength failed — then ordered his men to dismount and strike.

entries.zh: 短兵始交，周人大潰。
entries.en: Close combat had barely begun when the Zhou broke completely.
entries.literal: Close combat had barely begun when the Zhou broke completely.

entries.zh: 其中軍所當者，亦一時瓦解，投墜溪谷而死者甚衆。
entries.en: Those who met the center wing collapsed at once as well; very many fell into ravines and gullies and died.
entries.literal: Those who met the center wing collapsed at once as well; very many fell into ravines and gullies and died.

entries.zh: 洛城之圍，亦即奔遁，盡棄營幕，從邙山至榖水三十里中，軍資器物彌滿川澤。
entries.en: The siege of Luoyang also broke and fled, abandoning all camps and tents. From Mount Mang to Gushui for thirty li, military stores and equipment filled the streams and marshes.
entries.literal: The siege of Luoyang also broke and fled, abandoning all camps and tents; from Mount Mang to Gushui for thirty li, military stores and equipment filled the streams and marshes.

entries.zh: 車駕幸洛陽，親勞將士，於河陰置酒高會，策勳命賞，除太宰，封靈武縣公。
entries.en: The imperial carriage visited Luoyang and personally encouraged the soldiers. At Heyin a great feast of wine was set out; merits were assessed and rewards given — Shao was made grand steward and enfeoffed duke of Lingwu County.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage visited Luoyang and personally encouraged the soldiers; at Heyin a great feast of wine was set out, merits were assessed and rewards given — Shao was made Grand Steward and enfeoffed Duke of Lingwu County.

entries.zh: 天統三年，除左丞相，永昌郡公，食滄州幹。
entries.en: In the third year of Tiantong he was made left chancellor, duke of Yongchang Commandery, with revenue from Cang Province.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tiantong he was made Left Chancellor, Duke of Yongchang Commandery, with revenue from Cang Province.

entries.zh: 韶出總軍旅，入參帷幄，功既居高，重以婚媾，望傾朝野。
entries.en: Shao went out to command the armies and came in to counsel at the inner court; his merit stood highest, and with marriage ties besides, his prestige tilted court and realm.
entries.literal: Shao went out to command the armies and came in to counsel at the inner court; his merit stood highest, and with marriage ties besides, his prestige tilted court and realm.

entries.zh: 長於計略，善於禦衆，得將士之心，臨敵之日，人人爭奮。
entries.en: He excelled in stratagem and was skilled at commanding troops; he won the hearts of officers and soldiers, and on the day of battle every man strove to outdo the rest.
entries.literal: He excelled in stratagem and was skilled at commanding troops; he won the hearts of officers and soldiers, and on the day of battle every man strove to outdo the rest.

entries.zh: 又雅性溫慎，有宰相之風。
entries.en: By nature he was gentle and cautious, with the bearing of a chief minister.
entries.literal: By nature he was gentle and cautious, with the bearing of a chief minister.

entries.zh: 教訓子弟，閨門雍肅，事後母以孝聞，齊世勛貴之家罕有及者。
entries.en: He trained his sons and younger brothers; his household was orderly and solemn; he was famed for filial duty toward his stepmother — among the meritorious great houses of Qi, few could match him.
entries.literal: He trained his sons and younger brothers; his household was orderly and solemn; he was famed for filial duty toward his stepmother — among the meritorious great houses of Qi, few could match him.

entries.zh: 然僻於好色，雖居要重，微服間行。
entries.en: Yet he was partial to women; though he held weighty office, he would go about in plain dress.
entries.literal: Yet he was partial to women; though he held weighty office, he would go about in plain dress.

entries.zh: 有皇甫氏，魏黃門郎元瑀之妻，弟謹謀逆，皇甫氏因沒官。
entries.en: There was a Lady Huangfu, wife of Wei Attendant Gentleman Yuan Yu; when Yu's younger brother Jin plotted rebellion, Lady Huangfu was confiscated to the state.
entries.literal: There was a Lady Huangfu, wife of Wei Attendant Gentleman Yuan Yu; when Yu's younger brother Jin plotted rebellion, Lady Huangfu was confiscated to the state.

entries.zh: 韶美其容質，上啟固請，世宗重違其意，因以賜之。
entries.en: Shao admired her beauty and memorialized a firm request; Gao Cheng greatly disliked to refuse him and therefore bestowed her upon him.
entries.literal: Shao admired her beauty and memorialized a firm request; Shizong greatly disliked to refuse him and therefore bestowed her upon him.

entries.zh: 尤嗇於財，雖親戚故舊略無施與。
entries.en: He was especially stingy with wealth; even kin and old friends he scarcely gave anything.
entries.literal: He was especially stingy with wealth; even kin and old friends he scarcely gave anything.

entries.zh: 其子深尚公主，並省丞郎在家佐事十餘日，事畢辭還，人唯賜一杯酒。
entries.en: His son Shen had married a princess and served more than ten days at home as a provincial assistant — when the business was done and he took leave to return, Shao gave him only a cup of wine.
entries.literal: His son Shen had married a princess and served more than ten days at home as a provincial assistant — when the business was done and he took leave to return, Shao gave him only a cup of wine.

entries.zh: 長子懿嗣。
entries.en: His eldest son Yi succeeded him.
entries.literal: His eldest son Yi succeeded him.

entries.zh: 孝言本以勳戚緒餘，致位通顯，至此便驕奢放逸，無所畏憚。
entries.en: Xiaoyan had risen to eminence on the lingering credit of a martial clan — and once there he turned arrogant and unrestrained, afraid of nothing.
entries.literal: Xiaoyan had originally reached high office thanks to the residual prestige of meritorious kin; once there he grew arrogant, prodigal, and utterly without fear.

entries.zh: 曾夜行，過其賓客宋孝王家宿，喚坊民防援，不時應赴，遂拷殺之。
entries.en: Once on a night journey he passed the house where his guest Song Xiaowang was lodging and called out the ward watchmen; when they did not come at once, he had them beaten to death.
entries.literal: Once while traveling at night he passed the house where his guest Song Xiaowang was staying and summoned the ward watchmen; when they did not come at once, he had them beaten to death.

entries.zh: 又與諸淫婦密遊，為其夫覺，復恃官勢，拷掠而殞。
entries.en: He also kept secret company with adulterous women; when a husband caught him at it, Xiaoyan again leaned on his office and beat the man until he died.
entries.literal: He also carried on secret affairs with various adulterous women; when a husband discovered it, Xiaoyan again relied on official power and beat the man until he died.

entries.zh: 時苑內須果木，科民間及僧寺備輸，悉分向其私宅種植。
entries.en: When the palace gardens needed fruit trees, levies were laid on common households and Buddhist temples to supply them — yet Xiaoyan had the whole levy split off and planted at his private residence.
entries.literal: When the imperial gardens needed fruit trees, levies were laid on private households and Buddhist temples to supply them — but Xiaoyan had everything diverted to plant at his private residence.

entries.zh: 又殿內及園中須石，差車牛從漳河運載，復分車迴取。
entries.en: When the palace halls and gardens needed stone, cart oxen were sent to haul it from the Zhang River — and again he diverted the carts on the return trip for his own use.
entries.literal: When the palace halls and gardens needed stone, cart oxen were dispatched to haul it from the Zhang River — yet he diverted the carts to carry loads for himself on the return.

entries.zh: 事悉聞徹，出為海州刺史。
entries.en: When every detail reached the throne, he was sent out as governor of Haizhou.
entries.literal: When all these matters became fully known, he was sent out as governor of Haizhou.

entries.zh: 尋以其兄故，徵拜都官尚書，食陽城郡幹，仍加開府。
entries.en: Soon, on account of his elder brother, he was recalled and made minister of justice, drawing income from Yangcheng Commandery, with an opening establishment added.
entries.literal: Soon, because of his elder brother, he was recalled and appointed minister of justice, with income from Yangcheng Commandery, and additionally granted an opening establishment.

entries.zh: 遷太常卿，除齊州刺史，以贓賄為御史所劾。
entries.en: He was transferred to grand minister of ceremonies, then appointed governor of Qi Province — and impeached by the censorate for bribery and embezzlement.
entries.literal: He was transferred to grand minister of ceremonies, then made governor of Qi Province, and was impeached by the censorate for bribery and embezzlement.

entries.zh: 屬世祖崩，遇赦免。
entries.en: It happened that Emperor Wucheng died; he was pardoned in the general amnesty.
entries.literal: It happened that Shizu died; he received amnesty and was pardoned.

entries.zh: 拜太常卿，轉食河南郡幹，遷吏部尚書。
entries.en: He was made grand minister of ceremonies, transferred to income from Henan Commandery, and promoted to minister of personnel.
entries.literal: He was appointed grand minister of ceremonies, transferred to income from Henan Commandery, and promoted to minister of personnel.

entries.zh: 段榮 子韶
entries.en: Duan Rong; Duan Shao
entries.literal: Duan Rong; Duan Shao

entries.zh: 金性敦直，善騎射，行兵用匈奴法，望塵識馬步多少，嗅地知軍度遠近。
entries.en: Hulü Jin was honest and straightforward by nature, skilled at riding and archery; in campaigning he used Xiongnu methods — reading dust to know how many horse and foot were on the march, sniffing the ground to gauge an army's distance.
entries.literal: Jin was honest and straightforward by nature, skilled at riding and archery; in campaigning he used Xiongnu methods — reading dust to know how many horse and foot were on the march, sniffing the ground to gauge an army's distance.

entries.zh: 初為軍主，與懷朔鎮將楊鈞送茹茹主阿那瓌還北。
entries.en: At first he served as a military commander; with the garrison general of Huaishuo, Yang Jun, he escorted the Ruru ruler Anagui back north.
entries.literal: At first he served as a military commander; with the garrison general of Huaishuo, Yang Jun, he escorted the Ruru ruler Anagui back north.

entries.zh: 瓌見金射獵，深嘆其工。
entries.en: Anagui watched Hulü Jin hunting with bow and arrow and sighed deeply at his skill.
entries.literal: Anagui watched Jin hunting with bow and arrow and sighed deeply at his skill.

entries.zh: 後瓌入寇高陸，金拒擊破之。
entries.en: Later Anagui raided Gaolu; Hulü Jin resisted and defeated him.
entries.literal: Later Anagui raided Gaolu; Jin resisted and defeated him.

entries.zh: 正光末，破六韓拔陵構逆，金擁衆屬焉，陵假金王號。
entries.en: At the end of Zhenguang, Poliuhan Baling raised rebellion; Hulü Jin gathered troops and submitted to him, and Baling made Jin a nominal king.
entries.literal: At the end of Zhenguang, Poliuhan Baling raised rebellion; Jin gathered troops and submitted to him, and Baling made Jin a nominal king.

entries.zh: 金度陵終敗滅，乃統所部萬戶詣雲州請降，即授第二領民酋長。
entries.en: Hulü Jin judged that Baling would ultimately be destroyed and annihilated; he then led the ten thousand households under his command to Yunzhou to surrender and was at once appointed second chief of the submitted tribes.
entries.literal: Jin judged that Baling would ultimately be destroyed and annihilated; he then led the ten thousand households under his command to Yunzhou to surrender and was at once appointed Second Chief of the Submitted Tribes.

entries.zh: 稍引南出黃瓜堆，為杜洛周所破，部衆分散，金與兄平二人脫身歸尒朱榮。
entries.en: He gradually led his force south out of Huangguadui but was defeated by Du Luozhou; his troops scattered, and Hulü Jin and his elder brother Ping alone escaped to Erzhu Rong.
entries.literal: He gradually led his force south out of Huangguadui but was defeated by Du Luozhou; his troops scattered, and Jin and his elder brother Ping alone escaped to Erzhu Rong.

entries.zh: 榮表金為別將，累遷都督。
entries.en: Erzhu Rong memorialized to have Hulü Jin made a separate commander; he rose in succession to grand commander.
entries.literal: Rong memorialized to have Jin made a separate commander; he rose in succession to grand commander.

entries.zh: 孝莊立，賜爵阜城縣男，加寧朔將軍、屯騎校尉。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaozhuang ascended the throne, Hulü Jin was granted the title baron of Fucheng County and additionally made general who pacifies the north and colonel of the towered cavalry.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang ascended the throne, Jin was granted the title Baron of Fucheng County and additionally made General Who Pacifies the North and Colonel of the Towered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 從破葛榮、元顥，頻有戰功，加鎮南大將軍。
entries.en: He followed in the defeats of Ge Rong and Yuan Hao, earned repeated battle merit, and was promoted to grand general who pacifies the south.
entries.literal: He followed in the defeats of Ge Rong and Yuan Hao, earned repeated battle merit, and was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the South.

entries.zh: 及尒朱兆等逆亂，高祖密懷匡復之計，金與婁昭、厙狄干等贊成大謀，仍從舉義。
entries.en: When Erzhu Zhao and others rose in rebellion, Gao Huan secretly harbored a plan to restore the realm; Hulü Jin, together with Lou Zhao, Kudie Gan, and others, approved the great design and then followed in raising the righteous banner.
entries.literal: When Erzhu Zhao and others rose in rebellion, the Grand Ancestor secretly harbored a plan to restore the realm; Jin, together with Lou Zhao, Kudie Gan, and others, approved the great design and then followed in raising the righteous banner.

entries.zh: 高祖南攻鄴，留金守信都，領恒、雲、燕、朔、顯、蔚六州大都督，委以後事，別討李脩，破之，加右光祿大夫。
entries.en: When Gao Huan attacked Ye from the south, he left Hulü Jin to hold Xindu, made him grand commander of the six provinces of Heng, Yun, Yan, Shuo, Xian, and Yu, and entrusted him with rear affairs; separately Jin attacked Li Xiu and defeated him, and was promoted to right director of splendid honors.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor attacked Ye from the south, he left Jin to hold Xindu, made him Grand Commander of the six provinces of Heng, Yun, Yan, Shuo, Xian, and Yu, and entrusted him with rear affairs; separately Jin attacked Li Xiu and defeated him, and was promoted to Right Director of Splendid Honors.

entries.zh: 會高祖於鄴，仍從平晉陽，追滅尒朱兆。
entries.en: He joined Gao Huan at Ye and then followed in pacifying Jinyang and pursuing the destruction of Erzhu Zhao.
entries.literal: He joined the Grand Ancestor at Ye and then followed in pacifying Jinyang and pursuing the destruction of Erzhu Zhao.

entries.zh: 太昌初，以金為汾州刺史、當州大都督，進爵為侯。
entries.en: At the beginning of Taichang, Hulü Jin was made governor of Fen Province and grand commander of that province, and his rank was advanced to marquis.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, Jin was made Governor of Fen Province and Grand Commander of that province, and his rank was advanced to marquis.

entries.zh: 從高祖破紇豆陵於河西。
entries.en: He followed Gao Huan in defeating Hediouling west of the river.
entries.literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in defeating Hediouling west of the river.

entries.zh: 天平初，遷鄴，使金領步騎三萬鎮風陵以備西寇，軍罷，還晉陽。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianping, he moved to Ye; Hulü Jin was ordered to lead thirty thousand foot and horse to garrison Fengling against Western raiders; when the campaign ended, he returned to Jinyang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he moved to Ye; Jin was ordered to lead thirty thousand foot and horse to garrison Fengling against Western raiders; when the campaign ended, he returned to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 從高祖戰於沙苑，不利班師，因此東雍諸城復為西軍所據，遣金與尉景、厙狄干等討復之。
entries.en: He followed Gao Huan in battle at Shayuan; the army withdrew without success, and for this the cities of eastern Yong were again seized by the Western army; Hulü Jin was dispatched with Wei Jing, Kudie Gan, and others to recover them.
entries.literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in battle at Shayuan; the army withdrew without success, and for this the cities of eastern Yong were again seized by the Western army; Jin was dispatched with Wei Jing, Kudie Gan, and others to recover them.

entries.zh: 元象中，周文帝復大舉向河陽。
entries.en: In the Yuanxiang era, Yuwen Tai again launched a great campaign toward Heyang.
entries.literal: In the Yuanxiang era, the Zhou Emperor Wen again launched a great campaign toward Heyang.

entries.zh: 高祖率衆討之，使金徑往太州，為掎角之勢。
entries.en: Gao Huan led troops to attack him and sent Hulü Jin straight to Tai Province to form pincers.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor led troops to attack him and sent Jin straight to Tai Province to form pincers.

entries.zh: 金到晉州，以軍退不行，仍與行臺薛脩義共圍喬山之寇。
entries.en: When Hulü Jin reached Jin Province, because the army had withdrawn he did not advance; he then joined the mobile headquarters commander Xue Xiuyi in besieging the bandits at Qiaoshan.
entries.literal: When Jin reached Jin Province, because the army had withdrawn he did not advance; he then joined the mobile headquarters commander Xue Xiuyi in besieging the bandits at Qiaoshan.

entries.zh: 俄而高祖至，仍共討平之，因從高祖攻下南絳、邵郡等數城。
entries.en: Before long Gao Huan arrived; together they pacified the enemy, and Hulü Jin then followed Gao Huan in capturing several cities including Southern Jiang and Shao Commandery.
entries.literal: Before long the Grand Ancestor arrived; together they pacified the enemy, and Jin then followed the Grand Ancestor in capturing several cities including Southern Jiang and Shao Commandery.

entries.zh: 武定初，北豫州刺史高仲密據城西叛，周文帝入寇洛陽。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wuding, Gao Zhongmi, governor of Northern Yu Province, held the west of the city and rebelled, and Yuwen Tai invaded Luoyang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wuding, Gao Zhongmi, Governor of Northern Yu Province, held the west of the city and rebelled, and the Zhou Emperor Wen invaded Luoyang.

entries.zh: 高祖使金統劉豐、步大汗薩等步騎數萬守河陽城以拒之。
entries.en: Gao Huan had Hulü Jin command Liu Feng, Bu Dahan Sa, and others with several tens of thousands of foot and horse to hold Heyang city against him.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor had Jin command Liu Feng, Bu Dahan Sa, and others with several tens of thousands of foot and horse to hold Heyang city against him.

entries.zh: 高祖到，仍從破密。
entries.en: When Gao Huan arrived, Hulü Jin again followed in defeating Zhongmi.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor arrived, Jin again followed in defeating Zhongmi.

entries.zh: 軍還，除大司馬，改封石城郡公，邑一千戶，轉第一領民酋長。
entries.en: When the army returned, he was made grand marshal, his title was changed to duke of Shicheng Commandery with a fief of one thousand households, and he was transferred to first chief of the submitted tribes.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was made Grand Marshal, his title was changed to Duke of Shicheng Commandery with a fief of one thousand households, and he was transferred to First Chief of the Submitted Tribes.

entries.zh: 三年，高祖出軍襲山胡，分為二道。
entries.en: In the third year, Gao Huan led troops on a surprise attack against the Mountain Hu, dividing into two routes.
entries.literal: In the third year, the Grand Ancestor led troops on a surprise attack against the Mountain Hu, dividing into two routes.

entries.zh: 以金為南道軍司，由黃櫨嶺出。
entries.en: Hulü Jin was made army supervisor of the southern route and went out by Huanglu Ridge.
entries.literal: Jin was made army supervisor of the southern route and went out by Huanglu Ridge.

entries.zh: 高祖自出北道，度赤谼嶺，會金於烏突戍，合擊破之。
entries.en: Gao Huan himself went by the northern route, crossed Chihong Ridge, joined Hulü Jin at Wutu Fort, and together they attacked and defeated the enemy.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor himself went by the northern route, crossed Chihong Ridge, joined Jin at Wutu Fort, and together they attacked and defeated the enemy.

entries.zh: 軍還，出為冀州刺史。
entries.en: When the army returned, he went out as governor of Ji Province.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he went out as Governor of Ji Province.

entries.zh: 四年，詔金率衆從烏蘇道會高祖於晉州，仍從攻玉壁。
entries.en: In the fourth year, an edict ordered Hulü Jin to lead troops by the Wusu route to join Gao Huan at Jin Province, and he then followed in the attack on Yubi.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, an edict ordered Jin to lead troops by the Wusu route to join the Grand Ancestor at Jin Province, and he then followed in the attack on Yubi.

entries.zh: 軍還，高祖使金總督大衆，從歸晉陽。
entries.en: When the army returned, Gao Huan had Hulü Jin command the whole host on the return to Jinyang.
entries.literal: When the army returned, the Grand Ancestor had Jin command the whole host on the return to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 世宗嗣事，侯景據潁川降於西魏，詔遣金帥潘樂、薛孤延等固守河陽以備。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng succeeded to affairs, Hou Jing held Yingchuan and surrendered to Western Wei; an edict dispatched Hulü Jin to command Pan Le, Xue Guyuan, and others to hold Heyang in defense.
entries.literal: When Shizong succeeded to affairs, Hou Jing held Yingchuan and surrendered to Western Wei; an edict dispatched Jin to command Pan Le, Xue Guyuan, and others to hold Heyang in defense.

entries.zh: 西魏使其大都督李景和、若干寶領馬步數萬，欲從新城赴援侯景。
entries.en: Western Wei sent its grand commander Li Jinghe and Jogan Bao leading several tens of thousands of horse and foot, intending to go from Xincheng to relieve Hou Jing.
entries.literal: Western Wei sent its Grand Commander Li Jinghe and Jogan Bao leading several tens of thousands of horse and foot, intending to go from Xincheng to relieve Hou Jing.

entries.zh: 金率衆停廣武以要之，景和等聞而退走。
entries.en: Hulü Jin led troops and halted at Guangwu to intercept them; Jinghe and the others, hearing of it, withdrew and fled.
entries.literal: Jin led troops and halted at Guangwu to intercept them; Jinghe and the others, hearing of it, withdrew and fled.

entries.zh: 還為肆州刺史，仍率所部於宜陽築楊志、百家、呼延三戍，置守備而還。
entries.en: He returned as governor of Si Province and again led his division to build the three forts of Yangzhi, Baijia, and Huyan at Yiyang, posting garrisons before returning.
entries.literal: He returned as Governor of Si Province and again led his division to build the three forts of Yangzhi, Baijia, and Huyan at Yiyang, posting garrisons before returning.

entries.zh: 侯景之走南豫，西魏儀同三司王思政入據潁川。
entries.en: When Hou Jing fled to Southern Yu, Western Wei commissioner with protocol equal to three imperators Wang Sizheng entered and seized Yingchuan.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing fled to Southern Yu, Western Wei Commissioner with Protocol Equal to Three Imperators Wang Sizheng entered and seized Yingchuan.

entries.zh: 世宗遣高嶽、慕容紹宗、劉豐等率衆圍之。
entries.en: Gao Cheng dispatched Gao Yue, Murong Shaozong, Liu Feng, and others to lead troops and besiege the city.
entries.literal: Shizong dispatched Gao Yue, Murong Shaozong, Liu Feng, and others to lead troops and besiege the city.

entries.zh: 復詔金督彭樂、可朱渾道元等出屯河陽，斷其奔救之路。
entries.en: An edict again ordered Hulü Jin to supervise Peng Le, Kezhuhun Daoyuan, and others in going out to encamp at Heyang and cut off their route of rescue.
entries.literal: An edict again ordered Jin to supervise Peng Le, Kezhuhun Daoyuan, and others in going out to encamp at Heyang and cut off their route of rescue.

entries.zh: 又詔金率衆會攻潁川。
entries.en: An edict again ordered Hulü Jin to lead troops to join the attack on Yingchuan.
entries.literal: An edict again ordered Jin to lead troops to join the attack on Yingchuan.

entries.zh: 事平，復使金率衆從崿阪送米宜陽。
entries.en: When the affair was settled, Hulü Jin was again sent to lead troops from Eban to transport grain to Yiyang.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled, Jin was again sent to lead troops from Eban to transport grain to Yiyang.

entries.zh: 西魏九曲戍將馬紹隆據險要鬭，金破之。
entries.en: The Western Wei commander of Jiuchu Fort, Ma Shaolong, held a strategic pass and fought; Hulü Jin defeated him.
entries.literal: The Western Wei commander of Jiuchu Fort, Ma Shaolong, held a strategic pass and fought; Jin defeated him.

entries.zh: 以功別封安平縣男。
entries.en: For merit he was separately enfeoffed baron of Anping County.
entries.literal: For merit he was separately enfeoffed Baron of Anping County.

entries.zh: 光，字明月，少工騎射，以武藝知名。
entries.en: Guang, styled Mingyue, from youth was skilled at riding and archery and was renowned for martial prowess.
entries.literal: Guang, styled Mingyue, from youth was skilled at riding and archery and was renowned for martial prowess.

entries.zh: 魏末，從金西征，周文帝長史莫孝暉時在行間，光馳馬射中之，因擒於陣，光時年十七。
entries.en: At the end of Wei, he followed Hulü Jin on the western campaign; Yuwen Tai's chief administrator Mo Xiaohui was then in the ranks; Hulü Guang galloped forward and shot him, then captured him on the field — Guang was then seventeen.
entries.literal: At the end of Wei, he followed Jin on the western campaign; the Zhou Emperor Wen's chief administrator Mo Xiaohui was then in the ranks; Guang galloped forward and shot him, then captured him on the field — Guang was then seventeen.

entries.zh: 高祖嘉之，即擢為都督。
entries.en: Gao Huan praised this and at once promoted Hulü Guang to grand commander.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor praised this and at once promoted him to grand commander.

entries.zh: 世宗為世子，引為親信都督，稍遷征虜將軍，累加衛將軍。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng was heir apparent, Hulü Guang was brought in as a trusted commander; he was gradually promoted to general who represses barbarians and cumulatively advanced to general of the guard.
entries.literal: When Shizong was heir apparent, he was brought in as a trusted commander; he was gradually promoted to General Who Represses Barbarians and cumulatively advanced to General of the Guard.

entries.zh: 武定五年，封永樂縣子。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Wuding, he was enfeoffed viscount of Yongle County.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Wuding, he was enfeoffed Viscount of Yongle County.

entries.zh: 嘗從世宗於洹橋校獵，見一大鳥，雲表飛颺，光引弓射之，正中其頸。
entries.en: Once he followed Gao Cheng in a hunt at Huan Bridge; he saw a great bird soaring above the clouds; Hulü Guang drew his bow and shot it, striking it square in the neck.
entries.literal: Once he followed Shizong in a hunt at Huan Bridge; he saw a great bird soaring above the clouds; Guang drew his bow and shot it, striking it square in the neck.

entries.zh: 此鳥形如車輪，旋轉而下，至地，乃大雕也。
entries.en: The bird was the size of a wheel; it spun downward to earth — it was a great eagle.
entries.literal: The bird was the size of a wheel; it spun downward to earth — it was a great eagle.

entries.zh: 世宗取而觀之，深壯異焉。
entries.en: Gao Cheng took it to look at it and was deeply struck by the marvel.
entries.literal: Shizong took it to look at it and was deeply struck by the marvel.

entries.zh: 丞相屬邢子高見而嘆曰：「此射雕手也。」
entries.en: Xing Zichao, an aide in the chancellor's office, saw it and sighed, "This is an eagle-shooter."
entries.literal: Xing Zichao, an aide in the chancellor's office, saw it and sighed, "This is an eagle-shooter."

entries.zh: 當時傳號落雕都督。
entries.en: At the time he was known by the sobriquet Commander Who Drops Eagles.
entries.literal: At the time he was known by the sobriquet Commander Who Drops Eagles.

entries.zh: 尋兼左衛將軍，進爵為伯。
entries.en: Soon he also served as left general of the guard and his rank was advanced to baron.
entries.literal: Soon he also served as Left General of the Guard and his rank was advanced to baron.

entries.zh: 光入，常在朝堂垂簾而坐。
entries.en: When Guang entered court he would often sit behind the hanging curtain in the hall of audience.
entries.literal: When Guang entered court he would often sit behind the hanging curtain in the hall of audience.

entries.zh: 祖珽不知，乘馬過其前。
entries.en: Zu Ting did not know and rode past in front of him.
entries.literal: Zu Ting did not know and rode his horse past in front of him.

entries.zh: 光怒，謂人曰：「此人乃敢爾！」
entries.en: Guang was furious and said to others, "This man dares behave so!"
entries.literal: Guang was angry and said to others, "This man dares behave so!"

entries.zh: 後珽在內省，言聲高慢，光適過，聞之，又怒。
entries.en: Later Ting was in the inner secretariat speaking in a loud, insolent voice. Guang happened to pass by, heard it, and grew angry again.
entries.literal: Later Ting was in the inner secretariat speaking in a loud, insolent voice; Guang happened to pass by, heard it, and was angry again.

entries.zh: 珽知光忿，而賂光從奴而問之曰：「相王瞋孝徵耶？」
entries.en: Ting knew Guang's wrath and bribed one of Guang's attendants to ask, "Is the Prince angry with Xiaozheng?"
entries.literal: Ting knew Guang's wrath and bribed one of Guang's attendants to ask, "Is the Prince angry with Xiaozheng?"

entries.zh: 曰：「自公用事，相王每夜抱膝嘆曰：『盲人入，國必破矣！』」
entries.en: The answer came: "Since you took power, the Prince every night sits hugging his knees and sighs, ‘The blind man has entered; the state is sure to fall!’"
entries.literal: The answer came: "Since you took power, the Prince every night sits hugging his knees and sighs, ‘The blind man has entered; the state is sure to fall!’"

entries.zh: 穆提婆求娶光庶女，不許。
entries.en: Mu Tipo asked to marry Guang's concubine-born daughter; permission was refused.
entries.literal: Mu Tipo asked to marry Guang's concubine-born daughter; permission was refused.

entries.zh: 帝賜提婆晉陽之田，光言於朝曰：「此田神武帝以來常種禾，飼馬數千匹，以擬寇難，今賜提婆，無乃闕軍務也？」
entries.en: The emperor bestowed on Tipo fields at Jinyang. Guang said at court, "These fields since the Shenwu Emperor have always been sown with grain to feed several thousand horses against enemy raids. To give them to Tipo now — will this not cripple military affairs?"
entries.literal: The emperor bestowed on Tipo fields at Jinyang; Guang said at court, "These fields since the Shenwu Emperor have always been sown with grain to feed several thousand horses against enemy raids. To give them to Tipo now — will this not cripple military affairs?"

entries.zh: 由是祖、穆積怨。
entries.en: From this Zu and Mu nursed deep resentment.
entries.literal: From this Zu and Mu nursed deep resentment.

entries.zh: 羨，字豐樂，少有機警，尤善射藝，高祖見而稱之。
entries.en: Xian, styled Fengle, was quick-witted from youth and especially skilled in archery; Gao Huan saw him and praised him.
entries.literal: Xian, styled Fengle, from youth was quick-witted and especially skilled in archery; the Grand Ancestor saw him and praised him.

entries.zh: 世宗擢為開府參軍事。
entries.en: Gao Cheng promoted him to staff officer of Kaifu.
entries.literal: Shizong promoted him to staff officer of Kaifu.

entries.zh: 遷征虜將軍、中散大夫，加安西將軍，進封大夏縣子，除通州刺史。
entries.en: He was transferred to general who captures barbarians and palace attendant, additionally made general who pacifies the west, advanced in enfeoffment to viscount of Daxia County, and made governor of Tong Province.
entries.literal: He was transferred to General Who Captures Barbarians and Palace Attendant, additionally made General Who Pacifies the West, advanced in enfeoffment to Viscount of Daxia County, and made Governor of Tong Province.

entries.zh: 顯祖受禮，進號征西，別封顯親縣伯。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication, Xian's title was advanced to general who campaigns west and he was separately enfeoffed baron of Xianqin County.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication, Xian's title was advanced to General Who Campaigns West and he was separately enfeoffed Baron of Xianqin County.

entries.zh: 金兄平，便弓馬，有幹用。
entries.en: Jin's elder brother Ping was skilled with bow and horse and had real capacity for command.
entries.literal: Jin's elder brother Ping was skilled with bow and horse and possessed practical ability.

entries.zh: 魏景明中，釋褐殿中將軍，遷襄威將軍。
entries.en: In the Jingming era of Wei he entered service as a palace guard general and was transferred to Xiangwei General.
entries.literal: During the Jingming era of Wei he entered service as a palace guard general and was transferred to Xiangwei General.

entries.zh: 正光末，六鎮擾亂，隸大將軍尉賓北討。
entries.en: At the end of Zhengguang, when the six garrisons fell into turmoil, he served under Grand General Yu Bin on the northern campaign.
entries.literal: At the end of Zhengguang, when the six garrisons rose in turmoil, he served under Grand General Yu Bin on the northern campaign.

entries.zh: 軍敗，為賊所虜。
entries.en: The army was defeated and he was taken by the rebels.
entries.literal: The army was defeated and he was captured by the rebels.

entries.zh: 後走奔其弟金於雲州，進號龍驤將軍。
entries.en: Later he fled to his brother Jin at Yunzhou and was advanced to Dragon-Tiger General.
entries.literal: Later he fled to join his brother Jin at Yunzhou and was advanced to rank as Dragon-Tiger General.

entries.zh: 與金擁衆南出，至黃瓜堆，為杜洛周所破，部落離散。
entries.en: With Jin he led their following south. At Huangguadui they were broken by Du Luozhou and their tribes scattered.
entries.literal: With Jin he led their following south; at Huangguadui they were routed by Du Luozhou and their tribes scattered.

entries.zh: 及歸尒朱榮，待之甚厚，以平襲父爵第一領民酋長。
entries.en: When they returned to Erzhu Rong, he was treated with great favor, and Ping inherited their father's title as First Chieftain of Registered Tribal Peoples.
entries.literal: When they returned to Erzhu Rong, he was treated with great favor, and Ping inherited their father's title as First Chieftain of Registered Tribal Peoples.

entries.zh: 高祖起義，以都督從。
entries.en: When Gao Huan raised the righteous cause, Ping followed him as a commander.
entries.literal: When Gaozu raised the righteous cause, Ping followed as a commander.

entries.zh: 稍遷平北將軍、顯州刺史，加鎮南將軍，封固安縣伯。
entries.en: He was gradually promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xian Province, was additionally made General Who Pacifies the South, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Gu'an County.
entries.literal: He was gradually promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xian Province, additionally General Who Pacifies the South, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Gu'an County.

entries.zh: 尋進為侯，行肆州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he was advanced to marquis and acted as Inspector of Si Province.
entries.literal: Soon he was advanced to marquis and acted as Inspector of Si Province.

entries.zh: 周文帝遣其右將軍李小光據梁州，平以偏師討擒之。
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Zhou sent his Right General Li Xiaoguang to occupy Liang Province; Ping campaigned with a detached force and captured him.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou sent his Right General Li Xiaoguang to occupy Liang Province; Ping campaigned with a detached force and captured him.

entries.zh: 出為燕州刺史。
entries.en: He went out as Inspector of Yan Province.
entries.literal: He went out as Inspector of Yan Province.

entries.zh: 入兼左衛將軍，領衆一萬討北徐賊，破之，除濟州刺史。
entries.en: He entered court as acting Left Guard General, led ten thousand troops to attack the Northern Xu rebels, defeated them, and was appointed Inspector of Ji Province.
entries.literal: He entered court as acting Left Guard General, led ten thousand troops to attack the Northern Xu rebels, defeated them, and was appointed Inspector of Ji Province.

entries.zh: 侯景度江，詔平為大都督，率青州刺史敬顯俊、左衛將軍厙狄伏連等略定壽陽、宿預三十餘城。
entries.en: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi, Ping was appointed Grand Commander and led Inspector of Qing Province Jing Xianjun, Left Guard General Kudi Fulian, and others in securing more than thirty cities, including Shouyang and Suyu.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi, an edict made Ping Grand Commander; he led Inspector of Qing Province Jing Xianjun, Left Guard General Kudi Fulian, and others in taking and pacifying more than thirty cities including Shouyang and Suyu.

entries.zh: 事罷還州，加開府，進位驃騎大將軍，進爵為公。
entries.en: After the campaign ended he returned to his province, received Opening Office, was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, and advanced in rank to duke.
entries.literal: When the affair was over he returned to his province, was granted Opening Office, advanced to General of Agile Cavalry, and advanced in rank to duke.

entries.zh: 顯祖受禪，別封羨陽侯。
entries.en: When Xianzu received the abdication, Ping was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Xianyang.
entries.literal: When Xianzu received the abdication, Ping was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Xianyang.

entries.zh: 行兗州刺史，以黷貨除名。
entries.en: While acting as Inspector of Yan Province, he was dismissed from office for corruption.
entries.literal: Acting as Inspector of Yan Province, he was removed from the rolls for corruption.

entries.zh: 後除開府儀同三司。
entries.en: Later he was appointed Opening Office with the same honors as the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed Opening Office with the same honors as the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，拜特進，食滄州樂陵郡幹。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, Ping was appointed Specially Advanced and given income from Leling Commandery in Cang Province.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended the throne, he was appointed Specially Advanced and received income from Leling Commandery in Cang Province.

entries.zh: 皇建初，封定陽郡公，拜護軍。
entries.en: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dingyang Commandery and appointed Protector of the Army.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dingyang Commandery and appointed Protector of the Army.

entries.zh: 後為青州刺史，卒。
entries.en: Later he became Inspector of Qing Province and died.
entries.literal: Later he became Inspector of Qing Province and died.

entries.zh: 贈太尉。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：斛律金以高祖撥亂之始，翼成王業，忠款之至，成此大功，故能終享遐年，位高百辟。
entries.en: The historian writes: Hulü Jin, at the outset when Gao Huan was settling the chaos, helped establish the royal enterprise. His loyalty was complete, and so this great achievement was won — thus he lived out his years in full and stood above all the hundred ministers.
entries.literal: The historian writes: Hulü Jin, at the outset when Gao Huan was settling the chaos, helped establish the royal enterprise; his loyalty was complete, and so this great achievement was won — thus he lived out his years in full and stood above all the hundred ministers.

entries.zh: 觀其盈滿之戒，動之微也，才及後嗣，遂至誅夷，雖為威權之重，蓋符道家所忌。
entries.en: Yet see how the warning against overflowing fullness moves in small ways: it had scarcely touched the next generation when execution and extermination followed. Though the weight of power was great, it still matched what the Daoist masters warn against.
entries.literal: Yet see how the warning against overflowing fullness moves in small ways: it had scarcely touched the next generation when execution and extermination followed — though the weight of power was great, it still matched what the Daoist masters warn against.

entries.zh: 光以上將之子，有沈毅之姿，戰術兵權，暗同韜略，臨敵制勝，變化無方。
entries.en: Guang, as the son of a supreme general, bore a grave and resolute bearing. In tactical craft and military command he matched hidden stratagem — facing the enemy he seized victory, shifting without fixed form.
entries.literal: Guang, as the son of a supreme general, bore a grave and resolute bearing; in tactical craft and military command he matched hidden stratagem — facing the enemy he seized victory, shifting without fixed form.

entries.zh: 自關、河分隔，年將四紀。
entries.en: Since the passes and the Yellow River divided the realm, nearly four decades had passed.
entries.literal: Since the passes and the Yellow River divided the realm, nearly four decades had passed.

entries.zh: 以高祖霸王之期，屬宇文草創之日，出軍薄伐，屢挫兵鋒。
entries.en: At the height of Gao Huan's hegemony, in the very days when the Yuwen clan was first founding its state, their armies went forth on punitive raids and again and again blunted the enemy's edge.
entries.literal: At the height of Gao Huan's hegemony, in the very days when the Yuwen clan was first founding its state, their armies went forth on punitive raids and again and again blunted the enemy's edge.

entries.zh: 而大寧以還，東鄰浸弱，關西前收巴蜀，又殄江陵，叶建瓴而用武，成並吞之壯氣。
entries.en: But from the Daning era onward, the eastern neighbor weakened by degrees. In the west they first took Bashu, then destroyed Jiangling — the tide ran downhill for war, and the spirit of annexation gathered strength.
entries.literal: But from the Daning era onward, the eastern neighbor weakened by degrees; in the west they first took Bashu, then destroyed Jiangling — the tide ran downhill for war, and the spirit of annexation gathered strength.

entries.zh: 斛律治軍誓衆，式遏邊鄙，戰則前無完陣，攻則罕有全城，齊氏必致拘原之師，秦人無復啟關之策。
entries.en: The Hulü clan disciplined the army, rallied the host, and held the border fast — in battle no enemy line stood whole; in siege scarcely a city held intact. Qi could always bring the foe to bay; Qin no longer had a plan to force the passes open.
entries.literal: The Hulü clan disciplined the army, rallied the host, and held the border fast — in battle no enemy line stood whole; in siege scarcely a city held intact. Qi could always bring the foe to bay; Qin no longer had a plan to force the passes open.

entries.zh: 而世亂才勝，詐以震主之威；
entries.en: Yet in an age of disorder, talent itself became a triumph — and fraud clothed itself in the majesty that overawes a ruler.
entries.literal: Yet in an age of disorder, talent itself became a triumph — and fraud clothed itself in the majesty that overawes a ruler.

entries.zh: 主暗時艱，自毀藩籬之固。
entries.en: The ruler was dim, the times were hard, and the realm tore down its own ramparts.
entries.literal: The ruler was dim, the times were hard, and the realm tore down its own ramparts.

entries.zh: 昔李牧之為趙將也，北翦胡寇，西卻秦軍，郭開譖之，牧死趙滅。
entries.en: Long ago, when Li Mu served Zhao as general, he cut down the northern raiders and drove back the armies of Qin. Guo Kai slandered him; Li Mu died, and Zhao was destroyed.
entries.literal: Long ago, when Li Mu served Zhao as general, he cut down the northern raiders and drove back the armies of Qin — Guo Kai slandered him; Li Mu died, and Zhao was destroyed.

entries.zh: 其議誅光者，豈秦之反間歟，何同術而同亡也！
entries.en: Were those who counseled Guang's death perhaps Qin's agents of division? Same craft, same ruin!
entries.literal: Were those who counseled Guang's death perhaps Qin's agents of division? Same craft, same ruin!

entries.zh: 內令諸將解體，外為強鄰報讐。
entries.en: Within, they had the generals disband; without, they repaid a powerful neighbor's grudge.
entries.literal: Within, they had the generals disband; without, they repaid a powerful neighbor's grudge.

entries.zh: 嗚呼！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 後之君子，可為深戒。
entries.en: Men of later times — let this be a warning deeply taken.
entries.literal: Men of later times — let this be a warning deeply taken.

entries.zh: 斛律金 子光 羨
entries.en: Hulü Jin; son Guang; Xian
entries.literal: Hulü Jin; son Guang; Xian

entries.zh: 孫騰，字龍雀，咸陽石安人也。
entries.en: Sun Teng, styled Longque, was a native of Shi'an in Xianyang.
entries.literal: Sun Teng, styled Longque, was a native of Shi'an in Xianyang.

entries.zh: 祖通，仕沮渠氏為中書舍人，沮渠滅，入魏，因居北邊。
entries.en: His grandfather Tong served the Juqu clan as attendant drafting at the central secretariat; when the Juqu were destroyed he entered Wei and settled on the northern frontier.
entries.literal: His grandfather Tong served the Juqu clan as Attendant Drafting at the Central Secretariat; when the Juqu were destroyed he entered Wei and settled on the northern frontier.

entries.zh: 及騰貴，魏朝贈通使持節、侍中、都督雍華岐幽四州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、司徒公、尚書左僕射、雍州刺史，贈騰父機使持節、侍中、都督冀定滄瀛殷五州諸軍事、太尉公、尚書令、冀州刺史。
entries.en: When Sun Teng rose high, the Wei court posthumously granted his grandfather Tong bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the four provinces of Yong, Hua, Qi, and You, grand general of agile cavalry, duke over the masses, left vice director of the masters of writing, and governor of Yong Province; his father Ji was posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, and Yin, grand commandant, director of the masters of writing, and governor of Ji Province.
entries.literal: When Teng rose high, the Wei court posthumously granted Tong Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the four provinces of Yong, Hua, Qi, and You, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Duke over the Masses, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yong Province; Teng's father Ji was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, and Yin, Grand Commandant, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Ji Province.

entries.zh: 騰少而質直，明解吏事。
entries.en: From youth Sun Teng was honest and straightforward, with a clear grasp of administrative affairs.
entries.literal: Teng from youth was honest and straightforward, and clearly understood administrative affairs.

entries.zh: 魏正光中，北方擾亂，騰間關危險，得達秀容。
entries.en: In the Zhenguang era of Wei, when the north was in turmoil, Sun Teng threaded through danger and peril and reached Xiurong.
entries.literal: In the Zhenguang era of Wei, when the north was in turmoil, Teng threaded through danger and peril and reached Xiurong.

entries.zh: 屬尒朱榮建義，騰隋榮入洛，例除冗從僕射。
entries.en: When Erzhu Rong raised righteousness, Sun Teng followed him into Luoyang and by precedent was made supernumerary vice master of attendants.
entries.literal: When Erzhu Rong raised righteousness, Teng followed Rong into Luoyang and by precedent was made Supernumerary Vice Master of Attendants.

entries.zh: 尋為高祖都督府長史，從高祖東征邢杲。
entries.en: Soon he became chief clerk of Gao Huan's headquarters and followed Gao Huan east to campaign against Xing Gao.
entries.literal: Soon he became chief clerk of the Grand Ancestor's headquarters and followed the Grand Ancestor east to campaign against Xing Gao.

entries.zh: 師次齊城，有撫宜鎮軍人謀逆，將害督帥。
entries.en: When the army halted at Qi city, soldiers of the Fu Yi garrison plotted rebellion and were about to kill the commander.
entries.literal: When the army halted at Qi city, soldiers of the Fu Yi garrison plotted rebellion and were about to kill the commander.

entries.zh: 騰知之，密啟高祖。
entries.en: Sun Teng learned of it and secretly reported to Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Teng learned of it and secretly reported to the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 俄頃事發，高祖以有備，擒破之。
entries.en: Before long the affair broke out; because Gao Huan was prepared, he captured and crushed them.
entries.literal: Before long the affair broke out; because the Grand Ancestor was prepared, he captured and crushed them.

entries.zh: 高祖之為晉州，騰為長史，加後將軍，封石安縣伯。
entries.en: When Gao Huan became governor of Jin Province, Sun Teng served as chief clerk, was additionally made rear general, and was enfeoffed baron of Shi'an County.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor became governor of Jin Province, Teng served as chief clerk, was additionally made Rear General, and was enfeoffed Baron of Shi'an County.

entries.zh: 高祖自晉陽出滏口，行至襄垣，尒朱兆率衆追。
entries.en: When Gao Huan left Jinyang by Fukou and marched to Xiangyuan, Erzhu Zhao led troops in pursuit.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor left Jinyang by Fukou and marched to Xiangyuan, Erzhu Zhao led troops in pursuit.

entries.zh: 高祖與兆宴飲於水湄，誓為兄弟，各還本營。
entries.en: Gao Huan and Zhao feasted and drank at the water's edge, swore brotherhood, and each returned to his own camp.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor and Zhao feasted and drank at the water's edge, swore brotherhood, and each returned to his own camp.

entries.zh: 明旦，兆復招高祖，高祖欲安其意，將赴之，臨上馬，騰牽衣止之。
entries.en: Next day Zhao summoned Gao Huan again; Gao Huan wished to reassure him and was about to ride to him, but as he was mounting his horse Sun Teng seized his robe and held him back.
entries.literal: Next day Zhao again summoned the Grand Ancestor; the Grand Ancestor wished to reassure him and was about to go, but as he was mounting his horse Teng seized his robe and stopped him.

entries.zh: 兆乃隔水肆罵，馳還晉陽。
entries.en: Zhao cursed him from across the river and galloped back to Jinyang.
entries.literal: Zhao then railed wantonly across the water and galloped back to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 高祖遂東。
entries.en: Gao Huan thereupon marched east.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor thereupon marched east.

entries.zh: 及起義信都，騰以誠款，常預謀策。
entries.en: When Gao Huan raised righteousness at Xindu, Sun Teng for his loyalty and sincerity was constantly included in planning.
entries.literal: When he raised righteousness at Xindu, Teng for his loyalty and sincerity was constantly included in planning.

entries.zh: 騰以朝廷隔絕，號令無所歸，不權有所立，則衆將沮散，苦請於高祖。
entries.en: Sun Teng argued that with the court cut off, commands had nowhere to attach; if they did not provisionally establish a ruler, the army would lose heart and scatter — he urgently pleaded with Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Teng held that with the court cut off and isolated, commands had nowhere to attach; if they did not provisionally establish someone, the multitude would lose heart and scatter — he urgently pleaded with the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 高祖從之，遂立中興主。
entries.en: Gao Huan followed his counsel and thereupon established the restoration sovereign.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor followed his counsel and thereupon established the restoration sovereign.

entries.zh: 除侍中，尋加使持節、六州流民大都督、北道大行臺。
entries.en: Sun Teng was made palace attendant, and soon additionally bearer of the staff of authority, grand commander of displaced populations in six provinces, and grand chief of the northern circuit.
entries.literal: Teng was made Palace Attendant, and soon additionally Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commander of Displaced Populations in Six Provinces, and Grand Chief of the Northern Circuit.

entries.zh: 高祖進軍於鄴，初留段榮守信都，尋遣榮鎮中山，仍令騰居守。
entries.en: When Gao Huan marched on Ye, at first he left Duan Rong to hold Xindu; soon he sent Rong to garrison Zhongshan and still had Sun Teng remain to guard the city.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor marched on Ye, at first he left Duan Rong to hold Xindu; soon he sent Rong to garrison Zhongshan and still had Teng remain to guard the city.

entries.zh: 及平鄴，授相州刺史，改封咸陽郡公，增邑通前一千三百戶，入為侍中。
entries.en: When Ye was pacified, Sun Teng was appointed governor of Xiang Province, his title was changed to duke of Xianyang Commandery with a fief increased to one thousand three hundred households in all, and he entered court as palace attendant.
entries.literal: When Ye was pacified, Teng was appointed Governor of Xiang Province, his title was changed to Duke of Xianyang Commandery, his fief was increased to one thousand three hundred households in all, and he entered court as Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 時魏京兆王愉女平原公主寡居，騰欲尚之，公主不許。
entries.en: At that time the daughter of Prince Yu of Jingzhao, Princess Pingyuan, was widowed and living alone; Sun Teng wished to marry her, but the princess refused.
entries.literal: At that time the daughter of Prince Yu of Jingzhao, Princess Pingyuan, was widowed and living alone; Teng wished to marry her, but the princess refused.

entries.zh: 侍中封隆之無婦，公主欲之，騰妬隆之，遂相間構。
entries.en: Palace attendant Feng Longzhi had no wife, and the princess wished to marry him; Sun Teng, jealous of Longzhi, then sowed discord between them.
entries.literal: Palace Attendant Feng Longzhi had no wife, and the princess wished to marry him; Teng, jealous of Longzhi, then sowed discord between them.

entries.zh: 高祖啟免騰官，請除外任，俄而復之。
entries.en: Gao Huan memorialized to dismiss Sun Teng from office and requested that he be sent out on external appointment; before long he was restored.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor memorialized to dismiss Teng from office and requested that he be sent out on external appointment; before long he was restored.

entries.zh: 子如少機警，有口辯。
entries.en: Ziru from youth was quick-witted and had a gift for speech.
entries.literal: Ziru from youth was quick-witted and had a gift for speech.

entries.zh: 好交遊豪傑，與高祖相結托，分義甚深。
entries.en: He loved to befriend bold heroes and formed a deep bond of mutual trust with Gao Huan.
entries.literal: He loved to befriend bold heroes and formed a deep bond of mutual trust with the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 孝昌中，北州淪陷，子如攜家口南奔肆州，為尒朱榮所禮遇，假以中軍。
entries.en: In Xiaochang, when the northern provinces fell, Ziru led his household south to Si Province and was treated with honor by Erzhu Rong, who made him acting commander of the middle army.
entries.literal: In Xiaochang, when the northern provinces fell, Ziru led his household south to Si Province and was treated with honor by Erzhu Rong, who made him acting commander of the middle army.

entries.zh: 榮之向洛也，以子如為司馬、持節、假平南將軍，監前軍。
entries.en: When Rong marched on Luoyang, Ziru was made marshal, given credentials, and appointed acting general who pacifies the south, supervising the vanguard.
entries.literal: When Rong marched on Luoyang, Ziru was made marshal, given credentials, and appointed acting General Who Pacifies the South, supervising the vanguard.

entries.zh: 次高都，榮以建興險阻，往來沖要，有後顧之憂，以子如行建興太守、當郡都督。
entries.en: At Gaodu, Rong — because Jianxing was rugged and lay on a vital route with worries for the rear — made Ziru acting governor of Jianxing and commander of that commandery.
entries.literal: At Gaodu, Rong, because Jianxing was rugged and lay on a vital route with worries for the rear, made Ziru acting governor of Jianxing and commander of that commandery.

entries.zh: 永安初，封平遙縣子，邑三百戶，仍為大行臺郎中。
entries.en: At the beginning of Yongan he was enfeoffed baron of Pingyao County with a fief of three hundred households and continued as director in the Grand Mobilization Office.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongan he was enfeoffed Baron of Pingyao County with a fief of three hundred households and continued as director in the Grand Mobilization Office.

entries.zh: 榮以子如明辯，能說時事，數遣奉使詣闕，多稱旨，孝莊亦接待焉。
entries.en: Rong, because Ziru was clear in argument and could speak to the affairs of the time, often sent him on missions to court, where he mostly pleased the throne; Emperor Xiaozhuang also received him warmly.
entries.literal: Rong, because Ziru was clear in argument and could speak to the affairs of the time, often sent him on missions to court, where he mostly pleased the throne; Emperor Xiaozhuang also received him warmly.

entries.zh: 葛榮之亂，相州孤危，榮遣子如間行入鄴，助加防守。
entries.en: When Ge Rong's rebellion broke out and Xiang Province stood isolated and perilous, Rong sent Ziru by secret route into Ye to help strengthen its defense.
entries.literal: When Ge Rong's rebellion broke out and Xiang Province stood isolated and perilous, Rong sent Ziru by secret route into Ye to help strengthen its defense.

entries.zh: 葛榮平，進爵為侯。
entries.en: When Ge Rong was pacified, his rank was advanced to marquis.
entries.literal: When Ge Rong was pacified, his rank was advanced to marquis.

entries.zh: 元顥入洛，人情離阻，以子如曾守鄴城，頗有恩信，乃令行相州事。
entries.en: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang and hearts were divided, because Ziru had once held Ye and had some grace and trust there, he was ordered to administer Xiang Province.
entries.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang and hearts were divided and obstructed, because Ziru had once held Ye and had some grace and trust there, he was ordered to administer Xiang Province.

entries.zh: 顥平，徵為金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: When Hao was pacified, he was summoned as minister of splendid honors.
entries.literal: When Hao was pacified, he was summoned as Minister of Splendid Honors.

entries.zh: 尒朱榮之誅，子如知有變，自宮內突出，至榮宅，棄家隨榮妻子與尒朱世隆等走出京城。
entries.en: When Erzhu Rong was executed, Ziru knew there had been a coup. He burst out from within the palace, went to Rong's residence, abandoned his household, and followed Rong's wife and children with Erzhu Shilong and others in fleeing the capital.
entries.literal: When Erzhu Rong was executed, Ziru knew there had been a coup; he burst out from within the palace, went to Rong's residence, abandoned his household, and followed Rong's wife and children with Erzhu Shilong and others in fleeing the capital.

entries.zh: 世隆便欲還北，子如曰：「事貴應機，兵不厭詐，天下恟恟，唯強是視，於此際會，不可以弱示人。
entries.en: Shilong wished at once to return north, but Ziru said, "In affairs, what matters is seizing the moment; in war, deception is not to be despised. The realm is in uproar — all look only to strength. At a juncture like this, one cannot show weakness.
entries.literal: Shilong wished at once to return north, but Ziru said, "In affairs, what matters is seizing the moment; in war, deception is not to be despised. The realm is in uproar — all look only to strength. At a juncture like this, one cannot show weakness.

entries.zh: 若必走北，即恐變故隨起，不如分兵守河橋，迴軍向京，出其不意，或可離潰。
entries.en: If we must flee north, I fear upheaval will follow at once. Better to divide the army to hold Heqiao, turn the host back toward the capital, and strike where they do not expect it — perhaps we can break and scatter them.
entries.literal: If we must flee north, I fear upheaval will follow at once. Better to divide the army to hold Heqiao, turn the host back toward the capital, and strike where they do not expect it — perhaps we can break and scatter them.

entries.zh: 假不如心，猶足示有餘力，使天下觀聽，懼我威強。」
entries.en: Even if it does not go as we wish, it will still show that we have strength to spare and make the realm look on in fear of our might."
entries.literal: Even if it does not go as we wish, it will still show that we have strength to spare and make the realm look on in fear of our might."

entries.zh: 於是世隆還逼京城。
entries.en: Thereupon Shilong turned back and pressed on the capital.
entries.literal: Thereupon Shilong turned back and pressed on the capital.

entries.zh: 魏長廣王立，兼尚書右僕射。
entries.en: When the Northern Wei Prince of Changguang was enthroned, Sima Ziru concurrently served as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: When the Northern Wei Prince of Changguang was enthroned, Ziru concurrently served as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 前廢帝以為侍中、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，進爵陽平郡公，邑一千七百戶。
entries.en: The Deposed Emperor made him attendant-in-ordinary, grand cavalry general, and commissioner with protocol equal to the Three Dukes, advancing his enfeoffment to duke of Yangping Commandery with a fief of one thousand seven hundred households.
entries.literal: The Deposed Emperor made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Cavalry General, and Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes, advancing his enfeoffment to Duke of Yangping Commandery with a fief of one thousand seven hundred households.

entries.zh: 固讓儀同不受。
entries.en: He firmly declined the protocol rank and would not accept it.
entries.literal: He firmly declined the protocol rank and would not accept it.

entries.zh: 高祖起義信都，世隆等知子如與高祖有舊，疑慮，出為南岐州刺史。
entries.en: When Gao Huan raised the righteous banner at Xindu, Shilong and the others, knowing Ziru had old ties with Gao Huan, were suspicious and sent him out as governor of Nanqi Province.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised the righteous banner at Xindu, Shilong and the others, knowing Ziru had old ties with the Grand Ancestor, were suspicious and sent him out as governor of Nanqi Province.

entries.zh: 子如憤恨，泣涕自陳，而不獲免。
entries.en: Ziru, resentful and indignant, wept and pleaded his case, but could not escape removal.
entries.literal: Ziru, resentful and indignant, wept and pleaded his case, but could not escape removal.

entries.zh: 高祖入洛，子如遣使啟賀，仍敘平生舊恩。
entries.en: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, Ziru sent envoys to offer congratulations and again recalled their lifelong old kindness.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor entered Luoyang, Ziru sent envoys to offer congratulations and again recalled their lifelong old kindness.

entries.zh: 尋追赴京，以為大行臺尚書，朝夕左右，參知軍國。
entries.en: Soon he was summoned to the capital and made director in the Grand Mobilization Secretariat, attending day and night at Gao Huan's side and taking part in military and state affairs.
entries.literal: Soon he was summoned to the capital and made Director in the Grand Mobilization Secretariat, attending day and night at the Grand Ancestor's side and taking part in military and state affairs.

entries.zh: 天平初，除左僕射，與侍中高岳、侍中孫騰、右僕射高隆之等共知朝政，甚見信重。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianping he was made vice director of the left and, together with attendant-in-ordinary Gao Yue, attendant-in-ordinary Sun Teng, and vice director of the right Gao Longzhi, jointly managed court affairs; he was greatly trusted and honored.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was made Vice Director of the Left and, together with Attendant-in-Ordinary Gao Yue, Attendant-in-Ordinary Sun Teng, and Vice Director of the Right Gao Longzhi, jointly managed court affairs; he was greatly trusted and honored.

entries.zh: 高祖鎮晉陽，子如時往謁見，待之甚厚，並坐同食，從旦達暮，及其當還，高祖及武明後俱有賚遺，率以為常。
entries.en: When Gao Huan held Jinyang, Ziru would from time to time go to audience and was treated with great kindness — they sat together and ate from morning until evening. When it was time for him to return, Gao Huan and Empress Wuming both sent gifts; this became the rule.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor held Jinyang, Ziru would from time to time go to audience; he was treated with great kindness — they sat together and ate from morning until evening. When it was time for him to return, the Grand Ancestor and Empress Wuming both sent gifts; this became the rule.

entries.zh: 騰以高祖腹心，入居門下，與斛斯椿同掌機密。
entries.en: Because Sun Teng was Gao Huan's trusted confidant, he entered and dwelt in the secretariat, and together with Husi Chun managed confidential affairs.
entries.literal: Because Teng was the Grand Ancestor's trusted confidant, he entered and dwelt in the Secretariat, and together with Husi Chun managed confidential affairs.

entries.zh: 椿既生異端，觸塗乖謬。
entries.en: Chun then harbored divergent designs and went astray at every turn.
entries.literal: Chun then harbored divergent designs and went astray at every turn.

entries.zh: 騰深見猜忌，慮禍及己，遂潛將十餘騎馳赴晉陽。
entries.en: Sun Teng saw that he was deeply suspected, feared disaster would reach him, and secretly led more than ten horsemen in a dash to Jinyang.
entries.literal: Teng saw deeply that he was suspected, feared disaster would reach him, and secretly led more than ten horsemen in a dash to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 高祖入討斛斯椿，留騰行幷州事，又使騰為冀相殷定滄瀛幽安八州行臺僕射、行冀州事，復行相州事。
entries.en: When Gao Huan entered to punish Husi Chun, he left Sun Teng to administer Bing Province affairs; he also had Teng serve as vice master of the mobile office for the eight provinces of Ji, Xiang, Yin, Ding, Cang, Ying, You, and An, administering Ji Province affairs, and again administering Xiang Province affairs.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor entered to punish Husi Chun, he left Teng to administer Bing Province affairs; he also had Teng serve as Vice Master of the Mobile Office for the eight provinces of Ji, Xiang, Yin, Ding, Cang, Ying, You, and An, administering Ji Province affairs, and again administering Xiang Province affairs.

entries.zh: 天平初，入為尚書左僕射，內外之事，騰咸知之，兼司空、尚書令。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianping, Sun Teng entered court as left vice director of the masters of writing; in internal and external affairs he knew all, and concurrently held minister of works and director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, Teng entered court as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; in internal and external affairs Teng knew all, and concurrently held Minister of Works and Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 時西魏遣將寇南兗，詔騰為南道行臺，率諸將討之。
entries.en: At that time Western Wei sent generals to raid Southern Yan Province; an edict made Sun Teng grand chief of the southern circuit and ordered him to lead the generals in suppressing them.
entries.literal: At that time Western Wei sent generals to raid Southern Yan Province; an edict made Teng Grand Chief of the Southern Circuit and ordered him to lead the generals in suppressing them.

entries.zh: 騰性尫怯，無威略，失利而還。
entries.en: Sun Teng by nature was feeble and timid, without martial prestige or strategy; he lost the battle and returned.
entries.literal: Teng by nature was feeble and timid, without martial prestige or strategy; he lost the battle and returned.

entries.zh: 又除司徒。
entries.en: He was again made minister over the masses.
entries.literal: He was again made Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 初北境亂離，亡一女，及貴，遠加推訪，終不得，疑其為人婢賤。
entries.en: At first, when the northern frontier was in turmoil, he lost a daughter; when he rose high he searched for her far and wide but never found her, and suspected she had become someone's slave.
entries.literal: At first, when the northern frontier was in turmoil, he lost a daughter; when he rose high he searched for her far and wide but never found her, and suspected she had become someone's slave.

entries.zh: 及為司徒，奴婢訴良者，不研虛實，率皆免之，願免千人，冀得其女。
entries.en: When he became minister over the masses, slaves and maidservants claiming to be free persons — without investigating truth or falsehood — were in every case freed; he hoped to free a thousand persons and thereby recover his daughter.
entries.literal: When he became Minister over the Masses, slaves and maidservants claiming to be free persons — without investigating truth or falsehood — were in every case freed; he hoped to free a thousand persons and thereby recover his daughter.

entries.zh: 時高祖入朝，左右有言之者，高祖大怒，解其司徒。
entries.en: At that time Gao Huan entered court, and those around him spoke of it; Gao Huan was greatly angered and removed him from the ministry.
entries.literal: At that time the Grand Ancestor entered court, and those around him spoke of it; the Grand Ancestor was greatly angered and removed him from the ministry.

entries.zh: 武定中，使於青州，括浮逃戶口，遷太保。
entries.en: In the Wuding era he was sent to Qing Province to register floating and absentee households, and was transferred to grand preceptor.
entries.literal: In the Wuding era he was sent to Qing Province to register floating and absentee households, and was transferred to Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 初，博陵崔孝芬取貧家子賈氏以為養女，孝芬死，其妻元更適鄭伯猷，攜賈於鄭氏。
entries.en: At first, Cui Xiaofen of Boling took a poor family's daughter of the Jia clan as a foster daughter; when Xiaofen died, his wife Yuan remarried Zheng Boyou and took Jia with her to the Zheng household.
entries.literal: At first, Cui Xiaofen of Boling took a poor family's daughter of the Jia clan as a foster daughter; when Xiaofen died, his wife Yuan remarried Zheng Boyou and took Jia with her to the Zheng household.

entries.zh: 賈有姿色，騰納之，始以為妾。
entries.en: Jia was beautiful in appearance; Sun Teng took her in and at first made her a concubine.
entries.literal: Jia was beautiful in appearance; Teng took her in and at first made her a concubine.

entries.zh: 其妻袁氏死，騰以賈有子，正以為妻，詔封丹陽郡君，復請以袁氏爵迴授其女。
entries.en: When his wife Lady Yuan died, Sun Teng because Jia had borne a son formally made her his wife; an edict enfeoffed her as lady of Danyang Commandery, and he again requested that Lady Yuan's title be transferred to her daughter.
entries.literal: When his wife Lady Yuan died, Teng because Jia had borne a son formally made her his wife; an edict enfeoffed her as Lady of Danyang Commandery, and he again requested that Lady Yuan's title be transferred to her daughter.

entries.zh: 違禮肆情，多此類也。
entries.en: Disregarding ritual and indulging desire — there were many cases of this kind.
entries.literal: Disregarding ritual and indulging desire — there were many cases of this kind.

entries.zh: 騰早依附高祖，契闊艱危，勤力恭謹，深見信待。
entries.en: Sun Teng early attached himself to Gao Huan; through hardship and danger he labored diligently with respectful care and was deeply trusted and favored.
entries.literal: Teng early attached himself to the Grand Ancestor; through hardship and danger he labored diligently with respectful care and was deeply trusted and favored.

entries.zh: 及高祖置之魏朝，寄以心腹，遂志氣驕盈，與奪由己，求納財賄，不知紀極。
entries.en: When Gao Huan placed him in the Wei court and entrusted him as a confidant, his spirit grew proud and overbearing; granting and taking were at his own will, and he sought bribes beyond reckoning.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor placed him in the Wei court and entrusted him as a confidant, his spirit grew proud and overbearing; granting and taking were at his own will, and he sought bribes beyond reckoning.

entries.zh: 生官死贈，非貨不行，餚藏銀器，盜為家物，親狎小人，專為聚斂。
entries.en: Offices in life, posthumous gifts in death — none were granted without payment; stored silver vessels from tribute feasts he stole as household goods; he consorted closely with petty men and devoted himself solely to amassing wealth.
entries.literal: Offices in life, posthumous gifts in death — none were granted without payment; stored silver vessels from tribute feasts he stole as household goods; he consorted closely with petty men and devoted himself solely to amassing wealth.

entries.zh: 在鄴與高岳、高隆之、司馬子如號為四貴，非法專恣，騰為甚焉。
entries.en: At Ye, together with Gao Yue, Gao Longzhi, and Sima Ziru he was called one of the Four Dignitaries; lawless and willful, they did as they pleased — Sun Teng was the worst of them.
entries.literal: At Ye, together with Gao Yue, Gao Longzhi, and Sima Ziru he was called one of the Four Dignitaries; lawless and willful, they did as they pleased — Teng was the worst of them.

entries.zh: 高祖屢加譴讓，終不悛改，朝野深非笑之。
entries.en: Gao Huan repeatedly censured and reproved him, but in the end he would not repent and reform; court and countryside deeply scorned and mocked him.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor repeatedly censured and reproved him, but in the end he would not repent and reform; court and countryside deeply scorned and mocked him.

entries.zh: 武定六年四月薨，時年六十八。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the sixth year of Wuding he died, aged sixty-eight.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year of Wuding he died, aged sixty-eight.

entries.zh: 贈使持節、都督冀定等五州諸軍事、冀州刺史、太師、開府、錄尚書事，諡曰文。
entries.en: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, and the rest, governor of Ji Province, grand preceptor, opener of a government office, and recorder of the affairs of the masters of writing; his posthumous title was Wen.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, and the rest, Governor of Ji Province, Grand Preceptor, Opener of a Government Office, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing; his posthumous title was Wen.

entries.zh: 天保初，以騰佐命，詔祭告其墓。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianbao, because Sun Teng had aided in establishing the mandate, an edict ordered sacrifice announced at his tomb.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, because Teng had aided in establishing the mandate, an edict ordered sacrifice announced at his tomb.

entries.zh: 皇建中，配享高祖廟庭。
entries.en: In the Huangjian era he was given associated sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple court.
entries.literal: In the Huangjian era he was given associated sacrifice in the Grand Ancestor's temple court.

entries.zh: 子鳳珍嗣。
entries.en: His son Fengzhen succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Fengzhen succeeded.

entries.zh: 鳳珍庸暗，武平中，卒於開府儀同三司。
entries.en: Fengzhen was dull and dim; in the Wuping era he died while holding the rank of opener of a government office equal in protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.
entries.literal: Fengzhen was dull and dim; in the Wuping era he died while holding the rank of Opener of a Government Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.

entries.zh: 高隆之，字延興，本姓徐氏，云出自高平金鄉。
entries.en: Gao Longzhi, styled Yanxing, was originally surnamed Xu and claimed descent from Jinxiang in Gaoping.
entries.literal: Gao Longzhi, styled Yanxing, was originally surnamed Xu and claimed descent from Jinxiang in Gaoping.

entries.zh: 父幹，魏白水郡守，為姑婿高氏所養，因從其姓。
entries.en: His father Gan served as Administrator of Baishui Commandery in Wei; he was raised by his aunt's husband, a member of the Gao clan, and therefore took his surname.
entries.literal: His father Gan served as Administrator of Baishui Commandery in Wei; he was raised by his aunt's husband, a member of the Gao clan, and therefore took his surname.

entries.zh: 隆之貴，魏朝贈司徒公、雍州刺史。
entries.en: When Gao Longzhi rose high, the Wei court posthumously granted his father Gan duke over the masses and governor of Yong Province.
entries.literal: When Longzhi rose high, the Wei court posthumously granted Gan Duke over the Masses and Governor of Yong Province.

entries.zh: 隆之後有參議之功，高祖命為從弟，仍云渤海蓚人。
entries.en: Because Gao Longzhi later had merit in deliberation and counsel, Gao Huan ordered that he be treated as a younger cousin and still declared him a man of Tiao in Bohai.
entries.literal: Because Longzhi later had merit in deliberation and counsel, the Grand Ancestor ordered that he be treated as a younger cousin and still declared him a man of Tiao in Bohai.

entries.zh: 隆之身長八尺，美鬚髯，深沈有志氣。
entries.en: Gao Longzhi stood eight feet in height, with a fine beard and whiskers, and was deep and reserved in spirit with strong ambition.
entries.literal: Longzhi stood eight feet in height, with a fine beard and whiskers, and was deep and reserved in spirit with strong ambition.

entries.zh: 魏汝南王悅為司州牧，以為戶曹從事。
entries.en: When Prince Yue of Runan was governor of Si Province, Gao Longzhi was made a clerk in the household bureau.
entries.literal: When Prince Yue of Runan was Governor of Si Province, Longzhi was made a clerk in the household bureau.

entries.zh: 建義初，釋褐員外散騎常侍，與行臺于暉出討羊侃於太山，暉引隆之為行臺郎中，又除給事中。
entries.en: At the beginning of Jianyi, he first received office as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry; with the mobile office of Yu Hui he went out to suppress Yang Kan at Mount Tai; Hui brought Longzhi in as a mobile office director, and Longzhi was additionally made gentlemen attendant.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, he first received office as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; with the mobile office of Yu Hui he went out to suppress Yang Kan at Mount Tai; Hui brought Longzhi in as a mobile office director, and Longzhi was additionally made Gentlemen Attendant.

entries.zh: 與高祖深自結托。
entries.en: He and Gao Huan formed a deep personal bond.
entries.literal: He and the Grand Ancestor formed a deep personal bond.

entries.zh: 高祖之臨晉州，引為治中，行平陽郡事。
entries.en: When Gao Huan came to Jin Province, Gao Longzhi was brought in as administrator and administered Pingyang Commandery affairs.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor came to Jin Province, Longzhi was brought in as administrator and administered Pingyang Commandery affairs.

entries.zh: 從高祖起義山東，以為大行臺右丞。
entries.en: He followed Gao Huan in raising righteousness in Shandong and was made right deputy of the mobile office.
entries.literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in raising righteousness in Shandong and was made right deputy of the mobile office.

entries.zh: 魏中興初，除御史中尉，領尚食典御。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wei Zhongxing, he was made imperial censor and concurrently chief of the imperial kitchen.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wei Zhongxing, he was made Imperial Censor and concurrently Chief of the Imperial Kitchen.

entries.zh: 從高祖平鄴，行相州事。
entries.en: He followed Gao Huan in pacifying Ye and administered Xiang Province affairs.
entries.literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in pacifying Ye and administered Xiang Province affairs.

entries.zh: 從破四胡於韓陵，太昌初，除驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。
entries.en: He followed in the defeat of the four Erzhu at Hanling; at the beginning of Taichang he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Opener of a Government Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.
entries.literal: He followed in the defeat of the four Erzhu at Hanling; at the beginning of Taichang he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Opener of a Government Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.

entries.zh: 西魏文帝曾與隆之因酒忿競，文帝坐以黜免。
entries.en: Western Wei Emperor Wen once quarreled with Gao Longzhi over wine and was dismissed from office as a consequence.
entries.literal: Western Wei Emperor Wen once quarreled with Longzhi over wine; Emperor Wen was dismissed from office for it.

entries.zh: 高祖責隆之不能協和，乃啟出為北道行臺，轉幷州刺史，封平原郡公，邑一千七百戶。
entries.en: Gao Huan blamed Gao Longzhi for failing to keep harmony and memorialized to send him out as grand chief of the northern circuit; he was transferred to governor of Bing Province, enfeoffed duke of Pingyuan Commandery with a fief of one thousand seven hundred households.
