entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor blamed Longzhi for failing to keep harmony and memorialized to send him out as Grand Chief of the Northern Circuit; he was transferred to Governor of Bing Province, enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan Commandery with a fief of one thousand seven hundred households.

entries.zh: 隆之請減戶七百，並求降己四階讓兄騰，並加優詔許之，仍以騰為滄州刺史。
entries.en: Gao Longzhi requested a reduction of seven hundred households in his fief and also asked to lower his own rank by four steps in favor of his elder brother Sun Teng; both were granted by special edict, and Sun Teng was still made governor of Cang Province.
entries.literal: Longzhi requested a reduction of seven hundred households in his fief and also asked to lower his own rank by four steps in favor of his elder brother Teng; both were granted by special edict, and Teng was still made Governor of Cang Province.

entries.zh: 高祖之討斛斯椿，以隆之為大行臺尚書。
entries.en: When Gao Huan punished Husi Chun, Gao Longzhi was made director of the masters of writing of the grand mobile office.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor punished Husi Chun, Longzhi was made Director of the Masters of Writing of the Grand Mobile Office.

entries.zh: 及大司馬、清河王亶承制，拜隆之侍中、尚書右僕射，領御史中尉。
entries.en: When the Grand Marshal Yuan Dan, Prince of Qinghe, assumed delegated imperial authority, Gao Longzhi was appointed Palace Attendant, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and concurrently Imperial Censor.
entries.literal: When the Grand Marshal Yuan Dan, Prince of Qinghe, assumed delegated imperial authority, Longzhi was appointed Palace Attendant, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and concurrently Imperial Censor.

entries.zh: 廣費人工，大營寺塔，為高祖所責。
entries.en: He spent lavishly on labor and greatly built temples and pagodas, and was reproved by Gao Huan.
entries.literal: He spent lavishly on labor and greatly built temples and pagodas, and was reproved by the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 隆之雖不涉學，而欽尚文雅，縉紳名流，必存禮接。
entries.en: Although Longzhi had not studied, he admired literary refinement; among gentry and eminent men he always treated them with courtesy.
entries.literal: Although Longzhi had not studied, he admired and honored literary refinement; among gentry and eminent men he always treated them with courtesy.

entries.zh: 寡姊為尼，事之如母，訓督諸子，必先文義。
entries.en: His widowed elder sister became a nun; he served her as he would his mother and, when instructing his sons, always put literary learning and moral principle first.
entries.literal: His widowed elder sister became a nun; he served her as he would his mother and, when instructing his sons, always put literary learning and moral principle first.

entries.zh: 世甚以此稱之。
entries.en: The age widely praised him for this.
entries.literal: The age widely praised him for this.

entries.zh: 顯祖末年，既多猜害，追忿隆之，誅其子德樞等十餘人，並投漳水。
entries.en: In Xianzu's late years, when suspicion and harm were many, he turned his wrath on Longzhi and executed more than ten of Longzhi's sons, including Deshu, casting them all into the Zhang River.
entries.literal: In the late years of Xianzu, when suspicion and harm were many, he turned his wrath on Longzhi and executed more than ten of Longzhi's sons, including Deshu, casting them all into the Zhang River.

entries.zh: 又發隆之冢，出其屍，葬已積年，其貌不改，斬截骸骨，亦棄於漳流，遂絕嗣。
entries.en: He also opened Longzhi's tomb and took out the corpse; though it had been buried for years, the face was unchanged. The bones were hacked apart and likewise cast into the Zhang River, and the line ended.
entries.literal: He also opened Longzhi's tomb and took out the corpse; though it had been buried for years, the face was unchanged. The bones were hacked apart and likewise cast into the Zhang River, and the line ended.

entries.zh: 幹明中，詔其兄子子遠為隆之後，襲爵陽夏王，還其財產。
entries.en: In Ganming, an edict made his elder brother's son Ziyuan Longzhi's heir, granting succession to the title prince of Yangxia and restoring his property.
entries.literal: In Ganming, an edict made his elder brother's son Ziyuan Longzhi's heir, granting succession to the title Prince of Yangxia and restoring his property.

entries.zh: 初，隆之見信高祖，性多陰毒，睚眥之忿，無不報焉。
entries.en: Earlier, when Longzhi had enjoyed Gao Huan's trust, his nature was deeply malicious; no grudge, however small, went unavenged.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Longzhi had enjoyed the Grand Ancestor's trust, his nature was deeply malicious; no grudge, however small, went unavenged.

entries.zh: 儀同三司崔孝芬以結婚姻不果，太府卿任集同知營構，頗相乖異，瀛州刺史元晏請托不遂，前後構成其罪，並誅害之。
entries.en: Commissioner with protocol equal to the Three Dukes Cui Xiaofen, because a marriage alliance failed; grand steward Ren Ji, who jointly managed construction and often clashed with him; and Ying Province governor Yuan Yan, whose requests went unfulfilled — Longzhi, one after another, fabricated crimes against them, and all were executed.
entries.literal: Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes Cui Xiaofen, because a marriage alliance failed; Grand Steward Ren Ji, who jointly managed construction and often clashed with him; and Ying Province governor Yuan Yan, whose requests went unfulfilled — Longzhi, one after another, fabricated crimes against them, and all were executed.

entries.zh: 終至家門殄滅，論者謂有報應焉。
entries.en: In the end his own house was wiped out; commentators called it retribution.
entries.literal: In the end his own house was wiped out; commentators called it retribution.

entries.zh: 子如性既豪爽，兼恃舊恩，簿領之務，與奪任情，公然受納，無所顧憚。
entries.en: Ziru's nature was bold and openhanded; relying moreover on old favor, in ledger affairs he granted and withheld as he pleased, openly accepting bribes without the least scruple.
entries.literal: Ziru's nature was bold and openhanded; relying moreover on old favor, in ledger affairs he granted and withheld as he pleased, openly accepting bribes without the least scruple.

entries.zh: 興和中，以為北道行臺，巡檢諸州，守令已下，委其黜陟。
entries.en: In Xinghe he was made commissioner of the Northern Circuit, inspecting the various provinces; prefects, magistrates, and all below were subject to his promotions and demotions.
entries.literal: In Xinghe he was made commissioner of the Northern Circuit, inspecting the various provinces; prefects and magistrates and all below were subject to his promotions and demotions.

entries.zh: 子如至定州，斬深澤縣令；
entries.en: When Ziru reached Ding Province, he beheaded the magistrate of Shenze County;
entries.literal: When Ziru reached Ding Province, he beheaded the magistrate of Shenze County;

entries.zh: 至冀州，斬東光縣令。
entries.en: when he reached Ji Province, he beheaded the magistrate of Dongguang County.
entries.literal: when he reached Ji Province, he beheaded the magistrate of Dongguang County.

entries.zh: 皆稽留時漏，致之極刑。
entries.en: Both had delayed their reports past the deadline, and for this he inflicted the utmost penalty.
entries.literal: Both had delayed their reports past the deadline, and for this he inflicted the utmost penalty.

entries.zh: 若言有進退，少不合意，便令武士頓曳，白刃臨項。
entries.en: If someone's words on promotion or demotion fell even slightly short of his wish, he would order brawny men to drag him down and set a naked blade at his neck.
entries.literal: If someone's words on promotion or demotion fell even slightly short of his wish, he would order brawny men to drag him down and set a naked blade at his neck.

entries.zh: 士庶惶懼，不知所為。
entries.en: Gentry and commoners alike were terrified and did not know what to do.
entries.literal: Gentry and commoners alike were terrified and did not know what to do.

entries.zh: 轉尚書令。
entries.en: He was transferred to director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 子如義旗之始，身不參預，直以高祖故舊，遂當委重，意氣甚高，聚斂不息。
entries.en: From the first raising of the righteous banner, Ziru had taken no part in it; relying solely on being Gao Huan's old friend, he yet held heavy responsibility. His spirit was very high, and he amassed wealth without cease.
entries.literal: From the first raising of the righteous banner, Ziru had taken no part in it; relying solely on being the Grand Ancestor's old friend, he yet held heavy responsibility. His spirit was very high, and he amassed wealth without cease.

entries.zh: 時世宗入輔朝政，內稍嫌之，尋以贓賄為御史中尉崔暹所劾，禁止於尚書省。
entries.en: At that time Shizong was assisting in court governance and inwardly came to dislike him; soon he was impeached for graft by censor-in-chief Cui Xian and confined at the Imperial Secretariat.
entries.literal: At that time Shizong was assisting in court governance and inwardly came to dislike him; soon he was impeached for graft by Censor-in-Chief Cui Xian and confined at the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 詔免其大罪，削官爵。
entries.en: An edict pardoned him from the capital crime and stripped his office and rank.
entries.literal: An edict pardoned him from the capital crime and stripped his office and rank.

entries.zh: 未幾，起行冀州事。
entries.en: Before long he was restored to administer Ji Province.
entries.literal: Before long he was restored to administer Ji Province.

entries.zh: 子如能自厲改，甚有聲譽，發摘姦偽，僚吏畏伏之。
entries.en: Ziru was able to discipline himself and reform; he gained a fine reputation, exposing fraud and deceit, and his subordinate officials feared and submitted to him.
entries.literal: Ziru was able to discipline himself and reform; he gained a fine reputation, exposing fraud and deceit, and his subordinate officials feared and submitted to him.

entries.zh: 轉行幷州事。
entries.en: He was transferred to administer Bing Province.
entries.literal: He was transferred to administer Bing Province.

entries.zh: 詔復官爵，別封野王縣男，邑二百戶。
entries.en: An edict restored his office and rank; separately he was enfeoffed baron of Yewang County with a fief of two hundred households.
entries.literal: An edict restored his office and rank; separately he was enfeoffed Baron of Yewang County with a fief of two hundred households.

entries.zh: 子消難嗣。
entries.en: His son Xiaonan succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Xiaonan succeeded.

entries.zh: 尚高祖女，以主婿、貴公子，頻歷中書、黃門郎、光祿少卿。
entries.en: He married Gao Huan's daughter; as imperial son-in-law and a nobleman's heir, he repeatedly served as director in the Secretariat, as gentleman in the Yellow Gate Office, and as vice director of splendid honors.
entries.literal: He married the Grand Ancestor's daughter; as imperial son-in-law and a nobleman's heir, he repeatedly served as director in the Secretariat and as gentleman in the Yellow Gate Office and as Vice Director of Splendid Honors.

entries.zh: 出為北豫州刺史，鎮武牢。
entries.en: He went out as governor of Northern Yu Province and garrisoned Wulao.
entries.literal: He went out as governor of Northern Yu Province and garrisoned Wulao.

entries.zh: 消難博涉史傳，有風神，然不能廉潔，在州為御史所劾。
entries.en: Xiaonan was broadly read in histories and records and had a fine presence, yet he could not be clean and honest; in the province he was impeached by the censorate.
entries.literal: Xiaonan was broadly read in histories and records and had a fine presence, yet he could not be clean and honest; in the province he was impeached by the censorate.

entries.zh: 又於公主情好不睦，公主譖訴之，懼罪，遂招延鄰敵，走關西。
entries.en: Moreover he was on bad terms with the princess; the princess slandered and accused him. Fearing punishment, he then drew in neighboring enemies and fled to Guanxi.
entries.literal: Moreover he was on bad terms with the princess; the princess slandered and accused him. Fearing punishment, he then drew in neighboring enemies and fled to Guanxi.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：高祖以晉陽戎馬之地，霸圖攸屬，治兵訓旅，遙制朝權，京臺機務，委寄深遠。
entries.en: The historian writes: Gao Huan held Jinyang — land of war-horses, cradle of the hegemonic design — where he drilled troops and trained armies, held court power from afar, and entrusted the capital's affairs to men at great remove.
entries.literal: The historian writes: The Grand Ancestor, holding Jinyang — a land of war-horses where the hegemonic design was destined — drilled troops and trained armies, controlled court authority from afar, and entrusted affairs of the capital with deep reliance.

entries.zh: 孫騰等俱不能清貞守道，以治亂為懷，厚斂貨財，填彼溪壑。
entries.en: Sun Teng and the rest alike could not keep their integrity or hold order and disorder as their concern. They taxed without mercy and filled ravine and gully with plunder.
entries.literal: Sun Teng and the rest alike failed to keep integrity and hold to the Way, to make order and disorder their concern; they amassed goods in heavy exactions and filled ravine and gully.

entries.zh: 昔蕭何之鎮關中，荀彧之居許下，不亦異於是乎！
entries.en: Long ago Xiao He guarded Guanzhong and Xun Yu held Xudu — were they not utterly unlike this?
entries.literal: In old days when Xiao He guarded Guanzhong and Xun Yu dwelt at Xudu — were they not utterly unlike this?

entries.zh: 賴世宗入輔，責以驕縱，厚遇崔暹，奮其霜簡，不然則君子屬厭，豈易間焉。
entries.en: Only when Gao Cheng took charge, rebuked their arrogance, and empowered Cui Xian to wield the censor’s brush were they checked; otherwise they would simply have gone on glutting themselves.
entries.literal: It was thanks to Shizong’s entry as regent: he rebuked them for arrogance and indulgence, treated Cui Xian generously, and set his frosty censor’s tablet in motion. Otherwise, those gentlemen would have gone on glutting themselves; how could they readily have been checked?

entries.zh: 孫騰牽裾之誠，有足稱美。
entries.en: Sun Teng's sincerity when he seized Gao Huan's robe — that at least deserves praise.
entries.literal: Sun Teng's sincerity in seizing the robe has worth enough to be praised.

entries.zh: 隆之勞其志力，經始鄴京，又並是潛德僚寀，早申任遇，崇其名器，未失朝序。
entries.en: Longzhi toiled in will and strength to found Ye as capital. They were all men of hidden capacity among the staff — early given trust, raised in rank and emblem, not fallen from court order.
entries.literal: Longzhi toiled with will and strength in founding Ye; all were men of hidden virtue among the staff, early granted trust, honored in rank and emblem, not falling from court order.

entries.zh: 子如徒以少相親重，情深昵狎，義非草昧，恩結寵私，勳德莫聞，坐致臺輔。
entries.en: Ziru reached power on youthful intimacy alone — deep bonds and familiar warmth, not merit won in founding days, but favor woven in private attachment. No deed of merit is recorded; yet he sat and rose to the highest ministry.
entries.literal: Ziru gained his place solely through youthful intimacy and weight of affection — deep bonding and familiar closeness; this was not merit won at the founding, but favor tied in private attachment. No deeds of merit are heard; yet he sat and attained the highest ministry.

entries.zh: 猶子之愛，訓以義方，膺之風素可重，幼之清簡自立，有足稱也。
entries.en: Yet he loved his nephews as his own sons and instructed them in proper conduct; Yingzhi’s dignified character and Youzhi’s pure simplicity and independence are worthy of praise.
entries.literal: Yet he loved his nephews as his own sons and instructed them in proper conduct; Yingzhi’s dignified character and Youzhi’s pure simplicity and independence are worthy of praise.

entries.zh: 天平初，丁母艱解任，尋詔起為幷州刺史，入為尚書右僕射。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianping, he left office on his mother's death; soon an edict recalled him as governor of Bing Province, and he entered court as right vice director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he left office on his mother's death; soon an edict recalled him as Governor of Bing Province, and he entered court as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 時初給民田，貴勢皆占良美，貧弱咸受瘠薄。
entries.en: At that time land was first being allotted to commoners; the powerful and noble all seized the good and fertile, while the poor and weak all received the thin and poor.
entries.literal: At that time land was first being allotted to commoners; the powerful and noble all seized the good and fertile, while the poor and weak all received the thin and poor.

entries.zh: 隆之啟高祖，悉更反易，乃得均平。
entries.en: Gao Longzhi reported to Gao Huan, and all were reversed and exchanged, and thus fairness was achieved.
entries.literal: Longzhi reported to the Grand Ancestor, and all were reversed and exchanged, and thus fairness was achieved.

entries.zh: 又領營構大將軍，京邑制造，莫不由之。
entries.en: He also concurrently served as grand general of construction and oversaw all building in the capital.
entries.literal: He also concurrently served as Grand General of Construction and oversaw all building in the capital.

entries.zh: 增築南城，周迴二十五里。
entries.en: He expanded and built the southern city, twenty-five li in circuit.
entries.literal: He expanded and built the southern city, twenty-five li in circuit.

entries.zh: 以漳水近於帝城，起長堤以防泛溢之患。
entries.en: Because the Zhang River lay close to the imperial city, he raised a long dike to guard against flooding.
entries.literal: Because the Zhang River lay close to the imperial city, he raised a long dike to guard against flooding.

entries.zh: 又鑿渠引漳水周流城郭，造治水碾磑，並有利於時。
entries.en: He also dug canals to draw the Zhang River in circuit around the city walls, built water-powered mills, and all were of benefit to the age.
entries.literal: He also dug canals to draw the Zhang River in circuit around the city walls, built water-powered mills, and all were of benefit to the age.

entries.zh: 魏自孝昌已後，天下多難，刺史太守皆為當部都督，雖無兵事，皆立佐僚，所在頗為煩擾。
entries.en: From Xiaochang onward in Wei, the realm was much troubled; governors and prefects all served as commanders of their districts, and though there were no military affairs they all established assistant staffs — everywhere this became quite troublesome.
entries.literal: From Xiaochang onward in Wei, the realm was much troubled; governors and prefects all served as commanders of their districts, and though there were no military affairs they all established assistant staffs — everywhere this became quite troublesome.

entries.zh: 隆之表請自非實在邊要，見有兵馬者，悉皆斷之。
entries.en: Gao Longzhi submitted a memorial requesting that unless they were truly on the frontier and actually had troops and horses, all such appointments be cut off.
entries.literal: Longzhi submitted a memorial requesting that unless they were truly on the frontier and actually had troops and horses, all such appointments be cut off.

entries.zh: 又朝貴多假常侍以取貂蟬之飾，隆之自表解侍中，並陳諸假侍中服用者，請亦罷之。
entries.en: Also many court nobles falsely held the rank of regular attendant to obtain the insignia of the diao and chan; Gao Longzhi himself submitted a memorial resigning his palace attendant rank and also listed those who held false attendant rank and their regalia, requesting that they too be abolished.
entries.literal: Also many court nobles falsely held the rank of regular attendant to obtain the insignia of the diao and chan; Longzhi himself submitted a memorial resigning his palace attendant rank and also listed those who held false attendant rank and their regalia, requesting that they too be abolished.

entries.zh: 詔皆如表。
entries.en: An edict approved all as he had memorialized.
entries.literal: An edict approved all as he had memorialized.

entries.zh: 自軍國多事，冒名竊官者不可勝數，隆之奏請檢括，獲五萬餘人，而群小喧囂，隆之懼而止。
entries.en: Because military and state affairs were many, those who falsely claimed names and stole offices were beyond counting; Gao Longzhi submitted a request for inspection and registration, obtaining more than fifty thousand persons, but the petty men raised an uproar and Longzhi, in fear, stopped.
entries.literal: Because military and state affairs were many, those who falsely claimed names and stole offices were beyond counting; Longzhi submitted a request for inspection and registration, obtaining more than fifty thousand persons, but the petty men raised an uproar and Longzhi, in fear, stopped.

entries.zh: 詔監起居事，進位司徒公。
entries.en: An edict ordered him to supervise affairs of imperial record and advanced his rank to duke over the masses.
entries.literal: An edict ordered him to supervise affairs of imperial record and advanced his rank to Duke over the Masses.

entries.zh: 武定中，為河北括戶大使。
entries.en: In the Wuding era he served as commissioner for registering households in Hebei.
entries.literal: In the Wuding era he served as commissioner for registering households in Hebei.

entries.zh: 追還，授領軍將軍、錄尚書事，尋兼侍中。
entries.en: Recalled, he was appointed general of the palace guard and recorder of the affairs of the masters of writing, and soon additionally palace attendant.
entries.literal: Recalled, he was appointed General of the Palace Guard and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and soon additionally Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 續出行青州事。
entries.en: He again went out to administer Qing Province affairs.
entries.literal: He again went out to administer Qing Province affairs.

entries.zh: 追還，拜太子太師、兼尚書左僕射、吏部尚書，遷太保。
entries.en: Recalled, he was appointed grand preceptor of the heir apparent, concurrently left vice director of the masters of writing and director of the ministry of personnel, and transferred to grand preceptor.
entries.literal: Recalled, he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and transferred to Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 時世宗作宰，風俗肅清，隆之時有受納，世宗於尚書省大加責辱。
entries.en: At that time Gao Cheng was administering affairs; customs were stern and pure, but Gao Longzhi at times accepted bribes; Gao Cheng greatly reproached and humiliated him at the masters of writing office.
entries.literal: At that time Shizong was administering affairs; customs were stern and pure, but Longzhi at times accepted bribes; Shizong greatly reproached and humiliated him at the Masters of Writing office.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，進爵為王。
entries.en: When Qi received the abdication, Gao Longzhi's rank was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: When Qi received the abdication, Longzhi's rank was advanced to prince.

entries.zh: 尋以本官錄尚書事，領大宗正卿，監國史。
entries.en: Soon, retaining his former office, he recorded the affairs of the masters of writing, served as grand director of the imperial clan, and supervised the national history.
entries.literal: Soon, retaining his former office, he recorded the affairs of the Masters of Writing, served as Grand Director of the Imperial Clan, and supervised the national history.

entries.zh: 隆之性小巧，至於公家羽儀、百戲、服制時有改易，不循典故，時論非之。
entries.en: Gao Longzhi by nature was fussy over small things; as for the state's ceremonial regalia, the hundred entertainments, and dress regulations, he at times made changes and did not follow ancient precedent — contemporary opinion criticized this.
entries.literal: Longzhi by nature was fussy over small things; as for the state's ceremonial regalia, the hundred entertainments, and dress regulations, he at times made changes and did not follow ancient precedent — contemporary opinion criticized this.

entries.zh: 於射堋上立三像人為壯勇之勢。
entries.en: At the shooting butts he set up three human figures in a posture of martial valor.
entries.literal: At the shooting butts he set up three human figures in a posture of martial valor.

entries.zh: 顯祖曾至東山，因射，謂隆之曰：「射堋上可作猛獸，以存古義，何為置人？
entries.en: Gao Yang once came to the Eastern Hills and, while shooting, said to Gao Longzhi, "At the shooting butts one could make fierce beasts to preserve the ancient meaning — why set up human figures?
entries.literal: Xianzu once came to the Eastern Hills and, while shooting, said to Longzhi, "At the shooting butts one could make fierce beasts to preserve the ancient meaning — why set up human figures?

entries.zh: 終日射人，朕所不取。」
entries.en: Shooting at human figures all day — that I will not accept."
entries.literal: Shooting at human figures all day — that I will not accept."

entries.zh: 隆之無以對。
entries.en: Gao Longzhi had nothing to reply.
entries.literal: Longzhi had nothing to reply.

entries.zh: 初，世宗委任兼右僕射崔暹、黃門郎崔季舒等，及世宗崩，隆之啟顯祖並欲害之，不許。
entries.en: At first, Gao Cheng entrusted affairs to right vice director Cui Xian, gentlemen attendant Cui Jishu, and others; when Gao Cheng died, Gao Longzhi reported to Gao Yang that they should all be killed, but permission was not granted.
entries.literal: At first, Shizong entrusted affairs to Right Vice Director Cui Xian, Gentlemen Attendant Cui Jishu, and others; when Shizong died, Longzhi reported to Xianzu that they should all be killed, but permission was not granted.

entries.zh: 顯祖以隆之舊齒，委以政事，季舒等仍以前隙，乃譖云：「隆之每見訴訟者，輒加哀矜之意，以示非己能裁。」
entries.en: Because Gao Longzhi was elderly, Gao Yang entrusted government affairs to him; Jishu and the others, still nursing old grievances, slandered him, saying, "Whenever Longzhi sees litigants, he shows them pity, as if to show that he himself cannot judge the case."
entries.literal: Because Longzhi was advanced in years, Xianzu entrusted government affairs to him; Jishu and the others, still acting from old grievances, slandered him, saying, "Whenever Longzhi sees litigants, he always shows them pity, as if to show that he himself cannot judge the case."

entries.zh: 顯祖以其受任既重，知有冤狀，便宜申滌，何得委過要名，非大臣義。
entries.en: Since Gao Yang's commission to him was heavy, when he knew there were unjust cases he should readily have cleared them — how could he shift blame to win renown? This was not the conduct of a great minister.
entries.literal: Since Xianzu's commission to him was heavy, when he knew there were unjust cases he should readily have cleared them — how could he shift blame to win a name? This was not the conduct of a great minister.

entries.zh: 天保五年，禁止尚書省。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Tianbao, Gao Longzhi was confined at the Imperial Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao, he was confined at the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 隆之曾與元昶宴飲，酒酣，語昶曰：「與王交遊，當生死不相背。」
entries.en: Longzhi had once feasted with Yuan Chang; when the wine was deep, he told him, "In friendship with Your Highness, we should never turn our backs on each other, in life or in death."
entries.literal: Longzhi had once feasted and drunk with Yuan Chang; when the wine was deep, he told Chang, "In friendship with Your Highness, one should never turn one's back, in life or in death."

entries.zh: 人有密言之者。
entries.en: Someone reported this in secret.
entries.literal: Someone reported this in secret.

entries.zh: 又帝未登庸之日，隆之意常侮帝。
entries.en: Moreover, before the emperor had ascended the throne, Longzhi's bearing had often been contemptuous toward him.
entries.literal: Moreover, before the emperor had ascended the throne, Longzhi's bearing had often been contemptuous toward the emperor.

entries.zh: 帝將受魏禪，大臣咸言未可，隆之又在其中。
entries.en: When the emperor was about to receive the abdication from Wei, the ministers all said it was not yet permissible — and Longzhi was among them.
entries.literal: When the emperor was about to receive the abdication from Wei, the ministers all said it was not yet permissible, and Longzhi was among them.

entries.zh: 帝深銜之。
entries.en: The emperor deeply resented this.
entries.literal: The emperor deeply resented this.

entries.zh: 因此，遂大發怒，令壯士築百餘下。
entries.en: For this reason he flew into a great rage and ordered brawny men to beat Longzhi more than a hundred blows.
entries.literal: For this reason he flew into a great rage and ordered brawny men to beat him more than a hundred blows.

entries.zh: 放出，渴將飲水，人止之，隆之曰：「今日何在！」
entries.en: He was released. Parched, he was about to drink water, but people stopped him. Longzhi said, "What does today matter!"
entries.literal: He was released; parched, he was about to drink water, but people stopped him. Longzhi said, "What does today matter!"

entries.zh: 遂飲之。
entries.en: And he drank.
entries.literal: And he drank.

entries.zh: 因從駕，死於路中，年六十一。
entries.en: He then followed the imperial procession and died on the road. He was sixty-one.
entries.literal: He then followed the imperial procession and died on the road, aged sixty-one.

entries.zh: 贈冀定瀛滄幽五州諸軍事、大將軍、太尉、太保、冀州刺史、陽夏王。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted authority over military affairs in the five provinces Ji, Ding, Ying, Cang, and You, made grand general, grand tutor, and grand guardian, and enfeoffed prince of Yangxia with governorship of Ji Province.
entries.literal: Posthumously granted authority over military affairs in the five provinces Ji, Ding, Ying, Cang, and You; grand general; grand tutor; grand guardian; governor of Ji Province; Prince of Yangxia.

entries.zh: 竟不得諡。
entries.en: In the end he was never granted a posthumous epithet.
entries.literal: In the end he was never granted a posthumous epithet.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，以有翼贊之功，別封須昌縣公，尋除司空。
entries.en: When Northern Qi was founded, Ziru was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Xuchang County for his supporting merit and was soon appointed Minister of Works.
entries.literal: When Qi received the abdication, because of his merit in assisting and supporting the new regime, he was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Xuchang County and was soon appointed Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 子如性滑稽，不治檢裁，言戲穢褻，識者非之。
entries.en: Ziru was glib and given to joking, with little self-restraint; his banter was often filthy and obscene, and discerning men disapproved of him.
entries.literal: Ziru was by nature glib and jocular, did not regulate or restrain himself, and his joking words were filthy and obscene; knowledgeable people criticized him.

entries.zh: 而事姊有禮，撫諸兄子慈篤，當時名士並加欽愛，世以此稱之。
entries.en: Yet he treated his elder sister with proper respect and cared tenderly for his nephews, so eminent men of the time honored and loved him, and he was praised for it.
entries.literal: Yet in serving his elder sister he was observant of ritual, and in caring for the sons of his elder brothers he was deeply kind; eminent men of the time all honored and loved him, and the age praised him for this.

entries.zh: 然素無鯁正，不能平心處物。
entries.en: Even so, he lacked forthright integrity and could not handle affairs impartially.
entries.literal: However, he had never had forthright uprightness and could not deal with affairs with an impartial mind.

entries.zh: 世宗時，中尉崔暹、黃門郎崔季舒俱被任用。
entries.en: Under Shizong, Censor-in-Chief Cui Xian and Palace Gate Gentleman Cui Jishu were both entrusted with office.
entries.literal: In Shizong's time, Censor-in-Chief Cui Xian and Palace Gate Gentleman Cui Jishu were both employed in office.

entries.zh: 世宗崩，暹等赴晉陽。
entries.en: When Shizong died, Xian and the others went to Jinyang.
entries.literal: When Shizong died, Xian and the others went to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 子如乃啟顯祖，言其罪惡，仍勸誅之。
entries.en: Ziru then reported their alleged crimes to Xianzu and urged him to execute them.
entries.literal: Ziru then memorialized Xianzu, spoke of their crimes and evils, and proceeded to urge that they be executed.

entries.zh: 其後子如以馬度關，為有司所奏。
entries.en: Later, the authorities reported Ziru for taking a horse through the pass.
entries.literal: Afterward, Ziru was reported by the responsible officials for taking a horse through the pass.

entries.zh: 顯祖引子如數讓之曰：「崔暹、季舒事朕先世，有何大罪，卿令我殺之？」
entries.en: Xianzu summoned Ziru and reproached him: "Cui Xian and Jishu served my predecessor. What great crime had they committed, that you made me kill them?"
entries.literal: Xianzu summoned Ziru and repeatedly rebuked him, saying, "Cui Xian and Jishu served my predecessor. What great crime did they commit, that you made me kill them?"

entries.zh: 因此免官。
entries.en: Because of this, he was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: Because of this he was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 久之，猶以先帝之舊，拜太尉。
entries.en: After some time, because he had been an old associate of the former emperor, he was appointed Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: After a long time, still because he was an old associate of the Former Emperor, he was appointed Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 尋以疾薨，時年六十四。
entries.en: Soon afterward he died of illness, aged sixty-four.
entries.literal: Soon he died of illness, at the age of sixty-four.

entries.zh: 贈使持節、都督冀定瀛滄懷五州諸軍事、太師、太尉、懷州刺史，贈物一千段，諡曰文明。
entries.en: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, command of military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Ying, Cang, and Huai, and the titles Grand Tutor, Grand Commandant, and Inspector of Huai Province. He also received one thousand lengths of goods, and his posthumous name was Wenming.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Ying, Cang, and Huai, Grand Tutor, Grand Commandant, and Inspector of Huai Province; he was posthumously bestowed one thousand lengths of goods, and his posthumous name was Wenming.

entries.zh: 子如兄纂，先卒，子如貴，贈岳州刺史。
entries.en: Ziru's elder brother Zuan had died earlier; when Ziru rose high, Zuan was posthumously made governor of Yue Province.
entries.literal: Ziru's elder brother Zuan had died earlier; when Ziru rose high, Zuan was posthumously made governor of Yue Province.

entries.zh: 纂長子世雲，輕險無行，累遷衛將軍、潁州刺史。
entries.en: Zuan's eldest son Shiyun was reckless and without proper conduct; he rose in succession to guard general and governor of Ying Province.
entries.literal: Zuan's eldest son Shiyun was reckless and without proper conduct; he rose in succession to guard general and governor of Ying Province.

entries.zh: 世雲本無勳業，直以子如故，頻歷州郡。
entries.en: Shiyun by origin had no merit; relying solely on being Ziru's nephew, he repeatedly held provincial and commandery posts.
entries.literal: Shiyun by origin had no merit; relying solely on being Ziru's nephew, he repeatedly held provincial and commandery posts.

entries.zh: 恃叔之勢，所在聚斂，仍肆姦穢。
entries.en: Relying on his uncle's power, wherever he served he amassed wealth and still indulged in wickedness and corruption.
entries.literal: Relying on his uncle's power, wherever he served he amassed wealth and still indulged in wickedness and corruption.

entries.zh: 將見推治，內懷驚懼，侯景反，遂舉州從之。
entries.en: When he was about to be prosecuted, inwardly he was alarmed and afraid; when Hou Jing rebelled, he then raised the province and followed him.
entries.literal: When he was about to be prosecuted, inwardly he was alarmed and afraid; when Hou Jing rebelled, he then raised the province and followed him.

entries.zh: 時世雲母弟在鄴，便傾心附景，無復顧望。
entries.en: At that time Shiyun's younger maternal brother was in Ye; he gave his heart wholly to Jing and no longer looked back.
entries.literal: At that time Shiyun's younger maternal brother was in Ye; he gave his heart wholly to Jing and no longer looked back.

entries.zh: 諸將圍景於潁川，世雲臨城遙對諸將，言甚不遜。
entries.en: When the generals besieged Jing at Yingchuan, Shiyun from atop the walls shouted across at the generals, his words very insolent.
entries.literal: When the generals besieged Jing at Yingchuan, Shiyun from atop the walls shouted across at the generals, his words very insolent.

entries.zh: 世宗猶以子如恩舊，免其諸弟死罪，徙於北邊。
entries.en: Shizong still, for Ziru's old kindness, pardoned his younger brothers from the death penalty and exiled them to the northern frontier.
entries.literal: Shizong still, for Ziru's old kindness, pardoned his younger brothers from the death penalty and exiled them to the northern frontier.

entries.zh: 侯景於渦陽敗後，世雲復有異志，為景所殺。
entries.en: After Hou Jing was defeated at Woyang, Shiyun again harbored a different intent and was killed by Jing.
entries.literal: After Hou Jing was defeated at Woyang, Shiyun again harbored a different intent and was killed by Jing.

entries.zh: 孫騰 高隆之 司馬子如
entries.en: Sun Teng; Gao Longzhi; Sima Ziru
entries.literal: Sun Teng; Gao Longzhi; Sima Ziru

entries.zh: 莊帝之將誅尒朱榮也，蘭根聞其計，遂密告尒朱世隆。
entries.en: As Emperor Zhuang was about to execute Erzhu Rong, Langen heard of the plan and secretly informed Erzhu Shilong.
entries.literal: As Emperor Zhuang was about to execute Erzhu Rong, Langen heard of the plan and secretly informed Erzhu Shilong.

entries.zh: 榮死，蘭根恐莊帝知之，憂懼不知所出。
entries.en: When Rong died, Langen feared Zhuang would learn of his involvement and was anxious, not knowing what to do.
entries.literal: When Rong died, Langen feared the emperor would learn of it and was anxious, not knowing what course to take.

entries.zh: 時應詔王道習見信於莊帝，蘭根乃托附之，求得在外立功。
entries.en: At the time Wang Daoxi, attendant respondent to edicts, enjoyed Zhuang's trust. Langen attached himself to him, seeking merit in the field.
entries.literal: At the time, Attendant Respondent to Edicts Wang Daoxi enjoyed Zhuang's trust; Langen attached himself to him, seeking to win merit abroad.

entries.zh: 道習為啟聞，乃以蘭根為河北行臺，於定州率募鄉曲，欲防井陘。
entries.en: Daoxi memorialized on his behalf, and Langen was made Hebei mobile headquarters commissioner, recruiting local levies in Ding Province to guard Jingxing Pass.
entries.literal: Daoxi memorialized on his behalf; Langen was thereupon made Hebei Mobile Headquarters Commissioner, recruiting local levies at Ding Province, intending to guard Jingxing Pass.

entries.zh: 時尒朱榮將侯深自范陽趣中山，蘭根與戰，大敗，走依渤海高乾。
entries.en: At the time Erzhu Rong's general Hou Shen advanced from Fanyang toward Zhongshan. Langen fought him, was routed, and fled to join Gao Gan of Bohai.
entries.literal: At the time Erzhu Rong's general Hou Shen advanced from Fanyang toward Zhongshan; Langen fought him and was greatly defeated, fleeing to join Bohai Gao Gan.

entries.zh: 屬乾兄弟舉義，因在其中。
entries.en: When the Gan brothers raised the righteous banner, he was among them.
entries.literal: As the Gan brothers raised the righteous banner, he was among them.

entries.zh: 高祖至，以蘭根宿望，深禮遇之。
entries.en: When Gao Huan arrived, he treated Langen with deep courtesy because of his long-standing repute.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor arrived, because of Langen's long-standing repute he treated him with deep courtesy.

entries.zh: 中興初，加車騎大將軍、尚書右僕射。
entries.en: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was additionally made grand general of chariots and cavalry and right vice director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was additionally made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 及高祖將入洛陽，遣蘭根先至京師。
entries.en: When Gao Huan was about to enter Luoyang, he sent Langen ahead to the capital.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor was about to enter Luoyang, he dispatched Langen ahead to the capital.

entries.zh: 時廢立未決，令蘭根觀察魏前廢帝。
entries.en: As deposition and enthronement were still undecided, he ordered Langen to observe the Wei Former Deposed Emperor.
entries.literal: As deposition and enthronement were not yet decided, he ordered Langen to observe the Wei Former Deposed Emperor.

entries.zh: 帝神采高明，蘭根恐於後難測，遂與高幹兄弟及黃門崔㥄同心固請於高祖，言廢帝本是胡賊所推，今若仍立，於理不允。
entries.en: The emperor's bearing was lofty and bright; Langen feared he would prove hard to control later. He joined the Gan brothers and Cui Ling of the yellow gate in pressing Gao Huan: the deposed emperor had been set up by barbarian rebels — to restore him would not be just.
entries.literal: The emperor's spirit and bearing were lofty and bright; Langen feared he would be hard to fathom later, and thereupon joined the Gan brothers and Yellow Gate Cui Ling in a united plea to the Grand Ancestor, saying the deposed emperor had originally been promoted by barbarian bandits, and that to install him again would not accord with reason.

entries.zh: 高祖不得已，遂立武帝。
entries.en: Gao Huan, with no choice, thereupon enthroned Emperor Xiaowu.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor, having no choice, thereupon enthroned Emperor Wucheng.

entries.zh: 廢帝素有德業，而為蘭根等構毀，深為時論所非。
entries.en: The deposed emperor had long possessed virtue and achievement, yet Langen and others framed and defamed him — and were deeply censured by contemporary opinion.
entries.literal: The deposed emperor had long possessed virtue and achievement, yet because Langen and others framed and defamed him, they were deeply censured by contemporary opinion.

entries.zh: 太昌初，除儀同三司，尋加開府，封鉅鹿縣侯，邑七百戶。
entries.en: At the beginning of Taichang he was made equal in protocol to the Three Dukes, soon additionally opener of a government office, and enfeoffed marquis of Julu County with seven hundred households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was made Equal in Protocol to the Three Dukes, soon additionally Opener of a Government Office, enfeoffed Marquis of Julu County with a fief of seven hundred households.

entries.zh: 啟授兄子同達。
entries.en: He memorialized to grant his elder brother's son Tongda a portion of the fief.
entries.literal: He memorialized to grant his elder brother's son Tongda a share.

entries.zh: 蘭根既預義勳，位居端揆，至是始敘復岐州勳，封永興縣侯，邑千戶。
entries.en: Having shared in the founding merit and now at the summit of office, Langen at last had his Qi Province service recognized and was enfeoffed marquis of Yongxing with one thousand households.
entries.literal: Langen, having participated in the righteous merit, held a place at the tip of the scale; only then did he record the Qi Province merit and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yongxing with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 高乾之死，蘭根懼，去宅，避於寺。
entries.en: When Gao Gan died, Langen took fright, left his house, and took refuge in a monastery.
entries.literal: When Gao Gan died, Langen was afraid, left his residence, and took refuge in a monastery.

entries.zh: 武帝大加譴責，蘭根憂怖，乃移病解僕射。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowu severely condemned him. Langen, terrified, cited illness and resigned as Vice Director.
entries.literal: Emperor Wucheng severely condemned him; Langen, in terror, thereupon cited illness and resigned the vice directorship.

entries.zh: 天平初，以病篤上表求還鄉里。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianping, gravely ill, he memorialized asking to return home.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, gravely ill, he submitted a memorial asking to return to his home district.

entries.zh: 魏帝遣舍人石長宣就家勞問，猶以開府儀同，門施行馬，歸於本鄉。
entries.en: The Wei emperor sent Gentleman of the Household Shi Changxuan to visit his home with imperial consolation. He still held opener-of-office protocol and the gate display of posting horses, then returned to his native place.
entries.literal: The Wei emperor sent Gentleman of the Household Shi Changxuan to visit his home with imperial consolation; he still held opener-of-office protocol, and his gate was accorded the display of posting horses — then he returned to his native place.

entries.zh: 二年卒，時年六十一。
entries.en: In the second year he died, aged sixty-one.
entries.literal: In the second year he died, aged sixty-one.

entries.zh: 贈冀定殷三州軍事、定州刺史、司徒公、侍中，諡曰文宣。
entries.en: Posthumously granted supervisor of military affairs in Ji, Ding, and Yin provinces, inspector of Ding Province, duke over the masses, and palace attendant, with the posthumous title Wenxuan.
entries.literal: Posthumously granted supervisor of military affairs in the three provinces of Ji, Ding, and Yin, Inspector of Ding Province, Duke over the Masses, Palace Attendant, with posthumous title Wenxuan.

entries.zh: 蘭根雖以功名自立，然善附會，出處之際，多以計數為先，是以不為清論所許。
entries.en: Though Langen had risen by merit, he was skilled at trimming to circumstance; in advancing and withdrawing he often calculated first — and was not approved by men of pure judgment.
entries.literal: Though Langen established himself by merit and renown, he was skilled at attaching himself to power; in advancing and withdrawing he often put calculation first — hence he was not approved by pure opinion.

entries.zh: 蘭根族弟明朗，頗涉經史，粗有文性。
entries.en: Langen's clansman Minglang had some learning in the classics and histories and a rough literary bent.
entries.literal: Langen's clansman Minglang had some acquaintance with the classics and histories and a rough literary bent.

entries.zh: 累遷大司馬府法曹參軍，兼尚書金部郎中。
entries.en: He rose repeatedly to legal bureau clerk in the grand marshal's office and concurrently gentleman in the gold section of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to legal bureau clerk in the Grand Marshal's office and concurrently gentleman in the Gold Section of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 元顥入洛陽，明朗為南道行臺郎中，為顥所擒。
entries.en: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Minglang was attendant on the southern route mobile headquarters and was captured.
entries.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Minglang was southern route mobile headquarters attendant and was captured by Hao.

entries.zh: 後棄顥逃還，除龍驤將軍、中散大夫，賜爵鉅鹿侯。
entries.en: Later he abandoned Hao and fled back, was made general of nimble cavalry and regular grand master, and granted the noble rank marquis of Julu.
entries.literal: Later he abandoned Hao and fled back, was made General of Nimble Cavalry and Regular Grand Master, and granted the noble rank Marquis of Julu.

entries.zh: 永安末，蘭根為河北行臺，引明朗為左丞。
entries.en: At the end of Yong'an, when Langen was Hebei mobile headquarters commissioner, he brought in Minglang as left aide.
entries.literal: At the end of Yong'an, Langen was Hebei mobile headquarters commissioner and brought in Minglang as left aide.

entries.zh: 及蘭根中山之敗，俱歸高祖。
entries.en: When Langen was defeated at Zhongshan, both returned to Gao Huan.
entries.literal: When Langen was defeated at Zhongshan, both returned to the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 中興初，拜撫軍將軍，出為安德太守。
entries.en: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made general who pacifies the army and went out as administrator of Ande.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made General Who Pacifies the Army and went out as Administrator of Ande.

entries.zh: 後轉衛將軍、右光祿大夫、定州大中正。
entries.en: Later he became guard general, right grand master for splendid happiness, and great arbiter of Ding Province.
entries.literal: Later he transferred to Guard General, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Great Arbiter of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 武定初，為顯祖諮議參軍。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wuding he was advisory staff officer to Gao Yang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was Xianzu's advisory staff officer.

entries.zh: 出為平陽太守，為御史所劾，因被禁止。
entries.en: He went out as administrator of Pingyang, was impeached by the censor, and was detained.
entries.literal: He went out as Administrator of Pingyang, was impeached by the censor, and thereupon was detained.

entries.zh: 遇病卒。
entries.en: He fell ill and died.
entries.literal: He encountered illness and died.

entries.zh: 崔㥄，字長孺，清河東武城人也。
entries.en: Cui Ling, styled Changru, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
entries.literal: Cui Ling, styled Changru, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

entries.zh: 父休，魏七兵尚書，贈僕射。
entries.en: His father Xiu had been Wei minister of the seven armories and was posthumously granted vice director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: His father Xiu was Wei minister of the seven armories; posthumously granted vice director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 㥄狀貌偉麗，善於容止，少有名望，為當時所知。
entries.en: Ling was tall and striking, skilled in bearing; even in youth he had a name, and his contemporaries knew him.
entries.literal: Ling was of imposing stature and handsome appearance, skilled in deportment; from youth he had reputation, and men of the time knew him.

entries.zh: 初為魏世宗挽郎，釋褐太學博士。
entries.en: He began as a dirge-bearer for Emperor Shizong of Wei and, on leaving that post, was made erudite of the Imperial Academy.
entries.literal: At first he was a dirge-bearer for Emperor Shizong of Wei; upon leaving office he was made erudite of the Imperial Academy.

entries.zh: 永安中，坐事免歸鄉里。
entries.en: In the Yongan era he was dismissed for an offense and returned to his home district.
entries.literal: In the Yongan era, for an offense he was dismissed and returned to his home district.

entries.zh: 高祖於信都起義，㥄歸焉。
entries.en: When Gao Huan raised the righteous cause at Xindu, Ling came to join him.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous cause at Xindu, Ling came to join him.

entries.zh: 高祖見之，甚悅，以為諮議參軍。
entries.en: Gao Huan saw him and was greatly pleased, appointing him advisory aide.
entries.literal: Gao Huan saw him and was greatly pleased, making him advisory aide.

entries.zh: 尋除給事黃門侍郎，遷將軍、右光祿大夫。
entries.en: Soon he was made attendant of the yellow gate, then transferred to general and right grand master for splendid happiness.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate, then promoted to General and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 高祖入洛，議定廢立。
entries.en: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, they deliberated on deposing and enthroning.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, they deliberated on deposing and enthroning.

entries.zh: 太僕綦儁盛稱普泰王賢明，可以為社稷主。
entries.en: Grand master of the stud Qi Jun lavishly praised the Prince of Putai as worthy and bright, fit to be lord of the realm.
entries.literal: Grand Master of the Stud Qi Jun lavishly praised the Prince of Putai as worthy and bright, fit to be lord of the altars of soil and grain.

entries.zh: 㥄曰：「若其明聖，自可待我高王，徐登九五。
entries.en: Ling said, "If he were bright and sage, he could naturally await our Prince Gao and slowly take the throne.
entries.literal: Ling said: "If he were bright and sage, he could naturally await our Prince Gao and slowly ascend the throne.

entries.zh: 既為逆胡所立，何得猶作天子。
entries.en: Since rebellious barbarians enthroned him, how can he still be Son of Heaven?
entries.literal: Since he was enthroned by rebellious barbarians, how can he still act as Son of Heaven?

entries.zh: 若從儁言，王師何名義舉？」
entries.en: If we follow Jun's counsel, what righteous name does the royal army march under?"
entries.literal: If we follow Jun's words, under what righteous name does the royal army march?"

entries.zh: 由是中興、普泰皆廢，更立平陽王為帝。
entries.en: Thereupon both the Zhongxing and Putai rulers were deposed, and the Prince of Pingyang was enthroned instead.
entries.literal: Thereupon both the Zhongxing and Putai [emperors] were deposed, and the Prince of Pingyang was enthroned in their stead.

entries.zh: 以建義功，封武城縣公，邑一千四百戶，進位車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫，仍領黃門郎。
entries.en: For merit in raising the righteous cause he was enfeoffed duke of Wucheng County with a fief of fourteen hundred households, advanced to general of chariots and cavalry and left grand master for splendid happiness, and still headed the yellow gate office.
entries.literal: For merit in raising the righteous cause he was enfeoffed Duke of Wucheng County with a fief of fourteen hundred households; he advanced to general of chariots and cavalry and left grand master for splendid happiness, and still headed the Yellow Gate office.

entries.zh: 㥄居門下，恃預義旗，頗自矜縱。
entries.en: Ling served in the gate office, trusting in his share in the righteous banner, and grew rather proud and unrestrained.
entries.literal: Ling dwelt in the gate office, relying on his share in the righteous banner, and was rather self-conceited and unrestrained.

entries.zh: 尋以貪汙為御史糾劾，因逃還鄉里，遇赦始出。
entries.en: Soon the censorate impeached him for corruption; he fled home and emerged only after an amnesty.
entries.literal: Soon for corruption he was impeached by the censorate; he fled home, and only after an amnesty did he emerge.

entries.zh: 高祖以㥄本預義旗，復其黃門。
entries.en: Because Ling had originally joined the righteous banner, Gao Huan restored him to the yellow gate.
entries.literal: Gao Huan, because Ling had originally joined the righteous banner, restored him to the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 天平初，為侍讀，監典書。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianping he was lecturer-in-attendance and supervised the palace library.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was lecturer-in-attendance and supervised the palace library.

entries.zh: 尋除徐州刺史，給廣宗部曲三百、清河部曲千人。
entries.en: Soon he was made governor of Xu Province, with three hundred Guangzong retainers and a thousand Qinghe retainers granted him.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Inspector of Xu Province; he was given three hundred retainers from Guangzong and one thousand from Qinghe.

entries.zh: 㥄性豪慢，寵妾馮氏，假其威刑，恣情取受，風政不立。
entries.en: Ling was arrogant by nature; he favored his concubine Lady Feng and lent her his punitive authority, so she extorted at will and local government collapsed.
entries.literal: Ling was by nature arrogant and overbearing; he favored his concubine Lady Feng and lent her his punitive authority, so she extorted and accepted bribes at will — government and customs were not established.

entries.zh: 初㥄為常侍，求人修起居注。
entries.en: When Ling was first regular attendant, he sought someone to compile the imperial diary.
entries.literal: When Ling was first regular attendant, he sought someone to compile the imperial diary.

entries.zh: 或曰：「魏收可。」
entries.en: Someone said, "Wei Shou would do."
entries.literal: Someone said: "Wei Shou would do."

entries.zh: 㥄曰：「收輕薄徒耳。」
entries.en: Ling said, "Shou is nothing but a frivolous fellow."
entries.literal: Ling said: "Shou is but a frivolous fellow."

entries.zh: 更引祖鴻勛為之。
entries.en: He brought in Zu Hongxun instead.
entries.literal: He brought in Zu Hongxun instead.

entries.zh: 既居樞要，又以盧元明代收為中書郎，由是收銜之。
entries.en: Once he held a pivotal post, he also had Lu Yuanming replace Shou as secretariat gentleman — from this Shou bore a grudge.
entries.literal: Once he held a pivotal post, he also had Lu Yuanming replace Shou as secretariat gentleman; from this Shou bore a grudge.

entries.zh: 及收聘梁，過徐州，㥄備刺史鹵簿而送之，使人相聞魏曰：「勿怪儀衛多，稽古之力也。」
entries.en: When Shou went on a mission to Liang and passed through Xu Province, Ling sent him off with a governor's full train of insignia and had a man tell Wei, "Do not wonder at the many guards — it is the power of classical learning."
entries.literal: When Shou went on a mission to Liang and passed through Xu Province, Ling equipped the full insignia of a governor to escort him and had a man convey word to Wei: "Do not wonder at the many guards — it is the power of classical learning."

entries.zh: 收報曰：「白崔徐州，建義之勳，何稽古之有！」
entries.en: Shou replied, "Tell Governor Cui of Xu: merit in raising the righteous cause — what has that to do with classical learning!"
entries.literal: Shou replied: "Tell Governor Cui of Xu: for merit in raising the righteous cause, what classical learning is there!"

entries.zh: 㥄自以門閥素高，特不平此言。
entries.en: Ling, trusting in his clan's long eminence, was especially displeased at this remark.
entries.literal: Ling, trusting in his clan's long-standing eminence, was especially displeased at this remark.

entries.zh: 收乘宿憾，故以挫之。
entries.en: Shou seized on an old resentment and used the occasion to humiliate him.
entries.literal: Shou seized on an old resentment and therefore used this to humiliate him.

entries.zh: 罷州，除七兵尚書、清河邑中正。
entries.en: When he left the province he was made minister of the seven armories and chief clan elder of Qinghe.
entries.literal: When he left the province he was made minister of the seven armories and chief clan elder of Qinghe.

entries.zh: 㥄每以籍地自矜，謂盧元明曰：「天下盛門，唯我與爾，博崔趙李，何事者哉！」
entries.en: Ling often prided himself on his registered pedigree and said to Lu Yuanming, "Among the great houses under Heaven, only you and I; the Bo, Cui, Zhao, and Li clans — what are they worth!"
entries.literal: Ling often prided himself on his registered pedigree and said to Lu Yuanming: "Among the great houses under Heaven, only you and I; Bo, Cui, Zhao, and Li — what are they for!"

entries.zh: 崔暹聞而銜之。
entries.en: Cui Xian heard of it and bore a grudge.
entries.literal: Cui Xian heard of it and bore a grudge.

entries.zh: 高祖葬後，㥄又竊言：「黃頷小兒堪當重任不？」
entries.en: After Gao Huan's burial, Ling again spoke in private, "Can this yellow-bearded boy bear heavy responsibility?"
entries.literal: After Gao Huan's burial, Ling again spoke in private: "Can this yellow-bearded boy bear heavy responsibility?"

entries.zh: 暹外兄李慎以。
entries.en: Cui Xian's cousin by marriage Li Shen
entries.literal: Cui Xian's cousin by marriage Li Shen

entries.zh: 㥄言告暹。
entries.en: reported Ling's words to Xian.
entries.literal: reported Ling's words to Xian.

entries.zh: 暹啟世宗，絕㥄朝謁。
entries.en: Xian memorialized Emperor Wen, and Ling's court attendance was cut off.
entries.literal: Xian memorialized Emperor Wen, and Ling's court attendance was cut off.

entries.zh: 㥄要拜道左，世宗發怒曰：「黃頷小兒，何足拜也！」
entries.en: Ling wanted to bow by the roadside; Emperor Wen flared in anger and said, "Yellow-bearded boy — what is there to bow to!"
entries.literal: Ling wanted to bow by the roadside; Emperor Wen flared in anger and said: "Yellow-bearded boy — what is there to bow to!"

entries.zh: 於是鏁㥄赴晉陽而訊之。
entries.en: Thereupon Ling was shackled and taken to Jinyang for interrogation.
entries.literal: Thereupon Ling was shackled and taken to Jinyang for interrogation.

entries.zh: 㥄不伏，暹引刑子才為證，子才執無此言。
entries.en: Ling would not confess; Xian cited Xing Zicai of the ministry of justice as witness, and Zicai maintained that no such words had been spoken.
entries.literal: Ling would not confess; Xian cited Xing Zicai of the Ministry of Justice as witness, and Zicai held that there had been no such words.

entries.zh: 㥄在禁，謂子才曰：「卿知我意屬太丘不？」
entries.en: Ling, in detention, said to Zicai, "Do you know my mind is set on Taqiu?"
entries.literal: Ling, in detention, said to Zicai: "Do you know my mind is set on Taqiu?"

entries.zh: 子才出告㥄子瞻云：「尊公意正應欲結姻於陳元康。」
entries.en: Zicai went out and told Ling's son Zhan, "Your father's intent surely is to ally by marriage with Chen Yuankang."
entries.literal: Zicai went out and told Ling's son Zhan: "Your father's intent surely is to ally by marriage with Chen Yuankang."

entries.zh: 瞻有女，乃許妻元康子，求其父。
entries.en: Zhan had a daughter; he thereupon betrothed her to Yuankang's son and sought his father's release.
entries.literal: Zhan had a daughter; he thereupon betrothed her to Yuankang's son and sought [release for] his father.

entries.zh: 元康為言之於世宗曰：「崔㥄名望素重，不可以私處言語便以殺之。」
entries.en: Yuankang spoke for him to Emperor Wen, saying, "Cui Ling's renown has long been weighty; he must not be put to death over private words."
entries.literal: Yuankang spoke for him to Emperor Wen, saying: "Cui Ling's renown has long been weighty; one must not put him to death over private words."

entries.zh: 世宗曰：「若免其性命，猶當徙之遐裔。」
entries.en: Emperor Wen said, "If his life is spared, he should still be banished to the far marches."
entries.literal: Emperor Wen said: "If his life is spared, he should still be banished to the far marches."

entries.zh: 元康曰：「㥄若在邊，或將外叛。
entries.en: Yuankang said, "If Ling is on the frontier, he may yet defect abroad.
entries.literal: Yuankang said: "If Ling is on the frontier, he may yet defect abroad.

entries.zh: 以英賢資寇敵，非所宜也。」
entries.en: To supply the enemy with a man of talent is not fitting."
entries.literal: To supply the enemy with a man of talent is not fitting."

entries.zh: 世宗曰：「既有季圭之罪，還令輸作可乎？」
entries.en: Emperor Wen said, "Since he has the crime of Jigui, might he still be sent to corvée labor?"
entries.literal: Emperor Wen said: "Since he has the crime of Jigui, might he still be sent to corvée labor?"

entries.zh: 元康曰：「嘗讀《崔琰傳》，追恨魏武不弘。
entries.en: Yuankang said, "I once read the biography of Cui Yan and regretted that Wei Wu was not magnanimous.
entries.literal: Yuankang said: "I once read the biography of Cui Yan and regretted that Wei Wu was not magnanimous.

entries.zh: 㥄若在作所而殞，後世豈道公不殺也？」
entries.en: If Ling dies in the labor camp, will later ages not say that you killed him after all?"
entries.literal: If Ling dies in the labor camp, will later ages not say that Your Lordship killed him after all?"

entries.zh: 世宗曰：「然則奈何？」
entries.en: Emperor Wen said, "Then what is to be done?"
entries.literal: Emperor Wen said: "Then what is to be done?"

entries.zh: 元康曰：「崔㥄合死，朝野莫不知之，公誠能以寬濟猛，特輕其罰，則仁德彌著，天下歸心。」
entries.en: Yuankang said, "Cui Ling deserves death — court and countryside alike know it; if you can temper severity with leniency and especially lighten his punishment, benevolent virtue will shine the brighter and all under Heaven will turn their hearts to you."
entries.literal: Yuankang said: "Cui Ling deserves death — court and countryside alike know it; if Your Lordship can temper severity with leniency and especially lighten his punishment, then benevolent virtue will shine the brighter and all under Heaven will turn their hearts to you."

entries.zh: 乃舍之。
entries.en: Thereupon he was released.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was released.

entries.zh: 㥄進謁奉謝，世宗猶怒曰：「我雖無堪，忝當大任，被卿名作黃頷小兒，金石可銷，此言難滅！」
entries.en: Ling came forward to offer thanks; Emperor Wen was still angry and said, "Though I am unworthy, I shamefully bear great responsibility — yet you named me 'yellow-bearded boy.' Metal and stone may wear away; this saying is hard to extinguish!"
entries.literal: Ling came forward to audience to offer thanks; Emperor Wen was still angry and said: "Though I am unworthy, I shamefully bear great responsibility — yet you named me 'yellow-bearded boy.' Metal and stone may wear away; this saying is hard to extinguish!"

entries.zh: 㥄歷覽群書，兼有詞藻，自中興立後，迄於武帝，詔誥表檄，多㥄所為。
entries.en: Ling read widely and had literary talent; from the Zhongxing enthronement down to Emperor Wu, most edicts, mandates, memorials, and proclamations were his work.
entries.literal: Ling read widely among books and also had literary talent; from the enthronement in the Zhongxing era down to Emperor Wu, most edicts, mandates, memorials, and proclamations were Ling's work.

entries.zh: 然率性豪侈，溺於財色，諸弟之間，不能盡雍穆之美，世論以此譏之。
entries.en: Yet by nature he was extravagant and proud, sunk in wealth and women; among his brothers he could not fully achieve harmonious kinship — and public opinion reproached him for it.
entries.literal: Yet by nature he was extravagant and proud, sunk in wealth and women; among his brothers he could not fully achieve harmonious kinship — public opinion reproached him for this.

entries.zh: 㥄素與魏收不協，收既專典國史，㥄恐被惡言，乃悅之曰：「昔有班固，今則魏子。」
entries.en: Ling had long been at odds with Wei Shou; once Shou came to monopolize the national history, Ling feared slander and flattered him, saying, "In old times there was Ban Gu; today there is Master Wei."
entries.literal: Ling had long been at odds with Wei Shou; once Shou came to monopolize the national history, Ling feared slander and therefore flattered him, saying: "In old times there was Ban Gu; today there is Master Wei."

entries.zh: 收笑而憾不釋。
entries.en: Shou smiled, yet his resentment did not lift.
entries.literal: Shou smiled, yet his resentment did not lift.

entries.zh: 子瞻嗣。
entries.en: His son Zhan succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Zhan succeeded.

entries.zh: 瞻字彥通，聰明強學，有文情，善容止，神采嶷然，言不妄發。
entries.en: Zhan, styled Yantong, was bright and studied hard; he had literary sensibility, skilled bearing, a lofty and striking mien, and did not speak idly.
entries.literal: Zhan, styled Yantong, was bright and studied hard; he had literary sensibility, skilled deportment, a lofty and striking mien, and did not speak idly.

entries.zh: 年十五，刺史高昂召署主簿，清河公岳辟開府西閣祭酒。
entries.en: At fifteen Governor Gao Ang summoned him as chief clerk; the Duke of Qinghe, Yue, recruited him as libationer of the western pavilion of the open government.
entries.literal: At fifteen the governor Gao Ang summoned him to serve as chief clerk; the Duke of Qinghe, Yue, recruited him as libationer of the western pavilion of the open government.

entries.zh: 崔暹為中尉，啟除御史，以才望見收，非其好也。
entries.en: Cui Xian was commandant of justice; he memorialized to appoint Zhan censor — he was taken in for talent and reputation, which was not to Zhan's liking.
entries.literal: Cui Xian was commandant of justice; he memorialized to appoint [Zhan] as censor — he was taken in for talent and reputation, which was not to his (Zhan's) liking.

entries.zh: 高祖入朝，還晉陽，被召與北海王晞陪從，俱為諸子賓友。
entries.en: When Gao Huan entered court and returned to Jinyang, Zhan was summoned together with the Prince of Beihai Xi to attend in company; both became companion-friends to the sons.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan entered court and returned to Jinyang, [Zhan] was summoned together with the Prince of Beihai Xi to attend in company; both became guest-friends to the sons.

entries.zh: 仍為相府中兵參軍，轉主簿。
entries.en: He then served as middle army aide in the chancellor's government and was transferred to chief clerk.
entries.literal: He then served as middle army aide in the chancellor's government and was transferred to chief clerk.

entries.zh: 世宗崩，秘未發喪，顯祖命瞻兼相府司馬使鄴。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen died the death was kept secret; Emperor Wenxuan ordered Zhan concurrently to serve as marshal of the chancellor's government and go to Ye.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen died the death was kept secret; Emperor Wenxuan ordered Zhan concurrently to serve as marshal of the chancellor's government and go to Ye.

entries.zh: 魏孝靜帝以人日登雲龍門，其父㥄侍宴，又敕瞻令近御坐，亦有應詔詩，問邢卲等曰：「此詩何如其父？」
entries.en: Emperor Xiaojing of Wei, on the Human Day, ascended the Cloud Dragon Gate; his father Ling attended the feast, and the emperor also ordered Zhan to draw near the imperial seat; he too had a poem in response to the imperial command, and the emperor asked Xing Shao and the others, "How does this poem compare with his father's?"
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaojing of Wei, on the Human Day, ascended the Cloud Dragon Gate; his father Ling attended the feast, and [the emperor] also ordered Zhan to draw near the imperial seat; he too had a poem in response to the imperial command, and [the emperor] asked Xing Shao and the others: "How does this poem compare with his father's?"

entries.zh: 咸云：「㥄博雅弘麗，瞻氣調清新，並詩人之冠。」
entries.en: All said, "Ling is broad, elegant, and grand; Zhan's tone is fresh and clear — both crown the poets of the age."
entries.literal: All said: "Ling is broad, elegant, and grand; Zhan's tone is fresh and clear — both are crowns among poets."

entries.zh: 宴罷，共嗟賞之，咸云：「今日之讌，併為崔瞻父子。」
entries.en: When the feast ended they sighed in admiration together, all saying, "Today's banquet belonged alike to father and son, the Cui Zhan pair."
entries.literal: When the feast ended they sighed in admiration together, all saying: "Today's banquet was alike for the father and son Cui Zhan."

entries.zh: 㥄昆季仲文，有學尚，魏高陽太守、清河內史。
entries.en: Ling's brother Zhongwen pursued learning and held to what is right; under Wei he served as prefect of Gaoyang and interior minister of Qinghe.
entries.literal: Ling's brother Zhongwen had learning and cultivation; under Wei he was Administrator of Gaoyang and Interior Minister of Qinghe.

entries.zh: 興和中，為丞相掾。
entries.en: In the Xinghe reign he was a staff officer to the chancellor.
entries.literal: In the Xinghe era he was a staff member to the Chancellor.

entries.zh: 沙苑之敗，仲文持馬尾以渡河，波中乍沒乍出。
entries.en: When Shayuan was lost, Zhongwen seized a horse's tail to ford the river, now swallowed by the water, now breaking the surface again.
entries.literal: At the defeat at Shayuan, Zhongwen grasped a horse's tail to cross the river, now submerged, now emerging from the waves.

entries.zh: 高祖望見曰：「崔掾也。」
entries.en: Gao Huan saw him and said, "That is Staff Officer Cui."
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor saw him and said, "That is Staff Member Cui."

entries.zh: 遽遣船赴接。
entries.en: At once he sent a boat to bring him in.
entries.literal: He immediately sent a boat to fetch him.

entries.zh: 既濟，勞之曰：「卿為親為君，不顧萬死，可謂家之孝子，國之忠臣。」
entries.en: When he had crossed, Gao Huan comforted him: "You risked everything for family and for your lord — at home a filial son, to the state a loyal minister."
entries.literal: Once across, he comforted him: "You acted for kin and for your lord, heedless of ten thousand deaths — one may call you a filial son at home and a loyal minister to the state."

entries.zh: 加中軍將軍。
entries.en: He was promoted to general of the central army.
entries.literal: He was promoted to General of the Central Army.

entries.zh: 天保初，拜散騎常侍、光祿大夫。
entries.en: At the opening of Tianbao he was made regular attendant-in-ordinary and grand master for splendid happiness.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 七年卒，年六十。
entries.en: In the seventh year he died, aged sixty.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he died, aged sixty.

entries.zh: 子偃，武平中，歷太子洗馬、尚書郎。
entries.en: His son Yan, in the Wuping era, served in turn as palace secretary and gentleman of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: His son Yan, during Wuping, served in succession as Palace Secretary and Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 偃弟儦，學識有才思，風調甚高。
entries.en: Yan's younger brother Biao was learned and quick of mind, with real literary gift; his manner and tone were very high.
entries.literal: Yan's younger brother Biao had learning and knowledge with literary inventiveness; his bearing and tone were very lofty.

entries.zh: 武平中，瑯琊王大司馬中兵參軍。
entries.en: In Wuping he was military staff officer in the great army headquarters of the Prince of Langya.
entries.literal: During Wuping he was Military Staff Officer in the Great Army Headquarters of the Prince of Langya.

entries.zh: 參定五禮，待詔文林館。
entries.en: He took part in fixing the Five Rites and awaited orders at the Forest of Letters Hall.
entries.literal: He helped establish the Five Rites and awaited edicts at the Wenlin Hall.

entries.zh: 隋仁壽中，卒於通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: Under the Sui, in Renshou, he died in office as regular attendant-in-ordinary with unrestricted access.
entries.literal: Under Sui in Renshou he died while serving as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary with Unrestricted Access.

entries.zh: 叔仁，魏潁州刺史。
entries.en: Shuren served under Wei as administrator of Ying Province.
entries.literal: Shuren, under Wei Administrator of Ying Province.

entries.zh: 子彥武，有識用，朝歌令。
entries.en: His son Yanwu had judgment and practical ability; he was magistrate of Chaoge.
entries.literal: His son Yanwu had discernment and capacity; Magistrate of Chaoge.

entries.zh: 隋開皇初，魏州刺史。
entries.en: At the opening of Sui Kaihuang he was governor of Wei Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Sui Kaihuang he was Governor of Wei Province.

entries.zh: 子侃，魏末兼通直常侍，聘梁使。
entries.en: His son Kan, in the final years of Wei, also served as unrestricted regular attendant and went as envoy to the Liang court.
entries.literal: His son Kan, at the end of Wei also served as Unrestricted Regular Attendant and envoy on a mission to the Liang court.

entries.zh: 子極，武平初太子僕，卒於武德郡守。
entries.en: His son Ji, at the start of Wuping, was master of the palace household; he died in office as prefect of Wude Commandery.
entries.literal: His son Ji, at the beginning of Wuping was Master of the Palace Household; died while serving as Prefect of Wude Commandery.

entries.zh: 子聿，魏東莞太守。
entries.en: His son Yu was Wei administrator of Dongguan.
entries.literal: His son Yu, Wei Administrator of Dongguan.

entries.zh: 子約，司空祭酒。
entries.en: His son Yue was libationer to the minister of works.
entries.literal: His son Yue, Libationer to the Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 魏蘭根 崔㥄 子瞻
entries.en: Wei Langen; Cui Ling; and his son Zhan
entries.literal: Wei Langen; Cui Ling; son Zhan

entries.zh: 蕤、臺卿，並有學業。
entries.en: Rui and Taiqing both had learning.
entries.literal: Rui and Taiqing both had learning.

entries.zh: 臺卿文筆尤工，見稱當世。
entries.en: Taiqing's brush was especially fine, and his own age praised him.
entries.literal: Taiqing's literary brush was especially skilled and he was praised in his age.

entries.zh: 蕤字子美，武平中大理少卿，兼散騎常侍，聘陳使主。
entries.en: Rui, styled Zimei, in Wuping was vice director of the court of judicature and concurrent regular attendant, and headed the mission to Chen.
entries.literal: Rui, styled Zimei, in Wuping was vice director of the Court of Judicature and concurrent regular attendant, and chief of the mission to Chen.

entries.zh: 末年，吏部郎中。
entries.en: In his later years he was a langzhong in the ministry of personnel.
entries.literal: In his later years he was a langzhong in the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 隋開皇中，終於開州刺史。
entries.en: Under Sui Kaihuang he ended his days as inspector of Kai Province.
entries.literal: Under Sui Kaihuang he ended his days as inspector of Kai Province.

entries.zh: 臺卿字少山，歷中書、黃門侍郎，兼大著作、修國史。
entries.en: Taiqing, styled Shaoshan, served in turn as secretariat and Yellow Gate vice director, and concurrently as grand author and compiler of the national history.
entries.literal: Taiqing, styled Shaoshan, served in succession as secretariat and Yellow Gate vice director, and concurrently as grand author and compiler of the national history.

entries.zh: 武平末，國子祭酒，領尚書左丞。
entries.en: At the end of Wuping he was libationer of the imperial university and concurrently left vice director in the masters of writing.
entries.literal: At the end of Wuping he was libationer of the Imperial University and concurrently held the post of left vice director in the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 周武帝平齊，命尚書左僕射陽休之以下知名朝士十八人隨駕入關，蕤兄弟並不預此名。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he ordered eighteen noted court scholars from Yang Xiuzhi, left vice director of the masters of writing, downward to follow the train into Guan; the Rui brothers were not on the list.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he ordered eighteen noted court scholars from Yang Xiuzhi, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, downward to follow the imperial train into Guan; the Rui brothers were not among those named.

entries.zh: 臺卿後雖被徵，為其聾疾放歸。
entries.en: Taiqing was later summoned, but because of deafness he was released and sent home.
entries.literal: Taiqing was later summoned, but because of deafness he was released and sent home.

entries.zh: 隋開皇中，徵為著作郎，歲餘以年老致事，詔許之。
entries.en: Under Sui Kaihuang he was summoned as author in the masters of writing; after a little more than a year, on account of age he retired, and an edict allowed it.
entries.literal: Under Sui Kaihuang he was summoned as author in the Masters of Writing; after a little more than a year, on account of age he retired from office, and an edict permitted it.

entries.zh: 特優其禮，終身給祿，未幾而終。
entries.en: His rites were especially favored; salary was granted for life, and before long he died.
entries.literal: His rites were especially favored; salary was granted for life, and before long he died.

entries.zh: 孫搴 陳元康 杜弼
entries.en: Sun Cen; Chen Yuankang; Du Bi
entries.literal: Sun Cen; Chen Yuankang; Du Bi

entries.zh: 張纂，字徽纂，代郡平城人也。
entries.en: Zhang Zuan, styled Huizuan, came from Pingcheng in Dai Commandery.
entries.literal: Zhang Zuan, styled Huizuan, was a native of Pingcheng in Dai Commandery.

entries.zh: 父烈，桑幹太守。
entries.en: His father Lie had been governor of Sanggan.
entries.literal: His father Lie was governor of Sanggan.

entries.zh: 纂初事尒朱榮，又為尒朱兆都督長史。
entries.en: Zuan first served Erzhu Rong, then became chief of staff on Erzhu Zhao's staff.
entries.literal: Zuan first served Erzhu Rong, then became chief of staff to Erzhu Zhao's headquarters.

entries.zh: 為兆使於高祖，遂被顧識。
entries.en: Zhao sent him to Gao Huan, and he won notice and favor.
entries.literal: Zhao sent him to the Grand Ancestor, and he came to be noticed and favored.

entries.zh: 高祖舉義山東，劉誕據相州拒守，時纂亦在其中。
entries.en: When Gao Huan raised the standard in Shandong, Liu Dan held Xiang Province and resisted; Zuan was among the defenders.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised the righteous standard in Shandong, Liu Dan held Xiang Province in resistance; Zuan was then among them.

entries.zh: 高祖攻而拔之，以纂參丞相軍事。
entries.en: Gao Huan attacked and took the city, then made Zuan a staff officer on the chancellor's army.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor attacked and took it, and made Zuan a staff officer on the chancellor's military staff.

entries.zh: 王纮，字師羅，太安狄那人也，為小部酋帥。
entries.en: Wang Hong, styled Shiluo, was a native of Dina in Tai'an and was chief of a minor tribal division.
entries.literal: Wang Hong, styled Shiluo, was a native of Dina in Tai'an and was chief of a minor tribal division.

entries.zh: 父基，頗讀書，有智略。
entries.en: His father Ji was well read and possessed wisdom and strategy.
entries.literal: His father Ji was well read and possessed wisdom and strategy.

entries.zh: 初從葛榮反，榮授基濟北王、寧州刺史。
entries.en: At first he followed Ge Rong in rebellion; Ge Rong made Ji Prince of Jibei and governor of Ning Province.
entries.literal: At first he followed Ge Rong in rebellion; Ge Rong made Ji Prince of Jibei and governor of Ningzhou.

entries.zh: 後葛榮破，而基據城不下，尒朱榮遣使喻之，然後始降。
entries.en: Later, when Ge Rong was defeated, Ji held the city and would not submit; Erzhu Rong sent envoys to instruct him, and only then did he surrender.
entries.literal: Later, when Ge Rong was defeated, Ji held the city and would not submit; Erzhu Rong sent envoys to instruct him, and only then did he surrender.

entries.zh: 榮後以為府從事中郎，令率衆鎮磨川。
entries.en: Rong later made him staff attendant and ordered him to lead troops to garrison Mochuan.
entries.literal: Rong later made him staff attendant and ordered him to lead troops to garrison Mochuan.

entries.zh: 榮死，紇豆陵步藩虜基歸河西，後逃歸尒朱兆。
entries.en: When Rong died, Hedouling Bufan took Ji captive to Hexi; later he escaped and returned to Erzhu Zhao.
entries.literal: When Rong died, Hedouling Bufan took Ji captive to Hexi; later he escaped and returned to Erzhu Zhao.

entries.zh: 高祖平兆，以基為都督，除義寧太守。
entries.en: When Gao Huan pacified Zhao, Ji was made area commander and governor of Yining.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan pacified Zhao, Ji was made area commander and governor of Yining.

entries.zh: 基先於葛榮軍與周文帝相知，及文帝據有關中，高祖遣基與長史侯景同使於周文帝，文帝留基不遣。
entries.en: Ji had earlier known Zhou Wendi while in Ge Rong's army; when Wendi held Guanzhong, Gao Huan sent Ji with chief clerk Hou Jing on a mission to Zhou Wendi, and Wendi detained Ji and would not send him back.
entries.literal: Ji had earlier known Zhou Wendi while in Ge Rong's army; when Wendi held Guanzhong, Gao Huan sent Ji with chief clerk Hou Jing on a mission to Zhou Wendi, and Wendi detained Ji and would not send him back.

entries.zh: 基後逃歸，除冀州長史，後行肆州事。
entries.en: Ji later escaped and returned; he was made chief clerk of Ji Province, then acting administrator of Si Province.
entries.literal: Ji later escaped and returned; he was made chief clerk of Ji Province, then acting administrator of Si Province.

entries.zh: 元象初，累遷南益州、北豫州刺史。
entries.en: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he rose in succession to governor of Southern Yi and Northern Yu provinces.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he rose in succession to governor of Southern Yi and Northern Yu provinces.

entries.zh: 所歷皆好聚斂，然性和直，吏民不甚患之。
entries.en: In every post he loved to extort and gather wealth, yet his nature was upright and straightforward, and officials and commoners did not greatly resent him.
entries.literal: In every post he loved to extort and gather wealth, yet his nature was upright and straightforward, and officials and commoners did not greatly resent him.

entries.zh: 興和四年冬為奴所害，時年六十五。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Xinghe, in winter, he was killed by a slave; he was sixty-five.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Xinghe, in winter, he was killed by a slave; he was sixty-five.

entries.zh: 贈征東將軍、吏部尚書、定州刺史。
entries.en: Posthumously granted general who campaigns east, minister of the civil office, and governor of Ding Province.
entries.literal: Posthumously granted general who campaigns east, minister of the civil office, and governor of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 纂性便僻，左右出內，稍見親待，仍補行臺郎中。
entries.en: Zuan was accommodating by nature and quick at his errands. Moving in and out at Gao Huan's side, he gradually won intimate favor and was appointed gentleman of the mobile headquarters.
entries.literal: Zuan was obliging and unorthodox by nature; coming and going at his side, he gradually won intimate treatment, and was then appointed mobile headquarters gentleman.

entries.zh: 高祖啟減國封，分賞文武，纂隨例封壽張伯。
entries.en: Gao Huan memorialized to trim state enfeoffments and reward civil and military officials; Zuan received the usual grant and was enfeoffed baron of Shouzhang.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor memorialized to reduce state enfeoffments and distribute rewards to civil and military officials; Zuan was enfeoffed Marquis of Shouzhang according to precedent.

entries.zh: 魏武帝末，高祖赴洛，以趙郡公琛為行臺，守晉陽，以纂為右丞。
