entries.en: Late in the reign of Emperor Wu of Wei, Gao Huan went to Luoyang. He left the Duke of Zhao Commandery Chen as mobile headquarters at Jinyang and made Zuan his right vice director.
entries.literal: Late in Emperor Wu of Wei's reign, the Grand Ancestor went to Luoyang; he made the Duke of Zhao Commandery Chen mobile headquarters to guard Jinyang, and made Zuan right vice director.

entries.zh: 轉相府功曹參軍事，除右光祿大夫。
entries.en: He was transferred to merit staff officer in the chancellor's office and appointed right grand master for splendid happiness.
entries.literal: He was transferred to merit staff officer of the chancellor's office and appointed right grand master for splendid happiness.

entries.zh: 使於茹茹，以銜命稱旨。
entries.en: Sent on mission to the Rouran, he carried out his commission to satisfaction and won praise.
entries.literal: Sent on mission to the Rouran; for carrying out orders he won praise.

entries.zh: 歷中外、丞相二府從事中郎。
entries.en: He served in turn as gentleman attendant at the central and outer offices and at the chancellor's office.
entries.literal: He served successively as gentleman attendant at the central and outer offices and at the chancellor's office.

entries.zh: 邙山之役，大獲俘虜，高祖令纂部送京師，魏帝賜絹五百疋，封武安縣伯。
entries.en: At Mount Mang the army took many prisoners. Gao Huan ordered Zuan to escort them to the capital. The Wei emperor bestowed five hundred bolts of silk and enfeoffed him baron of Wu'an County.
entries.literal: At the battle of Mount Mang there was a great capture of prisoners; the Grand Ancestor ordered Zuan to escort them to the capital; the Wei emperor bestowed five hundred bolts of silk and enfeoffed him Baron of Wu'an County.

entries.zh: 復為高祖行臺右丞，從征玉壁。
entries.en: He again became right vice director on Gao Huan's mobile headquarters and followed the campaign against Yubi.
entries.literal: Again he became right vice director of the Grand Ancestor's mobile headquarters and followed the campaign against Yubi.

entries.zh: 大軍將還山東，行達晉州，忽值寒雨，士卒饑凍，至有死者。
entries.en: As the great army was returning to Shandong it reached Jin Province and was struck by cold rain. The troops went hungry and cold; some died.
entries.literal: As the great army was about to return to Shandong, reaching Jin Province, it suddenly met cold rain; the soldiers were hungry and freezing, and some died.

entries.zh: 州以邊禁不聽入城。
entries.en: Because of frontier restrictions the province would not let them enter the city.
entries.literal: The province, because of frontier prohibitions, would not allow entry into the city.

entries.zh: 于時纂為別使，遇見，輒令開門內之，分寄民家，給其火食，多所全濟。
entries.en: Zuan was then on separate mission. When he came upon them he ordered the gates opened at once, lodged the men in private homes, and gave them fire and food. Many were saved.
entries.literal: At that time Zuan was on separate mission; when he encountered them he at once ordered the gates opened to admit them, billeted them among the people, and supplied fire and food — many were saved.

entries.zh: 高祖聞而善之。
entries.en: Gao Huan heard of it and approved.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor heard and approved.

entries.zh: 纂事高祖二十餘歲，傳通教令，甚見親賞。
entries.en: Zuan served Gao Huan for more than twenty years, passing on his orders and instructions, and was held in great favor.
entries.literal: Zuan served the Grand Ancestor more than twenty years, transmitting orders and instructions, and was greatly favored.

entries.zh: 世宗嗣位，侯景作亂潁川，招引西魏。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng succeeded, Hou Jing rebelled in Yingchuan and called in Western Wei.
entries.literal: When the Heir Apparent succeeded, Hou Jing rebelled in Yingchuan and drew in Western Wei.

entries.zh: 以纂為南道行臺，與諸將率討之。
entries.en: Zuan was made south-route mobile headquarters and marched with the generals to suppress him.
entries.literal: Zuan was made south-route mobile headquarters and with the generals led the punitive campaign.

entries.zh: 還，除瀛州刺史。
entries.en: On his return he was appointed inspector of Ying Province.
entries.literal: On his return he was appointed inspector of Ying Province.

entries.zh: 會世宗入為太子少傅。
entries.en: It happened that Gao Cheng entered [the capital] as junior tutor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: It happened that the Heir Apparent entered [the capital] as junior tutor of the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 後與平原王段孝先、行臺尚書辛術等攻圍東楚，仍拔廣陵、涇州數城，斬賊帥東方白額。
entries.en: Later, with Prince of Pingyuan Duan Xiaoxian, mobile headquarters inspector of the masters of writing Xin Shu, and others, he besieged Eastern Chu, then took Guangling, Jing Province, and several cities and beheaded the bandit chieftain Dongfang Baie.
entries.literal: Later, with the Prince of Pingyuan Duan Xiaoxian, mobile headquarters inspector of the masters of writing Xin Shu, and others, he besieged Eastern Chu; he then took Guangling, Jing Province, and several cities and beheaded the bandit chieftain Dongfang Baie.

entries.zh: 授儀同三司，監築長城大使，領步騎數千鎮防北境。
entries.en: He was granted equal in protocol to three imperators, made commissioner for building the Great Wall, and commanded several thousand foot and horse to guard the northern frontier.
entries.literal: He was granted equal in protocol to three imperators, made commissioner for building the Great Wall, and commanded several thousand foot and horse to guard the northern border.

entries.zh: 還，遷護軍將軍，尋卒。
entries.en: On his return he was promoted to guards general; soon afterward he died.
entries.literal: On his return he was promoted to guards general; soon he died.

entries.zh: 張亮，字伯德，西河隰城人也。
entries.en: Zhang Liang, styled Bode, came from Yincheng in Xihe.
entries.literal: Zhang Liang, styled Bode, was a native of Yincheng in Xihe.

entries.zh: 少有幹用。
entries.en: From youth he showed ability and resolve.
entries.literal: In youth he had ability and usefulness.

entries.zh: 初事尒朱兆，拜平遠將軍。
entries.en: He first served Erzhu Zhao and was appointed general who pacifies the distant.
entries.literal: He first served Erzhu Zhao and was appointed general who pacifies the distant.

entries.zh: 以功封隰城縣伯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: For merit he was enfeoffed baron of Yincheng with a fief of five hundred households.
entries.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Yincheng with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 高祖討兆於晉陽，兆奔秀容。
entries.en: Gao Huan attacked Zhao at Jinyang; Zhao fled to Xiurong.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor attacked Zhao at Jinyang; Zhao fled to Xiurong.

entries.zh: 兆左右皆密通誠款，唯亮獨無啟疏。
entries.en: Zhao's close associates all secretly sent pledges of loyalty; only Liang sent no letter.
entries.literal: Zhao's close associates all secretly sent pledges of loyalty; only Liang sent no memorial.

entries.zh: 及兆敗，竄於窮山，令亮及倉頭陳山提斬己首以降，皆不忍，兆乃自縊於樹。
entries.en: When Zhao was defeated he hid in the mountains and ordered Liang and his steward Chen Shanti to cut off his head and surrender. Neither could bear to do it. Zhao then hanged himself from a tree.
entries.literal: When Zhao was defeated he hid in remote mountains and ordered Liang and the steward Chen Shanti to cut off his head to surrender; none could bear to do it, and Zhao then hanged himself on a tree.

entries.zh: 伯德伏屍而哭。
entries.en: Bode knelt by the corpse and wept.
entries.literal: Bode knelt by the corpse and wept.

entries.zh: 高祖嘉歎之。
entries.en: Gao Huan praised him and sighed with admiration.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor praised and sighed at this.

entries.zh: 授丞相府參軍事，漸見親待，委以書記之任。
entries.en: He was appointed staff officer in the chancellor's office, gradually won intimate favor, and was put in charge of correspondence.
entries.literal: He was appointed staff officer of the chancellor's office, gradually received intimate treatment, and was entrusted with secretary duties.

entries.zh: 天平中，為世宗行臺郎中，典七兵事。
entries.en: During Tianping he was Gao Cheng's mobile headquarters gentleman, in charge of the seven military bureaus.
entries.literal: During Tianping he was the Heir Apparent's mobile headquarters gentleman, in charge of the seven military bureaus.

entries.zh: 雖為臺郎，而常在高祖左右。
entries.en: Though a headquarters gentleman, he was constantly at Gao Huan's side.
entries.literal: Though a headquarters gentleman, he was constantly at the Grand Ancestor's side.

entries.zh: 遷行臺右丞。
entries.en: He was promoted to right vice director of the mobile headquarters.
entries.literal: He was promoted to right vice director of the mobile headquarters.

entries.zh: 亮性質直，勤力強濟，深為高祖、世宗所信，委以腹心之任。
entries.en: Liang was plain and upright by nature, diligent and forceful. Gao Huan and Gao Cheng trusted him deeply and gave him duties at the heart of power.
entries.literal: Liang was upright and plain by nature, diligent and forceful, and was deeply trusted by the Grand Ancestor and the Heir Apparent, who entrusted him with innermost duties.

entries.zh: 然少風格，好財利，久在左右，不能廉潔，及歷諸州，咸有黷貨之聞。
entries.en: Yet he lacked refinement and loved profit. Long at their side he could not stay clean, and in every province he held there were reports of corrupt taking.
entries.literal: Yet he lacked refinement, loved wealth, and though long at their side could not remain incorrupt; in every province he held office there were reports of bribery.

entries.zh: 武定末，征拜侍中、汾州大中正。
entries.en: At the end of Wuding he was summoned as palace attendant and chief rectifier of Fen Province.
entries.literal: At the end of Wuding he was summoned as palace attendant and chief rectifier of Fen Province.

entries.zh: 天保初，授光祿勳，加驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，別封安定縣男，轉中領軍。
entries.en: Early in Tianbao he was appointed grand warden of glory, given the added titles grand general of the flying cavalry and equal in protocol to three imperators, separately enfeoffed baron of Anding, and transferred to commander of the palace guards.
entries.literal: Early in Tianbao he was appointed grand warden of glory, added grand general of the flying cavalry and equal in protocol to three imperators, separately enfeoffed baron of Anding, and transferred to commander of the palace guards.

entries.zh: 尋卒於位，贈司空公。
entries.en: Soon he died in office and was posthumously granted duke of works.
entries.literal: Soon he died in office and was posthumously granted Duke of Works.

entries.zh: 張耀，字靈光，上谷昌平人也。
entries.en: Zhang Yao, styled Lingguang, came from Changping in Shanggu.
entries.literal: Zhang Yao, styled Lingguang, was a native of Changping in Shanggu.

entries.zh: 父鳳，晉州長史。
entries.en: His father Feng had been chief clerk of Jin Province.
entries.literal: His father Feng was chief clerk of Jin Province.

entries.zh: 耀少而貞謹，頗曉史職。
entries.en: From youth Yao was upright and careful and knew the work of records and administration well.
entries.literal: Yao from youth was upright and careful and well understood historical and administrative duties.

entries.zh: 解褐給事中，轉司徒水曹行參軍。
entries.en: On first appointment he was attendant within the palace gates, then transferred to water bureau attendant staff officer under the Ministry of Education.
entries.literal: On first appointment he was attendant within the palace gates; he was transferred to water bureau attendant staff officer of the Ministry of Education.

entries.zh: 義旗建，高祖擢為中軍大都督韓軌府長史。
entries.en: When the righteous standard was raised Gao Huan promoted him to chief clerk on General-in-Chief Han Gui's staff.
entries.literal: When the righteous standard was raised the Grand Ancestor promoted him to chief clerk of General-in-Chief Han Gui's headquarters.

entries.zh: 及軌除瀛、冀二州刺史，又以耀為軌諮議參軍。
entries.en: When Gui was made inspector of Ying and Ji, Yao again served as his consulting staff officer.
entries.literal: When Gui was made inspector of Ying and Ji, Yao was again made Gui's consulting staff officer.

entries.zh: 後為御史所劾，州府僚佐及軌左右以贓罪掛網者百有餘人，唯耀清白獨免。
entries.en: Later the censors impeached the case. More than a hundred prefectural staff and men close to Gui were caught in the net on corruption charges; only Yao was clear and escaped alone.
entries.literal: Later he was impeached by the censor; prefectural staff and Gui's close associates — over a hundred caught in the net on corruption charges — only Yao was clear and alone escaped.

entries.zh: 徵為丞相府倉曹。
entries.en: He was summoned to serve as warehouse clerk in the chancellor's office.
entries.literal: He was summoned as warehouse clerk of the chancellor's office.

entries.zh: 趙起，字興洛，廣平人也。
entries.en: Zhao Qi, styled Xingluo, came from Guangping.
entries.literal: Zhao Qi, styled Xingluo, was a native of Guangping.

entries.zh: 父達，幽州錄事參軍。
entries.en: His father Da had been recording clerk of You Province.
entries.literal: His father Da was recording clerk of You Province.

entries.zh: 起性沈謹有幹用。
entries.en: Qi was deep, careful, and capable.
entries.literal: Qi was deep, careful, and capable.

entries.zh: 義旗建，高祖以段榮為定州刺史，以起為榮典簽，除奉車都尉。
entries.en: When the righteous standard was raised Gao Huan made Duan Rong inspector of Ding and made Qi Rong's secretariat chief; Qi was appointed cavalier attendant for the carriage.
entries.literal: When the righteous standard was raised the Grand Ancestor made Duan Rong inspector of Ding and made Qi Rong's secretariat chief; he was appointed cavalier attendant for the carriage.

entries.zh: 天平中，徵為相府騎曹，累加中散大夫。
entries.en: During Tianping he was summoned to the horse bureau of the chancellor's office and rose repeatedly to palace gentleman for scattering ailments.
entries.literal: During Tianping he was summoned as horse bureau clerk of the chancellor's office and was repeatedly promoted to palace gentleman for scattering ailments.

entries.zh: 世宗嗣事，出為建州刺史，累遷侍中。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng succeeded Qi was sent out as inspector of Jian and rose repeatedly to palace attendant.
entries.literal: When the Heir Apparent succeeded to affairs Qi was sent out as inspector of Jian and was repeatedly promoted to palace attendant.

entries.zh: 起，高祖世頻為相府騎兵二局，典知兵馬十有餘年。
entries.en: Across Gao Huan's generation Qi repeatedly held the two cavalry bureaus of the chancellor's office and managed horses and troops for more than ten years.
entries.literal: Qi, across the Grand Ancestor's generation, repeatedly held the two cavalry bureaus of the chancellor's office and was in charge of horses and troops for more than ten years.

entries.zh: 至顯祖卽阼之後，起罷州還闕，雖歷位九卿、侍中，常以本官監兵馬，出內驅使，居腹心之寄，與二張相亞。
entries.en: After Gao Yang took the throne Qi left the provinces and returned to court. Though he held ranks of the nine ministers and palace attendant, he always kept his original post supervising troops, going in and out at command, trusted at the heart of power — second only to the two Zhangs.
entries.literal: After the Manifest Ancestor assumed the throne Qi left provincial office and returned to court; though he held ranks of the nine ministers and palace attendant, he always kept his original post supervising troops, coming and going at command, trusted as an inner confidant, second only to the two Zhangs.

entries.zh: 出為西兗州刺史，糾劾禁止，歲餘，以無驗獲免。
entries.en: He was sent out as inspector of West Yan Province, where he investigated and enforced prohibitions. After more than a year he was cleared when the charges could not be proved.
entries.literal: He was sent out as inspector of West Yan Province, investigated and prohibited [wrongdoing], and after more than a year was dismissed when nothing was proved.

entries.zh: 河清二年，徵還晉陽。
entries.en: In the second year of Heqing he was summoned back to Jinyang.
entries.literal: In the second year of Heqing he was summoned back to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 三年，又加祠部尚書、開府。
entries.en: In the third year he was additionally made minister of sacrificial worships and opener of government.
entries.literal: In the third year he was additionally made minister of sacrificial worships and opener of government.

entries.zh: 天統初，轉太常卿，食瑯邪郡幹。
entries.en: Early in Tiantong he was transferred to chamberlain for imperial ceremonial and drew his salary allotment from Langye Commandery.
entries.literal: Early in Tiantong he was transferred to chamberlain for imperial ceremonial with a salary allotment from Langye Commandery.

entries.zh: 二年，除滄州刺史，加六州都督。
entries.en: In the second year he was made inspector of Cang and added commander of six provinces.
entries.literal: In the second year he was made inspector of Cang and added commander of six provinces.

entries.zh: 武平中，卒於官。
entries.en: Midway through Wuping he died in office.
entries.literal: Midway through Wuping he died in office.

entries.zh: 徐遠，字彥遐，廣寧石門人也。
entries.en: Xu Yuan, styled Yanxia, came from Shimen in Guangning.
entries.literal: Xu Yuan, styled Yanxia, was a native of Shimen in Guangning.

entries.zh: 其先出自廣平。
entries.en: His ancestors had originally come from Guangping.
entries.literal: His ancestors originally came from Guangping.

entries.zh: 曾祖定，為雲中軍將、平朔戍主，因家於朔。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Ding had been general of the army in Yun and garrison chief of Pingshuo; the family then settled at Shuo.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Ding was general of the army in Yun and garrison chief of Pingshuo; the family then settled at Shuo.

entries.zh: 遠少習吏事，郡辟功曹。
entries.en: In youth Yuan studied clerical work; the commandery recruited him as merit officer.
entries.literal: Yuan in youth studied clerical affairs; the commandery recruited him as merit officer.

entries.zh: 未幾，與太守率戶赴義旗，署防城都督，除癭陶縣令。
entries.en: Before long he went with the inspector, leading local households to the righteous standard. He was appointed defense commander of the city and made magistrate of Yingtao.
entries.literal: Before long, with the inspector he led households to the righteous standard; he was appointed defense commander of the city and made magistrate of Yingtao.

entries.zh: 高祖以遠閑習書計，命為丞相騎兵參軍事，常征伐，克濟軍務，深為高祖所知。
entries.en: Because Yuan was skilled in documents and accounts Gao Huan appointed him cavalry staff officer in the chancellor's office. He was often on campaign, handled military affairs well, and came to be well known to Gao Huan.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor, because Yuan was skilled in documents and accounts, appointed him cavalry staff officer of the chancellor's office; he was often on campaigns, succeeded in military affairs, and was deeply known to the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 累歷鉅鹿、陳留二郡太守。
entries.en: He served in turn as inspector of Julu and Chenliu.
entries.literal: He successively served as inspector of Julu and Chenliu.

entries.zh: 天保初，為御史所劾，遇赦免，沉廢二年。
entries.en: Early in Tianbao the censors impeached him. He met an amnesty and was pardoned, then lay idle for two years.
entries.literal: Early in Tianbao he was impeached by the censor; he met an amnesty and was pardoned and was suspended for two years.

entries.zh: 顯祖以遠勳舊，特用為領軍府長史，累遷東徐州刺史，入為太中大夫。
entries.en: Because Yuan was an old meritorious servant, Gao Yang specially made him Chief Clerk of the Headquarters of the General Who Commands the Army. He rose repeatedly to Inspector of East Xu Province and entered the capital as Grand Master of the Palace.
entries.literal: Because Yuan was an old meritorious servant, Gao Yang specially made him Chief Clerk of the Headquarters of the General Who Commands the Army. He rose repeatedly to Inspector of East Xu Province and entered the capital as Grand Master of the Palace.

entries.zh: 河清初，加衛將軍。
entries.en: Early in Heqing he was made guard general.
entries.literal: Early in Heqing, he was made guard general.

entries.zh: 二年，除使持節、都督東楚州諸軍事、東楚州刺史。
entries.en: In the second year he was appointed bearer of the staff with extraordinary powers, area commander-in-chief of Eastern Chuzhou military affairs, and governor of Eastern Chuzhou.
entries.literal: In the second year he was appointed bearer of the staff of office with extraordinary powers, area commander-in-chief of Eastern Chuzhou military affairs, and governor of Eastern Chuzhou.

entries.zh: 天統二年，授儀同三司、衛尉。
entries.en: In the second year of Tian tong he was granted equal in insignia to three masters of ceremonies and made commandant of the guards.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tian tong he was granted equal in insignia to three masters of ceremonies and made commandant of the guards.

entries.zh: 四年，加開府、右光祿大夫。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was given opening of a government office and grand master for splendid happiness of the right.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was given opening of a government office and made grand master for splendid happiness of the right.

entries.zh: 武平初卒。
entries.en: He died at the beginning of Wuping.
entries.literal: He died at the beginning of Wuping.

entries.zh: 王峻，字巒嵩，靈丘人也。
entries.en: Wang Jun, styled Luansong, was a native of Lingqiu.
entries.literal: Wang Jun, styled Luansong, was a native of Lingqiu.

entries.zh: 明悟有幹略。
entries.en: He was clear-minded and possessed resource and strategy.
entries.literal: He was clear-minded and possessed resource and strategy.

entries.zh: 高祖以為相府墨曹參軍，坐事去官。
entries.en: Gao Huan made him ink-office clerk in the chancellor's government; for an offense he was removed from office.
entries.literal: Gao Huan made him ink-office clerk in the chancellor's government; for an offense he was removed from office.

entries.zh: 久之，顯祖為儀同開府，引為城局參軍。
entries.en: After a long while, when Gao Yang was equal in insignia with an opening office, he was brought in as clerk of the city bureau.
entries.literal: After a long while, when Gao Yang was equal in insignia with an opening office, he was brought in as clerk of the city bureau.

entries.zh: 累遷恒州大中正、世宗相府外兵參軍。
entries.en: He rose in succession to chief impartial judge of Heng Province and outer-troops clerk in Gao Cheng's chancellor's office.
entries.literal: He rose in succession to chief impartial judge of Heng Province and outer-troops clerk in Shizong's chancellor's office.

entries.zh: 隨諸軍平淮陰，賜爵北平縣男。
entries.en: Following the armies he pacified Huaiyin and was enfeoffed baron of Beiping county.
entries.literal: Following the armies he pacified Huaiyin and was enfeoffed baron of Beiping county.

entries.zh: 除營州刺史。
entries.en: He was made governor of Ying Province.
entries.literal: He was made governor of Ying Province.

entries.zh: 興和中，世宗召為庫直，除奉朝請。
entries.en: During Xinghe, Gao Cheng summoned him as vault attendant and made him court gentleman attendant.
entries.literal: In Xinghe Zhong, Shizong summoned him as vault attendant and made him court gentleman attendant.

entries.zh: 世宗暴崩，纮冒刃捍禦，以忠節賜爵平春縣男，賚帛七百段、綾錦五十疋、錢三萬並金帶駿馬，仍除晉陽令。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng died suddenly, Hong braved blades to ward off attack and for loyal fidelity was granted the rank baron of Pingchun county, given seven hundred bolts of cloth, fifty bolts of damask silk, thirty thousand cash, and a gold belt and fine horse, and was made magistrate of Jinyang.
entries.literal: When Shizong died suddenly, Hong braved blades to ward off attack and for loyal fidelity was granted the rank baron of Pingchun county, given seven hundred bolts of cloth, fifty bolts of damask silk, thirty thousand cash, and a gold belt and fine horse, and was made magistrate of Jinyang.

entries.zh: 武定初，拜太中大夫。
entries.en: Early in Wuding he was appointed grand master for splendid happiness.
entries.literal: Early in Wuding he was appointed grand master for splendid happiness in the central government.

entries.zh: 薛琡嘗夢亮於山上持絲，以告亮，且占之曰：「山上絲，幽字也。
entries.en: Xue Jun once dreamed of Liang on a mountain holding silk. He told Liang and divined, saying, "Silk on a mountain — that is the character for 'hidden' (you).
entries.literal: Xue Jun once dreamed of Liang on a mountain holding silk; he told Liang and divined, saying: "Silk on a mountain — the character for 'hidden' (you).

entries.zh: 君其為幽州乎？」
entries.en: Will you become inspector of You Province?"
entries.literal: Will you become inspector of You Province?"

entries.zh: 數月，亮出為幽州刺史。
entries.en: Several months later Liang was sent out as inspector of You Province.
entries.literal: Several months later Liang went out as inspector of You Province.

entries.zh: 屬侯景叛，除平南將軍、梁州刺史。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled, he was appointed general who pacifies the south and governor of Liang Province.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, he was made general who pacifies the south and governor of Liang Province.

entries.zh: 尋加都督揚、潁等十一州諸軍事，兼行臺殿中尚書，轉都督二豫、揚、潁等八州軍事、征西大將軍、豫州刺史、尚書右僕射、西南道行臺。
entries.en: Soon he was additionally commander of military affairs for eleven provinces including Yang and Ying, concurrently mobile headquarters director of palace masters in the interior, then transferred to commander of eight provinces including the two Yu, Yang, and Ying, grand general who campaigns west, inspector of Yu, right vice director of the masters of writing, and southwest-route mobile headquarters.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally made commander of military affairs for eleven provinces including Yang and Ying, concurrently mobile headquarters director of palace masters in the interior, then transferred to commander of military affairs for eight provinces including the two Yu, Yang, and Ying, grand general who campaigns west, inspector of Yu, right vice director of the masters of writing, and southwest-route mobile headquarters.

entries.zh: 攻梁江夏、潁陽等七城，皆下之。
entries.en: He attacked Liang's Jiangxia, Yingyang, and seven other cities; all fell.
entries.literal: He attacked Liang's Jiangxia, Yingyang, and seven other cities; all were taken.

entries.zh: 纮少好弓馬，善騎射，頗愛文學。
entries.en: Hong from youth loved bow and horse and was skilled in mounted archery; he also delighted in letters.
entries.literal: Hong from youth loved bow and horse and was skilled in mounted archery; he also delighted in letters.

entries.zh: 性機敏，應對便捷。
entries.en: His nature was sharp and quick, and his replies came readily.
entries.literal: His nature was sharp and quick, and his replies came readily.

entries.zh: 年十三，見揚州刺史太原郭元貞，元貞撫其背曰：「汝讀何書？」
entries.en: At thirteen he met Guo Yuanzhen of Taiyuan, governor of Yang Province; Yuanzhen stroked his back and said, "What books do you read?"
entries.literal: At thirteen he met Guo Yuanzhen of Taiyuan, governor of Yang Province; Yuanzhen stroked his back and said, "What books do you read?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「誦《孝經》。」
entries.en: He replied, "I recite the Classic of Filial Piety."
entries.literal: He replied, "I recite the Classic of Filial Piety."

entries.zh: 曰：「《孝經》云何？」
entries.en: He said, "What does the Classic of Filial Piety say?"
entries.literal: He said, "What does the Classic of Filial Piety say?"

entries.zh: 曰：「在上不驕，為下不亂。」
entries.en: He said, "He who is above is not arrogant; he who is below does not rebel."
entries.literal: He said, "He who is above is not arrogant; he who is below does not rebel."

entries.zh: 元貞曰：「吾作刺史，豈其驕乎？」
entries.en: Yuanzhen said, "I serve as governor — am I arrogant?"
entries.literal: Yuanzhen said, "I serve as governor — am I arrogant?"

entries.zh: 纮曰：「公雖不驕，君子防未萌，亦願留意。」
entries.en: Hong said, "Though you are not arrogant, a gentleman guards against what has not yet sprouted; I too hope you will take note."
entries.literal: Hong said, "Though you are not arrogant, a gentleman guards against what has not yet sprouted; I too hope you will take note."

entries.zh: 元貞稱善。
entries.en: Yuanzhen praised him.
entries.literal: Yuanzhen praised him.

entries.zh: 年十五，隨父在北豫州，行臺侯景與人論掩衣法為當左為當右。
entries.en: At fifteen he followed his father in Northern Yu Province; the traveling staff's Hou Jing debated with others whether the lapel should be right or left.
entries.literal: At fifteen he followed his father in Northern Yu Province; the traveling staff's Hou Jing debated with others whether the lapel should be right or left.

entries.zh: 尚書敬顯儁曰：「孔子云：『微管仲，吾其被發左衽矣』以此言之，右衽為是。」
entries.en: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."
entries.literal: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."

entries.zh: 纮進曰：「國家龍飛朔野，雄步中原，五帝異儀，三王殊制，掩衣左右，何足是非。」
entries.en: Hong advanced and said, "Our state rose like a dragon in the northern wilds and strides heroically through the Central Plain; the Five Emperors had different institutions and the Three Kings different systems — whether the lapel is left or right is hardly worth arguing over."
entries.literal: Hong advanced and said, "Our state rose like a dragon in the northern wilds and strides heroically through the Central Plain; the Five Emperors had different institutions and the Three Kings different systems — whether the lapel is left or right is hardly worth arguing over."

entries.zh: 景奇其早慧，賜以名馬。
entries.en: Jing marveled at his early brilliance and bestowed a famous horse on him.
entries.literal: Jing marveled at his early brilliance and bestowed a famous horse on him.

entries.zh: 耀歷事累世，奉職恪勤，咸見親待，未嘗有過。
entries.en: Yao served through successive reigns. He was diligent and careful in office, was trusted and treated closely in each reign, and never committed a fault.
entries.literal: Yao served through successive reigns; in carrying out his duties he was diligent and careful, and in each reign he was trusted and treated closely, never committing a fault.

entries.zh: 每得祿賜，散之宗族。
entries.en: Whenever he received salary or gifts, he distributed them among his clan.
entries.literal: Whenever he received salary or gifts, he distributed them among his clan.

entries.zh: 性節儉率素，車服飲食，取給而已。
entries.en: Frugal and plain by nature, he used only what was sufficient in carriages, clothing, food, and drink.
entries.literal: By nature he was frugal, simple, and plain; in carriage, clothing, food, and drink he took only what was sufficient.

entries.zh: 好讀《春秋》，月一遍，時人比之賈梁道。
entries.en: He loved reading the Spring and Autumn Annals and went through it once a month; contemporaries compared him to Jia Liangdao.
entries.literal: He loved reading the Spring and Autumn Annals and went through it once a month; people of the time compared him to Jia Liangdao.

entries.zh: 趙彥深嘗謂耀曰：「君研尋《左氏》，豈求服虔、杜預之紕繆邪？」
entries.en: Zhao Yanshen once said to Yao, "In studying the Zuo Tradition, are you trying to find errors in Fu Qian and Du Yu?"
entries.literal: Zhao Yanshen once said to Yao, "When you study and search the Zuo Tradition, are you seeking the errors of Fu Qian and Du Yu?"

entries.zh: 耀曰：「何為其然乎？
entries.en: Yao said, "Why would that be so?
entries.literal: Yao said, "Why would that be so?

entries.zh: 《左氏》之書，備敘言事，惡者可以自戒，善者可以庶幾。
entries.en: The Zuo Tradition fully sets forth words and events; the bad can warn oneself, and the good can be something to aspire to.
entries.literal: The book of the Zuo Tradition fully sets forth words and events; what is bad can be used to warn oneself, and what is good can be aspired to.

entries.zh: 故厲己溫習，非欲詆訶古人之得失也。」
entries.en: That is why I discipline myself by reviewing it; I am not trying to criticize the successes and failures of ancient men."
entries.literal: Therefore I discipline myself and review it; I do not wish to criticize and fault the gains and losses of men of antiquity."

entries.zh: 天統元年，世祖臨朝，耀奏事，遇暴疾，仆於御前。
entries.en: In the first year of Tiantong, while Shizu was holding court, Yao was presenting business when he suffered a sudden illness and collapsed before the emperor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tiantong, when Shizu held court, Yao was presenting affairs when he suffered a sudden illness and collapsed before the emperor.

entries.zh: 帝下座臨視，呼數聲不應。
entries.en: The emperor came down from his seat to look over him and called several times, but Yao did not respond.
entries.literal: The emperor descended from his seat and looked over him, calling several times, but Yao did not respond.

entries.zh: 帝泣曰：「豈失我良臣也！」
entries.en: The emperor wept and said, "Have I lost my good minister!"
entries.literal: The emperor wept and said, "Have I lost my good minister!"

entries.zh: 旬日卒，時年六十三。
entries.en: He died ten days later at the age of sixty-three.
entries.literal: After ten days he died, at the age of sixty-three.

entries.zh: 詔稱耀忠貞平直，溫恭廉慎。
entries.en: The edict praised Yao as loyal and steadfast, fair and upright, warm, respectful, incorrupt, and careful.
entries.literal: The edict praised Yao as loyal, steadfast, fair, upright, warm, respectful, incorrupt, and careful.

entries.zh: 贈開府儀同三司、尚書右僕射、燕州刺史，諡曰貞簡。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted Opening Office with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Inspector of Yan Province; his posthumous title was Zhenjian.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted Opening Office with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Inspector of Yan Province; his posthumous title was Zhenjian.

entries.zh: 天保初，加寧遠將軍，頗為顯祖所知待。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianbao he was made general who pacifies the distant and was much known and favored by Gao Yang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was made general who pacifies the distant and was much known and favored by Gao Yang.

entries.zh: 帝嘗與左右飲酒，曰：「快哉大樂。」
entries.en: Once when the emperor was drinking with his attendants he said, "How great the joy!"
entries.literal: Once when the emperor was drinking with his attendants he said, "How great the joy!"

entries.zh: 纮對曰：「亦有大樂，亦有大苦。」
entries.en: Hong replied, "There is also great joy and great bitterness."
entries.literal: Hong replied, "There is also great joy and great bitterness."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「何為大苦？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "What is great bitterness?"
entries.literal: The emperor said, "What is great bitterness?"

entries.zh: 纮曰：「長夜荒飲不寤，亡國破家，身死名滅，所謂大苦。」
entries.en: Hong said, "Long nights of reckless drinking without waking — ruined state and shattered house, body dead and name extinguished: that is what is called great bitterness."
entries.literal: Hong said, "Long nights of reckless drinking without waking — ruined state and shattered house, body dead and name extinguished: that is what is called great bitterness."

entries.zh: 帝默然。
entries.en: The emperor fell silent.
entries.literal: The emperor fell silent.

entries.zh: 後責纮曰：「爾與紇奚舍樂同事我兄，舍樂死，爾何為不死？」
entries.en: Later he reproached Hong: "You served my brother together with Hexi Shele; when Shele died, why did you not die?"
entries.literal: Later he reproached Hong: "You served my brother together with Hexi Shele; when Shele died, why did you not die?"

entries.zh: 纮曰：「君亡臣死，自是常節，但賊豎力薄斫輕，故臣不死。」
entries.en: Hong said, "When the lord perishes the minister dies — that is the constant rule; but the rebel brutes' blows were weak and their cuts light, so your servant did not die."
entries.literal: Hong said, "When the lord perishes the minister dies — that is the constant rule; but the rebel brutes' blows were weak and their cuts light, so your servant did not die."

entries.zh: 帝使燕子獻反縛纮，長廣王捉頭，帝手刃將下，纮曰：「楊遵彥、崔季舒逃走避難，位至僕射、尚書，冒死效命之士，反見屠戮，曠古未有此事。」
entries.en: The emperor had Yan Zixian bind Hong in reverse, the Prince of Changgang seized his head, and the emperor was about to strike with his blade; Hong said, "Yang Zunyian and Cui Jishu fled to avoid disaster yet rose to vice director and minister; men who risked death in loyal service are instead slaughtered — never in antiquity was there such a thing."
entries.literal: The emperor had Yan Zixian bind Hong in reverse, the Prince of Changgang seized his head, and the emperor was about to strike with his blade; Hong said, "Yang Zunyian and Cui Jishu fled to avoid disaster yet rose to vice director and minister; men who risked death in loyal service are instead slaughtered — never in antiquity was there such a thing."

entries.zh: 帝投刃於地曰：「王師羅不得殺。」
entries.en: The emperor cast his blade to the ground and said, "Wang Shiluo must not be killed."
entries.literal: The emperor cast his blade to the ground and said, "Wang Shiluo must not be killed."

entries.zh: 遂捨之。
entries.en: Thereupon he spared him.
entries.literal: Thereupon he spared him.

entries.zh: 張纂 張亮 張耀 趙起 徐遠 王峻 王紘
entries.en: Zhang Zuan; Zhang Liang; Zhang Yao; Zhao Qi; Xu Yuan; Wang Jun; Wang Hong
entries.literal: Zhang Zuan; Zhang Liang; Zhang Yao; Zhao Qi; Xu Yuan; Wang Jun; Wang Hong

entries.zh: 天平初，高祖引為丞相長史。
entries.en: Early in Tianping, Gao Huan brought him in as chief administrator of the chancellor's office.
entries.literal: Early in Tianping, the Grand Ancestor brought him in as chief administrator of the chancellor's office.

entries.zh: 琡宿有能名，深被禮遇，軍國之事，多所聞知。
entries.en: Chu had long been known for ability and was treated with great courtesy; he was consulted on many matters of army and state.
entries.literal: Chu had long been known for ability and was treated with great courtesy; he was consulted on many matters of army and state.

entries.zh: 琡亦推誠盡節，屢進忠讜。
entries.en: Chu likewise gave loyal service with full devotion and repeatedly offered forthright remonstrance.
entries.literal: Chu likewise gave loyal service with full devotion and repeatedly offered forthright remonstrance.

entries.zh: 高祖大舉西伐，將度蒲津。
entries.en: Gao Huan launched a great western campaign and was about to cross the Pu ford.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor launched a great western campaign and was about to cross the Pu ford.

entries.zh: 琡諫曰：「西賊連年饑饉，無可食啖，故冒死來入陜州，欲取倉粟。
entries.en: Chu remonstrated, saying, "The western rebels have suffered famine year after year; they have nothing to eat. That is why they risk death to enter Shaan Province — to seize grain from the granaries.
entries.literal: Chu remonstrated, saying, "The western rebels have suffered famine year after year; they have nothing to eat. That is why they risk death to enter Shaan Province — to seize grain from the granaries.

entries.zh: 今高司徒已圍陜城，粟不得出。
entries.en: Now Minister Gao has already invested Tong Pass; the grain cannot get out.
entries.literal: Now Minister Gao has already invested Tong Pass; the grain cannot get out.

entries.zh: 但置兵諸道，勿與野戰，比及來年麥秋，人民盡應餓死，寶炬、黑獺，自然歸降。
entries.en: Simply place troops on the roads and do not fight in the open field. By next year's wheat harvest the people will all have starved; Bao Ju and Hei Hu will surrender of themselves.
entries.literal: Simply place troops on the roads and do not fight in the open field. By next year's wheat harvest the people will all have starved; Bao Ju and Hei Hu will surrender of themselves.

entries.zh: 願王無渡河也。」
entries.en: I beg Your Highness not to cross the river."
entries.literal: I beg Your Highness not to cross the river."

entries.zh: 侯景亦曰：「今者之舉，兵衆極大，萬一不捷，卒難收斂。
entries.en: Hou Jing also said, "This expedition's forces are immense; if by any chance we do not prevail, they will be hard to gather in again.
entries.literal: Hou Jing also said, "This expedition's forces are immense; if by any chance we do not prevail, they will be hard to gather in again.

entries.zh: 不如分為二軍，相繼而進，前軍若勝，後軍合力，前軍若敗，後軍承之。」
entries.en: Better to divide into two armies and advance in succession: if the vanguard wins, the rear joins its strength; if the vanguard falls, the rear takes up the fight."
entries.literal: Better to divide into two armies and advance in succession: if the vanguard wins, the rear joins its strength; if the vanguard falls, the rear takes up the fight."

entries.zh: 高祖皆不納，遂有沙苑之敗。
entries.en: Gao Huan accepted neither counsel, and thus came the defeat at Shaoyuan.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor accepted neither counsel, and thus came the defeat at Shaoyuan.

entries.zh: 累遷尚書僕射，卒。
entries.en: He rose in repeated promotions to vice director of the masters of writing and died.
entries.literal: He rose in repeated promotions to vice director of the masters of writing and died.

entries.zh: 臨終勑其子斂以時服，逾月便葬，不聽干求贈官。
entries.en: On his deathbed he charged his sons to lay him out in seasonable dress, bury him after a single month, and not solicit posthumous office by importuning.
entries.literal: On his deathbed he charged his sons to lay him out in seasonable dress, bury him after a single month, and not solicit posthumous office by importuning.

entries.zh: 自制喪車，不加雕飾，但用麻為流蘇，繩用網絡而已。
entries.en: He himself made his funeral carriage without carving or ornament, using only hemp for tassels and net cord for ropes.
entries.literal: He himself made his funeral carriage without carving or ornament, using only hemp for tassels and net cord for ropes.

entries.zh: 明器等物並不令置。
entries.en: He forbade altogether the setting out of spirit objects and the like.
entries.literal: He forbade altogether the setting out of spirit objects and the like.

entries.zh: 高祖起義信都，鑒自歸。
entries.en: When Gao Huan raised the righteous standard at Xindu, Jian came over to him of his own accord.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous standard at Xindu, Jian came over to him of his own accord.

entries.zh: 高祖謂鑒曰：「日者皇綱中弛，公已早竭忠誠。
entries.en: Gao Huan said to Jian, "In days past the imperial net slackened at the center, yet you had already early spent your loyalty.
entries.literal: Gao Huan said to Jian, "In days past the imperial net slackened at the center, yet you had already early exhausted your loyalty.

entries.zh: 今尒朱披猖，又能去逆從善。
entries.en: Now that Erzhu runs riot, you can again leave rebellion and follow what is right.
entries.literal: Now that Erzhu runs riot, you can again leave rebellion and follow what is right.

entries.zh: 搖落之時，方識松筠。」
entries.en: When the branches fall, one knows the pine and bamboo."
entries.literal: When the branches fall, one knows the pine and bamboo."

entries.zh: 即啟授征西。
entries.en: He at once recommended him and appointed him western campaign general.
entries.literal: He at once recommended him and appointed him western campaign general.

entries.zh: 懷州刺史。
entries.en: Inspector of Huai Province.
entries.literal: Inspector of Huai Province.

entries.zh: 敬顯儁，字孝英，平陽人。
entries.en: Jing Xianjun, styled Xiaoying, was a native of Pingyang.
entries.literal: Jing Xianjun, styled Xiaoying, was a native of Pingyang.

entries.zh: 少英俠有節操，交結豪傑。
entries.en: In youth he was heroic and chivalrous and kept his integrity; he formed ties with bold fellows.
entries.literal: In youth he was heroic and chivalrous and had integrity; he formed ties with bold fellows.

entries.zh: 為羽林監。
entries.en: He was made commandant of the forest guard.
entries.literal: He was made commandant of the forest guard.

entries.zh: 高祖臨晉州，儁因使謁見，與語說之，乃啟為別駕。
entries.en: When Gao Huan took up Jin Province, Xianjun used the occasion to pay his respects. Gao Huan spoke with him and was pleased, then had him appointed vice governor.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan took up Jin Province, Xianjun took the occasion to pay his respects. Gao Huan spoke with him and was pleased, then recommended him as vice governor.

entries.zh: 及義舉，以儁為行臺倉部郎中。
entries.en: When the righteous rising was launched, he was made mobile headquarters clerk in the supplies bureau.
entries.literal: When the righteous rising was launched, Xianjun was made mobile headquarters clerk in the supplies bureau.

entries.zh: 從攻鄴，令儁督造土山。
entries.en: On the attack on Ye he had Xianjun supervise construction of the earthen ramp.
entries.literal: Following the attack on Ye, he ordered Xianjun to supervise construction of the earthen ramp.

entries.zh: 城拔，又從平西胡。
entries.en: When the city fell he again followed in pacifying the western barbarians.
entries.literal: When the city was taken, he again followed in pacifying the western barbarians.

entries.zh: 轉都官尚書，與諸將征討，累有功。
entries.en: He was transferred to director of the imperial punishments bureau and, campaigning with the generals, won repeated merit.
entries.literal: He was transferred to director of the imperial punishments bureau and, with the generals on campaign, repeatedly had merit.

entries.zh: 又從高祖平寇難，破周文帝。
entries.en: He again followed Gao Huan in pacifying rebellion and defeated Yuwen Tai.
entries.literal: He again followed Gao Huan in pacifying rebellion and defeated Yuwen Tai.

entries.zh: 敗侯景，平壽春，定淮南。
entries.en: He defeated Hou Jing, pacified Shouchun, and settled Huainan.
entries.literal: He defeated Hou Jing, pacified Shouchun, and settled Huainan.

entries.zh: 又略地三江口，多築城戍。
entries.en: He also seized territory at Sanjiang Ford and built many garrison towns.
entries.literal: He also seized territory at Sanjiang Ford and built many garrison towns.

entries.zh: 累除兗州刺史，卒。
entries.en: In succession he was made inspector of Yan Province and died.
entries.literal: In succession he was made Yan Province inspector and died.

entries.zh: 平鑒，字明達，燕郡薊人。
entries.en: Ping Jian, styled Mingda, was a native of Ji in Yan Commandery.
entries.literal: Ping Jian, styled Mingda, was a native of Ji in Yan Commandery.

entries.zh: 父勝，安州刺史。
entries.en: His father Sheng was inspector of An Province.
entries.literal: His father Sheng was An Province inspector.

entries.zh: 鑒少聰敏，頗有志力。
entries.en: From youth Jian was clever and keen, with considerable resolve and strength.
entries.literal: Jian from youth was clever and keen, and had considerable resolve and strength.

entries.zh: 受學於徐遵明，不為章句，雖崇儒業，而有豪俠氣。
entries.en: He studied under Xu Zunming and did not pursue glosses on the text. Though he honored Confucian learning, he had a bold, chivalrous air.
entries.literal: He received learning from Xu Zunming and did not pursue glosses on the text. Though he honored Confucian studies, he had a bold, chivalrous air.

entries.zh: 孝昌末，盜賊蜂起，見天下將亂，乃之洛陽，與慕容儼騎馬為友。
entries.en: Late in Xiaochang bandits rose everywhere. Seeing that the realm would soon fall into disorder, he went to Luoyang and befriended Murong Yan as a fellow horseman.
entries.literal: Late in Xiaochang, bandits rose everywhere. Seeing that the realm would soon fall into disorder, he went to Luoyang and made friends with Murong Yan in the trade of hiring out horses.

entries.zh: 鑒性巧，夜則胡畫，以供衣食。
entries.en: Jian was skillful by nature; at night he painted for foreign patrons to pay for food and clothing.
entries.literal: Jian was skillful by nature; at night he painted for foreigners to supply food and clothing.

entries.zh: 謂其宗親曰：「運有污隆，亂極則治。
entries.en: He told his kinsmen, "Fortune has its stain and its rise; when disorder reaches the extreme, order comes.
entries.literal: He told his kinsmen, "Fortune has its stain and its rise; when disorder reaches the extreme, order comes.

entries.zh: 幷州戎馬之地，尒朱王命世之雄，杖義建旗，奉辭問罪，勞忠竭力，今也其時。」
entries.en: Bing Province is land of warhorses. Erzhu is the hero born for the age; he raises the banner of righteousness and marches under the charge to punish wrongdoing, toiling in loyalty and straining every force — now is the time."
entries.literal: Bing Province is land of warhorses. Erzhu is the hero born for the age; he raises the banner of righteousness and marches under the charge to punish wrongdoing, toiling in loyalty and straining every force — now is the time."

entries.zh: 遂相率奔尒朱榮於晉陽，因陳靜亂安民之策。
entries.en: Thereupon they went together to Erzhu Rong at Jinyang and set forth a plan to still disorder and settle the people.
entries.literal: Thereupon they went together to Erzhu Rong at Jinyang and set forth a plan to still disorder and settle the people.

entries.zh: 榮大奇之，即署參軍前鋒，從平鞏、密，每陣先登。
entries.en: Rong was greatly struck by him and at once appointed him staff officer of the vanguard. Following the pacification of Gong and Mi, in every battle he was first to charge.
entries.literal: Rong was greatly struck by him and at once appointed him staff officer of the vanguard. Following the pacification of Gong and Mi, in every battle he was first to charge.

entries.zh: 除撫軍、襄州刺史。
entries.en: He was made general who pacifies the army and inspector of Xiang Province.
entries.literal: He was made general who pacifies the army and inspector of Xiang Province.

entries.zh: 薛琡 敬顯儁 平鑒
entries.en: Xue Chu; Jing Xianjun; Ping Jian
entries.literal: Xue Chu; Jing Xianjun; Ping Jian

entries.zh: 万俟普 子 洛 可朱渾元 劉豐 破六韓常 金祚 韋子粲
entries.en: Moqi Pu; his son Luo; Kezhuhun Yuan; Liu Feng; Poliuhan Chang; Jin Zuo; Wei Zican
entries.literal: Moqi Pu; son Luo; Kezhuhun Yuan; Liu Feng; Poliuhan Chang; Jin Zuo; Wei Zican

entries.zh: 可朱渾元，字道元。
entries.en: Kezhuhun Yuan, styled Daoyuan.
entries.literal: Kezhuhun Yuan, styled Daoyuan.

entries.zh: 自云遼東人。
entries.en: He himself said he was from Liaodong.
entries.literal: He himself said he was from Liaodong.

entries.zh: 世為渠帥，魏時擁衆內附，曾祖護野肱終於懷朔鎮將，遂家焉。
entries.en: For generations his family had been tribal chiefs; in Wei times they led their followers in submission; his great-grandfather Huyegu died as general of Huaishuo garrison, and the family settled there.
entries.literal: For generations his family had been tribal chiefs; in Wei times they led their masses in submission; his great-grandfather Huyegu ended as general of Huaishuo garrison, and the family settled there.

entries.zh: 元寬仁有武略，少與高祖相知。
entries.en: Yuan was broad-minded and benevolent, with military strategy; in youth he knew Gao Huan well.
entries.literal: Yuan was broad and benevolent, with military strategy; in youth he knew Gao Huan well.

entries.zh: 北邊擾亂，遂將家屬赴定州，值鮮于修禮作亂，元擁衆屬焉。
entries.en: When the northern frontier was in turmoil he led his household to Dingzhou; they encountered Xianyu Xiuli raising rebellion, and Yuan led his followers to join him.
entries.literal: When the north border was in turmoil, he led his household to go to Dingzhou; they encountered Xianyu Xiuli raising rebellion, and Yuan led his masses to join him.

entries.zh: 葛榮併並修禮，復以元為梁王。
entries.en: Ge Rong swallowed up Xiuli and again made Yuan prince of Liang.
entries.literal: Ge Rong swallowed up Xiuli, and again made Yuan Prince of Liang.

entries.zh: 遂奔尒朱榮，以為別將，隸天光征關中，以功為渭州刺史。
entries.en: He then fled to Erzhu Rong, who made him a separate commander; he was attached to Tian Guang's campaign into Guanzhong and, for merit, was made inspector of Wei Province.
entries.literal: He then fled to Erzhu Rong, who made him a separate commander; he was attached to Tian Guang's campaign into Guanzhong, and for merit was made inspector of Wei Province.

entries.zh: 討西魏儀同金祚、皇甫智達於東雍，擒之。
entries.en: He attacked Western Wei yitong Jin Zuo and Huangfu Zhida at Dongyong and captured them.
entries.literal: He attacked Western Wei yitong Jin Zuo and Huangfu Zhida at Dongyong and captured them.

entries.zh: 遷幷州刺史。
entries.en: He was transferred to inspector of Bingzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to inspector of Bingzhou.

entries.zh: 又與諸將征伐，頻有克捷降下。
entries.en: Again campaigning with the generals, he had repeated victories in subduing foes.
entries.literal: Again with the generals on campaigns, he had repeated victories in subduing foes.

entries.zh: 天保初，封扶風王。
entries.en: Early in Tianbao he was enfeoffed prince of Fufeng.
entries.literal: Early in Tianbao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Fufeng.

entries.zh: 頻從顯祖討山胡、茹茹，累有戰功。
entries.en: He repeatedly followed Gao Yang in campaigns against the Shanhu and Ruru and won repeated battle merit.
entries.literal: He repeatedly followed Gao Yang in campaigns against the Shanhu and Ruru, with repeated battle merit.

entries.zh: 遷太師，薨。
entries.en: He was transferred to grand preceptor and died.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Grand Preceptor and died.

entries.zh: 贈假黃鉞、太宰、錄尚書。
entries.en: Posthumously he was given the yellow axe of authority, grand tutor, and recorder of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: Posthumously given the yellow axe of authority, Grand Tutor, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 元善於御衆，行軍用兵，務在持重，前後出征，未嘗負敗。
entries.en: Yuan was skilled at governing troops; in marching and using troops he always aimed at steadiness; in expedition after expedition he never suffered defeat.
entries.literal: Yuan was skilled at governing troops; in marching and using troops he always aimed at steadiness; in front and rear expeditions he never suffered defeat.

entries.zh: 及卒，朝廷深悼之。
entries.en: When he died the court deeply mourned him.
entries.literal: When he died the court deeply mourned him.

entries.zh: 皇建初，配享世宗廟庭。
entries.en: Early in Huangjian he was granted joint sacrifice in Gao Cheng's temple hall.
entries.literal: Early in Huangjian, he was granted joint sacrifice in Gao Cheng's temple hall.

entries.zh: 侯莫陳悅之殺賀拔岳也，周文帝率岳所部還，共圖悅。
entries.en: When Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue, Yuwen Tai led Yue's troops back and together they plotted against Houmochen Yue.
entries.literal: When Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue, Yuwen Tai led Yue's troops back and together they plotted against Houmochen Yue.

entries.zh: 元時助悅，悅走，元收其衆，入據秦州，為周攻圍，苦戰，結盟而罷。
entries.en: At that time Yuan helped Yue; when Yue fled, Yuan gathered his troops, entered and held Qinzhou, was besieged by Zhou forces, fought bitterly, and made an alliance to cease hostilities.
entries.literal: At that time Yuan helped Yue; when Yue fled, Yuan gathered his troops, entered and held Qinzhou, was besieged by Zhou, fought bitterly, and made an alliance to cease.

entries.zh: 元既早被高祖知遇，兼其母兄在東，嘗有思歸之志，恒遣表疏，與高祖陰相往來。
entries.en: Yuan had long been known and favored by Gao Huan; moreover his mother and elder brother were in the east; he always yearned to return, constantly sent memorials, and secretly corresponded with Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Yuan had early been known and favored by Gao Huan; moreover his mother and elder brother were in the east; he always had thoughts of returning home, constantly sent memorials, and secretly corresponded with Gao Huan.

entries.zh: 周文忌元智勇，知元懷貳，發兵攻之。
entries.en: Yuwen Tai feared Yuan's wisdom and courage, knew Yuan was of two minds, and sent troops to attack him.
entries.literal: Yuwen Tai feared Yuan's wisdom and courage, knew Yuan was of two minds, and sent troops to attack him.

entries.zh: 元乃率所部，發自渭州，西北渡烏蘭津。
entries.en: Yuan then led his division out from Wei Province and crossed Wulan ford to the northwest.
entries.literal: Yuan then led his division, setting out from Wei Province, and crossed Wulan ford northwestward.

entries.zh: 周文頻遣兵邀之，元戰必摧之。
entries.en: Yuwen Tai repeatedly sent troops to intercept him; whenever Yuan fought he crushed them.
entries.literal: Yuwen Tai repeatedly sent troops to intercept him; whenever Yuan fought he crushed them.

entries.zh: 引軍歷河、源二州境，乃得東出。
entries.en: He led his army through the territories of He and Yuan provinces and only then broke out eastward.
entries.literal: He led his army through the territories of He and Yuan provinces, and only then got out eastward.

entries.zh: 靈州刺史曹埿女婿劉豐與元深相交結，元因說豐以高祖英武非常，克成大業，豐自此便有委質之心，遂資遣元。
entries.en: Inspector of Lingzhou Cao Qi had a son-in-law, Liu Feng, who was deeply connected with Yuan; Yuan therefore persuaded Feng that Gao Huan was extraordinarily heroic and would accomplish great enterprise; from then on Feng had the heart to pledge allegiance, and supplied Yuan for his journey.
entries.literal: Inspector of Lingzhou Cao Qi had a son-in-law Liu Feng who was deeply connected with Yuan; Yuan therefore persuaded Feng that Gao Huan was extraordinarily heroic and would accomplish great enterprise; from then on Feng had the heart to submit his allegiance, and supplied Yuan for his journey.

entries.zh: 元從靈州東北入雲州。
entries.en: Yuan entered Yun Province from the northeast of Lingzhou.
entries.literal: Yuan entered Yun Province from the northeast of Lingzhou.

entries.zh: 高祖聞其來也，遣平陽守高嵩持金環一枚以賜元，並運資糧，遠遣候接。
entries.en: When Gao Huan heard he was coming, he sent the administrator of Pingyang, Gao Song, with a gold ring to bestow on Yuan, shipped provisions, and sent envoys far ahead to meet him.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan heard he was coming, he sent Administrator of Pingyang Gao Song with a gold ring to bestow on Yuan, and shipped provisions, sending envoys far to meet him.

entries.zh: 元至晉陽，引見執手，賜帛千匹並奴婢田宅。
entries.en: When Yuan reached Jinyang he was received in audience and they clasped hands; he was given a thousand bolts of silk together with slaves, maidservants, fields, and houses.
entries.literal: When Yuan reached Jinyang, he was received in audience and they clasped hands; he was given a thousand bolts of silk plus slaves, maidservants, fields and houses.

entries.zh: 兄弟四人先在幷州者，進官爵。
entries.en: His four brothers who were already in Bingzhou were promoted in rank and enfeoffment.
entries.literal: His four brothers who were earlier in Bingzhou were promoted in rank and enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 元所部督將，皆賞以爵邑。
entries.en: All the commanders and generals of Yuan's division were rewarded with ranks and fiefs.
entries.literal: All the commanders and generals of Yuan's division were rewarded with ranks and fiefs.

entries.zh: 封元縣公，除車騎大將軍。
entries.en: Yuan was enfeoffed duke of a county and appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry.
entries.literal: Yuan was enfeoffed Duke of a county and appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.

entries.zh: 万俟普，字普撥，太平人，其先匈奴之別種也。
entries.en: Moqi Pu, styled Pubo, came from Taiping; his forebears were a separate branch of the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: Moqi Pu, styled Pubo, was a native of Taiping; his ancestors were a separate branch of the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 雄果有武力。
entries.en: He was bold and resolute and possessed martial strength.
entries.literal: Bold and resolute, he had martial strength.

entries.zh: 正光中，破六韓拔陵構逆，授普太尉。
entries.en: In the Zhenguang era Poliuhan Baling raised rebellion; Pu was appointed grand commandant.
entries.literal: In the Zhenguang era, Poliuhan Baling raised rebellion; Pu was appointed Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 率部下降魏，授後將軍，第二領民酋長。
entries.en: He led his tribe in surrender to Wei and was made general of the rear guard and second leader of the tribal chieftains.
entries.literal: He led his tribe in surrender to Wei and was appointed General of the Rear Guard and second leader of the tribal chieftains.

entries.zh: 高祖起義，普遠通誠款，高祖甚嘉之。
entries.en: When Gao Huan raised the righteous standard, Pu sent pledges of loyalty from afar; Gao Huan greatly praised him.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous standard, Pu sent pledges of loyalty from afar; Gao Huan greatly praised him.

entries.zh: 斛斯椿逼帝西出，授司空、秦州刺史，據覆靺城。
entries.en: When Husu Chun forced the emperor westward, Pu was appointed minister of works and inspector of Qin Province, holding Fuche City.
entries.literal: When Husu Chun forced the emperor westward, Pu was appointed Minister of Works and inspector of Qin Province, holding Fuche City.

entries.zh: 高祖平夏州，普乃率其部落來奔，高祖躬自迎接，授普河西公。
entries.en: When Gao Huan pacified Xia Province, Pu led his tribe to submit; Gao Huan went out in person to receive him and made him duke of Hexi.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan pacified Xia Province, Pu then led his tribe to come and submit; Gao Huan personally went out to receive him and appointed Pu Duke of Hexi.

entries.zh: 累遷太尉、朔州刺史，卒。
entries.en: He rose through repeated promotions to grand commandant and inspector of Shuozhou, then died.
entries.literal: He rose in repeated promotions to Grand Commandant and inspector of Shuozhou, then died.

entries.zh: 韋子粲，字暉茂，京兆人。
entries.en: Wei Zican, styled Huimao, was a native of Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Wei Zican, styled Huimao, was a native of Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 曾祖閬，魏咸陽守。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Lang was Wei administrator of Xianyang.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Lang was Wei administrator of Xianyang.

entries.zh: 父雋，都水使者。
entries.en: His father Juan was commissioner of waterways.
entries.literal: His father Juan was commissioner of waterways.

entries.zh: 子粲仕郡功曹史，累遷為大行臺郎中，從尒朱天光平關右。
entries.en: Zican served as the commandery merit clerk and rose in succession to gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, following Erzhu Tianguang in pacifying Guanxi.
entries.literal: Zican served as merit clerk of the commandery and rose in succession to gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, following Erzhu Tianguang in pacifying Guanxi.

entries.zh: 孝武入關，以為南汾州刺史。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guanzhong, Zican was made governor of Southern Fen Province.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guanzhong, Zican was made governor of Southern Fen Province.

entries.zh: 神武命將出討，城陷，子弟俱破獲，送晉陽，蒙放免。
entries.en: Gao Huan ordered generals out to attack; the city fell, and sons and younger brothers were all captured and sent to Jinyang, where they were spared and released.
entries.literal: Gao Huan ordered generals out to attack; the city fell, and sons and younger brothers were all captured and sent to Jinyang, where they were spared and released.

entries.zh: 以粲為幷州長史，累遷豫州刺史，卒。
entries.en: Zican was made chief clerk of Bing Province and rose in succession to governor of Yu Province; he died.
entries.literal: Zican was made chief clerk of Bing Province and rose in succession to governor of Yu Province; he died.

entries.zh: 初，子粲兄弟十三人，子侄親屬，闔門百口悉在西魏。
entries.en: At first Zican had thirteen brothers; with sons, nephews, and kin, the whole gate counted a hundred mouths, all in Western Wei.
entries.literal: At first Zican had thirteen brothers, and with sons, nephews, and kin of the whole gate a hundred mouths all were in Western Wei.

entries.zh: 以子粲陷城不能死難，多致誅滅，歸國獲存，唯與弟道諧二人而已。
entries.en: Because Zican did not die when the city fell, many of his kin were put to death; after he returned to the Northern Qi state, only he and his younger brother Dao Xie survived.
entries.literal: Because Zican, when the city fell, could not die in loyalty, many were put to death; after returning to the state only he and his younger brother Dao Xie survived.

entries.zh: 諧與粲俱入國。
entries.en: Xie had entered the state together with Zican.
entries.literal: Xie entered the state together with Zican.

entries.zh: 粲富貴之後，遂特棄道諧，令其異居，所得廩祿，略不相及，其不顧恩義如此。
entries.en: After Zican grew rich and noble, he deliberately cast off Dao Xie, made him live apart, and scarcely shared his grain and salary with him — such was his disregard for kindness and righteousness.
entries.literal: After Zican grew rich and noble, he then deliberately cast off Dao Xie, made him live apart, and in grain and salary scarcely shared with him — such was his disregard for kindness and righteousness.

entries.zh: 劉豐，字豐生，普樂人也。
entries.en: Liu Feng, styled Fengsheng, came from Pule.
entries.literal: Liu Feng, styled Fengsheng, was a native of Pule.

entries.zh: 有雄姿壯氣，果毅絕人，有口辯，好說兵事。
entries.en: He had heroic bearing and stalwart spirit, resolution surpassing others, was eloquent, and loved to discuss military affairs.
entries.literal: He had heroic bearing and stalwart spirit, resolution surpassing others, was eloquent of speech, and loved to discuss military affairs.

entries.zh: 破六韓拔陵之亂，豐以守城之功，除普樂太守。
entries.en: In Poliuhan Baling's rebellion, Feng for merit in holding the city was appointed administrator of Pule.
entries.literal: In Poliuhan Baling's rebellion, Feng for merit in holding the city was appointed Administrator of Pule.

entries.zh: 魏永安初，除靈州鎮城大都督。
entries.en: At the beginning of Yong'an of Wei, he was made metropolitan commandant defending the city of Ling Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an of Wei, he was made metropolitan commandant defending the city of Ling Province.

entries.zh: 周文授以衛大將軍，豐不受，乃遣攻圍，不克。
entries.en: Yuwen Tai offered him the rank of grand general of the guard; Feng refused, and Yuwen sent troops to besiege him but could not take the city.
entries.literal: Yuwen Tai gave him the rank of Grand General of the Guard; Feng would not accept it, so Yuwen sent troops to besiege him but could not take the city.

entries.zh: 豐遠慕高祖威德，乃率戶數萬來奔。
entries.en: Feng had long admired Gao Huan's prestige and virtue; he thereupon led several tens of thousands of households to defect.
entries.literal: Feng greatly admired Gao Huan's prestige and virtue and thereupon led several tens of thousands of households to come over.

entries.zh: 高祖上豐為平西將軍、南汾州刺史。
entries.en: Gao Huan promoted Feng to general who pacifies the west and governor of Southern Fen Province.
entries.literal: Gao Huan promoted Feng to General Who Pacifies the West and governor of Southern Fen Province.

entries.zh: 遂與諸將征討，平定寇亂。
entries.en: He then campaigned with the generals and pacified the bandit disorders.
entries.literal: He then joined the generals on punitive campaigns and pacified bandit disorder.

entries.zh: 又從高祖破周文於河陰，豐功居多，高祖執手嗟賞。
entries.en: He again followed Gao Huan in defeating Yuwen Tai at Heyin; Feng's merit stood first, and Gao Huan took his hand and sighed in admiration.
entries.literal: He again followed Gao Huan in defeating Yuwen Tai at Heyin; Feng's merit was greatest, and Gao Huan took his hand and sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 入為左衛將軍，出除殷州。
entries.en: He entered court as left guard general and went out as governor of Yin Province.
entries.literal: He entered court as left guard general and went out as governor of Yin Province.

entries.zh: 子洛，字受洛干。
entries.en: His son Luo, styled Shouluogan.
entries.literal: His son Luo, styled Shouluogan.

entries.zh: 豪壯有武藝，騎射過人，為鄉閭所伏。
entries.en: Bold and stalwart, skilled in the martial arts; his mounted archery surpassed others, and the village community respected him.
entries.literal: Bold and stalwart, skilled in martial arts; his mounted archery surpassed others, and the village community respected him.

entries.zh: 拔陵反，隨父歸順，除顯武將軍。
entries.en: When Baling rebelled he followed his father in submitting and was appointed manifest martial general.
entries.literal: When Baling rebelled, he followed his father in submitting; he was appointed Manifest Martial General.

entries.zh: 隨尒朱榮每有戰功，累遷汾州刺史、驃騎將軍。
entries.en: Following Erzhu Rong he won merit in every battle; he rose in successive promotions to inspector of Fenzhou and general of agile cavalry.
entries.literal: Following Erzhu Rong he had battle merit in every engagement; he rose in successive promotions to inspector of Fenzhou and General of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 及起義信都，遠送誠款，高祖嘉其父子俱至，甚優其禮。
entries.en: When the righteous rising began at Xindu he sent pledges of loyalty from afar; Gao Huan praised that father and son had both come and treated them with exceptional courtesy.
entries.literal: When the righteous rising began at Xindu, he sent pledges of loyalty from afar; Gao Huan praised that father and son had both come and treated them with exceptional courtesy.

entries.zh: 除撫軍，兼靈州刺史。
entries.en: He was appointed to the Pacification Army and concurrently made inspector of Ling Province.
entries.literal: He was appointed Pacification Army [commander] and concurrently inspector of Ling Province.

entries.zh: 武帝入關，除左仆射。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu entered the passes he was appointed left vice director.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu entered the passes, he was appointed Vice Director of the Left.

entries.zh: 天平中，隨父東歸，封建昌郡公，再遷領軍將軍。
entries.en: In the Tianping era he followed his father east; he was enfeoffed duke of Jianchang commandery and promoted again to commander of the guards.
entries.literal: In the Tianping era he followed his father east; he was enfeoffed Duke of Jianchang commandery and promoted again to Commander of the Guards.

entries.zh: 與諸將圍獨孤如願於金墉，及河陰之戰，並有功。
entries.en: With the generals he besieged Dugu Ruyuan at Jinyong; at the battle of Heyin he had merit as well.
entries.literal: With the generals he besieged Dugu Ruyuan at Jinyong; at the battle of Heyin he had merit as well.

entries.zh: 高祖以其父普尊老，特崇禮之，嘗親扶上馬。
entries.en: Because his father Pu was honored as an elder, Gao Huan especially elevated his ritual treatment; he once personally helped him mount his horse.
entries.literal: Gao Huan, because his father Pu was honored as an elder, especially elevated his ritual treatment; he once personally helped him mount his horse.

entries.zh: 洛免冠稽首曰：「願出死力以報深恩。」
entries.en: Luo removed his cap and performed the forehead knock, saying: "I wish to give my utmost strength to repay your deep grace."
entries.literal: Luo removed his cap and performed the forehead knock, saying: "I wish to give my utmost strength to repay your deep grace."

entries.zh: 及此役也，諸軍北渡橋，洛以一軍不動。
entries.en: In this battle, when the armies crossed the bridge northward, Luo held one army motionless.
entries.literal: And in this battle, when the armies crossed the bridge northward, Luo held one army motionless.

entries.zh: 謂西人曰：「万俟受洛干在此，能來可來也！」
entries.en: He said to the westerners: "Moqi Shouluogan is here — if you can come, come!"
entries.literal: He said to the westerners: "Moqi Shouluogan is here — if you can come, come!"

entries.zh: 西人畏而去。
entries.en: The westerners feared him and withdrew.
entries.literal: The westerners feared and departed.

entries.zh: 高祖以雄壯，名其所營地為回洛城。
entries.en: Because of his heroism and stature, Gao Huan named the place he camped Huiluo City.
entries.literal: Gao Huan, because of his heroism and stature, named the place he camped Huiluo City.

entries.zh: 洛慷慨有氣節，勇銳冠時，當世推為名將。
entries.en: Luo was generous and high-minded; his courage and keenness crowned the age, and his contemporaries esteemed him a famous general.
entries.literal: Luo was generous and had moral resolve; his courage and sharpness crowned the age; his contemporaries esteemed him a famous general.

entries.zh: 興和初卒。
entries.en: He died early in the Xinghe era.
entries.literal: He died early in Xinghe.

entries.zh: 常沈敏有膽略，善騎射，累遷平西將軍。
entries.en: Chang was deep and keen, bold and resourceful, and skilled in mounted archery; he rose in succession to general who pacifies the west.
entries.literal: Chang was deep, keen, and had courage and resource; skilled in mounted archery; he rose in succession to General Who Pacifies the West.

entries.zh: 高祖起義，常為附化守，與万俟受洛干東歸，高祖嘉之，上為撫軍。
entries.en: When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Chang was defender of Fuhua; he returned east with Moqi Shouluogan. Gao Huan praised this and promoted him to military inspector.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Chang was defender of Fuhua; he returned east with Moqi Shouluogan; Gao Huan praised this and promoted him to Military Inspector.

entries.zh: 與諸將征討，又從高祖攻擊諸寇，累遷車騎大將軍、開府，封平陽公，除洛州刺史。
entries.en: On punitive campaigns with the generals he again followed Gao Huan against the bandits, rising in succession to grand general of chariots and cavalry, opener of a government office, duke of Pingyang, and governor of Luo Province.
entries.literal: With the generals on punitive campaigns he again followed Gao Huan in attacking the various bandits, rising in succession to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Opener of a Government Office, Duke of Pingyang, and governor of Luo Province.

entries.zh: 常啟世宗曰：「常自鎮河陽以來，頻出關口，太谷二道，北荊已北，洛州已南，所有要害，頗所知悉。
entries.en: Chang addressed Gao Cheng, saying, "Since I garrisoned Heyang I have repeatedly sallied through the passes. Of the two routes through Taiyu, north of Northern Jing and south of Luo Province, I know every strategic point.
entries.literal: Chang addressed Gao Cheng, saying: "Since I have garrisoned Heyang, I have repeatedly sallied through the passes. Of the two routes through Taiyu, north of Northern Jing and south of Luo Province, I know well all the strategic points.

entries.zh: 而太谷南口去荊路逾一百，經赤工阪，是賊往還東西大道，中間曠絕一百五十里，賊之糧饢，唯經此路。
entries.en: Yet the southern mouth of Taiyu lies more than a hundred li from the Jing route, passes Chigong Slope, and is the bandits' chief east-west thoroughfare. Between them lies open country a hundred and fifty li across; the bandits' grain and fodder must come only by this road.
entries.literal: Yet the southern mouth of Taiyu lies more than a hundred li from the Jing route, passes Chigong Slope, and is the bandits' chief east-west thoroughfare. In the middle lies open country of a hundred and fifty li; the bandits' grain and fodder must come only by this road.

entries.zh: 愚謂於彼選形勝之處，營築城戍，安置士馬，截其遠還，自然不能更有行送。」
entries.en: I humbly propose that we choose a place of natural advantage there, build garrison walls, station troops and horses, and cut their long supply line — then naturally they could no longer send convoys."
entries.literal: I humbly propose selecting a place of natural advantage there, building garrison walls, stationing troops and horses, and cutting off their long supply line — then naturally they could no longer send convoys."

entries.zh: 世宗納其計，遣大司馬斛律金等築楊志、百家、呼延三鎮。
entries.en: Gao Cheng adopted his plan and sent Grand Marshal Hulü Jin and others to build the three garrisons of Yangzhi, Baijia, and Huyan.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng adopted his plan and sent Grand Marshal Hulü Jin and others to build the three garrisons of Yangzhi, Baijia, and Huyan.

entries.zh: 常秩滿，還晉陽，拜太保、滄州刺史，卒。
entries.en: When Chang's term expired he returned to Jinyang, was made grand mentor and governor of Cang Province, and died.
entries.literal: When Chang's term expired he returned to Jinyang, was made Grand Mentor and governor of Cang Province, and died.

entries.zh: 贈尚書令、司徒公、太傅、第一領民酋長，假王，諡曰忠武。
entries.en: Posthumously he was made director of the masters of writing, duke of the department of state affairs, grand tutor, and chief of the first tribally enrolled division, with princely rank in title and the posthumous title Loyal and Martial.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Tutor, chief of the first tribally enrolled division, prince in title, posthumous title Zhongwu.

entries.zh: 金祚，字神敬，安定人也。
entries.en: Jin Zuo, styled Shenjing, was a native of Anding.
entries.literal: Jin Zuo, styled Shenjing, was a native of Anding.

entries.zh: 性驍雄，尚氣任俠。
entries.en: By nature he was fierce and heroic and prized spirit and chivalry.
entries.literal: By nature he was fierce and heroic and prized spirit and chivalry.

entries.zh: 魏正光中，隴右賊起，詔雍州刺史元猛討之，召募狼家，以為軍導，祚應選。
entries.en: In Zhenguang of Wei, bandits rose in Longyou; an edict ordered Governor of Yong Province Yuan Meng to suppress them and recruited Langjia men as army guides; Zuo answered the call.
entries.literal: In Zhenguang of Wei, bandits rose in Longyou; an edict ordered Governor of Yong Province Yuan Meng to suppress them and recruited men of Langjia as army guides; Zuo answered the call.

entries.zh: 以軍功累遷龍驤將軍、靈州刺史。
entries.en: For military merit he rose in succession to general of soaring dragon and governor of Ling Province.
entries.literal: For military merit he rose in succession to General of Soaring Dragon and governor of Ling Province.

entries.zh: 高祖舉義，尒朱天光率關右之衆與仲遠等北抗義師。
entries.en: When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Erzhu Tianguang led the forces of Guanxi and, with Erzhu Zhongyuan and others, resisted the righteous army in the north.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Erzhu Tianguang led the forces of Guanxi and, with Zhongyuan and others, resisted the righteous army in the north.

entries.zh: 天光留祚東秦，總督三州，鎮靜二州。
entries.en: Tianguang left Zuo in Eastern Qin with overall command of three provinces and charge of pacifying two.
entries.literal: Tianguang left Zuo in Eastern Qin, with overall command of three provinces and responsibility for pacifying two provinces.

entries.zh: 天光敗，歸高祖，除車騎大將軍。
entries.en: When Tianguang was defeated, Zuo submitted to Gao Huan and was made grand general of chariots and cavalry.
entries.literal: When Tianguang was defeated, Zuo submitted to Gao Huan and was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.

entries.zh: 邙山之戰，以大都督從破西軍。
entries.en: At the battle of Mount Mang he followed as grand commander in breaking the Western army.
entries.literal: At the battle of Mount Mang, as grand commander he followed in breaking the Western army.

entries.zh: 祚除華州刺史，加開府儀同三司，別封臨濟縣子，卒。
entries.en: Zuo was made governor of Hua Province, with added opener of a government office equal in insignia to three masters of ceremonies, and was separately enfeoffed viscount of Linji county; he died.
entries.literal: Zuo was made governor of Hua Province, with added opener of a government office equal in insignia to three masters of ceremonies, and was separately enfeoffed as Viscount of Linji county; he died.

entries.zh: 贈司空。
entries.en: Posthumously he was made minister of works.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 破六韓常，字保年，附化人，匈奴單于之裔也。
entries.en: Poliuhan Chang, styled Baonian, was a man of Fuhua and a descendant of the Xiongnu shanyu.
entries.literal: Poliuhan Chang, styled Baonian, was a man of Fuhua and a descendant of the Xiongnu Shanyu.

entries.zh: 右谷蠡王潘六奚沒於魏，其子孫以潘六奚為氏，後人訛誤，以為破六韓。
entries.en: The right kuuli prince Pan Liuxi perished in Wei; his descendants took Pan Liuxi as their clan name, and later men garbled it into Poliuhan.
entries.literal: Right kuuli prince Pan Liuxi perished in Wei; his descendants took Pan Liuxi as their clan name; later men garbled it into Poliuhan.

entries.zh: 世領部落，其父孔雀，世襲酋長。
entries.en: For generations they led their tribe; his father Kongque had inherited the chieftaincy in turn.
entries.literal: For generations they led their tribe; his father Kongque inherited the chieftaincy in succession.

entries.zh: 孔雀少驍勇。
entries.en: Kongque was fierce and brave from youth.
entries.literal: Kongque was from youth fierce and brave.

entries.zh: 時宗人拔陵為亂，以孔雀為大都督、司徒、平南王。
entries.en: At that time their clansman Baling raised rebellion and made Kongque grand commander of the north, director of state affairs, and prince who pacifies the south.
entries.literal: At that time their clansman Baling raised rebellion and made Kongque grand commander of the north, Director of State Affairs, and Prince Who Pacifies the South.

entries.zh: 孔雀率部下一萬人降於尒朱榮，詔加平北將軍、第一領民酋長，卒。
entries.en: Kongque led his division of ten thousand men and submitted to Erzhu Rong; an edict added general who pacifies the north and chief of the first tribally enrolled division, and he died.
entries.literal: Kongque led his division, ten thousand men, and submitted to Erzhu Rong; an edict added General Who Pacifies the North and chief of the first tribally enrolled division; he died.

entries.zh: 王思政據長社，世宗命豐與清河王岳攻之。
entries.en: Wang Sizheng held Changshe; Gao Cheng ordered Feng and Prince of Qinghe Yue to attack him.
entries.literal: Wang Sizheng held Changshe; Gao Cheng ordered Feng and Prince of Qinghe Yue to attack him.

entries.zh: 豐建水攻之策，遂遏洧水以灌之，水長，魚鱉皆遊焉。
entries.en: Feng devised a water assault: they dammed the Wei River to flood the city, and as the waters rose, fish and turtles swam in the streets.
entries.literal: Feng devised a plan of water assault and dammed the Wei River to flood the city; as the waters rose, fish and turtles swam there.

entries.zh: 九月至四月，城將陷。
entries.en: From the ninth month to the fourth month the city was on the verge of falling.
entries.literal: From the ninth month to the fourth month, the city was on the verge of falling.

entries.zh: 豐與行臺慕容紹宗見北有白氣同入船，忽有暴風從東北來，正晝昏暗，飛沙走礫，船纜忽絕，漂至城下。
entries.en: Feng and mobile-office commissioner Murong Shaozong saw a white vapor in the north and boarded a boat together. Suddenly a violent wind rose from the northeast; at high noon the sky went dark, sand flew and stones scoured the air, the mooring lines snapped, and the boat was driven to the foot of the city.
entries.literal: Feng and mobile-office commissioner Murong Shaozong saw a white vapor in the north and entered a boat together. Suddenly a violent wind came from the northeast; at high noon it grew dark, sand flew and stones dashed; the boat cables snapped at once, and they drifted to the foot of the city.

entries.zh: 豐遊水向土山，為浪所激，不時至，西人釣之，並為敵人所害。
entries.en: Feng swam toward an earthen hill but was beaten by the waves and could not reach it in time; Western troops hooked him with poles, and both were killed by the enemy.
entries.literal: Feng swam toward an earthen hill but was driven by the waves and did not arrive in time; men of the west hooked him with poles, and both were killed by the enemy.

entries.zh: 豐壯勇善戰，為諸將所推。
