entries.en: Feng was stalwart, brave, and skilled in battle, and the generals held him in high esteem.
entries.literal: Feng was stalwart, brave, and skilled in battle, and was acclaimed by the generals.

entries.zh: 死之日，朝野駭惋。
entries.en: On the day he died, court and countryside alike were struck with dismay and grief.
entries.literal: On the day he died, court and countryside alike were struck with dismay and lament.

entries.zh: 贈大司馬、司徒公、尚書令，諡曰忠。
entries.en: Posthumously he was made grand marshal, duke of the department of state affairs, and director of the masters of writing, with the posthumous title Loyal.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given Grand Marshal, Duke of the Department of State Affairs, Director of the Masters of Writing, posthumous title Zhong.

entries.zh: 子曄嗣。
entries.en: His son Ye succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Ye succeeded.

entries.zh: 孝武初，其兄樹見禽。
entries.en: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, his elder brother Shu was captured.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, his elder brother Shu was captured.

entries.zh: 坦見樹既長且賢，慮其代己，密勸朝廷以法除之。
entries.en: Tan saw that Shu was older and more worthy and feared he would be displaced; he secretly urged the court to eliminate Shu by law.
entries.literal: Tan saw that Shu was both older and worthy, and feared Shu would replace him; he secretly urged the court to eliminate Shu by law.

entries.zh: 樹知之，泣渭坦曰：「我往因家難，不能死亡，寄食江湖，受其爵命。
entries.en: When Shu learned of it, he wept on the Wei River and said to Tan, "Long ago, because of our family's calamity, I could not die; I lived on others' food along rivers and lakes and accepted their ranks and commands.
entries.literal: When Shu learned of it, he wept at the Wei River and said to Tan: "I once, because of family calamity, could not die; I lived on others' food on rivers and lakes and accepted their ranks and commands.

entries.zh: 今者之來，非由義至，求活而已，豈望榮華。
entries.en: My coming now is not from righteousness — I seek only to live. How could I hope for glory?
entries.literal: My coming now is not from righteousness — I seek only to live; how could I hope for glory.

entries.zh: 汝何肆其猜忌，忘在原之義，腰背雖偉，善無可稱。」
entries.en: Why do you indulge your suspicions and forget the bond of those from one root? Though your back and waist are imposing, there is no goodness in you worth praising."
entries.literal: Why do you indulge your suspicions and forget the bond of kin from one root? Though your back and waist are imposing, your goodness is nothing worth praising."

entries.zh: 坦作色而去。
entries.en: Tan flushed and left.
entries.literal: Tan flushed and left.

entries.zh: 樹死，竟不臨哭。
entries.en: When Shu died, Tan never went to mourn at his coffin.
entries.literal: When Shu died, Tan never went to mourn at his coffin.

entries.zh: 元韶，字世胄，魏孝莊之侄。
entries.en: Yuan Shao, styled Shizhou, was a nephew of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei.
entries.literal: Yuan Shao, styled Shizhou, was a nephew of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei.

entries.zh: 避尒朱之難，匿於嵩山。
entries.en: To escape the turmoil caused by the Erzhus, he hid on Mount Song.
entries.literal: Avoiding the disorder of the Erzhus, he hid on Mount Song.

entries.zh: 性好學，美容儀。
entries.en: He loved learning by nature and had a handsome appearance and bearing.
entries.literal: By nature he loved learning and had fine appearance and bearing.

entries.zh: 初，尒朱榮將入洛，父劭恐，以韶寄所親滎陽太守鄭仲明。
entries.en: Earlier, when Erzhu Rong was about to enter Luoyang, Shao's father feared for him and entrusted him to Zheng Zhongming, the administrator of Xingyang and a close associate.
entries.literal: At first, when Erzhu Rong was about to enter Luoyang, his father Shao was afraid and entrusted Shao to Zheng Zhongming, administrator of Xingyang, a man close to him.

entries.zh: 仲明尋為城人所殺，韶因亂與乳母相失，遂與仲明兄子僧副避難。
entries.en: Zhongming was soon killed by the townspeople. In the chaos Shao was separated from his wet nurse, and he fled with Zhongming's nephew Sengfu.
entries.literal: Zhongming was soon killed by the people of the city; in the disorder Shao became separated from his wet nurse and then fled danger with Zhongming's brother's son Sengfu.

entries.zh: 路中為賊逼，僧副恐不免，因令韶下馬。
entries.en: On the road bandits pressed them hard. Sengfu feared they would not escape, so he ordered Shao to dismount.
entries.literal: On the road they were pressed by bandits; Sengfu feared they would not escape, and accordingly ordered Shao to dismount.

entries.zh: 僧副謂客曰：「窮鳥投入，尚或矜愍，況諸王如何棄乎？」
entries.en: Sengfu said to his followers, "If even an exhausted bird that flies into one's arms deserves pity, how could we abandon one of the princes?"
entries.literal: Sengfu said to his retainers, "When an exhausted bird flies into one's arms, one may still pity it; how could one abandon one of the princes?"

entries.zh: 僧副舉刃逼之，客乃退。
entries.en: Sengfu raised his blade and forced them back, and his followers withdrew.
entries.literal: Sengfu raised his blade and forced them back, and the retainers then withdrew.

entries.zh: 韶逢一老母姓程，哀之，隱於私家十餘日，莊帝訪而獲焉，襲封彭城王。
entries.en: Shao met an old woman surnamed Cheng, who pitied him and hid him in her home for more than ten days. Emperor Zhuang searched for him and found him, and Shao inherited the title Prince of Pengcheng.
entries.literal: Shao encountered an old woman surnamed Cheng, who pitied him and hid him in her private home for more than ten days; Emperor Zhuang searched for him and found him, and he inherited the title Prince of Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 齊神武帝以孝武帝後配之。
entries.en: Emperor Shenwu of Qi married Emperor Xiaowu's empress to him.
entries.literal: Emperor Shenwu of Qi gave Emperor Xiaowu's empress to him as wife.

entries.zh: 魏室奇寶，多隨後入韶家。
entries.en: Many rare treasures of the Wei imperial house came into Shao's household along with the empress.
entries.literal: Many rare treasures of the Wei imperial house followed the empress into Shao's household.

entries.zh: 有二玉缽相盛，可轉而不可出；
entries.en: There were two jade bowls nested together; they could be turned but not separated;
entries.literal: There were two jade bowls nested inside one another; they could be turned but could not be separated;

entries.zh: 馬瑙榼容三升，玉縫之。
entries.en: and an agate wine vessel held three sheng and had jade seams.
entries.literal: an agate wine vessel held three sheng and had seams of jade.

entries.zh: 皆稱西域鬼作也。
entries.en: All were said to be uncanny works from the Western Regions.
entries.literal: All were said to be the work of spirits from the Western Regions.

entries.zh: 歷位太尉、侍中、錄尚書、司州牧，進太傅。
entries.en: He successively served as grand commandant, palace attendant, recorder of the masters of writing, and governor of Sizhou, and was advanced to grand tutor.
entries.literal: He successively held posts as grand commandant, palace attendant, recorder of the masters of writing, and governor of Sizhou, and was advanced to grand tutor.

entries.zh: 齊天保元年，降爵為縣公。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianbao under Qi, his title was reduced to county duke.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianbao under Qi, his title was reduced to county duke.

entries.zh: 元坦 元斌 元孝友 元暉業 元弼 元韶
entries.en: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao
entries.literal: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao

entries.zh: 元斌，字善集，祖魏獻文皇帝。
entries.en: Yuan Bin, styled Shanji — his grandfather was Emperor Xianwen of Wei.
entries.literal: Yuan Bin, styled Shanji, his grandfather was Emperor Xianwen of Wei.

entries.zh: 父高陽王雍，從孝莊於河陰遇害。
entries.en: His father Prince Gaoyang Yong followed Emperor Xiaozhuang to Heyin and met disaster there.
entries.literal: His father Prince Gaoyang Yong followed Emperor Xiaozhuang at Heyin and met disaster there.

entries.zh: 斌少襲祖爵，歷位侍中、尚書左僕射。
entries.en: Bin in youth inherited his grandfather's title and held posts including palace attendant and left vice director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: Bin in youth inherited his grandfather's title; he held posts including palace attendant and left vice director of the masters of writing.

entries.zh: 斌美儀貌，性寬和，居官重慎，頗為齊文襄愛賞。
entries.en: Bin had fine looks; his nature was mild and broad; in office he was cautious and weighty — Gao Cheng greatly loved and appreciated him.
entries.literal: Bin had fine appearance; his nature was mild and broad; in office he was cautious and weighty — Gao Cheng greatly loved and appreciated him.

entries.zh: 齊天保初，準例降爵，為高陽縣公，拜右光祿大夫。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianbao under Qi, per precedent his rank was reduced; he became duke of Gaoyang county and was appointed right grand master for the brilliant.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao, per precedent his rank was reduced; he became Duke of Gaoyang county and was appointed right grand master for the brilliant.

entries.zh: 二年，從文宣討契丹還，至白狼河，以罪賜死。
entries.en: In the second year, returning from campaigning against the Khitan with Gao Yang, at the Bailang River he was ordered to die for his crime.
entries.literal: In the second year, returning from campaigning against the Khitan with Emperor Wenxuan, at the Bailang River he was ordered to die for his crime.

entries.zh: 元孝友，祖魏太武皇帝。
entries.en: Yuan Xiaoyou — his grandfather was Emperor Taiwu of Wei.
entries.literal: Yuan Xiaoyou — his grandfather was Emperor Taiwu of Wei.

entries.zh: 兄臨淮王彧無子，令孝友襲爵。
entries.en: His elder brother Prince Linhuai Yu had no son; Xiaoyou was made to inherit the title.
entries.literal: His elder brother Prince Linhuai Yu had no son; he had Xiaoyou inherit the title.

entries.zh: 累遷滄州刺史，為政溫和，好行小惠，不能清白，而無所侵犯，百姓亦以此便之。
entries.en: He rose through repeated promotions to inspector of Cangzhou; his governance was mild and harmonious, and he liked to do small favors. He could not be upright, yet he did not violate or harass others — the common people found this convenient.
entries.literal: He rose through repeated promotions to inspector of Cangzhou; his governance was mild and harmonious, he liked to do small favors; he could not be upright but did not violate or harass others — the common people found this convenient.

entries.zh: 魏靜帝宴文襄於華林，孝友因醉自譽，又云：「陛下許賜臣能。」
entries.en: Emperor Jing of Wei feasted Gao Cheng at Hualin; Xiaoyou, drunk, praised himself and also said, "Your Majesty promised to grant me ability."
entries.literal: Emperor Jing of Wei feasted Gao Cheng at Hualin; Xiaoyou, drunk, praised himself, and also said: "Your Majesty promised to grant me ability."

entries.zh: 帝笑曰：「朕恒聞王自道清。」
entries.en: The emperor laughed and said, "I constantly hear the Prince speak of his own integrity."
entries.literal: The Emperor laughed and said: "I constantly hear the Prince speak of his own integrity."

entries.zh: 文襄曰：「臨淮王奉旨舍罪。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng said, "Prince Linhuai has received the decree and is pardoned of guilt."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng said: "Prince Linhuai received the decree and is pardoned of guilt."

entries.zh: 於是君臣俱笑而不罪。
entries.en: Thereupon ruler and ministers all laughed and did not punish him.
entries.literal: Thereupon ruler and ministers all laughed and did not punish him.

entries.zh: 元暉業，字紹遠，魏景穆皇帝之玄孫。
entries.en: Yuan Huiye, styled Shaoyuan, was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Jingmu of Wei.
entries.literal: Yuan Huiye, styled Shaoyuan, was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Jingmu of Wei.

entries.zh: 少險薄，多與寇盜交通。
entries.en: In youth he was mean and unscrupulous and kept company with bandits.
entries.literal: In youth he was crafty and mean, and often associated with bandits and robbers.

entries.zh: 長乃變節，涉子史，亦頗屬文，而慷慨有志節。
entries.en: When grown he mended his ways, took up the Masters and histories, wrote passable prose, and bore himself with generous resolve.
entries.literal: When grown he changed his ways, studied the Masters and histories, was also rather skilled at composition, and was ardent in spirit and aspiration.

entries.zh: 歷位司空、太尉，加特進，領中書監，錄尚書事。
entries.en: He rose to minister of works and grand commandant, was given supernumerary rank, headed the secretariat, and recorded affairs for the masters of writing.
entries.literal: He rose through offices to Minister of Works, Grand Commandant, was given the supernumerary rank, headed the Secretariat Supervisor, and recorded affairs for the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 文襄嘗問之曰：「此何所披覽？」
entries.en: Gao Cheng once asked him, "What are you reading?"
entries.literal: Gao Cheng once asked him: "What are you perusing here?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「數尋伊、霍之傳，不讀曹、馬之書。」
entries.en: He replied, "I pore over the lives of Yi Yin and Huo Guang — not the chronicles of Cao Cao and the Sima clan."
entries.literal: He replied: "I often seek the biographies of Yi Yin and Huo Guang; I do not read the books of Cao [Cao] and the Sima [clan]."

entries.zh: 元弼，字輔宗，魏司空暉之子。
entries.en: Yuan Bi, styled Fuzong, was son of Hui, minister of works of Wei.
entries.literal: Yuan Bi, styled Fuzong, was son of Hui, Minister of Works of Wei.

entries.zh: 性剛正，有文學。
entries.en: By nature he was upright and learned.
entries.literal: By nature he was firm and upright and possessed literary learning.

entries.zh: 位中散大夫。
entries.en: He held the post of regular attendant.
entries.literal: He held the post of Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 以世嫡應襲先爵。
entries.en: As heir of the main line he should have inherited the family enfeoffment.
entries.literal: As heir of the main line he should have inherited his predecessor's enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 為季父尚書僕射麗因于氏親寵，遂奪弼王爵，橫授同母兄子誕，於是弼絕棄人事，托疾還私第。
entries.en: His uncle Li, vice director of the masters of writing, used the Yu clan's favor at court to strip Bi of his princely rank and grant it to his uterine brother's son Dan. Bi thereupon withdrew from public life, pleaded illness, and retired to his private residence.
entries.literal: But his younger uncle Li, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, through the Yu clan's favor in kinship, thereupon seized Bi's princely rank and arbitrarily granted it to his elder uterine brother's son Dan; Bi then abandoned human affairs, feigned illness, and returned to his private residence.

entries.zh: 宣武中為侍中，弼上表固讓。
entries.en: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was made palace attendant; Bi submitted a memorial firmly declining.
entries.literal: In Xuanwu's time he was made Palace Attendant; Bi submitted a memorial firmly declining.

entries.zh: 入嵩山，以穴為室，布衣蔬食，卒。
entries.en: He entered Mount Song, made a cave his home, wore hemp and ate greens, and died.
entries.literal: He entered Mount Song, took a cave for his chamber, wore plain cloth and ate vegetables, and died.

entries.zh: 建元元年，子暉業訴復王爵。
entries.en: In Jianyuan year one his son Huiye petitioned to restore the princely rank.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, his son Huiye petitioned to restore the princely rank.

entries.zh: 永安三年，追贈尚書令、司徒公，諡曰文獻。
entries.en: In Yong'an year three he was posthumously made director of the masters of writing and duke of the department of state affairs, with the posthumous title Cultured and Offering.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yong'an, posthumously he was given Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the Department of State Affairs, posthumous title Wenxian.

entries.zh: 初，弼嘗夢人謂之曰：「君身不得傳世封，其紹先爵者，君長子紹遠也。」
entries.en: Earlier Bi had dreamed that someone told him, "You will not pass the enfeoffment down in your own lifetime; your eldest son Shaoyuan will restore the former rank."
entries.literal: Earlier, Bi once dreamed that someone told him: "Your person will not transmit the enfeoffment of the age; he who will continue the former rank is your eldest son Shaoyuan."

entries.zh: 弼覺，即告暉業，終如其言。
entries.en: When Bi awoke he told Huiye at once, and in the end it proved true.
entries.literal: When Bi awoke he at once told Huiye, and in the end it was as spoken.

entries.zh: 十年，太史奏云：「今年當除舊布新。」
entries.en: In year ten the grand astrologer reported, "This year the old must yield to the new."
entries.literal: In the tenth year, the Grand Astrologer memorialized: "This year old shall be removed and new spread."

entries.zh: 文宣謂韶曰：「漢光武何故中興？」
entries.en: Gao Yang asked Shao, "Why did Emperor Guangwu of Han restore the dynasty?"
entries.literal: Gao Yang said to Shao: "Why did Han Guangwu restore the dynasty?"

entries.zh: 韶曰：「為誅諸劉不盡。」
entries.en: Shao said, "Because the Liu were not all killed."
entries.literal: Shao said: "Because the Liu were not all killed."

entries.zh: 於是乃誅諸元以厭之。
entries.en: Thereupon they slaughtered the Yuan to satisfy the omen.
entries.literal: Thereupon they killed the various Yuan to satisfy the omen.

entries.zh: 遂以五月誅元世哲、景武等二十五家，餘十九家並禁止之。
entries.en: In the fifth month they executed Yuan Shizhe, Jingwu, and twenty-five other households; the remaining nineteen households were all placed under restraint.
entries.literal: Then in the fifth month they executed Yuan Shizhe, Jingwu, and twenty-five other households; the remaining nineteen households were all placed under restraint.

entries.zh: 韶幽於京畿地牢，絕食，啖衣袖而死。
entries.en: Shao was imprisoned in the capital dungeon, denied food, and died gnawing his sleeves.
entries.literal: Shao was imprisoned in the capital-district dungeon, denied food, and died gnawing his sleeves.

entries.zh: 及七月，大誅元氏，自昭成已下並無遺焉。
entries.en: By the seventh month came the great slaughter of the Yuan; from Emperor Zhaocheng down, none were spared.
entries.literal: By the seventh month came the great slaughter of the Yuan; from Zhaocheng down, none were spared.

entries.zh: 或父祖為王，或身常貴顯，或兄弟強壯，皆斬東市。
entries.en: Some had fathers or grandfathers who had been kings, some had themselves long held high rank, some had brothers in their prime — all were beheaded at the Eastern Market.
entries.literal: Some had fathers or grandfathers who were kings, some had themselves long held high rank, some had brothers in their prime — all were beheaded at the Eastern Market.

entries.zh: 其嬰兒投於空中，承之以矟。
entries.en: Their infants were tossed into the air and caught on spears.
entries.literal: Their infants were tossed into the air and caught on spears.

entries.zh: 前後死者凡七百二十一人，悉投屍漳水，剖魚多得爪甲，都下為之久不食魚。
entries.en: Seven hundred twenty-one died in all; every corpse was cast into the Zhang River. When fish were gutted, claws and nails were found inside; for a long time the capital would not eat fish.
entries.literal: In all, before and after, seven hundred twenty-one died; all corpses were cast into the Zhang River. When fish were gutted many claws and nails were found; for a long time the capital would not eat fish.

entries.zh: 李渾 子湛 渾弟繪 族子公緒 李璵 弟瑾 族弟曉 鄭述祖 子元德
entries.en: Li Hun; his son Zhan; Hun's brother Hui; clansman Gongxu; Li Yu; brother Jin; clansman Xiao; Zheng Shuzu; son Yuande
entries.literal: Li Hun; his son Zhan; Hun's brother Hui; clansman Gongxu; Li Yu; brother Jin; clansman Xiao; Zheng Shuzu; son Yuande

entries.zh: 繪，字敬文。
entries.en: Hui, styled Jingwen.
entries.literal: Hui, styled Jingwen.

entries.zh: 年六歲，便自願入學，家人偶以年俗忌，約而弗許。
entries.en: At age six he himself wished to enter school; his family, by chance observing a taboo of the year, restrained him and would not allow it.
entries.literal: At age six he himself wished to enter school; his family, by chance observing a taboo of the year, restrained him and would not allow it.

entries.zh: 伺其伯姊筆牘之間，而輒竊用，未幾遂通《急就章》。
entries.en: He watched his elder cousin sister between brush and inkstone and would steal use of them; before long he had mastered the Jijiuzhang.
entries.literal: He watched his elder cousin sister between brush and inkstone and would steal use of them; before long he had mastered the Jijiuzhang.

entries.zh: 內外異之，以為非常兒也。
entries.en: Inside and outside the family marveled at him, considering him no ordinary child.
entries.literal: Inside and outside the family marveled at him, considering him no ordinary child.

entries.zh: 及長，儀貌端偉，神情朗儁。
entries.en: When grown, his bearing was dignified and imposing, his spirit bright and outstanding.
entries.literal: When grown, his bearing was dignified and imposing, his spirit bright and outstanding.

entries.zh: 河間邢晏，卽繪舅也，與繪清言，歎其高遠。
entries.en: Xing Yan of Hejian — Hui's maternal uncle — conversed in pure talk with Hui and admired his loftiness.
entries.literal: Xing Yan of Hejian — Hui's maternal uncle — conversed in pure talk with Hui and admired his loftiness.

entries.zh: 每稱曰：「若披雲霧，如對珠玉，宅相之寄，良在此甥。」
entries.en: He often praised him, "As if parting the clouds and mist, as if facing pearls and jade — the hopes of the clan seat rest on this nephew."
entries.literal: He often praised him: "As if parting the clouds and mist, as if facing pearls and jade — the hopes of the clan seat rest on this nephew."

entries.zh: 齊王蕭寶夤引為主簿記室，專管表檄，待以賓友之禮。
entries.en: Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin brought him in as chief clerk and recorder, put him in charge of memorials and proclamations, and treated him with the courtesy due a guest and friend.
entries.literal: Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin brought him in as chief clerk and recorder, put him in charge of memorials and proclamations, and treated him with the courtesy due a guest and friend.

entries.zh: 司徒高邕辟為從事中郎，徵至洛。
entries.en: Grand Secretary Gao Yong summoned him as attendant gentleman; he was called to Luoyang.
entries.literal: Grand Secretary Gao Yong summoned him as attendant gentleman; he was called to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 時勑侍中西河王、秘書監常景選儒學十人緝撰五禮，繪與太原王乂同掌軍禮。
entries.en: At the time an edict had the attendant-in-ordinary Prince of Xihe and Secretary Director Chang Jing select ten Confucian scholars to compile the Five Rites; Hui and Wang Yi of Taiyuan together took charge of military rites.
entries.literal: At the time an edict had the attendant-in-ordinary Prince Xihe of the Western River, Secretary Director Chang Jing, and ten Confucian scholars compile the Five Rites; Hui and Wang Yi of Taiyuan together took charge of military rites.

entries.zh: 魏靜帝於顯陽殿講《孝經》、《禮記》，繪與從弟騫、裴伯茂、魏收、盧元明等俱為錄議。
entries.en: Emperor Jing of Wei lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Record of Rites at the Xianyang Hall; Hui and his cousin Qian, Pei Bomo, Wei Shou, Lu Yuanming, and others were all recorders and discussants.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing of Wei lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Record of Rites at the Xianyang Hall; Hui and his cousin Qian, Pei Bomo, Wei Shou, Lu Yuanming, and others were all recorders and discussants.

entries.zh: 素長筆札，尤能傳受，緝綴詞議，簡舉可觀。
entries.en: He had long excelled at letters; he was especially able to transmit and receive; in compiling and stitching together discussions, his selections were worth viewing.
entries.literal: He had long excelled at letters; he was especially able to transmit and receive; in compiling and stitching together discussions, his selections were worth viewing.

entries.zh: 天平初，世宗用為丞相司馬。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianping, Gao Cheng employed him as staff officer to the chancellor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, Gao Cheng employed him as staff officer to the chancellor.

entries.zh: 每罷朝，文武總集，對揚王庭，常令繪先發言端，為群僚之首。
entries.en: Whenever court adjourned, civil and military officials would all assemble and debate before the royal court; he was regularly made to open the discussion, first among the officials.
entries.literal: Whenever court adjourned, civil and military officials would all assemble and debate before the royal court; he was regularly made to open the discussion, first among the officials.

entries.zh: 音辭辯正，風儀都雅，聽者悚然。
entries.en: His words were clear and correct, his bearing altogether elegant; listeners were awed.
entries.literal: His words were clear and correct, his bearing altogether elegant; listeners were awed.

entries.zh: 使還，拜平南將軍、高陽內史。
entries.en: On his return he was appointed general who pacifies the south and inner administrator of Gaoyang.
entries.literal: On his return he was appointed general who pacifies the south and inner administrator of Gaoyang.

entries.zh: 郡境舊有猛獸，民常患之。
entries.en: Within the commandery there had long been fierce beasts; the people often suffered from them.
entries.literal: Within the commandery there had long been fierce beasts; the people often suffered from them.

entries.zh: 繪欲修檻，遂因鬬死。
entries.en: Hui wished to build a cage-trap; the beast thereupon died in a fight.
entries.literal: Hui wished to build a cage-trap; the beast thereupon died in a fight.

entries.zh: 咸以為化感所致，皆請申上。
entries.en: All considered it an effect of transforming influence and asked to report it upward.
entries.literal: All considered it an effect of transforming influence and asked to report it upward.

entries.zh: 繪曰：「猛獸因鬥而斃，自是偶然，貪此為功，人將窺我。」
entries.en: Hui said, "The fierce beast died fighting — that was mere chance; if I greedily claim it as merit, people will peer into me."
entries.literal: Hui said: "The fierce beast died fighting — that was mere chance; if I greedily claim it as merit, people will peer into me."

entries.zh: 竟不聽。
entries.en: In the end he would not listen.
entries.literal: In the end he would not listen.

entries.zh: 高祖東巡郡國，在瀛州城西駐馬久立，使慰之曰：「孤在晉，知山東守唯卿一人用意。
entries.en: Gao Huan toured the commanderies eastward; west of Yingzhou city he halted his horse and stood long; he sent word of comfort, "When I was in Jin, I knew that among the governors east of the mountains only you alone applied your mind.
entries.literal: Gao Huan toured the commanderies eastward; west of Yingzhou city he halted his horse and stood long; he sent word of comfort: "When I was in Jin, I knew that among the governors east of the mountains only you alone applied your mind.

entries.zh: 及入境觀風，信如所聞。
entries.en: Now that I have entered your territory and observed the winds, it is as I heard.
entries.literal: Now that I have entered your territory and observed the winds, it is as I heard.

entries.zh: 但善始令終，將位至不次。」
entries.en: Only see that you begin well and end well — your rank will rise beyond the ordinary."
entries.literal: Only see that you begin well and end well — your rank will rise beyond the ordinary."

entries.zh: 河間守崔謀恃其弟暹勢，從繪乞麋角鴿羽。
entries.en: Administrator of Hejian Cui Mou relied on the power of his younger brother Xian and begged from Hui elk horns and pigeon feathers.
entries.literal: Administrator of Hejian Cui Mou relied on the power of his younger brother Xian and begged from Hui elk horns and pigeon feathers.

entries.zh: 繪答書曰：「鴿有六翮，飛則沖天，麋有四足，走便入海。
entries.en: Hui replied in a letter, "The pigeon has six pinions — in flight it pierces the sky; the elk has four legs — in running it soon reaches the sea.
entries.literal: Hui replied in a letter: "The pigeon has six pinions — in flight it pierces the sky; the elk has four legs — in running it soon reaches the sea.

entries.zh: 下官膚體疏懶，手足遲鈍，不能逐飛追走，遠事佞人。」
entries.en: This humble officer's flesh is slack and lazy, his hands and feet slow and dull; I cannot chase what flies or pursue what runs, and go far to serve a flatterer."
entries.literal: This humble officer's flesh is slack and lazy, his hands and feet slow and dull; I cannot chase what flies or pursue what runs, and go far to serve a flatterer."

entries.zh: 是時世宗使暹選司徒長史，暹薦繪，旣而不果，咸謂由此書。
entries.en: At the time Gao Cheng had Xian select the chief clerk of the Minister over the Masses; Xian recommended Hui, but in the end it did not come to pass — all said it was because of this letter.
entries.literal: At the time Gao Cheng had Xian select the chief clerk of the Minister over the Masses; Xian recommended Hui, but in the end it did not come to pass — all said it was because of this letter.

entries.zh: 天保初，為司徒右長史。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianbao he was chief clerk on the right of the Minister over the Masses.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was chief clerk on the right of the Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 繪質性方重，未嘗趨事權勢，以此久而屈沈。
entries.en: Hui's nature was square and weighty; he never hurried to serve the powerful — for this reason he long remained suppressed and obscure.
entries.literal: Hui's nature was square and weighty; he never hurried to serve the powerful — for this reason he long remained suppressed and obscure.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 贈南青州刺史，謚曰景。
entries.en: He was posthumously made governor of Southern Qingzhou; his posthumous title was Jing.
entries.literal: He was posthumously made governor of Southern Qingzhou; his posthumous title was Jing.

entries.zh: 武定初，兼常侍，為聘梁使主。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wuding he was concurrent regular attendant and chief envoy on a mission to Liang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was concurrent regular attendant and chief envoy on a mission to Liang.

entries.zh: 梁武帝問繪：「高相今在何處？」
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Liang asked Hui, "Where is Chancellor Gao now?"
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang asked Hui: "Where is Chancellor Gao now?"

entries.zh: 繪曰：「今在晉陽，肅遏邊寇。」
entries.en: Hui said, "He is now at Jinyang, sternly repelling border raiders."
entries.literal: Hui said: "He is now at Jinyang, sternly repelling border raiders."

entries.zh: 梁武曰：「黑獺若為形容？
entries.en: Emperor Wu said, "What is Black Badger's appearance like?
entries.literal: Emperor Wu said: "What is Black Badger's appearance like?

entries.zh: 高相作何經略？」
entries.en: What strategy does Chancellor Gao pursue?"
entries.literal: What strategy does Chancellor Gao pursue?"

entries.zh: 繪曰：「黑獺遊魂關右，人神厭毒，連歲凶災，百姓懷土。
entries.en: Hui said, "Black Badger is a stray spirit in the west, loathed by men and spirits alike; year after year brings fierce calamity and the people yearn for their homeland.
entries.literal: Hui said: "Black Badger is a stray spirit in the west, loathed by men and spirits alike; year after year brings fierce calamity and the people yearn for their homeland.

entries.zh: 丞相奇略不世，畜銳觀釁，攻昧取亡，勢必不遠。」
entries.en: The chancellor's stratagems are unmatched in the age; he gathers sharp blades and watches for an opening — attacking the benighted to take the doomed — victory cannot be far."
entries.literal: The chancellor's stratagems are unmatched in the age; he gathers sharp blades and watches for an opening — attacking the benighted to take the doomed — victory cannot be far."

entries.zh: 梁武曰：「如卿言極佳。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu said, "As you say — excellent."
entries.literal: Emperor Wu said: "As you say — excellent."

entries.zh: 與梁人泛言氏族，袁狎曰：「未若我本出自黃帝，姓在十四之限。」
entries.en: With the men of Liang he spoke at large on clans; Yuan Xia said, "Still not as good as my house — we issue from the Yellow Emperor and our surname stands within the fourteen."
entries.literal: With the men of Liang he spoke at large on clans; Yuan Xia said: "Still not as good as my house — we issue from the Yellow Emperor and our surname stands within the fourteen."

entries.zh: 繪曰：「兄所出雖遠，當共車千秋分一字耳。」
entries.en: Hui said, "Though what you issue from is remote, you should share one character with Che Qianqiu."
entries.literal: Hui said: "Though what you issue from is remote, you should share one character with Che Qianqiu."

entries.zh: 一坐大笑。
entries.en: The whole company laughed aloud.
entries.literal: The whole company laughed aloud.

entries.zh: 前後行人，皆通啟求市，繪獨守清尚，梁人重其廉潔。
entries.en: Envoys who came before and after all sent letters opening relations and seeking trade; Hui alone kept to purity and loftiness — the men of Liang respected his integrity.
entries.literal: Envoys who came before and after all sent letters opening relations and seeking trade; Hui alone kept to purity and loftiness — the men of Liang respected his integrity.

entries.zh: 子湛，字處元。
entries.en: His son Zhan, styled Chuyuan.
entries.literal: His son Zhan, styled Chuyuan.

entries.zh: 涉獵文史，有家風。
entries.en: He ranged widely in letters and histories and had the family's manner.
entries.literal: He ranged widely in letters and histories and had the family's manner.

entries.zh: 為太子舍人，兼常侍，聘陳使副。
entries.en: He served as attendant to the heir apparent, concurrent regular attendant, and deputy envoy on a mission to Chen.
entries.literal: He served as attendant to the heir apparent, concurrent regular attendant, and deputy envoy on a mission to Chen.

entries.zh: 襲爵涇陽縣男。
entries.en: He inherited the title baron of Jingyang county.
entries.literal: He inherited the title Baron of Jingyang county.

entries.zh: 渾與弟繪、緯俱為聘梁使主，湛又為使副，是以趙郡人士，目為四使之門。
entries.en: Hun and his brothers Hui and Wei had all been chief envoys on missions to Liang; Zhan again served as deputy envoy — hence men of Zhao commandery called them the Gate of Four Envoys.
entries.literal: Hun and his brothers Hui and Wei had all been chief envoys on missions to Liang; Zhan again served as deputy envoy — hence men of Zhao commandery called them the Gate of Four Envoys.

entries.zh: 李渾，字季初，趙郡栢人人也。
entries.en: Li Hun, styled Jichu, was a man of Bairen in Zhao commandery.
entries.literal: Li Hun, styled Jichu, was a man of Bairen in Zhao commandery.

entries.zh: 曾祖靈，魏鉅鹿公。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Ling was duke of Julu under Wei.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Ling was Duke of Julu under Wei.

entries.zh: 父遵，魏冀州征東府司馬，京兆王愉冀州起逆，遇害。
entries.en: His father Zun was staff officer of the eastern campaigning headquarters in Jizhou under Wei; when Prince Jingzhao Yu rose in revolt in Jizhou, he met disaster and was killed.
entries.literal: His father Zun was staff officer of the Eastern Campaigning Headquarters in Jizhou under Wei; when Prince Jingzhao Yu rose in revolt in Jizhou, he met disaster and was killed.

entries.zh: 渾以父死王事，除給事中。
entries.en: Because his father died in the prince's service, Hun was appointed attendant within the yellow gates.
entries.literal: Because his father died in the prince's service, Hun was appointed attendant within the yellow gates.

entries.zh: 時四方多難，乃謝病，求為青州征東府司馬。
entries.en: When troubles multiplied on all sides, he resigned on grounds of illness and sought appointment as staff officer of the eastern campaigning headquarters in Qingzhou.
entries.literal: When troubles multiplied on all sides, he resigned on grounds of illness and sought appointment as staff officer of the Eastern Campaigning Headquarters in Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 與河間邢卲、北海王昕俱奉老母、攜妻子同赴青、齊。
entries.en: Together with Xing Shao of Hejian and Wang Xin of Beihai, they all supported their aged mothers and took wives and children on the same journey to Qing and Qi.
entries.literal: Together with Xing Shao of Hejian and Wang Xin of Beihai, they each supported their aged mothers and took wives and children on the same journey to Qing and Qi.

entries.zh: 未幾而尒朱榮入洛，衣冠殲盡。
entries.en: Before long Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and the gentry were wiped out.
entries.literal: Before long Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and the gentry were wiped out.

entries.zh: 論者以為知機。
entries.en: Commentators held that he had read the times aright.
entries.literal: Those who commented considered that he had shown foresight.

entries.zh: 永安初，除散騎常侍。
entries.en: At the beginning of Yong'an he was appointed attendant cavalier in regular attendance.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was appointed attendant cavalier in regular attendance.

entries.zh: 璵從弟曉，字仁略。
entries.en: Yu's cousin Xiao, styled Renlue.
entries.literal: Yu's cousin Xiao, styled Renlue.

entries.zh: 魏太尉虔子。
entries.en: He was a son of Wei grand commandant Qian.
entries.literal: He was a son of Wei Grand Commandant Qian.

entries.zh: 學涉有思理。
entries.en: Broad in learning, with a keen mind.
entries.literal: Broad in learning, with power of thought.

entries.zh: 釋褐員外侍郎。
entries.en: Upon removing mourning he became an outer secretariat attendant.
entries.literal: Upon removing mourning he became an outer secretariat attendant.

entries.zh: 尒朱榮之害朝士，將行，曉衣冠為鼠所噬，遂不成行，得免河陰之難。
entries.en: When Erzhu Rong was about to slaughter the court gentlemen and Xiao was to go, rats gnawed his robe and cap; he could not set out and so escaped the disaster at Heyin.
entries.literal: When Erzhu Rong was about to harm the court gentlemen and Xiao was to go, rats gnawed his robe and cap; he could not go and so escaped the disaster at Heyin.

entries.zh: 及遷都鄴，曉便寓居清河，託從母兄崔悛宅。
entries.en: When the capital moved to Ye, Xiao lodged in Qinghe at the home of his mother's sister's son, Cui Juan.
entries.literal: When the capital moved to Ye, Xiao lodged in Qinghe and entrusted himself to his mother's sister's son Cui Juan's house.

entries.zh: 給良田三十頃，曉遂築室安居，訓勗子侄，無復宦情。
entries.en: He was granted thirty qing of fertile land; Xiao built a house, settled in peace, and schooled his nephews — with no further wish for office.
entries.literal: He was granted thirty qing of fertile fields; Xiao then built a house and dwelt at ease, instructing and urging his nephews, with no further desire for office.

entries.zh: 武定末，以世道方泰，乃入都從仕。
entries.en: At the end of Wuding, seeing the age at peace, he entered the capital to serve.
entries.literal: At the end of Wuding, seeing the age was at peace, he entered the capital to take office.

entries.zh: 除頓丘守，卒。
entries.en: He was made magistrate of Dunqiu and died in office.
entries.literal: He was made magistrate of Dunqiu and died in office.

entries.zh: 後除光祿大夫，兼常侍，聘使至梁。
entries.en: Later he was appointed grand master for illuminating government and concurrent regular attendant, and sent as envoy to Liang.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed grand master for illuminating government and concurrent regular attendant, envoy to Liang.

entries.zh: 梁武謂之曰：「伯陽之後，久而彌盛，趙李人物，今實居多。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Liang said to him, "Descendants of Boyang — the longer the line runs, the more it flourishes; men of the Zhao Li clan are truly numerous today.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang said to him: "Descendants of Boyang — the longer, the more they flourish; men of the Zhao Li clan are truly numerous today.

entries.zh: 常侍曾經將領，今復充使，文武不墜，良屬斯人。」
entries.en: You once served as a commander; now again you fill an envoy's post — civil and military alike unbroken. How fitting in such a man."
entries.literal: The attendant once served as a commander; now again you fill an envoy's post — civil and military alike unbroken: how fitting in such a man."

entries.zh: 使還，為東郡太守，以贓徵還。
entries.en: On his return he became administrator of Dong commandery; he was recalled on charges of corruption.
entries.literal: On return he became administrator of Dong commandery; he was recalled on charges of corruption.

entries.zh: 世宗使武士提以入，渾抗言曰：「將軍今日猶自禮賢耶？」
entries.en: Gao Cheng had warriors seize and bring him in; Hun spoke up boldly, "Does the general still treat the worthy with courtesy today?"
entries.literal: Gao Cheng had warriors seize and bring him in; Hun spoke up boldly: "Does the general still treat the worthy with courtesy today?"

entries.zh: 世宗笑而捨之。
entries.en: Gao Cheng laughed and let him go.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng laughed and let him go.

entries.zh: 元德從父弟元禮，字文規。
entries.en: Yuande's cousin Yuan Li, styled Wengui.
entries.literal: Yuande's cousin Yuan Li, styled Wengui.

entries.zh: 少好學，愛文藻，有名望。
entries.en: In youth he loved learning and prized literary ornament; he had fame and standing.
entries.literal: In youth he loved learning and prized literary ornament; he had fame and standing.

entries.zh: 世宗引為館客，歷太子舍人。
entries.en: Gao Cheng retained him as retainer-guest; he served in turn as crown prince attendant.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng retained him as a retainer-guest and he served in succession as crown prince attendant.

entries.zh: 崔昂妻，卽元禮之姊也，魏收又昂之妹夫。
entries.en: Cui Ang's wife was Yuan Li's elder sister; Wei Shou was also Ang's brother-in-law.
entries.literal: Cui Ang's wife was Yuan Li's elder sister; Wei Shou was also Ang's brother-in-law.

entries.zh: 昂嘗持元禮數篇詩示盧思道，乃謂思道云：「看元禮比來詩詠，亦當不減魏收？」
entries.en: Ang once showed several of Yuan Li's poems to Lu Sidao and said, "Look at Yuan Li's recent poems — are they not the equal of Wei Shou?"
entries.literal: Ang once showed several of Yuan Li's poems to Lu Sidao and said to Sidao: "Look at Yuan Li's recent poems — are they not the equal of Wei Shou?"

entries.zh: 答云：「未覺元禮賢於魏收，但知妹夫疏於婦弟。」
entries.en: He answered, "I do not feel Yuan Li is better than Wei Shou — I only know a brother-in-law is cold to his wife's brother."
entries.literal: He answered: "I do not feel Yuan Li is better than Wei Shou — I only know a brother-in-law is cold to his wife's brother."

entries.zh: 元禮入周，卒於始州別駕。
entries.en: Yuan Li entered Zhou and died as vice governor of Shi prefecture.
entries.literal: Yuan Li entered Zhou and died as vice governor of Shi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 暹前後表彈尚書令司馬子如及尚書元羨、雍州刺史慕容獻，又彈太師咸陽王坦、幷州刺史可朱渾道元，罪狀極筆，並免官。
entries.en: Xian successively memorialized and impeached Minister of Works Sima Ziru, the minister Yuan Xian, and Administrator of Yong province Murong Xian, and also impeached Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang Tan and inspector of Bing province Kezhuhun Daoyuan—the charges written to the utmost; all were removed from office.
entries.literal: Xian successively memorialized and impeached Minister of Works Sima Ziru and the minister Yuan Xian and Administrator of Yong province Murong Xian, also impeached Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang Wang Tan and Inspector of Bing province Kezhuhun Daoyuan—the charges written to the utmost; all were removed from office.

entries.zh: 其餘死黜者甚衆。
entries.en: Of the rest, those killed or dismissed were very many.
entries.literal: Of the rest, those killed or dismissed were very many.

entries.zh: 高祖書與鄴下諸貴曰：「崔暹昔事家弟為定州長史，後吾兒開府諮議，及遷左丞吏部郎，吾未知其能也。
entries.en: Gao Huan wrote to the nobles at Ye, "Cui Xian once served my younger brother as chief clerk of Dingzhou, later my son's grand marshalate deliberator, and when moved to left vice director and director of the ministry of personnel I did not yet know his ability.
entries.literal: Gao Huan wrote to the nobles at Ye: "Cui Xian once served my younger brother as chief clerk of Dingzhou, later my son's grand marshalate deliberator, and when moved to left vice director and director of the ministry of personnel I did not yet know his ability.

entries.zh: 始居憲臺，乃爾糾劾。
entries.en: Only when he took the inspectorate did he correct and impeach thus.
entries.literal: Only when he took the inspectorate did he correct and impeach thus.

entries.zh: 咸陽王、司馬令並是吾對門布衣之舊，尊貴親昵，無過二人，同時獲罪，吾不能救，諸君其慎之。」
entries.en: Prince of Xianyang and Minister Sima were both my old companions of common cloth opposite the gate, honored and intimate beyond all others; at the same time they incurred guilt—I could not save them; gentlemen, be wary."
entries.literal: Prince of Xianyang and Minister Sima were both my old companions of common cloth opposite the gate, honored and intimate beyond all others; at the same time they incurred guilt—I could not save them; gentlemen, be wary."

entries.zh: 高祖如京師，羣官迎於紫陌。
entries.en: When Gao Huan went to the capital, the officials welcomed him at Zimo.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan went to the capital, the officials welcomed him at Zimo.

entries.zh: 高祖握暹手而勞之曰：「往前朝廷豈無法官，而天下貪婪，莫肯糾劾。
entries.en: Gao Huan took Xian's hand and praised him, "Before, was there no judge in the court? Yet greed ran through the realm and none would impeach.
entries.literal: Gao Huan took Xian's hand and praised him: "Before, was there no judge in the court? Yet greed ran through the realm and none would impeach.

entries.zh: 中尉盡心為國，不避豪強，遂使遠邇肅清，羣公奉法。
entries.en: The chief inspector has devoted his heart to the state, not avoiding the powerful, and thus near and far are brought to order and the lords uphold the law.
entries.literal: The chief inspector has devoted his heart to the state, not avoiding the powerful, and thus near and far are brought to order and the lords uphold the law.

entries.zh: 衝鋒陷陣，大有其人，當官正色，今始見之。
entries.en: To charge battle lines—there are many such men; to hold office with upright countenance—only now do I see it.
entries.literal: To charge battle lines—there are many such men; to hold office with upright countenance—only now do I see it.

entries.zh: 今榮華富貴，直是中尉自取，高歡父子，無以相報。」
entries.en: Wealth and glory today are simply what the chief inspector has earned for himself; father and son Gao Huan have no way to repay it."
entries.literal: Wealth and glory today are simply what the chief inspector has earned for himself; father and son Gao Huan have no way to repay it."

entries.zh: 賜暹良馬，使騎之以從，且行且語。
entries.en: He granted Xian a fine horse and had him ride alongside, talking as they went.
entries.literal: He granted Xian a fine horse and had him ride alongside, talking as they went.

entries.zh: 暹下拜，馬驚走，高祖為擁之而授轡。
entries.en: Xian bowed; the horse bolted in fright; Gao Huan embraced him and handed him the reins.
entries.literal: Xian bowed; the horse bolted in fright; Gao Huan embraced him and handed him the reins.

entries.zh: 魏帝宴於華林園，謂高祖曰：「自頃朝貴、牧守令長、所在百司多有貪暴，侵削下人。
entries.en: The Wei emperor feasted at Hualin Garden and said to Gao Huan, "Of late, court nobles, prefects and county chiefs, and the hundred offices in every place have many been greedy and violent, encroaching on inferiors.
entries.literal: The Wei emperor feasted at Hualin Garden and said to Gao Huan: "Of late, court nobles, prefects and county chiefs, and the hundred offices in every place have many been greedy and violent, encroaching on inferiors.

entries.zh: 朝廷之中有用心公平，直言彈劾，不避親戚者，王可勸酒。」
entries.en: In the court there are those who apply their hearts with fairness and impeach in straight speech, not avoiding kin—Wang may urge them to drink."
entries.literal: In the court there are those who apply their hearts with fairness and impeach in straight speech, not avoiding kin—Wang may urge them to drink."

entries.zh: 高祖降階，跪而言曰：「唯御史中尉崔暹一人。
entries.en: Gao Huan descended the steps, knelt, and said, "Only Chief Inspector Cui Xian, one man.
entries.literal: Gao Huan descended the steps, knelt, and said: "Only Chief Inspector Cui Xian, one man.

entries.zh: 謹奉明旨，敢以酒勸，並臣所射賜物千疋，乞回賜之。」
entries.en: Reverently following the clear command, I dare urge wine upon him—and furthermore the thousand bolts of cloth from my archery gift, I beg they be turned and given to him."
entries.literal: Reverently following the clear command, I dare urge wine upon him—and furthermore the thousand bolts of cloth from my archery gift, I beg they be turned and given to him."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「崔中尉為法，道俗齊整。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Chief Inspector Cui upholds the law; ways and customs are alike regulated."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Chief Inspector Cui upholds the law; ways and customs are alike regulated."

entries.zh: 暹謝曰：「此自陛下風化所加，大將軍臣澄勸獎之力。」
entries.en: Xian thanked him, "This is from Your Majesty's transforming influence, and the urging and reward of my lord Grand General Cheng."
entries.literal: Xian thanked him: "This is from Your Majesty's transforming influence, and the urging and reward of my lord the Grand General Cheng."

entries.zh: 世宗退謂暹曰：「我尚畏羨，何況餘人。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng withdrew and said to Xian, "I still fear those impeachments—how much more others."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng withdrew and said to Xian: "I still fear those impeachments—how much more others."

entries.zh: 由是威名日盛，內外莫不畏服。
entries.en: Thereafter his awe-inspiring name grew daily; inside and outside all feared him and submitted.
entries.literal: Thereafter his awe-inspiring name grew daily; inside and outside none did not fear and submit.

entries.zh: 崔暹，字季倫，博陵安平人，漢尚書寔之後也，世為北州著姓。
entries.en: Cui Xian, styled Jilun, was a man of Anping in Boling commandery, a descendant of Cui Shi, Han minister of works, and for generations a leading house of the northern provinces.
entries.literal: Cui Xian, styled Jilun, was a man of Anping in Boling commandery, a descendant of Cui Shi, Han Minister of Works, and for generations a prominent clan of the northern provinces.

entries.zh: 父穆，州主簿。
entries.en: His father Mu was a provincial clerk.
entries.literal: His father Mu was a commandery clerk.

entries.zh: 暹少為書生，避地渤海，依高乾，以妹妻乾弟慎。
entries.en: In youth Xian was a student; he fled to Bohai and attached himself to Gao Gan, giving his sister in marriage to Gan's brother Shen.
entries.literal: In youth Xian was a student; he fled to Bohai and relied on Gao Gan, giving his sister in marriage to Gan's brother Shen.

entries.zh: 慎後臨光州，啟暹為長史。
entries.en: When Shen later governed Guangzhou, he had Xian appointed chief clerk.
entries.literal: When Shen later held Guangzhou, he had Xian appointed chief clerk.

entries.zh: 趙郡公琛鎮定州，辟為開府諮議。
entries.en: Duke of Zhao Commandery Chen, defending Dingzhou, engaged him as deliberator of the grand marshalate.
entries.literal: Duke of Zhao Commandery Chen, defending Dingzhou, engaged him as deliberator of the grand marshalate.

entries.zh: 隨琛往晉陽，高祖與語說之，以兼丞相長史。
entries.en: Following Chen to Jinyang, Gao Huan conversed with him and was pleased, appointing him acting chief clerk to the chancellor.
entries.literal: Following Chen to Jinyang, Gao Huan conversed with him and was pleased, appointing him acting chief clerk to the chancellor.

entries.zh: 高祖舉兵將入洛，留暹佐琛知後事。
entries.en: When Gao Huan raised troops to enter Luoyang, he left Xian to assist Chen in managing affairs behind the lines.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan raised troops to enter Luoyang, he left Xian to assist Chen in managing rear affairs.

entries.zh: 謂之曰：「丈夫相知，豈在新舊。
entries.en: He said to him, "When men know one another, is it a matter of new or old?
entries.literal: He said to him: "When men know one another, is it a matter of new or old?

entries.zh: 軍戎事重，留守任切，家弟年少，未閑事宜，凡百後事，一以相屬。」
entries.en: Military affairs are weighty and the duty of holding the rear is pressing; my younger brother is young and not yet versed in affairs—for every matter behind, I entrust all to you."
entries.literal: Military affairs are weighty, and the duty of staying behind is pressing; my younger brother is young and not yet versed in affairs—for every matter behind, I entrust all to you."

entries.zh: 握手殷勤，至於三四。
entries.en: They clasped hands earnestly, three or four times over.
entries.literal: They clasped hands earnestly, three or four times.

entries.zh: 後遷左丞、吏部郎，主議《麟趾格》。
entries.en: Later he was moved to left vice director and director of the ministry of personnel, and took chief part in deliberating the Linzhi Code.
entries.literal: Later he was moved to left vice director and director of the ministry of personnel, and took chief part in deliberating the Linzhi Code.

entries.zh: 德政還未至，帝便發晉陽，至平城都，召諸勳將入，告以禪讓之事。
entries.en: Before Dezheng returned, Gao Yang had already left Jinyang, reached the fortress at Pingcheng, summoned the meritorious generals, and told them of the abdication.
entries.literal: Before Dezheng could return, the emperor had already set out from Jinyang, reached the fortress at Pingcheng, summoned the meritorious generals in, and told them of the abdication.

entries.zh: 諸將等忽聞，皆愕然，莫敢答者。
entries.en: The generals heard it all at once and stood stunned; none dared speak.
entries.literal: The generals heard it suddenly; all were stunned, and none dared answer.

entries.zh: 時杜弼為長史，密啟顯祖云：「關西是國家勁敵，若今受魏禪，恐其稱義兵挾天子而東向，王將何以待之？」
entries.en: Du Bi was chief clerk at the time; he secretly reported to Gao Yang, "Guanxi is the state's hard enemy. If you accept Wei's abdication now, I fear they will call it a righteous army, take the Son of Heaven in hand, and march east — how will you meet them?"
entries.literal: At the time Du Bi was chief clerk; he secretly reported to Gao Yang: "Guanxi is the state's formidable foe. If you now accept Wei's abdication, I fear they will raise a righteous army, take the Son of Heaven in hand, and march east — how will Your Highness meet them?"

entries.zh: 顯祖入，召弼入與徐之才相告。
entries.en: Gao Yang went in and summoned Bi to tell Xu Zhicai together.
entries.literal: Gao Yang entered and summoned Bi in to tell Xu Zhicai together.

entries.zh: 之才云：「今與王爭天下者，彼意亦欲為帝，譬如逐兔滿市，一人得之，衆心皆定。
entries.en: Xu Zhicai said, "Whoever contends with you for the realm today wants to be emperor too — like chasing a rabbit through a crowded market: once one man catches it, every heart settles.
entries.literal: Xu Zhicai said: "He who contends with you for the realm today likewise means to become emperor — like chasing a rabbit through a crowded market: once one man catches it, every heart is settled.

entries.zh: 今若先受魏禪，關西自應息心。
entries.en: Accept Wei's abdication first and Guanxi should quiet of itself.
entries.literal: If you accept Wei's abdication first, Guanxi should of itself quiet its heart.

entries.zh: 縱欲屈強，止當逐我稱帝。
entries.en: Even if they mean to force the issue, at most they will chase us in declaring themselves emperor.
entries.literal: Even if they wish to bend their strength against us, at most they will chase us in proclaiming emperorship.

entries.zh: 必宜知機先覺，無容後以學人。」
entries.en: You must know the moment and move first — no learning from others after the fact."
entries.literal: You must seize the moment and be first to perceive the chance — no room to learn from others afterward."

entries.zh: 弼無以答。
entries.en: Bi had nothing to say.
entries.literal: Bi had nothing to answer.

entries.zh: 帝已遣馳驛向鄴，書與太尉高岳、尚書令高隆之、領軍婁睿、侍中張亮、黃門趙彥深、楊愔等。
entries.en: Gao Yang had already sent post-horses toward Ye with letters to Grand Commandant Gao Yue, Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi, army supervisor Lou Rui, palace attendant Zhang Liang, yellow gate Zhao Yanshen, Yang Yin, and the rest.
entries.literal: The emperor had already sent post-horses toward Ye with letters to Grand Commandant Gao Yue, Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi, Army Supervisor Lou Rui, Palace Attendant Zhang Liang, Yellow Gate Zhao Yanshen, Yang Yin, and others.

entries.zh: 岳等馳傳至高陽驛，帝使約曰：「知諸貴等意，不須來。」
entries.en: Yue and the others rode express to the Gaoyang post-station; Gao Yang sent word, "I know what you nobles intend — you need not come."
entries.literal: Yue and the others rode express to the Gaoyang post-station; the emperor sent word: "I know what you nobles intend — no need to come."

entries.zh: 唯楊愔見，高岳等並還。
entries.en: Only Yang Yin was received; Gao Yue and the others all turned back.
entries.literal: Only Yang Yin was received; Gao Yue and the rest all returned.

entries.zh: 帝以衆人意未協，又先得太后旨云：「汝父如龍，汝兄如虎，尚以人臣終，汝何容欲行舜、禹事？
entries.en: Because the men's hearts were not yet one, Gao Yang had also received the empress dowager's word earlier: "Your father was like a dragon and your brother like a tiger, yet both died as subjects — how can you think to play Yao and Shun?
entries.literal: The emperor, because the men's hearts were not yet aligned, had also earlier received the empress dowager's charge: "Your father was like a dragon, your brother like a tiger — and both ended as subjects. How can you think to play Yao and Shun?

entries.zh: 此亦非汝意，正是高德政教汝。」
entries.en: This is not your thought either; it is Gao Dezheng teaching you."
entries.literal: This is not your own thought either; it is Gao Dezheng who is teaching you."

entries.zh: 又說者以為昔周武王再駕盟津，然始革命，於是乃旋晉陽。
entries.en: Others said that in old times King Wu of Zhou crossed the Meng Ford twice before he began the revolution — and so he turned back to Jinyang.
entries.literal: Others also urged that in old times King Wu of Zhou crossed the Meng Ford twice before he began the revolution — and so he turned back to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 自是居常不悅。
entries.en: From then on he was often ill at ease.
entries.literal: From then on he was habitually displeased.

entries.zh: 徐之才、宋景業等每言卜筮雜占陰陽緯侯，必宜五月應天順人，德政亦勸不已。
entries.en: Xu Zhicai, Song Jingye, and others kept speaking of divination, mixed auguries, yin and yang, and omens in the weft-texts — that May was the time to answer Heaven and win men; Dezheng urged on without pause.
entries.literal: Xu Zhicai, Song Jingye, and others constantly spoke of divination, miscellaneous auguries, yin and yang, and the weft-texts of omens — that May was surely the time to answer Heaven and accord with men; Dezheng too urged without cease.

entries.zh: 仍白帝追魏收。
entries.en: They also reported to Gao Yang to recall Wei Shou.
entries.literal: They also reported to the emperor to summon Wei Shou back.

entries.zh: 收至，令撰禪讓詔册、九錫建臺及勸進文表。
entries.en: When Shou arrived, he was ordered to draft the abdication edicts and registers, the Nine Bestowals, the founding terrace, and the memorials urging accession.
entries.literal: When Shou arrived, he was ordered to draft the abdication edicts and proclamations, the Nine Bestowals, establishment of the terrace, and the memorial tables urging accession.

entries.zh: 高祖崩，未發喪，世宗以暹為度支尚書，兼僕射，委以心腹之寄。
entries.en: When Gao Huan died, before the mourning was announced, Gao Cheng made Xian Director of Revenue and concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat, entrusting him with confidential responsibilities.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan died, before the mourning was announced, Gao Cheng made Xian Director of Revenue and concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat, entrusting him with confidential responsibilities.

entries.zh: 暹憂國如家，以天下為己任。
entries.en: Xian worried for the state as for his home, taking the realm as his charge.
entries.literal: Xian worried for the state as for his home, taking the realm as his charge.

entries.zh: 世宗車服過度，誅戮變常，言談進止，或有虧失，暹每厲色極言，世宗亦為之止。
entries.en: Gao Cheng's carriages and dress exceeded measure, executions were irregular, and in speech and conduct there were sometimes faults; Xian each time spoke sternly and to the utmost, and Gao Cheng also stopped on his account.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng's carriages and dress exceeded measure, executions were irregular, and in speech and conduct there were sometimes faults; Xian each time spoke sternly and to the utmost, and Gao Cheng also stopped on his account.

entries.zh: 有囚數百，世宗盡欲誅之，每催文帳。
entries.en: Several hundred prisoners—Gao Cheng wished to execute them all and daily pressed for the documents.
entries.literal: Several hundred prisoners—Gao Cheng wished to execute them all and daily pressed for the documents.

entries.zh: 暹故緩之，不以時進，世宗意釋，竟以獲免。
entries.en: Xian deliberately delayed them and did not submit in time; Gao Cheng's intent relaxed and in the end they were spared.
entries.literal: Xian deliberately delayed them and did not submit in time; Gao Cheng's intent relaxed and in the end they were spared.

entries.zh: 暹親遇日隆，好薦人士。
entries.en: Xian's personal favor grew day by day; he delighted in recommending men of talent.
entries.literal: Xian's personal favor grew day by day; he delighted in recommending men of talent.

entries.zh: 言邢卲宜任府僚，兼任機密，世宗因以徵卲，甚見親重。
entries.en: He said Xing Shao was fit for a staff post with access to secret affairs; Gao Cheng thereupon summoned Shao, who was greatly favored and trusted.
entries.literal: He said Xing Shao was fit for a staff post with access to secret affairs; Gao Cheng thereupon summoned Shao, who was greatly favored and trusted.

entries.zh: 言論之際，卲遂毀暹。
entries.en: In the course of talk, Shao then slandered Xian.
entries.literal: In the course of talk, Shao then slandered Xian.

entries.zh: 世宗不悅，謂暹曰：「卿說子才之長，子才專言卿短，此癡人也。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng was displeased and said to Xian, "You speak of Zicai's strengths, yet Zicai speaks only of your faults—this is a foolish man."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng was displeased and said to Xian: "You speak of Zicai's strengths, yet Zicai speaks only of your faults—this is a foolish man."

entries.zh: 暹曰：「子才言暹短，暹說子才長，皆是實事，不為嫌也。」
entries.en: Xian said, "Zicai speaks of Xian's faults; Xian speaks of Zicai's strengths—each states what is true, without rancor."
entries.literal: Xian said: "Zicai speaks of Xian's faults; Xian speaks of Zicai's strengths—each states what is true, without rancor."

entries.zh: 高慎之叛，與暹有隙，高祖欲殺之，世宗救免。
entries.en: When Gao Shen rebelled, having a rift with Xian, Gao Huan wished to kill him; Gao Cheng rescued and pardoned him.
entries.literal: When Gao Shen rebelled, having a rift with Xian, Gao Huan wished to kill him; Gao Cheng rescued and pardoned him.

entries.zh: 顯祖初嗣霸業，司馬子如等挾舊怨，言暹罪重，謂宜罰之。
entries.en: When Gao Yang first succeeded to the hegemony, Sima Ziru and others, nursing old grudges, said Xian's crimes were heavy and that he ought to be punished.
entries.literal: When Gao Yang first succeeded to the hegemony, Sima Ziru and others, nursing old grudges, said Xian's crimes were heavy and that he ought to be punished.

entries.zh: 高隆之亦言宜寬政網，去苛察法官，黜崔暹，則得遠近人意。
entries.en: Gao Longzhi also said the government net should be widened, harsh inspecting judges removed, and Cui Xian dismissed—then near and far would be satisfied.
entries.literal: Gao Longzhi also said the government net should be widened, harsh inspecting judges removed, and Cui Xian dismissed—then near and far would be satisfied.

entries.zh: 顯祖從之。
entries.en: Gao Yang followed this.
entries.literal: Gao Yang followed this.

entries.zh: 及踐祚，譖毀之者猶不息。
entries.en: When he took the throne, those who slandered him still did not cease.
entries.literal: When he took the throne, those who slandered him still did not cease.

entries.zh: 帝乃令都督陳山提等搜暹家，甚貧匱，唯得高祖、世宗與暹書千餘紙，多論軍中大事。
entries.en: Gao Yang then had Commander Chen Shanti and others search Xian's house—it was very poor; only a thousand-odd pages of letters from Gao Huan and Gao Cheng to Xian, mostly discussing great military affairs.
entries.literal: The emperor then had Commander Chen Shanti and others search Xian's house—it was very poor; only a thousand-odd pages of letters from Gao Huan and Gao Cheng to Xian, mostly discussing great military affairs.

entries.zh: 帝嗟賞之。
entries.en: Gao Yang sighed in admiration.
entries.literal: The emperor sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 仍不免衆口，乃流暹於馬城，晝則負土供役，夜則置地牢。
entries.en: Still he could not silence everyone's mouths; he exiled Xian to Macheng—by day he carried earth for corvée, by night he was shut in a dungeon.
entries.literal: Still he could not silence everyone's mouths; he exiled Xian to Macheng—by day he carried earth for corvée, by night he was shut in a dungeon.

entries.zh: 歲餘，奴告暹謀反，鎖赴晉陽，無實，釋而勞之。
entries.en: After more than a year, a slave reported Xian plotted rebellion; he was chained and taken to Jinyang—without substance; he was released and comforted.
entries.literal: After more than a year, a slave reported Xian plotted rebellion; he was chained and taken to Jinyang—without substance; he was released and comforted.

entries.zh: 高德政，字士貞，渤海蓚人。
entries.en: Gao Dezheng, styled Shizhen, was a man of Su in Bohai.
entries.literal: Gao Dezheng, styled Shizhen, was a man of Su in Bohai.

entries.zh: 父顥，魏滄州刺史。
entries.en: His father Hao was Wei inspector of Cangzhou.
entries.literal: His father Hao was Wei inspector of Cangzhou.

entries.zh: 德政幼而敏慧，有風神儀表。
entries.en: Dezheng was clever and keen in youth, with spirit and dignified bearing.
entries.literal: Dezheng was clever and keen in youth, with spirit and dignified bearing.

entries.zh: 顯祖引為開府參軍，知管記事，甚相親狎。
entries.en: Gao Yang brought him in as staff officer to the grand marshalate in charge of records, and was very intimate.
entries.literal: Gao Yang brought him in as staff officer to the grand marshalate in charge of records, and was very intimate.

entries.zh: 高祖又擢為相府掾，委以腹心。
entries.en: Gao Huan also promoted him as staff officer to the chancellor's residence, entrusting him as confidant.
entries.literal: Gao Huan also promoted him as staff officer to the chancellor's residence, entrusting him as confidant.

entries.zh: 遷黃門侍郎。
entries.en: He was moved to gentleman of the yellow gates.
entries.literal: He was moved to gentleman of the yellow gates.

entries.zh: 世宗嗣業，如晉陽，顯祖在京居守，令德政參掌機密，彌見親重。
entries.en: Gao Cheng succeeded to the enterprise and went to Jinyang; Gao Yang remained in the capital as defender and had Dezheng share in secret affairs, and favor grew still greater.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng succeeded to the enterprise; he went to Jinyang; Gao Yang remained in the capital as defender; he had Dezheng share in secret affairs, and favor grew still greater.

entries.zh: 世宗暴崩，事出倉卒，羣情草草。
entries.en: Gao Cheng died suddenly; affairs came in haste and the mood of the masses was disorderly.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng died suddenly; affairs came in haste and the mood of the masses was disorderly.

entries.zh: 勳將等以纘戎事重，勸帝早赴晉陽。
entries.en: The meritorious generals held that continuing the military enterprise was weighty and urged Gao Yang to go quickly to Jinyang.
entries.literal: The meritorious generals held that continuing the military enterprise was weighty and urged the emperor to go quickly to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 帝亦回遑不能自決，夜中召楊愔、杜弼、崔季舒及德政等，始定策焉。
entries.en: Gao Yang also hesitated and could not decide; in the night he summoned Yang Yin, Du Bi, Cui Jishu, Dezheng, and others, and only then settled the plan.
entries.literal: The emperor also hesitated and could not decide; in the night he summoned Yang Yin, Du Bi, Cui Jishu, and Dezheng and others, and only then settled the plan.

entries.zh: 以楊愔居守。
entries.en: Yang Yin was left to hold the capital.
entries.literal: Yang Yin was left to hold the capital.

entries.zh: 尋遷太常卿。
entries.en: Soon he was moved to grand minister of ceremonial.
entries.literal: Soon he was moved to grand minister of ceremonial.

entries.zh: 帝謂羣臣曰：「崔太常清正，天下無雙，卿等不及。」
entries.en: Gao Yang said to the assembled ministers, "Grand Minister of Ceremonial Cui is pure and upright, without peer under heaven—you do not equal him."
entries.literal: The emperor said to the assembled ministers: "Grand Minister of Ceremonial Cui is pure and upright, without peer under heaven—you do not equal him."

entries.zh: 初，世宗欲以妹嫁暹子，而會世宗崩，遂寢。
entries.en: Earlier, Gao Cheng had wished to marry his sister to Xian's son, but when Gao Cheng died the matter was dropped.
entries.literal: Earlier, Gao Cheng had wished to marry his sister to Xian's son, but when Gao Cheng died the matter was dropped.

entries.zh: 至是，羣臣宴於宣光殿，貴戚之子多在焉。
entries.en: At this time the ministers feasted in Xuanguang Hall; many sons of noble kin were there.
entries.literal: At this time the ministers feasted in Xuanguang Hall; many sons of noble kin were there.

entries.zh: 顯祖歷與之語，於坐上親作書與暹曰：「賢子達拏，甚有才學。
entries.en: Gao Yang went round speaking with them; at the seat he personally wrote to Xian, "Your worthy son Dana is very talented in learning.
entries.literal: Gao Yang went round speaking with them; at the seat he personally wrote to Xian: "Your worthy son Dana is very talented in learning.

entries.zh: 亡兄女樂安主，魏帝外甥，內外敬待，勝朕諸妹，思成大兄宿志。」
entries.en: My late elder brother's daughter, Princess Le'an, the Wei emperor's niece, honored inside and outside, surpasses my sisters—I think to fulfill my elder brother's longstanding wish."
entries.literal: My late elder brother's daughter, Princess Le'an, the Wei emperor's niece, honored inside and outside, surpasses my sisters—I think to fulfill my elder brother's longstanding wish."

entries.zh: 乃以主降達拏。
entries.en: He then gave the princess to Dana in marriage.
entries.literal: He then gave the princess to Dana in marriage.

entries.zh: 天保末，為右僕射。
entries.en: At the end of Tianbao he was right vice director.
entries.literal: At the end of Tianbao he was right vice director.

entries.zh: 帝謂左右曰：「崔暹諫我飲酒過多，然我飲何所妨？」
entries.en: Gao Yang said to those about him, "Cui Xian admonishes me for drinking too much—but what harm is my drinking?"
entries.literal: The emperor said to those about him: "Cui Xian admonishes me for drinking too much—but what harm is my drinking?"

entries.zh: 常山王私謂暹曰：「至尊或多醉，太后尚不能致言，吾兄弟杜口，僕射獨能犯顏，內外深相感愧。」
entries.en: Prince of Changshan said privately to Xian, "The Supreme One may often be drunk; the empress dowager cannot yet speak up; we brothers hold our tongues—only you, vice director, dare to offend his countenance; inside and outside we are deeply moved and ashamed."
entries.literal: Prince of Changshan said privately to Xian: "The Supreme One may often be drunk; the empress dowager cannot yet speak up; we brothers hold our tongues—only you, vice director, dare to offend his countenance; inside and outside we are deeply moved and ashamed."

entries.zh: 十年，暹以疾卒，帝撫靈而哭。
entries.en: In the tenth year Xian died of illness; Gao Yang stroked the bier and wept.
entries.literal: In the tenth year Xian died of illness; the emperor stroked the bier and wept.

entries.zh: 贈開府。
entries.en: He was posthumously enfeoffed as grand marshalate.
entries.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as grand marshalate.

entries.zh: 世宗欲假暹威勢，諸公在坐，令暹高視徐步，兩人掣裾而入，世宗分庭對揖。
entries.en: Gao Cheng wished to lend Xian imposing bearing; with the lords seated, he had Xian walk in with head high and slow steps, two men tugging his robes to lead him in; Gao Cheng faced him across the hall and bowed with equal ceremony.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng wished to lend Xian imposing bearing; with the lords seated, he had Xian walk in with head high and slow steps, two men tugging his robes to lead him in; Gao Cheng faced him across the hall and bowed with equal ceremony.

entries.zh: 暹不讓席而坐，觴再行，便辭退。
entries.en: Xian would not yield the seat but sat down; after two rounds of wine he took his leave.
entries.literal: Xian would not yield the seat but sat down; after two rounds of wine he took his leave.

entries.zh: 世宗曰：「下官薄有蔬食，願公少留。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng said, "This humble officer has a modest vegetarian meal; I hope you will stay a little."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng said: "This humble officer has a modest vegetarian meal; I hope you will stay a little."

entries.zh: 暹曰：「適受勑在臺檢校。」
entries.en: Xian said, "I have just received orders to inspect at the bureau."
entries.literal: Xian said: "I have just received orders to inspect at the bureau."

entries.zh: 遂不待食而去，世宗降階送之。
entries.en: Without waiting for the meal he left; Gao Cheng descended the steps to see him off.
entries.literal: Without waiting for the meal he left; Gao Cheng descended the steps to see him off.

entries.zh: 旬日後，世宗與諸公出之東山，遇暹於道，前驅為赤棒所擊，世宗回馬避之。
entries.en: Ten days later, Gao Cheng went out to the eastern hills with the lords and met Xian on the road; the outriders were struck with red staffs and Gao Cheng turned his horse aside to avoid him.
entries.literal: Ten days later, Gao Cheng went out to the eastern hills with the lords and met Xian on the road; the outriders were struck with red staffs and Gao Cheng turned his horse aside to avoid him.

entries.zh: 崔昂，字懷遠，博陵安平人也。
entries.en: Cui Ang, styled Huaiyuan, was a man of Anping in Boling.
entries.literal: Cui Ang, styled Huaiyuan, was a man of Anping in Boling.

entries.zh: 祖挺，魏幽州刺史。
entries.en: His grandfather Ting was Wei inspector of You province.
entries.literal: His grandfather Ting was Wei inspector of You province.

entries.zh: 昂年七歲而孤，伯父吏部尚書孝芬嘗謂所親曰：「此兒終當遠至，是吾家千里駒也。」
entries.en: Ang was orphaned at seven; his father's elder brother, minister of personnel Xiaofen, once told those close to him, "This boy will go far in the end — he is our family's thousand-li colt."
entries.literal: Ang was orphaned at seven; his father's elder brother, Minister of Personnel Xiaofen, once told those close to him: "This boy will in the end go far — he is our family's thousand-li colt."

entries.zh: 昂性端直少華，沈深有志略，堅實難傾動。
entries.en: Ang was upright and sparing of show, deep and steady in design — firm and hard to move.
entries.literal: Ang's nature was upright with little ornament, deep and steady with design and stratagem — firm and hard to shake.

entries.zh: 少好章句，頗綜文詞。
entries.en: In youth he loved exegetical study and was fairly versed in literary phrasing.
entries.literal: In youth he loved exegetical study and was fairly versed in literary phrasing.

entries.zh: 世宗廣開幕府，引為記室參軍，委以腹心之任。
entries.en: Gao Cheng broadly opened his headquarters and brought him in as Recorder and Staff Officer, entrusting him with confidential duties.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng broadly opened his headquarters and brought him in as Recorder and Staff Officer, entrusting him with confidential duties.

entries.zh: 世宗入輔朝政，召為開府長史。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng entered to assist at court, he was summoned as chief clerk of the opening office.
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng entered to assist court governance, he was summoned as chief clerk of the opening office.

entries.zh: 時勳將親族兵客在都下放縱，多行不軌，孫騰、司馬子如之門尤劇。
entries.en: At the time the meritorious generals' kin and military retainers in the capital ran wild, many acting outside the law — the households of Sun Teng and Sima Ziru were worst.
entries.literal: At the time the meritorious generals' kin and military retainers in the capital ran wild, many acting outside the law — the households of Sun Teng and Sima Ziru were worst.

entries.zh: 昂受世宗密旨，以法繩之，未幾之間，內外齊肅。
entries.en: Ang received Gao Cheng's secret order and bound them with law; within no long time inner and outer were alike disciplined.
entries.literal: Ang received Gao Cheng's secret order and bound them with law; within no long time inner and outer were alike disciplined.

entries.zh: 遷尚書左丞，其年，又兼度支尚書。
entries.en: He was moved to left assistant in the Masters of Writing; that same year he also held minister of revenue concurrently.
entries.literal: He was moved to left assistant in the Masters of Writing; that same year he also held concurrently minister of revenue.

entries.zh: 左丞之兼尚書，近代未有，唯昂獨為冠首，朝野榮之。
entries.en: An assistant concurrently holding a ministry had not occurred in recent times — Ang alone was first; court and country honored him.
entries.literal: An assistant concurrently holding a ministry post had not occurred in recent times — Ang alone was first; court and country honored him.

entries.zh: 八日，楊愔書中旨，以魏襄城王旭並司空公潘相樂、侍中張亮、黃門趙彥深入通奏事。
entries.en: On the eighth day Yang Yin wrote the central order, sending Wei Prince of Xiangcheng Xu with grand master of ceremonies Pan Xiangyue, palace attendant Zhang Liang, and yellow gate Zhao Yanshen to report at court.
entries.literal: On the eighth day Yang Yin wrote the central order, sending Wei Prince of Xiangcheng Wang Xu together with Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan Xiangyue, Palace Attendant Zhang Liang, and Yellow Gate Zhao Yanshen to communicate matters at court.

entries.zh: 魏孝靜在昭陽殿引見。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaojing of Wei received them in the Zhaoyang Hall.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaojing of Wei received them at the Zhaoyang Hall.

entries.zh: 旭云：「五行遞運，有始有終，齊王聖德欽明，萬方歸仰，臣等昧死聞奏，願陛下則堯禪舜。」
entries.en: Xu said, "The Five Agents turn in succession — all things have beginning and end. The Prince of Qi's sacred virtue is bright; the ten thousand regions look to him. We risk death to report: we pray Your Majesty will follow Yao in yielding to Shun."
entries.literal: Xu said: "The Five Agents move in succession — there is beginning and end. The Prince of Qi's sacred virtue is revered and bright; the ten thousand regions turn to him in homage. We, your servants, risk death to report: we pray Your Majesty will follow Yao in yielding to Shun."

entries.zh: 魏帝便斂容曰：「此事推挹已久，謹當遜避。」
entries.en: The Wei emperor composed himself and said, "This has long been pressed upon me — I shall respectfully yield."
entries.literal: The Wei emperor drew himself up and said: "This matter has long been pressed upon me — I shall respectfully yield and withdraw."

entries.zh: 又道：「若爾，須作詔。」
entries.en: He added, "If so, an edict must be made."
entries.literal: He added: "If so, an edict must be drafted."

entries.zh: 中書侍郎崔劼奏云：「詔已作訖。」
entries.en: Secretariat gentleman Cui Jie reported, "The edict is already done."
entries.literal: Secretariat Gentleman Cui Jie reported: "The edict is already finished."

entries.zh: 卽付楊愔進於魏靜帝。
entries.en: It was at once given to Yang Yin to present to Emperor Jing of Wei.
entries.literal: It was at once handed to Yang Yin to present to Emperor Jing of Wei.

entries.zh: 凡有十餘條，悉書。
entries.en: There were more than ten articles in all, each written out.
entries.literal: There were more than ten articles in all, all written out.

entries.zh: 魏靜云：「安置朕何所，復若為去？」
entries.en: Emperor Jing said, "Where will you lodge me — and how am I to leave?"
entries.literal: Emperor Jing said: "Where will you place me — and how am I to go?"

entries.zh: 楊愔對：「在北城別有館宇，還備法駕，依常仗衛而去。」
entries.en: Yang Yin replied, "In the northern city there is a separate lodge; the imperial equipage will be prepared, and you will go with the usual guards and escort."
entries.literal: Yang Yin replied: "In the northern city there is a separate lodge; the imperial equipage will be made ready, and you will go with the usual guards and escort."

entries.zh: 魏靜帝於是下御坐，就東廊，口詠範蔚宗《後漢書贊》云：「獻生不辰，身播國屯，終我四百，永作虞賓。」
entries.en: Emperor Jing of Wei stepped down from the throne, went to the eastern gallery, and recited Fan Ye's encomium from the History of Later Han: "Xian was born untimely, his person cast upon the state's ordeal — ending our four hundred years, forever guest of Yu."
entries.literal: Emperor Jing of Wei thereupon stepped down from the imperial seat, went to the eastern gallery, and intoned Fan Ye's encomium from the History of Later Han: "The Emperor Xian was born untimely, his person cast upon the state's ordeal — ending our four hundred years, forever to be guest of Yu."

entries.zh: 所司尋奏請發。
entries.en: The responsible office soon memorialized asking that he depart.
entries.literal: The responsible office soon memorialized requesting departure.

entries.zh: 魏靜帝曰：「人念遺簪弊屨，欲與六宮別，可乎？」
entries.en: Emperor Jing said, "Men cherish even a lost hairpin or worn shoes — may I bid farewell to the six palaces?"
entries.literal: Emperor Jing said: "Men recall even a lost hairpin or worn-out shoes — may I take leave of the six palaces?"

entries.zh: 乃入與夫人嬪御以下訣別，莫不歔欷掩涕。
entries.en: He went in to take leave of the ladies, consorts, attendants, and those below — none without weeping and covering their faces.
entries.literal: He then went in to bid farewell to the ladies, consorts, attendants, and those below — none without sobbing and covering their tears.

entries.zh: 嬪趙國李氏口誦陳思王詩云：「王其愛玉體，俱享黃髮期。」
entries.en: Lady Li of Zhao recited Prince Si of Chen's lines: "My lord, cherish your jade body — may we together reach the years of yellow hair."
entries.literal: Lady Li of Zhao recited Prince Si of Chen's poem: "My lord, cherish your jade body — may we together enjoy the years of yellow hair."

entries.zh: 魏靜帝登車出萬春門，直長趙道德在車中陪侍，百官在門外拜辭。
entries.en: Emperor Jing mounted his carriage and went out the Wanchun Gate; chief controller Zhao Daode attended him in the carriage; the hundred officials bowed farewell outside the gate.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing mounted his carriage and went out through the Wanchun Gate; chief controller Zhao Daode attended him in the carriage; the hundred officials bowed farewell outside the gate.

entries.zh: 遂入北城下司馬子如南宅。
entries.en: He entered the northern city and lodged at Sima Ziru's southern residence.
entries.literal: He then entered the northern city and lodged at Sima Ziru's southern residence.

entries.zh: 武定六年，甘露降於宮闕，文武官僚同賀顯陽殿。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Wuding, sweet dew fell on the palace gates; civil and military officials together offered congratulations at the Xianyang Hall.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Wuding, sweet dew fell upon the palace gates; civil and military officials together offered congratulations at the Xianyang Hall.

entries.zh: 魏帝問僕射崔暹、尚書楊愔等曰：「自古甘露之瑞，漢、魏多少，可各言往代所降之處，德化感致所由。」
entries.en: The Wei emperor asked vice director Cui Xian, minister Yang Yin, and others, "Since antiquity the auspice of sweet dew — in Han and Wei, how often? Tell where it fell in past ages and by what moral transformation it was drawn down."
entries.literal: The Wei emperor asked Vice Director Cui Xuan, Minister Yang Yin, and others: "Since antiquity the auspice of sweet dew — in Han and Wei, how many times? You may each tell where it fell in past ages and by what moral transformation it was drawn down."

entries.zh: 次問昂，昂曰：「案《符瑞圖》，王者德致於天，則甘露降。
entries.en: Ang was asked next; Ang said, "According to the Charts of Omens, when a king's virtue reaches Heaven, sweet dew descends.
entries.literal: Ang was asked next; Ang said: "According to the Charts of Omens, when a king's virtue reaches Heaven, sweet dew descends.

entries.zh: 吉凶兩門，不由符瑞，故桑雉為戒，實啟中興，小鳥孕大，未聞福感。
