entries.en: Good fortune and ill are two gates — they do not turn on omens. The mulberry cock was a warning yet truly opened restoration; a small bird bearing a great thing — I have not heard that called a blessing drawn down.
entries.literal: Good fortune and ill are two gates — they do not depend on omens. Thus the mulberry cock was a warning yet truly opened restoration; a small bird bearing a great thing — I have not heard that called a blessing drawn down.

entries.zh: 所願陛下雖休勿休。」
entries.en: What I wish is that Your Majesty, though blessed with auspicious signs, not rest on them."
entries.literal: What I wish is that Your Majesty, though at rest, never cease to rest."

entries.zh: 帝為斂容曰：「朕旣無德，何以當此。」
entries.en: The emperor composed himself and said, "I have no virtue — how could I deserve this?"
entries.literal: The emperor drew himself up and said: "I have no virtue — how could I deserve this?"

entries.zh: 帝至城南頓所。
entries.en: Gao Yang reached the halt south of the city.
entries.literal: The emperor reached the halt at the south of the city.

entries.zh: 受禪之日，除德政為侍中，尋封藍田公。
entries.en: On the day the mandate was received, Dezheng was made palace attendant; soon after he was enfeoffed as duke of Lantian.
entries.literal: On the day the mandate was received, Dezheng was appointed palace attendant; soon after he was enfeoffed as Duke of Lantian.

entries.zh: 七年，遷尚書右僕射，兼侍中，食渤海郡幹。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was moved to right vice director of the Masters of Writing, concurrently palace attendant, with income from Bohai commandery.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to right vice director of the Masters of Writing, concurrently palace attendant, with a territorial income from Bohai commandery.

entries.zh: 德政與尚書令楊愔綱紀政事，多有弘益。
entries.en: Dezheng and Director Yang Yin set the order of government; they brought much that profited the realm.
entries.literal: Dezheng with Director Yang Yin regulated state affairs; they brought many broad benefits.

entries.zh: 自出身從官，常日晏乃歸。
entries.en: From his first entry into office he normally returned only at day's end.
entries.literal: From his first entry into office he normally returned only at day's end.

entries.zh: 侵曉則與兄弟問母之起居，暮則嘗食視寢，然後至外齋對親賓。
entries.en: At dawn he and his brothers would ask after their mother's health; at evening he would taste food and look in on her sleep, then go to the outer study to face kin and guests.
entries.literal: At dawn he and his brothers would ask after their mother's health; at evening he would taste food and look in on her sleep, then go to the outer study to face kin and guests.

entries.zh: 一生不問家事。
entries.en: In a lifetime he did not inquire into household affairs.
entries.literal: In a lifetime he did not inquire into household affairs.

entries.zh: 魏、梁通和，要貴皆遣人隨聘使交易，暹惟寄求佛經。
entries.en: When Wei and Liang made peace, the great and favored all sent men with the envoys to trade; Xian only asked that Buddhist sutras be sent.
entries.literal: When Wei and Liang made peace, the great and favored all sent men with the envoys to trade; Xian only asked that Buddhist sutras be sent.

entries.zh: 梁武帝聞之，為繕寫，以幡花寶蓋贊唄送至館焉。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Liang heard of it, had them copied, and sent them to the lodge with streamers, flowers, precious canopies, hymns, and chants.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang heard of it, had them copied, and sent them to the lodge with streamers, flowers, precious canopies, hymns, and chants.

entries.zh: 然而好大言，調戲無節。
entries.en: Yet he loved grand talk and joking without restraint.
entries.literal: Yet he loved grand talk and joking without restraint.

entries.zh: 密令沙門明藏著《佛性論》而署己名，傳諸江表。
entries.en: He secretly had the monk Mingzang compose the Treatise on Buddha-nature and affix his own name, transmitting it throughout the Jiang region.
entries.literal: He secretly had the monk Mingzang compose the Treatise on Buddha-nature and affix his own name, transmitting it throughout the Jiang region.

entries.zh: 子達拏年十三，暹命儒者權會教其說《周易》兩字，乃集朝貴名流，令達拏升高座開講。
entries.en: His son Dana was thirteen; Xian had a Confucian named Quan Hui teach him to speak two words on the Book of Changes, then gathered court nobles and famous men and had Dana ascend the high seat to open a lecture.
entries.literal: His son Dana was thirteen; Xian had a Confucian named Quan Hui teach him to speak two words on the Book of Changes, then gathered court nobles and famous men and had Dana ascend the high seat to open a lecture.

entries.zh: 趙郡睦仲讓陽屈服之，暹喜，擢為司徒中郎。
entries.en: Mu Zhongrang of Zhao commandery was made to yield on the spot; Xian was pleased and promoted him to gentleman of the secretariat.
entries.literal: Mu Zhongrang of Zhao commandery was made to yield on the spot; Xian was pleased and promoted him to gentleman of the secretariat.

entries.zh: 鄴下為之語曰：「講義兩行得中郎。」
entries.en: Ye had a saying, "Two lines of lecture win a gentleman of the secretariat."
entries.literal: Ye had a saying: "Two lines of lecture win a gentleman of the secretariat."

entries.zh: 此皆暹之短也。
entries.en: These were all Xian's failings.
entries.literal: These were all Xian's failings.

entries.zh: 崔暹 高德政 崔昂
entries.en: Cui Xian; Gao Dezheng; Cui Ang
entries.literal: Cui Xian; Gao Dezheng; Cui Ang

entries.zh: 累遷東萊太守。
entries.en: He rose in succession to administrator of Donglai.
entries.literal: He rose in succession to Administrator of Donglai.

entries.zh: 後吏部尚書李神儁奏言，比因多故，常侍遂無員限，今以王元景等為常侍，定限八員。
entries.en: Later Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun memorialized that because of many disturbances the attendant-at-court posts had long had no fixed quota; now Wang Yuanjing and others were made attendants, fixed at eight.
entries.literal: Later Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun memorialized saying that because of many disturbances the attendant-at-court posts had long had no fixed quota; now Wang Yuanjing and others were made attendants, fixed at eight.

entries.zh: 加金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: He was given the additional title grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon.
entries.literal: He was given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 武帝或時袒露，與近臣戲狎，每見昕，即正冠而斂容焉。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Wei sometimes went bare-chested and sported familiarly with close ministers; whenever he saw Xin, he would straighten his cap and compose his bearing.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei sometimes went bare-chested and sported familiarly with close ministers; whenever he saw Xin, he would straighten his cap and compose his bearing.

entries.zh: 昕體素甚肥，遭喪後，遂終身羸瘠。
entries.en: Xin's body had always been very stout; after mourning he remained gaunt for life.
entries.literal: Xin's body had always been very stout; after mourning he remained gaunt for life.

entries.zh: 楊愔重其德業，以為人之師表。
entries.en: Yang Yin valued his virtue and learning and took him as a model for men.
entries.literal: Yang Yin valued his virtue and learning and took him as a model for men.

entries.zh: 遷秘書監。
entries.en: He was moved to director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: He was moved to Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 昕雅好清言，詞無淺俗。
entries.en: Xin was fond of pure talk; his words had nothing shallow or vulgar.
entries.literal: Xin was fond of pure talk; his words had nothing shallow or vulgar.

entries.zh: 在東萊，獲殺其同行侶者，詰之未服，昕謂之曰：「彼物故不歸，卿無恙而反，何以自明？」
entries.en: In Donglai he caught one who had killed a traveling companion; questioned, the man would not confess; Xin said to him, "That man died and did not return; you came back unharmed—how will you clear yourself?"
entries.literal: In Donglai he caught one who had killed a traveling companion; questioned, the man would not confess; Xin said to him: "That man died and did not return; you came back unharmed—how will you clear yourself?"

entries.zh: 邢卲後見世宗，說此言以為笑樂。
entries.en: Later Xing Shao saw Gao Cheng and told this remark for a laugh.
entries.literal: Later Xing Shao saw Gao Cheng and told this remark for a laugh.

entries.zh: 昕聞之，故詣卲曰：「卿不識造化。」
entries.en: When Xin heard of it, he went deliberately to Shao and said, "You do not understand creation."
entries.literal: When Xin heard of it, he went deliberately to Shao and said: "You do not understand creation."

entries.zh: 還謂人曰：「子才應死，我罵之極深。」
entries.en: Returning, he told others, "Zicai ought to die; I cursed him to the utmost."
entries.literal: Returning, he told others: "Zicai ought to die; I cursed him to the utmost."

entries.zh: 齊神武訪朝廷子弟忠孝謹密者，令與諸子遊。
entries.en: Gao Huan sought sons of the court who were loyal, filial, careful, and steady, to keep company with his sons.
entries.literal: Gao Huan sought sons of the court who were loyal, filial, careful, and steady, to keep company with his sons.

entries.zh: 晞與清河崔瞻、頓丘李度、范陽盧正通首應此選。
entries.en: Xi and Cui Zhan of Qinghe, Li Du of Dunqiu, and Lu Zhengtong of Fanyang were the first chosen for this.
entries.literal: Xi and Cui Zhan of Qinghe, Li Du of Dunqiu, and Lu Zhengtong of Fanyang were the first chosen for this.

entries.zh: 文襄時為大將軍，握晞等手曰：「我弟並向成長，志識未定，近善狎惡，不能不移。
entries.en: Gao Cheng was then grand general; he took Xi and the others by the hand and said, "My younger brothers are all growing up; their aims and knowledge are not yet fixed—near goodness they draw close, near evil they inevitably shift.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng was then grand general; he took Xi and the others by the hand and said: "My younger brothers are all growing up; their aims and knowledge are not yet fixed—near goodness they draw close, near evil they cannot but shift.

entries.zh: 吾弟成立，不負義方，卿祿位常亞吾弟。
entries.en: If my younger brothers are established, they will not betray righteous teaching; your rank and salary will always rank just below my younger brothers.
entries.literal: If my younger brothers are established, they will not betray righteous teaching; your rank and salary will always rank just below my younger brothers.

entries.zh: 若茍使迴邪，致相詿誤，罪及門族，非止一身。」
entries.en: If you would make them turn crooked and lead one another astray, guilt will reach the clan—not you alone."
entries.literal: If you would make them turn crooked and lead one another astray, guilt will reach the clan—not you alone."

entries.zh: 晞隨神武到晉陽，補中外府功曹參軍，帶常山王演友。
entries.en: Xi followed Gao Huan to Jinyang, was made staff officer of the inner and outer offices, and attended Prince of Changshan Yan as companion.
entries.literal: Xi followed Gao Huan to Jinyang, was made staff officer of the inner and outer offices, and attended Prince of Changshan Yan as companion.

entries.zh: 齊天保初，行太原郡事。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianbao in Qi he acted as administrator of Taiyuan commandery.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao in Qi he acted as administrator of Taiyuan commandery.

entries.zh: 及文宣昏逸，常山王數諫，帝疑王假辭於晞，欲加大辟。
entries.en: When Gao Yang grew dissolute, Prince of Changshan remonstrated repeatedly; Gao Yang suspected the prince borrowed his words from Xi and wished to impose the death penalty.
entries.literal: When Gao Yang grew dissolute, Prince of Changshan remonstrated repeatedly; the emperor suspected the prince borrowed his words from Xi and wished to impose the death penalty.

entries.zh: 王私謂晞曰：「博士，明日當作一條事，為欲相活，亦圖自全，宜深體勿怪。」
entries.en: The prince said privately to Xi, "Doctor, tomorrow you must do one thing—for I mean to keep you alive and also to save myself; understand deeply and do not take it amiss."
entries.literal: The prince said privately to Xi: "Doctor, tomorrow you must do one thing—for I mean to keep you alive and also to save myself; understand deeply and do not take it amiss."

entries.zh: 乃於衆中杖晞二十。
entries.en: He then had Xi beaten twenty strokes before the assembly.
entries.literal: He then had Xi beaten twenty strokes before the assembly.

entries.zh: 帝尋發怒，聞晞得杖，以故不殺，髡鉗配甲坊。
entries.en: Gao Yang soon flared in anger; hearing Xi had been beaten, on that account he did not kill him but shaved his head, put him in fetters, and assigned him to the armorer's ward.
entries.literal: The emperor soon flared in anger; hearing Xi had been beaten, on that account he did not kill him but shaved his head, put him in fetters, and assigned him to the armorer's ward.

entries.zh: 居三年，王又固諫爭，大被毆撻，閉口不食。
entries.en: After three years the prince again remonstrated firmly; he was beaten severely, closed his mouth and would not eat.
entries.literal: After three years the prince again remonstrated firmly; he was beaten severely, closed his mouth and would not eat.

entries.zh: 太后極憂之。
entries.en: The empress dowager was deeply grieved.
entries.literal: The empress dowager was deeply grieved.

entries.zh: 帝謂左右曰：「儻小兒死，奈我老母何？」
entries.en: Gao Yang said to those about him, "If the boy dies, what of my old mother?"
entries.literal: The emperor said to those about him: "If the boy dies, what of my old mother?"

entries.zh: 於是每問王疾，謂曰：「努力強食，當以王晞還汝。」
entries.en: He then each day inquired after the prince's illness and told him, "Strive and force yourself to eat; I will give Wang Xi back to you."
entries.literal: He then each day inquired after the prince's illness and told him: "Strive and force yourself to eat; I will give Wang Xi back to you."

entries.zh: 乃釋晞令往。
entries.en: He released Xi and sent him to the prince.
entries.literal: He released Xi and sent him to the prince.

entries.zh: 王抱晞曰：「吾氣力綴然，恐不復相見。」
entries.en: The prince embraced Xi and said, "My breath and strength are failing; I fear we shall not meet again."
entries.literal: The prince embraced Xi and said: "My breath and strength are failing; I fear we shall not meet again."

entries.zh: 晞流涕曰：「天道神明，豈令殿下遂斃此舍。
entries.en: Xi wept and said, "Heaven's way and the spirits—how could they let Your Highness die in this house!
entries.literal: Xi wept and said: "Heaven's way and the spirits—how could they let Your Highness die in this house!

entries.zh: 至尊親為人兄，尊為人主，安可與校計。
entries.en: The Supreme One is elder brother in person and sovereign in rank—how can you contend with him?
entries.literal: The Supreme One is elder brother in person and sovereign in rank—how can you contend with him?

entries.zh: 殿下不食，太后亦不食，殿下縱不自惜，不惜太后乎？」
entries.en: Your Highness will not eat; the empress dowager will not eat either—if Your Highness will not spare yourself, will you not spare the empress dowager?"
entries.literal: Your Highness will not eat; the empress dowager will not eat either—if Your Highness will not spare yourself, will you not spare the empress dowager?"

entries.zh: 言未卒，王強坐而飯。
entries.en: Before he finished speaking, the prince forced himself to sit up and eat.
entries.literal: Before he finished speaking, the prince forced himself to sit up and eat.

entries.zh: 晞由是得免徙，還為王友。
entries.en: Xi was thereby spared exile and returned as the prince's companion.
entries.literal: Xi was thereby spared exile and returned as the prince's companion.

entries.zh: 顯祖以昕疏誕，非濟世所須，罵之曰：「好門戶，惡人身。」
entries.en: Gao Yang, because Xin was loose and insolent and not what the age required, reviled him, "Fine house, vile person."
entries.literal: Gao Yang, because Xin was loose and insolent and not what the age required, reviled him: "Fine house, vile person."

entries.zh: 又有讒之者曰：「王元景每嗟水運不應遂絕。」
entries.en: There were also slanderers who said, "Wang Yuanjing often sighs that the water transport ought not to have been cut off."
entries.literal: There were also slanderers who said: "Wang Yuanjing often sighs that the water transport ought not to have been cut off."

entries.zh: 帝愈怒，乃下詔徙幽州。
entries.en: Gao Yang grew angrier still and issued an edict exiling him to Youzhou.
entries.literal: The emperor grew angrier still and issued an edict exiling him to Youzhou.

entries.zh: 後徵還，除銀青光祿大夫，判祠部尚書事。
entries.en: Later he was recalled and made grand master of splendid happiness with silver seal and purple ribbon, with concurrent charge of the ministry of rites.
entries.literal: Later he was recalled and made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Purple Ribbon, with concurrent charge of the ministry of rites.

entries.zh: 帝怒臨漳令嵇曄及舍人李文師，以曄賜薛豐洛、文師賜崔士順為奴。
entries.en: Gao Yang in anger toward Linzhang magistrate Ji Ye and palace attendant Li Wenshi gave Ye as slave to Xue Fengluo and Wenshi as slave to Cui Shishun.
entries.literal: The emperor in anger toward Linzhang magistrate Ji Ye and palace attendant Li Wenshi gave Ye as slave to Xue Fengluo and Wenshi as slave to Cui Shishun.

entries.zh: 鄭子默私謂昕曰：「自古無朝士作奴。」
entries.en: Zheng Zimo said privately to Xin, "From antiquity there have been no court gentlemen made slaves."
entries.literal: Zheng Zimo said privately to Xin: "From antiquity there have been no court gentlemen made slaves."

entries.zh: 昕曰：「箕子為之奴，何言無也？」
entries.en: Xin said, "Jizi became a slave—how say there were none?"
entries.literal: Xin said: "Jizi became a slave—how say there were none?"

entries.zh: 子默遂以昕言啟顯祖，仍曰：「王元景比陛下於殷紂。」
entries.en: Zimo then reported Xin's words to Gao Yang, adding, "Wang Yuanjing compares Your Majesty to King Zhou of Shang."
entries.literal: Zimo then reported Xin's words to Gao Yang, adding: "Wang Yuanjing compares Your Majesty to King Zhou of Shang."

entries.zh: 楊愔微為解之。
entries.en: Yang Yin mildly excused him.
entries.literal: Yang Yin mildly excused him.

entries.zh: 帝謂愔曰：「王元景是爾博士，爾語皆元景所教。」
entries.en: Gao Yang said to Yin, "Wang Yuanjing is your doctoral mentor; your every word is what Yuanjing taught."
entries.literal: The emperor said to Yin: "Wang Yuanjing is your doctoral mentor; your every word is what Yuanjing taught."

entries.zh: 帝後與朝臣酣飲，昕稱病不至。
entries.en: Later Gao Yang drank deep with the court ministers; Xin pleaded illness and did not attend.
entries.literal: Later the emperor drank deep with the court ministers; Xin pleaded illness and did not attend.

entries.zh: 帝遣騎執之，見方搖膝吟詠，遂斬於御前，投尸漳水，天保十年也。
entries.en: Gao Yang sent riders to seize him; they found him swaying his knees and chanting poetry; he was beheaded before the throne, the corpse cast into the Zhang River—in the tenth year of Tianbao.
entries.literal: The emperor sent riders to seize him; they found him swaying his knees and chanting poetry; he was beheaded before the throne, the corpse cast into the Zhang River—in the tenth year of Tianbao.

entries.zh: 有文集二十卷。
entries.en: He left collected works in twenty scrolls.
entries.literal: He left a collection of writings in twenty scrolls.

entries.zh: 子顗。
entries.en: His son Yan.
entries.literal: His son Yan.

entries.zh: 帝欲以晞為侍中，苦辭不受。
entries.en: The emperor wished to make Wang Xi palace attendant; he firmly declined and would not accept.
entries.literal: The emperor wished to make Xi palace attendant; he firmly declined and would not accept.

entries.zh: 或勸晞勿自疏，晞曰：「我少年以來，閱要人多矣，充詘少時，鮮不敗績。
entries.en: Some urged Wang Xi not to distance himself; Wang Xi said, "From youth I have seen many men in power; puffed up for a little while, few did not end in ruin.
entries.literal: Some urged Xi not to distance himself; Xi said: "From youth I have seen many men in power; puffed up for a little while, few did not end in ruin.

entries.zh: 且性實疏緩，不堪時務，人主恩私，何由可保，萬一披猖，求退無地。
entries.en: Moreover my nature is truly loose and slow, unfit for the times; a sovereign's private favor — how can it be kept? If by chance I lose restraint, there is nowhere to seek withdrawal.
entries.literal: Moreover my nature is truly loose and slow, unfit for the times; a sovereign's private favor — how can it be kept? If by chance I lose restraint, there is nowhere to seek withdrawal.

entries.zh: 非不愛作熱官，但思之爛熟耳。」
entries.en: It is not that I do not love the hot office — I have only chewed it over to the end."
entries.literal: It is not that I do not love the hot office — I have only chewed it over to the end."

entries.zh: 百官嘗賜射，晞中的，當得絹，為不書箭，有司不與。
entries.en: Once the hundred officials were granted an archery contest; Wang Xi hit the target and should have received silk, but because he did not mark his arrow, the office would not give it.
entries.literal: Once the hundred officials were granted an archery contest; Xi hit the target and should have received silk, but because he did not mark his arrow, the office would not give it.

entries.zh: 晞陶陶然曰：「我今可謂武有餘文不足矣。」
entries.en: Wang Xi said with easy content, "Today I may be called abundant in martial, short in literary."
entries.literal: Xi said with easy content: "Today I may be called abundant in martial, short in literary."

entries.zh: 晞無子，帝將賜之妾，使小黃門就宅宣旨，皇後相聞晞妻。
entries.en: Wang Xi had no son; the emperor would grant him a concubine; a yellow gate attendant went to his house to announce the edict; the empress also sent word to Wang Xi's wife.
entries.literal: Xi had no son; the emperor would grant him a concubine; a yellow gate attendant went to his house to announce the edict; the empress also sent word to Xi's wife.

entries.zh: 晞令妻答，妻終不言，晞以手拊胸而退。
entries.en: Wang Xi had his wife answer; the wife never spoke; Wang Xi patted his chest with his hand and withdrew.
entries.literal: Xi had his wife answer; the wife never spoke; Xi patted his chest with his hand and withdrew.

entries.zh: 帝聞之笑。
entries.en: When the emperor heard it he laughed.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard it he laughed.

entries.zh: 孝昭崩，哀慕殆不自勝，因以羸敗。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, he mourned almost beyond bearing and fell ill from weakness.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, he mourned almost beyond bearing and fell ill from weakness.

entries.zh: 武成本忿其儒緩，由是彌嫌之，因奏事大被訶叱，而雅步晏然。
entries.en: Emperor Wucheng had long resented his scholarly slowness and therefore disliked him the more; on presenting business he was roundly scolded, yet walked with elegant pace, unruffled.
entries.literal: Emperor Wucheng had long resented his scholarly slowness and therefore disliked him the more; on presenting business he was roundly scolded, yet walked with elegant pace, unruffled.

entries.zh: 歷東徐州刺史、秘書監。
entries.en: He passed through posts as governor of eastern Xuzhou and director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: He passed through posts as governor of eastern Xuzhou and director of the secretariat.

entries.zh: 武平初，遷大鴻臚，加儀同三司，監修起居注，待詔文林館。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wuping he was moved to grand director of ceremonies, given the same ceremonial rank as the three masters, supervised revision of the veritable records, and attended at the Forest of Literary Brilliance.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wuping he was moved to grand director of ceremonies, given the same ceremonial rank as the three masters, supervised revision of the veritable records, and attended at the Forest of Literary Brilliance.

entries.zh: 齊亡，周武以晞為儀同大將軍、太子諫議大夫。
entries.en: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou made Xi Equal-in-Honor Grand General and grand remonstrant of the crown prince.
entries.literal: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou made Xi Equal-in-Honor Grand General and Grand Remonstrant of the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 隋開皇元年，卒於洛陽，年七十一。
entries.en: In the first year of Kaihuang under Sui, he died at Luoyang at the age of seventy-one.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang under Sui, he died at Luoyang at the age of seventy-one.

entries.zh: 贈儀同三司、曹州刺史。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted Equal in Honors to the Three Excellencies and inspector of Caozhou.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted Equal in Honors to the Three Excellencies and inspector of Caozhou.

entries.zh: 王昕 弟晞
entries.en: Wang Xin; Wang Xi
entries.literal: Wang Xin; younger brother Xi

entries.zh: 及侯景始告降於梁，法和謂南郡朱元英曰：「貧道共檀越擊侯景去。」
entries.en: When Hou Jing first announced surrender to Liang, Fahe said to Zhu Yuanying of Nan commandery, "This humble monk together with my patron shall drive Hou Jing away."
entries.literal: When Hou Jing first announced surrender to Liang, Fahe said to Zhu Yuanying of Nan commandery: "This humble monk together with my patron shall drive Hou Jing away."

entries.zh: 元英曰：「侯景為國立效，師云擊之，何也？」
entries.en: Yuanying said, "Hou Jing is rendering service to the state; Master, you say strike him—why?"
entries.literal: Yuanying said: "Hou Jing is rendering service to the state; Master, you say strike him—why?"

entries.zh: 法和曰：「正自如此。」
entries.en: Fahe said, "It is precisely for that reason."
entries.literal: Fahe said: "It is precisely for that reason."

entries.zh: 及景渡江，法和時在青谿山，元英往問曰：「景今圍城，其事云何？」
entries.en: When Jing crossed the Yangtze, Fahe was then on Mount Qingxi; Yuanying went to ask, "Jing now besieges the capital—how stands the matter?"
entries.literal: When Jing crossed the Yangtze, Fahe was then on Mount Qingxi; Yuanying went to ask: "Jing now besieges the capital—how stands the matter?"

entries.zh: 法和曰：「凡人取果，宜待熟時，不撩自落。
entries.en: Fahe said, "When mere men take fruit, they should wait until it is ripe; without plucking, it falls of itself.
entries.literal: Fahe said: "When mere men take fruit, they should wait until it is ripe; without plucking, it falls of itself.

entries.zh: 檀越但待侯景熟，何勞問也。」
entries.en: My patron need only wait until Hou Jing ripens—why trouble to ask?"
entries.literal: My patron need only wait until Hou Jing ripens—why trouble to ask?"

entries.zh: 固問之，乃曰：「亦克亦不克。」
entries.en: Pressed repeatedly, he at last said, "He may be taken, and he may not."
entries.literal: Pressed repeatedly, he at last said: "He may be taken, and he may not."

entries.zh: 景遣將任約擊梁湘東王於江陵，法和乃詣湘東乞征約，召諸蠻弟子八百人在江津，二日便發。
entries.en: Jing sent his general Ren Yue to strike the Prince of Xiangdong at Jiangling; Fahe then went to the Prince of Xiangdong begging to campaign against Yue, mustered eight hundred barbarian disciples at the river crossing, and set out within two days.
entries.literal: Jing sent his general Ren Yue to strike the Prince of Xiangdong at Jiangling; Fahe then went to the Prince of Xiangdong begging to campaign against Yue, mustered eight hundred barbarian disciples at the river crossing, and set out within two days.

entries.zh: 湘東遣胡僧佑領千餘人與同行。
entries.en: The Prince of Xiangdong sent Hu Sengyou leading more than a thousand men to march with him.
entries.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong sent Hu Sengyou leading more than a thousand men to march with him.

entries.zh: 法和登艦大笑曰：「無量兵馬。」
entries.en: Fahe boarded the ship and laughed aloud, "Measureless troops and horses."
entries.literal: Fahe boarded the ship and laughed aloud: "Measureless troops and horses."

entries.zh: 江陵多神祠，人俗恒所祈禱，自法和軍出，無復一騐，人以為神皆從行故也。
entries.en: Jiangling had many spirit shrines; the custom was constant prayer, but from the day Fahe's army marched out not one prayer was answered—the people thought the spirits had all gone with the army.
entries.literal: Jiangling had many spirit shrines; the custom was constant prayer, but from the day Fahe's army marched out not one prayer was answered—the people thought the spirits had all gone with the army.

entries.zh: 至赤沙湖，與約相對，法和乘輕船，不介胄，沿流而下，去約軍一里乃還。
entries.en: At Chisha Lake they faced Yue; Fahe took a light boat, wore no armor, drifted downstream, and turned back a li from Yue's army.
entries.literal: At Chisha Lake they faced Yue; Fahe took a light boat, wore no armor, drifted downstream, and turned back a li from Yue's army.

entries.zh: 謂將士曰：「聊觀彼龍睡不動，吾軍之龍甚自踴躍，卽攻之。
entries.en: He told the officers and men, "I have only come to see whether their dragon lies asleep; our army's dragon is leaping on its own—attack at once.
entries.literal: He told the officers and men: "I have only come to see whether their dragon lies asleep; our army's dragon is leaping on its own—attack at once.

entries.zh: 若得待明日，當不損客主一人而破賊，然有惡處。」
entries.en: If we could wait until tomorrow, we might break the bandits without losing a man on either side, but there would be an ill turn."
entries.literal: If we could wait until tomorrow, we might break the bandits without losing a man on either side, but there would be an ill turn."

entries.zh: 遂縱火舫於前，而逆風不便，法和執白羽麾風，風勢卽返。
entries.en: They then sent fire-ships ahead, but the headwind was unfavorable; Fahe waved a white feather to command the wind, and the wind at once reversed.
entries.literal: They then sent fire-ships ahead, but the headwind was unfavorable; Fahe waved a white feather to command the wind, and the wind at once reversed.

entries.zh: 約衆皆見梁兵步於水上，於是大潰，皆投水而死。
entries.en: Yue's host all saw Liang infantry walking on the water; at that they broke utterly and threw themselves into the river to die.
entries.literal: Yue's host all saw Liang infantry walking on the water; at that they broke utterly and threw themselves into the river to die.

entries.zh: 約逃竄不知所之。
entries.en: Yue fled and was lost to sight.
entries.literal: Yue fled and was lost to sight.

entries.zh: 法和曰：「明日午時當得。」
entries.en: Fahe said, "At noon tomorrow he will be taken."
entries.literal: Fahe said: "At noon tomorrow he will be taken."

entries.zh: 及期而未得，人問之，法和曰：「吾前於此洲水幹時建一剎，語檀越等，此雖為剎，實是賊標，今何不向標下求賊也？」
entries.en: When the hour came and he was not taken, men asked him; Fahe said, "I earlier built a shrine on this islet when the water was dry and told you patrons that though it is a shrine, in truth it is a bandit-marker—why not seek the bandit beneath the marker now?"
entries.literal: When the hour came and he was not taken, men asked him; Fahe said: "I earlier built a shrine on this islet when the water was dry and told you patrons that though it is a shrine, in truth it is a bandit-marker—why not seek the bandit beneath the marker now?"

entries.zh: 如其言，果於水中見約抱剎仰頭，裁出鼻，遂擒之。
entries.en: As he said, they indeed saw Yue in the water clinging to the shrine with head thrown back, only his nose above the surface; they seized him.
entries.literal: As he said, they indeed saw Yue in the water clinging to the shrine with head thrown back, only his nose above the surface; they seized him.

entries.zh: 約言求就師目前死，法和曰：「檀越有相，必不兵死，且於王有緣，決無他慮，王於後當得檀越力耳。」
entries.en: Yue begged to die before the Master's eyes; Fahe said, "My patron has the look of fortune—he will surely not die by the sword; moreover he has karmic tie with the prince—set your mind at rest. The prince hereafter will gain my patron's strength."
entries.literal: Yue begged to die before the Master's eyes; Fahe said: "My patron has the look of fortune—he will surely not die by the sword; moreover he has karmic tie with the prince—set your mind at rest. The prince hereafter will gain my patron's strength."

entries.zh: 湘東果釋用為郡守。
entries.en: The Prince of Xiangdong indeed released him and employed him as commandery administrator.
entries.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong indeed released him and employed him as commandery administrator.

entries.zh: 及魏圍江陵，約以兵赴救，力戰焉。
entries.en: When Wei besieged Jiangling, Yue came with troops to the rescue and fought fiercely.
entries.literal: When Wei besieged Jiangling, Yue came with troops to the rescue and fought fiercely.

entries.zh: 法和旣平約，往進見王僧辯於巴陵，謂曰：「貧道已斷侯景一臂，其更何能為，檀越宜卽遂取。」
entries.en: After Fahe had pacified Yue, he went forward to see Wang Sengbian at Baling and said, "This humble monk has already cut off one arm of Hou Jing—what more can he do? My patron should press the attack at once."
entries.literal: After Fahe had pacified Yue, he went forward to see Wang Sengbian at Baling and said: "This humble monk has already cut off one arm of Hou Jing—what more can he do? My patron should press the attack at once."

entries.zh: 乃請還，謂湘東王曰：「侯景自然平矣，無足可慮。
entries.en: He then asked leave to return and told the Prince of Xiangdong, "Hou Jing will naturally be pacified—nothing to worry over.
entries.literal: He then asked leave to return and told the Prince of Xiangdong: "Hou Jing will naturally be pacified—nothing to worry over.

entries.zh: 蜀賊將至，法和請守巫峽待之。」
entries.en: Shu bandits are about to arrive; Fahe asks to hold Wuxia Gorge and await them."
entries.literal: Shu bandits are about to arrive; Fahe asks to hold Wuxia Gorge and await them."

entries.zh: 乃總諸軍而往，親運石以填江。
entries.en: He then gathered all armies and went, himself hauling stone to fill the river.
entries.literal: He then gathered all armies and went, himself hauling stone to fill the river.

entries.zh: 三日，水遂分流，橫之以鐵鎖。
entries.en: In three days the water split into channels; he spanned them with iron chains.
entries.literal: In three days the water split into channels; he spanned them with iron chains.

entries.zh: 武陵王紀果遣蜀兵來渡，峽口勢蹙，進退不可。
entries.en: The Prince of Wuling Ji indeed sent Shu troops to cross; the gorge mouth was cramped and they could neither advance nor retreat.
entries.literal: The Prince of Wuling Ji indeed sent Shu troops to cross; the gorge mouth was cramped and they could neither advance nor retreat.

entries.zh: 王琳與法和經略，一戰而殄之。
entries.en: Wang Lin and Fahe laid plans together; one battle and they were annihilated.
entries.literal: Wang Lin and Fahe laid plans together; one battle and they were annihilated.

entries.zh: 太清二年，侯景渡江，遣琳獻米萬石。
entries.en: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi; Lin was sent to present ten thousand piculs of grain.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi; Lin was sent to present ten thousand piculs of grain.

entries.zh: 未至，都城陷，乃中江沉米，輕舸還荊州。
entries.en: Before he arrived the capital fell. He sank the grain mid-river and returned by light boat to Jingzhou.
entries.literal: Before he arrived the capital fell; he sank the grain mid-river and returned by light boat to Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 稍遷岳陽內史，以軍功封建寧縣侯。
entries.en: He was gradually promoted to administrator of Yueyang and, for military merit, enfeoffed Marquis of Jianning.
entries.literal: He was gradually promoted to Administrator of Yueyang and, for military merit, enfeoffed Marquis of Jianning.

entries.zh: 侯景遣將宋子仙據郢州，琳攻剋之，擒子仙。
entries.en: Hou Jing sent General Song Zixian to hold Yingzhou; Lin attacked and took it, capturing Zixian.
entries.literal: Hou Jing sent General Song Zixian to hold Yingzhou; Lin attacked and took it, capturing Zixian.

entries.zh: 又隨王僧辯破景。
entries.en: He also followed Wang Sengbian in defeating Hou Jing.
entries.literal: He also followed Wang Sengbian in defeating Jing.

entries.zh: 後拜湘州刺史。
entries.en: Later he was made governor of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: Later he was made Governor of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 琳果勁絕人，又能傾身下士，所得賞物，不以入家。
entries.en: Lin was fierce beyond ordinary men, yet could humble himself before his troops; whatever rewards he received he did not bring home.
entries.literal: Lin was fierce and surpassing among men, yet could humble himself before soldiers; rewards he received he did not bring home.

entries.zh: 麾下萬人，多是江淮羣盜。
entries.en: Under his command were ten thousand men, mostly bandits of the Jiang and Huai.
entries.literal: Under his command were ten thousand men, mostly river-and-Huai bandits.

entries.zh: 平景之勛，與杜龕俱為第一，恃寵縱暴於建業。
entries.en: In merit for pacifying Jing he ranked first with Du Kan; relying on favor he ran riot in Jiankang.
entries.literal: In merit for pacifying Jing he ranked first with Du Kan; relying on favor he ran riot in Jiankang.

entries.zh: 王僧辯禁之不可，懼將為亂，啟請誅之。
entries.en: Wang Sengbian forbade it but could not; fearing Lin would stir rebellion, he memorialized asking that he be executed.
entries.literal: Wang Sengbian forbade it but could not; fearing he would stir rebellion, he memorialized asking execution.

entries.zh: 琳亦疑禍，令長史陸納率部曲前赴湘州，身徑上江陵。
entries.en: Lin also suspected disaster. He ordered chief clerk Lu Na to lead his troops ahead to Xiangzhou while he himself went straight up to Jiangling.
entries.literal: Lin also suspected disaster; he ordered Chief Clerk Lu Na to lead his troops ahead to Xiangzhou while he himself went straight up to Jiangling.

entries.zh: 將行，謂納等曰：「吾若不返，子將安之？」
entries.en: About to depart, he said to Na and the rest, "If I do not return, where will you go?"
entries.literal: About to depart, he said to Na and the rest: "If I do not return, where will you go?"

entries.zh: 咸曰：「請死相報。」
entries.en: All said, "We ask only to die in your service."
entries.literal: All said: "We ask only to die in your service."

entries.zh: 泣而別。
entries.en: They wept and parted.
entries.literal: They wept and parted.

entries.zh: 及至，帝以下吏，而廷尉卿黃羅漢、太府卿張載宣喻琳軍。
entries.en: When he arrived, the emperor had him sent down to the law; but Chamberlain for Law Enforcement Huang Luohan and minister of the grand treasury Zhang Zai went to announce the decree to Lin's army.
entries.literal: When he arrived, the emperor had him sent down to the law; but Chamberlain for Law Enforcement Huang Luohan and Minister of the Grand Treasury Zhang Zai went to announce the decree to Lin's army.

entries.zh: 陸納等及軍人並哭對使者，莫肯受命，乃報黃羅漢，殺張載。
entries.en: Lu Na and the soldiers all wept facing the envoys and would not accept orders; they reported to Huang Luohan and killed Zhang Zai.
entries.literal: Lu Na and the soldiers all wept facing the envoys and would not accept orders; they reported to Huang Luohan and killed Zhang Zai.

entries.zh: 載性深刻，為帝所信，荊州疾之如仇，故納等因人之欲，抽腸系馬腳，使繞而走，腸盡氣絕，又臠割備五刑而斬之。
entries.en: Zai was harsh by nature and trusted by the emperor; Jingzhou hated him like an enemy. So Na and the rest, playing on men's desires, drew out his entrails and tied them to a horse's leg, making the horse run until the guts were gone and breath ended; then they carved him piecemeal through the five punishments and beheaded him.
entries.literal: Zai was harsh by nature, trusted by the emperor; Jingzhou hated him like an enemy — so Na and the rest, playing on men's desires, drew out his entrails and tied them to a horse's leg, making the horse run until the guts were gone and breath ended; then they carved him piecemeal through the five punishments and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 梁元遣王僧辯討納，納等敗走長沙。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan of Liang sent Wang Sengbian to attack Na; Na and the rest were defeated and fled to Changsha.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang sent Wang Sengbian to attack Na; Na and the rest were defeated and fled to Changsha.

entries.zh: 是時湘州未平，武陵王兵又甚盛，江陵公私恐懼，人有異圖。
entries.en: At that time Xiangzhou was not yet pacified, and the Prince of Wuling's troops were very strong; public and private in Jiangling were afraid, and men harbored other schemes.
entries.literal: At that time Xiangzhou was not yet pacified, and the Prince of Wuling's troops were very strong; public and private in Jiangling were afraid, and men harbored other schemes.

entries.zh: 納啟申琳罪，請復本位，永為奴婢。
entries.en: Na memorialized stating Lin's crimes, asking that he be restored to his original post and offering that they would be slaves forever.
entries.literal: Na memorialized stating Lin's crimes, asking restoration to his original post, willing to be slaves forever.

entries.zh: 梁元乃鎖琳送長沙。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan then shackled Lin and sent him to Changsha.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan then shackled Lin and sent him to Changsha.

entries.zh: 時納兵出方戰，會琳至，僧辯升諸樓車以示之。
entries.en: At the time Na's troops were out fighting; when Lin arrived, Sengbian mounted the tower chariots to show him.
entries.literal: At the time Na's troops were out fighting; when Lin arrived, Sengbian mounted the tower chariots to show him.

entries.zh: 納等投戈俱拜，舉軍皆哭，曰：「乞王郎入城，卽出。」
entries.en: Na and the rest cast down their weapons and bowed together; the whole army wept and said, "We beg Young Master Wang enter the city — we will come out at once."
entries.literal: Na and the rest cast down their weapons and bowed together; the whole army wept and said: "We beg Young Master Wang enter the city — we will come out at once."

entries.zh: 及放琳入，納等乃降，湘州平。
entries.en: When Lin was released and entered, Na and the rest then surrendered, and Xiangzhou was pacified.
entries.literal: When Lin was released and entered, Na and the rest then surrendered, and Xiangzhou was pacified.

entries.zh: 仍復本位，使琳拒蕭紀。
entries.en: Lin was restored to his post and ordered to resist Xiao Ji.
entries.literal: Lin was restored to his post and ordered to resist Xiao Ji.

entries.zh: 紀平，授衡州刺史。
entries.en: When Ji was pacified, Lin was made governor of Hengzhou.
entries.literal: When Ji was pacified, Lin was made Governor of Hengzhou.

entries.zh: 陳霸先旣殺王僧辯，推立敬帝，以侍中司空徵。
entries.en: Chen Baxian had killed Wang Sengbian and raised Emperor Jing, summoning Lin as attendant and minister of works.
entries.literal: Chen Baxian had killed Wang Sengbian and raised Emperor Jing, summoning Lin as attendant and minister of works.

entries.zh: 琳不從命，乃大營樓艦，將圖義舉。
entries.en: Lin did not obey; he greatly built tower-ships, intending a righteous rising.
entries.literal: Lin did not obey; he greatly built tower-ships, intending a righteous rising.

entries.zh: 琳將帥各乘一艦，每行，戰艦以千數，以「野豬」為名。
entries.en: Lin's commanders each rode one vessel; whenever he moved, battle ships numbered in thousands, named "Wild Boar."
entries.literal: Lin's commanders each rode one vessel; whenever he moved, battle ships numbered in thousands, named "Wild Boar."

entries.zh: 陳武帝遣將侯安都、周文育等誅琳，仍受梁禪。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Chen sent generals Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyu to execute Lin, then accepted Liang's abdication.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Chen sent Generals Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyu to execute Lin, then accepted Liang's abdication.

entries.zh: 安都嘆曰：「我其敗乎，師無名矣。」
entries.en: Andu sighed, "Shall I be defeated? The army has no righteous name."
entries.literal: Andu sighed: "Shall I be defeated? The army has no righteous name."

entries.zh: 逆戰於沌口，琳乘平肩輿，執鉞而麾之，禽安都、文育，其餘無所漏。
entries.en: They fought upstream at Zhunkou. Lin rode a level-shouldered litter, grasped an axe and directed them, capturing Andu and Wenyu; of the rest none escaped.
entries.literal: They fought upstream at Zhunkou; Lin rode a level-shouldered litter, grasped an axe and directed them, capturing Andu and Wenyu; of the rest none escaped.

entries.zh: 唯以周鐵虎一人背恩，斬之。
entries.en: Only Zhou Tiehu alone betrayed kindness — him he beheaded.
entries.literal: Only Zhou Tiehu alone betrayed kindness — him he beheaded.

entries.zh: 鎖安都、文育置琳所坐艦中，令一閹豎監守之。
entries.en: He shackled Andu and Wenyu aboard the vessel where Lin sat and set a eunuch to guard them.
entries.literal: He shackled Andu and Wenyu aboard the vessel where Lin sat and set a eunuch to guard them.

entries.zh: 琳乃移湘州軍府就郢城，帶甲十萬，練兵於白水浦。
entries.en: Lin then moved the Xiangzhou military headquarters to Yingcheng, with armor on a hundred thousand, drilling troops at Baisuipu.
entries.literal: Lin then moved the Xiangzhou military headquarters to Yingcheng, with armor on a hundred thousand, drilling troops at Baisuipu.

entries.zh: 琳巡軍而言曰：「可以為勤王之師矣，溫太真何人哉！」
entries.en: Lin inspected the army and said, "This can be an army to relieve the ruler — who was Wen Taizhen!"
entries.literal: Lin inspected the army and said: "This can be an army to relieve the ruler — who was Wen Taizhen!"

entries.zh: 江南渠帥熊曇朗、周迪懷貳，琳遣李孝欽、樊猛與余孝頃同討之。
entries.en: The channel lords of Jiangnan, Xiong Tanlang and Zhou Di, wavered in loyalty; Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang together to attack them.
entries.literal: The channel lords of Jiangnan, Xiong Tanlang and Zhou Di, wavered in loyalty; Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang together to attack them.

entries.zh: 三將軍敗，並為敵所囚。
entries.en: All three generals were defeated and taken prisoner by the enemy.
entries.literal: All three generals were defeated and taken prisoner by the enemy.

entries.zh: 安都、文育等盡逃還建業。
entries.en: Andu, Wenyu, and the rest all escaped back to Jiankang.
entries.literal: Andu, Wenyu, and the rest all escaped back to Jiankang.

entries.zh: 初，魏剋江陵之時，永嘉王莊年甫七歲，逃匿人家，後琳迎還湘中，衛送東下。
entries.en: Earlier, when Wei took Jiangling, Prince Zhuang of Yongjia was only seven; he hid in a household; later Lin welcomed him back to Xiang and escorted him east.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Wei took Jiangling, Prince Zhuang of Yongjia was only seven; he hid in a household; later Lin welcomed him back to Xiang and escorted him east.

entries.zh: 及敬帝立，出質於齊，請納莊為梁主。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing was enthroned, Zhuang was sent as hostage to Qi, asking that Zhuang be received as ruler of Liang.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing was enthroned, Zhuang was sent as hostage to Qi, asking that Zhuang be received as ruler of Liang.

entries.zh: 文宣遣兵援送，仍遣兼中書令李騊駼冊拜琳為梁丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。
entries.en: Wenxuan sent troops to escort him and also dispatched concurrent secretariat supervisor Li Taotu to invest Lin as Liang chancellor, commander of all armies within and without, and recorder of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: Wenxuan sent troops to escort him and also dispatched Concurrent Secretariat Supervisor Li Taotu to invest Lin as Liang Chancellor, Commander of All Armies Within and Without, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 舍人羊愨、遊詮之等齎璽書江表宣勞，自琳以下皆有頒賜。
entries.en: Attendant Yang Que and You Quanzhi and others carried imperial writs to proclaim favors in the Jiang region; from Lin downward all received gifts.
entries.literal: Attendant Yang Que and You Quanzhi and others carried imperial writs to proclaim favors in the Jiang region; from Lin downward all received gifts.

entries.zh: 琳乃遣兄子叔寶率所部十州刺史子弟赴鄴，奉莊纂梁祚於郢州。
entries.en: Lin sent his nephew Shubao to lead sons of the ten provincial governors' families to Ye, to install Zhuang in Liang's mandate at Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Lin sent his nephew Shubao to lead sons of the ten provincial governors' families to Ye, to install Zhuang in Liang's mandate at Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 莊授琳侍中、使持節、大將軍、中書監，改封安城郡公，其餘並依齊朝前命。
entries.en: Zhuang made Lin attendant, bearer of credentials, grand general, and director of the secretariat, changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Ancheng, and the rest followed Qi's earlier orders.
entries.literal: Zhuang made Lin attendant, bearer of credentials, grand general, and director of the secretariat, changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Ancheng, and the rest followed Qi's earlier orders.

entries.zh: 及陳霸先卽位，琳乃輔莊次於濡須口。
entries.en: When Chen Baxian took the throne, Lin then supported Zhuang encamped at Ruxukou.
entries.literal: When Chen Baxian took the throne, Lin then supported Zhuang encamped at Ruxukou.

entries.zh: 齊遣揚州道行臺慕容儼率衆臨江，為其聲援。
entries.en: Qi sent acting governor of the Yangzhou route Murong Yan with troops to the river as his rear support.
entries.literal: Qi sent Acting Governor of Yangzhou Route Murong Yan with troops to the river as his rear support.

entries.zh: 陳遣安州刺史吳明徹江中夜上，將襲湓城。
entries.en: Chen sent Wu Mingche, inspector of Anzhou, up the Yangzi by night, intending a surprise on Pencheng.
entries.literal: Chen sent Wu Mingche, inspector of Anzhou, up the Yangzi by night, intending a surprise on Pencheng.

entries.zh: 琳遣巴陵太守任忠大敗之，明徹僅以身免。
entries.en: Lin sent Ren Zhong, administrator of Baling, who inflicted a great defeat; Mingche barely escaped with his life.
entries.literal: Lin sent Ren Zhong, Administrator of Baling, who inflicted a great defeat; Mingche barely escaped with his life.

entries.zh: 琳十七子。
entries.en: Lin had seventeen sons.
entries.literal: Lin had seventeen sons.

entries.zh: 長子敬，在齊襲王爵，武平末，通直常侍。
entries.en: The eldest, Jing, inherited the princedom in Qi; at the end of Wuping he was regular attendant of the palace gate.
entries.literal: The eldest son Jing inherited the princely title in Qi; at the end of Wuping he was Regular Attendant of the Palace Gate.

entries.zh: 第九子衍，隋開皇中開府儀同三司，大業初，卒於渝州刺史。
entries.en: The ninth son, Yan, under Sui Kaihuang held opening office, equal in insignia with three departments; early in Daye he died as inspector of Yuzhou.
entries.literal: The ninth son Yan, in Sui's Kaihuang era was Opening Office, Equal in Insignia with Three Departments; at the start of Daye he died as Inspector of Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 陸法和 王琳
entries.en: Lu Fahe; Wang Lin
entries.literal: Lu Fahe; Wang Lin

entries.zh: 蕭明，蘭陵人，梁武帝長兄長沙王懿之子。
entries.en: Xiao Ming was from Lanling, son of Prince of Changsha Yi, eldest brother of Emperor Wu of Liang.
entries.literal: Xiao Ming was a man of Lanling, son of Prince of Changsha Yi, the Liang emperor Wu's eldest brother's son.

entries.zh: 在其本朝，甚為梁武所親愛。
entries.en: In his own court he was greatly beloved by Emperor Wu of Liang.
entries.literal: In his own dynasty he was greatly beloved by Liang Wu.

entries.zh: 少歷顯職，封湞陽侯。
entries.en: In youth he held eminent posts and was enfeoffed Marquis of Zhenyang.
entries.literal: In youth he passed through eminent offices and was enfeoffed Marquis of Zhenyang.

entries.zh: 太清中，以為豫州刺史。
entries.en: During the Taiqing era he was made inspector of Yuzhou.
entries.literal: In the Taiqing era he was made inspector of Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 梁主旣納侯景，詔明率水陸諸軍趨彭城，大圖進取。
entries.en: After the Liang ruler accepted Hou Jing, an edict ordered Ming to lead land and river forces toward Pengcheng for a major advance.
entries.literal: After the Liang ruler had accepted Hou Jing, an edict ordered Ming to lead land and river forces toward Pengcheng, with a grand design of advance.

entries.zh: 又命兗州刺史南康嗣王會理總馭群帥，指授方略。
entries.en: He also ordered Yanzhou inspector Heir Prince of Nankang Hui Li to take overall command of the generals and set strategy.
entries.literal: He also ordered Yanzhou inspector Heir Prince of Nankang Hui Li to command all commanders and assign strategy.

entries.zh: 明渡淮未幾，官軍破之，盡俘其衆。
entries.en: Ming had crossed the Huai only a short while when the government army defeated him and took his entire force captive.
entries.literal: Ming had crossed the Huai only a short while when the government army defeated him and took all his host captive.

entries.zh: 魏帝升門樓，親引見明及諸將帥，釋其禁，送於晉陽。
entries.en: The Wei emperor ascended the gate tower, received Ming and the generals in person, released their bonds, and sent them to Jinyang.
entries.literal: The Wei emperor ascended the gate tower and personally received Ming and the generals, released their bonds, and sent them to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 世宗禮明甚重，謂之曰：「先王與梁主和好十有餘年，聞彼禮佛文，常雲奉為魏主，並及先王，此甚是梁主厚意。
entries.en: Gao Cheng treated Ming with great courtesy and said to him, "The late king and the Liang ruler were on good terms for more than ten years; I heard that when he performed Buddhist rites he would say he did them for the Wei ruler and for the late king as well—this was truly the Liang ruler's great kindness.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng treated Ming with great courtesy and said to him: "The late king and the Liang ruler were on good terms for more than ten years; I heard that when he performed Buddhist rites he would say he did them for the Wei ruler and for the late king as well—this was truly the Liang ruler's great kindness.

entries.zh: 不謂一朝失信，致此紛擾。
entries.en: Who would have thought that in a single morning faith would be broken and bring this turmoil.
entries.literal: Who would have thought that in a single morning faith would be broken and bring this turmoil.

entries.zh: 自出師薄伐，無戰不克，無城不陷，今自欲和，非是力屈。
entries.en: Since our armies went forth on a light campaign, there has been no battle we did not win, no city we did not take; now that we ourselves wish peace, it is not because our strength is spent.
entries.literal: Since our armies went forth on a light campaign, there has been no battle we did not win, no city we did not take; now that we ourselves wish peace, it is not because our strength is spent.

entries.zh: 境上之事，知非梁主本心，當是侯景違命扇動耳。
entries.en: Matters on the border—I know they are not the Liang ruler's true intent; surely Hou Jing defied orders and stirred this up.
entries.literal: Matters on the border—I know they are not the Liang ruler's true intent; surely Hou Jing defied orders and stirred this up.

entries.zh: 侯可遣使諮論，若猶存先王分義，重成通和者，吾不必違先王之旨，侯及諸人並卽放還。」
entries.en: You may send envoys to consult; if he still honors the late king's bond and restores friendly relations, I need not go against the late king's wish—you and the others will all be released at once."
entries.literal: You may send envoys to consult; if he still honors the late king's bond and restores friendly relations, I need not go against the late king's wish—you and the others will all be released at once."

entries.zh: 於是使人以明書告梁主，梁主乃致書以慰世宗。
entries.en: Thereupon he had men report to the Liang ruler with Ming's letter; the Liang ruler then sent a letter in reply to comfort Gao Cheng.
entries.literal: Thereupon he had men report to the Liang ruler with Ming's letter; the Liang ruler then sent a letter in reply to comfort Gao Cheng.

entries.zh: 及綜入魏，三軍散走，之才退至呂梁，橋斷路絕，遂為魏統軍石茂孫所止。
entries.en: When Zong entered Wei the three armies scattered and fled; Zhicai retreated to Lüliang; the bridge was cut and the road gone, and he was stopped by Wei commanding general Shi Maosun.
entries.literal: When Zong entered Wei the three armies scattered and fled; Zhicai retreated to Lüliang; the bridge was cut and the road gone, and he was stopped by Wei commanding general Shi Maosun.

entries.zh: 綜入魏旬月，位至司空。
entries.en: Within a month of Zong's entering Wei he reached the rank of minister of works.
entries.literal: Within a month of Zong's entering Wei he reached the rank of minister of works.

entries.zh: 魏聽綜收斂僚屬，乃訪之才在彭泗，啟魏帝云：「之才大善醫術，兼有機辯。」
entries.en: Wei allowed Zong to gather his staff; he then inquired after Zhicai at Peng and Si and reported to the Wei emperor, "Zhicai is greatly skilled in medicine and also has ready wit."
entries.literal: Wei allowed Zong to gather his staff; he then inquired after Zhicai at Peng and Si and reported to the Wei emperor: "Zhicai is greatly skilled in medicine and also has ready wit."

entries.zh: 詔徵之才。
entries.en: An edict summoned Zhicai.
entries.literal: An edict summoned Zhicai.

entries.zh: 孝昌二年，至洛，勑居南館，禮遇甚優。
entries.en: In the second year of Xiaochang he reached Luoyang; he was ordered to lodge in the Southern Lodge and received very generous treatment.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xiaochang he reached Luoyang; he was ordered to lodge in the Southern Lodge and received very generous treatment.

entries.zh: 從祖謇子踐啟求之才還宅。
entries.en: Cousin Zhan's son Jian memorialized asking that Zhicai return home.
entries.literal: Cousin Zhan's son Jian memorialized asking that Zhicai return home.

entries.zh: 之才藥石多效，又闚涉經史，發言辯捷，朝賢競相要引，為之延譽。
entries.en: Zhicai's medicines were often effective; he also dipped into the classics and histories; when he spoke he was sharp and quick; court worthies vied to invite him and spread his fame.
entries.literal: Zhicai's medicines were often effective; he also dipped into the classics and histories; when he spoke he was sharp and quick; court worthies vied to invite him and spread his fame.

entries.zh: 武帝時，封昌安縣侯。
entries.en: In the time of Emperor Wu he was enfeoffed Marquis of Chang'an county.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu he was enfeoffed Marquis of Chang'an county.

entries.zh: 天平中，齊神武徵赴晉陽，常在內館，禮遇稍厚。
entries.en: In the Tianping era Gao Huan summoned him to Jinyang; he was constantly in the inner lodge and his treatment grew somewhat richer.
entries.literal: In the Tianping era Gao Huan summoned him to Jinyang; he was constantly in the inner lodge and his treatment grew somewhat richer.

entries.zh: 武定四年，自散騎常侍轉秘書監。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Wuding he was transferred from attendant-in-ordinary to secretariat director.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Wuding he was transferred from attendant-in-ordinary to secretariat director.

entries.zh: 文宣作相，普加黜陟。
entries.en: When Gao Yang became chancellor he promoted and demoted widely.
entries.literal: When Gao Yang became chancellor he promoted and demoted widely.

entries.zh: 楊愔以其南土之人，不堪典秘書，轉授金紫光祿大夫，以魏收代領之。
entries.en: Yang Yin, because he was a man of the southern lands and unfit to direct the secretariat, transferred him to golden purple light grand master and had Wei Shou replace him in that office.
entries.literal: Yang Yin, because he was a man of the southern lands and unfit to direct the secretariat, transferred him to golden purple light grand master and had Wei Shou replace him in that office.

entries.zh: 之才甚怏怏不平。
entries.en: Zhicai was very resentful and displeased.
entries.literal: Zhicai was very resentful and displeased.

entries.zh: 蕭祗，字敬式，梁武弟南平王偉之子也。
entries.en: Xiao Zhi, style Jingshi, was son of Emperor Wu of Liang's younger brother Prince of Nanping Wei.
entries.literal: Xiao Zhi, style Jingshi, was son of Liang Wu's younger brother Prince of Nanping Wei.

entries.zh: 少聰敏，美容儀。
entries.en: In youth he was clever and keen, with fine looks.
entries.literal: In youth he was clever and keen, with fine looks.

entries.zh: 在梁封定襄侯，位東揚州刺史。
entries.en: In Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang and held the post of eastern Yangzhou inspector.
entries.literal: In Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang and held the post of eastern Yangzhou inspector.

entries.zh: 於時江左承平，政寬人慢，祗獨莅以嚴切，梁武悅之。
entries.en: At that time the lands east of the Yangtze were at peace; government was lax and people grew slack—Zhi alone governed with severity, and Emperor Wu of Liang was pleased.
entries.literal: At that time the lands east of the Yangtze were at peace; government was lax and people grew slack—Zhi alone governed with severity, and Liang Wu was pleased.

entries.zh: 遷北兗州刺史。
entries.en: He was transferred to northern Yanzhou inspector.
entries.literal: He was transferred to northern Yanzhou inspector.

entries.zh: 太清二年，侯景圍建鄴。
entries.en: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged Jiankang.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged Jiankang.

entries.zh: 祗聞臺城失守，遂來奔。
entries.en: Zhi heard the capital had fallen and came to surrender.
entries.literal: Zhi heard the capital had fallen and came to surrender.

entries.zh: 以武定七年至鄴，文襄令魏收、邢卲與相接對。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Wuding he reached Ye; Gao Cheng had Wei Shou and Xing Shao meet and converse with him.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Wuding he reached Ye; Gao Cheng had Wei Shou and Xing Shao meet and converse with him.

entries.zh: 歷位太子少傅，領平陽王師，封清河郡公。
entries.en: He passed through the posts of heir apparent junior tutor and tutor to Prince of Pingyang, and was enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe commandery.
entries.literal: He passed through the posts of heir apparent junior tutor and tutor to Prince of Pingyang, and was enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe commandery.

entries.zh: 齊天保初，授右光祿大夫，領國子祭酒。
entries.en: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao he was made right bright light grand master and director of the imperial university.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao he was made Right Bright Light Grand Master and director of the Imperial University.

entries.zh: 時梁元帝平侯景，復與齊通好，文宣欲放祗等還南。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan of Liang had pacified Hou Jing and renewed friendly relations with Qi, Gao Yang wished to release Zhi and the others to return south.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang had pacified Hou Jing and renewed friendly relations with Qi, Gao Yang wished to release Zhi and the others to return south.

entries.zh: 俄而西魏剋江陵，遂留鄴都，卒。
entries.en: Before long Western Wei took Jiangling; he therefore remained at Ye and died.
entries.literal: Before long Western Wei took Jiangling; he therefore remained at Ye and died.

entries.zh: 贈中書監、車騎大將軍、揚州刺史。
entries.en: Posthumous gifts: secretariat director, chariot and cavalry grand general, Yangzhou inspector.
entries.literal: Posthumous gifts: secretariat director, chariot and cavalry grand general, Yangzhou inspector.

entries.zh: 蕭退，梁武帝弟司空鄱陽王恢之子也。
entries.en: Xiao Tui was son of Emperor Wu of Liang's younger brother minister of works Prince of Poyang Hui.
entries.literal: Xiao Tui was son of Liang emperor Wu's younger brother Minister of Works Prince of Poyang Hui.

entries.zh: 退在梁封湘潭侯，位青州刺史。
entries.en: In Liang Tui was enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangtan and held Qingzhou inspector.
entries.literal: In Liang Tui was enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangtan and held Qingzhou inspector.

entries.zh: 建鄴陷，與從兄祗俱入東魏。
entries.en: When Jiankang fell, he entered Eastern Wei together with his elder cousin Zhi.
entries.literal: When Jiankang fell, he entered Eastern Wei together with his elder cousin Zhi.

entries.zh: 齊天保中，位金紫光祿大夫，卒。
entries.en: In Qi Tianbao he held the post of golden purple light grand master and died.
entries.literal: In Qi Tianbao he held the post of golden purple light grand master and died.

entries.zh: 子慨，深沉有禮，樂善好學，攻草隸書。
entries.en: His son Kai was deep and reserved, courteous, fond of goodness and eager to learn, and skilled at cursive and clerical script.
entries.literal: His son Kai was deep and reserved, courteous, fond of goodness and eager to learn, and skilled at cursive and clerical script.

entries.zh: 南士中稱為長者。
entries.en: Among southern gentlemen he was called an elder.
entries.literal: Among southern gentlemen he was called an elder.

entries.zh: 歷著作佐郎，待詔文林館，卒於司徒從事中郎。
entries.en: He passed through associate editor of the historiography office and attendant at Wenslin Hall, and died as aide to the director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: He passed through associate editor of the Historiography Office and attendant at Wenslin Hall, and died as aide to the director of the masters of writing.

entries.zh: 歷事諸帝，以戲狎得寵。
entries.en: Serving several emperors, he won favor through jesting familiarity.
entries.literal: Serving several emperors, he won favor through jesting familiarity.

entries.zh: 武成生齻牙，問諸醫。
entries.en: Emperor Wucheng had buck teeth and asked the physicians about them.
entries.literal: Emperor Wucheng had buck teeth; he asked the physicians.

entries.zh: 尚藥典御鄧宣文以實對，武成怒而撻之。
entries.en: Director of the imperial pharmacy Deng Xuanwen answered truthfully; Wucheng in anger had him flogged.
entries.literal: Director of the Imperial Pharmacy Deng Xuanwen answered truthfully; Wucheng in anger had him flogged.

entries.zh: 後以問之才，拜賀曰：「此是智牙，生智牙者聰明長壽。」
entries.en: Later he asked Zhicai, who bowed in congratulation and said, "These are wisdom teeth; one who grows wisdom teeth is clever and long-lived."
entries.literal: Later he asked Zhicai, who bowed in congratulation and said, "These are wisdom teeth; one who grows wisdom teeth is clever and long-lived."

entries.zh: 武成悅而賞之。
entries.en: Wucheng was pleased and rewarded him.
entries.literal: Wucheng was pleased and rewarded him.

entries.zh: 為僕射時，語人曰：「我在江東，見徐勉作僕射，朝士莫不佞之。
entries.en: When he was vice director he told people, "In the southeast I saw Xu Mian serve as vice director, and no court gentleman failed to flatter him.
entries.literal: When he was vice director he said to people, "In the southeast I saw Xu Mian serve as vice director, and no court gentleman failed to flatter him.

entries.zh: 今我亦是徐僕射，無一人佞我，何由可活！」
entries.en: Now I too am Vice Director Xu—yet not one person flatters me. How am I to live!"
entries.literal: Now I too am Vice Director Xu—yet not one person flatters me. How am I to live!"

entries.zh: 之才妻魏廣陽王妹，之才從文襄求得為妻。
entries.en: Zhicai's wife was a sister of the prince of Guangyang of Wei; Zhicai had obtained her as wife through Gao Cheng.
entries.literal: Zhicai's wife was a sister of the Prince of Guangyang of Wei; Zhicai had obtained her as wife through Gao Cheng.

entries.zh: 和士開知之，乃淫其妻。
entries.en: He Shikai learned of this and violated his wife.
entries.literal: He Shikai learned of this and violated his wife.

entries.zh: 之才遇見而避之，退曰：「妨少年戲笑。」
entries.en: Zhicai happened upon them and avoided them. He withdrew and said, "I am hindering the young man's sport."
entries.literal: Zhicai happened upon them and avoided them; he withdrew and said, "I am hindering the young man's sport."

entries.zh: 其寬縱如此。
entries.en: His indulgence ran to such lengths.
entries.literal: His indulgence was like this.

entries.zh: 年八十，卒。
entries.en: He died at the age of eighty.
entries.literal: He died at the age of eighty.

entries.zh: 贈司徒公、錄尚書事，諡曰文明。
entries.en: He was posthumously made duke of the state of Situ and recorder of affairs of the imperial secretariat, with the posthumous title Civil and Bright.
entries.literal: He was posthumously made Duke of the State of Situ and Recorder of Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, with the posthumous title Civil and Bright.

entries.zh: 天保六年，梁元為西魏所滅，顯祖詔立明為梁主，前所獲梁將湛海珍等皆聽從明歸，令上黨王渙率衆以送。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Tianbao, when Emperor Yuan of Liang was destroyed by Western Wei, Gao Yang issued an edict installing Ming as Liang ruler; Liang generals previously captured, such as Zhan Haizhen, were all allowed to follow Ming home, and Prince of Shangdang Huan was ordered to lead troops to escort them.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao, when Emperor Yuan of Liang was destroyed by Western Wei, Gao Yang issued an edict installing Ming as Liang ruler; Liang generals previously captured, such as Zhan Haizhen, were all allowed to follow Ming home, and Prince of Shangdang Huan was ordered to lead troops to escort them.

entries.zh: 是時梁太尉王僧辯、司空陳霸先在建鄴，推晉安王方智為丞相。
entries.en: At that time Liang grand commandant Wang Sengbian and minister of works Chen Baxian were at Jiankang; they installed Prince of Jin'an Fang Zhi as chancellor.
entries.literal: At that time Liang Grand Commandant Wang Sengbian and Minister of Works Chen Baxian were at Jiankang; they installed Prince of Jin'an Fang Zhi as chancellor.

entries.zh: 顯祖賜僧辯、霸先璽書，僧辯未奉詔。
entries.en: Gao Yang bestowed sealed letters on Sengbian and Baxian; Sengbian did not obey the edict.
entries.literal: Gao Yang bestowed sealed letters on Sengbian and Baxian; Sengbian did not obey the edict.

entries.zh: 上黨王進軍，明又與僧辯書，往復再三，陳禍福，僧辯初不納。
entries.en: Prince of Shangdang advanced his army; Ming also exchanged letters with Sengbian back and forth several times, setting out fortune and calamity, but at first Sengbian would not accept him.
entries.literal: Prince of Shangdang advanced his army; Ming also exchanged letters with Sengbian back and forth several times, setting out fortune and calamity, but at first Sengbian would not accept him.

entries.zh: 旣而上黨王破東關，斬裴之橫，江表危懼，僧辯乃啟上黨求納明，遣舟艦迎接。
entries.en: Then Prince of Shangdang broke Dongguan and beheaded Pei Zhiheng; the lands south of the Yangtze were gripped with fear, and Sengbian then memorialized Prince of Shangdang asking to admit Ming and sent warships to receive him.
entries.literal: Then Prince of Shangdang broke Dongguan and beheaded Pei Zhiheng; the lands south of the Yangtze were gripped with fear, and Sengbian then memorialized Prince of Shangdang asking to admit Ming and sent warships to receive him.

entries.zh: 王饗梁朝將士，及與明刑牲歃血，載書而盟。
entries.en: The prince feasted Liang officers and men and, with Ming, slaughtered a victim and drank the blood, loading the covenant onto a chariot.
entries.literal: The prince feasted Liang officers and men and, with Ming, slaughtered a victim and drank the blood, loading the covenant onto a chariot.

entries.zh: 於是梁輿東度，齊師北反。
entries.en: Thereupon the Liang carriage went east across the river and the Qi army turned north.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Liang carriage went east across the river and the Qi army turned north.

entries.zh: 侍中裴英起衛送明入建鄴，遂稱尊號，改承聖四年為天成元年，大赦天下，宇文黑獺、賊詧等不在赦例。
entries.en: Palace attendant Pei Yingqi guarded and escorted Ming into Jiankang; he then assumed the imperial title, changed the fourth year of Chengsheng to the first year of Tiancheng, and proclaimed a general amnesty—Yuwen Heitu, the rebel Cha, and the like were not within the amnesty.
entries.literal: Palace attendant Pei Yingqi guarded and escorted Ming into Jiankang; he then assumed the imperial title, changed the fourth year of Chengsheng to the first year of Tiancheng, and proclaimed a general amnesty—Yuwen Heitu, the rebel Chao, and the like were not within the amnesty.

entries.zh: 以方智為太子，授王僧辯大司馬。
entries.en: Fang Zhi was made heir apparent; Wang Sengbian was appointed grand marshal.
entries.literal: Fang Zhi was made heir apparent; Wang Sengbian was appointed grand marshal.

entries.zh: 明上表遣第二息章馳到京都，拜謝宮闕。
entries.en: Ming submitted a memorial sending his second son Zhang hurrying to the capital to bow in thanks before the palace.
entries.literal: Ming submitted a memorial sending his second son Zhang hurrying to the capital to bow in thanks before the palace.

entries.zh: 冬，霸先襲殺僧辯，復立方智，以明為太傅、建安王。
entries.en: In winter Baxian attacked and killed Sengbian, restored Fang Zhi, and made Ming grand tutor and Prince of Jian'an.
entries.literal: In winter Baxian attacked and killed Sengbian, restored Fang Zhi, and made Ming grand tutor and Prince of Jian'an.

entries.zh: 霸先奉表朝廷，云僧辯陰謀篡逆，故誅之。
entries.en: Baxian submitted a memorial to the court saying Sengbian had plotted treason in secret and was therefore executed.
entries.literal: Baxian submitted a memorial to the court saying Sengbian had plotted treason in secret and was therefore executed.

entries.zh: 方智請稱臣，永為藩國，齊遣行臺司馬恭及梁人盟於歷陽。
entries.en: Fang Zhi asked to style himself subject and remain a vassal state forever; Qi sent acting commissioner Sima Gong and Liang men to covenant at Liyang.
entries.literal: Fang Zhi asked to style himself subject and remain a vassal state forever; Qi sent acting commissioner Sima Gong and Liang men to covenant at Liyang.

entries.zh: 明年，詔徵明。
entries.en: The next year an edict summoned Ming.
entries.literal: The next year an edict summoned Ming.

entries.zh: 霸先猶稱藩，將遣使送明，會明疽發背死。
entries.en: Baxian still styled himself vassal and was about to send envoys to deliver Ming, but Ming died of a carbuncle on his back.
entries.literal: Baxian still styled himself vassal and was about to send envoys to deliver Ming, but Ming died of a carbuncle on his back.

entries.zh: 梁將王琳在江上與霸先相抗，顯祖遣兵納梁永嘉王蕭莊主梁祀。
entries.en: Liang general Wang Lin on the river resisted Baxian; Gao Yang sent troops to install Liang Prince of Yongjia Xiao Zhuang to uphold the Liang succession.
entries.literal: Liang general Wang Lin on the river resisted Baxian; Gao Yang sent troops to install Liang Prince of Yongjia Xiao Zhuang to uphold the Liang succession.

entries.zh: 九年二月，自湓城濟江，三月，卽帝位於郢州，年號天啟，王琳總其軍國，追諡明曰閔皇帝。
entries.en: In the second month of the ninth year he crossed the river from Pencheng; in the third month he took the throne at Yingzhou, era name Tianqi; Wang Lin directed state and army; posthumous title for Ming was Emperor Min.
entries.literal: In the second month of the ninth year he crossed the river from Pencheng; in the third month he took the throne at Yingzhou, era name Tianqi; Wang Lin directed state and army; posthumous title for Ming was Emperor Min.

entries.zh: 明年，莊為陳人所敗，遂入朝，封為侯。
entries.en: The next year Zhuang was defeated by Chen men and then entered court; he was enfeoffed marquis.
entries.literal: The next year Zhuang was defeated by Chen men and then entered court; he was enfeoffed marquis.

entries.zh: 朝廷許以興復，竟不果。
entries.en: The court had promised restoration, but in the end it did not come to pass.
entries.literal: The court had promised restoration, but in the end it did not come to pass.

entries.zh: 後主亡之日，莊在鄴飲氣而死。
entries.en: On the day the Last Lord perished, Zhuang died in Ye from pent-up grief.
entries.literal: On the day the Last Lord perished, Zhuang died in Ye from pent-up grief.

entries.zh: 徐之才，丹陽人也。
entries.en: Xu Zhicai was a man of Danyang.
entries.literal: Xu Zhicai was a man of Danyang.

entries.zh: 父雄，事南齊，位蘭陵太守，以醫術為江左所稱。
entries.en: His father Xiong served Southern Qi as administrator of Lanling and was famed in the lands east of the Yangtze for medical skill.
entries.literal: His father Xiong served Southern Qi as administrator of Lanling and was famed in the lands east of the Yangtze for medical skill.

entries.zh: 之才幼而儁發，五歲誦《孝經》，八歲略通義旨。
entries.en: Zhicai in childhood was precocious; at five he recited the Classic of Filial Piety, and at eight he had a rough grasp of its meaning.
entries.literal: Zhicai in childhood was precocious; at five he recited the Classic of Filial Piety, and at eight he had a rough grasp of its meaning.

entries.zh: 曾與從兄康造梁太子詹事汝南周舍宅聽《老子》。
entries.en: Once he went with his elder cousin Kang to the house of Liang heir apparent's household chief Runan Zhou She to hear the Laozi.
entries.literal: Once he went with his elder cousin Kang to the house of Liang heir apparent's household chief Runan Zhou She to hear the Laozi.

entries.zh: 捨為設食，乃戲之曰：「徐郎不用心思義，而但事食乎？」
entries.en: She set out food and then teased him, saying, "Master Xu, you do not apply your mind to meaning but only to eating?"
entries.literal: She set out food and then teased him, saying: "Master Xu, you do not apply your mind to meaning but only to eating?"

entries.zh: 之才答曰：「蓋聞聖人虛其心而實其腹。」
entries.en: Zhicai answered, "I have heard that the sage empties his mind and fills his belly."
entries.literal: Zhicai answered: "I have heard that the sage empties his mind and fills his belly."

entries.zh: 捨嗟賞之。
entries.en: She sighed in admiration.
entries.literal: She sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 年十三，召為太學生，粗通《禮》、《易》。
entries.en: At thirteen he was summoned as imperial academy student and had a rough mastery of the Rites and the Changes.
entries.literal: At thirteen he was summoned as Imperial Academy student and had a rough mastery of the Rites and the Changes.

entries.zh: 彭城劉孝綽、河東裴子野、吳郡張嵊等每共論《周易》及《喪服》儀，酬應如響。
entries.en: Pengcheng Liu Xiaochuo, Hedong Pei Ziye, Wu commandery Zhang Sheng, and others often debated the Book of Changes and mourning-garment ritual with him; his replies came like an echo.
entries.literal: Pengcheng Liu Xiaochuo, Hedong Pei Ziye, Wu commandery Zhang Sheng, and others often debated the Book of Changes and mourning-garment ritual with him; his replies came like an echo.

entries.zh: 咸共歎曰：「此神童也。」
entries.en: They all sighed together, "This is a divine child."
entries.literal: They all sighed together: "This is a divine child."

entries.zh: 孝綽又云：「徐郎燕頷，有班定遠之相。」
entries.en: Xiaochuo also said, "Master Xu has a swallow jaw—he has the look of Ban Chao the Distance-Pacifier."
entries.literal: Xiaochuo also said: "Master Xu has a swallow jaw—he has the look of Ban Chao the Distance-Pacifier."

entries.zh: 陳郡袁昂領丹陽尹，辟為主簿，人務事宜，皆被顧訪。
entries.en: Chen commandery Yuan Ang held Danyang prefect; he recruited Zhicai as chief clerk, and whenever men had business affairs they were all referred to him for counsel.
entries.literal: Chen commandery Yuan Ang held Danyang prefect; he recruited Zhicai as chief clerk, and whenever men had business affairs they were all referred to him for counsel.

entries.zh: 郡廨遭火，之才起望，夜中不著衣，披紅服帕出房，映光為昂所見。
entries.en: The prefectural offices suffered fire; Zhicai rose to look and in the night wore no clothes, but came out of the room in a red kerchief over his shoulders; the light caught him and Ang saw it.
entries.literal: The prefectural offices suffered fire; Zhicai rose to look and in the night wore no clothes, but came out of the room in a red kerchief over his shoulders; the light caught him and Ang saw it.

entries.zh: 功曹白請免職，昂重其才術，仍特原之。
entries.en: The merit officer memorialized asking that he be dismissed; Ang valued his talent and skill and specially pardoned him.
entries.literal: The merit officer memorialized asking that he be dismissed; Ang valued his talent and skill and specially pardoned him.

entries.zh: 豫章王綜出鎮江都，復除豫章王國左常侍，又轉綜鎮北主簿。
entries.en: Prince of Yuzhang Zong went out to garrison Jiangdu; Zhicai was again made left regular attendant of the Yuzhang kingdom, then transferred to Zong's northern campaign chief clerk.
entries.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Zong went out to garrison Jiangdu; Zhicai was again made left regular attendant of the Yuzhang kingdom, then transferred to Zong's northern campaign chief clerk.

entries.zh: 蕭明 蕭祗 蕭退 蕭放 徐之才
entries.en: Xiao Ming; Xiao Zhi; Xiao Tui; Xiao Fang; Xu Zhicai
entries.literal: Xiao Ming; Xiao Zhi; Xiao Tui; Xiao Fang; Xu Zhicai

entries.zh: 正光中，隨父之幷州。
entries.en: In the Zhenguang era he followed his father to Bing province.
entries.literal: In the Zhenguang era he followed his father to Bing province.

entries.zh: 性旣恬默，又好山水，遂入晉陽西縣甕山讀書。
entries.en: His nature being tranquil and silent and also fond of mountains and rivers, he entered Weng Mountain in Jinyang West county to read books.
entries.literal: His nature being tranquil and silent and also fond of mountains and rivers, he entered Weng Mountain in Jinyang West county to read books.

entries.zh: 孝昌初，津為定州刺史，愔亦隨父之職。
entries.en: At the beginning of Xiaochang, Jin became inspector of Dingzhou and Yin also followed his father to his post.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, Jin became inspector of Dingzhou and Yin also followed his father to his post.

entries.zh: 以軍功除羽林監，賜爵魏昌男，不拜。
entries.en: For military merit he was made supervisor of the Feathered Forest, enfeoffed as Baron of Weichang, and did not accept.
entries.literal: For military merit he was made supervisor of the Feathered Forest, enfeoffed as Marquis of Weichang, and did not accept.

entries.zh: 及中山為杜洛周陷，全家被囚縶。
entries.en: When Zhongshan fell to Du Luozhou, the whole family was taken prisoner.
entries.literal: When Zhongshan fell to Du Luozhou, the whole family was taken prisoner.

entries.zh: 未幾，洛周滅，又沒葛榮。
entries.en: Before long Luozhou was destroyed and they fell again to Ge Rong.
entries.literal: Before long Luozhou was destroyed and they fell again to Ge Rong.

entries.zh: 榮欲以女妻之，又逼以偽職。
entries.en: Rong wished to marry his daughter to him and also pressed a false office on him.
entries.literal: Rong wished to marry his daughter to him and also pressed a false office on him.

entries.zh: 愔乃託疾，密含牛血數合，於衆中吐之，仍佯喑不語。
entries.en: Yin then feigned illness, secretly held several he of ox blood in his mouth, spat it out in the crowd, and still pretended to be mute and speechless.
entries.literal: Yin then feigned illness, secretly held several he of ox blood in his mouth, spat it out in the crowd, and still pretended to be mute and speechless.

entries.zh: 榮以為信然，乃止。
entries.en: Rong believed it real and thereupon stopped.
entries.literal: Rong believed it real and thereupon stopped.

entries.zh: 永安初，還洛，拜通直散騎侍郎，時年十八。
entries.en: At the beginning of Yong'an he returned to Luoyang and was appointed attendant gentleman of the unimpeded staff; he was then eighteen.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he returned to Luoyang and was appointed attendant gentleman of the Unimpeded Staff; he was then eighteen.

entries.zh: 元顥入洛，時愔從父兄侃為北中郎將，鎮河梁。
entries.en: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yin at the time had a cousin Kan serving as general of the north center, garrisoning He Bridge.
entries.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yin at the time had a cousin Kan serving as General of the North Center, garrisoning He Bridge.

entries.zh: 愔適至侃處，便屬乘輿失守，夜至河。
entries.en: Yin happened to reach Kan's post just as the imperial carriage lost its place; at night they came to the river.
entries.literal: Yin happened to reach Kan's post just as the imperial carriage lost its place; at night they came to the river.

entries.zh: 侃雖奉迎車駕北渡，而潛欲南奔，愔固諫止之。
entries.en: Though Kan received the carriage and escorted it north across the river, in secret he wished to flee south; Yin firmly remonstrated and stopped him.
entries.literal: Though Kan received the carriage and escorted it north across the river, in secret he wished to flee south; Yin firmly remonstrated and stopped him.

entries.zh: 遂相與扈從達建州。
entries.en: They thereupon together escorted the court as far as Jian province.
entries.literal: They thereupon together escorted the court as far as Jian province.

entries.zh: 除通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: He was made regular attendant gentleman of the unimpeded staff.
entries.literal: He was made regular attendant gentleman of the Unimpeded Staff.

entries.zh: 愔以世故未夷，志在潛退，乃謝病，與友人中直侍郎河間邢卲隱於嵩山。
entries.en: Yin, because worldly troubles were not yet settled, wished to withdraw in seclusion; he therefore pleaded illness and with his friend Hejian Xing Shao, attendant gentleman of the central straight, hid on Mount Song.
entries.literal: Yin, because worldly troubles were not yet settled, wished to withdraw in seclusion; he therefore pleaded illness and with his friend Hejian Xing Shao, attendant gentleman of the Central Straight, hid on Mount Song.

entries.zh: 及莊帝誅尒朱榮，其從兄侃參贊帷幄。
