entries.en: When Emperor Zhuang executed Erzhu Rong, his cousin Kan took part in planning within the curtains.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuang executed Erzhu Rong, his cousin Kan took part in planning within the curtains.

entries.zh: 朝廷以其父津為幷州刺史、北道大行臺，愔隨之任。
entries.en: The court made his father Jin inspector of Bingzhou and grand commissioner of the northern route; Yin followed him to his appointment.
entries.literal: The court made his father Jin inspector of Bingzhou and grand commissioner of the northern route; Yin followed him to his appointment.

entries.zh: 有邯鄲人楊寬者，求義從出藩，愔請津納之。
entries.en: There was a Handan man named Yang Kuan who sought to follow in righteous service when Jin went out to his province; Yin asked Jin to take him in.
entries.literal: There was a Handan man named Yang Kuan who sought to follow in righteous service when Jin went out to his province; Yin asked Jin to take him in.

entries.zh: 俄而孝莊幽崩，愔時適欲還都，行達邯鄲，過楊寬家，為寬所執。
entries.en: Before long Emperor Xiaozhuang was imprisoned and died; Yin at the time was about to return to the capital, reached Handan on the road, passed Yang Kuan's house, and was seized by Kuan.
entries.literal: Before long Emperor Xiaozhuang was imprisoned and died; Yin at the time was about to return to the capital, reached Handan on the road, passed Yang Kuan's house, and was seized by Kuan.

entries.zh: 至相州，見刺史劉誕，以愔名家盛德，甚相哀念，付長史慕容白澤禁止焉。
entries.en: Reaching Xiang province he saw inspector Liu Yan; because Yin was of a famous house and lofty virtue, Yan greatly pitied him and handed him to chief clerk Murong Baize to detain.
entries.literal: Reaching Xiang province he saw Inspector Liu Yan; because Yin was of a famous house and lofty virtue, Yan greatly pitied him and handed him to Chief Clerk Murong Baize to detain.

entries.zh: 遣隊主鞏榮貴防禁送都。
entries.en: He sent squad chief Gong Ronggui to guard and escort him to the capital.
entries.literal: He sent squad chief Gong Ronggui to guard and escort him to the capital.

entries.zh: 至安陽亭，愔謂榮貴曰：「僕家世忠臣，輸誠魏室，家亡國破，一至於此。
entries.en: At Anyang Pavilion Yin said to Ronggui, "My house for generations has been loyal ministers, pouring sincerity into the Wei house; now family is destroyed and state broken—things have come to this.
entries.literal: At Anyang Pavilion Yin said to Ronggui: "My house for generations has been loyal ministers, pouring sincerity into the Wei house; now family is destroyed and state broken—things have come to this.

entries.zh: 雖曰囚虜，復何面目見君父之讐仇！
entries.en: Though called a captive, what face have I to see our lord and father's mortal foes!
entries.literal: Though called a captive, what face have I to see our lord and father's mortal foes!

entries.zh: 得自縊於一繩，傳首而去，君之惠也。」
entries.en: If I may hang myself on one cord and send my head away, that will be your kindness."
entries.literal: If I may hang myself on one cord and send my head away, that will be your kindness."

entries.zh: 榮貴深相憐感，遂與俱逃。
entries.en: Ronggui deeply pitied and was moved, and thereupon fled together with him.
entries.literal: Ronggui deeply pitied and was moved, and thereupon fled with him together.

entries.zh: 愔乃投高昂兄弟。
entries.en: Yin then threw himself on Gao Ao's brothers.
entries.literal: Yin then threw himself on Gao Ao's brothers.

entries.zh: 旣潛竄累載，屬神武至信都，遂投刺轅門。
entries.en: Having lurked in hiding for several years, when Gao Huan reached Xindu he thereupon presented his card at the camp gate.
entries.literal: Having lurked in hiding for several years, when Gao Huan reached Xindu he thereupon presented his card at the camp gate.

entries.zh: 便蒙引見，贊揚興運，陳訴家禍，言辭哀壯，涕泗橫集，神武為之改容。
entries.en: He was at once granted audience, praised the rising fortune, and stated his family's calamity; his words were mournful and strong, tears streamed across his face, and Gao Huan changed countenance for it.
entries.literal: He was at once granted audience, praised the rising fortune, and stated his family's calamity; his words were mournful and strong, tears streamed across his face, and Gao Huan changed countenance for it.

entries.zh: 即署行臺郎中。
entries.en: He was immediately appointed gentleman of the mobile staff.
entries.literal: He was immediately appointed gentleman of the mobile staff.

entries.zh: 大軍南攻鄴，歷楊寬村，寬於馬前叩頭請罪。
entries.en: When the great army attacked Ye southward and passed Yang Kuan's village, Kuan knelt before the horse and begged forgiveness.
entries.literal: When the great army attacked Ye southward and passed Yang Kuan's village, Kuan knelt before the horse and begged forgiveness.

entries.zh: 愔謂曰：「人不識恩義，蓋亦常理，我不恨卿，無遐驚怖。」
entries.en: Yin said to him, "Men not knowing grace and righteousness is also the ordinary rule; I bear you no hatred—have no distant terror."
entries.literal: Yin said to him: "Men not knowing grace and righteousness is also the ordinary rule; I bear you no hatred—have no distant terror."

entries.zh: 時鄴未下，神武命愔作祭天文，燎畢而城陷。
entries.en: At the time Ye had not yet fallen; Gao Huan ordered Yin to compose the text for a sacrifice to Heaven; when the burning was done the city fell.
entries.literal: At the time Ye had not yet fallen; Gao Huan ordered Yin to compose the text for a sacrifice to Heaven; when the burning was done the city fell.

entries.zh: 由是轉大行臺右丞。
entries.en: Thereupon he was transferred to right aide of the grand mobile staff.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was transferred to right aide of the grand mobile staff.

entries.zh: 于時霸圖草創，軍國務廣，文檄教令，皆自愔及崔㥄悛出。
entries.en: At that time the hegemonic design was newly begun and military and state affairs were broad; proclamations, orders, and edicts all issued from Yin and Cui Lingquan.
entries.literal: At that time the hegemonic design was newly begun and military and state affairs were broad; proclamations, orders, and edicts all issued from Yin and Cui Ling-Quan.

entries.zh: 遭離家難，以喪禮自居，所食唯鹽米而已，哀毀骨立。
entries.en: Having met family disaster, he took mourning ritual as his own rule; what he ate was only salt and rice, and in grief he wasted until only bone remained.
entries.literal: Having met family disaster, he took mourning ritual as his own rule; what he ate was only salt and rice, and in grief he wasted until only bone remained.

entries.zh: 神武愍之，恒相開慰。
entries.en: Gao Huan pitied him and constantly comforted him.
entries.literal: Gao Huan pitied him and constantly comforted him.

entries.zh: 及韓陵之戰，愔每陣先登，朋僚咸共怪嘆曰：「楊氏儒生，今遂為武士，仁者必勇，定非虛論。」
entries.en: At the battle of Hanling, Yin each time took the van in the line; colleagues all marveled together and said, "The Yang clan's Confucian—now he has become a warrior; the benevolent must be brave—surely no empty saying."
entries.literal: At the battle of Hanling, Yin each time took the van in the line; colleagues all marveled together and said: "The Yang clan's Confucian—now he has become a warrior; the benevolent must be brave—surely no empty saying."

entries.zh: 燕子獻，字季則，廣漢下洛人。
entries.en: Yan Zixian, styled Jize, was from Xialuo in Guanghan.
entries.literal: Yan Zixian, styled Jize, was from Xialuo in Guanghan.

entries.zh: 少時相者謂之曰：「使役在胡代，富貴在齊趙。」
entries.en: When he was young, a physiognomist told him, "Your service will be among Hu and Dai, and your wealth and rank in Qi and Zhao."
entries.literal: When he was young, a physiognomist said to him, "Your service will be among Hu and Dai, and your wealth and rank in Qi and Zhao."

entries.zh: 其後，遇宇文氏稱霸關中，用為典簽，將命使於茹茹。
entries.en: Later, when the Yuwen clan rose to hegemony in Guanzhong, he was employed as a records clerk and sent on a mission to Rouran.
entries.literal: Later, when the Yuwen clan claimed hegemony in Guanzhong, he was employed as a records clerk and was sent on a mission to Rouran.

entries.zh: 子獻欲驗相者之言，來歸。
entries.en: Zixian wanted to test the physiognomist's prediction, so he came over in submission.
entries.literal: Zixian wished to test the physiognomist's words and came over in submission.

entries.zh: 高祖見之大悅，尚淮陽公主，甚被待遇。
entries.en: Gaozu was delighted when he met him; Zixian married Princess Huaiyang and received especially favorable treatment.
entries.literal: Gaozu saw him and was greatly pleased; he married Princess Huaiyang and was treated very favorably.

entries.zh: 顯祖時，官至侍中、開府。
entries.en: In Xianzu's time, he rose to palace attendant and opening office.
entries.literal: In Xianzu's time, his offices reached palace attendant and opening office.

entries.zh: 濟南即位之後，委任彌重，除右僕射。
entries.en: After Jinan ascended the throne, he was entrusted with even greater responsibility and appointed right vice director.
entries.literal: After Jinan ascended the throne, his entrusted responsibilities became still weightier, and he was appointed right vice director.

entries.zh: 子獻素多力，頭又少發，當狼狽之際，排衆走出省門，斛律光逐而擒之。
entries.en: Zixian was always strong and had little hair. In the panic he pushed through the crowd and fled out the office gate, but Hulu Guang pursued and seized him.
entries.literal: Zixian had always been strong and had little hair on his head; in the moment of panic he pushed through the crowd and fled out the office gate, but Hulu Guang pursued and seized him.

entries.zh: 子獻嘆曰：「丈夫為計遲，遂至於此矣。」
entries.en: Zixian sighed, "A man planned too late, and so it has come to this."
entries.literal: Zixian sighed and said, "A man made his plan too late and so has come to this."

entries.zh: 二叔率高歸彥、賀拔仁、斛律金擁愔等唐突入雲龍門。
entries.en: The two princes led Gao Guiyan, Heba Ren, and Hulu Jin in hustling Yang Yin and the others through Cloud Dragon Gate.
entries.literal: The two uncles led Gao Guiyan, Heba Ren, and Hulu Jin in hustling Yin and the rest in a rush through Cloud Dragon Gate.

entries.zh: 見都督叱利騷，招之不進，使騎殺之。
entries.en: They saw commander Chilü Sao, summoned him, and when he would not advance they had horsemen cut him down.
entries.literal: They saw Commander Chilü Sao, summoned him; he would not advance; they had horsemen kill him.

entries.zh: 開府成休寧拒門，歸彥喻之，乃得入。
entries.en: Cheng Xiuning, who held privy chamber rank, blocked the gate; Guiyan persuaded him, and they entered.
entries.literal: Acting Three Excellencies Cheng Xiuning barred the gate; Guiyan instructed him, and only then could they enter.

entries.zh: 送愔等於御前。
entries.en: They brought Yang Yin and the others before the emperor.
entries.literal: They sent Yin and the rest before the emperor.

entries.zh: 長廣王及歸彥在朱華門外。
entries.en: The prince of Changgung and Guiyan waited outside Vermilion Flower Gate.
entries.literal: The prince of Changgung and Guiyan were outside Vermilion Flower Gate.

entries.zh: 太皇太后臨昭陽殿，太后及帝側立。
entries.en: The grand empress dowager presided in Zhaoyang Hall; the empress dowager and the emperor stood at her side.
entries.literal: The grand empress dowager came to Zhaoyang Hall; the empress dowager and the emperor stood at the side.

entries.zh: 常山王以磚叩頭，進而言曰：「臣與陛下骨肉相連。
entries.en: The prince of Changshan kowtowed on the brick floor and said, "Your servant and Your Majesty are bound in the same flesh.
entries.literal: The prince of Changshan knocked his head with brick and advanced, saying, "Your servant and Your Majesty are bone and flesh joined.

entries.zh: 楊遵彥等欲擅朝權，威福自己，王公以還，皆重足屏氣。
entries.en: Yang Zunyan and his circle meant to monopolize court power and keep bounty in their own hands; from kings and dukes down everyone stood in dread.
entries.literal: Yang Zunyan and the rest wished to monopolize court power; authority and blessing were theirs alone; from kings and dukes down all stood on tiptoe and held their breath.

entries.zh: 共相唇齒，以成亂階，若不早圖，必為宗社之害。
entries.en: They were mouth and gum to one another and piled step on step toward chaos; unless checked early they would ruin the altars of state.
entries.literal: They were lip and teeth to each other and made the steps of disorder; if not plotted against early, they would surely harm the altars of state.

entries.zh: 臣與湛等為國事重，賀拔仁、斛律金等惜獻皇帝基業，共執遵彥等領入宮，未敢刑戮，專輒之失，罪合萬死。」
entries.en: Your servant and Zhan took the weight of state upon ourselves; Heba Ren and Hulu Jin cherished Emperor Xian's foundation; we seized Zunyan and his fellows and brought them into the palace. We have not yet executed them; for our presumption we deserve ten thousand deaths."
entries.literal: Your servant and Zhan and the rest took state affairs as weighty; Heba Ren, Hulu Jin and the rest cherished Emperor Xian's foundation; together we seized Zunyan and the rest and led them into the palace; we did not yet dare execution and punishment; the fault of arrogating authority deserves ten thousand deaths."

entries.zh: 帝時默然，領軍劉桃枝之徒陛衛，叩刀仰視，帝不睨之，太皇太后令卻仗，不肯。
entries.en: The emperor said nothing. Garrison-general Liu Taozhi and his guards stood on the stairs, hands on their blades, looking up at him; the emperor would not meet their eyes. The grand empress dowager ordered them to stand down; they refused.
entries.literal: The emperor was silent; Liu Taozhi of the garrison-general and his kind guarded the steps, striking blades and looking up; the emperor would not glance at them; the grand empress dowager ordered them to lay aside weapons; they would not.

entries.zh: 又厲聲曰：「奴輩即今頭落。」
entries.en: She shouted again, "Slaves—off with your heads this instant!"
entries.literal: She again said in a harsh voice, "Slaves—your heads fall this instant."

entries.zh: 乃卻。
entries.en: Then they withdrew.
entries.literal: Then they withdrew.

entries.zh: 因問楊郎何在，賀拔仁曰：「一目已出。」
entries.en: She asked where Master Yang was; Heba Ren said, "One eye is already gone."
entries.literal: She then asked where Master Yang was; Heba Ren said, "One eye is already out."

entries.zh: 太皇太后愴然曰：「楊郎何所能，留使不好耶！」
entries.en: The grand empress dowager said in grief, "What harm could Master Yang have done—was it not better to keep him!"
entries.literal: The grand empress dowager said mournfully, "What could Master Yang do—would it not have been better to keep him!"

entries.zh: 乃讓帝曰：「此等懷逆，欲殺我二兒，次及我，爾何縱之？」
entries.en: She reproached the emperor: "These men plotted rebellion; they meant to kill my two sons and next would reach me—why did you indulge them?"
entries.literal: She then reproached the emperor: "These men harbored rebellion, wished to kill my two sons, next would reach me—why did you indulge them?"

entries.zh: 帝猶不能言。
entries.en: The emperor still could not speak.
entries.literal: The emperor still could not speak.

entries.zh: 太皇太后怒且悲，王公皆泣。
entries.en: The grand empress dowager was torn between anger and grief; the princes and dukes wept.
entries.literal: The grand empress dowager was angry and grieved; kings and dukes all wept.

entries.zh: 太皇太后曰：「豈可使我母子受漢老嫗斟酌。」
entries.en: The grand empress dowager said, "How can you let us mother and son be ruled by an old Han woman!"
entries.literal: The grand empress dowager said, "How can you let us mother and son be measured out by an old Han crone!"

entries.zh: 太后拜謝。
entries.en: The empress dowager bowed in apology.
entries.literal: The empress dowager bowed in apology.

entries.zh: 常山王叩頭不止。
entries.en: The prince of Changshan kept knocking his head on the floor.
entries.literal: The prince of Changshan knocked his head without cease.

entries.zh: 太皇太后謂帝：「何不安尉爾叔？」
entries.en: The grand empress dowager said to the emperor, "Why do you not comfort your uncle?"
entries.literal: The grand empress dowager said to the emperor, "Why do you not comfort and soothe your uncle?"

entries.zh: 帝乃曰：「天子亦不敢與叔惜，豈敢惜此漢輩？
entries.en: The emperor then said, "Even the Son of Heaven dares not withhold them from his uncle—how much less these Han fellows?
entries.literal: The emperor then said, "The Son of Heaven also dares not spare them for his uncle's sake—how much less spare these Han fellows?

entries.zh: 但願乞兒性命，兒自下殿去，此等任叔父處分。」
entries.en: I beg only for my son's life; your son will leave the hall—dispose of this lot as you will."
entries.literal: I only wish to beg my son's life; your son will leave the hall—this lot is left to uncle's disposal."

entries.zh: 遂皆斬之。
entries.en: Thereupon all were beheaded.
entries.literal: Thereupon all were beheaded.

entries.zh: 長廣王以子默昔讒己作詔書，故先拔其舌，截其手。
entries.en: The prince of Changgung, because Zimo had once slandered him in an edict, first tore out his tongue and cut off his hands.
entries.literal: The prince of Changgung, because Zimo had once slandered him in drafting an edict, first pulled out his tongue and cut off his hands.

entries.zh: 太皇太后臨愔喪，哭曰：「楊郎忠而獲罪。」
entries.en: The grand empress dowager attended Yang Yin's mourning and wept, "Master Yang was loyal yet was punished."
entries.literal: The grand empress dowager attended Yin's mourning and wept, saying, "Master Yang was loyal yet received punishment."

entries.zh: 以御金為之一眼，親內之，曰：「以表我意。」
entries.en: She had an eye made of imperial gold and placed it in the coffin herself, saying, "This shows my heart."
entries.literal: She used imperial gold to make one eye, personally placed it within, and said, "To show my mind."

entries.zh: 常山王亦悔殺之。
entries.en: The prince of Changshan also regretted the killing.
entries.literal: The prince of Changshan also regretted killing him.

entries.zh: 先是童謠曰：「白羊頭尾禿，羖䍽頭生角。」
entries.en: Earlier a children's rhyme ran, "The white sheep's head and tail are bare; the black ram grows horns on its brow."
entries.literal: Before this, a children's rhyme said, "The white sheep's head and tail are bald; the black ram's head grows horns."

entries.zh: 又曰：「羊羊喫野草，不吃野草遠我道，不遠打爾腦。」
entries.en: Another ran, "Sheep, sheep, graze the wild grass; leave the grass and you leave my road; stay near and I'll crack your skull."
entries.literal: It also said, "Sheep, sheep eat wild grass; if you don't eat wild grass, keep far from my road; if you don't keep far, I'll beat your brains."

entries.zh: 又曰：「阿麼姑禍也，道人姑夫死也。」
entries.en: Another said, "Auntie brings ruin; the tonsured princess's husbands die."
entries.literal: It also said, "Auntie brings calamity; the Daoist nun's brother-in-law dies."

entries.zh: 羊為愔也，「角」文為用刀，「道人」謂廢帝小名，太原公主嘗作尼，故曰「阿麼姑」，愔子獻、天和皆帝姑夫云。
entries.en: Sheep stood for Yin; the character for 'horn' splits into 'use' and 'knife'; 'Daoist' meant the deposed emperor's childhood name; the princess of Taiyuan had once been a nun, hence 'Auntie'; Zixian and Tianhe, both sons-in-law of the house, were tied to the rhyme.
entries.literal: Sheep was Yin; 'horn' written was using a knife; 'Daoist' meant the deposed emperor's childhood name; the princess of Taiyuan had once been a nun, hence 'Auntie'; Yin, Zixian, and Tianhe were all the emperor's aunts' husbands.

entries.zh: 於是乃以天子之命下詔罪之，罪止一身，家口不問。
entries.en: Thereupon an edict in the emperor's name condemned them, limiting guilt to the men themselves and exempting their households.
entries.literal: Thereupon by the Son of Heaven's command an edict was issued condemning their crimes; guilt stopped at one person; households were not questioned.

entries.zh: 尋復簿錄五家，王晞固諫，乃各沒一房，孩幼兄弟皆除名。
entries.en: Before long registers were drawn up against five families; Wang Xi protested firmly; in the end one branch of each house was confiscated and brothers and children were struck from the rolls.
entries.literal: Soon registers were again made of five families; Wang Xi firmly remonstrated; thereupon one branch of each was confiscated; infant children and brothers were all struck from the rolls.

entries.zh: 神武知愔存，遣愔從兄寶猗賫書慰喻，仍遣光州刺史奚思業令搜訪，以禮發遣。
entries.en: Gao Huan knew Yin was alive, sent Yin's cousin Baoyi with a letter to comfort and instruct him, and still sent Guangzhou inspector Xi Siye to search him out and send him off with ritual.
entries.literal: Gao Huan knew Yin was alive, sent Yin's cousin Baoyi with a letter to comfort and instruct him, and still sent Guangzhou inspector Xi Siye to search him out and send him off with ritual.

entries.zh: 神武見之悅，除太原公開府司馬，轉長史，復授大行臺右丞，封華陰縣侯，遷給事黃門侍郎，妻以庶女。
entries.en: Gao Huan was pleased to see him, made him staff officer of the Prince of Taiyuan's establishment, transferred him to chief clerk, again gave him right aide of the grand mobile staff, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huayin county, promoted him to attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, and gave him a concubine's daughter in marriage.
entries.literal: Gao Huan was pleased to see him, made him staff officer of the Prince of Taiyuan's establishment, transferred him to chief clerk, again gave him right aide of the grand mobile staff, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huayin county, promoted him to attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and gave him a concubine's daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 又兼散騎常侍，為聘梁使主。
entries.en: He also concurrently served as regular attendant gentleman and was chief envoy on a mission of betrothal to Liang.
entries.literal: He also concurrently served as regular attendant gentleman and was chief envoy on a mission of betrothal to Liang.

entries.zh: 至碻磝戍，州內有愔家舊佛寺，入精廬禮拜，見太傅容像，悲感慟哭，嘔血數升，遂發病不成行，輿疾還鄴。
entries.en: Reaching Qiaoqiu garrison, within the prefecture was an old Buddhist temple of Yin's family; he entered the pure hall to bow in worship, saw the image of the grand tutor, was moved to grief and wailed, vomited several sheng of blood, and thereupon fell ill and could not travel; he was carried ill back to Ye.
entries.literal: Reaching Qiaoqiu garrison, within the prefecture was an old Buddhist temple of Yin's family; he entered the pure hall to bow in worship, saw the image of the Grand Tutor, was moved to grief and wailed, vomited several sheng of blood, and thereupon fell ill and could not travel; he was carried ill back to Ye.

entries.zh: 久之，以本官兼尚書吏部郎中。
entries.en: After a long while, in his former office he was made concurrently gentleman of the ministry of personnel in the masters of writing.
entries.literal: After a long while, in his former office he was made concurrently gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the masters of writing.

entries.zh: 武定末，以望實之美，超拜吏部尚書，加侍中、衛將軍，侍學典選如故。
entries.en: At the end of Wuding, for the beauty of his reputation and substance he was promoted over others to director of the ministry of personnel, with concurrent palace attendant and guards general; he attended study and directed selection as before.
entries.literal: At the end of Wuding, for the beauty of his reputation and substance he was promoted over others to director of the ministry of personnel, with concurrent palace attendant and guards general; he attended study and directed selection as before.

entries.zh: 愔從兄幼卿為岐州刺史，以直言忤旨見誅。
entries.en: Yin's cousin Youqing was inspector of Qi province; for blunt words that offended the intent he was put to death.
entries.literal: Yin's cousin Youqing was inspector of Qi province; for blunt words that offended the intent he was put to death.

entries.zh: 愔聞之悲懼，因哀感發疾，後取急就雁門溫湯療疾。
entries.en: When Yin heard it he was grieved and afraid; grief and shock brought on illness, and later he took urgent leave to go to the hot springs at Yanmen to treat his illness.
entries.literal: When Yin heard it he was grieved and afraid; grief and shock brought on illness, and later he took urgent leave to go to the hot springs at Yanmen to treat his illness.

entries.zh: 郭秀素害其能，因致書恐之曰：「高王欲送卿於帝所。」
entries.en: Guo Xiu by nature envied his ability and therefore sent a letter threatening him, saying, "The Prince of Qi wishes to send you to the Emperor's place."
entries.literal: Guo Xiu by nature envied his ability and therefore sent a letter threatening him, saying: "The Prince of Qi wishes to send you to the Emperor's place."

entries.zh: 仍勸其逃亡。
entries.en: He also urged him to flee.
entries.literal: He also urged him to flee.

entries.zh: 愔遂棄衣冠於水濱若自沉者，變易名姓，自稱劉士安，入嵩山，與沙門曇謨徵等居成削迹。
entries.en: Yin thereupon cast off hat and robes at the water's edge as though drowning himself, changed his name, called himself Liu Shi'an, entered Mount Song, and with the monk Tan Mo and others dwelt in seclusion, his traces cut away.
entries.literal: Yin thereupon cast off hat and robes at the water's edge as though drowning himself, changed his name, called himself Liu Shi'an, entered Mount Song, and with the monk Tan Mo and others dwelt in seclusion, his traces cut away.

entries.zh: 又潛之光州，因東入田橫島，以講誦為業。
entries.en: He also lurked in Guang province and then went east into Tianheng Island, making lecturing and recitation his livelihood.
entries.literal: He also lurked in Guang province and then went east into Tianheng Island, making lecturing and recitation his livelihood.

entries.zh: 海隅之士，謂之劉先生。
entries.en: Gentlemen of the sea's edge called him Master Liu.
entries.literal: Gentlemen of the sea's edge called him Master Liu.

entries.zh: 太守王元景陰佑之。
entries.en: Grand administrator Wang Yuanjing secretly aided him.
entries.literal: Grand Administrator Wang Yuanjing secretly aided him.

entries.zh: 楊愔 燕子獻 宋欽道 鄭頤
entries.en: Yang Yin; Yan Zixian; Song Qindao; Zheng Yi
entries.literal: Yang Yin; Yan Zixian; Song Qindao; Zheng Yi

entries.zh: 第二弟諏之奔關右，兄弟五人皆拘繫。
entries.en: His second brother Souzhi fled to the western passes; all five brothers were imprisoned.
entries.literal: His second younger brother Souzhi fled to Guanxi; all five brothers were detained.

entries.zh: 神武問曰：「諏之何在？」
entries.en: Gao Huan asked, "Where is Souzhi?"
entries.literal: Gao Huan asked, "Where is Souzhi?"

entries.zh: 答曰：「昔吳、蜀二國，諸葛兄弟各得遂心，況讓之老母在，君臣分定，失忠與孝，愚夫不為。
entries.en: He answered, "Long ago Wu and Shu were two realms, yet the Zhuge brothers each got his way; all the more when Rangzhi's aged mother is here—lord and subject each have his place; to lose loyalty and filial piety together is what no fool would choose.
entries.literal: He answered, "In former times Wu and Shu were two states, yet the Zhuge brothers each had his wish fulfilled; how much more when Rangzhi's old mother is here—ruler and minister roles are fixed; to lose both loyalty and filial piety is what a fool would not do.

entries.zh: 伏願明公以誠信待物，若以不信處物，物亦安能自信？
entries.en: I beg you, my lord, to meet the world with sincerity; if you meet the world without trust, how can the world trust you in return?
entries.literal: I humbly wish the lord will treat things with sincerity and trust; if you treat things without trust, how can things in turn trust you?

entries.zh: 以此定霸，猶卻行而求道耳。」
entries.en: To found dominion on that is like walking backward to find the road."
entries.literal: To settle hegemony on this basis is like walking backward to seek the Way."

entries.zh: 神武善其言，兄弟俱釋。
entries.en: Gao Huan approved his reply, and the brothers were all freed.
entries.literal: Gao Huan approved his words, and the brothers were all released.

entries.zh: 歷文襄大將軍主簿，兼中書舍人，後兼散騎常侍，聘梁。
entries.en: He served as chief clerk on Gao Cheng's staff as grand general, then as concurrent secretariat attendant and later as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry on a mission to Liang.
entries.literal: He served successively as chief clerk to Gao Cheng as grand general, concurrently secretariat attendant, later concurrently regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and as envoy to Liang.

entries.zh: 文襄嘗入朝，讓之導引，容儀蘊藉，文襄目之曰：「士禮佳舍人。」
entries.en: Once when Gao Cheng went to court Rangzhi led him in with composed, refined bearing; Gao Cheng glanced at him and said, "Shili is a fine gentleman of the secretariat."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng once entered court; Rangzhi guided him in; his bearing was composed and refined; Gao Cheng looked at him and said, "Shili is a fine attendant."

entries.zh: 遷長兼中書侍郎，領舍人。
entries.en: He was promoted to senior concurrent secretariat vice director while retaining his attendant post.
entries.literal: He was transferred to senior concurrent secretariat vice director, still holding attendant.

entries.zh: 讓之少好學，有文俊辯，早得聲譽。
entries.en: Rangzhi loved learning from youth; gifted in letters and sharp in debate, he won an early reputation.
entries.literal: Rangzhi from youth loved learning, had literary talent, sharp eloquence, and early won reputation.

entries.zh: 魏天平中舉秀才，對策高第。
entries.en: Under Wei in the Tianping era he was recommended as xiucai and ranked first in the policy examination.
entries.literal: In Wei times under Tianping he was recommended as xiucai; in policy responses he ranked at the top.

entries.zh: 累遷屯田主客郎中，省中語曰：「能賦詩，裴讓之。」
entries.en: He rose to director of agriculture and master of guests in the masters of writing; at court they said, "Who can write poetry? Pei Rangzhi."
entries.literal: He rose repeatedly to Director of Agriculture and Master of Guests in the Masters of Writing; within the ministry they said, "Who can compose poetry? Pei Rangzhi."

entries.zh: 為太原公開府記室。
entries.en: He became recorder on the staff of the Prince of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: He served as recorder for the Prince of Taiyuan's establishment.

entries.zh: 與楊愔友善，相遇則清談竟日。
entries.en: He was close to Yang Yin; whenever they met they talked the day away.
entries.literal: He was friendly with Yang Yin; when they met they held pure talk the whole day.

entries.zh: 愔每云：「此人風流警拔，裴文季為不亡矣。」
entries.en: Yin often said, "This man's spirit is striking and outstanding—Pei Wenji lives on in him."
entries.literal: Yin would often say, "This man's spirit is alert and outstanding—Pei Wenji is not dead after all."

entries.zh: 梁使至，帝令讓之攝主客郎。
entries.en: When a Liang envoy arrived, the emperor had Rangzhi serve as acting master of guests.
entries.literal: When a Liang envoy arrived, the emperor had Rangzhi act as master of guests attendant.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，靜帝遜居別宮，與諸臣別，讓之流涕歔欷。
entries.en: When Qi took the throne, Emperor Jing retired to a side palace to bid the ministers farewell; Rangzhi wept aloud.
entries.literal: When Qi received the mandate, Emperor Jing withdrew to a separate palace to take leave of the ministers; Rangzhi wept and sobbed.

entries.zh: 以參掌儀注，封寧都縣男。
entries.en: For helping draft ritual regulations he was enfeoffed as baron of Ningdu county.
entries.literal: For helping manage ritual regulations he was enfeoffed as Baron of Ningdu.

entries.zh: 帝欲以為黃門郎，或言其體重，不堪趨侍，乃除清河太守。
entries.en: The emperor wished to appoint him yellow gate attendant, but some said he was too heavyset for palace attendance, so he was made grand administrator of Qinghe instead.
entries.literal: The emperor wished to make him yellow gate attendant; some said his body was too heavy and he could not bear hurrying in attendance, so he was instead made grand administrator of Qinghe.

entries.zh: 至郡未幾，楊愔謂讓之諸弟曰：「我與賢兄交款，企聞善政。
entries.en: Soon after he took office in the commandery, Yang Yin told Rangzhi's brothers, "Your elder brother and I are close; I have been eager to hear of his good rule.
entries.literal: Not long after he reached the commandery, Yang Yin said to Rangzhi's younger brothers, "Your worthy elder brother and I are close in friendship; I look forward to hearing of good government.

entries.zh: 適有人從清河來，云姦吏斂跡，盜賊清靖。
entries.en: Someone has just arrived from Qinghe saying corrupt officials have pulled back and robbers are subdued.
entries.literal: Just now someone came from Qinghe and said corrupt clerks have drawn in their claws and bandits are quiet.

entries.zh: 期月之期，翻然更速。」
entries.en: What should have taken a month has come about even sooner."
entries.literal: The target of a full month has been overturned still faster."

entries.zh: 清河有二豪吏田轉貴、孫舍興久吏姦猾，多有侵削，因事遂脅人取財。
entries.en: Qinghe had two powerful clerks, Tian Zhuanggui and Sun Shexing—veteran, cunning officials who often skimmed funds and used any pretext to extort money.
entries.literal: In Qinghe were two powerful clerks, Tian Zhuangui and Sun Shexing—long-serving, crafty and slippery, who often shaved off shares and, using incidents, then extorted people's wealth.

entries.zh: 計贓依律不至死。
entries.en: By law the amount of stolen goods did not warrant death.
entries.literal: Calculating the booty by law did not reach death.

entries.zh: 讓之以其亂法，殺之。
entries.en: Rangzhi executed them for subverting the law.
entries.literal: Rangzhi, because they had disrupted the law, killed them.

entries.zh: 時清河王岳為司州牧，遣部從事案之。
entries.en: At the time Prince Yue of Qinghe was governor of Si province and sent a staff investigator to review the case.
entries.literal: At the time Prince Yue of Qinghe was inspector of Si province; he sent a bureau aide to investigate the case.

entries.zh: 侍中高德政舊與讓之不協，案奏言：「當陛下受禪之時，讓之眷戀魏朝，嗚咽流涕，比為內官，情非所願。」
entries.en: Palace attendant Gao Dezheng had long disliked Rangzhi; in his report he wrote, "When Your Majesty took the throne, Rangzhi clung to the Wei house and wept; service at court was not what he wished."
entries.literal: Palace attendant Gao Dezheng had long been at odds with Rangzhi; in the memorial of investigation he said, "When Your Majesty received the mandate, Rangzhi cherished the Wei court, sobbed and wept; compared with being an inner-court official, his heart was not in it."

entries.zh: 旣而楊愔請救之，云：「罪不合死。」
entries.en: Yang Yin then pleaded for him, saying, "The offense does not deserve death."
entries.literal: Before long Yang Yin pleaded for his life, saying, "The crime does not merit death."

entries.zh: 文宣大怒，謂愔曰：「欲得與裴讓之同冢耶！」
entries.en: Gao Yang flew into a rage and said to Yin, "Do you want to lie in the same grave as Pei Rangzhi?"
entries.literal: Gao Yang was greatly enraged and said to Yin, "Do you wish to share a tomb with Pei Rangzhi?"

entries.zh: 於是無敢言者。
entries.en: After that no one dared speak up.
entries.literal: Thereupon none dared speak further.

entries.zh: 事奏，竟賜死於家。
entries.en: When the case was finalized, he was ordered to take his own life at home.
entries.literal: When the matter was reported, in the end he was ordered to die at home.

entries.zh: 讓之次弟諏之。
entries.en: Rangzhi's next younger brother was Souzhi.
entries.literal: Rangzhi's next younger brother was Souzhi.

entries.zh: 劉禕，字彥英，彭城人。
entries.en: Liu Yi, style Yanying, was from Pengcheng.
entries.literal: Liu Yi, style Yanying, was a man of Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 父世明，魏兗州刺史。
entries.en: His father Shiming had been Wei inspector of Yan province.
entries.literal: His father Shiming had been Wei inspector of Yan province.

entries.zh: 禕性弘裕，有威重，容止可觀，雖昵友密交，朝夕遊處，莫不加敬。
entries.en: Yi was magnanimous and dignified, with a bearing men admired; even close friends who spent every day with him treated him with respect.
entries.literal: Yi's nature was broad and generous; he had weight and dignity; his bearing was admirable. Though intimate friends kept close company day and night, none failed to treat him with respect.

entries.zh: 好學，善《三禮》，吉凶儀制，尤所留心。
entries.en: He loved learning and excelled in the Three Rites, especially the ceremonies of fortune and mourning.
entries.literal: He loved learning and was skilled in the Three Rites; rites of fortune and calamity especially held his attention.

entries.zh: 魏孝昌中，釋巾太學博士。
entries.en: In the Wei Xiaochang era he entered the academy as erudite.
entries.literal: In the Xiaochang era of Wei he doffed his headcloth and became Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

entries.zh: 累遷睢州刺史，邊人服其威信，甚得疆埸之和。
entries.en: He rose to inspector of Sui province; frontier people trusted his authority and the border was at peace.
entries.literal: He rose through posts to inspector of Sui province; the frontier people submitted to his prestige and trust, and the borderlands knew great peace.

entries.zh: 世宗輔政，降書褒獎，云：「以卿家世忠純，奕代冠冕，賢弟賢子，並與吾共事，懷抱相托，亦自依然。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng was regent he sent a letter of praise, saying, "Your house has been loyal for generations and worn court rank for ages; worthy brothers and sons serve at my side, and the trust between us is unchanged.
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng held the regency he sent a letter of commendation, saying, "With your family's generations of loyal purity and successive generations in caps and coronets, worthy younger brothers and worthy sons all serve with me—hearts entrusted to one another, still as before.

entries.zh: 宜勗心力，以副所委，莫慮不富貴。」
entries.en: Exert yourself to fulfill what I entrust to you; do not doubt that honor and wealth will follow."
entries.literal: You should exert your mind and strength to answer what is entrusted—do not worry that wealth and rank will not come."

entries.zh: 秩滿，逕歸鄉里侍父疾，竟不入朝。
entries.en: When his term ended he went home to tend his father's illness and never returned to court.
entries.literal: When his term ended he went straight home to nurse his father's illness and never entered court.

entries.zh: 父喪，沉頓累年，非杖不起。
entries.en: After his father's death he lay prostrate for years and could not rise without a staff.
entries.literal: On his father's death he was prostrate for years and could not rise without a staff.

entries.zh: 世宗致辟，禕稱疾不動。
entries.en: Gao Cheng summoned him, but Yi pleaded illness and refused to come.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng summoned him, but Yi pleaded illness and would not go.

entries.zh: 五子，璇、玘、璞、瑗、瓚，並有志節，為世所稱。
entries.en: Five sons—Xuan, Qi, Pu, Yuan, and Zan—all had moral resolve and were praised in their time.
entries.literal: Five sons—Xuan, Qi, Pu, Yuan, and Zan—all had resolve and principle and were praised by the age.

entries.zh: 陸卬，字雲駒。
entries.en: Lu Ang, styled Yunju.
entries.literal: Lu Ang, styled Yunju.

entries.zh: 少機悟，美風神，好學不倦，博覽群書，五經多通大義。
entries.en: From youth he was quick and perceptive, handsome in spirit and bearing; he studied tirelessly, read widely, and grasped the main sense of the Five Classics.
entries.literal: From youth he was quick and perceptive, of fine spirit and bearing; he loved learning without tiring, broadly reading many books, and mostly penetrated the great meaning of the Five Classics.

entries.zh: 善屬文，甚為河間邢卲所賞。
entries.en: Skilled in writing, he was greatly admired by Xing Shao of Hejian.
entries.literal: Skilled at composing literature, he was greatly prized by Xing Shao of Hejian.

entries.zh: 卲又與卬父子彰交遊，嘗謂子彰曰：「吾以卿老蚌，遂出明珠，意欲為羣拜紀可乎？」
entries.en: Xing Shao also associated with Ang and his father Zizhang. He once said to Zizhang, "I take you as the old clam that bore the pearl—shall I have the company all bow in homage?"
entries.literal: Shao also associated with Ang and his father Zizhang in friendship. He once said to Zizhang, "I take you as the old clam that bore the pearl—do you wish the assembly all to bow in homage?"

entries.zh: 由是名譽日高，儒雅搢紳，尤所推許。
entries.en: From this his reputation rose day by day; cultivated officials especially praised him.
entries.literal: Thereupon his reputation rose daily; the refined scholar-gentry especially praised and upheld him.

entries.zh: 起家員外散騎侍郎，歷文襄大將軍主簿，中書舍人，兼中書侍郎，以本職兼太子洗馬。
entries.en: He began as outer attendant of the scattered cavalry, then served as secretary to Grand General Gao Cheng, as secretariat gentleman and concurrent secretariat vice director, and in that post also as crown prince preceptor.
entries.literal: He began his career as Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; he served as secretary to Gao Cheng, Grand General; Secretariat Gentleman; concurrently Secretariat Vice Director; and in his regular post concurrently Crown Prince Preceptor.

entries.zh: 自梁、魏通和，歲有交聘，卬每兼官燕接。
entries.en: Once Liang and Wei were at peace, embassies were exchanged every year; Ang repeatedly held concurrent posts to host the banquets.
entries.literal: From the time Liang and Wei made peace, each year brought mutual embassies; Ang each time held a concurrent post for banquet reception.

entries.zh: 在帝席賦詩，卬必先成，雖未能盡工，以敏速見美。
entries.en: At imperial feasts when poems were set, Ang always finished first; though not always masterly, he was praised for his speed.
entries.literal: At imperial banquets when composing verse, Ang always finished first; though his work was not fully polished, he was admired for quickness.

entries.zh: 除中書侍郎，修國史。
entries.en: He was made secretariat vice director and edited the national history.
entries.literal: He was appointed Secretariat Vice Director and edited the national history.

entries.zh: 以父憂去職，居喪盡禮，哀毀骨立。
entries.en: He left office for his father's mourning and observed every rite until grief had wasted him to skin and bone.
entries.literal: On his father's death he left office; in mourning he fulfilled every rite, his grief wasting him to skin and bone.

entries.zh: 詔以本官起。
entries.en: An edict recalled him to his former post.
entries.literal: An edict recalled him to his former post.

entries.zh: 文襄時鎮鄴，嘉其至行，親詣門以慰勉之。
entries.en: While Gao Cheng was stationed at Ye he admired Ang's conduct, came to his door in person, and comforted him.
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng held Ye, he prized Ang's utmost conduct and came in person to his gate to console and encourage him.

entries.zh: 卬母魏上庸公主，初封藍田，高明婦人也，甚有志操。
entries.en: Ang's mother was the Wei princess of Shangyong, first enfeoffed as princess of Lantian—a woman of high principle and strong moral resolve.
entries.literal: Ang's mother was the Wei Princess of Shangyong, first enfeoffed as Princess of Lantian—a woman of high principle and very strong resolve.

entries.zh: 卬昆季六人，並主所生。
entries.en: Ang and his brothers were six in all, all children of the same mother.
entries.literal: Ang and his brothers numbered six, all born of the mistress.

entries.zh: 故邢卲常謂人云：「藍田生玉，固不虛矣。」
entries.en: Xing Shao often said, "Lantian breeds jade—the saying is no empty boast."
entries.literal: Thus Xing Shao often told people, "Lantian breeds jade—indeed it is no empty saying."

entries.zh: 主教訓諸子，皆稟義方，雖創巨痛深，出於天性，然動依禮度，亦母氏之訓焉。
entries.en: Their mother trained them in the right way; though their overwhelming grief came from nature, they still acted by ritual—her teaching as well.
entries.literal: The mistress instructed her sons; all received righteous training. Though their crushing grief sprang from inborn nature, in action they still followed ritual measure—also their mother's instruction.

entries.zh: 卬兄弟相率廬於墓側，負土成墳，朝廷深所嗟尚，發詔褒揚，改其所居裏為孝終里。
entries.en: Ang and his brothers built mourning huts beside the tomb and heaped the grave with their own hands; the court admired them deeply, issued a commendation, and renamed their lane Xiaozhong, "Filial End."
entries.literal: Ang and his brothers together led huts by the tomb, carried earth to form the mound; the court deeply admired this, issued an edict of praise, and renamed their lane Xiaozhong Lane.

entries.zh: 服竟當襲，不忍嗣侯。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was to inherit the title, but he could not bring himself to take the marquisate.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was due to inherit, but he could not bear to succeed to the marquisate.

entries.zh: 王松年，少知名。
entries.en: Wang Songnian was known from his youth.
entries.literal: Wang Songnian was known from youth.

entries.zh: 文襄臨幷州，辟為主簿，累遷通直散騎常侍，副李緯使梁。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng took Bingzhou he made Songnian his secretary; he rose to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and went to Liang as deputy to Li Wei.
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng took Bingzhou he summoned him as secretary; he rose through posts to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and served as deputy to Li Wei on an embassy to Liang.

entries.zh: 還，歷位尚書郎中。
entries.en: After his return he served in successive director posts in the ministry.
entries.literal: On his return he held successive posts as director in the ministry.

entries.zh: 魏收撰《魏書》成，松年有謗言，文宣怒，禁止之，仍加杖罰。
entries.en: When Wei Shou completed the Book of Wei, Songnian spoke against it; Gao Yang was furious, had him imprisoned, and had him beaten.
entries.literal: When Wei Shou finished compiling the Book of Wei, Songnian spoke slanderously of it; Gao Yang was angry, had him detained, and also had him beaten with the staff.

entries.zh: 歲餘得免，除臨漳令，遷司馬、別駕、本州大中正。
entries.en: After more than a year he was freed, made magistrate of Linzhang, then promoted to aide, chief administrator, and provincial grand selection officer.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was released, appointed magistrate of Linzhang, then promoted to aide, chief administrator, and grand selection officer of his province.

entries.zh: 孝昭擢拜給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: Gao Yan promoted him to supervising secretary of the yellow gate attendant.
entries.literal: Gao Yan promoted him to Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate Attendant.

entries.zh: 帝每賜坐，與論政事，甚善之。
entries.en: Whenever the emperor gave him a seat and discussed affairs, he favored him greatly.
entries.literal: Whenever the emperor granted him a seat and discussed state affairs with him, he was well pleased with him.

entries.zh: 孝昭崩，松年馳驛至鄴都宣遺詔，發言涕泗，迄於宣罷，容色無改，辭吐諧韻。
entries.en: When Gao Yan died, Songnian raced by post to Ye to proclaim the deathbed edict; he wept as he spoke, yet from beginning to end his composure did not alter and his delivery stayed measured.
entries.literal: When Gao Yan died, Songnian galloped by post relay to Ye to proclaim the testament; as he spoke, tears streamed down, yet from the start of the proclamation to its end his bearing did not change and his words kept their rhythm.

entries.zh: 宣訖，號慟自絕於地，百官莫不感慟。
entries.en: When the reading ended he collapsed wailing; every official was moved.
entries.literal: When the proclamation ended he wailed and threw himself to the ground; the hundred officials were all deeply moved.

entries.zh: 還晉陽，兼侍中，護梓宮還鄴。
entries.en: He returned to Jinyang as concurrent palace attendant and escorted the coffin to Ye.
entries.literal: He returned to Jinyang, concurrently Palace Attendant, and escorted the coffin back to Ye.

entries.zh: 諸舊臣避形跡，無敢盡哀，唯松年哭甚流涕，朝士咸恐。
entries.en: Former ministers held themselves in check and none dared mourn openly; only Songnian wept freely, and courtiers were uneasy.
entries.literal: The old ministers restrained their bearing; none dared show full grief—only Songnian wept with streaming tears, and the courtiers were all afraid.

entries.zh: 武成雖忿松年戀舊情切，亦雅重之。
entries.en: Though Gao Zhan resented Songnian's loyalty to the late emperor, he still respected him.
entries.literal: Though Gao Zhan resented Songnian's deep attachment to the old reign, he also held him in high esteem.

entries.zh: 以本官加散騎常侍，食高邑縣幹，參定律令，前後大事多委焉。
entries.en: He was additionally made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry with the salary of Gaoyi county, helped compile laws and statutes, and was entrusted with one major affair after another.
entries.literal: In his regular post he was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, granted the salary of Gaoyi county, and took part in compiling laws and statutes; major affairs before and after were largely entrusted to him.

entries.zh: 兼御史中丞。
entries.en: He also served as imperial censor.
entries.literal: He concurrently served as Imperial Censor.

entries.zh: 發晉陽之鄴，在道遇疾卒。
entries.en: Leaving Jinyang for Ye, he fell ill on the road and died.
entries.literal: Setting out from Jinyang for Ye, he fell ill on the road and died.

entries.zh: 贈吏部尚書、幷州刺史，諡曰平。
entries.en: He was posthumously made minister of personnel and inspector of Bing province, with the posthumous name Ping.
entries.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Personnel and inspector of Bing province; his posthumous title was Ping.

entries.zh: 第三子卲，最知名。
entries.en: The third son, Shao, was the most famous.
entries.literal: The third son Shao was the most renowned.

entries.zh: 讞之，字士平，七歲便勤學，早知名。
entries.en: Yanzhi, styled Shiping, was studying hard by age seven and was known early.
entries.literal: Yanzhi, styled Shiping, at seven sui was already diligent in study and early won fame.

entries.zh: 累遷司徒主簿。
entries.en: He rose to chief clerk in the ministry of education.
entries.literal: He rose repeatedly to chief clerk of the Ministry of Education.

entries.zh: 楊愔每稱嘆云：「河東士族，京官不少，唯此家兄弟，全無鄉音。」
entries.en: Yang Yin often praised him, saying, "Hedong has many families with capital officials, but only these brothers speak without a hometown accent."
entries.literal: Yang Yin would often praise him, saying, "Among the gentry clans of Hedong there are many capital officials, but only this household's brothers have no trace of home accent."

entries.zh: 讞之雖年少，不妄交遊，唯與隴西辛術、趙郡李繪、頓丘李構、清河崔瞻為忘年之友。
entries.en: Though still young, Yanzhi did not socialize lightly; only Xin Shu of Longxi, Li Hui of Zhao commandery, Li Gou of Dunqiu, and Cui Zhan of Qinghe were his friends despite the age gap.
entries.literal: Though Yanzhi was still young, he did not make friends lightly; only Longxi Xin Shu, Zhao commandery Li Hui, Dunqiu Li Gou, and Qinghe Cui Zhan were his friends across the years.

entries.zh: 昭帝梓宮將還鄴，轉儀曹郎，尤悉歷代故事、儀註，喪禮皆能裁正。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaozhao's coffin was to return to Ye, he was made gentleman of the rituals bureau; he knew dynastic precedent and ceremonial law especially well and could set right every mourning rite.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao's coffin was about to return to Ye, he was transferred to gentleman of the rituals bureau; he especially knew past dynasties' precedents and ritual regulations, and could correct all mourning rites.

entries.zh: 為永昌太守，客旅過郡，出私財供給，人間無所，預代下出，為吏人所懷。
entries.en: As grand administrator of Yongchang, he paid traveling guests from his own purse when the commandery had nothing on hand, advancing funds for them in advance, and officials and commoners alike were grateful.
entries.literal: As grand administrator of Yongchang, when travelers passed through the commandery he supplied them from private funds; where the district had nothing, he advanced payment on their behalf, and the clerks and people were grateful.

entries.zh: 齊亡仕周，卒伊川太守。
entries.en: After Qi fell he served Zhou and died as grand administrator of Yichuan.
entries.literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou's service and died as grand administrator of Yichuan.

entries.zh: 構從父弟庶，魏大司農諧子。
entries.en: Gou's younger cousin on the father's side was Shu, son of Wei grand minister of agriculture Xie.
entries.literal: Gou's younger cousin by the father's line was Shu; in Wei he was son of the grand minister of agriculture Xie.

entries.zh: 方雅好學，風流規檢，甚有家風。
entries.en: Refined and fond of learning, he kept strict standards of conduct and upheld the family reputation.
entries.literal: Correct and elegant, he loved learning, had refined standards of conduct, and bore a strong family style.

entries.zh: 稍遷臨漳令。
entries.en: He was promoted step by step to magistrate of Linzhang.
entries.literal: He rose gradually to magistrate of Linzhang.

entries.zh: 《魏書》出，庶與盧斐、王松年等訟其不平，並繫獄。
entries.en: When the History of Wei was published, Shu joined Lu Fei, Wang Songnian, and others in suing over its bias and was imprisoned with them.
entries.literal: When the History of Wei appeared, Shu together with Lu Fei, Wang Songnian, and others sued over its unfairness and were all imprisoned.

entries.zh: 魏收書王慧龍自云太原人，又言王瓊不善事；
entries.en: Wei Shou wrote that Wang Huilong claimed to be from Taiyuan and also said Wang Qiong was inept in his duties;
entries.literal: Wei Shou wrote that Wang Huilong called himself a man of Taiyuan, and also said Wang Qiong was poor at serving;

entries.zh: 盧同附《盧玄傳》；
entries.en: Lu Tong was tucked into the biography of Lu Xuan;
entries.literal: Lu Tong was attached to the biography of Lu Xuan;

entries.zh: 李平為陳留人，云其家貧賤。
entries.en: Li Ping was called a man of Chenliu and described as coming from a poor, humble house.
entries.literal: Li Ping was made a man of Chenliu, saying his family was poor and base.

entries.zh: 故裴等致訟，語楊愔云：「魏收合誅。」
entries.en: Hence the Pei party and others brought suit, telling Yang Yin, "Wei Shou deserves execution."
entries.literal: Therefore the Pei clan and others brought the suit, saying to Yang Yin, "Wei Shou ought to be put to death."

entries.zh: 愔黨助魏收，遂白顯祖罪斐等，並髡頭，鞭二百。
entries.en: Yin took Wei Shou's side; they then denounced Fei and the rest to Gao Yang, and all were shaved and flogged two hundred strokes.
entries.literal: Yin sided with Wei Shou; they thereupon reported to Gao Yang that Fei and the others were guilty, and all were shaved and given two hundred lashes.

entries.zh: 庶死於臨漳獄中，庶兄岳痛之，終身不歷臨漳縣門。
entries.en: Shu died in Linzhang jail; his elder brother Yue mourned him so deeply that he never again went through Linzhang's gate while he lived.
entries.literal: Shu died in Linzhang prison; Shu's elder brother Yue grieved for him and to the end of his life never passed Linzhang's county gate.

entries.zh: 張宴之，字熙德。
entries.en: Zhang Yanzhi, styled Xide.
entries.literal: Zhang Yanzhi, styled Xide.

entries.zh: 幼孤有至性，為母鄭氏教誨，動依禮典。
entries.en: Orphaned young, he was deeply dutiful; his mother Lady Zheng raised him by the rites, and he followed them in everything.
entries.literal: Orphaned young, he had utmost nature; his mother the Lady Zheng taught and admonished him, and in action he always followed the ritual canon.

entries.zh: 從尒朱榮平元顥，賜爵武成子，累遷尚書二千石郎中。
entries.en: He followed Erzhu Rong in defeating Yuan Hao, was enfeoffed baron of Wucheng, and rose to gentleman of the two-thousand-dan rank in the masters of writing.
entries.literal: He followed Erzhu Rong in pacifying Yuan Hao, was given the enfeoffment Baron of Wucheng, and rose repeatedly to gentleman of the two-thousand-dan rank in the masters of writing.

entries.zh: 高岳征潁川，復以為都督中兵參軍兼記室。
entries.en: When Gao Yue campaigned in Yingchuan, he again appointed Yanzhi commanding aide of central troops with concurrent recorder.
entries.literal: When Gao Yue campaigned in Yingchuan, he again made Yanzhi commanding aide of central troops with concurrent recorder.

entries.zh: 宴之文士，兼有武幹，每與岳帷帳之謀，又常以短兵接刃，親獲首級，深為岳所嗟賞。
entries.en: Yanzhi was a literatus with martial skill; he often joined Yue's council in the tent and just as often fought hand to hand with a short blade, taking heads himself—much to Yue's admiration.
entries.literal: Yanzhi was a man of letters who also had martial ability; he often joined Yue in planning within the curtains, and also often took short weapons to clash at close quarters, personally taking heads—deeply admired by Yue.

entries.zh: 天保初，文宣為高陽王納宴之女為妃，令赴晉陽成禮。
entries.en: At the start of Tianbao, Gao Yang as Prince of Gaoyang married Yanzhi's daughter and ordered him to Jinyang to finish the wedding.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, Gao Yang as Prince of Gaoyang took Yanzhi's daughter as consort and ordered Yanzhi to go to Jinyang to complete the rites.

entries.zh: 宴之後園陪宴，坐客皆賦詩。
entries.en: Later, at a feast in the rear garden, every guest was asked to compose a poem.
entries.literal: Afterward in the rear garden he attended a feast; seated guests all composed poetry.

entries.zh: 宴之詩云：「天下有道，主明臣直，雖休勿休，永貽世則。」
entries.en: Yanzhi's poem ran, "When the Way holds the realm, the ruler is bright and his ministers straight; though all is calm, do not grow calm—leave the age a lasting model."
entries.literal: Yanzhi's poem said, "When the realm has the Way, the lord is bright and ministers upright; though there is rest, do not rest—forever leave a model to the age."

entries.zh: 文宣笑曰：「得卿箴諷，深以慰懷。」
entries.en: Gao Yang laughed and said, "Your verse of counsel comforts me deeply."
entries.literal: Gao Yang laughed and said, "To gain your admonition in verse deeply comforts my heart."

entries.zh: 後行北徐州事，尋卽真，為吏人所愛。
entries.en: He later administered North Xu province, soon received the regular appointment, and was beloved by officials and people.
entries.literal: Later he acted for North Xu province and soon received the full appointment; officials and people loved him.

entries.zh: 御史崔子武督察州郡，至北徐州，無所案劾，唯得百姓所制《清德頌》數篇。
entries.en: Censor Cui Ziwu inspected provinces and commanderies; at North Xu he found no charges to bring, only several "Hymns of Pure Virtue" written by the people.
entries.literal: Censor Cui Ziwu inspected the provinces and commanderies; reaching North Xu he found nothing to impeach, only several pieces of "Pure Virtue Praise" composed by the common people.

entries.zh: 乃歎曰：「本求罪狀，遂聞頌聲。」
entries.en: He sighed, "I came looking for offenses and instead heard praise."
entries.literal: He thereupon sighed and said, "I came seeking crimes and instead heard songs of praise."

entries.zh: 遷兗州刺史，未拜，卒。
entries.en: He was transferred to inspector of Yan but died before assuming the post.
entries.literal: He was transferred to inspector of Yan province; before he could take up the post he died.

entries.zh: 贈齊州刺史。
entries.en: He was posthumously made inspector of Qi province.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given inspector of Qi province.

entries.zh: 裴讓之 弟諏之 讞之 皇甫和 李構 張宴之 陸卬 王松年 劉禕
entries.en: Pei Rangzhi; younger brothers Souzhi and Yanzhi; Huangfu He; Li Gou; Zhang Yanzhi; Lu Ang; Wang Songnian; Liu Yi
entries.literal: Pei Rangzhi; younger brothers Souzhi and Yanzhi; Huangfu He; Li Gou; Zhang Yanzhi; Lu Ang; Wang Songnian; Liu Yi

entries.zh: 釋巾為魏宣武挽郎，除奉朝請，遷著作佐郎。
entries.en: Leaving mourning, he served as a Wei mourning officer for Emperor Xuanwu, was made gentleman attendant at court, and rose to assistant editorial director.
entries.literal: He doffed mourning and became a Wei mourning officer for Emperor Xuanwu, was appointed gentleman attendant at court, and was promoted Assistant Editorial Director.

entries.zh: 深為領軍元叉所禮，叉新除尚書令，神儁與陳郡袁翻在席，叉令卲作謝表，須臾便成，以示諸賓。
entries.en: The commander of the guards Yuan Cha treated him with great respect; when Cha had just become director of the masters of writing, Shenjun and Yuan Fan of Chen were present, and Cha had Shao write a letter of thanks—it was finished at once and shown round.
entries.literal: He was deeply honored by the commander of the guards Yuan Cha; when Cha had just been appointed Director of the Masters of Writing, Shenjun and Yuan Fan of Chen commandery were at the feast, and Cha had Shao draft a letter of thanks—in a moment it was done, and shown to the guests.

entries.zh: 神儁曰：「邢卲此表，足使袁公變色。」
entries.en: Shenjun said, "This table from Xing Shao alone would make Master Yuan flush."
entries.literal: Shenjun said: "This memorial of Xing Shao's is enough to make Master Yuan change color."

entries.zh: 孝昌初，與黃門侍郎李琰之對典朝儀。
entries.en: At the opening of Xiaochang he and yellow gate attendant Li Yanzhi jointly directed court ceremonial.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang he and Yellow Gate Attendant Li Yanzhi jointly oversaw court ritual.

entries.zh: 自孝明之後，文雅大盛，卲雕蟲之美，獨步當時，每一文初出，京師為之紙貴，讀誦俄遍遠近。
entries.en: After Emperor Xiaoming of Wei, literary culture flourished; Shao's ornamental prose stood alone—each new piece made paper dear in the capital, and within moments it was read and recited across the realm.
entries.literal: After Emperor Xiaoming, letters flourished greatly; Shao's ornamental beauty in writing stood alone in his age—whenever a piece first appeared, the capital ran short of paper for it, and within moments it was read and chanted near and far.

entries.zh: 于時袁翻與范陽祖瑩位望通顯，文筆之美，見稱先達，以卲藻思華贍，深共嫉之。
entries.en: Yuan Fan and Zu Ying of Fanyang were then eminent in office and fame, their writing praised by seniors; Shao's lush brilliance they jointly resented.
entries.literal: At the time Yuan Fan and Zu Ying of Fanyang, lofty in rank and repute, were praised by elders for the beauty of their brush; seeing Shao's florid, brilliant thought, they deeply envied him together.

entries.zh: 每洛中貴人拜職，多憑卲為謝表。
entries.en: Whenever a Luoyang grandee assumed a new post, he usually had Shao draft the letter of thanks.
entries.literal: Whenever a noble in Luoyang took a new post, he mostly relied on Shao for the letter of thanks.

entries.zh: 嘗有一貴勝初受官，大集賓食，翻與卲俱在坐。
entries.en: Once a powerful man had just received appointment and held a great banquet; Fan and Shao were both present.
entries.literal: Once a powerful man had just received office and gave a great feast for guests; Fan and Shao were both seated.

entries.zh: 翻意主人托其為讓表，遂命卲作之。
entries.en: Fan assumed the host meant him to write the declination and ordered Shao to do it instead.
entries.literal: Fan supposed the host had entrusted him with the declination memorial and thereupon ordered Shao to write it.

entries.zh: 翻甚不悅，每告人云：「邢家小兒當客作章表，自買黃紙，寫而送之。」
entries.en: Fan was deeply displeased and often said, "That Xing boy ought to write his own memorials as a guest—buy his own yellow paper, draft it, and submit it himself."
entries.literal: Fan was very displeased and often told others: "The Xing boy should, when a guest, compose his own memorials—buy his own yellow paper, write it, and send it in."

entries.zh: 卲恐為翻所害，乃辭以疾。
entries.en: Shao feared Fan would injure him and pleaded illness.
entries.literal: Shao feared harm from Fan and pleaded illness.

entries.zh: 屬尚書令元羅出鎮青州，啟為府司馬。
entries.en: When director of the masters of writing Yuan Luo took command of Qing province, he had Shao appointed headquarters staff secretary.
entries.literal: When Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo went out to command Qing province, he recommended Shao as staff secretary of the headquarters.

entries.zh: 遂在青土，終日酣賞，盡山泉之致。
entries.en: He stayed in the east, feasting and savoring all day, draining every delight of hill and stream.
entries.literal: He remained in the eastern lands, drinking and enjoying himself all day, exhausting the charm of mountains and springs.

entries.zh: 世室明堂，顯於周、夏；
entries.en: The Ancestral Chamber and Bright Hall shone forth under Zhou and Xia;
entries.literal: The Ancestral Chamber and Bright Hall were illustrious in Zhou and Xia;

entries.zh: 一黌兩學，盛自虞、殷。
entries.en: a single academy and paired schools flourished from Yu and Yin.
entries.literal: one academy and two schools flourished from the time of Yu and Yin.

entries.zh: 所以宗配上帝，以著莫大之嚴；
entries.en: By them the realm sacrificed to the Lord on High and showed the greatest solemnity;
entries.literal: Thereby to sacrifice to the Lord on High and display the utmost majesty;

entries.zh: 宣布下土，以彰則天之軌。
entries.en: they proclaimed to the four quarters and embodied Heaven's model of rule.
entries.literal: to proclaim across the lower realm and manifest the pattern of matching Heaven.

entries.zh: 養黃發以詢哲言，育青衿而敷教典，用能享國長久，風徽萬祀者也。
entries.en: They nourished gray hair to seek wisdom and reared blue collars to spread the teaching canon—thus realms endured and their fame lasted ten thousand generations.
entries.literal: To nourish white-haired elders in seeking wise words, to rear blue-collared youths in spreading the teaching canon—thereby states enjoyed long endurance and their emblems through ten thousand sacrifices.

entries.zh: 爰暨亡秦，改革其道，坑儒滅學，以蔽黔黎。
entries.en: Then Qin fell, altered the Way, buried scholars and ended learning, and darkened the common folk.
entries.literal: When it reached the fallen Qin, it reformed their Way, buried the ru and extinguished learning, to blind the black-haired people.

entries.zh: 故九服分崩，祚終二代。
entries.en: The nine domains shattered and the throne passed after only two generations.
entries.literal: Hence the nine domains split apart and the mandate ended after two generations.

entries.zh: 炎漢勃興，更修儒術。
entries.en: Han rose in flame and again restored Confucian learning.
entries.literal: The blazing Han rose vigorously and again repaired ru learning.

entries.zh: 故西京有六學之義，東都有三本之盛。
entries.en: In the western capital stood the six schools; in the eastern capital the glory of three academies.
entries.literal: Hence in the Western Capital were the meaning of six schools; in the Eastern Capital the splendor of three academies.

entries.zh: 逮自魏、晉，撥亂相因，兵革之中，學校不絕。
entries.en: From Wei and Jin onward, rebellion followed rebellion, yet amid war the schools never ceased.
entries.literal: Down through Wei and Jin, in turmoil one after another, amid arms and armor the schools did not perish.

entries.zh: 仰惟高祖孝文皇帝稟聖自天，道鏡今古，列校序於鄉黨，敦詩書於郡國。
entries.en: We look up to Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, the High Ancestor, who received the sage from Heaven and whose Way reflects all ages—he ordered schools in the hamlets and spread the Odes and Documents through every commandery.
entries.literal: Looking up, Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, the High Ancestor, received the sage from Heaven; his Way mirrors present and past; he arrayed schools in the districts and thickly spread the Odes and Documents through the commanderies.

entries.zh: 但經始事殷，戎軒屢駕，未遑多就，弓劍弗追。
entries.en: Yet the founding work pressed hard and the war chariot rode out again and again; he had no leisure to finish—bow and sword were left behind.
entries.literal: But the founding enterprise was pressing, the martial chariot was repeatedly driven forth; there was no leisure to accomplish much—the bow and sword could not be followed up.

entries.zh: 世宗統歷，聿遵先緒，永平之中，大興板築。
entries.en: Emperor Shizong of Wei took up the former thread; in Yongping he launched great construction.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong of Wei continued the former thread; in Yongping he greatly raised timber and earthworks.

entries.zh: 續以水旱，戎馬生郊，雖逮為山，還停一簣。
entries.en: Then flood and drought came, war-horses at the suburbs; though the mound was nearly made, one basket of earth remained undone.
entries.literal: Then came flood and drought, war-horses at the suburbs; though the mountain was nearly heaped, one basket of earth still halted.

entries.zh: 而明堂禮樂之本，乃鬱荊棘之林；
entries.en: The root of rites and music, the Bright Hall, became a tangle of thorns;
entries.literal: Yet the root of Bright Hall, rites and music, became a thicket of brambles and thorns;

entries.zh: 膠序德義之基，空盈牧豎之跡；
entries.en: the school halls, foundation of virtue and duty, stood empty but for herd-boys' footprints;
entries.literal: the foundation of virtue and righteousness in the school halls stood empty, filled only with the tracks of herd-boys;

entries.zh: 城隍嚴固之重，闕磚石之功；
entries.en: the ramparts, weight of defense, lacked brick and stone;
entries.literal: the weight of stern ramparts and walls lacked the work of brick and stone;

entries.zh: 墉構顯望之要，少樓榭之飾。
entries.en: the lofty terraces that display imperial majesty had scarcely tower or pavilion.
entries.literal: the essentials of lofty terraces and structures had little adornment of towers and pavilions.

entries.zh: 加以風雨稍侵，漸致虧墜。
entries.en: Wind and rain wore at them until they crumbled.
entries.literal: Added to this, wind and rain gradually encroached, and bit by bit they fell into ruin.

entries.zh: 非所謂追隆堂構，儀刑萬國者也。
entries.en: This is not to pursue a lofty hall nor to make ritual the model for ten thousand states.
entries.literal: This is not what is called pursuing the loftiness of the hall's frame and taking the rites as model for ten thousand states.

entries.zh: 伏聞朝議以高祖大造區夏，道侔姬文，提記明堂，式配上帝。
entries.en: We hear the court argues that because the High Ancestor shaped the realm within the four seas and his Way matched King Wen of Zhou, he raised the Bright Hall to sacrifice to the Lord on High.
entries.literal: We have heard that court discussion, because the High Ancestor greatly fashioned the realm within the four seas and his Way matched King Wen of Zhou, raised the record of the Bright Hall to match the Lord on High.

entries.zh: 今若基址不修，乃同丘畎，即使高皇神享，闕於國陽，宗事之典，有聲無實。
entries.en: If the foundations are not restored, it is but a mound in a field—even the High Emperor's spirit lacks its seat in the national altar; ancestral rite has sound without substance.
entries.literal: If now the foundation is not repaired, it is the same as a hillock in a field; even if the High Emperor's spirit is offered to, it is lacking at the national yang; the canon of ancestral service has sound without substance.

entries.zh: 此臣子所以匪寧，億兆所以佇望也。
entries.en: Hence ministers cannot rest and the people wait in hope.
entries.literal: This is why ministers and sons are uneasy and the hundred millions stand waiting.

entries.zh: 永安初，累遷中書侍郎，所作詔誥，文體宏麗。
entries.en: At the beginning of Yong'an he rose repeatedly to secretariat attendant; his edicts and pronouncements were magnificent in diction.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was promoted repeatedly to Secretariat Attendant; the edicts and pronouncements he drafted were grand and beautiful in style.

entries.zh: 及尒朱榮入洛，京師擾亂，卲與弘農楊愔避地嵩高山。
entries.en: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and the capital fell into chaos, Shao and Yang Yin of Hongnong fled to Mount Song.
entries.literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang the capital was in turmoil; Shao and Yang Yin of Hongnong took refuge on Mount Song.

entries.zh: 普泰中，兼給事黃門侍郎，尋為散騎常侍。
entries.en: In Putai he was made concurrent attendant of the yellow gate in the secretariat, then regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: In Putai he was concurrently Attendant of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat; soon after he became Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 太昌初，勑令恒直內省，給御食，令覆按尚書門下事，凡除大官，先問其可否，然後施行。
entries.en: At the beginning of Taichang he was ordered to keep constant watch in the inner court, supplied with imperial food, and told to review business of the masters of writing and secretariat; major appointments were first referred to him for approval.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was ordered to remain constantly on duty in the inner court, given imperial meals, and charged to review affairs of the Masters of Writing and the Secretariat; for every great appointment he was first asked whether it was permissible, and only then was it carried out.

entries.zh: 除衛將軍、國子祭酒。
entries.en: He was made general of the guards and grand master of the imperial academy.
entries.literal: He was appointed General of the Guards and Grand Master of the Imperial Academy.

entries.zh: 以親老還鄉，詔所在特給兵力五人，並令歲一入朝，以備顧問。
entries.en: When his parents grew old he went home; the throne ordered his district to assign him five guards and to let him attend court once a year for consultation.
entries.literal: Because his parents were aged he returned home; an edict ordered the locality to grant him especially five soldiers of force, and also to enter court once a year as adviser.

entries.zh: 丁母憂，哀毀過禮。
entries.en: Mourning his mother, he grieved beyond what the rites prescribed.
entries.literal: On observing mourning for his mother his grief exceeded the rites.

entries.zh: 論曰：子才少有盛名，鼓動京洛，文宗學府，獨秀當年，舉必任真，情無飾智，疏通簡易，罕見其人，足為一代之模楷也。
entries.en: The appraisal says: Zicai enjoyed a great reputation from youth and stirred the capital and Luoyang. As a master of letters and a repository of learning, he stood alone in his time. His actions were always genuine, his feelings free of clever display; open, accessible, and simple, he was rare indeed and could serve as a model for a generation.
entries.literal: The appraisal says: Zicai had a great reputation from youth and stirred the capital and Luoyang. As a master of letters and repository of learning, he alone shone in his time. In action he always followed genuineness, and in feeling he did not embellish his intelligence. Open, accessible, and simple, such a man was rarely seen and was enough to be a model for a generation.

entries.zh: 及明崔甗之謗言，執侯景之奸使，昔人稱孟軻為勇，于文簡公見之。
entries.en: When he exposed Cui Yan's slander and seized Hou Jing's treacherous envoy, one can see in Duke Wenjian the courage that earlier men praised in Meng Ke.
entries.literal: When he exposed Cui Yan's slanderous words and seized Hou Jing's treacherous envoy, what men of old called Meng Ke's courage can be seen in Duke Wenjian.

entries.zh: 唯嘗短崔暹，頗為累德。
entries.en: Only his past disparagement of Cui Xian somewhat blemished his virtue.
entries.literal: Only, he once disparaged Cui Xian, and this rather blemished his virtue.

entries.zh: 阮籍未嘗品藻人物，斯亦良有以焉。
entries.en: Ruan Ji never passed judgment on people, and there was good reason for that.
entries.literal: Ruan Ji never appraised people; this too had good reason.

entries.zh: 邢卲，字子才，河間鄚人，魏太常貞之後。
entries.en: Biography of Xing Shao. Xing Shao, styled Zicai, was from Mo in Hejian commandery; he descended from Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhen of Wei.
entries.literal: Xing Shao, styled Zicai, a man of Mo in Hejian, descendant of Wei Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhen.

entries.zh: 父虬，魏光祿卿。
entries.en: His father Xing Qiu had served Wei as director of the imperial household.
entries.literal: His father Qiu was Wei Director of the Imperial Household.

entries.zh: 卲小字吉，少時有避，遂不行名。
entries.en: Shao's childhood name was Ji; while young he observed a naming taboo and did not use his formal name.
entries.literal: Shao's childhood name was Ji; in youth there was a taboo, and so he did not use his formal name.

entries.zh: 年五歲，魏吏部郎清河崔亮見而奇之，曰：「此子後當大成，位望通顯。」
entries.en: At five, Cui Liang of Qinghe, a lang in the Wei ministry of personnel, saw him and marveled, saying, "This child will one day achieve great things; office and fame will spread far and wide."
entries.literal: At age five, Cui Liang of Qinghe, Lang of the Ministry of Personnel in Wei, saw him and was struck, saying: "This boy will in time achieve great things; rank and repute will be universally manifest."

entries.zh: 十歲便能屬文，雅有才思，聰明強記，日誦萬餘言。
entries.en: By ten he could write compositions; gifted and inventive, sharp-witted and retentive, he recited more than ten thousand words each day.
entries.literal: At ten he could compose in writing; elegant in talent and thought, clever and with a strong memory, he recited more than ten thousand words a day.

entries.zh: 族兄巒，有人倫鑒，謂子弟曰：「宗室中有此兒，非常人也。」
entries.en: His kinsman Luan, skilled at judging men, told the younger generation, "Our house has produced this boy—he is no ordinary person."
entries.literal: His clansman Luan, who had judgment of human character, told the younger kin: "In our lineage there is this boy—a man not of the common sort."

entries.zh: 少在洛陽，會天下無事，與時名勝專以山水遊宴為娛，不暇勤業。
entries.en: While young in Luoyang, the empire was quiet; with celebrated contemporaries he gave himself only to landscape outings and banquets, leaving no time for steady application.
entries.literal: In youth he was in Luoyang; the realm was at peace, and with the day's eminent men he devoted himself solely to touring mountains and waters and feasting for pleasure, with no leisure for diligent study.

entries.zh: 嘗因霖雨，乃讀《漢書》，五日，略能遍記之。
entries.en: Once, during long rains, he took up the History of Han and within five days could recall most of it.
entries.literal: Once during prolonged rain he read the History of Han; in five days he could largely remember it through.

entries.zh: 後因飲謔倦，方廣尋經史，五行俱下，一覽便記，無所遺忘。
entries.en: Later, tired of drink and banter, he turned widely to the classics and histories; reading five lines at a glance, he retained each passage at once.
entries.literal: Later, wearied of drinking and jesting, he broadly sought out the classics and histories; with five lines at once under his eye, one reading and he remembered—nothing was lost.

entries.zh: 文章典麗，既贍且速。
entries.en: His writing was elegant and polished, copious yet quick.
entries.literal: His compositions were classical and beautiful, ample yet swift.

entries.zh: 年未二十，名動衣冠。
entries.en: Before twenty his reputation had shaken the official class.
entries.literal: Before he was twenty his name stirred the gentry.

entries.zh: 嘗與右北平陽固、河東裴伯茂、從兄罘、河南陸道暉等至北海王昕舍宿飲，相與賦詩，凡數十首，皆在主人奴處。
entries.en: Once he stayed overnight drinking at Prince Xin of Beihai's residence with Yang Gu of Youbeiping, Pei Bomo of Hedong, his paternal cousin Fei, and Lu Daohui of Henan; they composed several dozen poems together, all left with the host's servant.
entries.literal: He once lodged and drank overnight at the house of the Prince of Beihai, Xin, with Youbeiping Yang Gu, Hedong Pei Bomo, his cousin from the father's line Fei, and Henan Lu Daohui; together they composed poems, several dozen in all, and all were left with the host's servant.

entries.zh: 旦日奴行，諸人求詩不得，卲皆為誦之。
entries.en: At dawn the servant went abroad; the others could not find their poems, but Shao recited them all.
entries.literal: Next morning the servant went out; the others could not recover their poems, but Shao recited every one from memory.

entries.zh: 諸人有不認詩者，奴還得本，不誤一字。
entries.en: Some did not recognize their own work; when the servant brought back the originals, not one character differed.
entries.literal: Some among them did not recognize their own poems; when the servant returned with the originals, not a single character was wrong.

entries.zh: 諸人方之王粲。
entries.en: The company then compared him to Wang Can.
entries.literal: The company thereupon ranked him with Wang Can.

entries.zh: 吏部尚書隴西李神儁大相欽重，引為忘年之交。
entries.en: Li Shenjun of Longxi, minister of personnel, held him in high regard and took him as a friend despite the age gap.
entries.literal: Li Shenjun of Longxi, Minister of Personnel, greatly esteemed him and made him a friend across the years.

entries.zh: 所引史官，恐其淩逼，唯取學流先相依附者。
entries.en: Among the historians he enlisted, fearing they might crowd him, he took only scholars of his own circle who had long attached themselves to him.
entries.literal: Of the historians he cited, fearing they might press upon him, he took only those of the scholarly current who had long relied on him.

entries.zh: 房延佑、辛元植、眭仲讓雖夙涉朝位，並非史才。
entries.en: Fang Yanyou, Xin Yuanzhi, and Sui Zhongrang had long held court posts, yet none had a gift for history.
entries.literal: Fang Yanyou, Xin Yuanzhi, and Sui Zhongrang, though long involved in court posts, were none of them talents for history.

entries.zh: 刁柔、裴昂之以儒業見知，全不堪編緝。
entries.en: Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi were known for Confucian learning and were wholly unfit for compilation.
entries.literal: Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi were known for Confucian learning and were wholly unfit to compile and edit.

entries.zh: 高孝幹以左道求進。
entries.en: Gao Xiaogan sought advancement through heterodox arts.
entries.literal: Gao Xiaogan sought advancement through heterodox arts.

entries.zh: 修史諸人祖宗姻戚多被書錄，飾以美言。
entries.en: The ancestors and affines of those who revised the history were for the most part written up and dressed in fine words.
entries.literal: The ancestors and affines of the men who revised the history were for the most part entered in the record and adorned with fine words.

entries.zh: 收性頗急，不甚能平，夙有怨者，多沒其善。
entries.en: Shou was quick-tempered and not very even-handed; those who had long borne him grudges found much of their merit omitted.
entries.literal: Shou's nature was rather quick-tempered and not very even-handed; those who had long borne grudges against him had much of their good left out.

entries.zh: 每言：「何物小子，敢共魏收作色！
entries.en: He would often say, "What sort of stripling dares stand up to Wei Shou!
entries.literal: He would often say, "What sort of stripling dares show color to Wei Shou!

entries.zh: 舉之則使上天，按之當使入地。」
entries.en: Lift him and he goes to heaven; press him down and he goes into the earth."
entries.literal: Lift him and he goes to heaven; press him down and he goes into the earth."

entries.zh: 初，收在神武時為太常少卿，修國史，得陽休之助，因謝休之曰：「無以謝德，當為卿作佳傳。」
entries.en: In Gao Huan's day, when Shou was vice director of the imperial clan and revised the national history, Yang Xiuzhi helped him; Shou thanked Xiuzhi, saying, "I have no other way to repay you than to write you a fine biography."
entries.literal: When Shou was in Gao Huan's time Vice Director of the Imperial Clan and revised the national history, he received Yang Xiuzhi's help and therefore thanked Xiuzhi, saying, "I have no other way to repay your kindness than to write you a fine biography."

entries.zh: 休之父固，魏世為北平太守，以貪虐為中尉李平所彈獲罪，載在《魏起居註》。
entries.en: Xiuzhi's father Gu had been governor of Beiping in Wei and, for greed and cruelty, was impeached and punished by chief commandant of justice Li Ping, as recorded in the Wei Daily Records.
entries.literal: Xiuzhi's father Gu in Wei times had been governor of Beiping and, for greed and cruelty, was impeached and punished by Chief Commandant of Justice Li Ping, as recorded in the Wei Daily Records.

entries.zh: 收書云：「固為北平，甚有惠政，坐公事免官。」
entries.en: In Shou's book it says, "Gu governed Beiping with great benevolent rule and was removed from office over a public matter."
entries.literal: In Shou's book it says, "Gu governed Beiping with great benevolent rule and was removed from office for a public matter."

entries.zh: 又云：「李平深相敬重。」
entries.en: It also says, "Li Ping deeply respected him."
entries.literal: It also says, "Li Ping deeply respected him."

entries.zh: 尒朱榮於魏為賊，收以高氏出自尒朱，且納榮子金，故減其惡而增其善，論云：「若修德義之風，則韓、彭、伊、霍，夫何足數。」
