entries.en: Erzhu Rong was a rebel against Wei; because the Gao house sprang from the Erzhu line and Shou had also taken gold from Rong's son, he softened Rong's crimes and magnified his virtues, writing in a disquisition, "If one cultivates virtue and righteousness, then Han Xin, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang—how are they worth counting?"
entries.literal: Erzhu Rong was a rebel against Wei; because the Gao clan sprang from the Erzhu line and Shou moreover accepted gold from Rong's son, he reduced Rong's evil and increased his good, writing in a disquisition, "If one cultivates the wind of virtue and righteousness, then Han Xin, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang—what are they worth counting?"

entries.zh: 魏收，字伯起，小字佛助，鉅鹿下曲陽人也。
entries.en: Biography of Wei Shou. Wei Shou, styled Bowei, childhood name Fozhu, was from Xiaquyang in Julu commandery.
entries.literal: Wei Shou, styled Bowei, childhood name Fozhu, a man of Xiaquyang in Julu.

entries.zh: 曾祖緝，祖韶。
entries.en: His great-grandfather was Ji; his grandfather was Shao.
entries.literal: Great-grandfather Ji, grandfather Shao.

entries.zh: 父子建，字敬忠，贈儀同、定州刺史。
entries.en: His father Wei Zijian, styled Jingzhong, was posthumously made pillar of the state and governor of Dingzhou.
entries.literal: Father Zijian, styled Jingzhong, posthumously granted Pillar of the State and Governor of Dingzhou.

entries.zh: 收年十五，頗已屬文。
entries.en: At fifteen Shou could already write compositions.
entries.literal: Shou at age fifteen could already compose in writing.

entries.zh: 及隨父赴邊，好習騎射，欲以武藝自達。
entries.en: When he followed his father to the frontier, he took to riding and archery, hoping to make his name by martial arts.
entries.literal: When he followed his father to the frontier, he delighted in practicing mounted archery, wishing to distinguish himself through martial skill.

entries.zh: 滎陽鄭伯調之曰：「魏郎弄戟多少？」
entries.en: Zheng Bo of Xingyang jested, "Young Wei, how fond are you of waving halberds?"
entries.literal: Zheng Bo of Xingyang teased him, saying: "Young Wei, how much do you play with halberds?"

entries.zh: 收慚，遂折節讀書。
entries.en: Ashamed, Shou bent his will to books.
entries.literal: Shou was ashamed and thereupon bent his will to study books.

entries.zh: 夏月坐板床，隨樹陰諷誦，積年，板床為之銳減，而精力不輟。
entries.en: In summer he sat on a plank bed and chanted as he moved with the shade; over the years the bed wore thin at the edges, yet his vigor never flagged.
entries.literal: In summer months he sat on a plank bed, chanting along with the tree shade; year after year the plank bed was worn sharp by it, yet his energy did not slacken.

entries.zh: 以文華顯。
entries.en: He won fame through literary brilliance.
entries.literal: He became renowned through literary brilliance.

entries.zh: 辛術，字懷哲，少明敏，有識度。
entries.en: Xin Shu, styled Huaizhe, was clever and perceptive from boyhood, with a steady sense of what mattered.
entries.literal: Xin Shu, styled Huaizhe, from youth was bright and keen, with judgment and discernment.

entries.zh: 解褐司空胄曹參軍，與僕射高隆之共典營構鄴都宮室，術有思理，百工克濟。
entries.en: His first appointment was staff member in the registrar's office of the directorate of works; with vice director Gao Longzhi he directed the building of Ye's palaces. Shu planned well, and every trade met its mark.
entries.literal: Upon first office he was Staff Member in the Registrar's Office of the Directorate of Works; together with Vice Director Gao Longzhi he oversaw the construction of Ye's palaces—Shu had thoughtful designs, and all the crafts were brought to completion.

entries.zh: 再遷尚書右丞。
entries.en: He was promoted again to right vice director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: He was promoted again to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 出為清河太守，政有能名。
entries.en: Sent out as administrator of Qinghe, he earned a name for capable rule.
entries.literal: Sent out as Administrator of Qinghe; his governance won a reputation for ability.

entries.zh: 追授幷州長史，遭父憂去職。
entries.en: He was retroactively made chief clerk of Bing province, then left office to mourn his father.
entries.literal: Retroactively appointed Chief Clerk of Bing province; he left office on father's mourning.

entries.zh: 清河父老數百人詣闕請立碑頌德。
entries.en: Several hundred Qinghe elders went to court to ask that a stele be raised in praise of his virtue.
entries.literal: Several hundred elders of Qinghe went to the capital to request a stele praising his virtue.

entries.zh: 文襄嗣事，與尚書左丞宋遊道、中書侍郎李繪等並追詣晉陽，俱為上客。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng assumed power, he went with left vice director Song Youdao, secretariat attendant Li Hui, and others to Jinyang and was received as an honored guest.
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng took up the succession, together with Left Vice Director Song Youdao, Secretariat Attendant Li Hui, and others he hurried to Jinyang; all became honored guests.

entries.zh: 累遷散騎常侍。
entries.en: He rose through repeated promotions to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 遷鄴以後，大選之職，知名者數四，互有得失，未能盡美。
entries.en: After the court moved to Ye, four famous men held the great selection office in turn; each had strengths and flaws, and none achieved perfection.
entries.literal: After the move to Ye, the great selection posts had four well-known holders, each with gain and loss, none attaining perfection.

entries.zh: 文襄帝少年高朗，所弊者疏；
entries.en: Gao Cheng in his youth was bright and open; his fault was looseness.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng in his youth was lofty and clear; what harmed him was laxity.

entries.zh: 袁叔德沉密謹厚，所傷者細；
entries.en: Yuan Shude was grave, careful, and thorough; his fault was excessive detail.
entries.literal: Yuan Shude was deep, close, and cautious; what harmed him was minuteness.

entries.zh: 楊愔風流辨給，取士失於浮華。
entries.en: Yang Yin was eloquent and quick; in choosing men he favored show over substance.
entries.literal: Yang Yin was polished and quick in debate; in selecting men he erred toward flashiness.

entries.zh: 唯術性尚貞明，取士以才器，循名責實，新舊參舉，管庫必擢，門閥不遺。
entries.en: Only Shu, upright by nature, chose by talent and office, matched names to reality, mixed veterans and newcomers, promoted men from the storehouses, and did not overlook great families.
entries.literal: Only Shu, by nature upright and clear, chose men by talent and capacity, held names to facts, mixed old and new in nomination, must promote from storehouses, and did not leave out noble houses.

entries.zh: 考之前後銓衡，在術最為折衷，甚為當時所稱舉。
entries.en: Comparing earlier and later rounds of selection, Shu's was the most even-handed, and his age praised him highly.
entries.literal: Reviewing selection before and after, Shu's was most balanced, and was greatly praised by the age.

entries.zh: 天保末，文宣嘗令術選百員官，參選者二三千人，術題目士子，人無謗讟，其所旌擢，後亦皆致通顯。
entries.en: Late in Tianbao, Gao Yang once ordered Shu to choose a hundred officials from two or three thousand candidates. Shu tested the scholars; no one murmured against him, and those he advanced later all rose to high rank.
entries.literal: Late in Tianbao, Gao Yang once had Shu select a hundred officials; those who competed numbered two or three thousand; Shu examined the scholars; none slandered; those he honored and promoted later all attained high prominence.

entries.zh: 初為尚書令司馬子如賤客，供寫書。
entries.en: At first he was a lowly guest of Minister over the Masses Sima Ziru, hired to copy documents.
entries.literal: At first he was a menial guest of Minister over the Masses Sima Ziru, supplying copy work.

entries.zh: 子如善其無誤，欲將入觀省舍。
entries.en: Ziru was pleased that he never erred and meant to bring him inside to see the offices.
entries.literal: Ziru was pleased that he made no mistakes and wanted to bring him in to view the administration quarters.

entries.zh: 隱靴無氊，衣帽穿弊，子如給之。
entries.en: Yin wore unlined boots and threadbare hat and clothes; Ziru furnished him.
entries.literal: Yin wore boots without felt lining, hat and clothes worn and tattered — Ziru supplied him.

entries.zh: 用為書令史，月餘，補正令史。
entries.en: He was made a secretariat clerical officer and, after a month, promoted to regular clerical officer.
entries.literal: He was employed as a clerical officer in the secretariat, and after a month was promoted to regular clerical officer.

entries.zh: 神武在晉陽，索二史，子如舉彥深。
entries.en: Gao Huan was at Jinyang and asked for the two histories; Ziru recommended Yanshen.
entries.literal: Gao Huan was at Jinyang and asked for the two histories; Ziru recommended Yanshen.

entries.zh: 後拜子如開府參軍，超拜水部郎。
entries.en: Later he was made Ziru's metropolitan administration staff officer, then leap-promoted to director of the water section.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed Ziru's metropolitan administration staff officer, and was leap-promoted to director of the water section.

entries.zh: 及文襄為尚書令攝選，沙汰諸曹郎，彥深以地寒被出為滄州別駕，辭不行。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng became Minister over the Masses and took charge of selection, he culled the bureau directors. Yanshen, judged too humble in origin, was sent out as administrator in support of Cangzhou; he declined and would not go.
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng became Minister over the Masses and oversaw selection, he culled the various bureau directors — Yanshen, because of low birth, was dismissed to be Administrator in Support of Cangzhou, and he declined and did not go.

entries.zh: 子如言於神武，徵補大丞相功曹參軍，專掌機密，文翰多出其手，稱為敏給。
entries.en: Ziru spoke to Gao Huan; Yanshen was summoned and made staff officer for merit affairs in the Great Chancellor's office, handling secrets alone. Most papers passed through his hand, and men called him quick and sure.
entries.literal: Ziru spoke to Gao Huan; he was summoned and made staff officer for merit affairs in the Great Chancellor's office, exclusively handling secrets; most documents came from his hand, and he was called quick and responsive.

entries.zh: 神武曾與對坐，遣造軍令，以手捫其額曰：「若天假卿年，必大有所至。」
entries.en: Gao Huan once sat facing him and ordered a military command drafted; he stroked Yanshen's forehead and said, "If Heaven grants you years, you will go far."
entries.literal: Gao Huan once sat facing him and ordered him to draft a military command; he stroked Yanshen's forehead and said: "If Heaven grants you years, you will surely reach great heights."

entries.zh: 每謂司徒孫騰曰：「彥深小心恭慎，曠古絕倫。」
entries.en: He often told Minister over the Masses Sun Teng, "Yanshen is careful and reverent beyond anything in antiquity."
entries.literal: He often told Minister over the Masses Sun Teng: "Yanshen is careful and reverent beyond anything in antiquity."

entries.zh: 及神武崩，秘喪事，文襄慮河南有變，仍自巡撫，乃委彥深後事，轉大行臺都官郎中。
entries.en: When Gao Huan died the mourning was kept secret. Gao Cheng feared trouble in Henan and went to inspect in person, leaving the aftermath to Yanshen and making him metropolitan administration section director.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan died they concealed the mourning; Gao Cheng feared trouble in Henan and went to inspect on his own, entrusting the aftermath to Yanshen and making him metropolitan administration section director.

entries.zh: 臨發，握手泣曰：「以母弟相托，幸得此心。」
entries.en: As he was leaving he clasped Yanshen's hands and wept: "I entrust my mother and younger brother to you — trust that my heart is with you."
entries.literal: When about to depart he clasped hands and wept: "I entrust my mother and younger brother to you — may I have this heart."

entries.zh: 旣而內外寧靜，彥深之力。
entries.en: Inside and outside thereupon grew quiet — Yanshen's doing.
entries.literal: Thereupon inside and outside were quiet — Yanshen's doing.

entries.zh: 及還發喪，深加褒美，乃披郡縣簿為選，封安國縣伯。
entries.en: When he returned to announce the mourning he praised Yanshen at length, opened the commandery-and-county register for selection, and enfeoffed him as baron of Anguo county.
entries.literal: When [Gao Cheng] returned to announce the mourning he praised him greatly, opened the register of commanderies and counties for selections, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Anguo county.

entries.zh: 從征潁川，時引水灌城，城雉將沒，西魏將王思政猶欲死戰。
entries.en: On the Yingchuan campaign they diverted water to flood the city; the battlements would soon go under, yet Western Wei general Wang Sizheng still meant to fight to the death.
entries.literal: On the campaign at Yingchuan they diverted water to flood the city; the battlements would soon be submerged, yet Western Wei general Wang Sizheng still wanted to fight to the death.

entries.zh: 文襄令彥深單身入城告喻，卽日降之，便手牽思政出城。
entries.en: Gao Cheng sent Yanshen into the city alone to persuade them; that same day they surrendered, and he led Sizheng out by the hand.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng ordered Yanshen to enter the city alone to persuade; that same day they surrendered, and he personally led Sizheng out by the hand.

entries.zh: 先是，文襄謂彥深曰：「吾昨夜夢獵，遇一群豕，吾射盡獲之，獨一大豕不可得。
entries.en: Earlier Gao Cheng had told Yanshen, "Last night I dreamed I was hunting and met a herd of swine; I shot and took them all, but one great boar I could not get.
entries.literal: Earlier, Gao Cheng had said to Yanshen: "Last night I dreamed of hunting and met a herd of swine; I shot and took them all, but one great boar I could not get.

entries.zh: 卿言當為吾取，須臾獲豕而進。」
entries.en: You said you would take it for me — and in a moment you had the boar and came in."
entries.literal: You said you would take it for me — in a moment you had the boar and came in."

entries.zh: 至是，文襄笑曰：「夢驗矣。」
entries.en: Now Gao Cheng laughed: "The dream is fulfilled."
entries.literal: At this Gao Cheng laughed: "The dream is fulfilled."

entries.zh: 卽解思政佩刀與彥深曰：「使卿常獲此利。」
entries.en: He then took Sizheng's belt dagger and gave it to Yanshen, saying, "May you always win such profit."
entries.literal: Thereupon he removed Sizheng's belt dagger and gave it to Yanshen, saying: "May you always win such profit."

entries.zh: 起家員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: He began office as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, outside the regular quota.
entries.literal: His first office was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, outside the regular quota.

entries.zh: 遭父喪，服闋，除太尉東閤祭酒。
entries.en: After his father's death and mourning, he was made libationer in the eastern pavilion of the grand marshal.
entries.literal: He suffered father's mourning; when mourning ended, made Libationer in the Eastern Pavilion of the Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 以天下方亂，遂解官侍養，隱於林慮山。
entries.en: With the realm in turmoil, he resigned to care for his mother and lived in seclusion on Mount Linlü.
entries.literal: As the realm was in turmoil, he resigned office to tend his mother and hid on Mount Linlü.

entries.zh: 武定中，文襄徵為大將軍府功曹。
entries.en: In the Wuding era Gao Cheng summoned him as staff officer in the grand general's office.
entries.literal: In Wuding, Gao Cheng summoned him as Staff Officer of the Grand General's government office.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，於登壇所受中書舍人，宣傳文武號令。
entries.en: When Qi received the mandate, at the enthronement altar he was made secretariat drafting officer and proclaimed civil and military orders.
entries.literal: When Qi received the mandate, at the altar of enthronement he received the post of Secretariat Drafting Officer, proclaiming civil and military orders.

entries.zh: 楊遵彥每云：「堪解穰侯印者，必在斯人。」
entries.en: Yang Zunyian often said, "The man who can take the Marquis of Rang's seal must be this one."
entries.literal: Yang Zunyian often said: "He who can take the Marquis of Rang's seal must be this man."

entries.zh: 後忽被中旨幽執，竟不知所由。
entries.en: Later he was suddenly seized on a secret imperial order; in the end no one knew why.
entries.literal: Later he was suddenly imprisoned by secret imperial order, and in the end none knew the reason.

entries.zh: 如此積年。
entries.en: He remained so for many years.
entries.literal: Thus for many years.

entries.zh: 文宣後自幸禁獄，執手愧謝，親解所著金帶及御服賜之，卽日起為尚書祠部郎中。
entries.en: Later Gao Yang himself visited the prison, took his hand in apology, removed his own gold belt and court robes to give him, and that same day made him lang in the sacrificial affairs section of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: Later Gao Yang himself visited the prison, took his hand in ashamed apology, personally removed his gold belt and imperial robes and bestowed them, and that same day raised him to Lang in the Sacrificial Affairs section of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 孝昭攝政，除大丞相府功曹參軍，典機密。
entries.en: When Gao Yan acted as regent, Wenyao was made staff officer in the grand chancellor's office and handled confidential matters.
entries.literal: When Gao Yan acted as regent, appointed Staff Officer in the Grand Chancellor's government office, overseeing secrets.

entries.zh: 及踐祚，除中書侍郎，封永樂縣伯，參軍國大事。
entries.en: When Gao Yan took the throne, Wenyao was made secretariat attendant, enfeoffed as baron of Yongle county, and took part in great affairs of state.
entries.literal: When he ascended the throne, made Secretariat Attendant, enfeoffed as Baron of Yongle county, and deliberated on great affairs of state.

entries.zh: 及帝大漸，與平秦王歸彥、趙郡王叡等同受顧託，迎立武成。
entries.en: When the emperor was near death, he and Prince of Pingqin Guiyan, Prince of Zhao Jun Rui, and others received the final charge and installed Gao Zhan.
entries.literal: When the emperor was gravely ill, together with Prince of Pingyuan Guiyan, Prince of Zhao Jun Rui, and others he received final charge and welcomed Gao Zhan to the throne.

entries.zh: 卽位，任遇轉隆，歷給事黃門侍郎、散騎常侍、侍中、中書監。
entries.en: After Gao Zhan took the throne, Wenyao's favor rose still higher. He served in turn as attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, chamberlain for attendants, and supervisor of the secretariat.
entries.literal: Upon enthronement his favor grew ever higher; he passed through Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Chamberlain for Attendants, Supervisor of Secretariat.

entries.zh: 天統二年，詔特賜姓高氏，籍屬宗正，子弟依例歲時入朝。
entries.en: In the second year of Tiantong an edict specially granted him the surname Gao, registered him with the director of the imperial clan, and allowed his sons and younger brothers to attend seasonal court audiences by regulation.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tiantong, an edict specially granted the surname Gao; registration placed under the Director of Imperial Clan; sons and younger brothers per regulation attended court at the seasons.

entries.zh: 再遷尚書左僕射，進封寧都郡公、侍中。
entries.en: He was promoted again to left vice director of the masters of writing and advanced to duke of Ningdu commandery while retaining the post of chamberlain for attendants.
entries.literal: Promoted again to Left Vice Director of Masters of Writing; advanced to Duke of Ningdu commandery, still chamberlain for attendants.

entries.zh: 武定八年，侯景叛，除東南道行臺尚書，封江夏縣男，與高岳等破侯景，擒蕭明。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Wuding, Hou Jing rebelled. Shu was made masters of writing on the southeastern mobile grand secretariat and enfeoffed as nan (baron) of Jiangxia county. With Gao Yue and others he broke Hou Jing and took Xiao Ming prisoner.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Wuding, Hou Jing rebelled; Shu was appointed Masters of Writing on the Southeastern Circuit Mobile Grand Secretariat, enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangxia county (male), and with Gao Yue and others defeated Hou Jing and captured Xiao Ming.

entries.zh: 遷東徐州刺史，為淮南經略使。
entries.en: He was transferred to governor of Eastern Xuzhou and made commissioner for Huainan pacification.
entries.literal: Transferred to Governor of Eastern Xuzhou; made Commissioner for the Pacification of Huainan.

entries.zh: 齊天保元年，侯景徵江西租稅，術率諸軍渡淮斷之，燒其稻數百萬石。
entries.en: In Qi's first Tianbao year, Hou Jing levied rents from Jiangxi. Shu led troops across the Huai to block him and burned several million shi of his grain.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianbao of Qi, Hou Jing levied rents and taxes from Jiangxi; Shu led the armies across the Huai to cut it off and burned several million shi of his rice.

entries.zh: 還鎮下邳，人隨術北渡淮者三千餘家。
entries.en: When he returned to garrison Xiapi, more than three thousand households followed him north across the Huai.
entries.literal: Returning to garrison at Xiapi, more than three thousand households followed Shu north across the Huai.

entries.zh: 東徐州刺史郭誌殺郡守。
entries.en: Guo Zhi, governor of Eastern Xuzhou, killed his commandery administrator.
entries.literal: Guo Zhi, Governor of Eastern Xuzhou, killed the commandery administrator.

entries.zh: 文宣聞之，勑術自今所統十餘州地諸有犯法者，刺史先啟聽報，以下先斷後表聞。
entries.en: Gao Yang heard of it and ordered Shu that in the dozen-odd provinces under him, whenever anyone broke the law the governor must first report and wait for word; lower officials might decide first and memorialize later.
entries.literal: Gao Yang heard of it and ordered Shu: from now on in the more than ten provinces under his command, wherever anyone violated the law, the governor should first report and await instruction; subordinates might judge first and memorialize afterward.

entries.zh: 齊代行臺兼總人事，自術始也。
entries.en: In Qi the practice of a mobile grand secretariat also holding personnel authority began with Shu.
entries.literal: In Qi, a mobile grand secretariat concurrently overseeing personnel matters began with Shu.

entries.zh: 安州刺史、臨清太守、盱眙蘄城二鎮將犯法，術皆案奏殺之。
entries.en: The governor of Anzhou, the administrator of Linqing, and the garrison commanders of Xuyi and Qicheng all committed capital crimes; Shu investigated, memorialized, and had them put to death.
entries.literal: The Governor of Anzhou, Administrator of Linqing, and the two garrison commanders of Xuyi and Qicheng all violated capital crimes; Shu investigated, memorialized, and had them executed.

entries.zh: 睢州刺史及所部郡守俱犯大辟，朝廷以其奴婢百口及資財盡賜術，三辭不見許，術乃送詣所司，不復以聞。
entries.en: The governor of Suizhou and every commandery administrator under him faced capital punishment. The court granted Shu all their slaves—more than a hundred households—and their property. He declined three times and was refused; Shu then turned everything over to the proper office and did not keep it.
entries.literal: The Governor of Suizhou and all the commandery administrators under him committed capital offenses; the court granted Shu all their hundred-odd slaves and entire assets; he declined three times but was not permitted; Shu then sent them to the relevant office and no longer kept them for himself.

entries.zh: 邢卲聞之，遺術書曰：「昔鐘離意云『孔子忍渴於盜泉』，便以珠璣委地，足下今能如此，可謂異代一時。」
entries.en: Xing Shao heard and wrote Shu: "Long ago Zhongli Yi said that Confucius would endure thirst rather than drink from Robber Spring, and so cast pearls and jade aside; you, sir, can do as much today—truly one moment in another age."
entries.literal: Xing Shao heard of it and sent Shu a letter, saying: "In antiquity Zhongli Yi said, 'Confucius bore thirst at Robber Spring,' and thereby cast pearls and jades to the ground; you, sir, can do the same today—one may call it the same moment across different ages."

entries.zh: 及王僧辯破侯景，術招攜安撫，城鎮相繼款附，前後二十餘州。
entries.en: When Wang Sengbian defeated Hou Jing, Shu won men over and pacified the land; towns and garrisons submitted one after another—more than twenty provinces in all.
entries.literal: When Wang Sengbian defeated Hou Jing, Shu recruited and pacified; cities and garrisons in succession submitted; in all more than twenty provinces.

entries.zh: 於是移鎮廣陵。
entries.en: He then shifted his headquarters to Guangling.
entries.literal: Thereupon he moved his command to Guangling.

entries.zh: 獲傳國璽送鄴，文宣以璽告於太廟。
entries.en: He recovered the dynastic seal and sent it to Ye; Gao Yang presented it at the imperial ancestral temple.
entries.literal: He obtained the dynastic seal and sent it to Ye; Gao Yang reported the seal at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 此璽卽秦所制，方四寸，上紐交盤龍，其文曰：「受命于天，旣壽永昌。」
entries.en: This was the seal Qin had made: four inches square, with a knob of interlaced dragons. Its inscription read, "Ordered by Heaven; long life and eternal prosperity."
entries.literal: This seal was that made by Qin, four inches square, with a knob of interlaced dragons; its inscription read: "Ordered by Heaven; long life and eternal prosperity."

entries.zh: 二漢相傳，又傳魏、晉。
entries.en: The two Han dynasties passed it down; Wei and Jin passed it down as well.
entries.literal: The Two Han transmitted it; it was also transmitted through Wei and Jin.

entries.zh: 懷帝敗，沒於劉聰。
entries.en: When Emperor Huai was defeated, it was lost to Liu Cong.
entries.literal: When Emperor Huai was defeated, it was lost among Liu Cong.

entries.zh: 聰敗，沒於石氏。
entries.en: When Cong fell, it passed to the Shi clan.
entries.literal: When Cong was defeated, it was lost among the Shi clan.

entries.zh: 石氏敗，晉穆帝永和中，濮陽太守戴僧施得之，遣督護何融送于建鄴。
entries.en: When the Shi fell, in the Yonghe reign of Jin's Emperor Mu, Dai Sengshi, administrator of Puyang, obtained it and sent supervisor He Rong to deliver it to Jiankang.
entries.literal: When the Shi clan was defeated, in the Yonghe era of Emperor Mu of Jin, Dai Sengshi, Administrator of Puyang, obtained it and sent Supervisor He Rong to deliver it to Jiankang.

entries.zh: 歷宋、齊、梁，梁敗，侯景得之。
entries.en: It passed through Song, Qi, and Liang; when Liang fell, Hou Jing took it.
entries.literal: It passed through Song, Qi, and Liang; when Liang fell, Hou Jing obtained it.

entries.zh: 景敗，侍中趙思賢以璽投景南兗州刺史郭元建，送于術，故術以進焉。
entries.en: When Jing was defeated, attendant-in-ordinary Zhao Sixian gave the seal to Jing's southern Yanzhou governor Guo Yuanjian, who sent it to Shu; thus Shu was able to present it.
entries.literal: When Jing was defeated, Attendant Zhong Zhao Sixian cast the seal upon Jing's Southern Yanzhou Governor Guo Yuanjian, who sent it to Shu; therefore Shu presented it.

entries.zh: 尋徵為殿中尚書，領太常卿，仍與朝賢議定律令。
entries.en: He was soon summoned as palace masters of writing and director of the imperial ancestral temple, and still joined court worthies in revising laws and ordinances.
entries.literal: Soon summoned as Masters of Writing in the Palace, leading Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and still deliberated on laws and ordinances with court worthies.

entries.zh: 遷吏部尚書，食南兗州梁郡幹。
entries.en: He was promoted to director of personnel and drew salary as titular chief of Liang commandery in southern Yanzhou.
entries.literal: Promoted to Director of Personnel; drew salary as titular chief of Liang commandery in Southern Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 辛術 元文遙 趙彥深
entries.en: Xin Shu; Yuan Wenyao; Zhao Yanshen
entries.literal: Xin Shu; Yuan Wenyao; Zhao Yanshen

entries.zh: 崔季舒，字叔正，博陵安平人。
entries.en: Cui Jishu, styled Shuzheng, came from Anping in Boling commandery.
entries.literal: Cui Jishu, styled Shuzheng, was a man of Anping in Boling.

entries.zh: 父瑜之，魏鴻臚卿。
entries.en: His father Yuzhi had been Wei chamberlain for dependent states.
entries.literal: His father Yuzhi was Chamberlain for Dependent States under Wei.

entries.zh: 季舒少孤，性明敏，涉獵經史，長於尺牘，有當世才具。
entries.en: Orphaned young, Jishu was bright and quick, read widely in classics and histories, wrote excellent dispatches, and had real gifts for his time.
entries.literal: Jishu was orphaned young; by nature bright and keen, he ranged through the classics and histories, excelled at correspondence, and had the talent and equipment of his age.

entries.zh: 年十七，為州主簿，為大將軍趙郡公琛所器重，言之於神武。
entries.en: At seventeen he served as provincial chief clerk. Grand General the Duke of Zhao commandery, Chen, favored him and recommended him to Gao Huan.
entries.literal: At seventeen he was chief clerk of the province; the Grand General, Duke of Zhao commandery Chen, valued him highly and spoke of him to Gao Huan.

entries.zh: 神武親簡丞郎，補季舒大行臺都官郎中。
entries.en: Gao Huan personally screened chancellery and department officers and made Jishu lang in the mobile grand secretariat bureau of offices.
entries.literal: Gao Huan personally screened chancellery and department men and appointed Jishu lang in the Mobile Grand Secretariat Bureau of Offices.

entries.zh: 文襄輔政，轉大將軍中兵參軍，甚見親寵。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng assumed regency, Jishu was moved to staff officer in the grand general central troops bureau and won close favor.
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng took up regency he was transferred to staff officer in the grand general central troops bureau and was greatly favored.

entries.zh: 以魏帝左右，須置腹心，擢拜中書侍郎。
entries.en: The Wei emperor needed trusted men at his side, so Jishu was promoted secretariat gentleman.
entries.literal: Because the Wei emperor needed trusted men at his side, Jishu was promoted secretariat gentleman.

entries.zh: 文襄為中書監，移門下機事總歸中書，又季舒善音樂，故內伎亦通隸焉，內伎屬中書。
entries.en: Gao Cheng supervised the secretariat; secretariat-gate business was folded into it. Because Jishu knew music, inner palace performers also came under him—inner performers now belonged to the secretariat.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng was supervisor of the secretariat; the business of the Secretariat Gate was folded into the secretariat, and because Jishu was skilled at music the inner performers also reported through him—the inner performers belonged to the secretariat.

entries.zh: 自季舒始也。
entries.en: That practice began with Jishu.
entries.literal: This began with Jishu.

entries.zh: 文襄每進書魏帝，有所諫請，或文辭繁雜，季舒輒修飾通之，得申勸戒而已。
entries.en: Whenever Gao Cheng sent the Wei emperor memorials with remonstrance, Jishu would trim tangled wording so the counsel itself could pass.
entries.literal: Whenever Gao Cheng presented memorials to the Wei emperor with remonstrances, if the wording grew tangled Jishu would polish and render it clear so only the admonition stood forth.

entries.zh: 靜帝報答霸朝，恒與季舒論之，云：「崔中書是我妳母。」
entries.en: When Emperor Jing drafted replies to the hegemonic court, he always discussed them with Jishu and said, "Secretariat Gentleman Cui is our wet nurse."
entries.literal: Emperor Jing, when answering the hegemonic court, always discussed it with Jishu, saying, "Secretariat Gentleman Cui is our wet nurse."

entries.zh: 轉黃門侍郎，領主衣都統。
entries.en: He was then made gentleman of the yellow gate and also oversaw the directorate of imperial wardrobe.
entries.literal: He was transferred to gentleman of the yellow gate and concurrently oversaw the directorate of imperial wardrobe.

entries.zh: 雖迹在魏朝，而心歸霸府，密謀大計，皆得預聞。
entries.en: Though he still walked the Wei court, his heart was with the hegemonic government, and he was let in early on major plans.
entries.literal: Though his footprints lay in the Wei court, his heart belonged to the hegemonic government; on weighty plans he was always allowed to hear in advance.

entries.zh: 於是賓客輻湊，傾心接禮，甚得名譽，勢傾崔暹。
entries.en: Guests gathered in force; he met them with open courtesy, won wide renown, and his power eclipsed Cui Xian.
entries.literal: Guests then gathered in numbers; he received them with open courtesy and won a great name, until his power outshone Cui Xian.

entries.zh: 暹嘗於朝堂屏人拜之曰：「暹若得僕射，皆叔父之恩。」
entries.en: Once at court Xian dismissed everyone else and bowed to him, saying, "If Xian wins vice director of the masters of writing, it will be entirely my uncle's favor."
entries.literal: Once Xian at the hall dismissed others and bowed to him, saying, "If Xian should obtain vice director of the masters of writing, it is all Uncle's grace."

entries.zh: 其權重如此。
entries.en: His weight in power was such.
entries.literal: Such was his weight in power.

entries.zh: 時勳貴多不法，文襄無所縱捨，外議以季舒及崔暹等所為，甚被怨疾。
entries.en: Many meritorious nobles then broke the law, and Gao Cheng would not spare them. Outsiders blamed Jishu, Cui Xian, and the rest, and hated them bitterly.
entries.literal: At that time many meritorious nobles acted lawlessly; Gao Cheng would not spare them, and outsiders blamed Jishu and Cui Xian and others for it and bitterly resented them.

entries.zh: 及文襄遇難，文宣將赴晉陽，黃門郎陽休之勸季舒從行，曰：「一日不朝，其間容刀。」
entries.en: When Gao Cheng was killed, Gao Yang was bound for Jinyang. Gentleman of the yellow gate Yang Xiuzhi urged Jishu to go with him, saying, "Miss one day at court and a blade may hide in the interval."
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng met disaster, Gao Yang was about to go to Jinyang; Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yang Xiuzhi urged Jishu to go along, saying, "One day without attending court, and in between a blade may be hidden."

entries.zh: 季舒性愛聲色，心在閑放，遂不請行，欲恣其行樂。
entries.en: Jishu loved music and women and wanted leisure, so he did not ask to go and meant to enjoy himself.
entries.literal: Jishu loved music and women; his heart was set on leisure, so he did not ask to go and meant to indulge his pleasures.

entries.zh: 司馬子如緣宿憾，及尚食典御陳山提等共列其過狀，由是季舒及暹各鞭二百，徙北邊。
entries.en: Sima Ziru, holding an old grudge, joined Director of Palace Provisions Chen Shanti and others in listing his offenses. Jishu and Xian were each flogged two hundred strokes and exiled north.
entries.literal: Sima Ziru, nursing an old grudge, together with Director of Palace Provisions Chen Shanti and others jointly listed his offenses, and thereby Jishu and Xian were each flogged two hundred strokes and sent to the northern marches.

entries.zh: 天保初，文宣知其無罪，追為將作大匠，再遷侍中。
entries.en: Early in Tianbao, Gao Yang knew they were innocent and recalled Jishu as director of imperial works, then promoted him again to regular attendant.
entries.literal: Early in Tianbao Gao Yang knew they were guiltless and recalled Jishu as director of imperial works, then again promoted him to regular attendant.

entries.zh: 俄兼尚書左僕射、儀同三司，大被恩遇。
entries.en: Soon he was also left vice director of the masters of writing and ceremonial peer of the three ranks, and was deeply favored.
entries.literal: Soon he was concurrently made left vice director of the masters of writing and ceremonial peer of the three ranks, and was deeply favored.

entries.zh: 乾明初，楊愔以文宣遺旨，停其僕射。
entries.en: Early in Qianming, Yang Yin, acting on Gao Yang's final instruction, removed him from vice director.
entries.literal: Early in Qianming Yang Yin, on Gao Yang's dying instruction, stopped his vice directorship.

entries.zh: 遭母喪解任，起復，除光祿勳，兼中兵尚書。
entries.en: He left office for his mother mourning, then was recalled and made director of splendid happiness while also chief of the central troops bureau in the masters of writing.
entries.literal: On his mother mourning he left office; recalled from mourning he was made director of splendid happiness and concurrently chief of the central troops bureau in the masters of writing.

entries.zh: 出為齊州刺史，坐遣人渡淮互市，亦有贓賄事，為御史所劾，會赦不問。
entries.en: Sent out as governor of Qi, he was impeached for sending men across the Huai to trade and for bribery as well, but was pardoned and not pursued.
entries.literal: Sent out as governor of Qi province; because he sent men across the Huai for mutual trade and had bribery matters as well, he was impeached by the censorate, but pardoned and not pursued.

entries.zh: 武成居藩，曾病，文宣令季舒療病，備盡心力。
entries.en: When Gao Zhan held a princely fief he once fell ill; Gao Yang ordered Jishu to treat him, and Jishu spared no effort.
entries.literal: When Gao Zhan held a princely fief he once fell ill; Gao Yang ordered Jishu to treat him and he spared no effort.

entries.zh: 大寧初，追還，引入慰勉，累拜度支尚書、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: Early in Daning he was recalled, comforted at court, and promoted in turn to director of revenue in the masters of writing and grand ceremonial peer with an opened government office.
entries.literal: Early in Daning he was recalled, brought in and comforted, and repeatedly promoted to director of revenue in the masters of writing and grand ceremonial peer opening a government office.

entries.zh: 營昭陽殿，敕令監造。
entries.en: When the Zhaoyang Palace was raised, he was ordered to oversee construction.
entries.literal: When the Zhaoyang Palace was being built he was ordered to oversee construction.

entries.zh: 以判事式為胡長仁密言其短，出為西兗州刺史。
entries.en: Hu Changren privately denounced his faults in a case-review form, and he was sent out as governor of Western Yanzhou.
entries.literal: Because in a case-review form Hu Changren privately denounced his faults, he was sent out as governor of Western Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 為進典籖於吏部，被責免官，又以詣廣寧王宅，決馬鞭數十。
entries.en: As advance registry clerk in the personnel directorate he was rebuked and dismissed; for visiting the Prince of Guangning's mansion he was also sentenced to several dozen horsewhip strokes.
entries.literal: Serving as advance registry clerk in the personnel directorate he was rebuked and removed from office; again for visiting the mansion of Prince of Guangning he was sentenced to several dozen strokes of the horsewhip.

entries.zh: 及武成崩，不得預於哭泣。
entries.en: When Gao Zhan died he was not allowed to join the mourning rites.
entries.literal: When Gao Zhan died he was not allowed to take part in the mourning rites.

entries.zh: 久之，除膠州刺史，遷侍中、開府，食新安、河陰二郡幹。
entries.en: Long afterward he was made governor of Jiao, then regular attendant and grand ceremonial peer, drawing salary from Xin'an and Heyin commanderies.
entries.literal: After a long interval he was made governor of Jiao province, then transferred to regular attendant and grand ceremonial peer, with salary from the two commanderies of Xin'an and Heyin.

entries.zh: 加左光祿大夫，待詔文林館，監撰《御覽》。
entries.en: He was advanced to left grand master of splendid happiness, attended at the Wenslin Hall, and supervised compilation of the Imperial Overview.
entries.literal: Advanced to left grand master of splendid happiness, attended at the Wenslin Hall, and supervised compilation of the Imperial Overview.

entries.zh: 加特進、監國史。
entries.en: He was made special advancement and supervisor of the national history.
entries.literal: Made special advancement and supervisor of the national history.

entries.zh: 季舒素好圖籍，暮年轉更精勤，兼推薦人士，獎勸文學，時議翕然，遠近稱美。
entries.en: Jishu had always loved books and grew keener in old age. He also recommended men and encouraged letters; opinion converged, and praise spread near and far.
entries.literal: Jishu had always loved books; in his later years he grew still more diligent, and he also recommended men and encouraged letters—opinion converged, and near and far praised him.

entries.zh: 祖珽，字孝征，范陽狄遒人也。
entries.en: Zu Ting, styled Xiaozheng, came from Di Dao in Fanyang.
entries.literal: Zu Ting, styled Xiaozheng, was a man of Di Dao in Fanyang.

entries.zh: 父瑩，魏護軍將軍。
entries.en: His father Ying was Wei defender-general.
entries.literal: His father Ying was defender-general of Wei.

entries.zh: 珽神情機警，詞藻遒逸，少馳令譽，為世所推。
entries.en: Ting was quick-witted and alert, his phrasing forceful and fluent; from youth he won fame and the age praised him.
entries.literal: Ting was alert in spirit and quick in wit, his diction forceful and fluent; from youth he won a fine reputation and was praised by the world.

entries.zh: 起家秘書郎，對策高第，為尚書儀曹郎中，典儀注。
entries.en: He began as secretariat lang, ranked high in the policy examination, and became lang in the ritual protocols section of the masters of writing, in charge of ceremonial regulations.
entries.literal: He first took office as secretariat lang; in the policy-response examination he ranked high and became lang in the ritual protocols section of the masters of writing, in charge of ceremonial regulations.

entries.zh: 嘗為冀州刺史万俟受洛制《清德頌》，其文典麗，由是神武聞之。
entries.en: He once composed the "Eulogy of Pure Virtue" for Moqi Shouluo, Inspector of Ji Province. Its writing was elegant, and because of this Gao Huan heard of him.
entries.literal: He once composed the "Eulogy of Pure Virtue" for Moqi Shouluo, Inspector of Ji Province. Its writing was elegant, and because of this Gao Huan heard of him.

entries.zh: 時文宣為幷州刺史，署珽開府倉曹參軍。
entries.en: At that time Gao Yang was governor of Bing and appointed Ting army-camp staff officer with an opened government office.
entries.literal: At that time Gao Yang was governor of Bing province and appointed Ting as army-camp staff officer of an opened government office.

entries.zh: 神武口授珽三十六事，出而疏之，一無遺失，大為僚類所賞。
entries.en: Gao Huan dictated thirty-six items to Ting; Ting wrote them into a memorial without losing one, and colleagues admired him greatly.
entries.literal: Gao Huan dictated thirty-six items to Ting; when he came out Ting wrote them up in a memorial and not one was lost—greatly admired by colleagues.

entries.zh: 時神武送魏蘭陵公主出塞嫁蠕蠕，魏收賦《出塞》及《公主遠嫁詩》二首，珽皆和之，大為時人傳詠。
entries.en: Then Gao Huan was sending Princess Lanling of Wei beyond the frontier to marry the Rouran. Wei Shou wrote "Crossing the Frontier" and "The Princess Far Marriage"; Ting harmonized with both, and the age chanted them widely.
entries.literal: Then Gao Huan was sending Princess Lanling of Wei beyond the frontier to marry the Rouran; Wei Shou composed two pieces, "Crossing the Frontier" and "The Princess Far Marriage"; Ting harmonized with both, and they were widely chanted in the age.

entries.zh: 珽性疏率，不能廉慎守道。
entries.en: Ting was careless by nature and could not keep office with integrity and caution.
entries.literal: Ting was by nature careless and coarse, unable to keep integrity and caution in office.

entries.zh: 倉曹雖云州局，乃受山東課輸，由此大有受納，豐於財產。
entries.en: Though the army-camp post was called a provincial bureau, he took levies from east of the mountains, accepted bribes in quantity, and grew very rich.
entries.literal: Though the army-camp post was called a provincial bureau, he received the levies from east of the mountains and thereby took bribes in great quantity, growing rich in assets.

entries.zh: 又自解彈琵琶，能為新曲，招城市年少歌舞為娛，遊集諸倡家。
entries.en: He could play pipa and compose new tunes, gathered city youths to sing and dance for pleasure, and haunted singing-houses.
entries.literal: He himself could play the pipa and compose new tunes; he summoned city youths to sing and dance for pleasure and frequented every singing-house.

entries.zh: 與陳元康、穆子容、任胄、元士亮等為聲色之遊。
entries.en: With Chen Yuankang, Mu Zirong, Ren Zhou, Yuan Shiliang, and others he pursued music and women.
entries.literal: With Chen Yuankang, Mu Zirong, Ren Zhou, Yuan Shiliang, and others he indulged in music and women.

entries.zh: 諸人嘗就珽宿，出山東大文綾幷連珠孔雀羅等百餘疋，令諸嫗擲樗蒲賭之，以為戲樂。
entries.en: When they once lodged with him, he brought out east-of-the-mountains damask and linked-pearl peacock gauze, more than a hundred bolts, and had the women gamble at dice for sport.
entries.literal: When the men once lodged with Ting, he brought out from east of the mountains large-pattern damask and linked-pearl peacock gauze and the like, more than a hundred bolts, and had the women cast dice for stakes as a pastime.

entries.zh: 參軍元景獻，故尚書令元世雋子也，其妻司馬慶雲女，是魏孝靜帝姑博陵長公主所生。
entries.en: Staff officer Yuan Jingxian was son of former Minister over the Masses Yuan Shijun; his wife was daughter of Sima Qingyun, child of Emperor Jing's aunt, the great Princess of Boling.
entries.literal: Staff officer Yuan Jingxian was son of the former minister over the masses Yuan Shijun; his wife was daughter of Sima Qingyun, born of the former Wei Emperor Jing's aunt, the Great Princess of Boling.

entries.zh: 珽忽迎景獻妻赴席，與諸人遞寢，亦以貨物所致。
entries.en: Ting suddenly brought Jingxian wife to the feast and passed her among the company in turn—again for gain.
entries.literal: Ting suddenly brought Jingxian wife to the feast and shared her in turn with the company—this too came from greed for goods.

entries.zh: 其豪縱淫逸如此。
entries.en: His license was such.
entries.literal: So wild and dissolute was he.

entries.zh: 常云：「丈夫一生不負身。」
entries.en: He often said, "A man lives once and must not betray his body."
entries.literal: He often said, "A man in one lifetime must not fail his person."

entries.zh: 已文宣罷州，珽例應隨府，規為倉局之間，致請於陳元康，元康為白，由是還任倉曹。
entries.en: After Gao Yang left the province Ting should have followed headquarters, but schemed for the grain-store post through Chen Yuankang, who spoke for him, and he returned to army-camp duty.
entries.literal: After Gao Yang left his provincial post Ting should by rule follow the headquarters; scheming for the grain-store post, he made request through Chen Yuankang, and Yuankang spoke for him, so he returned to the army-camp post.

entries.zh: 珽又委體附參軍事攝典簽陸子先，並為畫計，請糧之際，令子先宣教，出倉粟十車，為僚官捉送。
entries.en: Ting also attached himself to chief registry clerk Lu Zixian, acting military staff officer, and they plotted together; when grain was requested Zixian proclaimed the order, ten cartloads were issued, and colleagues seized them for trial.
entries.literal: Ting also threw himself on Chief Registry Clerk Lu Zixian, who held acting military staff duties, and together they drew up plans; at the time of requesting grain he had Zixian proclaim the order, and ten cartloads of granary grain were issued—caught by a colleague and sent for trial.

entries.zh: 神武親問之，珽自言不受署，歸罪子先，神武信而釋之。
entries.en: Gao Huan questioned him in person. Ting said he had no commission and blamed Zixian; Gao Huan believed him and released him.
entries.literal: Gao Huan questioned him in person; Ting said himself he had not received appointment and blamed Zixian, and Gao Huan believed him and released him.

entries.zh: 珽出而言曰：「此丞相天緣明鑒，然實孝徵所為。」
entries.en: Coming out he said, "The chancellor heaven-sent clarity sees through—but in truth Xiaozheng did it."
entries.literal: Coming out he said, "This chancellor heaven-bestowed discernment—but in truth Xiaozheng did it."

entries.zh: 性不羈放縱，曾至膠州刺史司馬世雲家飲酒，遂藏銅疊二面。
entries.en: Unrestrained by nature, he once drank at Jiao governor Sima Shiyun home and hid two bronze mirrors.
entries.literal: Unrestrained by nature, he once drank at the home of Governor of Jiao province Sima Shiyun and hid two bronze mirrors.

entries.zh: 廚人請搜諸客，果於珽懷中得之，見者以為深恥。
entries.en: The cook asked to search the guests; they were found in Ting bosom, and onlookers thought it deep shame.
entries.literal: The cook asked to search the guests; they were indeed found in Ting bosom, and witnesses thought it a deep shame.

entries.zh: 所乘老馬，常稱騮駒。
entries.en: The old horse he rode he always called a piebald colt.
entries.literal: The old horse he rode he always called a piebald colt.

entries.zh: 又與寡婦王氏姦通，每人前相聞往復。
entries.en: He also lay with the widow Wang, exchanging messages openly before others.
entries.literal: He also committed adultery with the widow surnamed Wang, each time exchanging word before others.

entries.zh: 裴讓之與珽早狎，於衆中嘲珽曰：「卿那得如此詭異，老馬十歲，猶號騮駒；
entries.en: Pei Rangzhi, long intimate with him, mocked him before the crowd: "How can you be so strange—a ten-year horse still called a piebald colt;
entries.literal: Pei Rangzhi was early intimate with Ting and before the crowd mocked him, saying, "How can you be so strange—an old horse of ten years still called a piebald colt;

entries.zh: 一妻耳順，尚稱娘子。」
entries.en: a sixty-year wife still called Mistress."
entries.literal: a wife at sixty still called Mistress."

entries.zh: 于時喧然傳之。
entries.en: The crowd roared and the story spread.
entries.literal: At the time it spread with a roar.

entries.zh: 後為神武中外府功曹，神武宴僚屬，於坐失金叵羅，竇泰令飲酒者皆脫帽，於珽髻上得之，神武不能罪也。
entries.en: Later he was merit officer in Gao Huan inner and outer government office. At a feast Gao Huan lost a gold bowl; Dou Tai made every drinker remove his cap—it was found in Ting's hair; Gao Huan could not punish him.
entries.literal: Later he was merit officer in Gao Huan inner and outer government office; at a feast of subordinates Gao Huan lost a gold bowl, and Dou Tai ordered all who drank to remove their caps—in Ting topknot it was found; Gao Huan could not punish him.

entries.zh: 後為秘書丞，領舍人，事文襄。
entries.en: Later he was secretariat assistant, leading gentlemen-in-attendance, serving Gao Cheng.
entries.literal: Later he was secretariat assistant and led gentlemen-in-attendance, serving Gao Cheng.

entries.zh: 州客至，請賣《華林遍略》。
entries.en: A provincial visitor came offering to sell the Forest Compendium.
entries.literal: A provincial visitor came asking to sell the Forest Compendium.

entries.zh: 文襄多集書人，一日一夜寫畢，退其本曰：「不須也。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng gathered copyists and finished a copy in one day and one night, then returned the original, saying, "Not needed."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng gathered many copyists and in one day and one night finished the copy, then returned the original, saying, "Not needed."

entries.zh: 珽以《遍略》數帙質錢樗蒲，文襄杖之四十。
entries.en: Ting pledged several volumes of the Compendium for dice gambling; Gao Cheng had him flogged forty strokes.
entries.literal: Ting pledged several volumes of the Compendium for dice stakes; Gao Cheng had him flogged forty.

entries.zh: 又與令史李雙、倉督成祖等作晉州啟，請粟三千石，代功曹參軍趙彥深宣神武教，給城局參軍事過典簽高景略，疑其定不實，密以問彥深，彥深答都無此事，遂被推檢，珽卽引伏。
entries.en: Again with clerk Li Shuang, granary overseer Cheng Zu, and others he drafted a Jinzhou memorial for three thousand shi of grain; standing in for merit officer Zhao Yanshen he proclaimed Gao Huan order to garrison merit officer and passing registry clerk Gao Jinglue. Jinglue doubted the amount, secretly asked Yanshen, and Yanshen said there was no such order. Investigation followed, and Ting confessed at once.
entries.literal: Again with clerk Li Shuang, granary overseer Cheng Zu, and others he drafted a Jinzhou memorial requesting three thousand shi of grain; standing in for merit officer Zhao Yanshen he proclaimed Gao Huan order and gave it to garrison-bureau merit officer and passing registry clerk Gao Jinglue, who doubted the quota was not real and secretly asked Yanshen; Yanshen answered there was no such matter at all—thereupon investigation was pushed, and Ting confessed at once.

entries.zh: 神武大怒，決鞭二百，配甲坊，加鉗，其穀倍徵。
entries.en: Gao Huan was furious: two hundred strokes, assignment to the armor ward, irons added, and the grain levied at double.
entries.literal: Gao Huan was greatly angered; sentenced him to two hundred strokes, assigned to the armor ward, and iron added; the grain was levied at double.

entries.zh: 未及科，會幷州定國寺新成，神武謂陳元康、溫子升曰：「昔作《芒山寺碑》文，時稱妙絕，今《定國寺碑》當使誰作詞也？」
entries.en: Before the levy was collected, the new Dingguo Temple in Bingzhou was finished. Gao Huan said to Chen Yuankang and Wen Zisheng, "The Mangshan Temple stele was called peerless—who should write the Dingguo Temple stele now?"
entries.literal: Before the levy was exacted, the new Dingguo Temple in Bingzhou was completed; Gao Huan said to Chen Yuankang and Wen Zisheng, "When we composed the Mangshan Temple stele text it was called peerless—now for the Dingguo Temple stele whose words should compose it?"

entries.zh: 元康因薦珽才學，並解鮮卑語。
entries.en: Yuankang recommended Ting learning and said he also understood Xianbei.
entries.literal: Yuankang thereupon recommended Ting learning and that he also understood Xianbei speech.

entries.zh: 乃給筆札就禁所具草。
entries.en: Brush and paper were sent, and he drafted it in confinement.
entries.literal: Brush and paper were given and in the prison ward the draft was produced.

entries.zh: 二日內成，其文甚麗。
entries.en: He finished in two days; the text was very fine.
entries.literal: Within two days it was finished; the text was very beautiful.

entries.zh: 神武以其工而且速，特恕不問，然猶免官，散參相府。
entries.en: Gao Huan, impressed by his skill and speed, especially pardoned him, though he still removed him from office to serve scattered in the chancellor office.
entries.literal: Gao Huan, because he was skilled and swift, especially pardoned and did not pursue, yet still removed him from office to serve scattered in the chancellor office.

entries.zh: 文襄嗣事，以為功曹參軍。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng took up the succession he made him army-camp merit officer.
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng took up the succession he made him merit officer in the army-camp.

entries.zh: 及文襄遇害，元康被傷創重，倩珽作書屬家累事，幷云：「祖喜邊有少許物，宜早索取。」
entries.en: When Gao Cheng was killed Yuankang wounds were grave; he had Ting write a letter entrusting family matters, and also said, "Zu Xi at the border has a little property—take it soon."
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng met disaster Yuankang wounds were grave; he had Ting compose a letter entrusting family burdens, and also said, "At the border Zu Xi has a little property—take it soon."

entries.zh: 珽乃不通此書，喚祖喜私問，得金二十五鋌，唯與喜二鋌，餘盡自入己。
entries.en: Ting did not deliver the letter but summoned Zu Xi privately; he got twenty-five ingots of gold, gave Xi only two, and kept the rest.
entries.literal: Ting did not deliver this letter but summoned Zu Xi in private to ask; he got twenty-five ingots of gold and gave Xi only two—the rest all entered his own purse.

entries.zh: 又盜元康家書數千卷。
entries.en: He also stole several thousand scrolls from Yuankang's house.
entries.literal: He also stole several thousand scrolls of books from Yuankang's house.

entries.zh: 祖喜懷恨，遂告元康二弟叔諶、季璩等。
entries.en: Zu Xi nursed a grudge and told Yuan Kang's younger brothers Shu Chen and Ji Qu, among others.
entries.literal: Zu Xi bore a grudge and thereupon informed Yuan Kang's two younger brothers, Shu Chen and Ji Ji, and the others.

entries.zh: 叔諶以語楊愔，愔嚬眉答曰：「恐不益亡者。」
entries.en: Shu Chen told Yang Yin. Yin knit his brow and said, "I doubt that will help the dead."
entries.literal: Shu Chen told Yang Yin; Yin frowned and answered, "I fear it will not benefit the dead."

entries.zh: 因此得停。
entries.en: On that account the matter was dropped.
entries.literal: Because of this it was halted.

entries.zh: 文宣作相，珽擬補令史十餘人，皆有受納，據法處絞，上尋捨之。
entries.en: When Wenxuan was regent, Ting proposed more than ten clerk appointments, every one of them bought. By law they merited strangulation, but in the end the sovereign let them off.
entries.literal: When Wenxuan was regent, Ting proposed to fill more than ten clerk posts; all had taken bribes; by law they should be strangled, but the sovereign eventually pardoned them.

entries.zh: 又盜官《遍略》一部。
entries.en: He also stole an office copy of the Comprehensive Digest.
entries.literal: He also stole one copy of the official Comprehensive Digest from the office.

entries.zh: 事發，文宣付從事中郎王土雅推檢，並書與平陽公淹，令錄珽付禁，勿令越逸。
entries.en: When the theft came to light, Wenxuan put Attendant of the Masters of Writing Wang Tuya in charge of the inquiry and wrote Prince of Pingyang Yan as well, telling him to take Ting into custody and allow no escape.
entries.literal: When it came to light, Wenxuan entrusted Attendant of the Masters of Writing Wang Tuya to investigate, and also wrote to Prince of Pingyang Yan, ordering him to take Ting into custody and not allow escape.

entries.zh: 淹遣田曹參軍孫子寬往喚，珽受命，便爾私逃。
entries.en: Yan sent field officer Sun Zikuan to fetch him. Ting answered the summons, then slipped away the same night.
entries.literal: Yan sent Field Officer Sun Zikuan to summon him; Ting accepted the summons, then at once fled in secret.

entries.zh: 黃門郎高德正副留臺事，謀云：「珽自知有犯，驚竄是常，但宣一命向秘書，稱『奉幷州約束頒《五經》三部，仰丞親檢校催遣』，如此則珽意安，夜當還宅，然後掩取。」
entries.en: Yellow gate gentleman Gao Dezheng was deputy for affairs at the secondary capital. They plotted: "Ting knows he is guilty and will bolt—that is only natural. But issue an order to the secretariat, saying, 'By Bingzhou's command, distribute three sets of the Five Classics; the deputy director is to inspect and hurry delivery in person.' Then Ting will feel safe, come home at night, and we can take him."
entries.literal: Yellow Gate Gentleman Gao Dezheng was deputy for matters at the secondary capital; they plotted, saying, "Ting knows his guilt—panic flight is only natural, but proclaim an order to the Secretariat, saying, 'By Bingzhou constraint, distribute three sets of the Five Classics; the Deputy Director is to inspect and expedite in person'—thus Ting will feel secure and return home at night; then seize him."

entries.zh: 珽果如德正圖，遂還宅。
entries.en: Ting did exactly as Dezheng had planned and went home.
entries.literal: Ting did indeed follow Dezheng's plan and returned home.

entries.zh: 薄晚，就家掩之，縛珽送廷尉。
entries.en: Near dusk they raided his house, bound him, and sent him to the minister of justice.
entries.literal: Toward evening they raided his house, bound Ting, and sent him to the Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 據犯枉法處絞刑。
entries.en: By the charges, his illegal acts called for strangulation.
entries.literal: According to the crimes, illegal conduct warranted strangulation.

entries.zh: 文宣以珽伏事先世，諷所司命特寬其罰，遂奏免死除名。
entries.en: Wenxuan, because Ting had served the house in earlier reigns, hinted that the office should show special leniency. The memorial asked to spare his life and strike his name from the rolls.
entries.literal: Wenxuan, because Ting had served previous generations, hinted to the office to specially mitigate the punishment; a memorial was submitted to spare death and remove his name from the register.

entries.zh: 天保元年，復被召從駕，依除免例，參於晉陽。
entries.en: In Tianbao's first year he was summoned again to follow the carriage. Under the usual rule for men struck from office, he took part at Jinyang.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianbao he was again summoned to follow the imperial carriage; by precedent for removal from office he participated at Jinyang.

entries.zh: 珽善為胡桃油以塗畫，乃進之長廣王，因言「殿下有非常骨法，孝徵夢殿下乘龍上天」。
entries.en: Ting knew how to make walnut oil for painting and offered it to the Prince of Changguang, saying, "Your Highness has the bones of an uncommon man. I, Xiaozheng, dreamed you rode a dragon into heaven."
entries.literal: Ting was skilled at making walnut oil for painting and presented it to the Prince of Changgang, saying, "Your Highness has extraordinary bone structure; Xiao Zheng dreamed that Your Highness rode a dragon into heaven."

entries.zh: 王謂曰：「若然，當使兄大富貴。」
entries.en: The prince said, "If that is so, my elder brother should grow very rich indeed."
entries.literal: The prince said to him, "If that is so, then my elder brother ought to grow very rich."

entries.zh: 及卽位，是為武成皇帝，擢拜中書侍郎。
entries.en: When he took the throne as Emperor Wucheng, he promoted Ting to secretariat attendant.
entries.literal: When he took the throne he was Emperor Wucheng and promoted Ting to Secretariat Attendant.

entries.zh: 帝於後園使珽彈琵琶，和士開胡舞，各賞物百段。
entries.en: In the rear garden the emperor had Ting play the pipa while He Shikai danced the Hu step. Each man received a hundred bolts of goods.
entries.literal: The emperor had Ting play the pipa in the rear garden while He Shikai performed Hu dance; each was rewarded with a hundred bolts of goods.

entries.zh: 士開忌之，出為安德太守，轉齊郡太守，以母老乞還侍養，詔許之。
entries.en: Shikai envied him and sent him out as administrator of Ande, then moved him to Qi commandery. His mother was old; he begged to return and tend her, and the edict allowed it.
entries.literal: Shikai envied him and had him sent out as Administrator of Ande, then transferred to Administrator of Qi commandery; because his mother was old he begged to return and serve her, and an edict permitted it.

entries.zh: 會江南使人來聘，為中勞使。
entries.en: When envoys came from the south on a courtesy mission, he was made commissioner for receiving them.
entries.literal: It happened that envoys from the south came on a mission of courtesy; he was made commissioner for receiving guests.

entries.zh: 尋為太常少卿、散騎常侍、假儀同三司，掌詔誥。
entries.en: Soon he was vice director of the imperial ancestral temple, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and acting three excellencies of honor, drafting edicts.
entries.literal: Soon he was Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Acting Three Excellencies of Honor, drafting edicts.

entries.zh: 初，珽於乾明、皇建之時，知武成陰有大誌，遂深自結納，曲相祗奉。
entries.en: Early in the Qianming and Huangjian reigns Ting saw that Wucheng nursed great designs in secret and bound himself to him, flattering him at every turn.
entries.literal: At first, during the Qianming and Huangjian eras, Ting knew that Wucheng harbored great designs in secret and therefore bonded with him deeply, currying favor with obsequious devotion.

entries.zh: 武成於天保世頻被責，心常銜之。
entries.en: In the Tianbao years Wucheng had been blamed again and again and carried the grudge in his heart.
entries.literal: Wucheng in the Tianbao era had often been blamed and always harbored resentment in his heart.

entries.zh: 珽至是希旨，上書請追尊太祖獻武皇帝為神武，高祖文宣皇帝改為威宗景烈皇帝，以悅武成，從之。
entries.en: Ting now played to the throne and memorialized to posthumously honor Grand Ancestor Emperor Xianwu as Emperor Shenwu and change High Ancestor Emperor Wenxuan's temple style to Weizong Jinglie Emperor. Wucheng was pleased and assented.
entries.literal: Ting now toed the emperor's wishes memorialized to posthumously honor Grand Ancestor as Emperor Shenwu and change High Ancestor Emperor Wenxuan's title to Weizong Jinglie Emperor, to please Wucheng; the emperor assented.

entries.zh: 武成崩，後主憶之，就除海州刺史。
entries.en: When Wucheng died, the Later Sovereign remembered him and at once made him inspector of Hai province.
entries.literal: When Wucheng died, the Later Sovereign remembered him and at once appointed him Inspector of Hai province.

entries.zh: 是時陸令萱外干朝政，其子穆提婆愛幸。
entries.en: Lu Lingxuan then meddled in court affairs from outside, and her son Mu Tipo stood in favor.
entries.literal: At the time Lu Lingxuan meddled in court affairs from outside; her son Mu Tipo was a favorite.

entries.zh: 珽乃遺陸媼弟悉達書曰：「趙彥深心腹深沈，欲行伊、霍事，儀同姊弟豈得平安，何不早用智士耶？」
entries.en: Ting sent a letter to Dame Lu's younger brother Sida: "Zhao Yanshen's heart runs deep and hidden. He means to play Yi Yin and Huo Guang—the lady's brother and sister, how will they stay safe? Why not take a clever man into counsel early?"
entries.literal: Ting therefore sent a letter to Dame Lu's younger brother Sida, saying, "Zhao Yanshen's heart is deep and hidden; he wishes to perform the Yi and Huo deed—the Lady's brother and sister, how can they be secure? Why not early employ a man of counsel?"

entries.zh: 和士開亦以珽能決大事，欲以為謀主，故棄除舊怨，虛心待之。
entries.en: He Shikai too, because Ting could decide great affairs, wanted him for chief strategist, set aside old grudges, and received him with an open heart.
entries.literal: He Shikai also, because Ting could decide great affairs, wished to make him chief strategist; therefore he set aside old enmity and waited on him with an open heart.

entries.zh: 與陸媼言於帝曰：「襄、宣、昭三帝，其子皆不得立，今至尊猶在帝位者，實由祖孝徵。
entries.en: With Dame Lu he told the emperor, "Of Emperors Xiang, Xuan, and Zhao, not one son could take the throne. That the Present Sovereign still sits there is truly Zu Xiaozheng's doing.
entries.literal: Together with Dame Lu he spoke to the emperor, saying, "Of the three emperors Xiang, Xuan, and Zhao, none of their sons could be enthroned; that the Present Sovereign still holds the imperial position is truly because of Zu Xiaozheng.

entries.zh: 此人有大功，宜報重恩。
entries.en: The man has great merit and should be repaid in full.
entries.literal: This man has great merit and ought to be repaid with heavy grace.

entries.zh: 孝徵心行雖薄，奇略出人，緩急真可憑仗。
entries.en: Xiao Zheng's heart is thin, but his stratagems surpass other men; in urgency he may truly be trusted.
entries.literal: Though Xiao Zheng's heart and conduct are thin, his strange stratagems surpass other men; in urgency he may truly be relied upon.

entries.zh: 且其雙盲，必無反意，請喚取問其謀計。」
entries.en: And he is blind in both eyes—surely he has no thought of rebellion. Summon him and ask his counsel."
entries.literal: Moreover he is blind in both eyes and surely has no thought of rebellion; please summon him and ask his plans."

entries.zh: 從之，入為銀青光祿大夫、秘書監，加開府儀同三司。
entries.en: The emperor agreed. Ting entered as silver-green grand master of the palace, director of the secretariat, and acting grand three excellencies of honor.
entries.literal: The emperor followed this; he entered office as Silver-Green Grand Master of the Palace, Director of the Secretariat, and Acting Grand Three Excellencies of Honor.

entries.zh: 和士開死後，仍說陸媼出彥深，以珽為侍中。
entries.en: After He Shikai died, Ting again urged Dame Lu to remove Yanshen and was made attendant-in-ordinary.
entries.literal: After He Shikai died, he again persuaded Dame Lu to remove Yanshen and made Ting Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 在晉陽，通密啟請誅琅邪王。
entries.en: At Jinyang he sent a secret memorial asking to execute the Prince of Langya.
entries.literal: At Jinyang he sent a secret memorial asking to execute the Prince of Langya.

entries.zh: 其計旣行，漸被任遇。
entries.en: Once the plan succeeded, favor on him grew step by step.
entries.literal: Once the plan was carried out, he was gradually entrusted with greater favor.

entries.zh: 崔季舒 祖珽
entries.en: Cui Jishu; Zu Ting
entries.literal: Cui Jishu; Zu Ting

entries.zh: 尉瑾，字安仁。
entries.en: Yu Jin, styled Anren.
entries.literal: Yu Jin, styled Anren.

entries.zh: 父慶賓，為魏肆州刺史。
entries.en: His father Qingbin had been Wei governor of Sizhou.
entries.literal: His father Qingbin was Wei governor of Sizhou.

entries.zh: 瑾少而敏悟，好學慕善。
entries.en: From youth Jin was quick-witted, loved study, and sought what was good.
entries.literal: Jin from youth was quick and perceptive, loved learning, and admired goodness.

entries.zh: 稍遷直後。
entries.en: He rose in turn to straight attendant.
entries.literal: He was gradually promoted to straight attendant.

entries.zh: 司馬子如執政，瑾取其外生皮氏女，由此擢拜中書舍人。
entries.en: When Sima Ziru held power, Jin married his maternal niece of the Pi clan and was promoted secretariat vice-director.
entries.literal: When Sima Ziru held power, Jin took his maternal niece, daughter of the Pi clan, and was thereby promoted and appointed secretariat vice-director.

entries.zh: 旣是子如姻戚，數往參詣，因與先達名輩微相款狎。
entries.en: As Ziru's kin by marriage he often called on him and grew familiar with eminent elders and men of name.
entries.literal: Being Ziru's affinal kin, he often went to call on him and thereby came to be on easy terms with eminent predecessors and noted men of the age.

entries.zh: 世宗入朝，因命瑾在鄴北宮共高德正典機密。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng came to court, Jin was ordered to Ye's northern palace to manage confidential affairs with Gao Dezheng.
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng entered the court, Jin was ordered to be at Ye's northern palace together with Gao Dezheng managing confidential affairs.

entries.zh: 肅宗輔政，累遷吏部尚書。
entries.en: When Gao Yan assisted in government, Jin rose repeatedly to minister of personnel.
entries.literal: When Gao Yan assisted in government, Jin was repeatedly promoted to minister of personnel.

entries.zh: 世祖踐祚，趙彥深本子如賓僚，元文遙、和士開並帝鄉故舊，共相薦達，任遇彌重。
entries.en: When Gao Zhan took the throne, Zhao Yanshen had been Ziru's guest-officer, and Yuan Wenyao and He Shikai were all old friends from the imperial hometown. They recommended him together, and his rank and favor grew heavier still.
entries.literal: When Gao Zhan ascended the throne, Zhao Yanshen had been a guest-officer of Ziru, Yuan Wenyao and He Shikai were all old acquaintances from the imperial hometown, and they jointly recommended and advanced him; his appointment and favor grew ever heavier.

entries.zh: 又吏部銓衡所歸，事多秘密，由是朝之幾事，頗亦預聞。
entries.en: Personnel weighing and selection also rested with him; much was secret, and so he often heard the court's weighty affairs in advance.
entries.literal: Moreover the personnel directorate's weighing and selection fell to him; affairs were mostly secret, and thereby he often heard beforehand of the court's weighty matters.

entries.zh: 尋兼右僕射，攝選，未幾即真。
entries.en: Soon he was also right vice director, acting in selection; before long the post was made formal.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally right vice director, acting in selection; before long he received the formal appointment.

entries.zh: 病卒，世祖方在三臺飲酒，文遙奏聞，遂命徹樂罷飲。
entries.en: He died of illness while Gao Zhan was drinking at Santai. Wenyao reported it, and the emperor ordered the music stopped and the drinking ended.
entries.literal: He died of illness; Gao Zhan was at the time drinking at Santai; Wenyao reported it, and the emperor ordered music withdrawn and drinking stopped.

entries.zh: 赫連子悅，字士欣，勃勃之後也。
entries.en: Helian Ziyue, styled Shixin, was descended from Helian Bobo.
entries.literal: Helian Ziyue, styled Shixin, was a descendant of Helian Bobo.

entries.zh: 魏永安初，以軍功為濟州別駕。
entries.en: In Wei's first Yong'an year he was made Jizhou separate-assistant for military merit.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yong'an under Wei he was made, for military merit, separate-assistant of Jizhou.

entries.zh: 及高祖起義，侯景為刺史，景本尒朱心腹，子悅勸景起義，景從之。
entries.en: When Gao Huan raised the righteous army, Hou Jing was governor. Jing had been Erzhu Rong's trusted man; Ziyue urged him to join the uprising, and Jing followed.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous army, Hou Jing was governor; Jing had originally been Erzhu Rong's trusted man, and Ziyue urged Jing to join the uprising; Jing followed him.

entries.zh: 除林慮守。
entries.en: He was appointed defender of Linyu.
entries.literal: He was appointed defender of Linyu.

entries.zh: 世宗往晉陽，路由是郡，因問所不便。
entries.en: Gao Cheng was bound for Jinyang and passed through the commandery, so he asked what was inconvenient.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng was going to Jinyang and passed through that commandery; he therefore asked what was inconvenient.

entries.zh: 悅答云：「臨水、武安二縣去郡遙遠，山嶺重疊，車步艱難，若東屬魏郡，則地平路近。」
entries.en: Ziyue answered, "The counties of Linshui and Wu'an lie far from the seat; mountains pile up and travel by cart or on foot is hard. If they were placed under Wei's commandery to the east, the land would be level and the road short."
entries.literal: Ziyue answered, saying, "The two counties of Linshui and Wu'an lie far from the commandery seat; mountains and ridges overlap, and cart and foot travel are hard. If they were attached east to Wei's commandery, the land would be level and the road near."

entries.zh: 世宗笑曰：「卿徒知便民，不覺損幹。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng laughed and said, "You only know how to ease the people and do not see the harm to the trunk."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng laughed and said, "You only know how to benefit the people and do not notice the harm to the trunk."

entries.zh: 子悅答云：「所言因民疾苦，不敢以私潤負心。」
entries.en: Ziyue answered, "What I said follows the people's hardship; I dare not let private gain outweigh my heart."
entries.literal: Ziyue answered, saying, "What I spoke of follows the people's hardship; I dare not let private gain outweigh my heart."

entries.zh: 世宗云：「卿能如此，甚善甚善。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng said, "You can be like this—excellent, excellent."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng said, "You can be like this—very good, very good."

entries.zh: 仍勑依事施行。
entries.en: He then ordered the change carried out as proposed.
entries.literal: He then ordered it carried out according to the proposal.

entries.zh: 在郡滿，更徵為臨漳令。
entries.en: When his commandery term ended he was summoned again as magistrate of Linzhang.
entries.literal: When his term in the commandery was complete, he was summoned again as magistrate of Linzhang.

entries.zh: 後除鄭州刺史，于時新經河清大水，民多逃散，子悅親加恤隱，戶口益增，治為天下之最。
entries.en: Later he was made governor of Zheng. The region had just suffered the Heqing great flood; many people had fled. Ziyue went in person to comfort them, households increased, and his governance ranked first in the realm.
entries.literal: Later he was made governor of Zhengzhou; at the time the region had just suffered the great flood of the Heqing era, and the people had fled in great numbers; Ziyue personally went to comfort and shelter them, households increased, and his governance ranked first in the realm.

entries.zh: 入為都官尚書，鄭州民八百餘請立碑頌德，有詔許焉。
entries.en: He entered court as director of the ministry of justice. More than eight hundred men of Zheng asked to raise a stele praising his virtue, and an edict permitted it.
entries.literal: He entered court as director of the ministry of justice; more than eight hundred men of Zhengzhou asked to erect a stele praising his virtue, and an edict permitted it.

entries.zh: 後以本官兼吏部。
entries.en: Later, while keeping his original office, he was additionally made acting in the personnel directorate.
entries.literal: Later, in his original office, he was additionally made acting in the personnel directorate.

entries.zh: 子悅在官，唯以清勤自守，旣無學術，又闕風儀，人倫清鑒，去之彌遠，一旦居銓衡之首，大招物議。
entries.en: In office Ziyue held himself only by purity and diligence. He had neither learning nor bearing, and in judging men he fell ever farther short—yet once he stood at the head of weighing and selection, he drew heavy criticism.
entries.literal: Ziyue in office relied only on purity and diligence to hold himself; he had neither learning nor bearing, and in human discernment he fell ever farther away—yet once he stood at the head of weighing and selection, he drew great criticism from the age.

entries.zh: 由是除太常卿，卒。
entries.en: Thereupon he was made director of the ministry of rites and died.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was made director of the ministry of rites and died.

entries.zh: 邕善書計，強記默識，以幹濟見知，擢為世宗大將軍府參軍。
entries.en: Yong was skilled at reckoning and accounts, remembered silently, and was known for practical ability. He was promoted staff officer in Gao Cheng's grand general's office.
entries.literal: Yong was skilled at reckoning and accounts, had a strong memory and silent retention, and was known for practical ability; he was promoted staff officer in Gao Cheng's grand general's office.

entries.zh: 及世宗崩，事出倉卒，顯祖部分將士，鎮壓四方，夜中召邕支配，造次便了，顯祖甚重之。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng died, affairs broke out in haste. Gao Yang deployed generals and soldiers to hold the four quarters, summoned Yong at night to arrange matters, and at once it was done. Gao Yang valued him greatly.
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng died, affairs arose in sudden haste; Gao Yang deployed the generals and soldiers and suppressed the four quarters; in the night he summoned Yong to arrange matters, and at once it was done—Gao Yang valued him greatly.

entries.zh: 顯祖頻年出塞，邕必陪從，專掌兵機。
entries.en: Year after year Gao Yang went beyond the frontier; Yong always accompanied him and specialized in military plans.
entries.literal: Gao Yang year after year went beyond the frontier; Yong always accompanied him and specialized in military plans.

entries.zh: 識悟閑明，承受敏速，自督將以還，軍吏以上，勞效由緒，無不諳練，每有顧問，占對如響。
entries.en: His discernment was clear and unhurried, his reception quick. From supervising generals down and army clerks up, merit and service followed the thread and none was unfamiliar; whenever he was asked, he answered like an echo.
entries.literal: His discernment was clear and unhurried, his reception quick; from supervising generals down, and military clerks and above, merit and service followed the thread and none was unfamiliar—whenever there was inquiry, his reply came like an echo.

entries.zh: 或於御前簡閱，雖三五千人，邕多不執文簿，暗唱官位姓名，未常謬誤。
entries.en: Sometimes the emperor reviewed troops before him; though three or five thousand men, Yong often held no ledger and recited office, rank, and name from memory without error.
entries.literal: Sometimes before the emperor he would review troops; though three to five thousand men, Yong often held no ledger and would recite in the dark their offices, ranks, and names, and never erred.

entries.zh: 七年，於羊汾堤講武，令邕總為諸軍節度。
entries.en: In the seventh year, at the Yangfen embankment, he lectured on military affairs and ordered Yong to command discipline for all armies.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, at the Yangfen embankment he lectured on military affairs and ordered Yong to command the discipline of all armies.

entries.zh: 事畢，仍監宴射之禮。
entries.en: When the affair ended he still oversaw the review feast and archery ritual.
entries.literal: When the affair was finished, he still oversaw the ritual of the review feast and archery.

entries.zh: 是日，顯祖親執邕手，引至太后前，坐於丞相斛律金之上，啟太后云：「唐邕強幹，一人當千。」
entries.en: That day Gao Yang took Yong's hand, led him before the empress dowager, seated him above chancellor Hulü Jin, and told her, "Tang Yong is strong and capable—one man equals a thousand."
entries.literal: That day Gao Yang personally took Yong's hand, led him before the empress dowager, seated him above Chancellor Hulü Jin, and told the empress dowager, saying, "Tang Yong is strong and capable—one man equals a thousand."

entries.zh: 仍別賜錦彩錢帛。
entries.en: He then separately bestowed brocade, silk, cash, and goods.
entries.literal: He then separately bestowed brocade, silk, cash, and goods.

entries.zh: 邕非唯強濟明辨，然亦善揣上意，進取多途，是以恩寵日隆，委任彌重。
entries.en: Yong was not only strong, capable, bright, and discerning; he also knew how to read the sovereign's intent and had many paths of advance, so favor grew daily and commission grew heavier.
entries.literal: Yong was not only strong, capable, bright, and discerning; he also knew how to gauge the sovereign's intent, and his paths of advancement were many—therefore favor daily grew and commission grew ever heavier.

entries.zh: 顯祖又嘗對邕白太后云：「唐邕分明強記，每有軍機大事，手作文書，口且處分，耳又聽受，實是異人。」
entries.en: Gao Yang also once told the empress dowager before Yong, "Tang Yong distinguishes clearly and remembers strongly. On great military affairs he writes documents by hand, gives orders by mouth, and listens with his ear at once—truly a different man."
entries.literal: Gao Yang also once said to Yong before the empress dowager, "Tang Yong distinguishes clearly and remembers strongly; whenever there is a weighty military affair, he writes documents by hand, gives orders by mouth, and listens with his ear at the same time—truly a different man."

entries.zh: 一日之中，六度賜物。
entries.en: In a single day he was given gifts six times.
entries.literal: In a single day he was six times given gifts.

entries.zh: 又嘗解所服青鼠皮裘賜邕，云：「朕意在車馬衣裘與卿共弊。」
entries.en: He also once removed the blue sable coat he was wearing and gave it to Yong, saying, "My intent is that carriages, horses, clothes, and furs be worn out together with you."
entries.literal: He also once removed the blue sable fur coat he was wearing and bestowed it on Yong, saying, "My intent is that carriages, horses, clothes, and furs be worn out together with you."

entries.zh: 十年，從幸晉陽，除兼給事黃門侍郎，領中書舍人。
entries.en: In the tenth year, on the progress to Jinyang, Yong was made acting attendant of the yellow gate and leading secretariat vice-director.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, accompanying the imperial progress to Jinyang, he was made acting attendant of the yellow gate and leading secretariat vice-director.

entries.zh: 顯祖嘗登童子佛寺，望幷州城曰：「此是何等城？」
entries.en: Gao Yang once climbed Tongzi Buddhist temple, looked toward Bingzhou city, and said, "What sort of city is this?"
entries.literal: Gao Yang once ascended the Tongzi Buddhist temple, looked toward Bingzhou city, and said, "What sort of city is this?"

entries.zh: 或曰：「此是金城湯池，天府之國。」
entries.en: Someone said, "This is a metal rampart and boiling moat—the realm's heavenly storehouse."
entries.literal: Someone said, "This is a metal rampart and boiling moat, a realm of heaven's storehouse."

entries.zh: 帝云：「我謂唐邕是金城，此非金城也。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "I say Tang Yong is the metal rampart; this is not the metal rampart."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "I say Tang Yong is the metal rampart; this is not the metal rampart."

entries.zh: 其見重如此。
entries.en: Such was the weight in which he was held.
entries.literal: Such was the weight in which he was held.

entries.zh: 其後語邕曰：「卿劬勞旣久，欲除卿作州，頻勑楊遵彥更求一人堪代卿者。
entries.en: Afterward he said to Yong, "Your toil has been long. I wished to make you governor of a province and repeatedly ordered Yang Zunyan to find another man who could replace you.
entries.literal: Afterward he said to Yong, "Your toil has been long; I wished to make you governor of a province and repeatedly ordered Yang Zunyan to find another man who could replace you.

entries.zh: 遵彥云比遍訪文武，如卿之徒實不可得，所以遂停此意。
entries.en: Zunyan said that having searched civil and military men everywhere, a man like you truly cannot be found, and so this intent was stopped.
entries.literal: Zunyan said that having searched everywhere among civil and military men, men like you truly cannot be obtained, and so this intent was stopped.

entries.zh: 卿宜勉之。」
entries.en: You should strive on."
entries.literal: You should strive on."

entries.zh: 顯祖或時切責侍臣不稱旨者：「觀卿等舉措，不中與唐邕作奴。」
entries.en: Gao Yang sometimes sharply rebuked attending ministers who missed his intent: "Watch how you comport yourselves—you are not fit to be Tang Yong's slaves."
