entries.literal: Gao Yang sometimes sharply rebuked attending ministers who did not suit his intent: "Watch how you comport yourselves—you are not fit to be Tang Yong's slaves."

entries.zh: 其見賞遇多此類。
entries.en: His favor and treatment were mostly of this sort.
entries.literal: His favor and treatment were mostly of this sort.

entries.zh: 及世祖崩，僕射和士開先恒侍疾，秘喪三日不發。
entries.en: When Gao Zhan died, vice director He Shikai had long attended his illness and kept the mourning secret for three days without announcing it.
entries.literal: When Gao Zhan died, Vice Director He Shikai had long attended his illness and kept the mourning secret for three days without announcing it.

entries.zh: 子琮問士開不發喪之意。
entries.en: Zicong asked He Shikai why he had not announced the mourning.
entries.literal: Zicong asked He Shikai why he did not announce the mourning.

entries.zh: 士開引神武、文襄初崩並秘喪不舉，至尊年少，恐王公有貳心，意欲普追集涼風堂，然後與詳議。
entries.en: He Shikai said that when Gao Huan and Gao Cheng first died, mourning had likewise been kept secret. The sovereign was young; he feared the princes and dukes might waver, and meant to gather everyone at the Cool Breeze Hall before discussing matters in full.
entries.literal: He Shikai cited that when Gao Huan and Gao Cheng first died, mourning was likewise kept secret; the sovereign was young and he feared the princes and dukes might harbor divided hearts; he intended to summon everyone to the Cool Breeze Hall and then discuss in detail.

entries.zh: 時太尉錄尚書事趙郡王叡先恒居內，預帷幄之謀，子琮素知士開忌叡及領軍臨淮王婁定遠，恐其矯遺詔出叡外任，奪定遠禁衛之權，因答云：「大行，神武之子，今上又是先皇傳位，群臣富貴者皆是至尊父子之恩，但令在內貴臣一無改易，王公已下必無異望。
entries.en: At the time grand mentor and recorder of the masters of writing affairs, Prince of Zhao commandery Rui, had long lived inside the palace and shared counsel at the curtain. Zicong knew He Shikai resented Rui and general-in-chief of the guards Prince of Linhuai Lou Dingyuan and feared they might forge the final edict to send Rui out on provincial duty and strip Dingyuan of the guard command. He answered, "The late emperor was Gao Huan's son, and the present sovereign too received the throne from his predecessor. Every minister's wealth came from the sovereign father and son. Leave the great men inside the court unchanged, and the princes and dukes below will surely have no other wish.
entries.literal: At the time Grand Mentor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Affairs Prince of Zhao commandery Rui had long dwelt within the palace and took part in counsel at the curtain; Zicong had long known He Shikai resented Rui and General-in-Chief of the Guards Prince of Linhuai Lou Dingyuan, and feared they might forge the final edict to send Rui out on external appointment and strip Dingyuan of guard authority; therefore he answered, saying, "The late emperor was Gao Huan's son, and the present sovereign likewise received the throne from the former emperor. Every minister's wealth and rank came from father and son's grace to the sovereign. If the honored men within the court are left wholly unchanged, the princes and dukes below will surely harbor no other intent.

entries.zh: 世異事殊，不得與霸朝相比。
entries.en: Times and affairs differ; this cannot be compared with the founding reign.
entries.literal: Times and affairs differ; this cannot be compared with the founding reign.

entries.zh: 且公出宮門已經數日，升遐之事，行路皆傳，久而不舉，恐有他變。」
entries.en: Moreover, sir, you have been outside the palace gates for days already, and news of the emperor's passing travels every road. Delay mourning too long and I fear some other turn may come."
entries.literal: Moreover, sir, you have been outside the palace gates already several days; news of the emperor's passing spreads on every road. If mourning is long delayed, I fear some other change may arise."

entries.zh: 於是乃發喪。
entries.en: Thereupon mourning was announced.
entries.literal: Thereupon mourning was announced.

entries.zh: 天統元年，世祖禪位後主。
entries.en: In the first year of Tiantong, Shizu abdicated in favor of the Later Sovereign.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tiantong, Shizu abdicated in favor of the Later Sovereign.

entries.zh: 世祖御正殿，謂子琮曰：「少君左右宜得正人，以卿心存正直，今以後事相委。」
entries.en: Shizu sat in the main hall and told Zicong, "The young lord should have upright men around him. Because your heart is upright and true, I now entrust later affairs to you."
entries.literal: Shizu sat in the main hall and said to Zicong, "The young lord should have upright men at his side. Because your heart is upright and true, I now entrust later affairs to you."

entries.zh: 除給事黃門侍郎，領主衣都統。
entries.en: He was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Chief Commander of Imperial Clothing.
entries.literal: He was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Chief Commander of Imperial Clothing.
